families.name: Warrior
families.tagline: Steel forgives nothing; the drill-yard rewards everything.
families.description: The Warrior asks for nothing you were born with. No bloodline, no pact, no whispered patron — only a body, a weapon, and the willingness to repeat one motion until it stops being a motion and becomes you. Warriors fill the world's garrisons and free companies, and from their mud-floored drill-yards every road of Might begins.

nodes.name: Warrior
nodes.role: Frontline melee — versatile and durable
nodes.lore: Every garrison keeps them: farm sons and gutter orphans who traded whatever came before for a spear and a bunk. Most die unremembered. The ones who survive their first winter learn what the drill-yards teach — that steel forgives nothing and rewards everything, and that a body, patiently punished, can be re-forged into an instrument.
nodes.playstyle: Straightforward frontline melee. Manage stamina, hold your ground, and trade blows with unglamorous efficiency while deciding which road calls louder — the perfected self, or the company.

abilities.name: Measured Cut
abilities.desc: A drilled strike that cannot glance; deals full weapon damage even against a raised guard.

abilities.name: Set the Feet
abilities.desc: Brace for one round: knockbacks, trips, and shoves against you fail, and blocked damage is halved.

abilities.name: Soldier's Wind
abilities.desc: Once per fight, recover a burst of stamina and shake off one bleed or daze.

abilities.name: Yard Callus
abilities.desc: Passive: each week of campaigning grants small permanent gains to carry weight and fatigue resistance.

progressionSteps: Present yourself at any muster, garrison, or free company; bring nothing but two working hands.
Survive your first winter of drills — the yard at dawn, the wall at dusk, blisters into callus.
Stand your first real fight without breaking. What you do after the fear arrives decides everything.
Bury a comrade, then report for drill the next morning.

nodes.name: Drillsworn
nodes.role: Melee striker — precision single-target
nodes.lore: Some soldiers discover the company was only ever a scabbard for the self. The Drillsworn take a private vow: ten thousand repetitions of every cut before they may claim its name. Officers find them in the yard at midnight, alone, correcting a wrist angle that no one else alive can see.
nodes.playstyle: Precise single-target melee. Build tempo through repeated engagement; feints and drilled counters punish anything predictable. Weaker amid chaos, lethal wherever the fight narrows to one.

abilities.name: Ten-Thousandth Repetition
abilities.desc: Passive: consecutive strikes against one target each land truer than the last, stacking until you switch targets.

abilities.name: Feint in Tempo
abilities.desc: Sell a false opening; if the enemy takes it, your true strike ignores their armor.

abilities.name: Single Combat
abilities.desc: Mark one foe: you read them fully, gaining counters against them while dropping guard against all others.

abilities.name: Edge Discipline
abilities.desc: Passive: your weapon never dulls, jams, or slips, and disarm attempts against you all but fail.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10 and swear the Drill-Vow before a witness who has themselves sworn it.
Perform one cut ten thousand times, counted honestly. The count restarts the first time you lie.
Defeat your own drill instructor using the weapon they taught you.
Fight one full campaign without a wasted motion — every strike thrown must land or teach.

nodes.name: Bannerhand
nodes.role: Frontline support — orders and morale
nodes.lore: When the standard-bearer falls, someone catches the pole before it touches the mud. That reflex — reaching for the weight of everyone else — is what quartermasters watch for. A Bannerhand holds no commission at first; they hold the thing itself, the cloth a company follows after its officers are dead.
nodes.playstyle: Frontline support and control. Plant the standard, anchor allies to its shadow, and spend your own guard freely to keep the line's shape from breaking.

abilities.name: Raise the Standard
abilities.desc: Plant your banner: allies within its shadow resist fear and strike steadier while it stands.

abilities.name: The Voice That Carries
abilities.desc: Shout an order over any din; one ally immediately moves or strikes out of turn.

abilities.name: Shoulder the Line
abilities.desc: Redirect a portion of the damage dealt to any adjacent ally onto your own guard.

abilities.name: Forced March
abilities.desc: Your company covers a further span each day and delays all fatigue penalties until camp.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10 and carry the company standard through one engagement without letting it touch the ground.
Learn every soldier's name in your file, and the name each one calls out in their sleep.
Rally a broken line using only your voice. If they re-form, the rank is yours.
Refuse a promotion that would take you off the line.

nodes.name: Halfsword
nodes.role: Duelist — bind, control, armor-piercing
nodes.lore: Duels in the border towns are settled close: gauntlet on the blade, pommel raised, breath shared. Halfswords study the crossing itself — that grinding half-second where two weapons argue. They are hired to end quarrels the courts cannot, and they walk out of rooms that other fighters are carried from.
nodes.playstyle: Close-range duelist. Bind the enemy's weapon, deny every disengage, and win the grapple-distance argument with armor-slipping thrusts and pommel strokes. Helpless against numbers, near-certain alone.

abilities.name: Grip the Blade
abilities.desc: A halfsword thrust at grappling range that slides through visor slits and joint gaps, ignoring plate entirely.

abilities.name: The Bind
abilities.desc: Lock weapons with a foe; neither of you may disengage, and you win every contested crossing.

abilities.name: Murder-Stroke
abilities.desc: Reverse the blade and swing the pommel; against a helmeted foe this dazes straight through the steel.

abilities.name: Read the Shoulder
abilities.desc: Passive: enemies telegraph to you; the first attack in each exchange grants you a free counter-thrust.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and win seven witnessed duels without taking a wound past the first.
Grip your own blade barehanded and drive it through a breastplate. Learn what the edge permits.
Study one opponent for a month before fighting them, then end the duel inside three exchanges.
Decline a duel you would have won, because the cause was rotten. The refusal is the lesson.

nodes.name: Edgewright
nodes.role: Burst striker — single decisive cuts
nodes.lore: In the high passes stand shrines of split stones, each cloven by a single stroke and signed with a maker's mark. Edgewrights leave them. They pursue the one honest cut — the motion with nothing extra in it — and grade their entire lives against falling silk and standing water.
nodes.playstyle: Deliberate burst striker. Long setups and ruinous single strikes; draw-cuts from the scabbard that resolve whole fights in one motion. Patience is the true resource.

abilities.name: Draw-Cut
abilities.desc: Strike from the scabbard in one motion; against an unwounded target it always lands first and cannot be parried.

abilities.name: One Motion
abilities.desc: Merge parry and cut: a successful defense this round is simultaneously a full-damage riposte.

abilities.name: Cut the Falling Leaf
abilities.desc: A strike so clean the target feels nothing for a breath; the delayed wound resolves doubled.

abilities.name: Whetstone Rite
abilities.desc: An hour's ritual sharpening: your next three cuts sever material one grade harder than steel should allow.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and cut a hanging silk scarf so cleanly that both halves settle before the wind notices.
Forge or commission a blade fitted to your hand alone, and never lend it.
Spend a season cutting only air, until an Edgewright of standing certifies your motion holds nothing wasted.
Split a standing stone with one stroke, and sign it.

nodes.name: Linebreaker
nodes.role: Assault leader — breach and momentum
nodes.lore: Every siege has a moment when the wall opens and someone must be first into the smoke. Linebreakers volunteer twice. They command the worst thirty yards in the world — the breach, the gate, the ladder-top — and free companies bid against each other for a muster-roll carrying such a name.
nodes.playstyle: Momentum-driven assault leader. Charge first, hit hardest at the point of entry, and drag your squad through the gap you tore before it closes.

abilities.name: First Through
abilities.desc: Entering a space held by three or more enemies grants you a surge of guard and a free strike.

abilities.name: Weight of the Charge
abilities.desc: Your first strike's damage scales with every yard you crossed to deliver it.

abilities.name: On Me
abilities.desc: Allies who follow your charge this round share your speed and half your momentum bonus.

abilities.name: Doorbreaker
abilities.desc: Your strikes deal quadruple damage to gates, barricades, shields, and anything else pretending to be a wall.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and be first through a defended breach three times. Volunteering counts only if you live.
Carry a wounded soldier back out through the gap you led them into.
Take a gate from the inside with fewer than ten at your back.
Have your name written first on a storming-party's roll — by someone else's hand.

nodes.name: Ironmuster
nodes.role: Line commander — discipline and attrition
nodes.lore: Armies are not raised; they are manufactured, and Ironmusters run the forge. They hammer levied plowboys into ranks that hold, count arrows and bread with the same cold arithmetic, and hold that glory is a rumor started by people who never smelled a supply train burn.
nodes.playstyle: Defensive line commander. Position allies precisely, ration everyone's stamina including the enemy's, and grind battles down into arithmetic your side was built to win.

abilities.name: Dress the Line
abilities.desc: Reposition any allies in earshot by one rank; the corrected line gains guard until it breaks formation.

abilities.name: Attrition Doctrine
abilities.desc: Passive: enemies attacking your formation spend double stamina; your ranks spend half.

abilities.name: Quartermaster's Eye
abilities.desc: Passive: your company consumes fewer supplies and shrugs off weather, hunger, and forced-march fatigue.

abilities.name: No Step Back
abilities.desc: Allies adjacent to you cannot be pushed, routed, or frightened out of position.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and train one hundred raw recruits to hold formation under a cavalry feint.
March a company two hundred miles and arrive with more discipline than you left with.
Hold ground you were ordered to hold until the order changes, whatever crosses the field.
Court-martial a friend fairly. The muster is owed the truth more than you are owed comfort.

nodes.name: Doomfencer
nodes.role: Execution duelist — sanctioned single combat
nodes.lore: When a verdict must lie beyond appeal, crowns send for a Doomfencer. They fight judicial duels as officers of the court, in black quilting, before witnesses the law requires to watch. Perhaps forty hold the office across the known kingdoms. Their arrival in a city settles most lawsuits by itself.
nodes.playstyle: Sanctioned execution duelist. Isolate one opponent under formal challenge, convert their every error into mounting counters, and close with strokes the law itself has blessed.

abilities.name: Sentence of Steel
abilities.desc: Formally challenge one foe: both of you are bound to the duel until one yields, falls, or dies.

abilities.name: Court of One
abilities.desc: While your duel stands, no outside blow can reach either duelist; the world is reduced to witness.

abilities.name: Weighed and Wanting
abilities.desc: Passive: every miss your duel opponent makes grants you an escalating counter that cannot itself miss.

abilities.name: Black Verdict
abilities.desc: Against a duel opponent below a quarter of their health, deliver the sanctioned stroke: it kills, cleanly, always.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and stand judicial champion in a capital trial, a kingdom's law resting on your point.
Kill a Doomfencer in office, or be named successor by one retiring — the office admits no third door.
Fight one duel you believe unjust, and let it teach you exactly what the office costs.
Swear before the bench to accept every lawful challenge, forever, regardless of who offers it.

nodes.name: Severant
nodes.role: Nova striker — one prepared, absolute cut
nodes.lore: High on the scarps lives an order that has cut everything else away — property, names, speech on certain days. Severants hold that every problem has a grain, like wood, and that a sufficiently honest edge will find it. Lowlanders climb for months to ask them for one stroke. Sometimes they descend.
nodes.playstyle: Ascetic nova striker. Fights last one motion or none; everything before the cut is positioning, breathing, and an absolute refusal to be hurried.

abilities.name: Sever the Question
abilities.desc: One prepared stroke that ignores all armor, guard, and mitigation; preparing it costs an entire round of stillness.

abilities.name: Cut Water
abilities.desc: Your strike passes through parries and blocks as if through current; only distance defends against it.

abilities.name: Nothing Wasted
abilities.desc: Passive: any cut that kills refunds its full cost; a finished fight leaves you unspent.

abilities.name: The Pared Self
abilities.desc: Passive: feints, taunts, illusions, and pain cannot move you; your tempo belongs to you alone.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40, climb to the Severed Order's scarp, and leave your possessions at the treeline.
Keep silence for a hundred days, drilling the same cut at dawn and at dusk.
Sever a falling waterfall so the stream stutters. The elders will hear it and come down.
Cut away one thing you love. The order does not say which. You will know.

nodes.name: Forlorn Captain
nodes.role: Vanguard commander — first-wave shock and rally
nodes.lore: The forlorn hope is the first wave into a breach — soldiers counted dead at signing. A Forlorn Captain has led it and lived, more than once, which armies regard as something between skill and blasphemy. Veterans wear their captains' names inked on their arms: a roll of the saved.
nodes.playstyle: Vanguard commander. Open every battle personally, convert the first minutes of violence into a beachhead, and make desperate allies fight like cornered kings.

abilities.name: Hope of the Doomed
abilities.desc: Allies below half health within your sight deal heavier damage and cannot flee while you still advance.

abilities.name: First Wave
abilities.desc: In an engagement's opening rounds, you and every soldier who signed your roll strike twice.

abilities.name: Carry the Fallen
abilities.desc: Drag a downed ally at full speed while fighting one-handed, without penalty.

abilities.name: The Breach Holds
abilities.desc: A gap you open in an enemy line stays open; enemies cannot re-form ranks around you.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and lead a forlorn hope through the wall, bringing more than half your roll out alive.
Be given up for dead by your own army, then report for duty.
Turn down the general's tent. Captains of the hope sleep where the ladders are stacked.
Learn your letters if you lack them — someone must write to the families afterward, and it should be you.

nodes.name: Standfast
nodes.role: Bulwark commander — immovable defense
nodes.lore: Some ground cannot be lost, so the crowns keep the Standfast: a small order sworn to hold named places — a bridge, a pass, a stair — until relieved or dead. Their muster-book lists positions, not people. In four centuries it records eleven retreats, each one ordered, none of them chosen.
nodes.playstyle: Immovable bulwark commander. Fortify a position, rotate your line like a machine, and outlast anything the enemy can afford to keep sending at it.

abilities.name: This Ground Is Ours
abilities.desc: Name the ground you hold: allies standing on it take reduced damage and cannot fail morale.

abilities.name: Rotation Drill
abilities.desc: Swap fatigued front-rank allies with rested rear ranks instantly, without ever opening the wall.

abilities.name: Outlast
abilities.desc: Passive: each hour a battle continues, your formation's guard and stamina recovery climb.

abilities.name: The Wall Speaks
abilities.desc: A single shout halts a rout; fleeing allies within earshot stop, turn, and re-form on you.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and hold a named position through a siege of no fewer than forty days.
Recite the muster-book's eleven retreats from memory before the order's eldest, and say what each one cost.
Refuse relief once, because the relieving column was needed elsewhere more.
Add one position to the book, and be the first name sworn to it.

nodes.name: Swordtaker
nodes.role: Control duelist — disarms and bloodless verdicts
nodes.lore: Where the Doomfencer's stroke closes a case, the Swordtaker's answer is that no case should close in a grave. They hire into blood-feuds as champions — sometimes for both sides at once — and end them by emptying every hand involved. Each taken sword hangs in the order's hall, labeled, until its owner comes to ask for it back politely.
nodes.playstyle: Nonlethal control duelist. Win the bind, strip weapons, exhaust tempers, and end fights with the opponent standing, empty-handed, and oddly grateful. Killing is available, and beneath you.

abilities.name: Empty the Hand
abilities.desc: Win a contested bind to send the enemy's weapon into your off hand; they cannot recover it while you stand.

abilities.name: Flat of the Blade
abilities.desc: Any strike of yours may deal its full damage nonlethally; a foe dropped this way wakes disarmed and honor-bound to yield the quarrel.

abilities.name: The Longer Argument
abilities.desc: Passive: each round a duel continues, your opponent's stamina drains faster and your binds grow harder to refuse.

abilities.name: Hang the Sword
abilities.desc: A foe you disarm must pass a test of will to continue the quarrel by any means; most do not.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and end seven blood-feuds as hired champion, leaving every principal alive — including the ones who fought hardest to die.
Take the sword of a duelist who came to kill you, and hang it in the hall with the edge dressed and the name spelled right.
Stand opposite a Doomfencer in a lawful duel and end it with both of you breathing. The courts are still arguing the verdict.
Refuse the killing stroke with your own life at stake, and win anyway. The order watches for exactly this.

nodes.name: Sellstroke
nodes.role: Burst striker — commissioned single cuts
nodes.lore: The Severed Order climbed away from the world; the Sellstrokes stayed to take its commissions. Guildhalls in every port post their rates: mooring chains parted in storms, millstones trued, gallows ropes cut at the king's late mercy. They hold that falling silk proves nothing — only need can grade an edge honestly, and need pays.
nodes.playstyle: Deliberate burst striker for hire. Scout the job, quote the stroke, deliver one exact cut under the worst conditions on offer — storm, riot, collapsing mine — and collect.

abilities.name: Working Conditions
abilities.desc: Passive: weather, darkness, footing, and panic impose no penalty on any cut you were given time to quote.

abilities.name: The Quoted Cut
abilities.desc: Name your target and price aloud; your next strike against that target cannot miss, glance, or be parried.

abilities.name: Journeyman's Eye
abilities.desc: Passive: you read the grain of any material or guard at a glance, and know where one stroke would part it.

abilities.name: Rope, Chain, and Bone
abilities.desc: Your cut severs one object per swing regardless of thickness, and deals doubled damage to rigging, harness, and siegework.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40, post your rates in a chartered guildhall, and honor the first seven commissions however bad the weather turns.
Part a mooring chain in a running storm, one stroke, before the ship is lost. Collect afterward.
Refuse the Severed Order's invitation to the scarp. Send back a fair quote for their waterfall instead.
Cut something for no fee, once, and tell no one. The guild pretends this rule is not written down.

nodes.name: Knockunder
nodes.role: Siege sapper — undermining and tunnel fighting
nodes.lore: The forlorn hope goes over the wall; the Knockunder has been beneath it since spring. They dig the galleries, fire the props, and fight the counter-mine knife-work no ballad has the stomach for — dark, close, listening. Garrisons name them for the sound that comes up through chapel floors when surrender has quietly stopped being an option.
nodes.playstyle: Subterranean siege specialist. Fight blind and close in spaces one shoulder wide, drop chosen ground under chosen enemies, and never once hurry.

abilities.name: Listening Watch
abilities.desc: Passive: you sense movement, weight, and digging through earth and stone within sixty feet, waking or sleeping.

abilities.name: Fire the Props
abilities.desc: Collapse a tunnel, floor, or wall you have undermined; whatever stood on it drops one story onto ground you prepared.

abilities.name: Gallery Fighting
abilities.desc: Passive: in darkness or confined spaces you strike first, and enemies larger than you lose every advantage of size.

abilities.name: The Knock
abilities.desc: Strike the earth three times; every enemy above who hears it must check morale, because they know what it means.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and bring down a curtain wall from below without losing one digger to the counter-mine.
Win a knife-fight in a gallery too low to kneel in. Then finish the shift.
Lie still a day and a night while counter-miners listen for you through three feet of clay.
Stay below during the storming. The wall coming down was the whole argument; the applause belongs to whoever wants it.

nodes.name: Barefield
nodes.role: Attrition commander — withdrawal and denial
nodes.lore: The Standfast hold that some ground cannot be lost; the Barefields have never met such ground. Their doctrine burns granaries, fouls wells, lifts whole villages onto carts, and hands the enemy mile after mile of nothing to eat. The order's muster-book records no positions at all — only armies, every one of which came home.
nodes.playstyle: Withdrawal-and-denial commander. Trade space for time, bleed pursuit at every ford, and run the deadliest rearguard alive. Done perfectly, winning looks exactly like leaving.

abilities.name: Bare the Field
abilities.desc: Country you withdraw through yields the enemy no forage, water, or shelter; their attrition losses double until they resupply from home.

abilities.name: Rearguard Arithmetic
abilities.desc: Passive: allies under your command take reduced damage while retreating, and your rearguard strikes pursuers as if charging.

abilities.name: Lift the Village
abilities.desc: Evacuate a settlement in one night — people, herds, hinges, bells — leaving nothing an army could use or avenge.

abilities.name: A Mile for a Day
abilities.desc: Each mile yielded in good order grants your army a day's worth of rest, repair, and rations saved.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and bring an outnumbered army home through two hundred hostile miles without offering battle once.
Burn your own family's granary first, so the order knows you will not flinch at anyone else's.
Hold a ford with twelve soldiers for one hour, then be gone before the enemy can write down what happened.
Read the Standfast muster-book, all eleven retreats, and account for what each would have cost your way: nothing.

nodes.name: The Unanswered
nodes.role: Apex duelist — perfect counters
nodes.lore: Histories disagree about everything except the count: no riposte has ever landed. The Unanswered is less a person than a standing question — dueling culture across three kingdoms is one long argument about a fighter most living people have never seen draw, because the draw is the end of it.
nodes.playstyle: Perfect counter-duelist. You act inside your opponent's hesitations; fights are decided before observers understand they have begun. Numbers do not matter — there is only ever one opponent at a time.

abilities.name: Final Tempo
abilities.desc: Passive: you act in the instant between an enemy's decision and their motion; you always move first.

abilities.name: No Second Exchange
abilities.desc: Your riposte resolves the duel: a landed counter ends the target's capacity to continue, one way or another.

abilities.name: Perfect Measure
abilities.desc: Passive: you dictate the exact distance of every engagement; enemies cannot flank, crowd, or reach you unwilled.

abilities.name: The Question
abilities.desc: An enemy who watches you draw must pass a test of will or decline to fight you at all.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 bearing no recorded wound from single combat since your Doomfencer oath.
Answer one hundred lawful challenges, and let none of them become a second exchange.
Duel a sitting Doomfencer before every crowned witness alive; leave them living, unmarked, and finished with swords.
Refuse the last challenge ever offered you, and let the silence that follows stand as your successor.

nodes.name: Hundredth Form
nodes.role: Apex striker — one absolute stroke
nodes.lore: The order teaches ninety-nine forms and admits a hundredth exists: unteachable, arrived at only by exhausting the others. Once in a generation, someone stops drilling mid-motion and does not resume, because they are finished. Mountainsides where such people have cut carry weather-smooth scars. Farmers plow around them without being told why.
nodes.playstyle: Apex single-strike fighter. One drawn breath, one motion, one ended thing per encounter; everything else is the walking between cuts.

abilities.name: The Hundredth Form
abilities.desc: Once per day, the unteachable cut: one target, structure, or obstacle simply ends. No roll is made.

abilities.name: Ten Thousand Days
abilities.desc: Passive: your techniques cost no stamina; a lifetime of drilling has paid every bill in advance.

abilities.name: Stillness Before
abilities.desc: While your blade is sheathed you cannot be surprised, hastened, or made to move first.

abilities.name: Cut the Uncuttable
abilities.desc: Your edge severs what edges cannot: stone, siege chain, tempered plate, and the momentum of a charge.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and perform all ninety-nine forms before the assembled order without one correction offered.
Cut something the order agrees cannot be cut, in a single stroke, with the elders watching.
Give away the blade fitted to your hand alone, and cut as well with whatever is handed to you.
Perform the hundredth form once. There is no second performance; the order will raise your shrine from the pieces.

nodes.name: Ruin of Gates
nodes.role: Apex assault — siege-ending offense
nodes.lore: Certain cities surrender when a particular banner crests the hill, reasoning that their walls are already gone in every way that matters. The Ruin of Gates has ended more sieges by arriving than by fighting, and the masons of six kingdoms curse the name professionally, the way sailors curse a reef.
nodes.playstyle: Siege-ending assault apex. Collapse fortifications personally, chain-rally whole armies into the gap, and convert one breach into a general surrender within the hour.

abilities.name: The Gate Remembers
abilities.desc: Passive: your melee strikes deal siege-engine damage; gates, walls, and towers count as valid single targets.

abilities.name: Follow Me or Mourn Me
abilities.desc: A battle-wide rally: every ally who can see your banner joins the charge carrying your momentum bonuses.

abilities.name: Hundredth Hope
abilities.desc: Once per battle, a blow that would kill you while advancing simply fails.

abilities.name: Terms at the Wall
abilities.desc: Offer surrender mid-assault; a shaken garrison must genuinely weigh it, checking morale at heavy penalty.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and take a city sung as untakeable, its gate opened by your own hands.
Survive your hundredth forlorn hope, until the muster-clerks stop entering your name among the dead.
Accept a fortress's surrender offered to your banner alone, before your army has arrived.
Rebuild one city you broke, stone by stone, and garrison it with the soldiers you led through its wall.

nodes.name: Sovereign of Hosts
nodes.role: Apex commander — army-scale command
nodes.lore: When the muster-horns pass a certain name down the valleys, farms empty by choice. The Sovereign of Hosts commands no standing army; they are owed one — by veterans, by veterans' sons, by kingdoms that remember. Historians have taken to measuring wars by whether this person was in them.
nodes.playstyle: Army-scale apex commander. Personally modest in the melee, overwhelming in aggregate: every ally fights as if drilled by your hand, because most of them were.

abilities.name: Ten Thousand Answer
abilities.desc: Sound the muster: within days, veteran companies arrive owing you service no coin could buy.

abilities.name: The Field Entire
abilities.desc: Passive: you perceive the whole battlefield as a single shape; all allies act on your initiative.

abilities.name: Worth a Legion
abilities.desc: An enemy force that learns you command must check morale before offering battle at all.

abilities.name: One Voice
abilities.desc: Your orders reach every ally on the field regardless of distance, din, or dying.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and raise ten thousand soldiers with no coin offered — only your name on the summons.
Win a war the historians agree was unwinnable, then disband the army when they beg you to keep it.
Train the sergeant who trains the sergeants of three kingdoms' armies.
Speak once on a field where two hosts stand ready, and send both home unblooded.

nodes.name: The Bloodless
nodes.role: Apex duelist — victory without harm
nodes.lore: Chroniclers quarrel over everything about the Bloodless except the count of the dead, which is nothing. Kingdoms now settle wars by sending champions against one, knowing both armies march home. Some witnesses swear they have never actually seen the Bloodless strike — only opponents discovering, mid-lunge, that their hands were somehow empty.
nodes.playstyle: Perfect nonlethal apex. Disarm anything that can be held, calm anything that can be angered, and end battles by subtraction until nobody present is armed. Including you.

abilities.name: Empty Every Hand
abilities.desc: Once per battle, disarm all enemies who can see you; their weapons arrive at your feet, politely arranged.

abilities.name: Quarrel's End
abilities.desc: Strike the weapon and not the wielder to cut the quarrel itself; the feud's cause must be argued again from nothing.

abilities.name: No Blood Today
abilities.desc: Passive: nothing dies in a fight you preside over unless you permit it; killing blows nearby resolve as yields instead.

abilities.name: The Gentle Terror
abilities.desc: Passive: enemies who know your record must pass a test of will or lay down arms; the gentleness is the frightening part.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 with no death recorded against your point since the day you swore to take swords, not lives.
End a war by champions' duel, and walk both champions home alive to their own camps.
Hang the thousandth taken sword in the order's hall, and let its owner die of nothing worse than age.
Be challenged by one who has studied every account of you, and leave them unharmed, holding nothing, unsure it has begun.

nodes.name: The Civil Blade
nodes.role: Apex striker — monumental public cuts
nodes.lore: Six towns keep documents proving the Civil Blade was born there; two are forgeries, and historians cannot agree which. What stands is the work: the winter pass opened in an afternoon, the flood turned down a channel one stroke wide, the harbor reef gone between tides. Whole provinces eat because of cuts that took one motion.
nodes.playstyle: Monumental apex striker. Your cuts operate at landscape scale — fell the cliff, not the soldiers on it — and every stroke doubles as engineering the enemy cannot answer.

abilities.name: One Stroke Wide
abilities.desc: Cut a permanent channel, breach, or pass through any terrain feature; the map is redrawn where you swung.

abilities.name: Civic Works
abilities.desc: Passive: allies moving through ground you have cut travel faster, camp safely, and drink clean; your work remembers its purpose.

abilities.name: Name the Day
abilities.desc: Declare a fortification and a date; unless honestly bought off, on that date it opens. Garrisons believe you, with reason.

abilities.name: The Day's Work
abilities.desc: Once per day, finish in one motion a cutting labor that should take a hundred workers a season.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and open a trade pass through standing mountain before the first snow closes it. Charge fairly.
Turn a river in flood down a channel of your own cutting, and accept the statue the city insists on, facing the water.
Cut for six crowns in one year without any of them learning what the others paid.
Make one cut nobody commissioned and nobody witnessed. Let the geographers find it slowly.

nodes.name: The Buried Siege
nodes.role: Apex sapper — fortress-scale undermining
nodes.lore: Somewhere under the border marches one siege has been running for decades, never lifted, and every fortress in the world may already stand inside it. Surveyors keep finding old galleries under keeps that were never besieged — shored, swept, patient. The Buried Siege has never demanded a surrender. Garrisons offer anyway, addressing the letters downward.
nodes.playstyle: Fortress-scale apex sapper. Any battlefield becomes yours after a night's digging; you decide what ground exists, and choose the moment it stops existing.

abilities.name: Already Beneath
abilities.desc: Passive: fortifications more than a decade old count as undermined by you; collapse one section of one per siege.

abilities.name: The Long Gallery
abilities.desc: Your galleries connect: move troops through workings no map records, emerging days ahead of any surface march.

abilities.name: The Chosen Acre
abilities.desc: Choose an acre of the field at dawn; at any later moment of your choosing, it stops being load-bearing.

abilities.name: Never Lifted
abilities.desc: Passive: sieges you conduct do not end when you leave; the works remain, patient, and resume when you return.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and take, from below and alone, a fortress that three field armies had failed to invest.
Dig one gallery for ten years under a keep you may never need. Because you may.
Let a garrison find your works, brick them up, and post a watch. Visit the watch-room anyway, from below, leaving only a knock.
Accept a fortress's surrender addressed to the ground itself, and file it with the others.

nodes.name: The Refused Battle
nodes.role: Apex commander — victory without engagement
nodes.lore: Three empires have marched against the Refused Battle. Their chronicles describe burned plains, missing bridges, winter arriving early, and no enemy — then describe going home, thinner. Whether the Refused Battle has ever actually fought anyone is the liveliest dispute in military letters; the armies that never found them agree it does not matter.
nodes.playstyle: Apex evasion commander. Your army is always elsewhere; enemies fight roads, hunger, and rumor while you spend soldiers on nothing and lose none of them.

abilities.name: Always Elsewhere
abilities.desc: Passive: enemy scouts, spies, and divinations place your army one full day behind wherever it actually is.

abilities.name: Hollow Country
abilities.desc: Territory you have withdrawn through turns hostile to pursuers: forage fails, wheels break, wells disappoint, maps argue.

abilities.name: Give Them the Field
abilities.desc: Decline an offered battle; the enemy suffers a defeat's worth of desertion and lost morale anyway, having won nothing.

abilities.name: The Unspent Army
abilities.desc: Passive: your army treats every march as rest and every winter as quarters; you end campaigns at full strength.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and defeat an empire's invasion without one pitched engagement, then decline the triumph the saved insist on holding.
Be declared dead by three enemy chronicles, each citing a different battle you were not at.
March your army the length of a hostile empire, unseen, fed by nothing you did not carry or cache.
Refuse the battle your own soldiers beg you to fight, and bring every one of them home to complain about it.

nodes.name: The Opponent
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the adversary in every duel
nodes.lore: The Unanswered refused the last challenge, and the silence that followed took up the office. Now every drill-yard shadow-fencer, every duelist rehearsing at midnight, is facing the same figure — the perfect adversary the mind supplies when nobody else is good enough. That figure holds a rank, and the rank is occupied. Occasionally, it fences back.
nodes.playstyle: Be the adversary all training imagines and the doubt inside every draw. Enter any single combat, anywhere, as the opponent both fighters were secretly expecting.

abilities.name: The Imagined Blade
abilities.desc: Manifest in any single combat you are aware of, on either side; you were always the expected opponent.

abilities.name: Second of All Duels
abilities.desc: Passive: you may attend any formal duel unbidden; while you watch, no dishonorable stroke can land.

abilities.name: The Perfect Adversary
abilities.desc: Passive: you fight each enemy at exactly their level plus one lesson; survivors leave better, which is the point.

abilities.name: The Standing Question
abilities.desc: An enemy raising arms against you must first answer why; those without an answer find their bodies decline the fight.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and answer, at last, the question you left standing — alone, at midnight, in the yard where you began.
Fence the silence you appointed as your successor, and win the office back from it.
Stand, the same dawn, in the mind's eye of every soldier drilling alone, and correct one wrist apiece.
Accept that no one will speak your name again. The office does not keep one; opponents are never introduced.

nodes.name: The Cloven Way
nodes.role: Apotheosis — perfect division made pilgrimage
nodes.lore: When a hundredth form is performed, the order raises a shrine from the pieces. Pilgrims walking between shrines noticed the paths connect: one line of split stones crossing the ranges, older in places than the shrines themselves. The Cloven Way is that line, still being cut from inside, and the order admits, when pressed, that it is held.
nodes.playstyle: Travel as the cut travels. Step out of any perfect parting — split stone, opened gate, the line dawn draws — and finish forms other hands began.

abilities.name: Walk the Parting
abilities.desc: Enter the Way through any flawless cut and leave it through any other, arriving with your blade already drawn.

abilities.name: Finish the Form
abilities.desc: Complete any technique an ally begins; it resolves as though you performed it, and they briefly learn what that felt like.

abilities.name: Maker's Signature
abilities.desc: Passive: anything you cut stays cut; no mending, healing, or restoration closes a parting you signed.

abilities.name: One Line, All Passes
abilities.desc: Passive: the Way runs under your feet everywhere; walls, formations, and difficult ground count as already parted for your movement.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and walk the whole Way on foot, shrine to shrine, greeting each stone by its maker's mark.
Find the stones no order remembers cutting, and learn what has been performing the form since before there were people.
Cut nothing for a year, and watch the Way lengthen anyway. Conclude what the elders concluded, and keep it as quietly.
Add your shrine to the Way while still alive to sweep it. The office is tenancy; the stone can wait.

nodes.name: The General Surrender
nodes.role: Apotheosis — every wall already yielded
nodes.lore: Six kingdoms learned from the Ruin of Gates that walls only decide when surrender happens, never whether. Jurists drew the full conclusion: all fortification is provisional, and yielding arrives for everyone eventually. The office holds every gate's eventual opening in trust. Three cities surrender to it annually, in advance, as civic insurance; the paperwork is considered devotional.
nodes.playstyle: Sieges are paperwork you personally embody. Arrive, and fortifications remember they are provisional; garrisons find themselves negotiating with the inevitable, which is you.

abilities.name: Provisional Architecture
abilities.desc: Passive: no door, gate, or wall is closed to you; each was always going to open, and you are when.

abilities.name: Surrender in Advance
abilities.desc: A garrison may yield to you before any war exists; many do, and the terms are famously kind.

abilities.name: The Oldest Terms
abilities.desc: Invoke a city's ancient surrender — every city has one filed somewhere — and its walls stand neutral while you walk in.

abilities.name: Nothing Personal
abilities.desc: Passive: defenders cannot hate you, and assaults you lead cost remarkably few lives; everyone present already understands the conclusion.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and accept the surrender of a city no army has approached in a century. It will know why you came.
Open, gently and alone, a gate the Ruin of Gates once spared, and leave it standing open.
Countersign the annual surrenders of the three prudent cities, and attend each festival held in the office's honor.
Open nothing for a year, so the doctrine remembers it is mercy and not appetite.

nodes.name: The Ten Thousand
nodes.role: Apotheosis — one soldier who is a host
nodes.lore: The Sovereign of Hosts was owed an army; the apotheosis is the army. Ten thousand stopped being a count and became a condition: wherever that many stand together in discipline — harvest crews, road gangs, pilgrim columns — the Ten Thousand is partly present, and can be wholly summoned. Kingdoms stopped asking who commands it. It commands itself, wearing one face.
nodes.playstyle: Singular and plural at will. Fight as one veteran or arrive as ten thousand; the difference is administrative, and you file it.

abilities.name: Muster of One
abilities.desc: Unfold into as many as ten thousand veteran soldiers for a day; you are each of them, and dismissal is instant.

abilities.name: The Rolls Eternal
abilities.desc: Passive: any living veteran of your musters hears your summons wherever they stand; most come.

abilities.name: One Face
abilities.desc: Passive: every ally in any army you join fights as if personally drilled by you, because at some remove they were.

abilities.name: An Army at Law
abilities.desc: Passive: treaties, morale, and logistics must treat you alone as a full host; you are spoken of in the plural.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and answer a muster-horn alone; let the clerks count you, recount, and enter ten thousand.
March one border's length as a column of one, and be reported by every watchtower as a field army with banners.
Disband yourself once, entirely, and see whether the world permits it. It will not; learn what that obligates.
End a war at roll-call by being discovered on both muster-rolls at once; send everyone home, confused and alive.

nodes.name: The Armistice
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the truce given a body
nodes.lore: When the Bloodless finally struck — histories agree it happened once, and agree on nothing else — the stroke did not land on anyone. It landed between. The gap it opened is still there: the pause in which truces are signed, the hour when both lines breathe. Treaties do not create that hour; they visit it. The office receives them politely.
nodes.playstyle: Fight by ending fights. Open the gap the first stroke cut, hold whole battles inside it, and make war negotiate its way back out past you.

abilities.name: The Stroke Between
abilities.desc: Cut a truce into an active battle: all hostilities in sight pause until someone dares to be first, and none wish to.

abilities.name: The Quiet Hour
abilities.desc: Declare one hour of armistice each day; within it, no weapon inside a mile of you can wound. Including yours.

abilities.name: Receive the Sword
abilities.desc: Any combatant anywhere may yield to you directly, vanishing from their battle and arriving at your hall — disarmed, safe, and embarrassed.

abilities.name: Both Lines Breathe
abilities.desc: Passive: you may stand in any no-man's-land untouched; while you hold it, neither side can cross it in anger.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and inherit the hall of yielded swords, then notice it has begun accepting them from wars you never attended.
Walk the length of an active front, unarmed, and leave it quiet behind you for a year.
Be written into a treaty as terrain.
Refuse to end one war, because its peace would have been crueler than its fighting. Carry the office's first exception.

nodes.name: Worldcut
nodes.role: Apotheosis — geography as standing commission
nodes.lore: Geographers reconciling old maps keep finding the same signature: this strait, that pass, the valley the river obviously did not make. The guild's conclusion, published quietly, is that the world's habitable shape is one commission, still being delivered — a single serving cut of continental length. The Civil Blade's apotheosis is tenure of that stroke. The rates remain posted.
nodes.playstyle: Continue the continental stroke. Cut at the scale of coastlines when commissioned, of doorways when not, and keep the world roughly navigable either way.

abilities.name: The Continuing Cut
abilities.desc: Once per season, extend the world-stroke: raise a strait, open a pass, or retire a mountain. Permanently.

abilities.name: Posted Rates
abilities.desc: Passive: anyone, anywhere, may commission you and learn your price by asking aloud. You always hear the asking.

abilities.name: Cut to Fit
abilities.desc: Passive: your strikes resize the field itself — narrow the front, widen the retreat, adjust the river to today's requirements.

abilities.name: Habitable Shape
abilities.desc: Allies live well on terrain you have cut: fresh water surfaces, winds gentle themselves, roads discover they were always convenient.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and find the world-stroke's living edge, somewhere past the last mapped cape, still warm.
Complete one commission the first hand left unfinished, matching the signature so exactly the geographers never notice the seam.
Set a fair price for a harbor, and a fairer one for the village that cannot pay. Deliver both.
Decline to finish the cut. The commission outlasts every holder; leave the world workable for whoever posts the rates next.

nodes.name: The Investment
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the siege that encircles everything
nodes.lore: Siegecraft begins by drawing a line around a place and calling it invested. The Buried Siege drew its last line somewhere out past the horizon, unhurried, and closed it. Nothing has escaped since; nothing has noticed. Every wall now stands inside the works, every border is a concession, and the office walks the circumvallation at its own pace, inspecting.
nodes.playstyle: Hold the lines of the world's one siege. Everything is already surrounded; battles are merely sorties, and you decide which sorties get back inside.

abilities.name: Lines of Circumvallation
abilities.desc: Passive: any enemy force you face counts as besieged: no reinforcement, resupply, or retreat crosses your unseen works.

abilities.name: Older Than Maps
abilities.desc: Passive: your trenches, galleries, and lines already exist wherever you arrive; you built them before the map was drawn.

abilities.name: Sortie Permit
abilities.desc: Nothing enters or leaves a place you invest without your stamp; armies, rivers, and rumors queue alike.

abilities.name: Time Served
abilities.desc: Once per siege, declare an invested stronghold reduced: its defenses count as breached, mined, and starved already.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and walk the whole line once — the one drawn past the horizon — repairing it where the world has worn thin.
Answer the knock that comes up through your own floor one night, and learn who has been besieging the besiegers.
Accept the surrender of something too large to know it had been invested — a range, a river, a republic.
Lift one siege, once, entirely, and watch the world fail to believe you. The office permits mercy; history does not record it.

nodes.name: The Mud Season
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the season war cannot march
nodes.lore: Every general owns two enemies: the one across the field and the one underfoot when the rains come. The second answers to an office. Since the Refused Battle refused its last pursuit, the mud arrives where it is needed — roads dissolve under invasions, fords deepen ahead of columns — and campaigns drown politely, without casualties. Almanacs print it. Farmers approve.
nodes.playstyle: Arrive as weather underfoot. Exhaust campaigns by existing, ration violence the way rain rations roads, and choose which invasions simply never arrive.

abilities.name: Declare the Season
abilities.desc: Open your season across a realm: armies cannot muster, march, or hold formation, while harvests and healing double.

abilities.name: Wrong Season for It
abilities.desc: Passive: hostile action against you is logistically impossible; attackers arrive under-supplied, mis-mustered, and rained on.

abilities.name: Struck from the Almanac
abilities.desc: Erase a declared battle before it is joined; both sides remember deciding against it and feel obscurely relieved.

abilities.name: Seedcorn
abilities.desc: Passive: whatever allies preserve through your season — soldiers, stores, patience — returns doubled when the roads finally dry.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and be predicted by an almanac before you have decided anything. Read your entry; it is accurate.
Walk an empire's border during your season and find every garrison helping with the harvest.
End the longest war alive by outlasting its reasons, then attend the treaty as the weather.
Refuse to make the season permanent, though every widow asks. A rest that cannot end is not peace; it is a cage.

families.name: Berserker
families.tagline: What winter could not kill, it armed.
families.description: The marches breed them: fighters raised where winter kills more than war does, taught that pain is fuel and fear a language they never learned. A Berserker does not hold formation; formation holds its breath. Whether they invite a beast-spirit under the skin or simply refuse to stop moving, they end fights by making restraint irrelevant.

nodes.name: Berserker
nodes.role: Melee bruiser — reckless sustained damage
nodes.lore: Born to the frozen marches, where winter culls the timid and the rage-fire is banked in every hearth-tale. The berserker learns early that pain is a door, not a wall. Villages feed them, fear them, and set them loose when the wolves, or worse, come down from the ice.
nodes.playstyle: Trade defense for damage. Build fury by taking and dealing hits, then spend it in short, terrifying windows where nothing else on the field matters.

abilities.name: Red Veil
abilities.desc: Enter a fury that raises all damage dealt and taken for twelve seconds; you cannot be feared or slowed while it lasts.

abilities.name: Blood Price
abilities.desc: Sacrifice a tenth of your current health to make the next strike unblockable and critical.

abilities.name: Howl of the Marches
abilities.desc: A shout that strips enemy courage effects and staggers everything in a cone before you.

abilities.name: Deaf to Fear
abilities.desc: Passive: fear, panic, and morale effects are ignored; gain fury whenever one is attempted against you.

progressionSteps: Survive a winter the elders call a culling year, and come out of it angrier than you went in.
Take your first true wound and stand back up before the count of ten.
Let the fury take you once in front of witnesses, and learn its cost when you wake.
Be turned away from the war-band's fire, then follow them anyway until they stop turning you away.

nodes.name: Skinbearer
nodes.role: Feral skirmisher — pursuit and bleed damage
nodes.lore: Some berserkers hear a second heartbeat inside the fury and go looking for its owner. Skinbearers keep the old bargains: meat left at treelines, blood given at solstice, a pelt worn until it stops being a garment. The spirit that answers moves in, and it is always hungry.
nodes.playstyle: Fast, low, and feral. Track wounded targets by scent, open bleeds that punish movement, and let the guest spirit sharpen every sense past human limits.

abilities.name: Guest Beneath the Skin
abilities.desc: Invite the beast-spirit in: attack speed and movement rise sharply, but you cannot disengage from wounded prey.

abilities.name: Borrowed Fangs
abilities.desc: A bite attack that opens a bleed which deepens each time the target moves.

abilities.name: Second Scent
abilities.desc: Detect hidden, invisible, and fleeing enemies within sixty paces; bleeding targets cannot break your tracking.

abilities.name: Winter Coat
abilities.desc: Grow a dense hide that halves cold damage and shortens every bleed laid on you.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10 and carry a killed beast home whole, wasting nothing; the spirit watches how you treat its kin.
Sleep three nights in an abandoned den without fire, until you dream in smells instead of words.
Cut your palm on a solstice altar and speak the invitation; if something answers, do not flinch.

nodes.name: Bloodwader
nodes.role: Frontline breaker — damage soak, forward pressure
nodes.lore: The marches remember warriors who walked into spear-hedges and came out the far side, annoyed. Bloodwaders court that memory. They learn to drink pain like mead, to keep moving when muscle says stop, and to make of their own body a weight the enemy cannot brace against.
nodes.playstyle: Walk forward through everything. Absorb hits to build momentum, ignore wounds until the fight ends, and be exactly where the enemy least wants you standing.

abilities.name: Wade the Spears
abilities.desc: Advance at full speed through enemy reach; each hit taken while moving forward grants fury.

abilities.name: Shrug the Grave
abilities.desc: Once per battle, reduce a killing blow to a flesh wound and keep swinging.

abilities.name: Drunk on Hurt
abilities.desc: Passive: damage taken converts to a stacking damage bonus that decays only outside combat.

abilities.name: Landslide Step
abilities.desc: A slow, unstoppable advance that shoves enemies back and cannot be halted by roots, bodies, or fear.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10 and stand in the practice line while five spearmen strike true; walk the field's length before you fall.
Take a wound the healers call mortal, and make them wrong by morning.
Carry a wounded shield-brother out of a rout, walking, without once looking back.

nodes.name: Vargr
nodes.role: Pursuit striker — single-target attrition hunter
nodes.lore: Named for the outlaw-wolves of the old tongue, Vargr leave the war-band for the long trail. They hunt what others flee: man-eaters, deserter kings, things that walk out of the ice. In three provinces, a Vargr's declaration of hunt is treated as a death already recorded.
nodes.playstyle: Choose one target and end them. Stack pursuit bonuses over days of chase, deny escape and healing, and strike when exhaustion has done half the work.

abilities.name: Speak the Quarry
abilities.desc: Name a single target; against them you ignore armor thresholds and always know their direction.

abilities.name: Tireless Lope
abilities.desc: Travel without rest for days equal to your fury, and arrive at full strength.

abilities.name: No Den Deep Enough
abilities.desc: Your quarry gains nothing from stealth, sanctuary, or door wards while you are within a mile.

abilities.name: Winter's Patience
abilities.desc: Each day the hunt continues, your first strike against the quarry grows stronger, without cap.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and follow a quarry through one full turn of the moon, eating only what the trail gives.
Refuse a hunt once — for coin, for cruelty, for a wrong scent — and be known for the refusal.
Run down something faster than you, and understand that speed was never the point.
Return with proof of the kill that the elders look at once and never again.

nodes.name: Urskin
nodes.role: Shapeshift bruiser — claws, hide, raw grapple
nodes.lore: The bear-shirt is the oldest rite the marches keep. Urskin let the guest spirit past the skin and into the bone: hands broaden, hide thickens, voice drops below language. They are welcome at fires in the wary way a tame avalanche would be welcome.
nodes.playstyle: Slow, huge, and horribly durable. Shift deeper into beast-shape as the fight lengthens, trading finesse for claws, hide, and a grip nothing slips.

abilities.name: Bear-Shirt
abilities.desc: Transform: gain claw attacks, doubled carrying strength, and hide that treats all weapons as blunt.

abilities.name: Winterhide
abilities.desc: Passive: regenerate steadily in combat; the rate doubles below half health.

abilities.name: Red Maul
abilities.desc: An overhead claw blow that crushes shields, breaks grapples, and flattens man-sized foes.

abilities.name: Below Language
abilities.desc: While transformed, mind-affecting magic finds nothing in you it can speak to.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and wear the raw pelt through a winter, until you cannot say where it ends.
Let the spirit take your hands for one fight, and win it without a weapon.
Winter in a den beside a true bear and leave in spring, unchallenged.

nodes.name: Woundtaker
nodes.role: Attrition bruiser — converts damage to power
nodes.lore: Where others bind wounds, Woundtakers open accounts. Every cut is entered, remembered, and spent later with interest. Old soldiers recognize the look — a fighter glancing at a fresh wound the way a merchant checks a purse. It unsettles men more than the axe does.
nodes.playstyle: Deliberate attrition. Invite hits you can afford, bank the pain as fury, and out-economy enemies who believe damage dealt means they are winning.

abilities.name: Open the Ledger
abilities.desc: Begin recording: a portion of all damage taken is stored as spendable fury.

abilities.name: Spend the Scar
abilities.desc: Consume stored pain to drive a strike beyond your weapon's normal ceiling.

abilities.name: Ask for the Knife
abilities.desc: Willingly take a small wound to end any bleed, poison, or curse; the pain crowds it out.

abilities.name: Second Heartbeat
abilities.desc: Passive: below half health, fury generation doubles and your hands stop shaking.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and name every scar you carry, in order, without touching them.
Accept a wound in a duel you could have dodged, and win with what it paid.
Go a full campaign without letting a healer close anything you can spend.

nodes.name: Breachwright
nodes.role: Line-breaker — charge, knockdown, formation collapse
nodes.lore: Sappers dig for weeks; a Breachwright arrives. They study walls the way duelists study opponents — where a gate hinges, where a shield-line breathes — then apply themselves like falling masonry. Siege captains list them in inventories, somewhere between rams and reasons to surrender.
nodes.playstyle: Momentum management. Build speed and mass across the field, spend both on walls, gates, and formations, and never fight standing still.

abilities.name: Gathering Slope
abilities.desc: Each stride in a straight line stacks momentum, raising damage and knockdown force.

abilities.name: Keystone Blow
abilities.desc: Strike a structure's weak point; walls, gates, and shield formations all count as structures.

abilities.name: Doorless
abilities.desc: Passive: doors, barricades, and lines of pikemen do not end your charge, merely tax it.

abilities.name: Press the Rout
abilities.desc: Enemies you knock down rise slower; enemies who flee you spread fear as they go.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and put a shield wall on the ground — the whole wall — before your war-band closes.
Carry the old gate beam from the quarry road to the walls without setting it down.
Walk through a burning granary because it was the shorter way, and be seen doing it.

nodes.name: Fangthane
nodes.role: Elite hunter — marked-prey execution
nodes.lore: A thane of the long hunt holds no hall. Their oath-torc hangs with a fang from every hunt completed, and no Fangthane's torc has a gap. Kingdoms retain them against horrors, then quietly pray never to earn a place on the torc themselves.
nodes.playstyle: The endgame of pursuit. Bind yourself by oath to impossible quarry, turn their fear into a leash, and close hunts other trackers died beginning.

abilities.name: Oathmark
abilities.desc: Swear a hunt: you cannot die of wounds while the quarry lives, and it knows you are coming.

abilities.name: Fear Is a Scent
abilities.desc: Frightened enemies are revealed, slowed, and take doubled bleed damage from you.

abilities.name: Culling Silence
abilities.desc: Your approach mutes sound and warning; sentries notice you only as the strike lands.

abilities.name: The Last Mile
abilities.desc: When the quarry falls below quarter strength, gain unstoppable speed and immunity to everything but the quarry itself.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and close a hunt that outlasted a season, alone, across a border war.
Have your torc weighed at the gathering of hunters and found without a gap.
Decline a king's price for a hunt, then take the hunt for a reason he cannot buy.
Kill something that had killed a Fangthane, and hang both their fangs together.

nodes.name: Ironpelt
nodes.role: Immovable shapeshifter — anchor tank, grapples
nodes.lore: An Ironpelt has stopped shifting all the way back. The claws fold, mostly; the hide stays. They den apart from villages that nonetheless leave meat and grievances at the treeline, because an Ironpelt settles both. Whole raiding cultures have rerouted around a single known den.
nodes.playstyle: Anchor the field. Grapple what cannot be cut, endure what cannot be dodged, and regenerate through punishment that erases shield-lines around you.

abilities.name: Pelt of Iron Winters
abilities.desc: Passive: your hide counts as heavy armor that regenerates and cannot be sundered.

abilities.name: Denfather's Grip
abilities.desc: Seize a foe up to horse-size; while held, they take your regeneration as damage.

abilities.name: The Long Sleep
abilities.desc: Out of combat, sleep to heal any injury, regrow what was lost, and shed one curse.

abilities.name: Treeline Law
abilities.desc: Mark ground as den; within it your grip cannot be broken and your allies cannot be moved.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and winter in the open den, sleeping the true sleep, and wake with the pelt grown inward.
Answer a village's grievance without being asked twice, and take payment in meat alone.
Hold a bridge through a cavalry charge, moving nothing but your arms.
Out-grapple the thing the spirit sends to test you, and let it leave alive.

nodes.name: Flayed Saint
nodes.role: Martyr tank — damage transfer and aura
nodes.lore: The order keeps no relics but skin. Each Saint's scars are read like scripture, a wound-history of battles that should have had no survivors. Soldiers touch their hems for luck and flinch doing it. The Saints bless shield-lines by standing in front of them.
nodes.playstyle: A martyr in the tactical sense. Intercept harm meant for others, convert it to power, and hold ground that has no business holding.

abilities.name: Give Me Yours
abilities.desc: Transfer any ally's wounds onto your own body; the pain converts to fury at double rate.

abilities.name: Litany of Scars
abilities.desc: Recite your wound-history aloud; allies in earshot cannot fear or rout while it continues.

abilities.name: Red Absolution
abilities.desc: A blow that grows stronger for every wound currently open on your body.

abilities.name: Standing Scripture
abilities.desc: Passive: while you are below half health, allies behind you take less damage and deal more.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and let the order read your skin, scar by scar, omitting nothing.
Stand before a shield-line as the volley lands, and take what was meant for all of them.
Refuse the healers three times in one campaign, and outlive the campaign.
Bless a coward with a scar he asked for, and watch him hold the line for it.

nodes.name: Towerbane
nodes.role: Siege striker — structure and formation destruction
nodes.lore: Fortresses keep two sets of plans: one for war, one for a Towerbane. The elite of the breach-trade end sieges by arriving; garrisons that see the banner — a black keystone on grey — are permitted by long custom to open the gates first.
nodes.playstyle: A one-man siege. Convert momentum into structural collapse, walk out of the rubble, and turn every fallen wall into a road for the army behind you.

abilities.name: Toll the Gate
abilities.desc: Announce yourself with a single blow to the gate; wood, iron, and defender morale all take it.

abilities.name: Rubble Stride
abilities.desc: Collapsing structures deal you nothing; you emerge from debris at full momentum.

abilities.name: Read the Masonry
abilities.desc: See every load-bearing weakness in a structure or formation at a glance.

abilities.name: Bring Down the Sky
abilities.desc: Topple a tower, arch, or gatehouse onto a chosen area after three uninterrupted blows.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and end a siege that had lasted a year, between one dawn and the next.
Take a standing tower down with nothing you did not carry in your two hands.
Be buried in a collapse of your own making, and let them hear you knocking from inside.
Accept the black keystone banner from a Towerbane grown too old to lift it.

nodes.name: Quietus
nodes.role: Elite hunter — undeclared single-strike kills
nodes.lore: The Fangthanes swear their hunts aloud; the Quietus finds that vanity, and worse, cruelty. Fear sours a quarry like panic sours meat. This order kills without declaration, without pursuit the prey ever notices, without a moment of dread. Shepherds pray for them by name. Their quarry never learns to.
nodes.playstyle: Stalk without ever being detected, keep the quarry calm and unaware, and end the hunt in one strike that lands before fear can.

abilities.name: Unspoken Hunt
abilities.desc: Choose a quarry in secret; it gains no warning instincts, omens, or premonitions of you while unaware of the hunt.

abilities.name: Calm the Herd
abilities.desc: Your presence soothes animals and sentries into inattention; alarms within sixty paces of you simply fail to be raised.

abilities.name: One Clean Breath
abilities.desc: A single strike against an unafraid target deals quadruple damage and kills without sound, struggle, or pain.

abilities.name: Spoiled Meat
abilities.desc: Passive: your damage drops against frightened targets, but all your bonuses double against targets that feel entirely safe.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and take a quarry a Fangthane has already sworn aloud, finishing it before the oath is a day old — unwitnessed, unfeared, unclaimed.
Sit at your quarry's fire as a guest, share its bread, and leave without doing the work; learn to wait for the kind hour.
Kill a man-eater in the middle of its sleeping pack without waking one of them.
Be credited by nobody. The order confirms your first true kill by finding no story of it anywhere.

nodes.name: Bearward
nodes.role: Shapeshift duelist — commanded transformation, controlled fury
nodes.lore: Where the Ironpelt surrendered and denned apart, the Bearward broke the guest to harness and stayed. They sit at the fire with human eyes, and the village never quite relaxes. The spirit hates the bit, obeys it, and waits. Every Bearward knows exactly how the arrangement ends, and wears it anyway.
nodes.playstyle: Precision shapeshifting. Don the beast for exact windows, spend its strength without its appetites, and pay for control with a spirit that fights the harness.

abilities.name: Broken to Harness
abilities.desc: Transform instantly, fully, and on command; the shape never lingers, slips, or acts without your order.

abilities.name: The Bit
abilities.desc: While transformed you keep speech, judgment, and craft; frenzy, bloodlust, and provocation effects find no purchase.

abilities.name: Let It Slip
abilities.desc: Loose the harness for six seconds of the spirit's full hatred, doubling all damage; regaining control costs health.

abilities.name: Fireside Manners
abilities.desc: Passive: you may halt any transformation mid-motion; beasts and beast-spirits within sight must acknowledge you before acting against allies.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and win the second wrestling — the one inside — pinning the guest until it accepts the bit.
Shift to the bear and back nine times between one bell and the next, ending each turn with clean hands and a full memory.
Sit through a village feast transformed, breaking nothing, frightening no one old enough to know better.
Refuse an Ironpelt's den-peace to their face, and explain why, and leave on speaking terms with everything but the spirit.

nodes.name: Weregild
nodes.role: Retaliation bruiser — instant wound-for-wound reprisal
nodes.lore: The marches never wrote their law; they remember it in weregild, the price paid for every hurt. This order made the price immediate. Where a Flayed Saint hoards wounds like scripture, a Weregild carries none: every blow is returned in kind before the blood cools, and the skin heals smooth, keeping nothing.
nodes.playstyle: Counter-attrition. Answer every hit with its equal in the same breath, close your own wounds without trace, and make striking you a losing trade.

abilities.name: Paid in Kind
abilities.desc: Every wound you take appears identically on its maker within a heartbeat, bypassing armor, wards, and distance.

abilities.name: Sealed Skin
abilities.desc: Passive: your wounds close without scarring once their price is collected; nothing lingers, bleeds, or festers on you.

abilities.name: The Set Price
abilities.desc: Name aloud what a blow against you costs; any enemy who strikes you regardless pays it doubled.

abilities.name: Whole and Even
abilities.desc: While you carry no open wounds, you cannot be slowed, weakened, or marked by any lingering effect.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and stand a full judicial duel returning only what you are given, blow for blow, and walk away unmarked while your opponent is carried.
Recite the weregild table of the marches from memory, then correct the elder reciting after you.
Let a Flayed Saint read your skin and find nothing — no scar, no history, no scripture — and hold their eye while they call it obscene.
Return a wound to a warlord across a battlefield, publicly, so the marches remember why the price exists.

nodes.name: Leveller
nodes.role: Siege zealot — total demolition, area denial
nodes.lore: The Towerbanes end sieges; the Levellers end places. Their creed is short — what can fall, must — and their work is never partial: walls, then foundations, then the memory of foundations. Captains hire them reluctantly, because a Leveller does not stop at the terms of surrender. Or, strictly speaking, at all.
nodes.playstyle: Methodical annihilation. Grind structures past rubble into ground, deny enemies anything to rebuild or rally behind, and grow stronger standing in what you have flattened.

abilities.name: What Can Fall, Must
abilities.desc: Passive: your blows against structures continue working after you move on; anything you crack keeps cracking until it is ground.

abilities.name: Down to the Root-Stone
abilities.desc: Destroy foundations, cellars, and wards anchored in them; ground you clear cannot support new construction or fortification magic.

abilities.name: Open Ground
abilities.desc: On ground bearing no standing structure, your damage, speed, and fury generation all rise by half.

abilities.name: The Creed Recited
abilities.desc: Speak the creed before a fortification; defenders inside fight at a penalty, already believing the walls temporary.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and finish what a Towerbane started: return to a breached fortress after the treaty and take it down to the root-stone.
Refuse the black keystone banner when it is offered; carry no banner at all, because banners are things that stand.
Sleep one full night on ground you levelled, in the open, and wake certain you did a kindness.
Grind a milestone to powder with your hands while the road's owner watches, as an estimate.

nodes.name: Wolf of the Long Night
nodes.role: Apex predator — inevitable single-target death
nodes.lore: Histories argue whether there has been one or many; the torc suggests one. When the Wolf speaks a name, chroniclers write the death first and the date after. Border tales say winter follows them out of courtesy, and that they have not slept since the oath.
nodes.playstyle: Play inevitability itself. Declared prey cannot heal, hide, or bargain a way out; everything and everyone else on the field is merely in the way.

abilities.name: Doom Spoken Once
abilities.desc: Name a living thing; it can no longer be healed, resurrected, or hidden by any power.

abilities.name: The Long Night
abilities.desc: Draw unnatural dusk across a mile; within it you see everything and your quarry sees only you.

abilities.name: The Hunt Remembers
abilities.desc: Inherit the tracking knowledge of every hunter who ever failed against your quarry.

abilities.name: No Last Door
abilities.desc: Wards, gates, and other planes do not bar your pursuit, and deaths you deliver cannot be undone.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and accept the hunt no gathering will speak aloud.
Follow the quarry past the map's last honest line, and keep the trail through places with no ground.
Kill what history says cannot be killed, and let the chroniclers strike its name.
Come back to the fires, and say nothing, and be believed.

nodes.name: First Beast
nodes.role: Primal avatar — escalating transformation, zone control
nodes.lore: The eldest spirit — the one that taught wolves hunger and bears winter — does not take guests. It takes a body. Once in an age, an Urskin walks into the high tundra, and what walks out answers no human name, though it still, for its own reasons, defends the fires.
nodes.playstyle: A permanent, deepening transformation. Cycle primal aspects mid-fight, hold ground through sheer presence, and grow stronger the longer the battle forgets to end.

abilities.name: Shape Before Names
abilities.desc: Cycle three primal aspects — fang, hide, antler — without pause; none can be dispelled or dismissed.

abilities.name: The Old Growl
abilities.desc: A subsonic warning: beasts obey, mounts throw riders, and lesser courage simply leaves the field.

abilities.name: Blood of the First Winter
abilities.desc: Your blood freezes to armor where it spills; every wound taken thickens it.

abilities.name: Den of the World
abilities.desc: All wild ground counts as your den: regeneration for you, fearlessness for allies who stand on it.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and climb past the treeline carrying no iron, wearing every pelt you have earned.
Offer the eldest spirit your name, and let it be eaten without asking what remains.
Walk back down in spring on feet that no longer print as human.
Defend one fire without being asked, so the marches know what came back is still theirs.

nodes.name: Agonarch
nodes.role: Immortal attrition — banked-damage burst
nodes.lore: The Agonarch has died before witnesses — the annals record where, and how often — and returned each time angrier. Pain no longer visits; it pays tribute. Veterans say a battlefield goes quiet when the Agonarch begins counting scars aloud, because everyone present knows a new entry is coming.
nodes.playstyle: Immortal attrition. Bank every point of damage taken across an entire battle, then repay the whole ledger at a moment of your choosing.

abilities.name: Throne of Scars
abilities.desc: Damage taken is banked instead of killing you; only the ledger's full total can end you.

abilities.name: All Debts Called
abilities.desc: Release the banked pain as a single strike or a field-wide shockwave of equal total.

abilities.name: Tribute
abilities.desc: Attackers take a share of the pain they deal you, doubled if they flee afterward.

abilities.name: The Wound That Rules
abilities.desc: Passive: your wounds close on their own, faster the more enemies can see them.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and read your full ledger of scars aloud to the order, one origin at a time, forgetting nothing.
Die before a hundred witnesses, and stand up while they are still deciding to grieve.
Forgive one debt — a single scar, freely — and learn what that mercy costs you.
Walk unarmored into a war and end it by demonstrating what its best blow is worth.

nodes.name: Walking Ruin
nodes.role: Catastrophe engine — army-scale momentum damage
nodes.lore: Chronicles class them with floods and fire-mountains rather than soldiers, and the insurance canons of three cities agree. A Walking Ruin does not besiege; it schedules. The last one to cross the marches is the reason two duchies now share one very wide road.
nodes.playstyle: Terminal momentum. Accumulate unstoppable mass and speed over an entire battle, and let geography, architecture, and armies resolve themselves around your path.

abilities.name: The Name Arrives First
abilities.desc: Enemies who learn you are coming begin the battle already shaken; some simply do not attend.

abilities.name: Nothing Holds
abilities.desc: Passive: no wall, ward, or formation counts as an obstacle, only as material.

abilities.name: Momentum of Ages
abilities.desc: Your momentum no longer decays; each battle begins at the force the last one ended.

abilities.name: Terminus
abilities.desc: Stop moving, once per war, and release all gathered momentum as a collapse felt for miles.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and cross a kingdom that refused you passage, in a straight line.
Have a fortress surrender to your name while you are still two days away.
End a war by attending it, once, briefly.
Leave one wall standing, deliberately, so the histories know it was a choice.

nodes.name: Winterkill
nodes.role: Mythic hunter — deaths indistinguishable from nature
nodes.lore: Chroniclers have no entry for the Winterkill, which the order considers the only proof required. Tyrants die of age early; horrors starve in good years. Every march keeps a count of quiet deaths no one questions, and the elders keep a second count, of which ones the winter cannot honestly claim.
nodes.playstyle: Erase the hunt itself. Kills read as accident, age, or weather; no alarm, oath, or vengeance can attach to a death that was never noticed as one.

abilities.name: Death of Natural Causes
abilities.desc: Your kills leave no wound, mark, or magical trace; divination reads them as misfortune and cannot name you.

abilities.name: The Lean Season
abilities.desc: Mark a region for culling; within it, your chosen quarry weaken daily as if wintering badly, and only you know why.

abilities.name: No Story
