abilities.desc: Passive: witnesses, wards, and recording magics fail to retain you; memory of your passing settles into something ordinary.

abilities.name: Mercy of Predators
abilities.desc: Targets that never feared you die instantly below a third of their health, painlessly, regardless of remaining defenses.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and cull a name from the world so cleanly that its own kin light no vengeance-fires, only mourning ones.
Take a tyrant in his guarded tower between heartbeats, and let the succession proceed grieving, unrobbed of even one night's sleep.
Refuse the gathering's torc when it is offered; the order's honor is that no gathering can prove you exist to honor.
Walk through the marches in a culling year and leave the count of quiet deaths exactly one short of what the elders feared.

nodes.name: The Yoke
nodes.role: Mythic spirit-breaker — commands what possesses others
nodes.lore: Beasts have hearth-tales of their own, told in scent and hackle, and the Yoke is what they frighten their young with. Somewhere below the tundra a thing older than hunger wears a bit, and carries a rider. Spirits that once took bodies now ask first, in case the answer is listening.
nodes.playstyle: Ride the broken eldest thing into battle. Command every beast-shape at once, conscript hostile spirits mid-fight, and spend their hatred as fuel.

abilities.name: Eldest, Bitted
abilities.desc: Call up the thing you broke: a primal spirit given flesh, mountain-shouldered, obedient, and furious; nothing it charges holds formation.

abilities.name: Ask First
abilities.desc: Possessing spirits, curses, and riding entities must petition you before touching anyone in your warband; you may refuse, or redirect them.

abilities.name: Harness of the Wild
abilities.desc: Any beast or beast-spirit you strike must serve you for a hundred heartbeats before it may flee or fight again.

abilities.name: Hatred as Harness
abilities.desc: Passive: hostile fury, fear auras, and dominating effects aimed at you are seized as fury for you and your mount.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and go below the tundra where the eldest spirits winter, carrying a harness you forged yourself, and do not come up alone.
Break a thing that taught the teaching spirits, and hold it pinned until it speaks your name as an owner's.
Ride it once through the gathering of hunters, slowly, so that every order revises its opinion of what can be tamed.
Dismount at your village fire and hang the harness where children can reach it, because the point was never the riding.

nodes.name: The Unwounded
nodes.role: Mythic retaliator — unwoundable, war-ending reciprocity
nodes.lore: Histories dispute whether the Unwounded has ever been hurt. Veterans know better: every wound it ever took is still out there, walking around in the bodies that made them. Armies now settle terms rather than engage, having done the arithmetic. Its skin is the only unmarked thing the marches have produced.
nodes.playstyle: Absolute reciprocity. Damage cannot rest on you — it returns doubled to its maker, and whole formations learn that harming you is simply harming themselves slower.

abilities.name: No Purchase
abilities.desc: Passive: wounds cannot remain on your body; each returns to its origin within three heartbeats, doubled if delivered from ambush.

abilities.name: Up the Chain
abilities.desc: Cross a battlefield untouched; any volley, spell, or charge aimed at you resolves against those who ordered it.

abilities.name: Even the Old Scores
abilities.desc: Touch a scarred ally; their oldest wound leaves them and finds whoever dealt it, wherever that maker now hides.

abilities.name: The Arithmetic
abilities.desc: Reveal to all enemies present exactly what attacking you will cost them; those who can read futures rout first.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and receive an army's opening volley alone; end the battle before your side arrives, without striking one blow of your own.
Find the man who scarred you first, before the order, before the law, and give it back grown thirty years older.
Be struck by something no law can price — a god, a season, a grief — and send even that home again.
Outlive the last chronicler who claims you were ever wounded, unmarked, and attend the funeral politely.

nodes.name: The Fallow
nodes.role: Mythic eraser — permanent razing, battlefield subtraction
nodes.lore: Three cities appear on old maps and no new ones, and the cartographers' guild lists the cause, in careful hand, as the Fallow. Where it finishes, ground refuses masonry the way scorched fields refuse seed. Scholars argue whether this is a person or a condition. The marches see no difference worth arguing.
nodes.playstyle: Erase fortification from the war entirely. Unmake structures at a glance's patience, salt ground against rebuilding, and fight best where nothing stands at all.

abilities.name: Let the Ground Rest
abilities.desc: Declare a razed site fallow; for a generation, no wall, ward, or siegework can be raised upon it.

abilities.name: Condition, Not Person
abilities.desc: Passive: while any structure you damaged still stands, you cannot be killed, bound, or turned away from it.

abilities.name: Harvest of Walls
abilities.desc: Every structure that falls within a mile feeds you fury; a city yields a war's worth.

abilities.name: Struck from the Maps
abilities.desc: Finish a place completely and it fades from maps, songs, and claims; armies cannot rally to defend what has no name.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and finish a city the wars began, alone, over a patient year, leaving standing water and good pasture.
Turn down a crown's ransom to spare a citadel, then take the citadel apart for nothing, so the creed stays clean.
Stand in the last archway of a place you have ended and let it fall on you, and walk out the far side of the dust.
Watch farmers plow your first great razing without knowing a city fed the soil, and tell no one.

nodes.name: Midwinter
nodes.role: Cosmic hunter — the year's dark made lethal
nodes.lore: The marches no longer say the Wolf hunts in winter; they say winter is the hunting. On the year's longest night, doors are barred not against cold but against appointments, for every doom ever spoken falls due at Midwinter, and the office that keeps the calendar has never been late.
nodes.playstyle: Hunt as a season hunts. Dooms you speak ripen on a calendar no power can appeal, and the world's dark hours are all your ground.

abilities.name: The Calendar of Teeth
abilities.desc: Speak a doom with a date; when it arrives, the target dies wherever and whatever they are, no save, no appeal.

abilities.name: All Nights Are One Night
abilities.desc: Step from any darkness into any other darkness you have ever hunted through, arriving mid-stride.

abilities.name: Season of the Wolf
abilities.desc: Passive: in every winter everywhere, your speed, senses, and inevitability effects act at double strength.

abilities.name: Bar the Door Anyway
abilities.desc: Nothing barred, warded, or hidden counts as shelter from you; entering costs you only the courtesy of knocking once.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and hunt the year itself through its shortest days, until the calendar concedes and gives its longest night your name.
Let the Wolf of the Long Night die in the histories — mourned, disputed, complete — and answer to the season instead.
Keep the calendar for one full year: every doom spoken anywhere falls due on your night, and none may come early.
Spare one door on the longest night, unknocked, so the marches keep lighting fires instead of despairing of them.

nodes.name: Hearthlaw
nodes.role: Primal warden — instinct-deep protection of the fires
nodes.lore: Wolves are born knowing not to cross firelight. Nothing taught them; something set it there, and the marches know what. When the First Beast finished defending the fires one by one, the defending settled into every wild thing's blood as law. Hearthlaw is what remains: a rank, an instinct, a boundary the dark obeys.
nodes.playstyle: Hold every fire at once. Project den-law across whole regions, command the instincts of wild things, and be present wherever firelight meets the dark.

abilities.name: Every Fire a Den
abilities.desc: Any lit fire counts as your den: allies within its light cannot be moved, feared, or hunted.

abilities.name: Bred in the Bone
abilities.desc: Passive: beasts and beast-spirits obey you as instinct, not command; compulsion cannot make them cross you.

abilities.name: Answer Every Fire
abilities.desc: Step out of any hearthfire within the marches when something threatens the people keeping it.

abilities.name: The Old Shape at the Edge
abilities.desc: Things from beyond the firelight must challenge you before touching anyone inside it; most, remembering, decline.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and defend one fire each night of a whole winter, no two fires alike, until the dark stops testing and starts remembering.
Give the eldest spirit back its shape and keep only the duty, so that what walks to the fires now is yours alone.
Be present at two fires at once, verifiably, on a night when both needed you.
Watch a wolf refuse to cross firelight, and know the refusal by name, because it is yours.

nodes.name: The Old Ache
nodes.role: Cosmic attrition — the world's pain answers to one
nodes.lore: Old scars ache when weather turns. Healers call it humors; the marches know the truth: something passes, taking a census. The Agonarch's ledger outgrew one body, and now every healed wound in the world reports to the office that survived it. Three faiths define damnation as a fraction of what it carries.
nodes.playstyle: Carry all pain that was ever survived. Draw on a world's worth of banked hurt, wake old wounds in enemies, and be past killing.

abilities.name: The Census of Scars
abilities.desc: Sense every scarred creature in a region, know each wound's story, and draw fury from the sum.

abilities.name: Every Wound Remembers
abilities.desc: Reopen any healed wound an enemy has ever taken; veterans face you carrying their whole careers.

abilities.name: Ache Before the Storm
abilities.desc: Passive: every scarred creature within a day's ride feels you coming, and chooses its side early.

abilities.name: Past Killing
abilities.desc: Passive: you cannot die of damage; anything that would kill you becomes pain, and pain has nowhere left to go but out.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and take on the ache of every scar you have ever caused, all at once, and remain standing while it settles.
Let the Agonarch's annals close with a death the witnesses agree on, and keep walking under a name only weather uses.
Answer one old soldier's aching knee in person, at his fire, and take the ache with you when you go.
Hold the world's whole hurt through one long night without spending any of it on anyone, to prove you keep it and not the reverse.

nodes.name: The Glacier
nodes.role: Geologic catastrophe — unstoppable mass on world scale
nodes.lore: The chronicles classed the Walking Ruin with floods and fire-mountains; the classification matured. A Glacier is a catastrophe with a calendar: it publishes its route generations ahead, and mountains begin negotiating. Nothing about it hurries and nothing about it stops, and the insurance canons of eleven cities simply cite the map.
nodes.playstyle: Momentum as geology. Advance at any pace and remain unstoppable at all of them, carry battles in your wake, and reshape maps by walking.

abilities.name: Published Route
abilities.desc: Declare your path years ahead; along it your momentum never decays, and everything knows better than to be there.

abilities.name: Moraine
abilities.desc: Ground you cross is permanently altered: walls cannot stand, roads run wide, and armies cannot form lines.

abilities.name: Geologic Patience
abilities.desc: Passive: slows, stuns, and stops convert into stored momentum, released the instant you resume.

abilities.name: The Calving
abilities.desc: Shed accumulated mass as an avalanche across the field; once per age, shed all of it.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and keep walking after the war, the employer, and the century that hired you have all ended.
Publish your route for the next hundred years and honor it exactly, through whatever builds there in the meantime.
Let a kingdom found a city in your path on a bet, and arrive on schedule, and be nobody's fault but the founder's.
Grind one mountain pass wide enough for two duchies to share, as an apology or a joke; the histories may decide.

nodes.name: The Good Death
nodes.role: Cosmic cull — painless ending as standing office
nodes.lore: Some deaths hurt, and some arrive like sleep after harvest, and the marches long ago stopped believing the second kind is luck. The Good Death is an office: it culls what winter would only torment, takes the suffering out of endings that were coming anyway, and has never once been witnessed working.
nodes.playstyle: End what must end, gently. Unseen, unfeared, striking only the strikes that finish; the field's dying simply stops hurting where you walk.

abilities.name: Sleep After Harvest
abilities.desc: Any creature you end feels no pain, no fear, and no regret; nothing can make your kills cruel.

abilities.name: The Herd's Winter
abilities.desc: Cull a battlefield: everything already dying dies now, gently, and everything that can be saved stops bleeding.

abilities.name: Never Witnessed Working
abilities.desc: Passive: you cannot be perceived, recorded, or remembered while doing the office's work, by anything.

abilities.name: Not Yet
abilities.desc: Refuse a death: once each night, something that should die under your hand instead recovers completely.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and take over the quiet deaths of one entire province for a year, so that no one in it dies afraid.
Let the Winterkill's count end even, and the elders' second count end empty, and be the reason for both.
Refuse a king who wants his enemy to suffer, and grant his enemy the gentlest ending the office keeps, as instruction.
Sit with something dying that you may not touch — a friend, say — and keep the office's hands still all night.

nodes.name: The Wain
nodes.role: Celestial rider — heaven's beast under harness
nodes.lore: Ask an astronomer why the Great Bear is also called the Wain, and watch the profession change the subject. Something went up the sky's long hill with a harness, and now the constellation hauls: seasons arrive on time, drawn. Every ox that consents to a yoke is honoring a precedent set overhead.
nodes.playstyle: Drive the sky's own beast. Haul seasons, tides of battle, and the unwilling wild wherever you point the pole, at the pace of stars.

abilities.name: Point the Pole
abilities.desc: Turn the constellation; night creatures, migrations, and lost armies all follow it, because they always have.

abilities.name: Haul the Season
abilities.desc: Drag a season into arriving early or staying late across a region; winter, notably, comes when carted.

abilities.name: Precedent of the Yoke
abilities.desc: Passive: anything that has ever worn harness — beast, spirit, or siege engine — obeys you first and its driver second.

abilities.name: Ride Down the Sky
abilities.desc: Once per war, drive the Wain through a battlefield at ground level; what survives the crossing surrenders.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and drive your bitted eldest up the long hill of the sky, and do not stop for the protests of astronomers.
Yoke it to something that must be pulled and cannot be — the year, say — and lean in until it moves.
Let the marches rename the stars for your cart while you are still using it, which is the only fame the office permits.
Come down once a year in deep winter to haul firewood for the village that fed you, because the point was never the sky.

nodes.name: The Cost
nodes.role: Universal reciprocity — violence priced, collected in person
nodes.lore: Old captains tell recruits to count the cost before drawing. They no longer mean it as figure of speech. Since the Unwounded's skin outlasted its chroniclers, every blow struck anywhere carries a price that is somewhere, patiently, being counted — and marshals who plan wars now leave one chair empty at the table.
nodes.playstyle: Make violence expensive. Every hostile act near you rebounds by law rather than reflex, and entire campaigns stall when the arithmetic is shown.

abilities.name: The Empty Chair
abilities.desc: Attend any council of war uninvited; plans made in your presence honestly price their own harms, aloud.

abilities.name: Law, Not Reflex
abilities.desc: Passive: within a mile of you, all damage dealt is simultaneously dealt to its dealer; no speed, ward, or god exempts.

abilities.name: Collect in Person
abilities.desc: Name a slaughter that went unpaid, however old; its price transfers to you to deliver, with your hands.

abilities.name: Waive Nothing
abilities.desc: You cannot be bribed, blessed, or argued out of the collection; effects that would compel mercy fail, expensively.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and stand between two armies at the charge, and let both learn at the first exchange what the morning will cost.
Collect the price of a massacre three generations cold, from the house that profited, in full view of the histories.
Take a blow meant for no one — spite, spent on a wall — and return it anyway, so the law admits no exceptions.
Sit in the empty chair at a war council, once, and watch the war be quietly cancelled.

nodes.name: The Common
nodes.role: World-law — ground unclaimable, walls impossible
nodes.lore: Where the Fallow finished, grass came back; where the Common walks, ownership does not. Ground it has crossed can never again be walled, deeded, or held — it becomes common land by a law no crown remembers passing and none has survived contesting. Shepherds graze three former empires and pay no one.
nodes.playstyle: Abolish the fortified world. Walls fail near you on principle, claims lapse, and battle becomes what it was first: bodies on open ground.

abilities.name: No Fences
abilities.desc: Passive: walls, wards, and borders within a mile of you stop functioning as barriers; they remain, embarrassed, as suggestions.

abilities.name: Common Ground
abilities.desc: Declare a battlefield common land; neither side may fortify, entrench, or hold it, and sieges there simply lapse.

abilities.name: The Grazing Right
abilities.desc: Allies on unowned ground heal, regain fury, and cannot be dispossessed of their footing by any force.

abilities.name: Older Than Crowns
abilities.desc: Laws, decrees, and magical claims of ownership have no hold on you or anything you stand upon.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and walk the borders of every land you ever levelled; where your feet pass, the fences forget which side is whose.
Outlast the last deed that names your first razing, and be present, politely, when the archive's wall comes down.
Refuse a throne offered by people who misunderstood you completely, and level nothing in the refusing.
Watch shepherds graze the ground where the citadel stood, arguing about weather, owing nothing, and go unrecognized among them.

families.name: Knight
families.tagline: The vow outlasts the flesh that swore it.
families.description: Every Knight begins the same way: kneeling, speaking words that cannot be unsaid. What follows differs. Some vows shine — a promise to stand between the helpless and the dark until one of them breaks. Others are grimmer bargains, taking curses and sins onto shoulders built to carry them. The armor is incidental. The Knight is whatever the oath, kept long enough, makes of a person.

nodes.name: Knight
nodes.role: Tank — frontline defense, damage mitigation
nodes.lore: Every hold keeps a few: squires who knelt in a cold chapel and rose owning nothing but a promise. A knight-errant of the first vow guards roads, wells, and other people's harvests. Most die unremembered. The rest learn what the vow is for, and what it will eventually cost.
nodes.playstyle: Plant your feet and make the enemy's choices for them. Taunt, intercept, and trade your own health for everyone else's, one blow at a time.

abilities.name: Sworn Interception
abilities.desc: Dash to an ally within 8 meters and absorb the next attack meant for them, taking 30% reduced damage.

abilities.name: Iron Tithe
abilities.desc: Taunt all enemies in melee range for 4 seconds; gain 2% damage reduction per enemy affected.

abilities.name: Kneel and Rise
abilities.desc: Once per battle, drop to one knee to block a killing blow, then rise with 20% temporary health.

abilities.name: Vow's Edge
abilities.desc: Your strikes deal 15% bonus damage to any enemy currently attacking someone other than you.

progressionSteps: Kneel a full night on chapel stone and speak the First Vow aloud to no one; the words must survive the cold.
Carry a wounded stranger seven miles in your own armor, and take nothing for it.
Stand your first watch on a wall that is attacked, and do not leave your post before relief comes.
Have your shield marked by a sworn knight who has watched you bleed for someone else.

nodes.name: Oathwarden
nodes.role: Bulwark tank — party-wide mitigation and zoning
nodes.lore: Oathwardens are what garrisons request by name when the dark presses in. They have learned the radiant discipline: that a shield is a wall, a wall is a promise, and a promise held long enough becomes a fact. Villages measure their worth in raids that turned back without a fight.
nodes.playstyle: Anchor the line with wide guard zones and interposed shields. You win by outlasting: every second you hold, the enemy's plan rots a little further.

abilities.name: Bulwark Litany
abilities.desc: Chant while guarding; allies behind you take 20% less damage for as long as you have not moved.

abilities.name: The Turning Hour
abilities.desc: After blocking ten attacks, release a radiant pulse that staggers every enemy engaging you.

abilities.name: Shieldmeet
abilities.desc: Lock shields with an adjacent ally to form a two-person wall that cannot be flanked for 6 seconds.

abilities.name: Beacon Guard
abilities.desc: Raise your shield overhead; ranged attacks aimed at allies within 5 meters strike you instead.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10, then hold a breach alone until the militia rallies behind you; a single step backward forfeits the trial.
Take the Radiant Oath at dawn before the people you failed to save, and name each of them without flinching.
Reforge your shield with a rim of temple silver and carry it unbloodied through one full season of war.

nodes.name: Knight Penitent
nodes.role: Sacrificial tank — damage transference, self-attrition
nodes.lore: The Dread Oath is signed, not spoken — in the petitioner's own blood, witnessed by whatever is listening. A Knight Penitent takes what others cannot survive carrying: a widow's curse, a village's plague-fear, a soldier's unforgivable order. The armor grows heavier every year, and none of the added weight is steel.
nodes.playstyle: Pull harm onto yourself deliberately — hexes, wounds, terrors — and convert the accumulating weight into grim endurance and slower, heavier blows.

abilities.name: Take This From Them
abilities.desc: Transfer one curse, debuff, or wound from an ally onto yourself; gain 5% damage per affliction carried.

abilities.name: Grief Iron
abilities.desc: Your armor hardens with each burden you bear, granting stacking damage reduction up to 40%.

abilities.name: The Heavier Hand
abilities.desc: A slow overhead blow dealing bonus damage equal to twice the number of burdens you currently carry.

abilities.name: Signed in Red
abilities.desc: Once per day, refuse a death: survive at 1 health and accept a permanent burden stack instead.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10 and sign the Dread Oath in your own blood, on a page that already bears ninety-nine names.
Take a dying man's confession and carry his sin a full year without telling a living soul.
Eat the curse laid on a stranger's child, and walk away before the family can thank you.

nodes.name: Gatesworn
nodes.role: Anchor tank — chokepoint denial, immovable guard
nodes.lore: A Gatesworn weds a threshold. Some hold a literal gate for decades; others carry a portable arch of blessed stone and declare any doorway theirs. Armies planning a route will pay well to learn where the Gatesworn stand, then plan a different route. Their funerals are held standing up.
nodes.playstyle: Choose the ground and become its law. Enemies pass you only diminished; you are weakest in the open field and monstrous in a doorway.

abilities.name: Threshold Decree
abilities.desc: Sanctify a doorway or chokepoint; enemies crossing it are slowed 50% and marked for allied attacks.

abilities.name: Root of the Arch
abilities.desc: Become immovable: immune to knockback, pulls, and forced movement while standing on ground you have sanctified.

abilities.name: None Pass Whole
abilities.desc: Strike freely at any enemy moving through your reach; each hit reduces their damage by 10%.

abilities.name: The Long Stand
abilities.desc: For every consecutive minute you do not move, gain 5% block chance, stacking until you step away.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and hold the Weeping Gate through a full assault; the count of those who passed you must be zero.
Sleep thirty nights standing armored in the arch you mean to swear to, and do not fall.
Speak your gate's true name; you will only have learned it if the stone has accepted you.
Turn away a king who demanded passage you were sworn to refuse, and survive what follows.

nodes.name: Lanternshield
nodes.role: Escort tank — mobile sanctuary, protective auras
nodes.lore: Where the Gatesworn hold ground, Lanternshields move it: refugees through night country, pilgrims through plague towns, children out of cities already burning. Each carries a consecrated flame in the shield's boss that has never gone out. It is said the dark itself follows a Lanternshield at a respectful distance.
nodes.playstyle: Herd the vulnerable inside your light and keep the column moving. You fight walking backward, shield high, always the last one through.

abilities.name: The Carried Flame
abilities.desc: Your shield casts a 6-meter light; allies inside are immune to fear and take 15% less damage.

abilities.name: Rearguard Psalm
abilities.desc: While withdrawing from combat, you and escorted allies gain 25% movement speed and cannot be slowed.

abilities.name: Shepherd's Rebuke
abilities.desc: Slam your shield to blind every enemy that entered your light this turn, driving them back 4 meters.

abilities.name: No One Left
abilities.desc: Pull a downed ally instantly into your light and stabilize them; usable once per encounter.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and lead a hundred souls through the Hollowing Fen by night, losing none. Not one.
Kindle your shield's flame from a temple hearth and keep it burning through storm, river, and battle for a year.
Walk into a plague quarter no priest will enter, and carry out whoever still breathes.
Refuse payment three times from people who owe you their lives; the flame dims for those who profit by it.

nodes.name: Hexdrinker
nodes.role: Attrition tank — curse absorption and conversion
nodes.lore: Hexdrinkers apprentice under witch-scarred elders, learning to open the body like a door and invite the curse inside. Their veins darken; their shadows misbehave. Cursed villages send for them the way other villages send for physicians, and pay in advance, since a Hexdrinker's gratitude is a complicated thing to hold.
nodes.playstyle: Seek out the worst magic on the field and drink it. Each swallowed hex disfigures you and empowers you in equal measure.

abilities.name: Open the Vein
abilities.desc: Draw an active curse, hex, or damaging field into your body, ending its effect and gaining a Draught stack.

abilities.name: Blackblood Riposte
abilities.desc: Spend a Draught to lash out with the stolen curse, afflicting your attacker with exactly what you swallowed.

abilities.name: Scar Ledger
abilities.desc: Each permanent curse scar grants 3% resistance to all magic, recorded visibly on your skin.

abilities.name: The Third Swallow
abilities.desc: At three Draughts your strikes apply a decaying weakness; at five, you begin to hear the curses speak.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and drink your first named curse from a witch-elder's cup, knowing she will not tell you which one.
Carry a plague-hex through a crowded city without letting it leap to a single soul, though it begs you in your own voice.
Map the scars on your body and recite what each one spared, without error, before the Penitent conclave.
Refuse the one curse you are not yet ready for. Knowing which one it is constitutes the trial.

nodes.name: Black Confessor
nodes.role: Dread vanguard — fear control, condemned execution
nodes.lore: Black Confessors hear what the dying cannot say to priests, and carry it so the dead may travel light. Where law fails, they execute the condemned themselves, the sin passing into the Confessor at the killing stroke. Towns are quieter after one leaves. So, forever after, is the Confessor.
nodes.playstyle: Fight under a mounting weight of borrowed guilt that terrifies enemies and fuels merciless finishing blows. Isolate the guilty, judge, and end it.

abilities.name: Last Rites
abilities.desc: Mark an enemy Condemned; your attacks against them cannot be blocked, and their allies flee the killing blow.

abilities.name: Litany of the Carried
abilities.desc: Recite the sins you bear; enemies within earshot suffer fear and drop their guard for 5 seconds.

abilities.name: Absolving Stroke
abilities.desc: Execute a Condemned enemy below 30% health, absorbing their sin as a Grief stack that empowers your next mark.

abilities.name: Weight Made Wrath
abilities.desc: Convert all Grief stacks into a single strike dealing damage for every confession you have ever carried.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and hear the deathbed confession of a man you hate, then bury him gently and tell no one.
Carry out one lawful execution the town's own headsman refused, and stay to dig the grave.
Sit vigil beside a mass grave until you can name the sin that filled it, then take that sin as your own.
Let a guilty man you could have judged walk free, because judgment was not yours that day.

nodes.name: Warden of the Last Door
nodes.role: Siege anchor — unbreakable line, threshold command
nodes.lore: The Order of the Last Door keeps the thresholds that must never open: sealed crypt-gates, breachways to the deep dark, the doors kingdoms pretend they do not have. Each Warden knows only their own door and one other's, so no captured mind can unmake the whole. Relief never comes; it is never requested.
nodes.playstyle: Not a defender but a fact of architecture. Project fields of absolute denial, punish anything that tests the line, and never, ever be lured out.

abilities.name: The Door Holds
abilities.desc: While you stand within a sanctified threshold, enemies beyond it cannot reduce you below 1 health.

abilities.name: Masonry of Will
abilities.desc: Raise a 10-meter rampart of force with your health and your stubbornness; it stands for 20 seconds.

abilities.name: Toll of Passage
abilities.desc: Every action an enemy takes inside your threshold costs them 5% of their maximum health.

abilities.name: Bar the Door
abilities.desc: Slam your door: hurl all enemies out of the threshold and lock it against them for 12 seconds.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and be summoned; no one petitions the Last Door. The Order watches, and the Order writes to you.
Hold a nameless door for a year against something that knocks politely every midnight, and never once answer.
Learn your predecessor's fate from the scratches on the inside of the door, and take the post anyway.
Swear the Warden's silence: you will tell no one what you guard, including yourself, in dreams.

nodes.name: Dawnward
nodes.role: Radiant guardian — mass aegis, battlefield deliverance
nodes.lore: Dawnwards carry morning into places that have forgotten it — mines gone wrong, cities under endless eclipse, the marches where night stopped ending. Their number is never more than twelve. When a Dawnward's flame enters a dark that has held for years, things with long patience finally learn what waiting costs.
nodes.playstyle: Project overwhelming sanctuary: vast light-fields, mass shields, allies dragged back from the brink. Your presence rewrites what the dark is permitted to do.

abilities.name: Borrowed Morning
abilities.desc: Ignite a 20-meter field of daylight for 15 seconds; creatures of darkness within it lose all damage bonuses.

abilities.name: Aegis Unnumbered
abilities.desc: Grant every ally standing in your light a shield equal to 25% of your maximum health.

abilities.name: The Waking Word
abilities.desc: Speak the old word for dawn; all downed allies in your light rise with a third of their health.

abilities.name: Eclipse Debt
abilities.desc: Damage prevented by your shields accumulates; release the total as a cone of searing light.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and carry your flame into the Sunless March, where it will either die or become something else.
Stand where dawn has not come in living memory, and hold your light aloft until it does.
Give your flame to a dying Dawnward's shield and receive theirs; twelve there are, and twelve there must remain.
Learn the old word for morning in the tongue the dark still fears, from the only mouth that remembers it.

nodes.name: The Leaden Chalice
nodes.role: Curse vessel — sealed affliction arsenal
nodes.lore: When a curse is too great to break — a king's bloodline blight, a battlefield that will not stop screaming — it is given to a Leaden Chalice to hold. Their bodies are engraved with binding scripture; their footsteps are recorded in three separate archives. They are venerated, escorted, and never, ever touched.
nodes.playstyle: Walk the field as a sealed arsenal. Endure almost anything passively, and choose with great care the moment to crack a seal and let one horror out on your terms.

abilities.name: Sealed Scripture
abilities.desc: Each Great Curse you carry radiates dread; enemies who strike you risk brief affliction by what leaks through.

abilities.name: Crack the First Seal
abilities.desc: Release one carried curse in a 12-meter burst, afflicting all enemies with its original, unweakened form.

abilities.name: Leaden Skin
abilities.desc: Your engraved flesh reflects 30% of magical damage back upon the caster as raw curse.

abilities.name: The Weight Rests
abilities.desc: Kneel and go inert for 6 seconds: untargetable and immovable while your seals fully restore.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and accept a Great Curse no circle of nine could break, sealed beneath your own engraved skin.
Endure the Scriving: a year of binding scripture cut into you, one verse each dawn, none taken under mercy of drink.
Walk to a war and stand between the armies until both remember what you carry. Then go home.
Name your successor and begin their scars yourself, for the curses must never be left ownerless.

nodes.name: Dolorous Guard
nodes.role: Terror arbiter — judgment burst, morale ruin
nodes.lore: The Dolorous Guard number whatever the age requires. They arrive uninvited wherever a realm's sin has grown too heavy — a massacre unpunished, a treaty signed in children's blood — and take the weight by force of judgment. Kings do not welcome them. Kings also do not stop them. No one does.
nodes.playstyle: Enter the field as a verdict. Break enemy morale in waves, isolate the guiltiest, and deliver executions that make the survivors lay down arms.

abilities.name: The Arrival
abilities.desc: Your first appearance in battle forces every enemy to check morale; the guilty are revealed and Marked.

abilities.name: Sentence Pronounced
abilities.desc: Declare a Marked enemy's sin aloud; they take 40% increased damage from all sources for 10 seconds.

abilities.name: Iron Requiem
abilities.desc: Advance slowly and unstoppably; each step releases carried griefs as waves of terror that break formations.

abilities.name: Take the Kingdom's Weight
abilities.desc: Absorb a battlefield's collective guilt: massive Grief stacks, at the cost of reduced maximum health until dawn.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and judge a crowned head before its own court, carrying every sin you name out of the hall.
Bear the massacre of Cold Hollow for a decade; the Guard will weigh you by how quietly you carry it.
Be feared correctly: let a burning village's raiders surrender at the mere sound of your approach.
Give judgment against a member of the Guard itself, and be the one who carries what they carried.

nodes.name: Ostiary
nodes.role: Sanctum host — open threshold, interior punishment
nodes.lore: Where the Last Door teaches that a perfected gate never opens, the Ostiaries hold the opposite heresy: a door that cannot open is only a wall with a title. They keep the sanctuary doors — open to anyone fleeing, at any hour — and answer personally for everything that follows the fleeing in.
nodes.playstyle: Fight with the door open. Let the enemy cross onto ground you have consecrated, then close it behind them; nothing you admit leaves unjudged.

abilities.name: Right of Entry
abilities.desc: Allies who reach your threshold gain sanctuary: untargetable for 5 seconds and healed for 15% of their maximum health.

abilities.name: Be Welcome
abilities.desc: Invite an enemy across your threshold; if they cross, they are slowed 30%, silenced, and cannot recross outward for 8 seconds.

abilities.name: The Door Answers
abilities.desc: Whenever an enemy crosses your threshold, strike them with an automatic counterblow that interrupts whatever they were attempting.

abilities.name: Guest-Law
abilities.desc: Admitted enemies deal 20% less damage to anyone but you; striking another guest brands them, increasing all damage they take by 25%.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and unbar a sanctuary door during a siege, because one family was still outside. The Order counts what you let in, and what you saved.
Keep a door open for a year in country where the Wardens sealed theirs, and bury what comes through wrongly with your own hands.
Refuse a Warden of the Last Door who orders your door shut, courteously, twice; the third refusal is traditionally made with drawn steel.
Learn the guest-law by heart and enforce it once against a guest you loved.

nodes.name: Lampblack
nodes.role: Covert escort — hooded light, unseen columns
nodes.lore: The Dawnwards burn the dark back; the Lampblacks call that vanity with a body count, since every blaze shows the wolves where the column walks. They soot their mail, hood the consecrated flame behind a shutter, and move the helpless through night country unseen, unheard, and unthanked — the flame still burning, merely private.
nodes.playstyle: Shepherd the column in silence. Muffle sound and lamplight, deny ambushes before they form, and when discovered, snap the shutter open and blind what found you.

abilities.name: Shuttered Flame
abilities.desc: Your consecrated light persists but casts nothing; allies within 6 meters are muffled and cannot be detected by sight or sound.

abilities.name: Soot and Psalm
abilities.desc: Whisper the psalm rather than sing it; escorted allies leave no tracks and make no sound above a heartbeat for 30 seconds.

abilities.name: Snap the Shutter
abilities.desc: Unhood the lantern into a foe's eyes: blinded for 6 seconds and marked, taking bonus damage from allies striking out of darkness.

abilities.name: Wolf-Count
abilities.desc: You always know how many hunters stalk your column, their bearing, and which one has noticed you.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and cross the Sunless March without your flame showing once; the Dawnwards crossed it burning, and the Order counts their dead differently.
Blacken your mail with soot from your own shield's flame, and let no smith polish it again.
Move a hundred souls past a thing that hunts by light, close enough to hear it breathing, and be gone before it learns the country was ever peopled.
Accept that no songs will be made of you; the Lampblacks keep their own count, and it is enough.

nodes.name: Gallglass
nodes.role: Retribution tank — swallowed hexes carried home
nodes.lore: The Leaden Chalices call containment sacred; the Gallglasses call it a hoard of other people's ruin. Their doctrine is short: every curse has an author, and an address. They drink the hex, temper it a year in their own blood, and deliver it home — armor quenched black and polished to a mirror, so the maker meets the work.
nodes.playstyle: Drink what the enemy casts, temper it in your blood, and hand it back sharpened. The more a foe curses you, the worse their homecoming.

abilities.name: Quenched in Gall
abilities.desc: Hostile magic striking you is dulled by 25% and remembered; your blackened plate records each caster's name in its tarnish.

abilities.name: Carried Home
abilities.desc: Return one drunk curse to its original author at triple potency; range is unlimited if you know their name.

abilities.name: The Maker's Face
abilities.desc: Enemies whose curse you carry see their own work in your mirror-plate and falter, losing 15% accuracy and all morale bonuses.

abilities.name: Honed Affliction
abilities.desc: Spend a Draught to edge your blade with a swallowed hex; your next three strikes afflict exactly as the original curse did.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and carry your first curse home: three years, two borders, and a witch who believed herself forgotten. Give it back gently. Once.
Quench your armor in your own hexed blood and polish it until the first curse-author flinches at their reflection.
Stand before the Leaden Chalice conclave and refuse the veneration; tell them what you told the road: nothing is kept.
Deliver one curse to an author already dead, and learn where curses go when the address fails.

nodes.name: Shriver
nodes.role: Redeeming vanguard — pacification, burden theft
nodes.lore: The Dolorous Guard lifts a realm's sin by ending the sinner; the Shrivers call the axe a confessor's failure of nerve. A Shriver takes the whole sin — the deed, the memory, the taste of it — and the shriven walk away clean, to their victims' fury. Mercy, the Order teaches, is heavier than the axe, and rarer.
nodes.playstyle: Win by unmaking the will to fight. Strip rage, guilt, and frenzy from enemies and carry it yourself; the emptied yield, and yielding is victory.

abilities.name: Take the Deed
abilities.desc: Strip an enemy's empowering rage, frenzy, or blood-rite and carry it as a burden stack; they fight sober and diminished.

abilities.name: Shrift Before Steel
abilities.desc: Offer shrift once per foe; one who accepts lays down arms, leaves the battle, and cannot be harmed by your allies.

abilities.name: Clean Hands
abilities.desc: Take an ally's kill as your own; whatever grief, curse, or consequence it earns falls to you instead.

abilities.name: Heavier Than the Axe
abilities.desc: Subduing strikes deal bonus damage per burden carried but can never kill; enemies dropped this way wake shriven and harmless.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and shrive a man the Dolorous Guard has already sentenced, then stand between him and the Guard until one of you kneels.
Carry a murderer's memory of the deed for a season, waking each night at the hour it happened, and return him nothing.
Face the victims' families with the man you cleaned, and take their fury too; it is also a weight, and also yours now.
Refuse to shrive one who wants the sin lifted but not left; learn the difference in their eyes, for the whole craft is there.

nodes.name: The Unfallen
nodes.role: Mythic bastion — absolute lockdown, undying stand
nodes.lore: Histories disagree on whether the Unfallen is one knight or a title passed down a chain of doors. What the sieges agree on: somewhere there is a threshold that has never been crossed, and a figure in fused armor who has not sat down in a hundred years. Armies route around the legend.
nodes.playstyle: Cease to be a combatant and become terrain. Nothing crosses your line, nothing moves in your presence uninvited, and nothing kills what stands behind you.

abilities.name: Terminal Threshold
abilities.desc: Declare a line; for 30 seconds no enemy, projectile, or spell crosses it while you draw breath.

abilities.name: The Standing Century
abilities.desc: You cannot die while holding your ground; lethal damage instead petrifies armor plates, shed when the battle ends.

abilities.name: Stone Remembers
abilities.desc: Every foe your line has ever stopped adds a permanent sliver to your block; the total no longer fits in ledgers.

abilities.name: Let Them Break
abilities.desc: Reflect one siege-scale attack in full back along its path, unmaking whatever engine sent it.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and hold your door through the Sundering Siege; the histories will record that it did not open, and not your name.
Outlast the thing that knocks: when midnight comes and no knock follows, your watch has changed something.
Let your armor fuse. A smith will offer to cut you free, once, and the refusal is the rite.
Be mistaken for a statue by the pilgrims who come to see you, and permit it.

nodes.name: The Last Lantern
nodes.role: Mythic sanctuary — inviolable light, mass deliverance
nodes.lore: Doctrine holds that when the final light in the world gutters, one flame will remain, carried on a shield. Refugee songs in twenty tongues describe the same figure at the rear of the column, walking backward, the dark keeping its distance like a whipped animal. No song describes them arriving. Only leaving last.
nodes.playstyle: Your light is sanctuary in law and in fact: absolute protection for everyone within it, and a slow, patient sentence for whatever waits outside.

abilities.name: Sanctum Absolute
abilities.desc: Allies in your light cannot be targeted, cursed, or frightened; the radius grows with each soul it shelters.

abilities.name: The Long Walk Home
abilities.desc: Escorted allies leave no tracks, feel no cold, and heal steadily so long as the column keeps moving.

abilities.name: Undimmed
abilities.desc: Your flame cannot be extinguished by any means yet recorded; each attempt blinds the attacker for 8 seconds.

abilities.name: Dawn Called Early
abilities.desc: Once per day, summon true daylight for one full minute, regardless of hour, depth, or curse.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and walk the Night That Stayed from edge to edge, gathering everyone still alive inside it.
Bring your column home with more souls than you set out with, and account for each addition.
Set your flame against the oldest dark and do not blink. The witnesses say the dark blinked.
Be sung of in a tongue you have never heard, by people you never reached; the light travels further than you do.

nodes.name: The Hollow Grail
nodes.role: Mythic vessel — curse singularity, cataclysmic release
nodes.lore: Scholars argue whether the Hollow Grail is a knight or a containment. Both are true. One vessel in an age drinks past the ninety-ninth seal and does not burst; what remains walks, speaks courteously, and holds enough bottled ruin to end a continent. Nations keep certain treaties specifically to avoid disturbing it.
nodes.playstyle: Carry apocalypse politely. Overwhelming passive dread, near-total immunity to magic, and the option — never yet fully taken — of opening every seal at once.

abilities.name: Ninety-Nine Seals
abilities.desc: You carry the great curses of an age; hostile magic cast near you is drawn in and simply kept.

abilities.name: A Sip Returned
abilities.desc: Pour a single measure from one seal onto an enemy; the affliction is centuries stronger than when it was bottled.

abilities.name: The Quiet Brim
abilities.desc: Lesser enemies cannot bring themselves to strike you; those who manage it are cursed by proximity alone.

abilities.name: Grail Overturned
abilities.desc: Open every seal at once. The codex does not record the effects, only the names of the craters.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and drink the hundredth curse, the one every Reliquary before you refused, and remain courteous.
Sit in the treaty hall while nations negotiate around your silence; understand that your presence is the peace.
Hear all ninety-nine speak at once and answer none of them, for a year and a day.
Choose, daily, not to overturn. The histories call this the longest vigil, and it is the whole of the rank.

nodes.name: The Nameless Vow
nodes.role: Mythic reckoning — inevitable judgment, terror incarnate
nodes.lore: Somewhere the weight of every carried sin passes a threshold, and the knight beneath it stops being anyone. The Nameless Vow has no face witnesses agree upon, no grave, no beginning. It is what arrives when a wrong has grown too vast for courts, gods, or armies — and kneels to lift it.
nodes.playstyle: You are the last consequence. Unstoppable advance, absolute terror, and judgments that end wars because no one present dares be found guilty.

abilities.name: The Unspoken Sentence
abilities.desc: Enemies who witness your judgment of another must flee, surrender, or share the sentence.

abilities.name: No Face, All Doors
abilities.desc: You cannot be scried, ambushed, or barred; guilt is a door, and everyone has one.

abilities.name: Kneel to Lift It
abilities.desc: Absorb a calamity-scale wrong whole — a razed city's grief, a broken god's oath — and rise armored in it.

abilities.name: The Vow Outlasts
abilities.desc: On death, the Vow does not end; it stands the body back up and finishes the judgment first.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and take up a sin so vast the carrying erases you; your name goes first, and you let it.
Judge a god's broken oath and make the judgment hold; the priesthoods will deny this happened, forever.
Walk out of every history that recorded you; the Dolorous Guard's own archive keeps an empty page in your honor.
Answer, when the last wrong asks who bears it now: no one does. And mean it.

nodes.name: The Errant Door
nodes.role: Mythic sanctum — wandering threshold, absolute refuge
nodes.lore: The same iron-banded door appears in accounts three centuries apart: in a hillside above a massacre, in a burning city's blind alley, once in the open sea. The hunted knock and are received into a hall that cannot be found again. Scholars dispute whether the knight keeps the door or the door keeps the knight.
nodes.playstyle: Carry refuge itself. Open your door where it is needed — behind the routed, ahead of the hunted — and make any battlefield a place with an exit.

abilities.name: A Door Where None Was
abilities.desc: Set your threshold into any surface; allies may pass through into your sheltered hall and out again, anywhere within 40 meters.

abilities.name: The Knock Received
abilities.desc: Answer an ally's knock from any distance; you and your door arrive at their side within 3 seconds.

abilities.name: Hall Beyond
abilities.desc: Allies within your hall cannot be tracked, scried, or harmed, and bleeding-out is suspended while they remain inside.

abilities.name: Closed Behind You
abilities.desc: When the last ally passes through, the door closes; pursuers who strike it take all the damage it refused that battle.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and open a door out of a city that has already fallen; the histories will record survivors and no explanation.
Unhinge your sworn door and carry it on your back until the road teaches it to wander.
Be knocked for from three hundred leagues away, and arrive before the knock has finished.
Open onto the sea, onto the sky, and once onto the inside of a sealed grave; a door is a promise that there is another side.

nodes.name: The Hooded Star
nodes.role: Mythic guide — unseen passage, hunter's bane
nodes.lore: Refugee columns that should have died speak of a star low over the treeline that no pursuer could see, moving when they moved, gone by morning. No song names the roads taken; the roads themselves seem not to remember. Twenty years of war have produced exactly one portrait, and the frame is empty.
nodes.playstyle: Be the light only your people can see. Guide entire columns invisibly, unmake pursuit itself, and leave the war unsure you were ever in it.

abilities.name: Star for the Hunted
abilities.desc: Allies anywhere on the field see your position as a low guiding light; no enemy sense or spell can perceive it.

abilities.name: The Road Forgets
abilities.desc: Paths your column travels close behind you; tracks, scent, and all memory of your passing fade within a minute.

abilities.name: Gone by Morning
abilities.desc: End an engagement at will: your escorted allies fade from enemy perception for 10 seconds of unmolested withdrawal.

abilities.name: One Lamp, No Shadow
abilities.desc: Your hooded flame casts no shadow and never has; magic that strikes at shadows finds nothing of you to hold.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and bring a nation's worth of hunted across a border watched by ten thousand eyes, and let the tally of the seen be zero.
Walk beneath the open sky for a year without casting a shadow the enemy's diviners can find.
Refuse the Dawnwards' twelfth shield when it is offered you, kindly; your flame answers a question they have stopped asking.
Become a rumor of a rumor: let the songs about the columns you saved credit the weather, and correct no one.

nodes.name: The Patient Mirror
nodes.role: Mythic reflector — inevitable return, stored malice
nodes.lore: Curse-speakers in six kingdoms now write their words down rather than say them, because the said ones come back. Not swiftly — the Mirror is patient — but entire covens have disbanded upon hearing a courteous greeting, decades late, and recognizing their own phrasing. What it carries, it carries politely, and it has never once arrived early.
nodes.playstyle: Absorb everything hostile without hurry, and return it on your own schedule. Your power is the certainty: nothing cast at you is ever wasted, only delayed.

abilities.name: Glass Remembers
abilities.desc: Store any hostile spell or curse instead of suffering it; there is no limit, and nothing stored decays.

abilities.name: On Your Own Words
abilities.desc: Return any stored affliction to its caster at a moment of your choosing; it arrives unblockable, phrased exactly as cast.

abilities.name: Decades Late
abilities.desc: When you enter battle, one curse you ever carried relapses upon its author, wherever in the world they are.

abilities.name: The Mirror Declines
abilities.desc: Once per battle, refuse a hostile effect outright; its caster suffers it instead, and understands that a schedule now exists.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and outwait a curse whose author will not die for forty years; the Order will teach you nothing about patience you do not already keep.
Carry one hundred curses at once without keeping a single one past its delivery; the Chalices hold, the Mirror only waits.
Be unsaid: hear a witch recall her words at the mere rumor of you, and let her; requital is for the said.
Answer the scholars who ask what you are with the only true thing: a schedule.

nodes.name: The Mercy
nodes.role: Mythic absolution — war's end, wrath unmade
nodes.lore: The misericorde is the thin blade that ends a fallen knight; the order retired the knife and kept the name. The Mercy has shriven things priests deny have souls, and once, an entire army the night before its battle — both sides woke emptied of the war, and the field stayed green. Kings find this more frightening than the Guard.
nodes.playstyle: End fights by removing what fuels them. Wrath, orders, causes — you take them all, and stand heavier each time, while armies discover they have no quarrel.

abilities.name: Shrive the Field
abilities.desc: Strip every enemy within 20 meters of rage, orders, and cause; those left with no reason to fight stop fighting.

abilities.name: The Retired Knife
abilities.desc: You cannot deliver a killing blow; anything that yields to you cannot be killed by anyone for one hour.

abilities.name: Take the War Itself
abilities.desc: Absorb a battle's collective grievance as burden stacks; both sides deal 5% less damage per stack while you stand.

abilities.name: Never Set Down
abilities.desc: Gain 1% damage reduction per burden carried, with no cap; you have not set one down in living memory.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and shrive something the priests deny has a soul, then decline to attend the theological crisis that follows.
Walk between two armies the night before their battle and take the war; the treaties will claim the credit, and you will let them.
Inherit the retired misericorde and let it rust shut in its sheath; the day you consider drawing it, begin the rank again.
Be found by the worst thing living, walking toward you, hoping. Do not turn it away.

nodes.name: The Immured
nodes.role: Apotheosis — living architecture, absolute permanence
nodes.lore: Masons know the rule though none can source it: a wall holds if someone is inside it. Somewhere the Unfallen stopped shedding the petrified plates and let the stone finish. Pilgrim maps mark a stretch of rampart that is warm in winter, where sieges fail for reasons engineers refuse to publish, and offerings are left in the arrow-slits.
nodes.playstyle: Become the fortification. Your body is wall, gate, and garrison at once; allies fight from you, and nothing you enclose can be reached at all.

abilities.name: Let the Stone Finish
abilities.desc: Become living rampart: forty meters of indestructible wall, you inside it, for 20 seconds.

abilities.name: Warm in Winter
abilities.desc: Allies sheltering at your wall heal steadily and cannot rout, freeze, or despair; the warmth deepens with each siege you have outlasted.

abilities.name: Load-Bearing Myth
abilities.desc: Structures you touch cannot collapse and lines you anchor cannot break; the rule holds because you are inside it.

abilities.name: Unpublished Reasons
abilities.desc: Siege engines and battering rams targeting your wall fail mechanically, inexplicably, and permanently; their engineers retire early.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and let the stone finish what the fusing began; the smith will not offer again, and you will not be asked to sit.
Hold a wall that is also you through a hundred-year siege; you may count the first fifty years as rest.
Feel the kingdom build onto you — towers, chapels, laundry lines — and permit all of it; a wall serves, or it is only stone.
Answer the pilgrims' offerings once a century, briefly, so the masons' rule stays a rule and never becomes a question.

nodes.name: The Kept Morning
nodes.role: Apotheosis — custodial dawn, light as law
nodes.lore: Astronomers keep missing it: dawn is not arriving on its own. Each morning is fetched, carried up over the rim of the world, and set burning by an office the doctrine finally has a name for. The Last Lantern walked out of its songs and into the schedule of the sky. The dark has filed no further objections.
nodes.playstyle: Carry daylight as an office, not a spell. Where you stand is morning, permanently; the dark must renegotiate the whole battlefield around that fact.

abilities.name: The Fetched Sun
abilities.desc: True morning exists within 30 meters of you regardless of hour, depth, curse, or eclipse, and does not expire.

abilities.name: Schedule of the Sky
abilities.desc: Declare dawn early; when it arrives, every ally rises reset, as if fully rested, once per day.

abilities.name: Relieved at Dawn
abilities.desc: Any ally who survives to your morning is healed whole and cleansed; their night watch, the office rules, is over.

abilities.name: No Further Objections
abilities.desc: Creatures of darkness inside your morning may not use darkness for anything; the matter has been ruled upon.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and fetch one morning yourself, from wherever mornings wait, because the sun was late and the columns could not be.
Give your flame to the horizon the way you once gave it to twelve shields, and take the horizon's watch in exchange.
Keep the schedule for a mortal lifetime without one late dawn; the world has stopped checking, which is the trust, which is the weight.
Walk backward out of your own songs, still facing the dark, and let morning answer to your office and not your name.

nodes.name: The Sealed Age
nodes.role: Apotheosis — era-scale custody, ruin annulled
nodes.lore: Historians divide time by it now: before the Sealing, and since. Somewhere the Hollow Grail made the daily choice so many times that it stopped being a choice and became a condition of the world — ruin flows downhill into one custody, and the age simply does not end the way its curses intended. Treaties cite it. None dare footnote it.
nodes.playstyle: Be where ruin goes. All catastrophe on the field drains toward you and is kept; your allies fight inside the calm you are keeping.

abilities.name: Before and Since
abilities.desc: Field-scale catastrophes — spells, plagues, collapses — occur inside your custody instead of the world; observers note only a quiet.

abilities.name: Ruin Runs Downhill
abilities.desc: All curses, afflictions, and hostile fields within 40 meters drain slowly into you, where they are kept indefinitely, politely.

abilities.name: The Condition of the World
abilities.desc: You cannot be possessed, unmade, or overturned; effects that attempt it are sealed on contact and counted among your keeping.

abilities.name: A Century, Poured
abilities.desc: Pour one measure of what the age gave you upon an enemy army; the effect predates description.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and keep the vigil past counting: when you notice you have stopped choosing, because there is no longer a choice, the age has sealed.
Outlive the treaties written around your silence, and be cited by their successors as terrain.
Accept the age's last unclaimed ruin — the small, spiteful, household kind — for the seal is not sealed while one curse sleeps outside it.
Answer the historians' one question — what happens when you die — by continuing not to.

nodes.name: The Assize
nodes.role: Apotheosis — judgment as natural law
nodes.lore: Above a certain weight, wrongs now answer for themselves — armies desert the day before atrocities, tyrants confess to empty rooms. Jurists call it the Assize: the court that convenes wherever it is needed, needing no summons, no bench, and no name for its judge. The empty page in the Guard's archive has begun issuing rulings.
nodes.playstyle: Convene rather than fight. Your presence is a sitting court: the guilty weaken under their own verdicts, and battles end as sentences, not slaughters.

abilities.name: Court in Session
abilities.desc: While you stand on a field, every combatant's guilt is weighed continuously; the guilty deal reduced damage proportional to the weight.

abilities.name: No Summons Needed
abilities.desc: Appear at any wrong of sufficient weight as it happens; distance, walls, and wards are procedural details, and overruled.

abilities.name: Sentence Without Judge
abilities.desc: Condemn an enemy without word or gesture; the sentence executes itself through their own hands, arms, and allies.

abilities.name: The Docket Endures
abilities.desc: Wrongs that flee your field are continued, not dismissed; they resume with greater weight wherever the offender next draws steel.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and convene where no one called you, for the wrong had no witnesses left; a court that requires summons is only a queue.
Sit in judgment of a wrong done to you, and recuse the last of yourself that could still be wronged; what remains is the court.
Let kingdoms write you into their law codes between flood and lightning, and be exactly as negotiable.
Adjourn once an age, wherever mercy files its appeal, and grant it; even the Assize answers to something.

nodes.name: Hinge of the World
nodes.role: Apotheosis — universal threshold, world-spanning sanctuary
nodes.lore: Somewhere the Errant Door stopped being a door and became the reason doors work. Cartographers note the phenomenon without explaining it: the cornered find hinges where there was stone, and things that hunt have learned to dread a rectangle of lamplight opening in the dark. The world turns on it. It still answers knocks personally.
nodes.playstyle: Doors are your jurisdiction. Step out of any of them, decide what every threshold on the field permits, and give whole armies somewhere to run.

abilities.name: Every Door Is Yours
abilities.desc: Emerge from any doorway, arch, or gate in the world; enemies learn that closed rooms are a courtesy you extend.

abilities.name: Jurisdiction of Thresholds
abilities.desc: Every doorway on the field obeys you — opening, shutting, admitting, refusing — at any distance, without your hand.

abilities.name: The World Ajar
abilities.desc: Once per battle, set before every ally a door that leads home; those who step through arrive, whatever stood between.

abilities.name: What the Hinge Bears
abilities.desc: You cannot be moved, sealed, or barred; force spent trying turns the hinge and heals you instead.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and let the door go through you: hinge, hasp, and grain, until knocking anywhere is knocking on you.
Answer, in one night, every knock in the world that no one else will answer; dawn is permitted to find you tired.
Decline every shrine the grateful raise over hillsides where your door once stood; a hinge that accepts worship begins to stick.
Be, at last, on both sides of every door at once, and keep each side's secret from the other.

nodes.name: The Kindly Dark
nodes.role: Apotheosis — sheltering night, hunters starved
nodes.lore: There are nights now that take sides. Hunted things — children, columns, whole routed armies — pass through them unseen, while hunters starve on empty roads. Peasants call it the kindly dark and leave a hooded lamp out for it. Somewhere inside the weather there is still a knight, walking rearguard for everyone at once.
nodes.playstyle: Be the night your allies move through. Extinguish enemy perception across the whole field, carry the desperate inside your weather, and let pursuit die of hunger.

abilities.name: The Dark Takes Sides
abilities.desc: Night falls across the battlefield for enemies only; allies see clearly, and every hostile lantern, spell-light, and torch gutters.

abilities.name: Rearguard for the World
abilities.desc: Any ally anywhere who flees something stronger gains your escort: unseen, untracked, and unslowed until they reach safety.

abilities.name: Hunter's Famine
abilities.desc: Enemies without a visible target weaken each second, losing damage and resolve; the stacks do not expire while night holds.

abilities.name: A Lamp Left Out
abilities.desc: Allies sheltering near any lamp left burning for you receive your protection whether or not you attend in person.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and give your name to the night; it will spend it better than you did.
Shelter, in a single winter, everyone who runs: the guilty and innocent alike, for the dark does not stop to try cases.
Let the last portrait's empty frame be buried with honors in your stead, and attend, unrecognized, at the back.
Teach one night, somewhere, to be kind without you, then walk on; the weather must outlive the walker.

nodes.name: Arc of Malison
nodes.role: Apotheosis — curses arc home, cursing ends
nodes.lore: In the latter histories, cursing simply stops paying. Malice thrown hard enough curves; the learned draw the arc on slates and cannot find the bend's cause, only its constancy. Grandmothers put it plainer: what you say comes home. Inside the law there is still a knight, walking the long curve, making certain.
nodes.playstyle: You are the bend in every hostile trajectory. Sorcery, arrows, and intentions curve back toward their sources while you walk the field, unhurried, confirming.

abilities.name: The Long Curve
abilities.desc: Hostile projectiles and spells within 30 meters bend homeward; their authors become valid targets for their own work.

abilities.name: Law of the Said
abilities.desc: Enemies who speak incantations, orders, or threats aloud in your presence suffer the stated effect themselves first.

abilities.name: Nothing Lands
abilities.desc: Once per battle, for 10 seconds, no hostile effect anywhere on the field lands except at its point of origin.

abilities.name: The Arc Confirmed
abilities.desc: When returned malice ends its author, every affliction on your allies departs early, homeward, at speed.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and bend one curse you did not carry: prove the road home now runs without a courier.
Survive the age's cursers uniting to curse the Arc itself, and let the field where they tried grow grass again in your lifetime.
Be demoted from person to proverb, and answer to it: what you say comes home.
Walk the long curve once, all the way around, and arrive behind the first word ever spoken in spite. The histories decline to record what you did there.

nodes.name: The Intercession
nodes.role: Apotheosis — suspended endings, sovereign mercy
nodes.lore: Every gallows in the world now hesitates. Between sentence and stroke there is a pause that was not there in older histories — one breath, in which anything may be said. Most say nothing, and the stroke falls. But the pause belongs to an office, and the office is occupied, and some breaths have lasted years.
nodes.playstyle: Stand inside the pause before every ending. Suspend deaths, verdicts, and final blows across the field, and decide which of them ever resume.

abilities.name: The Breath Between
abilities.desc: Every killing blow on the field is suspended for one breath; you may stand inside any of them, regardless of distance.

abilities.name: Mercy's Delay
abilities.desc: Suspend one death indefinitely; the target cannot die, act, or be acted upon until you release the breath.

abilities.name: Heard at Any Distance
abilities.desc: Every plea for mercy on the field reaches you, and grants the pleader your damage reduction until you have answered it.

abilities.name: Some Breaths Last Years
abilities.desc: Once per day, extend the pause over an entire battle; nothing ends — no death, no rout, no fall — until you exhale.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and lend your last breath to the pause; the world will return it whenever anything is about to end, which is always.
Attend every execution in the world for one season, unseen, and intervene at only one; the choosing is the office.
Hear your name become a legal term in kingdoms that never knew you, and let the lawyers keep it; they use it more gently than kings did.
Take the last unshriven weight, the world's own, and hold the pause while it confesses; it is still confessing.

families.name: Gladiator
families.tagline: The pit keeps count; the crowd keeps gods.
families.description: Nobody chooses the pit. It buys its fighters, sentences them, or accepts the rare fool who volunteers, and it teaches them all the same double lesson: survival is arithmetic — reach, footing, the cost of every swing — and the crowd is a second opponent, one that can be won. Some gladiators fight the thing in front of them. The great ones fight the ten thousand watching.

nodes.name: Gladiator
nodes.role: Melee striker — momentum and showmanship
nodes.lore: Sold, sentenced, or foolish enough to volunteer — the pit takes all kinds and issues them the same sand. A new gladiator owns nothing; even the sword is counted back at the gate. The first lesson is not swordwork. It is that ten thousand strangers are watching, and that this can be used.
nodes.playstyle: Fight loud. Showy strikes and taken risks feed Acclaim, and Acclaim feeds you; a quiet, careful bout is a losing one.

abilities.name: Face the Stands
abilities.desc: Deal 10% more damage while any creature other than your target can see you.

abilities.name: First Blood Flourish
abilities.desc: Drawing first blood in an encounter grants Acclaim and 15% attack speed for 8 seconds.

abilities.name: Sand in the Eyes
abilities.desc: Kick grit into a foe's face, blinding them for 3 seconds; the crowd approves of dirty fighting done crisply.

abilities.name: Counted Steel
abilities.desc: You take no penalty fighting with borrowed, broken, or improvised weapons; the pit rarely issues better.

progressionSteps: Enter by any of the three doors — sold, sentenced, or volunteered — and understand that the sand does not care which.
Survive your first bout, and hear one stranger in the stands say your name to another.
Learn the gate's arithmetic: the sword is counted out and counted back, and you are a smaller entry in the same tally.
Bleed once where everyone can see, and notice what the roar does to the pain.

nodes.name: Crowdheart
nodes.role: Acclaim striker — crowd-fed surges
nodes.lore: A Crowdheart is a fighter who has stopped hearing the roar as noise and started hearing it as rations. They fight facing the expensive seats, take wounds where wounds show, and finish bouts the way the stands want them finished. Promoters bill them early; the crowd bills them forever.
nodes.playstyle: Court the stands with risk and flourish to build Acclaim, then spend it in surges of strength the quiet fighter never gets.

abilities.name: Drink the Roar
abilities.desc: Gain Acclaim whenever the crowd reacts — first blood, a near miss, a flourish; at full Acclaim your strikes deal 30% more.

abilities.name: Play to the Gods
abilities.desc: Salute the cheapest seats; for 10 seconds every landed attack counts as a performance, generating double Acclaim.

abilities.name: Wound Them Pretty
abilities.desc: Your bleed effects are visible from any seat and demoralize enemies who can see them, reducing their damage 10%.

abilities.name: The Second Opponent
abilities.desc: You always know the crowd's mood; while it favors you, fear and taunt effects against you fail.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10 and top a bill for the first time; the promoter will spell your name wrong, and the crowd will correct him.
Fight one full bout facing the stands more often than the opponent, and win it.
Take a wound you could have avoided because the third tier could not see the fight, and make it worth their fare.
Refuse the quick kill at the crowd's whistle, and give them the long one they paid for.

nodes.name: Undercard
nodes.role: Survivalist skirmisher — scavenged arms, control
nodes.lore: The undercard fights at noon, when the seats are half empty and the beasts are half starved. No one bets much and no one is buried well. What the Undercard learns instead of applause: chain reaches farther than pride, nets beat pedigree, and everything on the sand is a weapon, including the sand.
nodes.playstyle: Win ugly. Scavenge weapons mid-fight, trip and tangle, spend nothing you cannot recover, and let better-armed fighters tire themselves on your patience.

abilities.name: The Pit Provides
abilities.desc: Any object you lift counts as a weapon you are proficient with; improvised arms in your hands strike 20% harder before breaking.

abilities.name: Length of Chain
abilities.desc: Sweep a three-meter chain to trip every enemy in an arc; downed foes lose their next action.

abilities.name: Cheap Blood
abilities.desc: Kills made with scavenged or improvised weapons restore 10% of your health; what the pit left lying around costs nothing.

abilities.name: Gate-Read
abilities.desc: Study the gate before it opens; learn what is released two seconds before your enemies do.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10 by staying alive through a season of noon slaughters, which is the only promotion the undercard offers.
Kill something with the weapon it broke off you.
Learn the tells of every beast in the menagerie by feeding them, cleaning them, and twice nearly being them.
Be the last fighter of your intake still breathing, and drink once for each of the others.

nodes.name: Ovant
nodes.role: Morale tank — adoration as armor
nodes.lore: An Ovant walks out to a wall of sound and wears it. The crowd's love is real and it is load-bearing: blades turn on it, fear breaks against it, and every chant of the name the stands invented adds a course of stone. An Ovant unloved is just meat, and trains accordingly.
nodes.playstyle: Hold the middle of the sand and be adored. Acclaim converts to mitigation; your work is to remain magnificent while everything hits you.

abilities.name: Worn Ovation
abilities.desc: Gain 1% damage reduction per stack of Acclaim, to a maximum of 40%; the reduction is audible.

abilities.name: They Came for This
abilities.desc: Taunt every enemy that can see you; while Acclaim is above half, taunted foes cannot target anyone else.

abilities.name: The Chant Holds
abilities.desc: While the crowd chants your name, you cannot be staggered, feared, or knocked from your feet.

abilities.name: Blindfold Trust
abilities.desc: Fight blind or in darkness without penalty; the stands call the blows as they come, and you have learned to listen.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and earn a name you did not choose; you will know it is yours when the stands teach it to strangers.
Fight a full bout blindfolded, guarded only by the crowd shouting the blows as they come, and take no serious wound.
Stand in the sand after a loss and be cheered anyway; adoration that only attends victory is a wage, not armor.
Visit the market unarmored and count how many hands touch you for luck. Above a hundred, you are ready.

nodes.name: Sandpainter
nodes.role: Burst striker — composed executions
nodes.lore: Sandpainters have the arena raked flat before their bouts, the way a canvas is stretched. They fight in arranged strokes — a wound here, a fall there — building toward a finish the connoisseurs in the good seats will describe for years. The kill is the picture; everything before it is underdrawing.
nodes.playstyle: Compose the bout. Place wounds deliberately to build the picture, then deliver the finishing stroke you designed, when the light is right.

abilities.name: Raked Canvas
abilities.desc: Your first exchange marks the foe as your subject; your critical chance against the subject rises 5% each round.

abilities.name: Placed Wounds
abilities.desc: Wounds you deal to a new location — brow, thigh, sword-arm — each grant a Composition stack; stacks empower your finisher.

abilities.name: The Stroke They Came For
abilities.desc: Consume all Composition stacks in one execute; below 35% health the subject dies if you hold three or more stacks.

abilities.name: Red Perspective
abilities.desc: Enemies who witness your finished work are shaken, losing 15% accuracy until they leave the field or the memory.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and finish a bout so cleanly that the good seats stay seated after, discussing it.
Take a patron's commission for a specific ending and deliver it exactly, to the wound.
Halt a winnable bout once because the light was wrong, and accept the fine without argument.
See a rival copy your finish in another city, and take it as the compliment it is.

nodes.name: Trammel
nodes.role: Controller — nets, chains, subtraction
nodes.lore: A Trammel's kit is a jailer's: net, hook, weighted cord, three ells of chain. The doctrine is subtraction — first the weapon, then the footing, then the air — until what remains of the opponent is a decision rather than a fight. Swordsmen call it cowardice, usually from the ground.
