nodes.playstyle: Strip choices. Disarm, entangle, and drag until the enemy has nothing left to fight with, then collect whatever the bout was for.

abilities.name: The Cast
abilities.desc: Throw a weighted net over a foe within 10 meters, immobilizing them for 4 seconds; strength shortens this, cunning does not.

abilities.name: Confiscation
abilities.desc: Rip a weapon from an enemy's grip; disarmed foes take 25% more damage from you and know it.

abilities.name: Short Leash
abilities.desc: Hook a tangled enemy and drag them to any point within your chain's reach, including through their allies.

abilities.name: Ells of Iron
abilities.desc: Your chain parries as a shield and strikes as a flail; nothing inside its circle keeps its footing for long.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and take a champion swordsman's blade, feet, and surrender, in that order, without giving him a wound worth stitching.
Net something that flies before it lands, and hold it down while it argues.
Fight one bout with nothing you brought: win with what the pit provides or do not come back for your kit.
Learn the eleven knots from a retired jailer, and pay whatever is asked; the price is famous and worth it.

nodes.name: Remainderman
nodes.role: Attrition fighter — outlasting, cost control
nodes.lore: The pit's clerks coined the title as a joke: when a bout's estate settles — beasts fed, wagers paid, sand raked — the Remainderman is what is left standing to inherit. They study the gate the way farmers study weather: everything it releases has a cost of moving, and can be made to spend it.
nodes.playstyle: Spend less than everything you fight. Evade, block cheaply, punish exhaustion, and be standing at the settlement, which is the whole of the craft.

abilities.name: Spend Them First
abilities.desc: Enemies attacking you burn stamina 30% faster; the pit pays patience better than fury.

abilities.name: Gait-Study
abilities.desc: After observing an enemy for six seconds, automatically evade the first use of their strongest attack.

abilities.name: The Cheap Parry
abilities.desc: Your blocks and parries cost no stamina against foes more tired than you.

abilities.name: Inheritance
abilities.desc: Each bout survived to the end grants a small permanent bonus to health; the estate accumulates.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and outlast a gate-beast without striking it once; the clerks will record the bout as weather.
Walk the sand at dawn and price every scrap on it — chain, splinter, bone — before the rakes come.
Survive the afternoon they empty the menagerie on you, and lodge a complaint about the scheduling.
Inherit a dead man's kit, oil it, and retire it with honors the day you can afford better. Keep the whetstone.

nodes.name: Chantborne
nodes.role: Communion tank — crowd-fed restoration, shared vigor
nodes.lore: Chantborne kneel to the stands before each bout, and mean it. Their doctrine holds the roar is the only honest god — ten thousand hearts agreeing at once — and it answers: wounds close at the chant's peak, and the fighter rises carried. Priests attend with notebooks and leave unhappy.
nodes.playstyle: Be the congregation's own. Build the chant, then stand inside it — healing, unbreakable, and generous — while it carries the whole bill.

abilities.name: The Roar Answers
abilities.desc: At peak chant, recover 25% health and shed every curse, fear, and poison; the stands do not permit them.

abilities.name: Carried on Voices
abilities.desc: While the chant sustains, you cannot be slowed or staggered, and you move fastest toward the greatest danger.

abilities.name: Give It Back
abilities.desc: Spend all Acclaim to grant every ally 20% damage and immunity to despair for 10 seconds; the love was never only yours.

abilities.name: Ten Thousand Hearts
abilities.desc: Enemies who strike you at peak chant are deafened and shaken by the crowd's fury for 4 seconds.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and kneel to the stands before a bout you may not survive, sincerely; the roar knows flattery from prayer.
Be healed of a wound the chirurgeons had priced as mortal, at the chant's peak, before witnesses including one furious priest.
Fill an arena in a plague year, and send every soul home well.
Answer the theologians' inquiry by inviting them to stand in the sand while ten thousand voices agree about you. None have accepted twice.

nodes.name: Coupsmith
nodes.role: Executioner — one rehearsed, perfect stroke
nodes.lore: Coupsmiths hold that the finishing stroke is the entire art and everything before it scaffolding. Each forges one named stroke and rehearses it for years — against posts, carcasses, weather — until cities book the stroke rather than the fighter. Their bouts are short. The queue for seats is not.
nodes.playstyle: Wind one spring all bout. Every feint and placed wound exists to set the named stroke, and the named stroke ends the conversation.

abilities.name: The Named Stroke
abilities.desc: Your signature execution: damage scales with every round spent preparing it, and the crowd knows it is coming, which is the point.

abilities.name: Scaffolding
abilities.desc: Your other attacks deal 20% less but build Craft twice as fast; nothing you do is for its own sake.

abilities.name: Unveiling
abilities.desc: Delivered at peak Acclaim, the Named Stroke cannot be parried, dodged, or survived by anything below half health.

abilities.name: Once, Cleanly
abilities.desc: If the Named Stroke kills, all Craft is refunded and every enemy who saw it loses their next action.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and forge your stroke: one motion, named, rehearsed ten thousand times against oak, carcass, and winter.
Deliver it before a full house on the first attempt; a Coupsmith who winds twice is a fencer with ambitions.
Decline to use it for an entire season of victories, so the name gathers weight while the queue gathers length.
Watch another fighter attempt your stroke and fail, and send the widow your fee for the lesson.

nodes.name: Quartergiver
nodes.role: Capture controller — nonlethal mastery, living leverage
nodes.lore: Quartergiver doctrine is arithmetic with a pulse: a corpse fetches one purse, a captive three — ransom, rematch, and gratitude. They net beasts for menageries, fighters for ransom, and once a warlord for a city's peace. The Haltermen call the practice sentiment with rope. The Quartergivers call it Tuesday.
nodes.playstyle: Take everything alive. Subdue, bind, and hold; every captive is leverage, and a field emptied by capture pays three times over.

abilities.name: Alive Is Worth More
abilities.desc: Your subduing strikes deal double effect; anything you reduce to helplessness is captured, not killed.

abilities.name: The Gentle Cast
abilities.desc: A net that pins without crushing; captives inside cannot act but take no harm from any source.

abilities.name: Custody
abilities.desc: Enemies will not strike through your captives; while you hold one, their formation must route around your position.

abilities.name: Terms of Release
abilities.desc: Release a captive under terms; they leave the field entirely, and their allies' resolve drops 15%.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and take a famous killer alive while the stands screamed for death; collect the ransom, the rematch, and — eventually — the gratitude.
Net a gate-beast a menagerie can display, unscarred; scarred stock is a butcher's trade, and you are not one.
Hold a warlord three days against his own army's arguments, and price the peace politely.
Keep count of everyone you have taken alive; the day the count means nothing to you, the Haltermen were right, and you must stop.

nodes.name: Reckoner
nodes.role: Attrition tank — counted certainty, perfect economy
nodes.lore: A Reckoner fights with a running count: swings the foe has left, breaths the beast spends per charge, blood a body can price before noon. They place no wagers — the creed holds that the only bet worth making is one already decided, which no odds-house will take. Bookmakers post their bouts as exhibitions.
nodes.playstyle: Count everything, risk nothing. Decline bad trades, tax enemy waste, and finish when the arithmetic says finished, not before.

abilities.name: Running Count
abilities.desc: You see every enemy's remaining stamina, uses of their strongest attacks, and roughly how long their courage lasts.

abilities.name: Declined
abilities.desc: Once per round, refuse an unfavorable exchange: automatically evade one attack that would cost you more than the counter earns.

abilities.name: Waste Tax
abilities.desc: Enemies who miss you lose 5% damage for the encounter, stacking; the count remembers.

abilities.name: Settled Early
abilities.desc: Against any foe whose count you have completed, your strikes deal 30% more; you are no longer fighting, only concluding.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and call a bout aloud before it happens — every exchange, every wound, the ending — and be right before witnesses.
Be refused by every odds-house in the city; certainty is bad business, and yours is now notorious.
Fight the bout your count says to decline by declining it, publicly, at cost to your name. The count outranks the crowd.
Teach one young fighter to count, and watch them live. It is the only profit the craft shares.

nodes.name: Impresario
nodes.role: Deception fighter — staged openings, scripted bouts
nodes.lore: Where the Chantborne kneel to the crowd, the Impresarios seat it. Their heresy is simple: the roar is not a god but an instrument, and instruments are for playing. An Impresario's stumbles are choreography, their near-defeats are acts, and their opponents die on cue, having rehearsed without knowing it.
nodes.playstyle: Script the bout. Feed the crowd manufactured peril, bait enemies into the openings you wrote for them, and collect on every cue.

abilities.name: Staged Stumble
abilities.desc: Feign a fatal opening; the first enemy to take it is countered for triple damage and the crowd's derision.

abilities.name: Rehearsed Without Knowing
abilities.desc: Study a foe for two exchanges; afterward, you may declare their next attack, and it is so.

abilities.name: House Lights
abilities.desc: Control what the crowd sees; gain Acclaim on your schedule rather than the fight's, one stack per second of theatre.

abilities.name: Die on Cue
abilities.desc: Your killing blows land at the exact peak of crowd noise, generating double Acclaim and staggering every enemy who watched the act.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and stage a near-defeat so exact that three physicians certify the peril; recover at the scripted beat.
Fight a bout in which every wound you take was budgeted the night before, and finish under budget.
Watch a Chantborne kneel to the stands, and understand you will never again feel what they feel. This is the fee, and it is paid once.
Fill the arena for a fighter nobody has heard of, twice; the second time proves it was not luck.

nodes.name: Showbleeder
nodes.role: Blood-fueled bruiser — wounds as escalating theatre
nodes.lore: Showbleeders call the Coupsmiths' art half a picture: the opponent's death is a stranger's story, but your own blood is the only paint you ever really own. They open themselves deliberately — a line across the chest before the first exchange — and rage never touches it. Every drop is budgeted.
nodes.playstyle: Bleed on schedule. Each shown wound buys Acclaim and power; build to the crescendo where you are almost dead and entirely unstoppable.

abilities.name: Overture Cut
abilities.desc: Open the bout by wounding yourself; gain 20 Acclaim and 15% damage while the cut shows.

abilities.name: Budgeted Drop
abilities.desc: Bleeding never kills you and cannot be inflicted on you by enemies; your blood spends only on your instruction.

abilities.name: Red Crescendo
abilities.desc: Below 30% health, your damage, speed, and Acclaim gains double; the last act is the whole reason for the ticket.

abilities.name: Cannot Look Away
abilities.desc: Enemies within sight of your open wounds lose 15% accuracy; fascination, the chirurgeons write, presents like fear.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and open your own cheek before a full house, smiling, and hear what silence sounds like the moment before a roar.
Map your body into what may be spent and what must be kept, and never once spend past the line.
Fight the crescendo bout: begin it whole, end it at the edge, win it there, and walk out unassisted.
Tell a Coupsmith, courteously, that his masterpiece dies with the other man; yours goes home with you every night.

nodes.name: Halterman
nodes.role: Lockdown executioner — binds that finish
nodes.lore: The Haltermen's creed fits on a knife: what the chain takes, the chain keeps. A thing spared is a rematch on delay, and rematches kill netmen — they have counted. So the bind is the sentence and the tightening is the verdict, and no Halterman has ever met an escaped opponent twice.
nodes.playstyle: Bind to end. Your chains close like verdicts — no rescue, no ransom, no rematch — and everything they hold, they conclude.

abilities.name: What the Chain Takes
abilities.desc: Enemies you bind cannot be healed, freed, teleported, or rescued by any strength or spell their allies have brought.

abilities.name: The Tightening
abilities.desc: Bound foes take mounting damage each second, doubling every third second; struggle accelerates the schedule.

abilities.name: Halter-Cast
abilities.desc: Hurl a noose that silences and drags a foe to your feet; casters find the silence the worse half.

abilities.name: No Rematch
abilities.desc: Execute any bound enemy below half health instantly; the stroke cannot be interrupted, and their allies must check morale.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and bind the thing that had escaped every pit in three provinces, then end it before the applause, not after.
Refuse a ransom that would have beggared a duke, with the rope already tight; the Quartergivers still tell it as a tragedy.
Keep the halter of everything you have concluded, knotted once each, and carry the weight without complaint.
Meet an opponent you spared in your netman days, survive the lesson, and never need it taught again.

nodes.name: Stakesman
nodes.role: Gambler bruiser — all-or-nothing violence
nodes.lore: Stakesmen call the Reckoners embalmed. A certainty pays even, they say, which is to say nothing; the pit only pays what you stake. So they post their own odds and fight under them — offhand only, blindfolded, two gates at once — and the stands love them the way they love a coin still in the air.
nodes.playstyle: Stake to win. Declare handicaps for multiplied returns, ride streaks, and treat your own blood as table money — feast or famine, nightly.

abilities.name: Posted Odds
abilities.desc: Declare a handicap at the bout's start — halved armor, wrong hand, no sight; win under it and all rewards triple.

abilities.name: Ride the Streak
abilities.desc: Each kill without taking a hit doubles your Acclaim gains; one clean hit against you clears the table.

abilities.name: Deadman's Flip
abilities.desc: When a blow would kill you, flip: heads, survive at 1 health with doubled damage; tails, it lands. Once per day.

abilities.name: Against the Line
abilities.desc: Gain 8% damage for every way the field outmatches you — numbers, size, reach, ground; hopeless is a stance.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and post your own death-odds at the gate, in numbers a child could check, then beat them before witnesses.
Wager your sword-hand on a bout and win; wear the unclaimed stake with more respect afterward.
Lose everything once — purse, kit, name on the bill — and rebuild it from one copper and an undercard slot.
Tell a Reckoner what the count leaves out, and fight the bout his arithmetic declined. Win or lose, that is the whole quarrel.

nodes.name: The Adored
nodes.role: Mythic bulwark — love as fortress
nodes.lore: Histories dispute whether the Adored is one fighter or a title the crowd re-bestows when needed. The accounts agree on the rest: cities riot when their bouts move elsewhere; wounds they take are felt, faintly, by everyone watching; and an army once refused battle rather than be hated by its own home crowd.
nodes.playstyle: Stand inside a love with structural properties. The chant absorbs what strikes you, turns crowds against your enemies, and rebuilds you mid-blow.

abilities.name: Ten Thousand Take It
abilities.desc: While the chant holds, a third of all damage you suffer disperses into the crowd, who consider it fair.

abilities.name: Beloved Past Reason
abilities.desc: Enemies must overcome the chant to strike you at all; most swings falter mid-arc, and the crowd counts each one aloud.

abilities.name: The Chant Rebuilds
abilities.desc: At peak chant, regenerate 5% health per second; chirurgeons have stopped attending your bouts.

abilities.name: Turn the Stands
abilities.desc: Point at one enemy; the crowd turns on them, stripping 20% speed and resolve and feeding you Acclaim each time they act.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and be adored in a city you have never visited, in a tongue you do not speak.
Take a wound before a full house and hear ten thousand people gasp with the pain of it — shared, divided, survivable.
Have a war postponed because you were fighting that day, and never learn which side asked.
Walk through a riot held in your honor, untouched, touching everyone.

nodes.name: The Immaculate Wound
nodes.role: Mythic executioner — the one perfect stroke
nodes.lore: Anatomists dispute that the stroke is possible; the exhibits disagree. The Immaculate Wound's kills leave one mark, exact, and nothing else — no bruise, no fear on the face, no second try in living memory. Those they decline to finish describe the same thing: a stillness, and a decision they were not consulted on.
nodes.playstyle: End bouts at the moment you select, with the wound you designed. The fight is a formality the stroke permits to occur.

abilities.name: One Mark Only
abilities.desc: Your Named Stroke now kills any foe below half health, through any armor, leaving armor and cloth uncut.

abilities.name: The Consultation
abilities.desc: Choose not to finish a helpless foe; they yield permanently, and every enemy who sees the mercy loses the will to test you.

abilities.name: The Drawn Breath
abilities.desc: For the breath before your stroke, no witness — friend, foe, or crowd — can act; the moment is attended.

abilities.name: Beyond Anatomy
abilities.desc: Your critical strikes ignore resistances, immunities, and arguments; the anatomists have withdrawn their objections.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and deliver the stroke through full plate, leaving the plate unmarked; the smith will exhibit it anyway.
Decline a kill an emperor commanded, in his own box, and leave the arena at your usual pace.
Let the anatomists' guild examine your work and publish that it is impossible; do not correct them.
Perform the stroke once with no audience but the opponent, and learn whether it is still art. Do not repeat the experiment.

nodes.name: The King's Ransom
nodes.role: Mythic captor — anything taken alive
nodes.lore: The nets are famous: the king taken mid-charge through his own guard and priced politely; the plague-beast displayed alive to prove it could be; the ransom that bought every fighter in one pit their freedom. Chroniclers note the pattern with unease — nothing, so far, has proven too large to take alive.
nodes.playstyle: Capture at any scale. Giants, cavalry wedges, small armies — everything is stock, leverage, or ransom, and killing is for fighters with no imagination.

abilities.name: Nothing Too Large
abilities.desc: Your casts bind creatures of any size for 6 seconds; siege beasts and giants count as merely awkward.

abilities.name: Priced Politely
abilities.desc: While you hold a captive, their allies must parley: enemies lose one action each round to hesitation and arithmetic.

abilities.name: Living Leverage
abilities.desc: Each captive held grants your party 10% damage reduction; formations cannot charge through their own.

abilities.name: The Great Haul
abilities.desc: Once per battle, cast the wide net: every enemy within 15 meters is captured at once, and the engagement is functionally concluded.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and take a crowned king alive through his household guard, returning him unbruised at a rate history calls polite.
Empty a battlefield by capture alone; the chroniclers will check the casualty rolls twice and find them insulting.
Take alive the thing the menageries refused, and build the cage yourself.
Spend one legendary ransom buying every fighter in the pit that made you, and post no notice of it.

nodes.name: The Unspent
nodes.role: Mythic survivor — expenditure without return
nodes.lore: Every currency the pit knows has been thrown at them — beasts, engines, other legends — and the count settles the same way: expenditure, no return. Odds-houses list their bouts as exhibitions, a wager requiring two possible outcomes. One school of clerks argues the Unspent died years ago and simply declined the deduction.
nodes.playstyle: Refuse to be spent. Perfect economy made mythic: attacks cost their makers more than they cost you, and the count only ever grows.

abilities.name: Two Possible Outcomes
abilities.desc: No single blow, spell, or fall may reduce you below 1 health; the second outcome has never been in stock.

abilities.name: No Sale
abilities.desc: Once per round, an attack against you simply does not profit: negate it entirely, and the attacker loses the stamina anyway.

abilities.name: The Count Only Grows
abilities.desc: Your Inheritance bonuses no longer cap, and half their value extends to every ally on your field.

abilities.name: Declined the Deduction
abilities.desc: The first death you suffer each day is refused as a clerical error; you continue from 30% health.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and survive the menagerie emptied in one afternoon, spending less blood than a barber's nick.
Be delisted by every odds-house on the continent; frame the letters.
Outlast the arena itself — attend the demolition of the stone that first tried to spend you, and pocket a keepsake chip.
Answer the clerks' question — what would it cost — the only honest way: more than anyone has.

nodes.name: The House
nodes.role: Mythic orchestrator — bout, odds, and gate
nodes.lore: At some point the Impresario stopped appearing on the bill and became the bill. The House owns names, gates, odds, and seasons; entire rivalries are its compositions, including — the rumor runs — several wars, booked as sincerely as any undercard. Fighters discover their careers were programs. Kings discover the same, later.
nodes.playstyle: Run the field like a booked house. Enemies enter on your schedule, act on your cues, and lose at the hour printed on the ticket.

abilities.name: On the Bill
abilities.desc: At battle's start, set the order in which enemies may act; improvisation against the program costs them 20% effect.

abilities.name: The Gate Is Yours
abilities.desc: Reinforcements, ambushes, and arrivals occur only through entrances you permit, at times you find dramatic.

abilities.name: A Word with the Odds
abilities.desc: Once per battle, declare one outcome — a miss, a crit, a stumble — and it occurs as declared.

abilities.name: The House Collects
abilities.desc: Whenever an enemy plan fails on your field, you gain Acclaim and 10% damage; failure is the house's percentage.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and own, quietly, the arena that once owned you — sand, gates, and the book of names.
Stage a bout every seat believes is fate, including both fighters.
Book a war's decisive battle, sell the seating, and be gone before either general understands whose show it was.
Keep one fight in every season honest, and tell no one which; a house that is all script forgets why crowds come.

nodes.name: The Encore
nodes.role: Mythic showpiece — death as intermission
nodes.lore: Nine deaths are attested by licensed chirurgeons; the Encore disputes only the order. No one can prove which deaths were staged, and the profession has stopped trying — the boundary has worn thin on them, and death, whatever it once believed, now waits for the applause to decide the matter.
nodes.playstyle: Die as programmed, return for the bow. The final act is your home ground, and you have never once missed a curtain.

abilities.name: Attested Death
abilities.desc: Once per battle, die convincingly: untargetable while mourned, then return at the moment of your choosing with full Acclaim.

abilities.name: The Order Disputed
abilities.desc: When a blow kills you, it may be retroactively part of the act: survive at 15% health. Once per day.

abilities.name: Home Ground
abilities.desc: Below a quarter health, your abilities cost nothing and your critical strikes are guaranteed; this is where you live.

abilities.name: Worn Openly
abilities.desc: Your scars unsettle professionals: enemies who study you lose 20% resolve; chirurgeons charge you double and attend anyway.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and die before a full house, certified thrice, then take your bow before the flowers land.
Buy the three chirurgeons dinner afterward and decline, kindly, to answer the only question they have.
Let connoisseurs travel to view the scars in order, and keep one — the first — covered, always; a body needs one privacy.
Miss your own funeral for a booking, and send regrets.

nodes.name: The Certainty
nodes.role: Mythic warden — binds that conclude
nodes.lore: Kingdoms send for the Certainty when a thing must not merely die but end. Whatever the chain closes on is finished in every telling; nothing bound has returned, echoed, or been rumored since. Priesthoods object that certain deaths belong to gods. The Certainty attends anyway, and the objections have grown quieter.
nodes.playstyle: Be the conclusion. Your chain cannot be escaped, its verdicts cannot be appealed, and what you end stays ended, everywhere.

abilities.name: Closed Is Closed
abilities.desc: Your binds cannot be broken by strength, magic, or divinity; struggling is noted but changes nothing.

abilities.name: Ended, Not Slain
abilities.desc: Anything you execute cannot be raised, echoed, haunted back, or renegotiated; the matter is concluded in all jurisdictions.

abilities.name: The Chain Recalls
abilities.desc: Your cast cannot miss anything it has ever touched, at any range, through anything.

abilities.name: Counted Seconds
abilities.desc: A bound foe learns exactly how many seconds remain to them, as do you; the figure is precise and has never been revised.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and hold what legend says cannot be held, through the night it does everything the legends promised; end it at dawn.
Decline a god's petition for a prisoner's release — respectfully once, then finally.
Chain something that unmakes chains, with the one link forged from your own certainty; it is the only link that matters.
Retire the halters of your predecessors into the sea, all but one, and never explain the exception.

nodes.name: The Long Odds
nodes.role: Mythic gambler — impossibility as fuel
nodes.lore: The odds-men no longer post numbers for their bouts; the numbers embarrassed the profession. Every wager of their own life has come in, including the famous loss — the name staked and forfeited, the year fought as no one, the name won back at longer odds than it was lost at.
nodes.playstyle: Grow with the impossibility. The worse your position — numbers, wounds, prophecy — the stronger you stand, and you engineer worse on purpose.

abilities.name: Worse Is Better
abilities.desc: All your capabilities scale with how lost your cause is; at truly hopeless, they double, and the stands know the smell of it.

abilities.name: Stake Anything
abilities.desc: Wager health, weapons, senses, or Acclaim before an exchange; victory returns the stake threefold.

abilities.name: The Coin Remembers
abilities.desc: Once per battle, a killing blow becomes a flip you win; the coin knows whose it is.

abilities.name: Nameless Year
abilities.desc: Stripped of gear, allies, sight, or name, you fight at full capability; you have done this before, for longer.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 having staked your name, lost it, fought a year as no one, and won it back at longer odds. The order is mandatory.
Post a wager at ten thousand to one, your life the stake, and collect.
Take the hopeless bet no one else would carry — a doomed line, strangers, no purse — and turn it.
Refuse one sure thing on principle, publicly; certainty is the only stake beneath you.

nodes.name: The Spectacle
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the watched moment itself
nodes.lore: The fighter and the roar have finished separating. Now, wherever many hearts rise at once — coronations, executions, dawn charges — the Spectacle is in attendance, and things fighting inside it fight larger than themselves. Crowds have begun gathering ahead of anything happening. Something, the constables note grimly, always then happens.
nodes.playstyle: Be the occasion. Everything near you becomes larger than life; allies fight as the legends of themselves while a single eye remains open.

abilities.name: Larger Than Life
abilities.desc: Any ally observed by anyone — friend, foe, crowd, you — gains 25% to everything; solitude is the only debuff you recognize.

abilities.name: The Roar Without Throats
abilities.desc: Summon the full-stands roar anywhere — crypt, field, empty hall; all crowd-fed powers on your side operate at capacity, always.

abilities.name: Every Eye
abilities.desc: Direct all attention to one ally's next action; it cannot miss, cannot be resisted, and will be retold badly for centuries.

abilities.name: Stage Fright
abilities.desc: Enemies act last while watched, and everything is watching; their finest abilities falter on the biggest night of their lives.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and walk out of your last bout mid-chant; the chant must continue without you. It has not yet stopped.
Attend, in the same hour, every full house in the world, and be felt in all of them.
Leave your name with the crowd on your way out; where you stand now, things do not have names, only audiences.
Grant one nobody, once a generation, the surge that made you; how they spend it is the show, and you no longer choose the ending.

nodes.name: The Better End
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the clean ending, everywhere
nodes.lore: Soldiers have always prayed for it; the prayer now has an address. Chaplains note that some endings arrive complete — instant, painless, at the right moment, witnessed — and that they cluster where they are most deserved. Executioners' guilds keep a feast-day. The dying, uniquely, file no complaints.
nodes.playstyle: Govern the quality of endings. On your field, death comes clean or not at all — and to those you attend, it comes as a courtesy.

abilities.name: One Stroke, Everywhere
abilities.desc: Any mortally wounded creature on the field may be finished by you instantly, from any distance, painlessly; the stroke is already travelling.

abilities.name: Only the Clean Stroke
abilities.desc: On your field, agony fails: torture effects, lingering poisons, and cruel deaths simply do not function. Endings meet a standard.

abilities.name: The Attended End
abilities.desc: When a great foe dies well by your hand, every ally who witnessed it is steeled: immune to fear and despair for the battle.

abilities.name: Below Standard
abilities.desc: Once per day, refuse a death as below standard; the target survives at 10% health. The office reserves the right to decline.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and give ten thousand better ends and not one bad one; the audit is conducted by the dying, and they are strict.
Attend every ending on a battlefield in one night, personally, and leave none of them botched.
Be prayed to by soldiers you will never fight, and answer the only way the office answers: eventually, cleanly, once.
Decline to attend one death — your own — until the work is done. The work is not done.

nodes.name: The Yield
nodes.role: Apotheosis — surrender as natural law
nodes.lore: The old soldiers insist battles once ended a single way. Now there is a moment in every hopeless fight — arms heavier, a knowing — when stopping becomes possible, and men take it. Generals call it a disease of morale. Mothers set a place for it at table. The word has become a proper noun.
nodes.playstyle: Make stopping real. Break the momentum of slaughter, shelter whoever lays arms down, and harvest strength from every life that walks away.

abilities.name: The Offered Moment
abilities.desc: Extend the Yield to the field: every enemy below half resolve may lay down arms, and most discover they want to.

abilities.name: Sanctuary of the Yielded
abilities.desc: Anyone who has yielded cannot be harmed by anyone; the law enforces itself and entertains no exceptions.

abilities.name: Arms Grown Heavy
abilities.desc: Enemies striking the beaten, the fleeing, or the helpless find their weapons suddenly enormous: 50% slower, and ashamed.

abilities.name: Harvest of the Standing
abilities.desc: At battle's end, gain enduring strength for every combatant, either side, who leaves the field alive; the Yield pays in survivors.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and accept the surrender of an army dispatched specifically to kill you — all of it, by name, before dusk.
Teach the word to a war that had none, in a tongue that had to borrow it.
Stand where routs happen and turn them into processions; the difference is whether anyone is trampled, and now no one is.
Refuse the surrender of one thing that offered it falsely, so the law keeps its edge; mercy with no teeth is only weather.

nodes.name: The Tally
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the count that is never zero
nodes.lore: After every slaughter, something counts the living, and the count comes up wrong: one more than the slaughter planned. Clerks of three empires have found the same impossible constant in the survivor rolls and blamed each other. The pit's old joke has hardened into law — something always remains, and remains standing.
nodes.playstyle: Be the remainder made law. While you stand, annihilation is an arithmetic error; you and whoever shelters in your count cannot be reduced to nothing.

abilities.name: Never Zero
abilities.desc: While you fight, your side cannot be wiped out: the last three allies standing take 60% reduced damage, always.

abilities.name: Arithmetic Error
abilities.desc: Each round, the single most lethal blow aimed at your side is subtracted before it lands; the clerks never find it.

abilities.name: Audit the Field
abilities.desc: Know precisely what everything on the field has left — health, stamina, arrows, courage — at all times, to the unit.

abilities.name: Carried Forward
abilities.desc: Your permanent per-bout growth now extends to allies who survive battles at your side; the estate has heirs.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and be the reason a massacre's count comes up wrong in forty provinces; sign nothing, correct nothing.
Survive the age's great slaughter carrying the full count of it, every name, and keep the count where no clerk will balance it.
Vanish from the records while never missing a battle; the constant works best unattributed.
Choose, at the end of something enormous, who the one-more-than-planned will be, and make it stick. This is the whole office, used once.

nodes.name: The Gallery
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the unseen audience of the world
nodes.lore: Duelists in empty halls have begun to feel it: a weight of attention, the sense of an aisle. The Gallery attends everything now — wars, oaths, small kindnesses at bad hours — and its regard has pressure. Somewhere behind the world there is seating, and the seating is never quite empty anymore.
nodes.playstyle: Provide the witness. Nothing on your field is hidden or unjudged; performances double, cowardice is reviewed, and history's bookings are yours.

abilities.name: No Empty Halls
abilities.desc: Everything on the field is witnessed: stealth, invisibility, and concealment fail entirely; every act is performed whether intended or not.

abilities.name: The Booking
abilities.desc: Once per round, defer one enemy's action to later in the program; they are simply not on yet.

abilities.name: Notices
abilities.desc: At each round's end the Gallery reviews: your best-performing ally gains 15% to everything, the worst-reviewed enemy loses the same.

abilities.name: Attendance Taken
abilities.desc: Enemies who flee your field are remembered; in every witnessed fight thereafter they falter, and every fight is witnessed now.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and quit the bill forever; discover, without surprise, that you cannot stop attending.
Sit, unseen, with a swordsman drilling alone at midnight, and let him feel the seat fill; his art was never for no one.
Book history's next great confrontation, attend it, and file the only review that will survive: the outcome.
Keep one seat empty in every house, always the same seat; who it is kept for is the Gallery's single secret.

nodes.name: The Curtain Call
nodes.role: Apotheosis — endings completed, witnessed, bowed
nodes.lore: At the end of every magnificent thing there is now a beat — held, attended — in which the world waits for the bow. Great deaths get their final act; great lives get their exit walked, not dragged. Undertakers report the change without approving of it: endings, lately, have been arriving finished.
nodes.playstyle: Complete endings beautifully. The fallen rise for final acts, exits happen on your timing, and nothing magnificent dies unseen or unfinished.

abilities.name: The Final Act
abilities.desc: Any ally who falls rises for ten unkillable seconds of brilliance before the curtain; many battles have ended inside them.

abilities.name: Transfixed
abilities.desc: Enemies witnessing a final act cannot intervene in it; interruptions are simply not taken.

abilities.name: Called Back for the Bow
abilities.desc: Once per battle, when any witness demands it, every downed ally rises at a third of their health; the demand is binding.

abilities.name: Strike the Set
abilities.desc: Once per day, declare the show over: enemies with no stake left accept the ending and withdraw from the field.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85, die your last attested death, and stay past it; the applause has not ended, and the office does not leave mid-ovation.
Give a dying stranger ten perfect final seconds, unwitnessed by anyone but you, and count yourself sufficient house.
Attend the age's worst ending — the one nobody could finish — and finish it: witnessed, bowed, complete.
Leave your own ending unscheduled, the only booking the office never makes; the curtain waits on you, and can.

nodes.name: The Great Chain
nodes.role: Apotheosis — restraint as world order
nodes.lore: Philosophers teach that creation hangs in order, link within link, each thing held to its station. They mean it as metaphor. Under the world, where the old monsters are kept, the metaphor is load-bearing: everything bound is bound to something, the something runs upward, and the far end is held. Occupied, in fact.
nodes.playstyle: Hold the far end. Bind anything at any scale, keep the world's kept things kept, and permit nothing on your field to exceed its station.

abilities.name: Link Within Link
abilities.desc: Chain every enemy on the field to each other; harm to one staggers all, and formations become arguments.

abilities.name: The Far End
abilities.desc: Reel anything bound — by you, by anyone, ever — to your hand from any distance; the chain runs through you now.

abilities.name: Held Below
abilities.desc: Bind one great foe down among the world's kept things until the battle ends; visiting hours are not observed.

abilities.name: Order of Links
abilities.desc: Nothing on your field may exceed its station: enemies cannot transform, enlarge, ascend, or become more than they arrived.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and take the far end of the chain; feel, arriving all at once, everything on it.
Walk the bottom of the world and tighten what your predecessors left slack, without waking what the slack was comforting.
Refuse to bind one thing that deserved binding, so the office remembers it has a hand and is not a mechanism.
Hold, on the day the oldest kept thing pulls, and be the reason that year has no history.

nodes.name: The Turning Coin
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the undecided, kept undecided
nodes.lore: Somewhere overhead a coin is still turning. Soldiers in hopeless lines report the same signs: a glint, a lightness, the sudden conviction that nothing is settled yet. Prophets find their surest pages hedging. The odds-men have begun paying out on battles arithmetic had closed, and have stopped asking why.
nodes.playstyle: Keep the outcome open. Certainties dissolve on your field, the doomed get their turn, and nothing is decided while the coin turns.

abilities.name: Not Yet Landed
abilities.desc: Nothing on your field may be certain: guaranteed hits, fated deaths, and prophecies all become honest coin flips.

abilities.name: The Doomed Turn
abilities.desc: The most hopeless ally on the field acts twice each round; despair, it turns out, was a scheduling error.

abilities.name: Heads
abilities.desc: Once per battle, call the coin: one impossible thing, declared aloud, succeeds.

abilities.name: Stakes Returned
abilities.desc: Any ally who risks everything and falls gets the stake back: they survive at 1 health, once each per battle.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85, stake the outcome itself — yours, everyone's — and toss; the coin has not landed, which is the office.
Attend every hopeless last stand in one night and leave each one merely possible; possible is enough, and all you deal in.
Pay out, personally, the wagers the arithmetic said were lost; the odds-men will learn not to ask, and you will not tell.
Never let it land. The day the coin comes down, the world is decided, and you have seen the world. Keep it turning.

families.name: Rogue
families.tagline: Fair fights are for the buried.
families.description: Born to alleys and taught by hunger, the Rogue learned that honor is a luxury of the well-fed. Locks open at a touch, lies sit easy on the tongue, and every shadow between two lamps is a door. Whether death arrives in a cup of wine or a city's crown vanishes overnight, somewhere a Rogue was paid — and no one saw a thing.

nodes.name: Rogue
nodes.role: Melee skirmisher — opportunistic strikes and escapes
nodes.lore: Every city breeds them: the quick-fingered children who learn doors before letters and knives before prayers. Most die young or hang younger. The ones who last become Rogues — not by ceremony, but by the quiet arithmetic of surviving one more winter than the trade usually allows.
nodes.playstyle: Strike from angles nobody watches, take what the moment offers, and be gone before the cry goes up. Positioning is everything; standing still is death.

abilities.name: Gutter Footwork
abilities.desc: Moving through enemy spaces provokes no reactions; gain bonus evasion for one round after disengaging.

abilities.name: First Cut
abilities.desc: Attacks against foes unaware of you deal doubled weapon damage.

abilities.name: Nimble Fingers
abilities.desc: Pick a lock, lift a purse, or palm an object as a free action once per turn.

abilities.name: Alley Instinct
abilities.desc: Sense hidden exits, tripwires, and watching eyes within thirty feet.

progressionSteps: Survive a winter in the gutters of a city that does not know your name.
Steal your first meal without waking the dog, the watchman, or your conscience.
Learn the rooftop roads until you can cross the ward blindfolded in rain.
Take a beating meant for a friend, and learn which debts are worth carrying.

nodes.name: Whisperknife
nodes.role: Melee striker — single-target ambush burst
nodes.lore: The guilds mark the difference between a cutpurse and a Whisperknife the way farmers mark the difference between a fox and a wolf. These are rogues who accepted the trade's oldest contract: that some deaths are bought, and the buyer never hears the sale close.
nodes.playstyle: Study the target, choose the hour, land one silent strike that ends the conversation. Patience before violence; the fight you avoid is the one you win.

abilities.name: Hushed Steel
abilities.desc: Kills made from stealth produce no sound and leave you hidden.

abilities.name: Vein Map
abilities.desc: Study a target for one round to learn its weakest point, increasing your next critical strike's damage.

abilities.name: Nightshade Coat
abilities.desc: Coat a blade with a minor toxin that dulls the victim's reflexes for three rounds.

abilities.name: Second Rooftop
abilities.desc: After a killing strike, immediately move half your speed without being tracked.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10, then bring the guild proof of a killing no watchman ever recorded.
Spend seven nights learning one stranger's habits, and never once be seen learning them.
Refuse a contract that smells wrong, and survive what the refusal costs you.
Bury your practice blade with the name you were born under.

nodes.name: Velvet Hand
nodes.role: Utility infiltrator — deception, evasion, acquisition
nodes.lore: Velvet Hands are the ones fences greet by their working names and magistrates by their false ones. They have stopped stealing to eat and started stealing to matter — a signet here, a letter there, until half the ward owes them a favor it cannot name.
nodes.playstyle: Talk your way through the front door and pick your way through the rest. Every guard has a price, every lock a temper, every mark a vanity.

abilities.name: Borrowed Face
abilities.desc: Assemble a convincing disguise in one minute; casual observers cannot penetrate it.

abilities.name: Featherlift
abilities.desc: Take a carried item from a person without triggering alarm, notice, or magical wards of lesser order.

abilities.name: Tumbler's Ear
abilities.desc: Open mundane locks at double speed by hearing the mechanism's flaw through the metal.

abilities.name: Small Debts
abilities.desc: Once per day, call in a favor: a door unbarred, a rumor planted, a witness gone traveling.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10, then sell the same forged deed to two collectors in a single evening.
Enter a guildhouse through the front door under a name you invented that morning.
Empty a strongbox and leave something behind, so the owner doubts the theft for a year.
Learn who actually runs your ward, then do them one favor they never asked for.

nodes.name: Cupbearer
nodes.role: Damage-over-time specialist — poisons and slow ruin
nodes.lore: Cupbearers serve at high tables under honest names, and the great families pretend not to know why certain rivals sicken after certain feasts. Their craft is chemistry and etiquette in equal measure: knowing which vintage hides bitterness, and which lord tastes his wife's cup first.
nodes.playstyle: Kill slowly and from a distance of days. Layer toxins, watch the symptoms bloom, and be provably elsewhere when the physicians finally give up.

abilities.name: Patient Vintage
abilities.desc: Administer a poison that lies dormant for hours before its first symptom shows.

abilities.name: Bitter Pairings
abilities.desc: Combine two toxins in one dose; victims suffer both effects and resist neither.

abilities.name: Physician's Shadow
abilities.desc: Identify any poison, antidote, or dosage by taste, scent, or symptom alone.

abilities.name: The Kind Cup
abilities.desc: Feign administering an antidote to gain a target's trust; the dose deepens the affliction instead.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and grow your own garden of banes, from smuggled seed to steeped extract.
Serve one full season in a great house, and leave with its kitchen keys copied.
Drink a measured dose of your own work each dawn until your body forgives it.
End a man at a feast of two hundred, then stand mourning at his funeral unsuspected.

nodes.name: Anatomist
nodes.role: Precision striker — critical single-target execution
nodes.lore: Anatomists buy corpses the way scholars buy books, and for the same reason. They can name every gate in the body where life enters and leaves, and price the toll of each. Their contracts specify not merely a death, but its exact posture, expression, and hour.
nodes.playstyle: One approach, one strike, one exit. Everything else is preparation: study the body, script the moment, and never improvise unless the improvisation was rehearsed.

abilities.name: Chart of Gates
abilities.desc: Ignore all armor when striking the vital points of a studied target.

abilities.name: Stillwork
abilities.desc: Hold perfectly motionless for hours; detection magic reads you as furniture, not flesh.

abilities.name: Measured Thrust
abilities.desc: Your first strike against an unaware target is always a critical hit.

abilities.name: Clean Table
abilities.desc: Kills leave no blood spray, struggle, or forensic sign; the scene reads as natural.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and map the body's twelve fatal gates, on subjects both dead and living.
Study under a barber-surgeon by day for one year, and let him praise your gentle hands.
Take a contract specifying that the victim smile at death, and deliver it as written.
Stand close enough to touch your mark for an evening, then leave without striking, because the contract said Thursday.

nodes.name: Nightlatch
nodes.role: Stealth infiltrator — mobility and objective seizure
nodes.lore: Nightlatch is a working name passed between second-storey artists of a certain calibre — those who treat locked as an opinion and guarded as a scheduling problem. The insurers of noble vaults keep a private list of everyone suspected of holding the title; the list is itself stolen most years.
nodes.playstyle: Case the target for a week, then move through it like water finding a crack. Fight nothing you can climb past; take only what was named.

abilities.name: Opinion of Locks
abilities.desc: Open any mundane lock by touch; magical locks take one quiet minute.

abilities.name: Cat's Covenant
abilities.desc: Climb sheer surfaces at full speed and fall forty feet without a sound or a bruise.

abilities.name: Weightless Step
abilities.desc: Cross pressure plates, brittle tiles, and alarm strings without triggering them.

abilities.name: The Named Thing
abilities.desc: Concentrate on a described object to sense its bearing within a hundred paces.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and take a named jewel from a vault its maker called perfect.
Spend a night inside a mark's bedchamber and take nothing, to prove appetite obeys you.
Return something you stole years ago, unseen, to a house that has since doubled its guards.
Leave your calling knot on the magistrate's own strongbox, tied from the inside.

nodes.name: Intelligencer
nodes.role: Support controller — secrets, misdirection, leverage
nodes.lore: Intelligencers deal in the only currency that never debases: what people would pay to keep unknown. Their archives are memorized, their informants unaware they inform, and their prices denominated in futures — a vote, a silence, a door left off the latch.
nodes.playstyle: Win fights by knowing which fights are scheduled. Gather secrets, sell misdirection, and enter every room already knowing who inside it is lying.

abilities.name: Ear in the Wall
abilities.desc: Nominate a location you have visited; learn the substance of conversations held there each day.

abilities.name: False Ledger
abilities.desc: Plant a document, rumor, or remembered meeting that survives professional scrutiny.

abilities.name: Read the Room
abilities.desc: Learn each visible creature's strongest current desire and most recent lie.

abilities.name: Denominated in Futures
abilities.desc: Trade a secret to a willing creature for a favor that is magically owed.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 knowing one true secret about every member of the ward council.
Sell the same secret to three buyers, priced by what each feared it meant.
Cultivate an informant for a year who believes, to this day, that you are the informant.
Predict a riot to the hour, and be paid once for the warning and once for the cause.

nodes.name: Hemlock Deacon
nodes.role: Attrition assassin — stacking toxins and denial
nodes.lore: The Deacons of Hemlock keep no temple, but they keep a doctrine: that some lives are questions only a quiet chemistry can answer. Kingdoms retain one the way they retain a headsman — rarely spoken of, precisely paid, and consulted only when law has run out of instruments.
nodes.playstyle: Turn whole rooms, wells, and households into instruments. Your poisons stack across days; the enemy is losing the battle before they know one has begun.

abilities.name: Doctrine of Draughts
abilities.desc: Your toxins ignore purification of a lesser order; only true miracles cleanse them.

abilities.name: Congregation of Symptoms
abilities.desc: Foes poisoned by you spread your affliction to allies they touch.

abilities.name: Clean Departure
abilities.desc: Touch a dying victim to erase every trace of the compound from flesh and record.

abilities.name: Tithe of Breath
abilities.desc: Each foe your poisons fell restores your vigor and quickens your hands for one minute.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40, then wait to be summoned; no one applies to the Hemlock, and it watches longer than you have been alive.
Compound a bane no living apothecary can name, and register its antidote with no one.
Poison a well and cure it by morning, to prove the doctrine is choice, not appetite.
Refuse a crown's gold once, so every crown afterward knows your price is not money.

nodes.name: Heartstiller
nodes.role: Burst executioner — traceless one-strike eliminations
nodes.lore: A Heartstiller's work is diagnosed, never witnessed: hale men who sat down mid-sentence and did not stand again. Physicians call it a failing of the heart, and are correct. The guild lends them out at the price of a warship, and only ever singly.
nodes.playstyle: Erase the distance, land the one touch that matters, and be a rumor before the body cools. Burst without noise; commitment without trace.

abilities.name: Stopped Clock
abilities.desc: A precise strike halts the heart; the victim dies without sound, wound, or spell-scar.

abilities.name: Between Heartbeats
abilities.desc: Move your full speed as a blur that mundane eyes cannot track.

abilities.name: Grave Composure
abilities.desc: Slow your own pulse to feign death or pass wards that detect the living.

abilities.name: Sentence Unfinished
abilities.desc: If your first strike kills, make a second strike against one witness within reach.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and still a bull's heart with two fingers, before witnesses sworn to the guild.
Kill a man in a locked room, and let three courts rule it a natural death.
Slow your own heart until the physicians pronounce you, and hear which colleagues weep.
Decline a contract worth a warship because the mark deserved better; the guild must fear your judgment more than your blade.

nodes.name: The Keyless
nodes.role: Elite infiltrator — total bypass and extraction
nodes.lore: The Keyless take their name literally: initiates surrender every key they own into the order's furnace, a promise that nothing will ever again be opened the easy way. Treasurers speak of them the way sailors speak of weather. Some vaults now hold only decoys, on actuarial advice.
nodes.playstyle: Nothing built keeps you out; the job is choosing which impossibility pays. Ghost through wards, unpick miracles, and vanish carrying the exact weight you came for.

abilities.name: Unbarred
abilities.desc: Once per day, pass a locked door, ward, or seal as if it stood open.

abilities.name: Inventory of Ghosts
abilities.desc: Glance at a room and know every hidden compartment, false panel, and counterfeit within it.

abilities.name: Toll Refused
abilities.desc: Magical traps and alarms fail to register you as a creature at all.

abilities.name: Six-Pocket Exit
abilities.desc: Declare an exit route when a job begins; while on it, nothing slows you below full speed.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40, then rob a sitting Keyless and return the prize with your admission letter inside.
Take a relic from a temple whose god was watching, and leave the god uncertain.
Walk out of the kingdom's inescapable prison twice: once as proof, once as a favor.
Retire an honest locksmith with an anonymous fortune; the order pays its respects to worthy adversaries.

nodes.name: Undercrown
nodes.role: Battlefield manipulator — proxies, favors, command
nodes.lore: Every great city has two governments, and the honest one meets in daylight. An Undercrown holds the other: fences, beggar-lines, watch-sergeants on quiet retainers, dock tallies that round in particular directions. Kings negotiate with them through intermediaries and record the payments as sanitation.
nodes.playstyle: Fight with other people's hands. Spend favors like arrows, turn the enemy's hirelings, and shape every encounter three moves before it starts.

abilities.name: Quiet Retainers
abilities.desc: In any settlement, summon armed assistance within minutes; someone nearby was already yours.

abilities.name: The Rounding Error
abilities.desc: Skim resources from any organization you have infiltrated; its own auditors defend the numbers.

abilities.name: Turned Coat
abilities.desc: Offer a visible enemy hireling a better deal mid-combat; morale decides the rest.

abilities.name: Sanitation
abilities.desc: Erase an event from a city's official memory: records altered, witnesses paid, ballads rewritten.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 holding debts from a magistrate, a dock-guild, and at least one honest priest.
End a gang war with three dinners and no funerals, and let both sides claim the victory.
Be robbed publicly, then have the goods returned with an apology before the story spreads.
Turn a crown tax collector into your most reliable expense.

nodes.name: Wormwood Herald
nodes.role: Terror assassin — poison as public proclamation
nodes.lore: The Heralds of Wormwood call the Hemlock's quiet work wasted: a death no one reads teaches nothing. Their kills happen at high table, mid-toast, unmistakably poison and unprovably theirs. Each carries a signature symptom in place of a seal. Courts that receive one death seldom require a second.
nodes.playstyle: Kill seldom and loudly. One theatrical death, correctly witnessed, wins the sieges, votes, and successions that follow; the fear does the remaining work for you.

abilities.name: The Public Cup
abilities.desc: Poison a vessel before a watching crowd; no witness, mundane or arcane, can name the moment your hand moved.

abilities.name: Signature Symptom
abilities.desc: Your toxins announce your order as they kill; creatures who witness the death fear you and yours for a season.

abilities.name: Bitter Proclamation
abilities.desc: After a witnessed kill, enemies of your patron in that court suffer dread: penalties to morale, command, and appetite.

abilities.name: Parley Dose
abilities.desc: Spare one poisoned victim; they recover wholly and must carry, verbatim, the message you set in their mouth.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40, then kill a man the Hemlock was paid to spare, publicly, and leave both employers alive to argue doctrine.
Devise your signature symptom and teach it to no one; the trade must learn to read it from the dead alone.
End a duke at his own victory feast, before four hundred guests, and let every physician testify to poison and none to you.
Send a warning instead of a dose once, and watch a border war cancel itself; fear, properly aged, outsells hemlock.

nodes.name: Exciseman
nodes.role: Precision controller — surgical, nonlethal subtraction
nodes.lore: Excisemen hold that death is a butcher's answer to a clerk's question. Their contracts name a levy, never a life: the duelist's sword-hand, the witch's voice, the treasurer's memory for numbers. The mark wakes lighter, the balance is settled, and the guild's ledgers record no murder at all.
nodes.playstyle: Fight to subtract, not to slay. Target the limb, sense, or skill that makes the enemy dangerous, take exactly that, and leave the rest breathing.

abilities.name: Levy in Kind
abilities.desc: Declare a faculty before striking; on a critical hit, the target loses it until your contract expires.

abilities.name: Anaesthete's Grace
abilities.desc: Your subtractions cause no pain and no waking; victims sleep through the procedure and heal clean by morning.

abilities.name: The Itemized Man
abilities.desc: Appraise a creature to learn which single capacity, removed, would most diminish it.

abilities.name: Return of Levy
abilities.desc: Restore any faculty you removed; the order's power to give back is why its terms are met.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40, then take a famous swordsman's grip so cleanly he wakes praising the mattress, and duel him honestly a year later.
Serve two years under the Anatomists' chart of gates, then map the forty lesser gates where skills live; publish nothing.
Surrender a levy of your own choosing to a senior Exciseman, so you never price what you have not paid.
Return a levy to a reformed man unasked, and record in the ledger: account closed.

nodes.name: Housefriend
nodes.role: Covert saboteur — insertion, planting, unseen presence
nodes.lore: Country folk blame a hearth-spirit when objects appear where none were left; the trade knows better. Housefriends hold that carrying things out is porterage — any porter can subtract. Mastery is addition: the letter in the dead man's desk, the knife on the sleeping king's pillow, sheathed, as instructed.
nodes.playstyle: Enter anywhere, take nothing. Seed rooms with evidence, gifts, and dread; shape what enemies discover and when. The knife on the pillow wins wars the knife in the chest cannot.

abilities.name: The Sheathed Knife
abilities.desc: Leave a token by a sleeping mark; on waking, they cannot believe themselves safe anywhere for a month.

abilities.name: Settled Dust
abilities.desc: Objects you place acquire the room's dust, wear, and history; investigation dates them as always having been there.

abilities.name: Nobody's Footprints
abilities.desc: While inside another's property you leave no scent, print, or magical residue of entry — only what you choose to leave.

abilities.name: Housewarming
abilities.desc: Spend an unseen hour in a dwelling to learn its household: names, quarrels, hiding places, and who checks the locks.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40, then spend a month's nights in a paranoid spymaster's home, leaving one white pebble weekly, until he confesses publicly to crimes no one suspected.
Place a forged codicil in a sealed strongbox the night before probate, and stand among the mourners while it is read aloud.
Return the Keyless order's admission test in reverse: enter their motherhouse and leave your own letter of refusal on the master's pillow.
Arm a coward: leave a loaded crossbow beside a clerk who witnessed too much, and read in the gazettes what courage you installed.

nodes.name: Tocsin
nodes.role: Disruption controller — weaponized disclosure and panic
nodes.lore: Where the Undercrown hoards leverage to govern quietly, the Tocsins hold that a kept secret only protects the strong. They are the bell no one admits installing: archives cracked open at the useful hour, confessions nailed to church doors, ministries emptied by morning. Cities fear the peal more than the fire.
nodes.playstyle: Gather what the powerful buried and detonate it on schedule. Enemies collapse into scandal, mutiny, and resignation before the first blade clears leather.

abilities.name: Nailed to the Door
abilities.desc: Publish a target's worst secret across a settlement overnight; their allies, retainers, and creditors act on it at dawn.

abilities.name: Dead Man's Bell
abilities.desc: Delay a disclosure to trigger on conditions you set: a signature, a coronation, your own death.

abilities.name: Mutineer's Proof
abilities.desc: Show a hireling documented proof of their employer's betrayal mid-combat; they stand down or turn.

abilities.name: Unsilenced
abilities.desc: Attempts to gag, censor, buy, or magically hush you fail; your words arrive somewhere, even from a cell.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40, then break a conspiracy of thirty with three pages, posted where each conspirator's wife, banker, and bishop would read them first.
Refuse to sell a secret at any price once, loudly, so the trade learns you are not a market.
Empty a ministry without a single death: publish its own ledgers and let the arithmetic do the shouting.
Survive the Undercrown's counteroffer — the last three Tocsins who took it are remembered as reliable, wealthy, and silent.

nodes.name: Mithridate
nodes.role: Mythic plague-blade — inevitable attrition
nodes.lore: Histories record perhaps four Mithridates, and dispute two. They are the poisoners whom poison abandoned: bodies steeped so long in bane that venom greets them as kin. Emperors have kept one imprisoned as a living antidote, and buried food-tasters who claimed the title falsely.
nodes.playstyle: You are immune to affliction and made of it. Wade through your own miasma, let enemies rot standing, and outlast anything that has blood.

abilities.name: A Thousand Draughts
abilities.desc: You are immune to all poisons and diseases; imbibing venom heals you instead.

abilities.name: Blood of the Bane-Eater
abilities.desc: Your blood is a lethal contact toxin; creatures that wound you in melee are poisoned.

abilities.name: Breath of the Garden
abilities.desc: Exhale a lingering miasma that fills a chamber and drifts obedient to your steps.

abilities.name: The Long Answer
abilities.desc: Mark a target; no rest, cure, or prayer removes your toxin until you die or relent.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 having drunk, in measured communion, every bane recorded in the guild's black herbal.
Survive your own funeral: let the trade bury you poisoned, and walk out of the tomb.
Unmake a plague you did not author, so history cannot decide whether to curse you.
Let a king's tasters kneel to you as the antidote of last resort, and refuse the pension.

nodes.name: Hush of Crowns
nodes.role: Mythic executioner — unstoppable single elimination
nodes.lore: Dynasties keep a private word for the Hush, and do not write it down. When succession stalls or a tyrant outlives every honest remedy, the word is spoken once, into a particular dark. No Hush has ever been caught, tried, described, or proven to exist twice.
nodes.playstyle: You are the ending other assassins pray to. Choose a name, cross any distance of guards and wards, and close the sentence history left open.

abilities.name: The Spoken Name
abilities.desc: Mark a named target; you always know their direction, distance, and degree of fear.

abilities.name: No Witness
abilities.desc: Creatures who see you kill forget the seeing; records of the moment fade within a day.

abilities.name: Regicide's Patience
abilities.desc: Keep a sleepless, foodless vigil for seven days; while vigilant, you cannot be surprised or scried.

abilities.name: The Perfect Hour
abilities.desc: Once a season, declare one strike unavoidable: it ignores armor, wards, luck, and prophecy.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 with a ledger of endings no two kingdoms can agree really happened.
End a tyrant that three usurpers, two armies, and one god had failed to reach.
Let the guild that trained you conclude, from the evidence, that you never existed.
Hear your work blamed on plague, treason, and heaven — and correct no one.

nodes.name: Moontaker
nodes.role: Mythic phantom — untouchable objective theft
nodes.lore: One autumn night, in the year the ballads argue about, the moon did not rise, and the pawnshops of seven cities refused all silver. The Moontaker is whoever holds the title's proof: a theft so far beyond dispute that the world simply revised its ledgers.
nodes.playstyle: Steal concepts as easily as coin. Objectives simply come to be in your hand, and guards remember doors that were never built.

abilities.name: The Reflected Moon
abilities.desc: Once per year, steal something abstract: a name, a flag's color, one night's moonrise.

abilities.name: Already Gone
abilities.desc: When detected, retroactively be somewhere else you could plausibly have reached this round.

abilities.name: Every Door Owed
abilities.desc: All doors, gates, and bridges in a city recognize you and open; none remember doing so.

abilities.name: Provenance
abilities.desc: Any object you hold for a full day believes it has always been yours; so do its wards.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 with a collection no vault could hold, because half of it is not things.
Steal the moon's reflection from every still water in a province for one full night.
Take the coronation crown mid-ceremony and return it before the arch-priest finishes the blessing.
Have the insurers of seven cities jointly petition the gods about you, and be declined.

nodes.name: The Rumor
nodes.role: Mythic puppeteer — total unseen orchestration
nodes.lore: Scholars can prove the Rumor only by absences: treaties with a signature space left blank, portraits with one figure painted over, wars that ended for no recorded reason. Whoever holds the rank owns favors from people who have never heard of them, which is the point.
nodes.playstyle: You have no face enemies can learn. Act through cutouts and coincidences; by the time anyone suspects a design, the design has already retired.

abilities.name: Redaction
abilities.desc: Remove yourself from a scene retroactively; all memory, record, and divination of your presence goes blank.

abilities.name: The Standing Favor
abilities.desc: Once per month, anything mortal hands could plausibly have arranged simply has been.

abilities.name: Author of Coincidence
abilities.desc: Script an accident up to a day ahead: a slipped axle, a misdelivered letter, a guard's fever.

abilities.name: Blank Signature
abilities.desc: Contracts, curses, and prophecies cannot bind you; your name-space in them stays empty.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60, then burn every record that you reached any level at all.
End a war with one forged letter, and let two historians duel over which general wrote it.
Own the debts of an emperor who has never heard any of your names.
Be erased so completely that this codex entry is, officially, a printer's error.

nodes.name: Kingsbane
nodes.role: Mythic terror — dread that precedes the dose
nodes.lore: Herbalists list kingsbane as a flower that grows where tyrants are buried; historians list it as a poisoner active across four centuries; both indexes are correct in the ways that matter. When the token arrives — one dried petal, no note — dynasties have abdicated by supper, uneaten.
nodes.playstyle: You rarely poison anyone anymore; the belief that you might is toxin enough. Send petals, empty thrones, and reserve the true dose for those who call the legend a bluff.

abilities.name: One Dried Petal
abilities.desc: Deliver your token to any named ruler regardless of distance or wards; they know its meaning and its sender.

abilities.name: Uneaten Supper
abilities.desc: Every meal in a chosen court reads as poisoned to every test; none of it is, probably.

abilities.name: Where Tyrants Grow
abilities.desc: Learn the crimes of anyone whose death you are considering; the flower does not bloom for the innocent.

abilities.name: The Honest Dose
abilities.desc: Once a season, one victim who dismissed your legend dies of it; no vigilance, taster, or miracle intervenes.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60, then empty a throne with a single dried petal and no poison at all.
Let a botanist prove kingsbane the flower cannot exist, then send him a pressed specimen with your compliments.
Kill one disbelieving emperor thoroughly enough that the next four require no killing.
Attend a symposium convened to determine whether you are a person, a plant, or a policy, and vote.

nodes.name: Clemency
nodes.role: Mythic subtractor — disarming the dangerous alive
nodes.lore: No one Clemency has visited has ever died of the visit, which is why the name is spoken with such fear. Generals wake unable to hold a sword; inquisitors, unable to enjoy cruelty; a conqueror once knelt at his own border, having mislaid the wanting of it. Histories file these as conversions.
nodes.playstyle: End threats by removing what makes them threatening — the hand, the appetite, the nerve. You take nothing away with you; the loss simply stays with them.

abilities.name: The Visit
abilities.desc: Reach any warded, guarded, or hidden target while they sleep; your work wakes no one, including them.

abilities.name: Kinder Arithmetic
abilities.desc: Choose what a defeated enemy loses instead of their life: a skill, a hunger, a hatred, a war.

abilities.name: Nothing Fatal
abilities.desc: Your strikes can no longer kill; in exchange no guard, armor, or oath may forbid them.

abilities.name: Counsel of the Lessened
abilities.desc: Enemies who parley with one of your survivors lose their stomach for the field; whole companies have resigned.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60, then end a war by visiting one man: the side that woke to find its genius for siegecraft gone sued for peace by noon.
Visit a tyrant three nights running, taking one appetite each night, and leave a mild administrator ruling competently by Friday.
Stand trial once, voluntarily, and walk free when no court can name a law against making men gentler.
Refuse to visit someone the guild wants unmade, because what makes them dangerous is also what makes them kind.

nodes.name: The Bequest
nodes.role: Mythic orchestrator — the placed and the found
nodes.lore: Scholars trace certain dynasties to a will no one wrote, a sword no one lost, a foundling no one abandoned. The Bequest is the name given, carefully, to whoever keeps arranging what posterity finds. Three royal houses rest on documents that entered locked archives overnight; all three know better than to check.
nodes.playstyle: Fight tomorrow's battles by furnishing them tonight. Cache weapons where heroes will stumble, plant proofs where judges will look, and let the finders believe in providence.

abilities.name: Left for You
abilities.desc: Objects you place are found only by the finder you name, at the hour you choose, however improbable the path.

abilities.name: Heirloom's Memory
abilities.desc: What you plant acquires generations of provenance: wear, records, and witnesses who honestly remember it.

abilities.name: The Furnished Future
abilities.desc: Once per month, declare you left something useful here weeks ago; it has, in fact, been waiting.

abilities.name: Anonymous Donor
abilities.desc: Nothing you place can be traced to you by craft, court, or divination; the trail ends politely elsewhere.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60, then found a dynasty with a birth certificate, a locket, and twenty years of patience.
Leave the right sword in the right lake for the right orphan, and decline all credit for the age that follows.
Let two archivists catalogue your insertions as genuine for thirty years, then leave both their pensions where they will find them.
Attend the coronation your paperwork caused, as nobody in particular, and leave before the toasts.

nodes.name: The Telling
nodes.role: Mythic discloser — truths that end regimes
nodes.lore: Some centuries end at a battle; the last one ended at a reading. The Telling is what the trade calls the one to whom buried truths travel of their own accord — and the event historians use the word for, when an empire's every secret stood up one morning and testified.
nodes.playstyle: Secrets come to you now; the craft is sequencing. Release one truth and a minister falls; release the docket in order, and the age does.

abilities.name: Pilgrim Secrets
abilities.desc: Buried truths seek you out: each dawn, learn one secret someone within a day's ride would kill to keep.

abilities.name: The Docket
abilities.desc: Schedule up to seven disclosures across a season; each lands with proof no tribunal can dismiss.

abilities.name: No Grave Deep Enough
abilities.desc: Learn any secret that every living keeper has died holding; the dead's paperwork survives them.

abilities.name: The Hushed Bell
abilities.desc: You cannot be made to reveal what you choose to keep; torture, magic, and bargains return empty.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 holding proof against every throne on the continent, and let each learn you hold it, and nothing else.
End an empire with a morning's reading in its own great square, and walk out through a crowd too quiet to stop you.
Keep one perfect secret forever, so the world knows your tellings are choices.
Decline to publish the truth that would have won your own pardon; the peal must never ring for the ringer.

nodes.name: The Theriac
nodes.role: Apotheosis — living cure and living plague
nodes.lore: Apothecaries in every kingdom sell theriac, the universal antidote, and freely admit the shelf stock is imitation. The original is walking. Where a Theriac lingers, plagues sputter and poisoners retire unpaid; when one dies, the office finds a new body, the way a cure finds its way into a cup.
nodes.playstyle: You are the dose the world takes against itself. Walk into afflictions and end them, or into courts and become one; both are the same errand now.

abilities.name: The Original Recipe
abilities.desc: Your touch ends any poison, plague, venom, or blight, natural or divine, in bodies, wells, or kingdoms.

abilities.name: Walking Dose
abilities.desc: Your presence in a region suppresses all disease and toxin for as long as you remain, and a season after.

abilities.name: Communion of Banes
abilities.desc: Every poison that has ever existed is remembered in your blood; distill any of them from a single drop.

abilities.name: The Refused Pension
abilities.desc: Kings who try to own you sicken of the attempt; no crown, chain, or contract holds the cure.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85, then walk unarmed into a plague city no god would enter, and walk out at the head of its survivors.
Let the apothecaries' colleges declare you a substance, taxable by weight, and pay the tax in cures.
Bury the previous Theriac with your own hands, and taste what the office leaves in the cup by the grave.
Be prescribed. Somewhere tonight a physician writes your name against a dying child, and you arrive because the dose must.

nodes.name: The Interregnum
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the ending written into thrones
nodes.lore: Constitutional scholars note that every crown, however absolute, behaves as though subject to review. The Interregnum is the review. No longer a person who ends kings so much as the standing possibility of it, given hands: the pause between reigns has a tenant, and coronation oaths are addressed to it.
nodes.playstyle: You no longer hunt tyrants; tyranny schedules its own appointment with you. Hold the silence between reigns, and end only where every other remedy has failed.

abilities.name: Subject to Review
abilities.desc: Any ruler you judge has, from that moment, a reign with an ending; you always know the shortest path to it.

abilities.name: Rights of Vacancy
abilities.desc: While a throne stands vacant you cannot be barred, watched, or slowed anywhere its writ once ran.

abilities.name: Addressed in Oaths
abilities.desc: Every coronation oath sworn anywhere binds its swearer to you; break it, and you hear.

abilities.name: One Word, Once
