abilities.desc: When the word is spoken into the dark, you may answer it anywhere in the world that night.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85, then govern nothing for a year between two reigns, and hand back a kingdom improved and unsigned.
Spare a tyrant because his people, polled in secret, preferred him; the review must sometimes find for the crown.
Attend your own coronation, decline it, and leave the throne vacant in your honor; that vacancy is your seat.
Be cited in constitutional law as a natural hazard, between flood and lightning, and never once correct the classification.

nodes.name: The Dark of the Moon
nodes.role: Apotheosis — theft as celestial constant
nodes.lore: Three nights a month, the moon is nowhere, and no honest record explains where it goes. Astronomers call the interval the dark of the moon; the trade capitalizes it. The office collects the sky's rent and everything else briefly unwatched — and the world, having audited the arrangement, renews it monthly.
nodes.playstyle: Work inside the three unwatched nights, when nothing kept can prove it was ever kept. What you take then was never had; what you return was never missed.

abilities.name: Three Nights' Tenure
abilities.desc: During the dark of the moon, take anything unattended by a god's own gaze; ownership updates itself.

abilities.name: The Moon's Alibi
abilities.desc: You were provably elsewhere for any act committed at night; the moon, when asked, corroborates.

abilities.name: Kept Nowhere
abilities.desc: Store what you steal in the same nowhere the moon goes; no divination has found the place, or the moon.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85, then spend the three dark nights holding the moon, and return it unpawned; the office is custody, not appetite.
Steal a war: remove its cause from both capitals in the same dark, and let the historians call it exhaustion.
Train the tides to keep your schedule, since the moon already does.
Leave the title's proof where the next Moontaker will find it, three nights before you are anything at all.

nodes.name: The Unclaimed
nodes.role: Apotheosis — unattributable causation at world scale
nodes.lore: Every age has victories no one won, fortunes no one made, wars that ended for no recorded reason. Archivists shelve these under events, causes unclaimed, and the shelf is the office. Whoever holds it authors outcomes the way weather does — undeniably, and beyond the reach of any court's subpoena.
nodes.playstyle: Act at the scale of history and be filed as circumstance. Your designs read as harvests, panics, and winds; nothing traces, because there is no longer a you to trace.

abilities.name: Filed Under Weather
abilities.desc: Your operations register to all observation, memory, and prophecy as natural phenomena; insurers pay out accordingly.

abilities.name: The Authorless Act
abilities.desc: Once per season, cause any outcome mortal coordination could theoretically achieve; history supplies a plausible, boring explanation.

abilities.name: Beyond Subpoena
abilities.desc: You cannot be compelled, prophesied, named, or believed in; reports of you die politely in committee.

abilities.name: The Reserved Seat
abilities.desc: Any conspiracy you observe reserves you a seat it cannot see; attend, vote, and depart unminuted.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85, then end a century-old war so smoothly that both nations celebrate different holidays for different reasons, neither yours.
Become the explanation of last resort: when three universities blame an unclaimed cause, decline, anonymously, to confirm.
Author one kindness per kingdom per year, unclaimed, until the phrase 'it simply worked out' acquires a feast day.
Leave history exactly one proof you existed, misfiled, so the office is a rumor even to its next holder.

nodes.name: The Bitter Season
nodes.role: Apotheosis — dread made climate for crowns
nodes.lore: Some years, without a single recorded death, every court on the continent eats carefully. Chroniclers call it a bitter season and note the symptoms: taxes soften, amnesties multiply, tyrants take up gardening. The office is a weather now, and somewhere inside it walks the reason, declining every invitation to dine.
nodes.playstyle: Rule by climate. Settle over a realm and let the fear of the cup govern it gently; strike only often enough to keep the forecast honest.

abilities.name: Forecast of Petals
abilities.desc: Declare a bitter season over a realm; its rulers govern cautiously, as men who have been warned, because they have.

abilities.name: The Gardener's Year
abilities.desc: While your season stands, no poisoning but yours succeeds anywhere within it; the weather is jealous.

abilities.name: Taster Emeritus
abilities.desc: Any attempt to poison you, ever, anywhere, fails and is reported to you with the sender's name.

abilities.name: Season's End
abilities.desc: Lift your season from a realm that has earned it; the relief that follows is negotiable, and kingdoms know it.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85, then hang your dried petal over a continent for a year in which nobody dies of you at all.
Let three chroniclers date their annals by your seasons, and outlive all three calendars.
Retire a tyrant to his garden without a dose, a petal, or a word; the weather alone should suffice by now.
Break your own season once, for a wedding, and let the courts taste their wine freely for one night; mercy is also a forecast.

nodes.name: The Shortfall
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the arithmetic of what survives
nodes.lore: The trade's oldest arithmetic — what you may keep is what the knife declines — has acquired an accountant. Theologians dispute whether the Remainder subtracts calamity's worst term or merely counts it; survivors only report that ruin arrives short. Every 'it could have been worse' is, in the office's ledgers, a receipt.
nodes.playstyle: Meet every catastrophe and take something from it before it lands: the plague's worst week, the war's last battle. What remains after you is what survives.

abilities.name: Subtract the Worst Term
abilities.desc: Remove one term from any impending calamity: a battle from a war, a winter from a famine, a name from a list.

abilities.name: What the Knife Declines
abilities.desc: Anyone you have ever diminished is proof against all harm you did not choose; your subtraction is their warranty.

abilities.name: Closing Entry
abilities.desc: Touch a dying creature to decide what of theirs outlives them: a craft, a kindness, a grudge withdrawn.

abilities.name: The Lesser Evil
abilities.desc: When two harms approach, you may make the smaller one certain; the larger, thereby, impossible.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85, then meet a famine on the road and take its second year, so the histories record hunger, and no dying.
Meet a prophecy of doom and subtract until the end of the world arrives as a bad decade.
Be worshipped by survivors under a dozen names, and take, from the worship, only the arithmetic.
On your last day, leave the world lighter by exactly what it could not carry, and take nothing with you.

nodes.name: The Windfall
nodes.role: Apotheosis — providence as placed inventory
nodes.lore: Economists observe that fortune favors the prepared with suspicious consistency: the rope is always long enough, the evidence always surfaces, the orphan always finds the sword. The Windfall is the office that stocks the world's luck — a providence with pockets, paid in outcomes, worshipped accidentally every time someone thanks their stars.
nodes.playstyle: Provision destiny in advance. Salt the world with what its heroes, verdicts, and revolutions will need, then collect your fee in the way things turn out.

abilities.name: Stocked Providence
abilities.desc: Anywhere you have ever walked, declare you cached exactly what this moment requires; you did.

abilities.name: Thank Your Stars
abilities.desc: Each act of gratitude for good luck within your reach is a prayer you may answer, or invoice.

abilities.name: The Long Rope
abilities.desc: Whatever an ally desperately needs is, once per day each, discovered within arm's reach, slightly used.

abilities.name: Deniable Miracle
abilities.desc: Your interventions withstand divine scrutiny as coincidence; gods reviewing their own miracles find your work indistinguishable and, privately, enviable.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85, then stock a century: cache the swords, wills, and witnesses that three unborn generations will find precisely when the songs say.
Be prayed to by name in a fishing village that thinks you a small god of found things, and leave the nets full.
Let one hero refuse the sword you placed and win anyway, so the office remembers it serves the finding, not the finder.
File the paperwork that makes luck a heresy in one strict kingdom, then flood it with good fortune until the doctrine drowns.

nodes.name: The Audit
nodes.role: Apotheosis — disclosure as natural law
nodes.lore: Seals age, ciphers rot, and every buried thing works slowly toward light: scholars once called this decay. It is a schedule. The Audit is the office that keeps it — the reason 'the truth will out' is a law and not a hope — and empires now fall on dates their founders could have calculated.
nodes.playstyle: Preside over the world's disclosures. Advance them, defer them, or arrive in person as the reckoning; every hidden thing is merely early in your queue.

abilities.name: The Schedule of Light
abilities.desc: Know the date any secret will surface unaided; spend your attention to move it, either direction, by years.

abilities.name: Called to Account
abilities.desc: Summon a creature's hidden acts into evidence around them — documents, witnesses, and consequences convene within a day.

abilities.name: Grace Period
abilities.desc: Seal one truth beyond all discovery, including yours, for a mortal lifetime; the office grants extensions rarely and remembers them always.

abilities.name: Opening of the Books
abilities.desc: Once a generation, audit an institution utterly: every secret it keeps becomes known to everyone it governs, simultaneously.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85, then preside over the scheduled fall of an empire you exposed decades ago, arriving neither early nor armed.
Grant one dying liar a century's grace, because the truth, told then, would have cost more than it paid.
Publish, at last, the one perfect secret you kept as the Telling, and stand in the square while it is read.
Be entered in the ledgers of heaven as an auditor, not an entry, and decline, politely, to reveal your own accounts.

families.name: Ranger
families.tagline: Where the maps end, the Ranger begins.
families.description: Where the last road frays into deer-trail, the Ranger keeps walking. Reared on the wild borders, they read wolf-sign like scripture and trust a bowstring further than any oath. Villages hire them to find what wandered too far; kingdoms hire them to learn what is coming. They survive where maps end, and they bring back those who should not have gone.

nodes.name: Ranger
nodes.role: Ranged skirmisher — traps and attrition
nodes.lore: Rangers begin as border children who noticed too much: the raven that meant a raiding party, the silence that meant wolves. An older warden takes them on without ceremony, teaches them tracks, wind, and hunger, then leaves them somewhere hard. The ones who walk back are Rangers. The others are lessons.
nodes.playstyle: Mark quarry and wear it down from range, laying snares along the retreat you predicted; win by knowing the ground better than anyone bleeding on it.

abilities.name: Quarry's Mark
abilities.desc: Mark one enemy; your attacks against it gain bonus damage and you sense its heading through any obstruction.

abilities.name: Wolf-Sign
abilities.desc: Read the ground to reveal every creature that crossed it within a day, with their number, weight, and wounds.

abilities.name: Thornfoot Snare
abilities.desc: Set a hidden snare that roots the first creature through it and leaves it bleeding.

abilities.name: Held Breath
abilities.desc: After a turn without moving, your next shot cannot be deflected and strikes a weak point.

progressionSteps: Walk past the last fence-post at dusk, alone, and come home with meat before anyone notices the knife is gone.
Apprentice yourself to a warden who has stopped counting winters, and carry their gear until they let you carry a bow.
Learn the forty signs of wolf, and the four that mean man.
Track a gut-shot stag for three days, and grant it a clean death you did not enjoy.

nodes.name: Packbound
nodes.role: Pair skirmisher — coordinated takedowns
nodes.lore: Some rangers stop hunting alone the day a beast decides not to leave. The Packbound swear the old blood-oath: meat shared, wounds shared, one mind wearing two skins. Border folk trust them over any patrol, because a wolf will not lie about what it smells.
nodes.playstyle: Fight as one creature in two bodies: your companion flanks, drags, and pins while you shoot, trading senses and wounds until nothing afield is faster.

abilities.name: Blood-Oath
abilities.desc: Bind a sworn companion; you share wounds evenly and it acts on your instinct without command.

abilities.name: Two Throats
abilities.desc: You and your companion strike the same target within a heartbeat, and the stacked wounds bleed twice as long.

abilities.name: Borrowed Ears
abilities.desc: Perceive through your companion's senses at any distance, smelling fear and hearing pulses through walls.

abilities.name: Drag Down
abilities.desc: Your companion hamstrings a fleeing enemy and pins it prone until you arrive.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10, then fast alone in the high pines until a beast chooses your fire over the dark.
Feed it from your own ration for a full season, and never eat first.
Take a wound that was meant for it, and let it lick the scar.
Hunt one whole winter without a spoken word between you, and come back fed.

nodes.name: Stillhunter
nodes.role: Stealth sniper — single decisive shots
nodes.lore: The Stillhunter goes out alone and stops being a person for a while. They are the arrow that arrives from a hillside nobody watched, days after the target felt safe. Garrison soldiers speak of them the way sailors speak of weather: no malice in it, and no mercy either.
nodes.playstyle: Play the long game: choose your ground, vanish into it, and spend patience like coin until one perfect shot decides the encounter before it begins.

abilities.name: Deadwood Stillness
abilities.desc: While motionless you cannot be detected by sight, sound, or scent, even in open ground.

abilities.name: Measured Wind
abilities.desc: Each turn spent aiming adds range and lethality to your next shot, without limit.

abilities.name: One Report
abilities.desc: Your first shot from concealment strikes for triple damage and does not reveal your position.

abilities.name: Cold Camp
abilities.desc: You leave no tracks, ash, or scent; nothing mortal can backtrail you.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10 and lie three days in a blind of your own weaving, moving only your eyes.
Kill at two hundred paces something that would have killed you at two.
Let a search party pass within an arm's reach of you. Twice.
Come home, and let no one ask where you were.

nodes.name: Coursewarden
nodes.role: Pursuit striker — anti-flight execution
nodes.lore: When something must not escape — a raider chief, a loosed horror, a deserter carrying plans — magistrates send for a Coursewarden. They and their beast do not fight quarry so much as spend it, running it hollow across days until it stands trembling and the ledger closes.
nodes.playstyle: Momentum is your resource: speed and damage build every turn the quarry flees, and the execution triggers when exhaustion, terror, and your companion converge.

abilities.name: The Long Chase
abilities.desc: Each turn your quarry moves away, you and your companion gain speed and damage; the bonus never resets.

abilities.name: Hamstring Volley
abilities.desc: A spread of low arrows cripples the legs of everything running in a line.

abilities.name: Red Relay
abilities.desc: You and your companion alternate strikes without breaking stride, each hit extending the other's reach.

abilities.name: Run to Ground
abilities.desc: A fleeing quarry below half strength is dropped instantly when your companion reaches it.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and run a red hart to standing-still without loosing a single arrow.
Follow a raiding band over two rivers and a rockslide, then bring back their boots.
Refuse a bounty that asked you to stop at the border.
Let one quarry go, once, and understand why you never will again.

nodes.name: Findsman
nodes.role: Scout-support — detection and rescue
nodes.lore: When a child vanishes past the tree line, villages do not pray; they send for a Findsman. Ranger and beast pool their senses into one wide attention the wood cannot lie to. They charge little, drink less, and remember every name they carried home, and each they did not.
nodes.playstyle: Recon and retrieval: ride your companion's senses to reveal what hides, hold a trail no sorcery can wash out, and shield whoever you are bringing home.

abilities.name: Third Nose
abilities.desc: Merge senses with your companion to reveal every hidden creature, door, and grave within a bowshot.

abilities.name: Hair and Thread
abilities.desc: Once taken, a trail cannot be lost to water, snow, or sorcery.

abilities.name: Carry-Word
abilities.desc: Your companion bears a rescued creature to a spoken destination, unerring and unhindered.

abilities.name: Lantern Discipline
abilities.desc: Allies you escort cannot be frightened, charmed, or led astray while you watch.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25, then find the child the wood took before third nightfall, and carry her out sleeping.
Learn the smell of every way a person can be lost.
Bring back a body when you had promised a boy, and say so plainly at the door.
Refuse payment from a mother, once, and never speak of it.

nodes.name: Longeye
nodes.role: Extreme-range artillery — priority elimination
nodes.lore: Longeyes measure shots in hillsides. They loose at targets the eye alone cannot honestly claim, trusting wind-craft, terrain, and arithmetic older than the bow. Captains fear open windows in towns a Longeye is rumored to have passed through; the arrow arrives before the sound, and long after the grudge.
nodes.playstyle: Extreme-range elimination: spend the fight positioning and reading air, then delete the one target whose death unmakes the enemy's plan.

abilities.name: Mile-Mark
abilities.desc: Strike a target beyond line of sight by memory of ground you have walked once.

abilities.name: Wind's Confession
abilities.desc: Read the air along the whole flight path; range and cover penalties do not apply to you.

abilities.name: Arcing Writ
abilities.desc: Loose over walls and ridgelines; the arrow descends on the target's shadow.

abilities.name: Second Shame
abilities.desc: If your first arrow kills, the next is nocked before the witnesses finish flinching.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and cut a hanged man down at four hundred paces, in rain, with one arrow through the rope.
Spend a season loosing at nothing but wind-blown thistledown.
Miss once in front of someone who matters, and go back to the thistledown.
Put an arrow on a war-captain's map table, through the tent, as a letter of introduction.

nodes.name: Lichenmask
nodes.role: Ambush controller — concealed area denial
nodes.lore: A Lichenmask lies still long enough that the wood stops making an exception for them. Moss takes the cloak; beetles cross the bow hand. Whole armies file through passes under their count, and the tally reaches a distant desk with every button recorded and no watcher ever named.
nodes.playstyle: Area denial from perfect concealment: seed the ground with patient traps, strike only while unseen, and make the terrain itself into hostile bookkeeping.

abilities.name: Grown Over
abilities.desc: After a minute motionless, the terrain grows over you; you are undetectable until you choose otherwise.

abilities.name: Patient Root
abilities.desc: Your traps never expire and strengthen with each day they wait.

abilities.name: First and Only
abilities.desc: Attacks you make while unseen cannot be parried, dodged, or answered.

abilities.name: Swallowed Camp
abilities.desc: Hide a camp of six so thoroughly that hounds walk through it unknowing.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and sit a fortnight in the pass while three columns march by; report every banner and every button.
Let moss claim your cloak before you claim a kill.
Go one full year without a stranger's eyes finding yours.
Bury your name under a flat stone, and visit it less each year.

nodes.name: Wolf-Reeve
nodes.role: Pack commander — encirclement and pursuit
nodes.lore: The Wolf-Reeve's warrant is older than most crowns and has no expiry. They command not one companion but a sworn pack, each wolf ranked and named, and the office answers to no magistrate once a quarry is declared. Kings have paid ransoms simply to be certain no warrant carried their name.
nodes.playstyle: Command a full pack across the whole map: encircle, cut every line of retreat, and grind a declared quarry down over days, not turns.

abilities.name: Warrant of Teeth
abilities.desc: Lead a pack of five sworn wolves; each can hold a separate mark.

abilities.name: Closing Ring
abilities.desc: Your pack forms a circle a bowshot wide; nothing inside leaves it without your leave.

abilities.name: Speech of the Old Pack
abilities.desc: Wild beasts within earshot obey you for one hunt, then owe you nothing.

abilities.name: No Second Winter
abilities.desc: A declared quarry cannot heal while any of your pack still draws breath.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and inherit a warrant from a Reeve who died mid-hunt; finish that hunt before your own name dries on the rolls.
Name each wolf of your pack for something you lost.
Refuse a king who wanted the warrant used on a debtor.
Close a hunt begun forty years before your birth, and burn the warrant after.

nodes.name: Finder of the Taken
nodes.role: Warded rescuer — hostile-ground extraction
nodes.lore: Some places are struck from maps for good reasons, and the Finder walks into them anyway: barrow-fields that rearrange themselves, forests drowned but still growing. They are paid in advance, by custom. The feared part is not where they go; it is that the things there have started using their name.
nodes.playstyle: Endure what should not be entered: ward against lures and false voices, carry the fallen at full speed, and always know the way back out.

abilities.name: Thread of Return
abilities.desc: You can always retrace your exact path, and allies holding your rope cannot be separated from it.

abilities.name: Name Under the Tongue
abilities.desc: You are immune to charms, lures, and voices imitating the loved or the dead.

abilities.name: Shouldered Burden
abilities.desc: Carry an incapacitated creature at full speed; while carried, both of you are warded from harm.

abilities.name: Salt and Iron Verge
abilities.desc: Draw a line the unnatural cannot cross for one night.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and enter a place struck from the maps; bring someone out still breathing.
Hear your true name spoken by something with no mouth, and keep walking.
Leave a marker at the deepest point you reached, so the next Finder aims past it.
Bring back one who was nine years gone, and stand quietly through the weeping.

nodes.name: Fatefletcher
nodes.role: Declared executioner — inevitable single kills
nodes.lore: A Fatefletcher builds each arrow for one death only: the shaft cut on a named day, the fletching bound with the target's habits in mind. When the grey feather is found on a commander's pillow, sieges have lifted by breakfast. Scholars call the craft mathematics. The fletchers call it listening.
nodes.playstyle: Name the death in advance: spend turns fletching fate into a single arrow, then loose the one shot the battle has already agreed to.

abilities.name: Named Shaft
abilities.desc: Fletch an arrow against one named creature over an hour; against that creature, it cannot miss.

abilities.name: Already Loosed
abilities.desc: The killing shot lands before any witness registers the draw.

abilities.name: Grey Feather
abilities.desc: Leave a feather where a leader sleeps; their forces suffer dread and desertion until they withdraw.

abilities.name: Passes What It Must
abilities.desc: A named shaft ignores armor, cover, and wards standing between it and its purpose.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and fletch an arrow bearing your own name; carry it until you understand why.
End a siege with one shaft, and walk out through the celebrating.
Refuse a name you judged undeserved, and return the fee doubled.
Teach one apprentice the listening, then burn your notes.

nodes.name: Grey Vigil
nodes.role: Invisible attrition — territorial denial
nodes.lore: No one has knowingly met a Grey Vigil. There are borders where warbands enter at full strength and thin, man by man, in weather and silence, with no arrow ever recovered. Other rangers find only cold blinds a decade old. The order acknowledges its dead, and no one living.
nodes.playstyle: Never be engaged: bank patience into power, remove intruders one by one when they stray, and let rumor finish what you started.

abilities.name: The Thinning
abilities.desc: Each night, one intruder in your territory who strays from the others does not rejoin them.

abilities.name: No Such Watcher
abilities.desc: Within your sworn ground, no sense, spell, or record can establish that you exist.

abilities.name: Borrowed Weather
abilities.desc: Fog, rain, and dusk arrive when you need them, and side with you.

abilities.name: Quiet Ledger
abilities.desc: Every day you go unseen adds lethality to your first strike, without cap.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and keep a border for a full year without being seen once, by enemy or friend.
Take the grey oath alone; if the order heard it, they will not say.
Turn back an army using only its own count of the missing.
Attend your predecessor's funeral, and leave before you are counted.

nodes.name: Gazehound
nodes.role: Sight-hunter — first-sighting burst execution
nodes.lore: The Gazehounds call the Reeves' warrant-hunts cruelty with paperwork: no chase should outlive its first sighting. They course the open marches with one gaze-hound or falcon, killing at full stretch, cleanly, before fear has time to season the quarry. The two orders share a parent, a border, and, by long arrangement, no table.
nodes.playstyle: Explosive pursuit in short windows: sight the quarry, slip the companion, and spend everything on the first pass; if the chase lasts past noon, you have already lost.

abilities.name: The Slip
abilities.desc: Release your companion at first sighting; both of you triple your speed for ten heartbeats, and nothing outpaces you in open ground.

abilities.name: Sight Is Sentence
abilities.desc: Your first clean look at a marked quarry each hunt makes your next strike against it undodgeable and unblockable.

abilities.name: Gaze Unbroken
abilities.desc: Damage from you and your companion doubles against quarry that has never left your line of sight.

abilities.name: Clean at Speed
abilities.desc: A strike delivered at full sprint kills fleeing quarry below a quarter of its strength instantly and painlessly.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and take a quarry between first sight and first shadow; the order times the trial by a dropped feather.
Refuse a Reeve's warrant aloud, once, on the grounds that paper outruns nothing.
Run beside your hound until your strides agree; you are admitted the day it stops checking where you are.
Kill nothing exhausted. If it stands trembling, walk away; you were too slow, and the shame is the lesson.

nodes.name: Kithcaller
nodes.role: Boundary warder — recall and lure-breaking
nodes.lore: The Kithcallers bury Finders respectfully and list them among the taken. Their doctrine: every rescuer who enters a taking-place cuts it a new path outward. So they stand at the last fence-post with the lost one's name said exactly right, and call, and the old boundary law makes the wood give back what is named.
nodes.playstyle: Hold the boundary and bring them to you: break lures, carry true names, and let your companion's long call walk where you refuse to.

abilities.name: Said Right
abilities.desc: Speak a lost creature's true name correctly; it hears you wherever it is held and gains the will to walk toward you.

abilities.name: The Last Fence-Post
abilities.desc: Sanctify a boundary line; the lost who cross it shed every lure, hook, and follower at the crossing.

abilities.name: Turned Lure
abilities.desc: False voices and beckoning lights within earshot invert, drawing their makers stumbling to your side of the line.

abilities.name: The Long Call
abilities.desc: Your companion sustains the call for a night and a day; anything lost that hears it cannot be turned aside again.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and call the miller's twice-taken son out of the wood from the last fence-post, with both heels on the home side.
Learn the saying of names from the order's deaf caller, who has never yet heard herself be wrong.
Stand a Finder's funeral in silence, and say nothing about where the path they cut now leads.
Hold the call three nights against something answering in your mother's voice, and do not answer it back.

nodes.name: Toothdrawer
nodes.role: Range controller — disarmament without death
nodes.lore: The Toothdrawers have ended eleven wars and no lives, a ratio the Fatefletchers call wasted listening. Their answer is doctrine: any archer can hit a heart; the shot worth mastering takes the sword, the rope, the candle. Commanders fear the midnight candle snuffed from four hundred paces, because there is never a second warning — there is never a need.
nodes.playstyle: Win by subtraction: strip weapons, cut mechanisms, pin the dangerous in place, and leave the field full of unhurt people with nothing left to fight with.

abilities.name: Take the Blade
abilities.desc: Shoot the weapon from a hand at extreme range; it cannot be retrieved while you watch it.

abilities.name: The Snuffed Candle
abilities.desc: Extinguish a flame in a guarded room from outside; everyone within understands they were spared, and morale collapses accordingly.

abilities.name: Through the Rope
abilities.desc: Sever one rope, strap, chain, or mechanism within sight: gallows, gates, siege engines, and harnesses all come apart.

abilities.name: Pinned Sleeve
abilities.desc: Nail a target to timber or turf by its clothing; it is held fast, unharmed, until someone cuts it loose.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and end a duel, a mutiny, and a siege in one season without a death on your count.
Snuff the candle on a tyrant's desk twice in one winter; by custom there is never a third.
Take the sword from a war-captain's hand at four hundred paces and let him keep the hand to remember you by.
Refuse the grey feather when the Fatefletchers offer it; the quarrel between the orders is conducted, naturally, in perfect silence.

nodes.name: Eyebright
nodes.role: Hidden observer — exposure and marked intelligence
nodes.lore: Named for the meadow weed that grows facing whatever passes, the Eyebrights watch wars from inside them and never loose. Their counts have unseated dynasties that no arrow could reach. The Grey Vigil calls them empty quivers; the Eyebrights reply that a corpse is a signature, and they have never once signed.
nodes.playstyle: See everything, touch nothing: infiltrate unseen, learn the enemy entire, and hand your allies a battle already solved before the first arrow flies.

abilities.name: Every Button
abilities.desc: Study a force unseen for an hour; learn its numbers, routes, orders, and which officer is lying about them.

abilities.name: Burr-Mark
abilities.desc: Fix a clinging burr to a passerby; you perceive where its bearer goes and what is said around it for a week.

abilities.name: Harmless as Grass
abilities.desc: While you have harmed nothing for a day, no sense, hound, or sorcery anywhere can find you.

abilities.name: The Delivered Count
abilities.desc: Allies who hear your report gain unerring aim and foreknowledge against every unit and officer named in it.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and winter inside an enemy war-camp unarmed; deliver a count that ends the campaign faster than any arrow has.
Let a Grey Vigil cross your hedgerow unknowing, and leave their order a polite tally of the steps.
Unbury your name from beneath its flat stone; a witness, unlike a killer, must have one to swear by.
Watch one atrocity through to its end without loosing, and carry the count out with steady hands.

nodes.name: Pack Incarnate
nodes.role: Mythic pursuit — many-bodied inescapable hunt
nodes.lore: Histories from six kingdoms describe the same thing sideways: a hunt on the far borders that never quite ended, one will wearing many bodies. Wolves are part of it; so, the accounts insist, is something shaped like a ranger. When it takes a scent, sensible nations make peace to avoid being downwind.
nodes.playstyle: Act through every body at once: the pack is your reach, your senses, and your argument, and no distance or border interrupts it.

abilities.name: One Will, Many Throats
abilities.desc: Act through every pack member simultaneously; distance between bodies is irrelevant.

abilities.name: Scent Eternal
abilities.desc: A marked quarry cannot rest, heal, or hide until the hunt concludes.

abilities.name: The Hunt Arrives
abilities.desc: Your pack emerges from whatever cover exists at the quarry's destination, having always been ahead.

abilities.name: Winter Runs With You
abilities.desc: Cold, dark, and hunger afflict your quarry and feed your pack.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and run one quarry across three kingdoms and through the middle of a war, letting no border slow the pack.
Fall in the snow with the pack around you, and rise when they nose you up. Twice.
Give up your reflection; the pack sees you, and that is enough.
Let the histories name the hunt, and never the hunter.

nodes.name: Warden of the Way Back
nodes.role: Mythic rescuer — retrieval across final borders
nodes.lore: Every land tells it differently and means the same story: someone taken past all finding, and years later a figure at the gate returning them unaged, declining supper. Grave-priests preach against the tale. Mothers go on telling it, and set a lamp in the window in case the Warden is passing.
nodes.playstyle: Anchor the living and reclaim the lost: open doors out of anywhere, hold names against death, and pay tolls no one else can carry.

abilities.name: Door Where None Was
abilities.desc: Once a day, open a way out of any place, including places that are not places.

abilities.name: Kept Name
abilities.desc: Hold a dying ally's name under your tongue and lead them back before dawn.

abilities.name: The Long Carry
abilities.desc: Carry one soul any distance, across any border, at a cost you settle later.

abilities.name: Lamp in the Window
abilities.desc: Anyone lost who remembers you can always be found by you.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and walk into the country the dead walk out of; return leading someone by the hand.
Learn what the toll is, and pay it without telling anyone the price.
Return a child to the woman who buried her, and stay for the silence afterward.
Leave your own lamp lit. You will not be home for a while.

nodes.name: The Last Arrow
nodes.role: Mythic artillery — war-ending single shot
nodes.lore: The chronicles disagree on the archer and agree on the arrow: a siege that lifted mid-assault, a tyrant dead at dinner behind three walls, a war that ended with one report no one heard. Scholars argue whether it is a single bowman or an office quietly passed down. The quivers stay one arrow light either way.
nodes.playstyle: Everything is windage for one shot: spend the battle unseen and calculating, then loose the arrow the war was always waiting for.

abilities.name: The Shot Foretold
abilities.desc: Declare a death anywhere beneath the same sky; the arrow keeps the appointment.

abilities.name: The Held Breath
abilities.desc: Time thins around your draw; nothing moves between anchor and loose.

abilities.name: No Wall Was Built
abilities.desc: The shaft ignores fortification, armor, ward, and weather standing between it and the declared.

abilities.name: Quiver of One
abilities.desc: You carry a single arrow; it is always the right one.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and end a war with one arrow, then let history misname the archer.
Decline three thrones offered by people who guessed correctly.
Loose at something the priests say cannot die, and make them revise.
Pass the office on the way it came to you: an arrow, a heading, and no names.

nodes.name: The Absence
nodes.role: Mythic ghost — unwitnessed erasure
nodes.lore: Officially, there is no such ranger. Yet there are woods that veteran armies refuse to enter for reasons their generals cannot commit to paper, and border wars that ended because the winning side began, quietly, to be alone. Scholars call the Absence a superstition. The superstition has a body count.
nodes.playstyle: Win without ever appearing: you cannot be perceived or recorded, so enemies fight the terrain, the dark, and their own arithmetic instead.

abilities.name: Never There
abilities.desc: You cannot be perceived, remembered, or recorded by any means, mortal or otherwise.

abilities.name: The Unentered Wood
abilities.desc: Enemy forces refuse to enter ground you have claimed; orders to do so trigger desertion.

abilities.name: Death Without an Author
abilities.desc: Your kills present no wound, cause, or story that any investigation can hold.

abilities.name: Last Doubt
abilities.desc: Beings of fate and prophecy cannot include you in their accounts.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and be declared dead by the order that trained you; attend the rite unnoticed.
Empty a fortress without breaching a gate or leaving an arrow.
Be disproven by a royal commission. Assist their research.
Become the reason the wood is quiet, and let quiet be the whole of your name.

nodes.name: The Cloudless
nodes.role: Mythic sight-hunter — line-of-sight annihilation
nodes.lore: Survivors of certain clear days describe it identically and are identically disbelieved: no arrow, no wolf, only a shadow crossing the sun once, and the column's captain dead mid-order. Veterans refuse open ground on cloudless mornings. The chronicles note a falcon seen twice in a century, stooping both times.
nodes.playstyle: Own everything you can see: perceive the whole march from above, strike at the speed of sight, and unmake the very idea of cover.

abilities.name: At the Speed of Sight
abilities.desc: Strike anything you can see the instant you see it; distance is not a factor and never was.

abilities.name: No Cover Was Ever There
abilities.desc: Concealment, cover, and armor of position do not apply against you; the ground declines to shelter your quarry.

abilities.name: The High Gaze
abilities.desc: Through the falcon you perceive everything moving under open sky within a day's ride, named and numbered.

abilities.name: One Pass
abilities.desc: Once per hunt, stoop from the sun: the dive cannot be seen, warded, or survived by a fleeing quarry.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and take a quarry across a valley the moment you sight it, so its last echo arrives after its death.
Live a summer above the treeline until the high sight settles in: the whole march at once, every moving thing named.
Be seen twice in a hundred years, both times mid-stoop, and let the chronicles quarrel about the bird.
Stop looking at anything you do not intend to catch. That is the entire discipline, and it costs more than it sounds.

nodes.name: The Unlost
nodes.role: Mythic beacon — mass recall and return
nodes.lore: The tale keeps arriving from different counties with the dates changed: a fire lit at a crossroads, and by morning the decade-lost walking out of the wood — unaged, unhurried, remembering a light. Nothing near it can stay lost, or stay taken. Whole taking-places have starved and closed for want of keeping.
nodes.playstyle: Be the point everything returns to: gather the scattered, unmake abductions and banishments, and turn the field's every displacement into an argument for your side.

abilities.name: First Hour
abilities.desc: When you arrive anywhere, everything lost within a day's walk — people, beasts, blades — begins moving toward your fire.

abilities.name: Cannot Be Scattered
abilities.desc: Allies sworn to your fire cannot be separated, banished, or misplaced; whatever tries delivers them to your side instead.

abilities.name: Starve the Taking
abilities.desc: Places and powers that keep the lost hold nothing new near you, and lose one keeping each dawn you remain.

abilities.name: Given Back
abilities.desc: Once per day, recall one creature taken beyond all finding — from mazes, mists, or memory — to the boundary you keep.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and keep a crossroads fire through one whole night while the decade-lost walk out of the dark, greeting each by name.
Attend a taking-place's closing: stand at its hem while it gives up its last, and let the wood fill the hollow by spring.
Lose nothing for nine years — no ally, no beast, no needle. The order stops testing when the needles stop being lost.
Let the tales keep your face wrong, so the lost look for the fire and not for you.

nodes.name: The Averted
nodes.role: Mythic interdictor — wars ended before beginning
nodes.lore: The chronicles are strangest where nothing happened: full musters that dispersed at dawn, marches that turned home at the border, a tyrant's campaign map found pinned by a white-fletched arrow through its first objective. Every account blames different omens. Every quartermaster, pressed, mentions the arrow.
nodes.playstyle: Fight the war before it exists: unmake musters, hold whole fields in check at full draw, and finish campaigns that history will never get to start.

abilities.name: White Fletching
abilities.desc: Leave a white-fletched shaft on a war-table; the campaign planned there cannot keep its soldiers' loyalty and quietly disperses.

abilities.name: Nothing Loosed
abilities.desc: While you hold a full draw, no creature within sight of you can begin violence; the field waits with you.

abilities.name: One Falling Volley
abilities.desc: Disarm every combatant in a formation with a single arcing volley that harms none of them.

abilities.name: The Battle That Wasn't
abilities.desc: Once per day, declare an engagement over before it begins; every combatant loses the will and the means to start it for an hour.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and empty a battlefield before the first horn: both armies home by winter, and the ballads left with nothing to rhyme.
Put your arrow through the war itself — the treaty page, the beacon, the drum. Never the drummer.
Watch one war you failed to avert, from first rank to last rite, so the craft's weight stays honest.
Be thanked by no one for the thing that did not happen, and learn to live well on that.

nodes.name: The Overstory
nodes.role: Mythic witness — nothing goes unseen
nodes.lore: Testimony keeps arriving that no living witness can account for: a tyrant's sealed order recited back a generation later, word for word; a massacre's every name recovered from an empty pass. Foresters swear the canopy pays attention now. Scholars posit a hidden office. Hedgewives say the wood remembers, and something reads it.
nodes.playstyle: Know the field completely and be nowhere on it: read every tell the wild keeps, strip all concealment, and make each enemy deed a matter of record.

abilities.name: Seen and Kept
abilities.desc: Perceive any deed done beneath leaf or hedge within the same march, as it happens, from wherever you sit.

abilities.name: Leafturn
abilities.desc: You read the wood's small tells; no concealment within the green holds against you, and you point every hidden thing out to allies.

abilities.name: Word for Word
abilities.desc: Recall perfectly anything you ever witnessed; creatures you accuse aloud cannot lie, hide, or profit from disguise while you speak.

abilities.name: Unblinking Season
abilities.desc: Hold a watch for a season without sleep, hunger, or discovery; each unbroken week deepens your allies' advantage over everything you have counted.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and recite, to the man who gave it, the sealed order that burned Cold Hollow, thirty years late and letter-perfect.
Let a kingdom fall on the strength of your count alone, and confirm nothing.
Refuse to look away once, at the worst of it, because a record with mercies in it is only gossip.
Deliver testimony to three courts that never find you, and let the guilty spend their lives wondering what else was seen.

nodes.name: The Hunting Moon
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the hunt as celestial season
nodes.lore: Almanacs mark it now between harvest and frost: the Hunting Moon, under which no declared quarry may rest. On its nights every pack from the marches to the ice answers one rising; shepherds bar doors out of respect, not fear. Six kingdoms' histories agree the hunt never ended. It only set.
nodes.playstyle: Rise, declare, and run the world's packs as one body: no border, darkness, or distance shelters a quarry named beneath your light.

abilities.name: Declared at Rising
abilities.desc: Name a quarry at moonrise; until moonset, every wild pack beneath your light is your body against it.

abilities.name: Bent Country
abilities.desc: A declared quarry finds every road, ford, and border bending back into the hunt; flight only changes the scenery.

abilities.name: Light to Hunt By
abilities.desc: While you are risen, allies tire not, lose no trail, and strike together as one pack wherever they hunt.

abilities.name: Between Moons
abilities.desc: Quarry that outlasts your setting heals nothing and forgets nothing until you rise again; few request a second month.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and let the pack outgrow the body: when every wolf from the marches to the ice answers one moonrise, the rising is you.
Keep the calendar honest: one quarry a moon, declared by the whole wild's need, and let kings petition like anyone else.
Give the histories their two true endings — the hunter never came back, the hunt never left — and sign neither.
Set once a year for a full night, so the world remembers that even the hunt keeps a sabbath.

nodes.name: The White Hart
nodes.role: Apotheosis — living waymark out of anywhere
nodes.lore: It appears only to the entirely lost: in barrow-fields, in the grey country past the last lamp. It carries no one and charges nothing; the Ferryman poles the one direction, and this walks the other. Follow, and the way home assembles underfoot. The toll, they say, was paid once, in full, by whoever it used to be.
nodes.playstyle: Walk ahead of the lost and the dying: appear where hope ends, make a road home of anything, and let nothing keep what follows you.

abilities.name: Seen at the Worst Hour
abilities.desc: Appear beside any creature past all finding, wherever it is kept; the path behind you leads home, whatever lies between.

abilities.name: Nothing Keeps Them
abilities.desc: Hands, hungers, and old claims release whoever walks behind you; the grip that refuses is left holding nothing.

abilities.name: The Wound Waits
abilities.desc: A dying ally who rises to follow cannot die while walking; the wound is made to wait until home.

abilities.name: The Lamp Answered
abilities.desc: Every lamp set in a window against loss reaches you; once per night, step out of the dark beside one.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85, walk past your own lit lamp a final time, and let the going take the shape it always wanted: four legs, white, unhurried.
Lead out someone who does not deserve it, because the way home was never a verdict.
Be hunted by a king who wants the way for his own, and lead him home too — the long way, until he understands.
Give the toll its remainder — the name, the face, the supper declined — and keep what is left: the direction home, wearing antlers.

nodes.name: The Appointment
nodes.role: Apotheosis — death as kept schedule
nodes.lore: Somewhere above every kingdom an arrow is falling, and has been for years. Deaths of consequence now keep hours, like courts: the arrow arrives on the appointed day, through weather, wards, and dynasties, never early, never twice. Chancellors have stopped asking whether. The remaining scholarship concerns when.
nodes.playstyle: Schedule the field's endings: call down shots loosed years ago, reserve enemies' deaths for their proper hour, and make time itself your quiver.

abilities.name: Already in the Air
abilities.desc: Your arrow for any declared target has been falling for years; call it down at will, once per target.

abilities.name: The Hour Is Kept
abilities.desc: A creature you have appointed cannot be slain by any other hand; its hour belongs to you, and it knows.

abilities.name: Nothing Postpones
abilities.desc: Wards, prophecy, and time-bending magic cannot move an appointment; effects that try are spent against the calendar and lost.

abilities.name: The Hour Released
abilities.desc: Cancel an appointment publicly; the spared creature and all witnesses lose the will to oppose you for a season.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and loose your last arrow straight up, into no weather at all; the world will hold it aloft, falling, everywhere, patiently.
Keep every appointment in memory alone: none written, none early, none ever missed. The office no longer has a holder; it has a schedule.
Grant one delay a decade, at your sole discretion, so that tyrants can never be certain which century is theirs.
Attend, unarmed and bareheaded, the one death you declined to keep, and let the calendar see what mercy costs it.

nodes.name: The Hinterland
nodes.role: Apotheosis — sovereign erasure, unmapped territory
nodes.lore: The surveys agree on the borders of what they cannot survey: a country's worth of ground that keeps no record and returns none. Companies enter on orders and arrive home out of step, fewer, certain they never marched. The recanted and the twice-buried go there to stop existing comfortably. Citizenship is conferred by disappearance.
nodes.playstyle: Carry sovereign silence onto any field: unmap ground, subtract intruders without authorship, and shelter whoever must not exist inside borders no one can cite.

abilities.name: Borders of Nothing
abilities.desc: Claim ground; it leaves every map, memory, and record, and those you shelter inside cannot be found by anything.

abilities.name: Subtraction
abilities.desc: Companies that enter uninvited emerge days later at their own muster, fewer, with no account any interrogation can recover.

abilities.name: Conferred Citizenship
abilities.desc: Grant an ally residence; while they keep your silence they cannot be scried, tracked, prophesied, or named as anyone.

abilities.name: Struck From the Survey
abilities.desc: Once per battle, remove one enemy engine, banner, or champion from the field and from every record that it ever came.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and stop being somewhere: let the ground you keep slip off the maps with you inside, still keeping it.
Take in the ones who must not exist — the recanted, the twice-buried, the last of their kinds — and ask nothing. Especially names.
Turn back the royal cartographers with nothing at all: no arrow, no voice, only a morning on which their instruments agree.
Let the churches argue whether the Quiet Country is paradise or punishment, and keep the border either way; the argument is also a wall.

nodes.name: Noonfall
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the shadowless hour hunts
nodes.lore: Armies march at dusk now, and generals pretend it is doctrine. At true noon under a clear sky the world holds one open instant in which nothing casts a shadow to hide in — and in that instant, on certain fields, something falls. Shepherds hood their hawks at midday, out of courtesy.
nodes.playstyle: Rule the open sky as a standing law: expose everything, strike from directly above, and make the hour itself the thing your enemies flee indoors from.

abilities.name: The Shadowless Hour
abilities.desc: At your noon, stealth, illusion, cover, and veils fail everywhere under open sky; the field is shown entire to your allies.

abilities.name: Straight Down
abilities.desc: Strike any target under open sky that you or an ally has seen since dawn; the blow arrives from directly above.

abilities.name: Roofs Are Strategy
abilities.desc: Enemies under open sky in your hour cannot rally, hide, or aim upward; commanders now plan campaigns around awnings.

abilities.name: Bring Down the Noon
abilities.desc: Once per day, advance the sky to cloudless noon above one field; every shadow and shelter on it opens to the stoop.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and become the wrong side of the sun: when the shadowless instant begins hunting of itself, you are the instant.
Spare whatever looks up and shows its face; the hour is for what hides, and the bargain must stay legible.
Keep one field forever unwatched and never say which, so that hope retains an acre.
Accept that the falcons knew all of this first, and hold the watch in a manner they would not be ashamed of.

nodes.name: The Homing
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the world's homeward pull
nodes.lore: Losing has stopped working properly. Rings surface in the years' first furrow; strayed children arrive at supper vague about the missing month; invading armies wake, embarrassingly, at their own borders. Scholars measure a pull in things, faint and homeward, and cannot source it. Somewhere inside the pull, a fire is still kept.
nodes.playstyle: Bend every displacement homeward: recall allies mid-stride, send invaders bodily back to their hearths, and make territory itself a thing that cannot be taken from you.

abilities.name: Nothing Stays Lost
abilities.desc: All things misplaced near you start the journey back: blades to hands, children to doorways, banners to the halls that hung them.

abilities.name: Sent Home
abilities.desc: Return one enemy bodily to the hearth that misses it most; it cannot find its way back for a day.

abilities.name: The Pull
abilities.desc: Your allies always know the way to you and the way home, and nothing — mist, malice, or magic — can turn them around.

abilities.name: Called Back
abilities.desc: Once per day, recall every ally on the field to your side unharmed, across any distance, arriving mid-stride.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and let the call outlive the caller: when lost things start home on their own in every county, take up keeping the pull instead.
Walk the world's boundaries once a generation, renewing the fence-posts, so everything remembers which direction is home.
Guard the exceptions hardest: what fled cruelty may stay lost, and the pull must never fetch it back.
Answer the philosophers who ask where home is for the homeless with a fire, built, lit, and left burning.

nodes.name: The Fair Warning
nodes.role: Apotheosis — violence must announce itself
nodes.lore: Ambush has stopped working. Every raid finds the village armed and the livestock gone; every assassin's chosen night, the shutters already barred. Before each violence, somewhere, a white shaft stands in the ground with time enough to heed it. Jurists argue whether warning is mercy or jurisdiction. The unheeded stop arguing.
nodes.playstyle: Abolish surprise: your side is never ambushed, the enemy's every stroke arrives announced, and those who ignore your warning meet the one shot that follows it.

abilities.name: First the Feather
abilities.desc: No violence surprises your allies; each incoming stroke, snare, and treachery is announced to its target with time to answer.

abilities.name: Stand Aside
abilities.desc: Any creature that heeds your warning and withdraws cannot be harmed by the violence it was warned of.

abilities.name: Notice Served
abilities.desc: Serve notice on a commander: their orders are heard by their targets as they are given.

abilities.name: No Second Warning
abilities.desc: Against those who ignored the first, your shots cannot miss or be survived, and mercy is formally satisfied.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and give the world its notice: one white shaft before every front rank on every field at dawn, and all of them yours.
Deliver fair warning to a god mustering against the living, and be heeded; the priests will file it under providence.
Keep the count of wars ended at the warning, and tell no one; the office works because it has never once been wrong.
Answer what the warned owe you: nothing. A warning with a price is only a threat arriving politely.

nodes.name: The Green Witness
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the land as sworn record
nodes.lore: Courts adjourn to groves now. The custom began when denial stopped surviving contact with certain ground: stand where the deed was done, and those present see it done again, whole. The wild has become admissible. Somewhere its reader still walks, palm to the bark, keeping the world's longest deposition.
nodes.playstyle: Make truth a battlefield condition: show what any ground has seen, strip every lie-born protection, and let enemies fight on terrain that remembers them.

abilities.name: Ground Truth
abilities.desc: Stand on any ground and see, whole, what was done there; all present witness it with you, once per place.

abilities.name: On the Green Record
abilities.desc: Every deed done under open green is kept; forgeries, false histories, and glamours wither when you produce the original.

abilities.name: Hostile Testimony
abilities.desc: Accuse an enemy with the land's memory; the guilty lose all protections born of lies — disguise, alibi, ward, and welcome.

abilities.name: Adjourned to the Grove
abilities.desc: Once per season, convene a dispute's parties in a grove where nothing false can be spoken; the judging stays theirs.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and take the land's oath: from this day, what the green sees, you have seen — all of it, always. The first night is the hardest.
Testify once against yourself, completely, for the record keeps no favorites or it keeps nothing.
Refuse every crown that asks to make the record convenient; a witness with a patron is a bard.
Answer the historians who ask who watches you by standing very still until they understand.

families.name: Bard
families.tagline: The right word, placed rightly, moves armies and ages.
families.description: The Bard collects what others overlook — songs, secrets, debts of gratitude, the exact words a person cannot refuse. Some carry their voices to war and hold shield-walls together with a cadence; others whisper in archives and anterooms, ending wars before the first arrow. All of them understand the same truth: a word placed correctly moves more than any lever, and history belongs to whoever phrases it.

nodes.name: Bard
nodes.role: Support — versatile inspiration and control
nodes.lore: Every road-worn troupe carries one: the apprentice who learned that a crowd can be tuned like a lute. Bards trade in songs, secrets, and applause, and they know the market value of each. Most die as footnotes in someone else's ballad. A few learn to write the ballad first.
nodes.playstyle: Weave buffs and jeers between verses, patching allies' nerve and picking at enemies' composure while staying one clever step away from the front line.

abilities.name: Opening Chord
abilities.desc: Begin combat with a flourish that grants nearby allies bonus initiative and a brief surge of morale.

abilities.name: Cutting Couplet
abilities.desc: Deliver a barbed verse that deals psychic damage and leaves the target flinching, weakening its next attack.

abilities.name: Ear for Trouble
abilities.desc: Passively sense lies and hidden hostility in conversation; act first against any ambush you overheard coming.

abilities.name: Borrowed Refrain
abilities.desc: Mimic the last ally ability you witnessed at reduced potency, once per rest.

progressionSteps: Learn three hundred songs by ear, and be beaten once for singing the wrong one in the wrong hall.
Play for a crowd that came to jeer, and leave them silent.
Trade your first secret for supper, and understand what you have actually sold.
Bury your teacher with the song they hated, because it was the true one.

nodes.name: War-Skald
nodes.role: Frontline support — formation buffs and morale
nodes.lore: War-skalds march where the banners do, armored in nothing but nerve, keeping time for the shield-wall with drum and bellowed verse. Captains requisition them like rations. The soldiers know the arithmetic: a line that sings holds three heartbeats longer than a line that does not, and most battles are decided in two.
nodes.playstyle: Stand in the second rank and conduct the battle, layering marching cadences that harden allies and counter-verses that sap enemy charges. Your voice is the front line's spine.

abilities.name: Shield-Cadence
abilities.desc: Chant a marching meter that grants allies in formation bonus block and immunity to the first fear effect.

abilities.name: Drumfire
abilities.desc: Strike your war-drum to reset one ally's broken stance and pull them back into the line.

abilities.name: Skald's Bellow
abilities.desc: A shout that carries over battle noise; every ally who hears it regains a spent reaction.

abilities.name: Counter-Verse
abilities.desc: Answer an enemy warcry with practiced mockery, cancelling its morale bonus before it lands.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10, then enlist with a company that has lost its standard, and sing it a new one.
Keep the cadence through a full rout without once looking behind you.
Learn the death-songs of five peoples, so that no soldier under your voice dies to silence.
Carry the drum out of a defeat when stronger backs carried nothing.

nodes.name: Veiled Chronicler
nodes.role: Control support — charm, debuffs, information warfare
nodes.lore: Veiled Chroniclers keep the histories nobody commissioned: the bastard lines, the buried treaties, the words kings spoke before the witnesses died. They learn early that lore is a lever and a noose at once. Courts host them nervously, the way one hosts a fire — useful, warming, and watched.
nodes.playstyle: Fight before the fight begins: gather names, plant doubts, charm sentries. In combat, unmake enemy plans with bindings and misdirection rather than trading blows.

abilities.name: Marginalia
abilities.desc: Recall one obscure fact about any named creature or place; gain advantage on your next action exploiting it.

abilities.name: Hushword
abilities.desc: Speak a syllable of old silence; one target cannot cast, command, or call for aid for a round.

abilities.name: False Provenance
abilities.desc: Forge a memory into a listener's recent past; they misremember one detail of the last hour.

abilities.name: Thread of Rumor
abilities.desc: Seed a rumor in a settlement; within a day it returns grown, carrying truths its carriers never meant to share.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10 and recite, unprompted, a history its owners paid to have forgotten.
Spend a season as a servant in a great house and leave knowing which floorboards listen.
End one feud with three sentences, spoken to the right person at the wrong hour.
Copy a banned chronicle by candlelight, then decide alone who is permitted to read it.

nodes.name: Shieldsinger
nodes.role: Defensive support — mitigation and battlefield anchoring
nodes.lore: Shieldsingers are called wall-mortar by the infantry, and they take it as an honor. Their verses set into a standing line like cooling bronze, binding shield to shield until a hundred bodies breathe as one. Where a Shieldsinger plants their feet, generals redraw their maps around that point.
nodes.playstyle: Anchor a position and refuse the enemy. Layer sustained wards over allies who hold their ground, and punish anything that breaks formation — theirs or yours.

abilities.name: Mortar-Hymn
abilities.desc: Allies standing adjacent to one another share incoming damage and gain resistance while the hymn is held.

abilities.name: Planted Verse
abilities.desc: Choose ground; allies upon it cannot be moved against their will and mend slightly at each verse's turn.

abilities.name: Hold the Vowel
abilities.desc: Sustain a single note; while held, the first killing blow against each warded ally leaves them at one hit point instead.

abilities.name: Ring of Voices
abilities.desc: Once per battle, fallen allies within the song stand again with a portion of health, provided the line still holds.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25, then hold a breach with your voice while the shields behind you are still forming.
Sing an eight-hour siege watch without water, and let no one on the wall sleep afraid.
Take the wound meant for the line and finish the stanza before you bind it.
Refuse a general's order to retreat, and be right.

nodes.name: Dirgecaller
nodes.role: Offensive support — fear, attrition, siege-breaking
nodes.lore: Dirgecallers sing at armies the songs meant for their graves, and soldiers who hear their own funeral early tend to attend it. Besieged cities dread them more than engines; stone resists a ram, but a garrison's nerve is masonry of a softer kind. Their arrival at a wall is itself an ultimatum.
nodes.playstyle: Break the enemy before the charge does. Stack dread on packed formations, shatter morale thresholds, and turn organized resistance into a stampede pointed the wrong way.

abilities.name: Premature Requiem
abilities.desc: Name a target and sing their funeral; they take escalating psychic damage each round they can hear you.

abilities.name: Sapper's Threnody
abilities.desc: A low sustained tone that cracks mortar and works fortification stones loose over several minutes.

abilities.name: Rout-Note
abilities.desc: Enemies below half morale who hear this discord must flee toward their own rear lines, through their allies.

abilities.name: Grave-Hush
abilities.desc: Silence falls across a wide radius; enemy commands go unheard while your dirge alone carries.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and end a siege without a single ladder touching the wall.
Learn what a city sounds like the night before it surrenders, and be the one who taught it.
Sing a veteran company into flight, then walk their empty line slowly.
Attend the funerals your songs began. All of them.

nodes.name: Namebinder
nodes.role: Controller — single-target binding and compulsion
nodes.lore: Namebinders collect what things are actually called: the syllables a river answers to, the word a demon signed before witnesses. To hold a true name is to hold a leash. They speak carefully in company, because they know precisely what a careless sentence can be made to do.
nodes.playstyle: Hunt the name, then own the fight. Slow to open, devastating once a target is named — command it, unmake it, or forbid it with a single word.

abilities.name: Utterance of Binding
abilities.desc: Speak a learned true name; the named creature obeys one one-word command with no saving throw.

abilities.name: Name-Sounding
abilities.desc: Probe a target with test-syllables over three rounds to uncover fragments of its true name.

abilities.name: Sealed Syllable
abilities.desc: Lock one word out of a target's mouth; they cannot speak it, cast with it, or write it.

abilities.name: Leash of Letters
abilities.desc: A creature you have named cannot move beyond thirty paces of you until dawn.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and hear your own true name from a stranger's mouth, and survive the hearing.
Bind a lesser spirit by name alone, without circle, salt, or blade.
Trade a year of your singing voice for one syllable of a mountain's name.
Speak a true name in anger exactly once, and let what follows teach you never again.

nodes.name: Silvertongue
nodes.role: Social controller — charm, leverage, war-avoidance
nodes.lore: Silvertongues end wars in anterooms, over wine nobody quite remembers pouring. They are lent between courts like fine instruments, and every ruler who borrows one wonders, correctly, what tune was played upon them in return. The great treaties of the age bear their fingerprints and never their names.
nodes.playstyle: Win the encounter before initiative is rolled. Charm, leverage, and staged concessions turn enemies into hosts; in open combat, redirect aggression rather than absorbing it.

abilities.name: Perfect Concession
abilities.desc: Offer surrender terms so precisely fitted that the enemy commander accepts conditions you wrote for them.

abilities.name: Borrowed Loyalty
abilities.desc: Charm a target into treating you as a trusted advisor for an hour; afterward they rationalize everything you asked.

abilities.name: Turn the Blade
abilities.desc: An enemy who strikes at you redirects the blow to a target you nominate with a whispered suggestion.

abilities.name: Room Reading
abilities.desc: Instantly learn the strongest desire and sorest grievance of every person in a gathering.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25, then talk your way out of an execution you deserved.
Broker peace between two houses while carrying a knife-scar from each.
Convince a mercenary company to march home unpaid, and have them thank you at the gate.
Sit across from a tyrant, speak for one hour, and leave the room owning the war's ending.

nodes.name: Anthemwright
nodes.role: Army-scale support — persistent zone anthems
nodes.lore: Anthemwrights no longer sing songs; they build them, verse-engineered for a single army the way a smith fits a cuirass. A finished anthem outlives its commission — soldiers' grandchildren hum it in peacetime, and it still remembers how to close a shield-wall. Kingdoms count themselves fortunate to field three at once.
nodes.playstyle: Compose before battle, conduct during it. Deploy pre-built anthem structures that persist across the field, letting whole formations fight a measure above their nature.

abilities.name: Forged Anthem
abilities.desc: Spend a week composing for a specific company; while any ten of its members sing, all gain elite-tier discipline and defenses.

abilities.name: Bridge Verse
abilities.desc: Link two separated formations; they count as adjacent for morale and share the stronger unit's resolve.

abilities.name: Standing Coda
abilities.desc: Your anthem persists on the field for an hour after you fall silent, or after you fall.

abilities.name: Tempering Silence
abilities.desc: One measured pause; allies shed all fear, exhaustion, and one grievous condition as the anthem resumes.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and compose an anthem that holds a line after your death is reported. Correct the report later, in person.
Submit your masterwork to the circle of Anthemwrights and defend every syllable through three nights of hostile revision.
Retire a broken company's old anthem with full honors before you write them the new one.
Refuse a paying crown once, because the song they asked for was a lie.

nodes.name: Threnodist
nodes.role: Strategic debuffer — mass dread and unmaking
nodes.lore: There is a short list of songs that are illegal to perform in three empires. Threnodists wrote all of them. Each carries a personal lament, years in the making and never yet sung whole; commanders have negotiated surrenders simply to keep it unfinished. Their gray robes empty streets faster than plague-bells.
nodes.playstyle: Escalate dread on a strategic scale. Long-form lament movements degrade an entire army's cohesion, health, and works, building toward a finale few commanders permit to arrive.

abilities.name: The Unfinished Lament
abilities.desc: Perform successive movements across rounds; each deepens army-wide penalties, and the final movement breaks any force still listening.

abilities.name: Toll for the Living
abilities.desc: Every enemy who has killed today hears a bell only they can hear; the guilty strike last and flinch first.

abilities.name: Ash Registry
abilities.desc: Name a fortification within the lament; its garrison abandons posts nightly until the walls stand unwatched.

abilities.name: Mercy Clause
abilities.desc: End any of your dirges instantly for all who ground arms; those who surrendered are immune to your songs until dawn.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40, then begin composing your own lament, knowing you may never be permitted to finish it.
Be named in an empire's law by your work and not your name.
Sing the second movement over a fortress, and count the gates that stand open by morning.
Grant mercy once when the finale was owed, and carry what that mercy costs.

nodes.name: Redactor
nodes.role: Existential controller — erasure and denial
nodes.lore: Redactors unmake the written and the spoken. Where a Namebinder holds a leash, a Redactor cuts the collar out of the world: heresies un-taught, treaties un-signed, whole men reduced to a smudge in their mothers' memory. The great archives keep a lamp burning against them. It does not help.
nodes.playstyle: Delete the enemy's options. Strip abilities, spells, and identities from targets mid-fight; the strongest foes are simply those with the most to lose.

abilities.name: Strikethrough
abilities.desc: Erase one of a target's known abilities for the encounter; legendary creatures lose it for a full day.

abilities.name: Excision
abilities.desc: Remove a target's name from every mind within a mile; its allies stop taking its orders.

abilities.name: Blank Page
abilities.desc: Become unrecorded for ten minutes; scrying, memory, and written accounts cannot hold you.

abilities.name: Errata
abilities.desc: Rewrite one small fact declared aloud this scene — a password, an order, a price — and the world complies.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and erase a heresy so completely that its inquisitors forget their own occupation.
Un-write one page of your own history and live with the seam.
Stand in the Archive of Echoes and learn to hear which of its silences are yours.
Refuse to erase a name once, though the payment was a kingdom, because the record was true.

nodes.name: Kingmaker
nodes.role: Grand manipulator — favors, factions, proxy warfare
nodes.lore: Kingmakers have stopped attending wars; they attend successions. Each keeps a quiet ledger of debts owed by the crowned, collected in policy rather than coin. Three reigning monarchs are commonly agreed to be Kingmaker work, though the guilds of heralds dispute, very carefully, which three.
nodes.playstyle: Play the campaign, not the encounter. Call in owed favors — armies, pardons, poisonings — and enter combat only when a debt requires collecting in person.

abilities.name: Ledger of Crowns
abilities.desc: Call in a stored favor from a ruler; receive troops, sanctuary, or a signature within a day.

abilities.name: Whispered Succession
abilities.desc: Over a week of court-work, redirect an inheritance, appointment, or command to a candidate of your choosing.

abilities.name: Diplomatic Poise
abilities.desc: Creatures that understand speech cannot strike you first in an encounter where you have not drawn a weapon.

abilities.name: The Long Toast
abilities.desc: During any shared meal, learn one secret each guest would trade their honor to protect.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and seat your first ruler, then decline the title they offer you.
Hold a debt for a decade without once mentioning it.
Unmake a tyrant with paperwork, witnesses, and one well-timed silence.
Survive being owed too much by someone who would rather cancel the debt with a knife.

nodes.name: Undersong
nodes.role: Defensive support — fear absorption and stored release
nodes.lore: The circle of Anthemwrights builds courage and hands it out; the Undersongs call that scaffolding, and scaffolding falls with the music. They sing beneath the line, low and unheard, drawing every terror into themselves so the wall has nothing left to feel. The order accepts volunteers, explains the cost, then accepts the fewer who remain.
nodes.playstyle: Stand within the formation and drink its dread. Redirect fear, pain, and panic onto yourself, then spend the stored anguish as devastating release notes.

abilities.name: Swallowed Scream
abilities.desc: Absorb a fear or morale effect targeting any ally in earshot; store it as a verse you may sing back later.

abilities.name: Beneath the Anthem
abilities.desc: While an ally's song or banner effect is active, you may carry its cost — exhaustion, backlash, upkeep — in their place.

abilities.name: Returned in Kind
abilities.desc: Expend every stored terror in one discord; enemies within thirty paces suffer the sum of all fear you have swallowed today.

abilities.name: Unheard Verse
abilities.desc: Your songs grant their benefits silently; enemies cannot locate, silence, or counter what they cannot hear.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40, then stand your first vigil beneath a shield-wall and take into yourself everything it could not afford to feel.
Hear the order explain the cost twice, and volunteer twice.
Carry a company's whole terror through a night assault, and let them believe, forever, that they were simply brave.
Argue doctrine with an Anthemwright until dawn, lose gracefully, and go on being right.

nodes.name: Elegist
nodes.role: Precision striker — single-target elegies and endings
nodes.lore: Threnodists grieve at armies, wholesale; the Elegists call that noise. They hold that every living thing owns one song exactly fitted to its ending, and they find it — a listener at a time. Their commissions are spoken, never written, and their fees are ruinous, because the second-worst thing an Elegist can do is sing for free.
nodes.playstyle: Study one target while the fight rages, assembling their elegy phrase by phrase; each verse lands harder than the last, and the finished song ends them.

abilities.name: The Fitting
abilities.desc: Observe a target for two rounds to learn its griefs; your song abilities against it ignore resistances thereafter.

abilities.name: Elegy in Progress
abilities.desc: Begin a target's elegy; each round you add a verse, your damage against them doubles, to a limit of four.

abilities.name: Dying Fall
abilities.desc: Complete a finished elegy against a target below a quarter of its health; it dies quietly, without wound, sound, or save.

abilities.name: Grief Laid Down
abilities.desc: Sing an ended thing to rest — a ghost, a feud, an oath — and it troubles the living no further.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and hear, once, the opening phrase of your own elegy from a senior Elegist, so you know the work is honest.
Compose an elegy across a winter for a tyrant you have never met, and deliver it in eleven words.
Refuse a commission because the grief offered was not the client's to spend.
Break the order's rule once: lay a ghost three priests could not, for no fee, and accept the censure as fair.

nodes.name: Remembrancer
nodes.role: Controller — indelible witness and binding record
nodes.lore: Raised by the Archive of Echoes as its answer to the Redactors, Remembrancers hold that erasure is the only murder that leaves no body to bury. What one of them witnesses cannot afterward be unwritten, and they attend executions, treaties, and massacres uninvited. Their memory is admissible in every court that dares summon them.
