nodes.playstyle: Fix the battlefield into record. Pin enemies to their names and deeds, lock conditions in place, and make every advantage you witness permanent.

abilities.name: Entered Into Record
abilities.desc: Declare a deed you witnessed this scene; no magic, erasure, or decree can afterward make it not have happened.

abilities.name: Pinned to the Name
abilities.desc: Speak a target's name and deed together; it cannot disguise, teleport, turn invisible, or deny the deed until dawn.

abilities.name: Mend the Seam
abilities.desc: Restore one erased or redacted thing you can prove once existed; Redactor work resists, but not forever.

abilities.name: Uninvited Witness
abilities.desc: You may attend any proceeding — court, coronation, execution — and no bar, ward, or writ may lawfully remove you.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40, then stand in the Archive of Echoes and answer one of its silences aloud, correctly, from memory.
Memorize a condemned library in the nine nights before it burns.
Witness an atrocity powerful men paid to have unhappen, and carry it, uncut, into a courtroom that does not want it.
Meet a Redactor over the same page, and leave with the page.

nodes.name: Demagogue
nodes.role: Mass persuader — crowds, uprisings, public leverage
nodes.lore: Kingmakers work successions in anterooms; Demagogues work squares, and hold that no throne was ever owed to anyone. They speak where the many gather, and the many become an argument with hands. Every city ordinance against public assembly is, one way or another, a monument to some Demagogue — the guilds of heralds keep the list.
nodes.playstyle: Raise the crowd and aim it. Convert bystanders into partisans mid-encounter, escalate numbers into power, and vanish into the very many you made.

abilities.name: Kindling Speech
abilities.desc: Address a crowd for one minute; a number of listeners equal to your level become your partisans for a day.

abilities.name: Borrowed Hands
abilities.desc: Your partisans within sight lend you their actions; spend up to three of them each round as your own.

abilities.name: One of the Crowd
abilities.desc: While at least ten people stand near you, attacks and divinations cannot single you out of the press.

abilities.name: Emptied Market
abilities.desc: Speak in a settlement at dusk; by morning its labor, markets, and garrisons answer to the crowd's demands, not the crown's.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40, then empty a tyrant's capital with nothing in your hands but a crate to stand on.
Be outlawed by name in three cities, and enter each one openly, inside a crowd that will not part.
Refuse the crown a grateful mob offers you, twice, because once convinces no one.
Watch a riot you raised burn something you loved, and decide, with open eyes, to keep speaking.

nodes.name: Voice of Legions
nodes.role: Mythic army-wide aura — unbreakable formations
nodes.lore: The histories record perhaps five Voices of Legions, and argue about two of them. When one sings, an army becomes a single instrument: ten thousand shields tuned to one pitch, fear engineered out of the design. Old soldiers swear the Song at Vessa's Ford still holds the ford, decades after its singer fell.
nodes.playstyle: You are the battle's tempo. Every allied soul in earshot fights within your meter — unbreakable, synchronized, and, for as long as you sing, slightly more than human.

abilities.name: Ten Thousand, One Throat
abilities.desc: All allies who can hear you share the highest morale, discipline, and resolve found among them.

abilities.name: The Held Line
abilities.desc: Declare a line upon the earth; while you sing, no ally behind it can die, only fall unconscious.

abilities.name: Vessa's Measure
abilities.desc: Once per war, the enemy army hears its own marching song played back, perfected, and hesitates a full round.

abilities.name: Song Without Singer
abilities.desc: Should you fall mid-battle, your anthem continues from every allied mouth until the field is decided.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60, then hold a field where every officer has fallen, conducting an army whose only commander is the song.
Have a truce called because both armies were singing your verse.
Teach the anthem to a child, a veteran, and an enemy, and hear all three keep it true.
Enter a history you did not commission, and find it needed no exaggeration.

nodes.name: Knell of Empires
nodes.role: Mythic dread — campaign-ending finales
nodes.lore: A Knell of Empires is less a person than a precedent. Chronicles credit the fall of Vhoria to eleven days of a single voice outside its walls, with no arrow loosed. Rulers keep the names of living Knells in sealed letters, opened only to learn what must never be provoked.
nodes.playstyle: Arrive as an ending. Your presence alone degrades enemy resolve at strategic range; your finished laments retire armies, dynasties, and the appetite for war itself.

abilities.name: The Finished Lament
abilities.desc: Complete your life's dirge over three days against one realm; its will to make war ends for a generation.

abilities.name: Eleven Days of Vhoria
abilities.desc: Besiege a fortification with voice alone; each dawn, a portion of its garrison lays down arms and walks out.

abilities.name: Funeral for the Future
abilities.desc: Show one commander their own succession dying within the song; they seek terms or break entirely.

abilities.name: Bell Unrung
abilities.desc: Any who have heard your finale and lived can never again be rallied against you.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60, then finish the lament you began decades ago, and choose whom it is for.
End an empire's war without an army — yours or theirs — taking the field.
Hear your name written into a treaty as a clause: that you will not be sent.
Sing once, at the last, for the dead of your own making, and mean it.

nodes.name: The Unwritten
nodes.role: Mythic erasure — editing what is real
nodes.lore: The Unwritten cut their own names out of the world's record and stepped through the gap. Nothing remembers them longer than a breath, which makes them the only editors history cannot flatter or bribe. Scholars infer their existence from the seams: wars that stop mid-sentence, tyrants nobody recalls obeying.
nodes.playstyle: Exist in the margins. Unwrite enemies, events, and consequences at will; the fight itself is trivial — choosing what deserves to remain in the record is not.

abilities.name: Total Redaction
abilities.desc: Remove a creature from the record entirely; it persists, but nothing can remember, follow, obey, or mourn it.

abilities.name: The Gap
abilities.desc: Step into an erased moment; you are untargetable and undetectable until you act upon the world.

abilities.name: Restored Passage
abilities.desc: Un-erase one thing you or any Redactor destroyed; the truth returns to every mind that once held it.

abilities.name: Authorial Doubt
abilities.desc: Force a legendary enemy to briefly disbelieve its own existence, losing all actions for a round.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60, then unwrite your own name and watch your mother's eyes pass over you.
Erase a war so cleanly that its widows wake merely sad, not knowing why.
Meet another Unwritten in the margins, and agree on nothing except the rules.
Choose one true, terrible thing and let it stand in the record forever, because someone must.

nodes.name: Author of Ages
nodes.role: Mythic orchestrator — history as an instrument
nodes.lore: An Author of Ages no longer moves rulers; they move the idea of rule. Their work is measured in centuries: a philosophy seeded in a border town, a marriage arranged two generations early, a war scheduled like a harvest. Historians call certain eras well-written. They do not know how right they are.
nodes.playstyle: Operate at the scale of eras. Every faction is a character you are developing; combat is a plot device, deployed sparingly and always foreshadowed.

abilities.name: Draft of the Century
abilities.desc: Set a hundred-year design in motion; once per age, declare one historical outcome inevitable and watch events comply.

abilities.name: Recurring Character
abilities.desc: Any person you have spoken with for an hour can be activated as an ally decades later, unaware they were written.

abilities.name: Foreshadowing
abilities.desc: Declare an event aloud; within a year, circumstances bend until it occurs at a moment of your choosing.

abilities.name: Narrative Weight
abilities.desc: You cannot die in a way history would find meaningless; fatal blows in trivial scenes simply fail.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60, then complete a design your predecessor began before your grandmother was born.
Start a renaissance with a rumor and a scholarship.
Watch a war you scheduled forty years ago arrive on time, and feel nothing you did not plan to feel.
Write the age's ending in advance, seal it, and be right.

nodes.name: The Fermata
nodes.role: Mythic absorber — army-scale dread transference
nodes.lore: The histories record armies that should have broken and instead walked home quiet, and they record, sometimes, a figure on the wall singing under the screams. A Fermata carries an entire war's worth of terror and speaks in a level voice. The order's physicians examine each one yearly and write, carefully, nothing at all.
nodes.playstyle: Nothing near you is permitted to despair. Absorb fear at army scale, hold it indefinitely, and release it — once, precisely — as something no enemy line survives.

abilities.name: Level Voice
abilities.desc: Allies within a mile cannot be frightened, demoralized, or driven to rout; you feel each prevented terror personally.

abilities.name: Carried Quiet
abilities.desc: Take a broken ally's condition — madness, despair, mortal fear — into yourself; they wake steady, and you do not say what it cost.

abilities.name: Full Voice
abilities.desc: Loose everything you carry in one measure; every foe in earshot suffers the accumulated terror of your entire career, all at once.

abilities.name: Composure
abilities.desc: Your saves cannot be worsened, your concentration cannot be broken, and your voice cannot be silenced while any ally can hear you.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60, then carry a whole war home inside you and answer every question about it kindly.
Walk a plague-city's night watch for a season, and leave it a city that remembers grief but not despair.
Release, exactly once, everything you carry, at a place of your choosing, and let the histories argue whether it was mercy.
Teach one student to carry less than you did, and call that the order's first victory.

nodes.name: The Perfect Grief
nodes.role: Mythic executioner — inevitable single-target endings
nodes.lore: Somewhere there is a song that ends each thing, and one living voice is agreed to know them all. Rulers pay the Perfect Grief simply to confirm that theirs exists; it does. The histories dispute only whether the grief is felt or performed, and those who could answer have all, notably, declined.
nodes.playstyle: Choose what ends. Any single foe, however legendary, can be sung to a close; the work of the fight is reaching the final verse intact.

abilities.name: The True Elegy
abilities.desc: Begin any creature's true elegy without study; it knows, and must choose each round between fleeing your voice and stopping it.

abilities.name: Grief for the Deathless
abilities.desc: Your elegies end what does not die — liches, oaths, institutions — retiring them from the world as concluded things.

abilities.name: Withheld Verse
abilities.desc: Halt an elegy one verse from its close; the target lives, and nothing can conceal from it how close it stood.

abilities.name: Confirmation
abilities.desc: Hear any named creature's elegy in your mind unbidden; learn its manner of ending, though never the day.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and finish, alone, the elegy of something the world agreed could not end, and attend what follows.
Confirm to a king that his song exists, decline to hum it, and charge him for both.
Withhold the final verse once, for reasons you never explain, and let the histories call it mercy or craft as they please.
Learn your own elegy whole, carry it calmly, and tell no one who holds the other copy.

nodes.name: The Fair Copy
nodes.role: Mythic witness — reality anchored by memory
nodes.lore: When two archives disagree, both send to the Fair Copy, and abide. They are the corrected text of the world walking around in a person: everything witnessed, nothing revised. The Unwritten leave seams where they cut; the Fair Copy is where the missing sentences are still, inconveniently for someone, whole.
nodes.playstyle: Be the record no power can amend. Recall anything that has ever happened near you, impose true versions over lies, and unmake illusions by contradiction.

abilities.name: Sic
abilities.desc: Declare one falsehood in play — an illusion, a forgery, a glamour — formally erroneous; it fails for all observers.

abilities.name: Retained in Full
abilities.desc: Anything you have perceived is permanently retained; no magic, age, or bargain can take a memory from you.

abilities.name: Variance Noted
abilities.desc: When a creature lies within your hearing, you and your allies know, and it takes psychic backlash proportional to the lie.

abilities.name: Recension
abilities.desc: Once per season, fully restore an erased person, place, or event to the world's memory; even Unwritten work yields.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60, then be summoned by two warring archives, settle their variance from memory, and be believed without oath.
Recite a page an Unwritten cut, word for word, into the silence where it used to be, and make it hold.
Remember, on behalf of a grieving nation, everything it begged you to help it forget, and refuse.
Carry one memory you know to be true and cruel and useless, forever, because accuracy does not bargain.

nodes.name: The Murmuration
nodes.role: Mythic crowd-shaper — cities moved as one
nodes.lore: A Demagogue raises a crowd; the Murmuration is one. Where they walk, the many arrive without being sent for, and think together like weather deciding to break. Three dynasties ended in a fortnight of their passing through, and no chronicler has ever found the speech that did it. There wasn't one.
nodes.playstyle: You no longer address crowds; you conduct populations. Entire districts act as your limbs, and tyrannies discover that arresting you means arresting everyone.

abilities.name: The Turnout
abilities.desc: People within a day's walk feel called and come; a crowd of any size assembles around you by dusk.

abilities.name: Sea of Strangers
abilities.desc: While any crowd holds you, you cannot be seized, struck, or scried; every attempt finds only willing strangers.

abilities.name: One Roar
abilities.desc: Focus a crowd's will into a single act — open the gates, stop the wagons, part for no cavalry — performed as one.

abilities.name: No Speech At All
abilities.desc: Your mere presence in a settlement for a night grants its people immunity to fear, censorship, and compulsion for a season.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60, then enter a capital under total curfew and let the streets fill behind you, window by window, in silence.
End a dynasty without giving a speech, and leave the chroniclers arguing over which words did it.
Stand in front of the crowd you raised when it turns the wrong way, and turn it, alone, with your back to the spears.
Go home to a village too small for history, and be, for one winter, obeyed by no one.

nodes.name: The Chorus
nodes.role: Apotheosis — every massed voice at once
nodes.lore: The Song at Vessa's Ford still holds the ford; scholars stopped asking how and started asking whom. The Chorus is what a Voice becomes when the singing no longer requires them: an office held by whoever the world's massed voices agree to be next. Armies that have never met them keep their meter anyway.
nodes.playstyle: Sing from every allied mouth at once. Wherever people raise one voice together, you are present, buffing, conducting, and impossible to silence short of silencing the world.

abilities.name: Everywhere Sung
abilities.desc: Manifest wherever ten or more voices sing together, at any distance, and fight from within their song.

abilities.name: The Second Ford
abilities.desc: Consecrate a position permanently; any ally who ever holds it gains your full anthem, singer or none.

abilities.name: Descant Without End
abilities.desc: Add your voice to any allied song, prayer, or warcry anywhere; it gains mythic potency for its duration.

abilities.name: Silence Insufficient
abilities.desc: You cannot be silenced while two allies remain alive anywhere; killing the song now requires killing the singing world.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85, then hear yourself sung at Vessa's Ford on a night you spent asleep three kingdoms away, and understand what you are becoming.
Be kept by the world: let every army that sings, on any side, keep your meter, and make your peace with the ones you would not have chosen.
Attend your own funeral as the music.
When the last veteran of your first company dies, sing at the graveside in ten thousand living voices, none of them yours.

nodes.name: The Passing Bell
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the toll that ends realms
nodes.lore: Rulers no longer keep the Knell's name in sealed letters; they keep an ear on their own bells. When a realm's time comes, its bells ring notes no founder cast into them, and the Passing Bell is both the ringing and the one who may still walk in afterward, unarmed, to confirm it. Protocol exists. It is short.
nodes.playstyle: Arrive as a verdict already delivered. Realms weaken at your attention; your presence ends sieges, reigns, and appetites for war before your first note sounds.

abilities.name: Rung Elsewhere
abilities.desc: Toll through any bell in the world; all who hear it know which realm is being mourned in advance.

abilities.name: The Short Protocol
abilities.desc: Enter any fortification unarmed and unopposed once its bells have rung you; garrisons stand aside by something older than orders.

abilities.name: Generation of Quiet
abilities.desc: A realm that hears your full toll cannot raise armies for thirty years; its people, oddly, prosper.

abilities.name: The Granted Year
abilities.desc: Refrain from ringing for a realm whose time has come; it gains a year, and knows precisely whose year it is.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85, then hear a city you never visited ring your notes, unbidden, on the night its dynasty ends.
Stop being sent for. Arrive only where the bells have already agreed.
Grant one realm its year, for reasons three chancelleries still dispute, and attend, at its end, what the year became.
Compose the toll for the age itself, file it with the guilds of heralds, and decline to say when.

nodes.name: The Lacuna
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the living gap in every record
nodes.lore: The Unwritten stepped through a gap in the record; the Lacuna is the gap, given office. Every archive owns a missing page, every history a sentence that stops — and all of them are the same room, and the room is occupied. Scholars leave offerings of blank paper. Sometimes, terribly, the offerings are accepted.
nodes.playstyle: Fight from inside the world's omissions. Step between any two erasures, remove events as they happen, and remain the one thing no account will ever hold.

abilities.name: Every Missing Page
abilities.desc: Travel instantly between any two erasures in the world; all gaps in all records adjoin your position.

abilities.name: As It Never Was
abilities.desc: Erase an event in the instant it occurs — the blow, the death, the order given — before consequence takes hold.

abilities.name: Kept in the Gap
abilities.desc: Swallow a secret whole: person, place, or deed vanishes from record and recall, retrievable only by your consent.

abilities.name: The Stopped Sentence
abilities.desc: End any speech, spell, or command mid-word, permanently; the rest of it never existed to be finished.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85, then find the page where your own record stopped, and choose to be the silence rather than the sentence.
Let the other Unwritten forget you, one by one, until even the margins hold no meeting you attended.
Keep the rules you once agreed in the margins, now that no one remains who could catch you breaking them.
Guard the one true, terrible thing you left standing in the record, forever, from every editor who comes after — including yourself.

nodes.name: The Canon
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the story history must follow
nodes.lore: An Author of Ages writes history; the Canon is what history is checked against. They no longer arrange events — events arrange themselves to remain in the telling, because exclusion from the Canon has become a kind of weather no dynasty survives. Historians call certain eras well-written. The eras, by now, are trying.
nodes.playstyle: Rule on what the story is. Admit or exclude deeds from mattering, grant allies narrative weight, and reduce enemies to characters whose arcs you have already closed.

abilities.name: Outside the Story
abilities.desc: Rule a deed outside the Canon; it still occurred, but no consequence, glory, or precedent may flow from it.

abilities.name: Protagonism
abilities.desc: Name an ally this era's protagonist for a season; fortune, allies, and timely coincidence bend toward their purpose.

abilities.name: Closed Arc
abilities.desc: Declare an enemy's story complete; they can win no further victories, only endings, until they change beyond recognition.

abilities.name: The Authorized Version
abilities.desc: Once per age, pronounce what an event meant; every telling, ballad, and archive amends itself to agree.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85, then watch the design you sealed come true and notice that the age now consults you before happening.
Outgrow authorship: let a century you did not plan argue its way into your approval, and grant it.
Refuse the Fair Copy's correction once, be wrong, and enter the error into the Canon under your own name.
Decide what the world's story is for, and do not tell it; a Canon that explains itself is merely a book.

nodes.name: The Stay
nodes.role: Apotheosis — despair held for the world
nodes.lore: A Fermata releases its carried terror exactly once; the Stay never will. They have become the place fear goes: a standing mercy soldiers swear by without knowing it is an office. Routs end mid-step. Plagues are endured with strange grace. Somewhere, someone is carrying it, and the world has learned to lean.
nodes.playstyle: Hold what the world cannot. Absorb despair at the scale of nations, anchor allies against any breaking, and remain — whatever arrives — level, present, and singing low.

abilities.name: Where Fear Goes
abilities.desc: All despair, panic, and breaking within a realm may be routed to you; you take it, and hold.

abilities.name: Leaned Upon
abilities.desc: Any ally anywhere may, once, refuse to break; they feel a low song under the moment, and stand.

abilities.name: Mainstay
abilities.desc: You cannot be moved, silenced, or unmade while you carry another's fear; the world requires you standing.

abilities.name: Quiet Census
abilities.desc: Know at all times who, in the world, is closest to breaking, and be able to hum to them.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85, then take up again everything you once released, add to it what others set down, and speak kindly at supper.
Become weather: let soldiers who never learned your name swear by you when the line holds for no reason they can find.
Decline, forever, the one release the rank permits, and do not be praised for it, because no one knows.
Choose your successor from among those who never once asked what you carry, and tell them everything, last.

nodes.name: The Epitaph
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the last word over all things
nodes.lore: Nothing now ends until it is said in them. The Perfect Grief knew every elegy; the Epitaph is what the elegies were for — the world keeps them as its final diction, and tombs three centuries old are found, on inspection, to be quoting. Endings without them are merely stoppages, and do not take.
nodes.playstyle: Speak endings into force. Conclude anything — creatures, curses, wars, eras — with a sentence, and unmake false endings by pronouncing them unfinished.

abilities.name: Said and Settled
abilities.desc: Pronounce a true ending over anything concluded in fact but not at rest; it ends, wholly, for good.

abilities.name: Not As Written
abilities.desc: Declare a death, defeat, or collapse unfinished; it reverses, because the ending had not been said.

abilities.name: Quoted in Stone
abilities.desc: Every epitaph, eulogy, and last word ever spoken is known to you, with what it concealed.

abilities.name: Era's End
abilities.desc: Conclude an age itself; calendars, on their own, begin again at one.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85, then say the last word over an age the Canon has closed, and feel the world set it down.
Visit the tombs that quote you and correct none of them; what a grave hears, it keeps.
Hold the other copy of your own elegy at last, read it without flinching, and file it unspoken.
Leave one thing eternally unconcluded — a door, a song, a love — so the world remembers what your silence is worth.

nodes.name: The Indelible
nodes.role: Apotheosis — witnessed truth made permanent law
nodes.lore: The Fair Copy was consulted; the Indelible is simply in force. What they have witnessed cannot now be otherwise — not remembered differently, not ruled against, not unwritten by anything that writes. Archives no longer send to them; archives are, by definition, whatever agrees with them. The Lacuna keeps a respectful distance. It is mutual.
nodes.playstyle: See it, and it is settled. Your witness locks reality against revision; fight by fixing the field's truths faster than enemies can lie about them.

abilities.name: Force of Record
abilities.desc: Whatever you witness becomes unalterable fact; no illusion, rewrite, erasure, or godly appeal stands against your seeing.

abilities.name: Adverse Testimony
abilities.desc: Recite a creature's true history aloud; it loses every power founded on a lie, permanently.

abilities.name: The Whole Answer
abilities.desc: Any person may ask you what truly happened, once in their life, and receive the answer whole.

abilities.name: Witness Everlasting
abilities.desc: Your memories persist past your death as a place scholars may visit; the office admits one visitor at a time.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85, then witness something a god denies, and hold the record until the god amends.
Become the standard: let the archives stop citing you and start being measured against you, and do not visit them again.
Keep the respectful distance. What the Lacuna holds and what you hold must never meet, and both of you know why.
Witness one kindness with the same finality you gave the atrocities, so the permanent record is not only wounds.

nodes.name: The Acclamation
nodes.role: Apotheosis — sovereignty by the crowd's roar
nodes.lore: Crowns are fitted in private and confirmed in squares, and the confirmation has become a person. The Acclamation is the roar itself, holding office wherever the many decide as one; kings date their reigns from its sound and their abdications from its absence. Constitutional scholars have proposed writing this down. The squares decline.
nodes.playstyle: Rule nothing; ratify everything. Crown and uncrown by massed voice, arrive wherever the many gather, and make legitimacy itself a sound you can withhold.

abilities.name: By Acclaim
abilities.desc: Raise any willing person to any office with the crowd's roar; the world treats the elevation as lawful.

abilities.name: Withdrawn Consent
abilities.desc: Fall silent toward a ruler; their commands lose force by degrees until even their guards merely watch them speak.

abilities.name: Every Square at Once
abilities.desc: Be present in every gathering of the many simultaneously; disperse one, and you remain in all the others.

abilities.name: The Roar
abilities.desc: Loose the assembled voice of a city as force; gates, walls, and shield-lines are argued out of the way.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85, then be the sound a coronation waits for, in a city you have never entered, and choose whether it comes.
Uncrown a good king once, because the many were wrong and had the right to be; carry what that teaches.
Decline, permanently, the Kingmakers' standing offer of dinner.
Become the absence too: teach the squares that your silence is a verdict, so that no tyrant ever again mistakes quiet for consent.

families.name: Corsair
families.tagline: Violence with a tide table.
families.description: The Corsair works the coasts the way a factor works a market: with a tide table, a powder budget, and no illusions about partners. The sea is a business associate with moods — generous, then murderous, then generous again. Corsairs have been rich twice and drowned once, and they hold both events against nobody. Their craft is violence, scheduled.

nodes.name: Corsair
nodes.role: Melee skirmisher — opportunist burst and mobility
nodes.lore: Every harbor with bad lighting keeps a few: deckhands who noticed that cargo pays better before it clears customs. A first-rank corsair owns a knife, a coil of rope, and a working respect for the tide. The sea has not decided about them yet. Neither, officially, has the law.
nodes.playstyle: Hit fast, in daylight, where the cargo is. Swing on ropes, fight dirty, and leave before anyone agrees on what happened.

abilities.name: Boarding Hook
abilities.desc: Hurl a hooked line 12 meters and haul yourself along it; arriving on an enemy staggers them and opens your next strike.

abilities.name: Powder Kiss
abilities.desc: Fire a point-blank pistol shot that blinds with smoke; deals double damage to targets already engaged with you.

abilities.name: Sea Legs
abilities.desc: Rolling terrain, rigging, and rails never slow you; you fight at full speed on any surface that moves.

abilities.name: Danger Money
abilities.desc: While outnumbered, every hit you land returns a little health and stamina; the rate improves with each additional enemy.

progressionSteps: Sign aboard any ship that asks few questions, and learn the tide tables before you learn the crew's names.
Survive your first storm on deck, not below; the sea remembers who watched.
Take your first prize in daylight, flag up, and count the take honestly in front of the whole crew.
Be drowned once — briefly. What you say to the water while it holds you is between you and it.

nodes.name: Boardswain
nodes.role: Melee assault — gap-close and opening burst
nodes.lore: Boardswains hold the rank the way a boatswain holds ropes: as the whole point. They are the first party over the rail, chosen for speed, nerve, and a documented indifference to falling. Merchant captains describe them to insurers in the past tense. The title is spoken with a straight face; the work isn't.
nodes.playstyle: Open every fight by arriving somewhere inconvenient. Chain grapples into strikes, keep momentum stacking, and end the boarding before the bell finds its rope.

abilities.name: Away Boarders
abilities.desc: Leap 15 meters to an enemy position; allies following within 3 seconds arrive with the same staggering impact.

abilities.name: Running Rigging
abilities.desc: Each grapple, swing, or vault grants momentum; spend 3 stacks to strike twice in one motion.

abilities.name: Before the Bell
abilities.desc: If no enemy has raised an alarm, your first strike on each target deals 40% bonus damage.

abilities.name: Teeth and Steel
abilities.desc: Clench a knife in your teeth while both hands work rope; you stay armed mid-swing, and swinging strikes cannot be parried.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10 and be first over a defended rail three times; the crew counts, and the crew does not round up.
Board a ship whose rail stands higher than your mast, and be waiting at the wheel when your captain arrives.
Fall between two hulls in a fight and climb back aboard the enemy's. Which ship you climb is the examination.
Take a prize so fast the log cannot name the hour; let the enemy's own bell, unrung, stand witness.

nodes.name: Saltwise
nodes.role: Skirmish support — foresight, positioning, weather edges
nodes.lore: Saltwise is what a crew calls the hand who says shorten sail an hour before the captain does, and is right. They read water the way rangers read ground — and are cheerfully useless a mile inland. The rank is not granted. It accumulates, voyage by voyage, like salt in a rope.
nodes.playstyle: Fight the conditions, not the enemy. Call swells, gusts, and footing before they happen, so your side is always standing where the sea helps.

abilities.name: Read the Water
abilities.desc: Study the surface to reveal currents, shoals, and anything swimming; allies gain movement speed along routes you call.

abilities.name: Glass Falling
abilities.desc: Call an incoming squall before the sky admits it; when it lands, braced allies hold footing while enemies stagger and slide.

abilities.name: Mast Coin
abilities.desc: Nail a coin to the mast at battle's start; once, a killing blow against any ally lands as a graze instead.

abilities.name: Tide Table
abilities.desc: You always know the tide, the moon, and the hour; abilities that depend on timing recharge 20% faster.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10 and call the weather right thirty days running; the thirty-first day, the helmsman asks you first.
Bring a ship through a strait at night by sound and swell alone, hands never leaving the rail.
Taste bottom-mud from the lead and name the coast blindfolded. Any coast. The sea has a finite number of flavors, and you know them.
Refuse an easy landing you cannot explain your unease about, and be right by morning.

nodes.name: Knifegrin
nodes.role: Shock striker — fear-driven melee burst
nodes.lore: The grin is literal: a knife held in the teeth leaves the mouth free to smile. Knifegrins study terror as a boarding tool — the scream timed to the swing, the pause on the rail in full view. Rogues work unseen; a Knifegrin's whole craft is being seen too late to matter.
nodes.playstyle: Arrive loudly and first. Feed on enemy fear: every foe who breaks or freezes fuels your next hit. Kill the brave ones early; the rest follow.

abilities.name: The Pause on the Rail
abilities.desc: Stand in full view for 2 seconds before engaging; enemies who watched suffer reduced accuracy against you all fight.

abilities.name: Blade-in-Teeth
abilities.desc: While your knife is clenched and visible, enemies below half health must check morale before attacking you.

abilities.name: Pick the Brave One
abilities.desc: Mark the steadiest enemy; killing your mark panics every foe who could see them fall.

abilities.name: Faster Than the Bell
abilities.desc: If you down an enemy within 6 seconds of engaging, the fight's alarm never sounds: reinforcements do not come.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and take a ship where no shot is fired after yours; terror must finish what powder introduces.
Learn to smile with a knife in your teeth. Practice on a mirror until the mirror is the one unsettled.
Board alone, in daylight, announced. If the crew still fights, you were not ready. Recover, and be louder.
Have your grin described, inaccurately and worse, in three ports you have never visited.

nodes.name: Slowmatch
nodes.role: Demolitionist — timed charges, area burst
nodes.lore: Slowmatches carry fire the way clerks carry ink: measured, budgeted, and always lit. They speak of hulls in ounces of powder and doors in seconds of cord. A good one boards with six charges and returns with one, having spent the other five like an apology — brief, loud, and final.
nodes.playstyle: Plan the fight in fuses. Place charges during the chaos your allies make, then collect the field in one rolling detonation, timed to the second.

abilities.name: Measured Ounce
abilities.desc: Set a shaped charge sized exactly to its target; structures breach, doors open, and nothing behind them is scratched.

abilities.name: Grenado
abilities.desc: Lob a fused iron grenado; it detonates on your count, not on impact, and you are always right.

abilities.name: Rolling Fuse
abilities.desc: Link up to four charges on one cord; they fire in sequence, herding survivors toward the last one.

abilities.name: Burnt Fingers
abilities.desc: Snuff any explosive, yours or theirs, bare-handed; you take minor fire damage and always think it was worth it.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and apprentice under a gunner with eight fingers; the missing two are the curriculum.
Cut a hundred fuses to a hundred counts and be wrong by less than a breath, total.
Open a strongroom through the hull beside it without waking the man asleep against the door.
Carry a lit slow-match through a powder magazine at a walk. The rank is the walk.

nodes.name: Weathereye
nodes.role: Forecaster support — vision, initiative, prediction
nodes.lore: A Weathereye reads the sky like a bill of lading: what's arriving, what it's carrying, and for whom. They take no credit for storms — the storm was coming anyway; they merely booked the good seats. Navies keep one on retainer and pretend it is for morale.
nodes.playstyle: Play two minutes ahead. Reveal what the enemy will do, position allies for weather that hasn't arrived, and take polite credit afterward.

abilities.name: Bill of Lading
abilities.desc: Read an enemy group like cargo: reveal their numbers, condition, and which one is carrying the thing worth taking.

abilities.name: Falling Glass
abilities.desc: Predict the field's next hazard aloud; allies gain evasion against it, and your accuracy rises while the prediction stands.

abilities.name: Weather Gauge
abilities.desc: Take the weather gauge: while your side holds the wind, your ranged attacks reach farther and theirs fall short.

abilities.name: Sailor's Warning
abilities.desc: Mark one enemy ability you have seen before; the next time it begins, everyone on your side knows.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and log a full year of dawns; the examiners read only the mornings you got wrong.
Predict the hour a hurricane makes landfall from three days out, and anchor your own ship on the strength of it.
Outsail a naval squadron using nothing but cloud, current, and their captain's impatience.
Refuse to explain how you knew, once, to someone important. The rank includes the silence.

nodes.name: Caulborn
nodes.role: Luck skirmisher — probability edges, death defiance
nodes.lore: Born behind the caul, sailors say, and the sea may not drown you; Caulborn corsairs test the clause professionally. Dice fall kindly near them, ropes fray elsewhere, and musket balls arrive slightly used. None of it is magic. It is favor — earned, the Caulborn insist, though none can say when.
nodes.playstyle: Court variance. Your numbers wobble where others' hold steady — and the wobble loves you. Push every long shot; the odds are lying in your favor.

abilities.name: Kind Dice
abilities.desc: Any failed critical chance rerolls once per attack; the reroll improves the worse the fight is going.

abilities.name: Frayed Elsewhere
abilities.desc: Once per battle, an attack that should hit you finds a reason not to: a stumble, a gust, a misfire.

abilities.name: Caul Clause
abilities.desc: You cannot drown, and any death by falling into water becomes instead a rescue, eventually, by something.

abilities.name: Spilled Salt
abilities.desc: Enemies adjacent to you suffer small mishaps: jams, slips, dropped guards. Individually explicable. Statistically damning.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and survive three deaths the crew has already mourned; attend your own wakes politely.
Win a coin toss eleven times running in front of witnesses, then decline the twelfth. Knowing when to decline is the rank.
Be the only survivor of something, once. Do not enjoy it. The sea checks.
Carry your caul, or buy one honestly from a midwife; the sea has never once checked the paperwork.

nodes.name: Noonflag
nodes.role: Terror controller — mass surrender, bloodless victory
nodes.lore: The Noonflag order hoists its colors at midday, in plain sight, with hours of sea room left to run. This is arithmetic, not mercy: a crew given every chance to flee and choosing surrender empties no more powder. Their prizes arrive unbloodied and their reputation does the boarding. Quarterless captains call them soft, carefully.
nodes.playstyle: Win the fight before it files itself as one. Stack dread, offer exits, and punish only the ones who refuse both. Bodies mean you played badly.

abilities.name: Colors at Noon
abilities.desc: Announce yourself to the field; every enemy who can see your flag loses damage for each escape route left open.

abilities.name: Strike Your Colors
abilities.desc: Offer terms mid-battle; enemies below half morale lay down arms and are removed from the fight as surrendered, not slain.

abilities.name: Sea Room
abilities.desc: Open an escape corridor; enemies who take it cannot return, and each departure demoralizes those who stayed.

abilities.name: The Price of Refusing
abilities.desc: Your first strike against any enemy who declined surrender deals triple damage, in front of everyone.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and take seven prizes in a season without a death on either ledger; the order audits both.
Sail into a harbor that has heard of you, flag up, and buy your supplies at fair prices from people who watch your hands.
Accept a surrender you wanted to refuse. The one you wanted to refuse is the examination.
Receive the noon colors from a captain who has never once fired first, and never once needed to.

nodes.name: Powder Surgeon
nodes.role: Precision demolitionist — surgical burst, structure removal
nodes.lore: Powder Surgeons open ships the way jewelers open lockets: to a diagram, ounce by ounce, sparing what must keep working. A prize sunk is a fee declined. They carry instruments in velvet rolls — drills, cords, brass scales — and despise the Hellburners as butchers who happen to own matches.
nodes.playstyle: Remove exactly what the fight requires: this mast, that gate, the third gun. Small charges, exact seconds, zero collateral. Your explosions have edges.

abilities.name: Charge to the Grain
abilities.desc: Place a charge weighed to the grain; it destroys its stated target completely and nothing else, ever.

abilities.name: Take It Intact
abilities.desc: Disable a mechanism, mount, or construct without destroying it; your side may use it once repaired.

abilities.name: Sounding Knock
abilities.desc: Rap a hull or wall to map its weak lines; your next charge there is half-cost and full-effect.

abilities.name: Ounce of Prevention
abilities.desc: Detonate an enemy's own powder store from a distance, having quietly under-fused it earlier in the fight.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and present a taken ship to the order with every deck intact and the strongroom door on its hinges, open.
Sink nothing for a year. The year resets if you are seen enjoying an explosion beyond professional satisfaction.
Blow the chains off a prisoner without bruising the wrists. The order provides volunteers; the volunteers are all senior surgeons.
Decline, in writing, an invitation from the Hellburners. Keep the reply courteous; you will meet their work again on the water.

nodes.name: Stormbroker
nodes.role: Weather tactician — forecast warfare, battlefield control
nodes.lore: Stormbrokers do not raise weather; they schedule engagements inside it. A commission names the prize, and the Stormbroker names the hour the gale will hold the prize's harbor shut. They speak of hurricanes the way factors speak of difficult but reliable colleagues. No magic is involved. Somehow this is worse.
nodes.playstyle: Fight where the forecast says to. Arrive with the squall at your back, leave inside the rain, and make the sky read like your battle plan.

abilities.name: Scheduled Gale
abilities.desc: If battle begins in weather you forecast aloud beforehand, allies gain initiative and enemies begin the fight drenched, deafened, and late.

abilities.name: Lee Shore Appointment
abilities.desc: Herd an enemy toward the coast for 10 seconds; wind and current cooperate, having been consulted in advance.

abilities.name: Difficult Colleague
abilities.desc: Call in the squall line early; a wall of wind and rain crosses the field on your side's schedule.

abilities.name: Act of Weather
abilities.desc: Damage your enemies take from weather is recorded as no one's fault; it bypasses armor, wards, and litigation.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and deliver three fleets to three storms on time; the storms' punctuality will be credited to you. Accept the credit.
Sit out a season's richest prize because the sky said no. The order confirms every refusal against the wrecks of those who went.
Negotiate — that is the word the rank insists on — with a hurricane, by sailing its edge for six days and never once being surprised.
Hand a rival captain a true forecast and watch them distrust it into their own wreck. File this under instruction, not malice.

nodes.name: Deepwager
nodes.role: Gambler striker — staked power, all-or-nothing spikes
nodes.lore: Deepwagers hold that luck unspent is luck insulted. They stake real things — blood, fingers, the ship, their own unfinished drowning — and play for outcomes no plan could purchase. Tithesmen call this robbing a patient partner. Deepwagers agree, and observe that the sea keeps dealing them in.
nodes.playstyle: Bet the fight on the fight. Ante health, gear, and position for doubled outcomes; fold early when the table turns. Never play sober odds — anyone can do that.

abilities.name: Blood Ante
abilities.desc: Stake a quarter of your health at combat's start; land the first blow and it returns doubled.

abilities.name: Double or Drown
abilities.desc: Declare double stakes on your next ability: twice the effect on success, and on failure the sea briefly collects you instead.

abilities.name: The Folded Hand
abilities.desc: Concede an exchange deliberately: take the hit, bank the insult, and gain guaranteed success on your next wager.

abilities.name: Drowned Man's Dice
abilities.desc: Roll bone dice mid-combat; on doubles, your cooldowns clear; on snake eyes, so do the enemy's. Roll anyway.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and win a ship on a single cut of the cards, having staked your own; sail your winnings home.
Lose everything once, completely, and pay without a word. The order watches the paying, not the losing.
Stake your unfinished drowning against a storm's crossing and arrive dry. Do not ask what the sea would have won.
Teach a Tithesman to play cards. Take everything except the coin they nailed to the mast. Leave that; you are not a fool.

nodes.name: Quarterless
nodes.role: Executioner — kill-chain momentum, area dread
nodes.lore: The Quarterless fly red and mean it. Their doctrine is older than the order: mercy is a tax every future prize collects, and one annihilated crew buys a hundred bloodless surrenders — for other people. They believe they perform the Noonflag's arithmetic honestly, at the bloody end where it balances. Ports pay them to exist elsewhere.
nodes.playstyle: Momentum is the weapon. Every kill accelerates the next; hesitation resets you. Leave one witness per engagement — the doctrine is strict about the arithmetic.

abilities.name: Red Colors
abilities.desc: Hoist the no-quarter flag: your side's damage rises, and no enemy may surrender, flee, or be healed past half.

abilities.name: The Next Is Faster
abilities.desc: Each kill grants attack and movement speed for 8 seconds; the stacks cap where your conscience should be.

abilities.name: One Witness
abilities.desc: Designate one enemy who cannot be harmed by anyone; when all their allies are dead, they are released to talk.

abilities.name: No Quarter Asked
abilities.desc: While below half health you deal the same bonus damage you would take; the doctrine cuts both ways.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and take the red flag from a Quarterless captain's body; the order has no other ceremony of succession.
Erase a pirate-hunter crew to the last name but one, and choose the one for the story they will tell.
Refuse a surrender you wanted to accept. The one you wanted to accept is the examination.
Read the Noonflag ledgers of prizes taken without blood, and understand exactly whose blood pre-paid them. Do not argue. Sail.

nodes.name: Hellburner
nodes.role: Area denial — walls of fire, zone control
nodes.lore: Hellburners hold that a ship is temporary and a lesson is not. Their craft is the fireship, the drifting magazine, the harbor that stops insuring itself. Where Powder Surgeons bill by the prize, Hellburners are paid by the absence: shipping lanes empty on rumor alone. Each carries their own pyre aboard, pre-rigged, as doctrine.
nodes.playstyle: Turn the field into a cost nobody will pay. Lay fire in walls and drifts, herd enemies with heat, and never plan a retreat you'd mourn.

abilities.name: Fireship
abilities.desc: Convert any vessel, cart, or construct into a drifting bomb that steers itself toward the largest enemy cluster.

abilities.name: Herding Fire
abilities.desc: Ignite lines of fire that move: the burn advances a meter per second in the direction you swept your arm.

abilities.name: Drifting Magazine
abilities.desc: Set a slow-drifting powder cache alight; enemies must scatter or share its final opinion.

abilities.name: Pre-Rigged
abilities.desc: When reduced to zero health, you detonate everything you have placed, and are found later, somehow, singed and swimming.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and ride your first fireship to the point of no return, then past it, then swim.
Cut loose a fortune in captured cargo and light it where its owners can watch. The lesson is the invoice.
Sleep aboard your own pre-rigged pyre for a season without once checking the fuses. Doctrine calls this faith. Insurers call it something else.
Watch the Powder Surgeons take a prize intact, and feel nothing but patience. Everything is kindling eventually; professionals can wait.

nodes.name: Graveyard Pilot
nodes.role: Terrain controller — hazard mastery, pursuit denial
nodes.lore: Every coast keeps a graveyard — the reef, the bar, the strait that eats keels — and every graveyard keeps a Pilot who uses it as a private road. Pursuit follows them in exactly once. Stormbrokers weaponize the sky; Pilots hold that the weapon is beneath them, and the road is not.
nodes.playstyle: Make geography pick sides. Lead allies through hazards at full speed, lure pursuers into water that finishes your arguments, and never fight where you stand — fight where they sink.

abilities.name: Private Road
abilities.desc: Allies you lead ignore terrain hazards and difficult ground while following within 10 meters of your path.

abilities.name: Follow Me In
abilities.desc: Mark a hazard as inviting; the next enemy to pursue you across it takes its full, undivided attention.

abilities.name: By the Mark
abilities.desc: Sound the depth aloud; for 8 seconds your side knows exactly where footing, cover, and drowning begin.

abilities.name: The Once
abilities.desc: Escape any engagement through terrain that closes behind you; each enemy may be taught this lesson only once, which suffices.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and take a laden ship through the Teethwater at night, on a falling tide, and gain the harbor by dawn.
Chart nothing. Your graveyard lives in your hands and inner ear; paper is how other people's heirs find it.
Lead a warship in and come out alone. Answer the inquiry with the tide tables, and be acquitted by arithmetic.
Memorize the wrecks by name and cargo. You will be sailing over your predecessors; know whom to thank.

nodes.name: Tithesman
nodes.role: Fortune warden — luck insurance, paid guarantees
nodes.lore: Tithesmen keep the old accounts: a share of every prize over the side, rum for the crossing, silence at the rail for the drowned. In return the sea is punctual with them, and lethal coincidence books elsewhere. Deepwagers sneer that favor bought is favor rented. Tithesmen pay that no mind, and pay everything else precisely.
nodes.playstyle: Spend resources to remove chance. Pay gold, gear, and your own share to guarantee crits, cancel enemy luck, and keep the crew inside the sea's goodwill.

abilities.name: The Sea's Share
abilities.desc: Cast a share of your gold into the water; the fight's next three attacks by your side cannot miss or misfire.

abilities.name: Paid in Full
abilities.desc: Cancel one enemy critical hit, dodge, or lucky escape per battle; a wet handprint marks where their luck used to stand.

abilities.name: Rum for the Crossing
abilities.desc: Pour a measure over the rail; allies gain resistance to drowning, despair, and cold for ten minutes.

abilities.name: Punctual Tide
abilities.desc: Once per day, the tide does exactly what your plan requires, at the minute your plan requires it.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and tithe the sea a fortune in front of a crew that thinks you mad, then bring that crew home through what sinks the thrifty.
Learn the full rite: the share, the rum, the silence, the coin beneath the mast. Omit nothing. The sea audits.
Keep the observances a full year aboard a ship of scoffers; by year's end, let the scoffers be doing them too.
Bury a drowned stranger with his name spoken and his pockets full. What washes ashore afterward is yours by custom.

nodes.name: The Black Sail
nodes.role: Mythic dread — surrender at sight
nodes.lore: Histories dispute whether the Black Sail is a ship, a captain, or a standing arrangement between the two. Sightings are better documented than battles, since there are no battles: convoys strike colors to a silhouette, and insurers pay out on testimony of weather. Forty years of prizes; the confirmed casualty list names one man, who fell down a hatch.
nodes.playstyle: Stop fighting; start appearing. Your presence is the ability. Engagements resolve in your favor when enemies can see you, and they can always see you.

abilities.name: Silhouette
abilities.desc: Appear on any horizon the enemy checks; while visible, enemy morale drains and no enemy buff can be maintained.

abilities.name: Colors Answered
abilities.desc: Any enemy group that can see your flag must vote on surrender every 10 seconds; abstentions count in favor.

abilities.name: The Casualty List
abilities.desc: Battles you enter without a death stay that way: killing blows on either side land as capture instead.

abilities.name: Compound Reputation
abilities.desc: Prizes taken without blood add permanent dread to your silhouette; veterans surrender fastest, having heard the most.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and take a treasure fleet without a shot; let the escort's log read only 'sail sighted, colors struck, weather fine.'
Be reported in two oceans in the same week, and correct neither report.
Sail past a port you once spared, and watch it surrender anyway. Send back their keys with a tide table.
Retire, verifiably, in front of witnesses. When the sightings continue anyway, you hold the rank.

nodes.name: The Narrow Thunder
nodes.role: Mythic precision — fortress-opening singular detonations
nodes.lore: Histories record the works and dispute the hand: the sea-fort of Carrent opened along one seam; a chain-boom parted at the link its maker doubted; a flagship surrendered to a bang no louder than a dropped book. The Narrow Thunder is what gunners call the idea that an explosion can be aimed like a needle. Somewhere, the idea has hands.
nodes.playstyle: One charge per problem, one problem per battle. Spend long setup for absolute results: what you detonate is deleted, and nothing beside it notices.

abilities.name: The Doubted Link
abilities.desc: Identify the one component holding an enemy formation, fortress, or plan together; your next charge is placed there.

abilities.name: No Louder Than a Book
abilities.desc: Your detonations make exactly as much sound as you allot them, including none; the damage is unrelated to the noise.

abilities.name: One Seam
abilities.desc: Destroy any single structure, gate, ward, or engine outright; everything within arm's reach of it survives untouched.

abilities.name: Grain Budget
abilities.desc: Your charges cost half powder against targets studied for 10 seconds; thrift, weaponized.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and open a fortress the siege-engineers had priced at a year, before their invoice clears.
Detonate a charge in a crowded market that harms one lock and nothing else. The order calls this the graduation; magistrates call it impossible.
Be blamed for lightning twice and thunder once, in writing, by people who watched you do it.
Refuse to write the method down. Apprentices learn it from your hands or not at all; the world is not ready to be this openable.

nodes.name: Squallmonger
nodes.role: Mythic forecaster — storms kept on retainer
nodes.lore: Histories argue whether the Squallmonger predicts weather or the weather consults them; both camps cite the same eleven engagements, each fought in impossible convenience. Gales arrive on their invoices. Fog lifts for their broadsides and closes for their exits. Admirals hire weather-clerks in self-defense; the clerks resign after reading the logs.
nodes.playstyle: Sell the sky's schedule to the fight. Every engagement opens in conditions you chose from a menu, and the menu keeps getting longer.

abilities.name: Menu of Skies
abilities.desc: Choose the weather any battle begins in from conditions you have personally survived; you have survived nearly everything.

abilities.name: Invoice the Gale
abilities.desc: Book a gale to arrive within the hour; it keeps the appointment, works the enemy flank, and leaves nothing in writing.

abilities.name: Convenient Fog
abilities.desc: Fog lifts where you aim and thickens where you retreat; enemies experience this as persecution, correctly.

abilities.name: Professional Courtesy
abilities.desc: Storms do not strike your ship, your crew, or your prizes; colleagues do not bill colleagues.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and win an engagement the almanac calls impossible, in weather that existed only over your half of the water.
Quote a hurricane's route to the day, publish it, and be wrong in exactly the ports that refused your fee.
Retire a naval squadron without firing: three appointments with three storms, all kept, none survived. The logs must call it weather; the admiralty won't.
Meet the Sorcerer's storm at sea — the one with blood in it — and tip your hat as it passes you by. It knows a colleague.

nodes.name: All Hands
nodes.role: Mythic gambler — impossible odds, total reversals
nodes.lore: The phrase means two things at sea: every sailor to the ropes, or every sailor to the bottom. All Hands is the gambler who has been both meanings. Histories cite the wreck of the Gilded Gull, lost with all hands — and the fifty players of its final card game, ashore by dawn, rich, and unable to explain the boat.
nodes.playstyle: Go all-in as a lifestyle. Your worst positions hold your best outcomes: the closer your side stands to lost, the harder your reversals hit.

abilities.name: Both Meanings
abilities.desc: While any ally is downed, all your wagers succeed automatically; the sea respects a table with real stakes.

abilities.name: The Final Game
abilities.desc: Challenge a stronger enemy to stakes they cannot decline; winner takes the loser's next ten minutes.

abilities.name: Ashore by Dawn
abilities.desc: When your side would be lost with all hands, you are all instead ashore by dawn, once per campaign, minus the boat.

abilities.name: Dead Even
abilities.desc: Equalize: set both sides' chances to exactly even, ignoring numbers, wounds, and sense. Then play your luck.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and stake everything you have ever won on one hand, against the sea, in a storm, and win.
Be lost with all hands. The step is written in the past tense for a reason nobody applying for the rank enjoys.
Give your winnings away entire, twice, to prove to the table that it was never about the money. The sea checks this one personally.
Play the Final Game against someone the histories say you cannot beat, and let fifty witnesses fail to agree afterward on what you wagered.

nodes.name: The Red Wake
nodes.role: Mythic slaughter — unstoppable momentum, fleet execution
nodes.lore: The histories agree a ship leaves a red wake; they disagree on when it began and why it never ends. Fleets that catch the Red Wake report nothing afterward, which is the report. One witness per engagement, the doctrine ran; the legend keeps the ledger current. Ports it passes declare mourning in advance, to save time.
nodes.playstyle: Never stop moving, never stop killing. Your momentum outlasts fleets: each engagement funds the next, and the wake behind you does half the work.

abilities.name: The Wake Runs Red
abilities.desc: Your kill-momentum no longer decays between fights, between days, or between wars.

abilities.name: Nothing Afterward
abilities.desc: Engagements you finish yield the enemy nothing: no logs, no lessons, no survivors past the one you chose.

abilities.name: Mourning in Advance
abilities.desc: Enemies who have heard of you begin the fight already suffering your first hit's morale cost.

abilities.name: Chosen Witness
abilities.desc: While your chosen witness lives, you cannot be slowed, silenced, or stopped; stories need endings, and you are theirs.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and break a punitive armada sent specifically for you; send its flag home folded, with the one witness carrying it.
Pass a coast at night and find every light already doused, every ship already beached. Accept the tribute of being believed.
Hear a false Red Wake is working your waters, and let the sea learn the difference. The difference should be legible from shore.
Spare, once, a ship full of children and choose to be seen doing it. Terror must have edges, or it is only weather.

nodes.name: The Ash Fleet
nodes.role: Mythic conflagration — fleet-scale fire, denial incarnate
nodes.lore: Port registries disagree on the Ash Fleet's size — one hull, or forty, or none since the night it burned itself as a demonstration. It anchors nowhere, takes nothing, and leaves shipping lanes the color of old campfires. Cities negotiate with its smoke on the horizon. The negotiations are short, and the Fleet's terms are always the same: elsewhere.
nodes.playstyle: Command fire as a formation. Your burns maneuver, screen, and flank like squadrons; the field is yours once everything flammable has picked a side.

abilities.name: Squadron of Flame
abilities.desc: Raise up to four autonomous fires that hold formation, obey signals, and pursue routed enemies with visible enthusiasm.

abilities.name: The Demonstration
abilities.desc: Burn something of your own, publicly; enemy morale breaks twice as fast for the rest of the engagement.

abilities.name: Smoke Negotiations
abilities.desc: Enemies inside your smoke may only retreat or surrender; both options are honored, which surprises them.

abilities.name: The Same Terms
abilities.desc: Designate a zone; anything that remains in it after 10 seconds is claimed by fire that arrives precisely on time.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and burn a blockade of forty hulls with three, at night, upwind, uninsured.
Anchor nowhere for a year. Fleets will report you in six seas; let the reports do the patrolling.
Accept a city's surrender delivered to your smoke, the actual ships being elsewhere. Sign as the Fleet. It is not lying if it burns.
Burn one of your own hulls as the demonstration, with your flag flying, and step ashore while it settles. The legend needs the silhouette.

nodes.name: Fairwater
nodes.role: Mythic pilot — lethal water made road
nodes.lore: Survivors' accounts agree on the wrong details: the reef was there, the chart was right, and the water went flat as poured glass exactly one keel wide. Fairwater is the pilot the graveyards will not take — some say out of respect, some say out of patience. Wreckers hate them. Widows name boats after them.
nodes.playstyle: Carve safe lanes through lethal ground for your whole side. Where you lead, hazards abstain; where you have not led, your enemies are welcome to find out.

abilities.name: One Keel Wide
abilities.desc: Flatten a corridor of calm through any hazard — reef, storm, battlefield — exactly wide enough for those you vouch for.

abilities.name: The Graveyards Abstain
abilities.desc: Environmental damage cannot touch you or allies within your wake; the sea is not done watching you work.

abilities.name: Poured Glass
abilities.desc: Still the water around an enemy vessel instead: becalmed, it drifts wherever the current you chose is going.

abilities.name: Wrecker's Grief
abilities.desc: False lights and lures fail within your sight; those who set them find their own marks moved by morning.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and bring a dismasted hull through the worst water on the chart with the tide against you and the sea, for once, polite.
Walk away from a pilotage worth a fortune because the water felt proud that day. Be right. Be unable to prove it.
Take a hundred ships through your graveyard without a loss, until the underwriters stop pricing the strait and start pricing you.
Refuse to pilot a slaver through, once, in front of witnesses, and let the reef handle the paperwork.

nodes.name: The Undrowned
nodes.role: Mythic constant — undrownable, favor made flesh
nodes.lore: Everyone drowns who stays long enough; the sea is patient and the arithmetic is not close. The Undrowned is the standing exception — paid up, the tithesmen say, in full and in advance, though none can name the sum. Storms part bruisingly around them. Three navies have hanged them. The dates are engraved on the mugs they drink from.
nodes.playstyle: Be the certainty your crew steers by. You do not die at sea, and everything near you dies less; spend the difference loudly.

abilities.name: Sum Unnamed
abilities.desc: You cannot die on, in, or under salt water; the sea declines to elaborate.

abilities.name: Bruising Courtesy
abilities.desc: Storms miss you narrowly and resentfully; whatever they meant for you lands on the nearest enemy instead.

abilities.name: Hanged Thrice
abilities.desc: Execution fails against you at sea or in sight of it; each failure permanently unnerves the executing authority.

abilities.name: Keep the Crew
abilities.desc: Allies aboard your vessel cannot drown while you live, a clause the sea honors and audits.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and be given up for drowned three times by three crews; interrupt each wake at the toast, sea-wet and thirsty.
Complete the great tithe. What it costs is between you and the water, and the water does not discuss its rates.
Go down with a ship, by choice, holding the manifest, and walk out of the surf a week later having delivered it.
Let the navies hang you once more, on a gallows in sight of the sea, and commission the third mug yourself.

nodes.name: The Second Sail
nodes.role: Apotheosis — omnipresent dread, campaigns conceded unfought
nodes.lore: Every lookout knows the moment: a second sail, hull-down at dusk, exactly where the wake was. It does not close and it does not leave. The Black Sail was a ship one could surrender to; the Second Sail is the knowledge that one already has. Admiralties list it as weather. Crews list it in their prayers.
nodes.playstyle: Exist at the edge of every enemy's plan. You are sighted, never engaged; whole campaigns re-route around your possibility, and what re-routes, you own.

abilities.name: Hull-Down
abilities.desc: You occupy every horizon simultaneously; enemies anywhere at sea count as within your dread presence.

abilities.name: Already Surrendered
abilities.desc: Enemy plans made within sight of water begin at half conviction; their retreats are pre-plotted and known to you.

abilities.name: Listed as Weather
abilities.desc: You cannot be targeted, warded against, or negotiated with by anything that classifies you correctly; nothing does.

abilities.name: Sail on the Wake
abilities.desc: Appear behind any fleeing enemy at dusk, exactly once per dusk; whatever they abandon to run faster becomes yours.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and be sighted, the same evening, from every masthead in a hemisphere; sign nothing, sink nothing, collect everything that turns back.
Let the Black Sail rot in a museum harbor while the sightings go on; attend the exhibit, unrecognized, and leave a good review.
Become a clause: when charters promise safe passage 'excepting weather,' be the exception both parties silently mean.
Once a generation, let one ship outrun you. Hope is the sail you fly now; keep it trimmed.

nodes.name: The Flaw
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the weakness in made things
nodes.lore: Masons whisper it, shipwrights curse it, armorers price it in: everything made has a flaw, and the Flaw has a favorite. It is the seam the builder dreamed about, the bolt tightened twice out of doubt. The Narrow Thunder aimed explosions; the Flaw no longer needs them. Attention suffices. Guilds post it apologies in advance.
nodes.playstyle: Look at things until they stop working. Armor, walls, fleets, plans — all of it was assembled, and you are the argument against assembly.

abilities.name: Attention Suffices
abilities.desc: Regard a made thing for 3 seconds; it fails at its weakest point, which you may nominate.

abilities.name: The Builder's Dream
abilities.desc: Learn every structure's secret seam on sight, including those the builder successfully forgot.

abilities.name: Priced In
abilities.desc: Constructed enemies and equipment within your presence operate at 75% effectiveness; engineers can feel you in their teeth.

abilities.name: The Favorite
abilities.desc: Choose one enemy work — a flagship, a citadel, a siege train — per season; by season's end it has quietly come apart.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and retire your instruments; from now on the velvet roll is ceremonial, and the ceremony is for other people's comfort.
Walk an arsenal's length and let nothing explode; restraint is the last calibration, and the loudest thing you will ever do.
Visit the shipyards annually, touching nothing. What the wrights reinforce after you leave was the flaw; they know you know.
Leave one perfect thing alone forever. The histories must record that it was possible to be spared.

nodes.name: The Hired Storm
nodes.role: Apotheosis — weather under standing engagement
nodes.lore: Every sea has one storm the others defer to, and that storm keeps accounts. Cities have paid it off; wars have waited on its availability. Sailors say the Squallmonger finally closed the deal from the other side of the counter — no longer booking weather but taking the bookings. It has never once broken an engagement, and never once explained one.
nodes.playstyle: Be the weather your allies plan around. Arrive as front, fight as squall, depart as rumor; your terms are posted and your schedule is the battle.

abilities.name: Open for Engagements
abilities.desc: Manifest as weather across the entire field: wind, rain, and pressure all answer to your intent while you preside.

abilities.name: Paid Off
abilities.desc: Honor payments: those who have paid you pass beneath you untouched; the receipts outlast their grandchildren.

abilities.name: Availability
abilities.desc: Wars within your waters cannot begin until you accept the booking; refusal has ended three wars unfought.

abilities.name: No Explanations
abilities.desc: You cannot be dispelled, forecast, or attributed; weather-clerks file you under 'seasonal' and say nothing further.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and stop traveling to weather; let weather admit it has been traveling to you. The admission is the ascension.
Take your first booking as a storm: one war, one coast, payment in advance. Keep the appointment so exactly that clocks are set by you afterward.
Refuse a tyrant's fee and rain gently on his fleet for a year, exactly enough to rot the rigging. Patience is also weather.
Keep one small harbor forever calm, unpaid and unexplained. Every storm needs somewhere it is only rain.

nodes.name: The Fool's Wind
nodes.role: Apotheosis — desperate luck made weather
nodes.lore: Old hands teach it grudgingly: there is a wind that favors idiots. It fills the sail nobody trimmed, misses the reef nobody watched for, and arrives precisely when deserving it would be impossible. Wise sailors never feel it. The Fool's Wind was a gambler once, the story runs, and stays fond of anyone playing badly enough to need it.
nodes.playstyle: Bless recklessness, yours and everyone's. The wilder the plan in your presence, the better it works; caution is the only thing you cannot save.

abilities.name: Favors Idiots
abilities.desc: Any ally attempting something with under one-in-ten odds succeeds; the wind keeps its own arithmetic and shows nobody.

abilities.name: The Untrimmed Sail
abilities.desc: Plans abandoned as hopeless complete themselves in your presence: the fire lights, the rope holds, the door was never locked.

abilities.name: To Specification
abilities.desc: Cautious enemies receive no luck at all in your presence: every plan performs exactly to specification, which is never enough.

abilities.name: The Needed Gust
abilities.desc: Once per battle, when all is lost by any sane accounting, the wind arrives; what it does is not your decision anymore.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and stop rolling; the dice fall for other people now. Your stake is permanent, and the table is every sea at once.
Blow gently for a decade on the desperate and the doomed; take no credit, keep no tally, accept no worship you cannot deflect into a drinking song.
Refuse the wise. When the careful admiral begs for one favorable hour, be a flat calm. He chose arithmetic; let them keep each other.
Fill one trimmed sail, once a century, for no reason at all, so the scholars can keep disproving you.

nodes.name: The Closed Sea
nodes.role: Apotheosis — maritime interdiction made law
nodes.lore: Some waters are closed. Not blockaded — closed, the way a court is closed: by an authority nobody elects and everybody obeys. Charts hatch the area in red and cite no statute. The Red Wake ended; the closure it patrolled did not. Insurers exclude it beside war and gods. Ships that enter are not sunk. They are simply not.
nodes.playstyle: Declare regions yours and enforce the declaration by existing. Within your waters you are jurisdiction itself: entry is consent, and consent is unwise.

abilities.name: Waters Closed
abilities.desc: Close the field: for 30 seconds nothing enters or leaves, and everything inside answers to you.

abilities.name: Cite No Statute
abilities.desc: Your authority cannot be dispelled, appealed, or countered, having never been written down anywhere it could be.

abilities.name: Red Hatching
abilities.desc: Mark a zone on the world's charts; enemies who enter it are permanently weakened, beginning with their certainty.

abilities.name: Simply Not
abilities.desc: Once per war, a vessel, company, or engine that violates your waters ceases: no wreck, no record, no argument.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and close your first sea. Fire nothing. Sink nothing. Let the third ship that fails to return draw the boundary for you.
Outlive your ship, your crew, and your description; a law needs no hull. Keep the wake out of habit.
Permit one pilgrimage a year across your water, unharmed, so the closure is read as judgment and never as appetite.
When admiralties finally print the red hatching, sign nothing; boundaries that require signatures can be renegotiated, and yours cannot.

nodes.name: The Ember Tide
nodes.role: Apotheosis — fire as recurring weather
nodes.lore: Certain coasts know a second tide. It comes in on no moon anyone charts, glowing at the waterline, smelling of powder and hot tar. Harbormasters rake their moorings bare and call it maintenance. The Ash Fleet was ships; the Ember Tide is schedule — fire that returns the way water returns, to any shore that forgets it was warned.
nodes.playstyle: Set fires that come back. Your burns ebb, flood, and recur on timetables you publish or withhold; enemies fight the clock, and the clock is yours.

abilities.name: Flood Fire
abilities.desc: Send fire in as a rising tide across the field; it ebbs on your mark and returns stronger each cycle.

abilities.name: No Moon Charted
abilities.desc: Your recurring burns cannot be predicted or warded against; almanacs decline to cover you, citing precedent.

abilities.name: Waterline Glow
abilities.desc: The sea itself carries your embers: any water an enemy crosses may ignite, having been warned first.

abilities.name: Rake the Moorings
abilities.desc: Coasts you have burned once obey you forever: their harbors close, open, or burn again at your low whistle.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and burn the same harbor twice, one year apart to the hour; punctuality is the point, and the warning.
Ebb. Let a decade pass without fire, so the coasts learn the difference between ash and low tide.
Come in glowing on a moonless flood against a fleet at anchor, and leave the anchors. Anchors are how they will remember the ships.
Accept the harbormasters' quiet arrangement: raked moorings, cleared berths, and no questions. Fire that keeps a schedule is due the courtesies of a tide.

nodes.name: The Landfall
nodes.role: Apotheosis — arrival, personified and enforced
nodes.lore: Sailors do not pray for good voyages; they pray for landfall, and something has started answering. Ships past hope raise coasts that were not there at sunset. Harbor bells ring for hulls the harbor never saw. Fairwater stopped taking ships through, the pilots say, and became the through. Every chart's last line now means someone.
nodes.playstyle: End journeys on your terms. Allies always arrive — somewhere, intact, together; enemies discover that arrival is a privilege you administer.

abilities.name: Raise the Coast
abilities.desc: Grant a desperate ally instant safe arrival: they are removed from danger and set down at the nearest defensible shore.

abilities.name: Bells for the Unseen
abilities.desc: Allies who would die at sea instead wash ashore alive, eventually, with a story they decline to tell.

abilities.name: No Arrival
abilities.desc: Declare an enemy voyage incomplete: their fleet remains at sea, provisioned but shoreless, until they abandon the campaign.

abilities.name: Chart's End
abilities.desc: Wherever you stand becomes, for one hour, a friendly port: repairs, rest, and resupply attend your side.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and be prayed to by name, correctly, by a crew you have never met; answer by existing where they needed a coast.
Bring home a ship the sea had fairly won. Do it once, apologize to the water, and do not make a habit of theft.
Refuse a landfall, once, to a hull full of plague, and hold it at sea gently until it is only a hull. Arrival is a judgment; render it.
Let the Ferryman keep the far crossings; yours is the near shore, the bell, and the breakfast after. Guard the difference jealously.

nodes.name: The Seventh Wave
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the sea settling accounts
nodes.lore: Count the swells: old hands swear the seventh runs largest, and older hands swear it chooses.
