It lifts the tithed hull over the bar and opens beneath the one that never paid — same water, same minute, ancient distinction. The Undrowned went under at last, the story runs, and came up as the wave itself: the sea, settling accounts by hand.
nodes.playstyle: Arrive seventh. Judge every hull, crew, and cause by what it has paid the water, then deliver the sea's answer in person, at scale.

abilities.name: The Count
abilities.desc: Combat runs in counts of seven around you; the seventh beat of any exchange belongs entirely to your side.

abilities.name: Over the Bar
abilities.desc: Lift an allied vessel, party, or cause past an impassable obstacle on one great swell, arriving intact and slightly blessed.

abilities.name: Opens Beneath
abilities.desc: Open the water under an enemy who has wronged the sea; the sea keeps its own list and shares it with you.

abilities.name: The Weighing
abilities.desc: Once per age, weigh a fleet against its conduct: the deserving float; the rest the sea keeps. Survivors say the wave read names.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and go under for the last time, mid-count, with the whole tithe paid; what surfaces on the seventh is the rank.
Learn the sea's list. Not its grievances — its accounts. You will find your own name there, marked settled, in your own hand.
Break over one harbor that cheated its sailors for a generation, once, at the height of market day, and recede without a second stroke.
Lift more than you drown. The old partnership holds even now: the sea is a business, and business needs the boats coming back.

families.name: Wizard
families.tagline: Every word costs a decade; speak carefully.
families.description: Wizards are not born to power; they purchase it, syllable by syllable, across decades of candlelit study. To them magic is a language older than the world that speaks it, with a grammar that punishes error in blood. Where others sing or borrow, the wizard conjugates. Each year in the archives adds another word no living rival can pronounce.

nodes.name: Wizard
nodes.role: Ranged caster — versatile, preparation-driven damage
nodes.lore: Every tower, hedge-school, and archive keeps a few: apprentices who traded their youth for letters. A wizard at first rank owns little — a copied grimoire, a stub of candle, three words that reliably work. The world calls them scholars until the third word lands. Then it calls them carefully.
nodes.playstyle: Prepare the right spells before the fight, then spend them precisely. Fragile and slow to ready, devastating when the situation matches the page you memorized.

abilities.name: Candle Logic
abilities.desc: Kindle a small, obedient flame that deals modest fire damage and never spreads beyond the word that lit it.

abilities.name: Inkbound Ward
abilities.desc: Trace a warding sentence midair that absorbs the next hit; the ward breaks into legible fragments enemies find briefly blinding.

abilities.name: Apprentice's Rebuttal
abilities.desc: Interrupt an enemy casting by mispronouncing it back at them; weak spells fizzle, strong ones merely stutter.

abilities.name: Recitation
abilities.desc: Recite memorized passages to restore mana over six seconds; taking damage forces you to start the page again.

progressionSteps: Learn your letters twice — once for men, once for the older things that listen beneath them.
Copy a dead wizard's grimoire by hand until your errors stop being errors.
Speak your first true word aloud, and survive being understood.
Swear the Candle Oath: study before sleep, accuracy before ambition, and never lend out your name.

nodes.name: Convoker
nodes.role: Ranged nuker — elemental burst and area denial
nodes.lore: Convokers choose the loud grammar: fire, frost, storm, and stone — the four dialects the material world speaks about itself. They are summoned to break sieges and end droughts, and paid to leave quickly. The Convocation grants the rank only to those the elements have answered by name, at least once each.
nodes.playstyle: Rotate four elemental dialects against resistances, earning short empowerments when you alternate. Loud, position-hungry casting that trades personal safety for overwhelming area damage.

abilities.name: Fire's First Name
abilities.desc: Speak the flame's birth-name to detonate a burning zone; enemies already ignited take double the blast.

abilities.name: Bedrock Clause
abilities.desc: Command the ground to object, erupting a stone rampart that launches and staggers whatever stood upon it.

abilities.name: Voltaic Refrain
abilities.desc: Repeat a thunder-word three times; each repetition forks lightning to one additional target at growing damage.

abilities.name: Hail Imperative
abilities.desc: Order the sky downward, dropping a slow-marching column of frost that chills everything it crosses, then shatters.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10 and address each of the four elements by its birth-name, without flattery and without flinching.
Stand in a mountain storm and correct its grammar; leave only when it thunders in the tense you chose.
Carry a live coal, a hailstone, an unspent bolt, and a fistful of grave-earth through the Convocation doors.
Answer the examiners in all four dialects while your own notes burn on the lectern.

nodes.name: Deepscribe
nodes.role: Battlefield controller — zones, wards, stolen tempo
nodes.lore: Deepscribes go down instead of out — past the elements, into the Undertext: the writing beneath the world that fixes where things are and when. Archives quarter them apart from other students. Their margins fill with runes that itch to be true, and their letters sometimes arrive before being sent.
nodes.playstyle: Shape the fight before it starts: inscribe traps, fold distances, tax enemy time. Weak in a fair exchange, so arrange that no exchange is fair.

abilities.name: Footnote
abilities.desc: Inscribe a rune in the field's margin; the first enemy to cross it triggers a rooting annotation.

abilities.name: Folded Footnote
abilities.desc: Crease the space between two points and step across; the fold snaps shut behind you, clipping pursuers.

abilities.name: Borrowed Minute
abilities.desc: Lift sixty seconds from an enemy's future; they slow now and stagger when the debt comes due.

abilities.name: Undertext Ward
abilities.desc: Rewrite your outline one line deeper than reality, reducing all damage while you stand still and read.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10 and read one full page of the Undertext without your own name changing.
Inscribe a rune that remains true after you stop believing in it.
Fold a map until two cities touch, and post a letter across the crease.
Descend to the archive's sealed floor, and return with the same number of shadows you took down.

nodes.name: Cindertongue
nodes.role: Ranged striker — single-target incineration burst
nodes.lore: Cindertongues speak the loud grammar so precisely it stops being weather and becomes intent. Their consonants scorch parchment at ten paces; taverns serve them in stoneware. Duelists dread the Held Word — fire kept behind the teeth for hours, then released as one immaculate, unsurvivable syllable.
nodes.playstyle: Charge held-word stacks between engagements, then discharge everything into a single target. Burst windows are short and total; missing one means minutes of silent rebuilding.

abilities.name: Held Word
abilities.desc: Bank fire on your tongue for up to an hour; its damage compounds silently until spoken.

abilities.name: Scorchword
abilities.desc: A single spoken bolt that ignores fire resistance in proportion to how long you have gone without speaking.

abilities.name: Fulminant Vowel
abilities.desc: One vowel of lightning that arcs from the burning target to whoever stands nearest in its defense.

abilities.name: Vitrify
abilities.desc: Fuse the ground beneath a burned enemy into glass, rooting them inside a mirror of the blast.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and hold a word of fire behind your teeth from dusk to dawn without swallowing.
Duel a Convoker of higher rank; win with one syllable, or never speak of it.
Whisper to a candle across a crowded hall and light it before anyone hears you.
Burn your apprentice notes; a Cindertongue carries every word ignited, or not at all.

nodes.name: Graven Lector
nodes.role: Area controller — walls, slows, siege attrition
nodes.lore: Graven Lectors read the quiet grammar: frost that outlasts argument, stone that never learned to hurry. Fortresses retain them as living gates. It is said a Lector reads a glacier the way clerks read ledgers — aloud, line by line, back to the first winter, and is never interrupted.
nodes.playstyle: Deny ground rather than take it. Layer walls, chills, and graven clauses until enemies are fighting inside a shrinking room of your punctuation.

abilities.name: Rime Parenthesis
abilities.desc: Enclose a zone in curved walls of ice; anything caught inside is parenthetical, and takes increased damage.

abilities.name: Graven Clause
abilities.desc: Carve a slowing sentence into the earth; enemies who read it — by standing on it — briefly turn to stone.

abilities.name: Hoarfrost Ledger
abilities.desc: Record every chill you inflict; at ten entries the ledger closes and all debtors freeze at once.

abilities.name: Weight of Strata
abilities.desc: Drop the memory of a mountain onto one point, crushing and half-burying whoever disagreed with you.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and read a glacier's strata aloud, oldest line first, until you reach a winter no calendar holds.
Raise a wall of ice before a siege, and still be standing behind it when the besiegers starve.
Carve one sentence into granite with a bare fingertip, without haste and without heat.
Spend a season in silence; the quiet grammar admits no student who fidgets.

nodes.name: Hourwright
nodes.role: Tempo support — haste, delay, small rewinds
nodes.lore: Hourwrights work time the way wheelwrights work oak: measured, joined, mended. Field commanders prize them, for a battle with an Hourwright runs on their clock. They keep pocketed minutes against emergencies and pay in memories, which is why old Hourwrights ask your name twice and apologize once.
nodes.playstyle: Bank seconds in calm moments and spend them in crisis: hastening allies, delaying blows, unwinding small disasters. Everything costs time you must already have saved.

abilities.name: Pocketed Hour
abilities.desc: Store an unspent hour; release it later to act freely while the field holds its breath.

abilities.name: Foregone Echo
abilities.desc: Replay your previous spell exactly; the echo costs no mana but ages you one visible day.

abilities.name: Clockwise Mercy
abilities.desc: Turn an ally's last three seconds backward, closing the wound that now has not happened yet.

abilities.name: Loitering Instant
abilities.desc: Stretch a single instant across a zone until arrows hang midair and oaths take minutes to finish.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and build a clock that keeps your pulse instead of the sun's.
Sit vigil over a candle burning backward, and record the hour at which it was lit.
Mend the shattered minute a dying Hourwright leaves you; waste nothing, not even the regret.
Give one year of your life to the guild's escrow, and do not ask what it is for.

nodes.name: Geometer
nodes.role: Zone manipulator — displacement and folded terrain
nodes.lore: Geometers measure the angles the world hopes nobody checks. Where they work, corridors shorten for friends and lengthen for creditors. The rank is conferred with a brass compass whose needle points to the bearer's true position — a courtesy, since after the third fold, few Geometers are entirely certain of it.
nodes.playstyle: Redraw the battlefield's floor plan mid-fight: fold charges into walls, open doors in distance, keep melee permanently arriving. Position is your entire vocabulary.

abilities.name: Foldstep
abilities.desc: Crease the floor and step over the crease, crossing thirty paces in one; the fold lingers for allies.

abilities.name: Impossible Corridor
abilities.desc: Bend an enemy's charge through a corner that was never there, delivering them neatly into your trap.

abilities.name: Proof by Collapse
abilities.desc: Demonstrate that a room's angles cannot all be true; the contradiction crushes everything inside it.

abilities.name: Squared Circle
abilities.desc: Inscribe a ring no straight line may cross; projectiles arrive politely at its edge and stop.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and walk a straight line that brings you home from the far side of the city.
Fold a locked room until its inside faces outward, and take nothing from it.
Survey a battlefield the night before, and leave one angle wrong on the enemy's map.
Accept the brass compass, and forgive it in advance for what it will stop knowing.

nodes.name: Ashen Rhetor
nodes.role: Artillery caster — sustained multi-target ruin
nodes.lore: The Rhetors of Ash are an order of nine, rarely eleven. Cities hire them to end wars with a single address; the address is fire, delivered in paragraphs. Treaties name them as weapons, not signatories. When a Rhetor rises to speak, veteran armies discover pressing business elsewhere.
nodes.playstyle: Channel long, escalating orations of flame. Each uninterrupted sentence widens the burn; interruption is your only true counter, so guard your speaking time jealously.

abilities.name: Burning Thesis
abilities.desc: Open an argument as a channeled beam of fire that grows wider each second you remain unrefuted.

abilities.name: Ash Sermon
abilities.desc: Deliver a falling homily over the field; ash accumulates, smothering enemy healing and igniting on the third stanza.

abilities.name: Closing Argument
abilities.desc: End the discussion: every enemy below one-quarter health within earshot is summarized in flame.

abilities.name: Firebreak Diction
abilities.desc: Clip your own consonants to raise a ring of burnt ground no fire — theirs or yours — may cross.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and address a city that hates you for one hour; leave it standing because you chose to.
Recite the Ninety Names of Fire from memory while your lectern burns beneath your notes.
Argue an old volcano back to sleep, or into eruption, as the order requires that year.
Submit your thesis in ash on stone pages, and defend it against nine Rhetors speaking at once.

nodes.name: Winter Grammarian
nodes.role: Fortress controller — mass denial and permanence
nodes.lore: Winter Grammarians parse motion out of sentences and armies alike. Where one stands, campaigns end in the declarative. Border kingdoms keep their names in sealed treaties, invoked only when a war must simply stop. Their corrections are permanent; thawing a Grammarian's work is heresy against grammar itself.
nodes.playstyle: Impose stillness at scale: freezes that hold, walls that outlive sieges, ground rewritten to winter. Slow, inevitable, immovable — you win by making the fight unaffordable.

abilities.name: Full Stop
abilities.desc: End every moving thing's sentence in a wide radius; the period is ice and lasts eight seconds.

abilities.name: Declension of Frost
abilities.desc: Conjugate an enemy through the cases of cold — chilled, slowed, brittle, held — one case per second.

abilities.name: Winter's Syntax
abilities.desc: Rewrite the ground's tense to past-perfect winter; the field becomes ice that remembers being a glacier.

abilities.name: Unmoved Clause
abilities.desc: Declare yourself grammatically fixed, immune to displacement and damage while you finish the current paragraph.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and hold a mountain pass closed for a full season using nothing that melts.
Correct a river in spring flood, and leave it a road.
Parse a cavalry charge into the passive voice before the third hoofbeat.
Write one sentence in frost upon the order's black gate; if it survives summer, so does your candidacy.

nodes.name: Chronarch
nodes.role: Tempo dominator — stolen turns and stasis
nodes.lore: A Chronarch keeps court over hours the way kings keep court over counties. Debtors bring them seconds; supplicants leave younger or older, per the judgment. Armies fear their arithmetic, for battles near a Chronarch are settled before they occur, in a ledger nobody else may audit.
nodes.playstyle: Tax enemy time and disburse it to allies. Rule engagements through stolen turns, commuted deaths, and courts of stasis. Bookkeeping wins the fight before swords do.

abilities.name: Tithe of Seconds
abilities.desc: Levy one second per second from every enemy in your court; your allies spend the surplus.

abilities.name: Regnal Hour
abilities.desc: Declare the hour yours; allies act twice within it, and interruptions are treason, punished with stasis.

abilities.name: Sentence Commuted
abilities.desc: Overturn a death within six seconds of its verdict; the sentence transfers, reduced, to the killer.

abilities.name: Adjournment
abilities.desc: Suspend the entire engagement for five seconds; only you may file motions during recess.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and audit your own life to the minute; unmake one hour and pay its full price.
Preside over a duel already fought, and deliver a different verdict.
Collect the year you escrowed as an Hourwright, with interest the guild cannot count.
Sit the Meridian Throne through one midnight; if dawn consents to arrive, the hour is yours to keep.

nodes.name: Axiom-Breaker
nodes.role: Rule-bender — negation and mass displacement
nodes.lore: Axiom-Breakers are banned in forty cities and consulted, quietly, by all forty. They disprove what battles depend on: that distance protects, that walls have insides, that ground is down. Each carries a list of postulates already broken; custom demands it be read aloud before accepting a surrender.
nodes.playstyle: Attack assumptions, not bodies. Negate signature abilities, relocate formations, invert cover. Your damage is modest; the enemy plan dying of contradictions is the win condition.

abilities.name: Counterexample
abilities.desc: Cite the one case where an enemy's ability fails; it fails now, and cannot be argued for twelve seconds.

abilities.name: Disproof of Distance
abilities.desc: Demonstrate that far is a superstition, exchanging the positions of two formations mid-maneuver.

abilities.name: Parallel Postulate
abilities.desc: Exist briefly along two parallel lines; both of you cast, and only one accepts the consequences.

abilities.name: Broken Compass
abilities.desc: Refute direction within a zone; enemy movement is redistributed by a geometry they never studied.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and disprove one law of nature before witnesses; survive nature's rebuttal.
Escape a cell the order built to hold you, without opening it and without leaving it.
Publish your broken postulate in the deep archive, and duel the first three scholars who object.
Return the brass compass to the room where you received it, though that room no longer adjoins anything.

nodes.name: Ember Anchorite
nodes.role: Aura caster — self-stoked heat and retaliation
nodes.lore: The Rhetors amplify; the Anchorites decline. Each takes the Held Word as a vow, not a weapon — fire swallowed whole and carried for decades, never spoken. They brick themselves into cells that glow faintly by the third winter. Rhetors call them wasted artillery. Anchorites call Rhetors spendthrifts who mistake noise for heat.
nodes.playstyle: Stand inside the enemy and radiate. Swallowed fire stacks endlessly while you stay silent; every ability spends none of it, and one forbidden word spends all.

abilities.name: Swallowed Syllable
abilities.desc: Bank a word of fire in your chest instead of your mouth; it compounds without limit and cannot be counterspelled, dispelled, or overheard.

abilities.name: Anchorite's Cell
abilities.desc: Raise a small brick sanctum around yourself; inside, your heat aura doubles and hostile speech arrives as harmless smoke.

abilities.name: Radiant Fast
abilities.desc: While you cast nothing and speak nothing, everything near you burns a little more each second, without flame or warning.

abilities.name: Vow's End
abilities.desc: Speak the word you have carried; damage equals every day of silence, and the vow, with the target, is gone.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and swallow a word of fire whole; keep it down for a year and a day without once clearing your throat.
Brick yourself into a cell with one window, facing away from anywhere you might be heard.
Refuse a city's commission to end its war; refuse it in writing, since you no longer speak.
Warm one stranger's winter without being found; the order counts the hearths you are not credited for.

nodes.name: Litanist of Dust
nodes.role: Attrition controller — permanent, stacking erosion
nodes.lore: Where Grammarians end sentences, Litanists refuse to. Their order holds permanence to be the one heresy the quiet grammar forbids: everything graven must someday be dust, and mastery is presiding over the journey. They repeat one word at a fortress until it agrees. Grammarians thaw nothing; Litanists, given time, unthaw everything.
nodes.playstyle: Stack small, unremovable erosions: armor thins, walls sift, resolve wears. Nothing you cast is impressive; nothing you cast can be undone, which proves sufficient.

abilities.name: Repetend
abilities.desc: Recite the same slow word each second; every repetition wears the target's armor and certainty by a margin that never recovers.

abilities.name: Sift
abilities.desc: Pronounce mortar into sand across a zone; walls and armor there shed a little of themselves each second, beginning with whatever is proudest.

abilities.name: Patient Landslide
abilities.desc: Start a hillside moving at one inch per hour toward a target; it arrives eventually, and it arrives entire.

abilities.name: Last Grain
abilities.desc: Declare one enemy already dust that has not settled yet; all erosion you have inflicted on them repeats at once.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and repeat one word at a standing stone until it kneels; schedule several decades.
Unmake, grain by grain, one work a Winter Grammarian sealed; leave the heresy trial to find an empty wall.
Carry a mountain through a sieve, one pocketful a day, and build nothing with it.
Recite the litany's single word to the assembled order and make no second point; admission is unanimous or eventual, which the order considers identical.

nodes.name: Eventualist
nodes.role: Foresight duelist — counters declared in advance
nodes.lore: Chronarchs amend the ledger; Eventualists hold it was never theirs to touch. Their order teaches that the Undertext fixed every hour at the first writing, and that rewinding is scribbling in a book one did not write. An Eventualist files tomorrow's battle-report today, unsigned. Generals resent this precisely as often as expected.
nodes.playstyle: Read ahead, then stand where the page says. You cannot change outcomes, only positions — so every counter, dodge, and ruin is announced early and arrives exactly.

abilities.name: Foreread
abilities.desc: Read the next six seconds aloud from the Undertext; whatever you pronounced cannot now be prevented, including by you.

abilities.name: Filed in Advance
abilities.desc: Lodge a counterspell against an enemy's next casting before they choose it; the paperwork predates the spell, and outranks it.

abilities.name: Appointment
abilities.desc: Name a place and second; the first enemy present is struck by everything you scheduled, which was waiting patiently.

abilities.name: Margin of Error
abilities.desc: You are always standing one annotation to the left of where the blow was written to land.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and deliver a battle's full report to the general the night before; attend the battle only to be thanked.
Watch a Chronarch commute a death, and file the objection that the death simply moved; be proven right within the year.
Grieve once for something that has not happened yet, thoroughly, so it is done.
Open your own sealed admission letter, written in the order's hand, dated before your birth.

nodes.name: Tessellant
nodes.role: Area architect — cells, walls, sealed ground
nodes.lore: Axiom-Breakers hold that mastery is the gap; Tessellants leave none. Their order tiles space whole — vault by vault, cell by cell — and builds the rooms other orders need built: the archive's sealed floor, the cells Axiom-Breakers must escape to graduate. A Tessellant's fee is standard. The door is extra.
nodes.playstyle: Tile the battlefield into cells you own. Each sealed shape strengthens the rest; enemies fight the floor plan first and you, if scheduled, second.

abilities.name: Perfect Tiling
abilities.desc: Divide the ground into locked cells; enemies may fight anything sharing their tile, which, increasingly, is nothing.

abilities.name: Keystone Proof
abilities.desc: Erect an instant vault overhead; while its keystone holds, nothing falls on anyone you shelter, including consequences.

abilities.name: Oubliette Lemma
abilities.desc: Prove a cell into being beneath one enemy; it contains them, by definition, until you misplace the proof deliberately.

abilities.name: Sealed Premises
abilities.desc: Close the field's boundary; nothing enters, leaves, or arrives by fold until you sign the release.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and tile one floor perfectly, in shapes no scholar has named, leaving no gap wider than a doubt.
Build a cell for an Axiom-Breaker and lose it to them graciously; build the second one differently.
Seal one floor of the deep archive and decline, permanently, to say what the tiles are holding down.
Live one year in a room with no visible door; on leaving, decline to show the guild where it was.

nodes.name: Voice of Ruin
nodes.role: Cataclysm caster — battlefield-scale annihilation
nodes.lore: Histories record three Voices of Ruin, and dispute the third. When a Voice speaks plainly, cartographers start over. The Third Siege of Vhal ended in one sentence — subject and verb, no survivors on the wrong side of the grammar. Nations do not fight Voices; they reschedule.
nodes.playstyle: Every cast is an event: long invocations, continental cooldowns, absolute outcomes. Played less like artillery and more like a treaty clause with a pulse.

abilities.name: Ninth Vowel
abilities.desc: Pronounce the vowel throats were shaped to prevent; everything in the sentence's path is unwritten to ash.

abilities.name: The Last Sentence
abilities.desc: Speak a target's ending, subject and verb; resistance becomes a matter of punctuation, not survival.

abilities.name: Silence After
abilities.desc: Following any ruin you utter, a hush falls in which no enemy magic can be pronounced.

abilities.name: Weather of Embers
abilities.desc: Change the region's weather to fire for one minute; it falls as rain that has forgotten water.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and speak, in a place already lost, one word the world was built never to hear.
Unmake a mountain's name by unmaking the mountain, and leave the cartographers to argue.
Stand before the surviving Rhetors and say nothing; be confirmed by their silence.
Teach one apprentice a single safe word, so the histories may claim you showed restraint.

nodes.name: Stillword
nodes.role: Absolute controller — stillness made terrain
nodes.lore: A Stillword is what remains when a Winter Grammarian stops needing sentences. The Hundred-Banner War ended when one arrived and declined it. Regions around a Stillword adopt their stillness: rivers slow, feuds pause mid-generation, avalanches wait. Historians write of them in the present tense, indefinitely.
nodes.playstyle: Impose an area of absolute quiet in which nothing hostile finishes: casts, charges, or wars. You barely act; the field simply forgets how to.

abilities.name: The Long Pause
abilities.desc: Halt every hostile action across the field for ten seconds; nothing ages, bleeds, or falls.

abilities.name: Unthawed Verdict
abilities.desc: Freeze one enemy outside all seasons; the ice is permanent until you, personally, reconsider.

abilities.name: Quiet That Holds
abilities.desc: An aura in which projectiles slow to a courtesy and spells must wait their turn to exist.

abilities.name: Winter, Considered
abilities.desc: Invite the first winter to revisit; the field becomes its memory, and only you may move at speed.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and sit one entire winter, unmoving, on the glacier you once read; let it finish your sentences.
Be declared dead, and correct no one.
Halt an avalanche mid-fall with your attention alone, then set it down gently, stone by stone.
Speak your final word aloud; everything after is punctuation.

nodes.name: The Unhoured
nodes.role: Time controller — causality spent like coin
nodes.lore: The Unhoured have stepped outside the clock entirely; calendars no longer agree on when they were born, and some now say never. They attend moments rather than inhabit them. Chronarchs rule hours; the Unhoured are owed by them. History treats each one as a rumor it cannot date.
nodes.playstyle: Spend causality directly: act inside others' moments, revoke events, arrive before your reasons do. The cost is continuity — yours, mostly, and paid without receipts.

abilities.name: Meanwhile
abilities.desc: Act during any other creature's action, as often as your unspent past allows.

abilities.name: Never
abilities.desc: Revoke one event from the last minute; the world keeps the scar but not the wound.

abilities.name: Grandfather Clause
abilities.desc: Damage that would kill you is referred backward to an ancestral moment that declines to allow it.

abilities.name: The Uncounted Hour
abilities.desc: Step into the hour clocks skip; return whenever you like, from any direction, rested.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and attend your own birth; introduce yourself to no one.
Misplace a year deliberately, and refuse every offered chance to recover it.
Preside over the Meridian Throne's final session, which occurred before the throne was built.
Let every calendar forget you, and forgive the friends who follow suit.

nodes.name: Worldscribe
nodes.role: Reality editor — rewrites the rules wholesale
nodes.lore: The Undertext has authors, and once a century one of them is living. A Worldscribe carries the pen the first draft was written with — or claims to, and the claim has never survived testing by anyone who tested it. Where they annotate, geography complies. The deep archive shelves their biographies under reference.
nodes.playstyle: Edit the engagement's source: terrain, rules, outcomes. Slow, deliberate revisions with total authority. You do not fight armies; you deprecate them.

abilities.name: Second Edition
abilities.desc: Issue a correction to the last six seconds; the field reloads to your amended version.

abilities.name: Deep Revision
abilities.desc: Rewrite a region's terrain wholesale — mountains struck through, rivers inserted — effective immediately and retroactively.

abilities.name: Authorial Intrusion
abilities.desc: Step directly into any scene the Undertext is currently running, regardless of distance or wards.

abilities.name: Binding Copy
abilities.desc: Declare one rule of your choosing canonical for an hour; reality enforces it without appeal.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and find the margin where the world's first author wrote; leave your reply.
Carve one rune upon the world's spine, where all the folds meet, and sign it.
Unwrite your own broken postulates and stand in the world as it was; then choose, freely, to break them again.
Outlive your biography in the deep archive by editing it, once, in your own hand.

nodes.name: The Banked Star
nodes.role: Immovable aura — zone-scale heat dominion
nodes.lore: Once a generation, an Anchorite's fire outgrows the vocabulary that could release it. What remains is a person-shaped warmth the size of a county: crops ripen early, winters arrive apologetically, and pilgrims mistake the cell for a shrine. Astronomers keep politely quiet about which star went missing, and when.
nodes.playstyle: Do not chase; be somewhere. Your presence is the spell — allies kindle, enemies cook, terrain remembers you warmly. Movement is rare, deliberate, and usually unnecessary.

abilities.name: Corona
abilities.desc: A permanent aura in rings: the nearest ignites, the next scorches, the outermost merely persuades enemies to reconsider their approach.

abilities.name: Gravity of Warmth
abilities.desc: Pull projectiles, spells, and the smaller sort of cavalry into slow orbits around you until they burn away.

abilities.name: Perihelion
abilities.desc: Mark an enemy as your nearest point; wherever they run, your heat calculates them as adjacent.

abilities.name: Vented Dawn
abilities.desc: Vent one hour of banked fire skyward; it falls back across the field as a dawn that sides with you.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and outgrow release: hold a fire that no remaining word in any language could pronounce.
Let a village settle inside your warmth for seven winters; bury none of them early.
Refuse the sun's own name when the order offers it; you did not fast this long to be renamed.
Be observed by astronomers as a fixed light on the earth, and decline, gently, to correct them.

nodes.name: The Slow Flood
nodes.role: Terrain engine — creeping mass and burial
nodes.lore: The order admits one living Slow Flood at a time, and denies that this one is late. Where they walk, geology keeps pace: hills follow at a respectful distance, rivers change their minds, moraines arrive like delayed correspondence. The Third Siege of Vhal ended in fire; the fourth was quietly buried.
nodes.playstyle: Set slow catastrophes moving early and fight inside their timetable. Everything you start finishes; the art is surviving long enough to inherit the landscape.

abilities.name: Advancing Moraine
abilities.desc: A wall of rubble crosses the field at walking pace, gathering everything it defeats into itself as mass.

abilities.name: Interment Clause
abilities.desc: Lower a zone one stratum per second; anything fully buried is archived beneath the field, alive, pending excavation.

abilities.name: Watershed
abilities.desc: Redirect the field's every slope toward one point; enemies fight uphill in all directions at once.

abilities.name: Angle of Repose
abilities.desc: Nothing within your sight may stand steeper than you permit; towers, stances, and morale all settle accordingly.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and start a landslide you will not live to see land; arrange to live anyway.
Bury a siege so gently the sentries notice nothing until the birds are walking.
Spend a year walking slower than stone; whatever still follows you afterward is yours.
Deliver the mountain you sieved, pocketful by pocketful, to wherever it is needed next; geography will adjust its expectations.

nodes.name: The Foregone
nodes.role: Inevitability caster — outcomes locked before combat
nodes.lore: A Foregone has finished the book. They know which winters are load-bearing, which dynasties are typographical errors, and how the world's last sentence runs — and they will not say, having read what saying does. Eventualists file predictions; a Foregone merely attends. Their arrival is not an omen. It is confirmation.
nodes.playstyle: Declare the ending first and spend the fight arriving at it. Deviations hurt you; fidelity to the read text makes you briefly, completely untouchable.

abilities.name: As Written
abilities.desc: Declare a fight's outcome at its start; while events comply, you take no damage the text does not mention.

abilities.name: Known Ending
abilities.desc: Show one enemy the paragraph where they lose; their morale fails, and their most confident ability forgets its own name.

abilities.name: Attendance
abilities.desc: Be present at any event you have read, stepping from the preceding sentence without crossing the intervening ground.

abilities.name: Unturned Page
abilities.desc: Refuse to read one future; within it, and only there, you may still choose anything, and enemies cannot predict you.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and read the world's last page; return the book to its shelf evenly, as though nothing were different.
Attend three endings you could have prevented, and prevent none; the order will know if you wept, and does not mind.
Keep one appointment in the uncounted hour; whatever waits there has been reading over your shoulder all along.
Stop making predictions; from you, they are quotations.

nodes.name: The Adytum
nodes.role: Living fortress — absolute defense, spatial custody
nodes.lore: A Tessellant perfects enclosure once, on themselves. The Adytum is less a person than an address: somewhere inside the folded vaults is someone who took final orders in geometry and sealed the door behind them. Petitioners address the outermost wall. Three empires keep maps of where the Adytum is not.
nodes.playstyle: Be the safest place in the war. Allies fight from inside you; sieges break on geometry they cannot see all of. Offense is a wall, repeated.

abilities.name: Nested Sanctum
abilities.desc: Enclose allies within your inner vaults; harm must solve each shell in order, and the shells are not in order.

abilities.name: Curtain Theorem
abilities.desc: Raise a wall that is also the proof of the next wall; every breach merely establishes the following rampart.

abilities.name: Custody of Ground
abilities.desc: Annex the ground an enemy stands on into your interior; house rules apply, and the house is you.

abilities.name: Withheld Door
abilities.desc: Reveal, once per battle, that there was always a door; allies leave through it, enemies learn of it afterward.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and seal yourself in absolutely; hold audiences anyway.
Outlast a siege by three dynasties without once clarifying whether you are inside.
House the archive's most dangerous shelf where even the index cannot follow; the librarians will sleep again, eventually.
Turn away the Axiom-Breaker who escaped your first cell; they will cite the precedent; the wall will not.

nodes.name: The Peroration
nodes.role: Apocalyptic orator — warfare ended by address
nodes.lore: Voices end sieges; something must end arguments. The Peroration is what a Voice of Ruin becomes when the address outgrows the speaker: history's closing statement, already in delivery, audible wherever a war runs long. Thunder is its rough draft. The three recorded Voices are now considered its opening remarks.
nodes.playstyle: Speak seldom and at the scale of history. Each clause retires part of the battlefield permanently; the fight ends when your paragraph does, and it does.

abilities.name: In Conclusion
abilities.desc: Open your address; each subsequent clause removes one category of thing — cavalry, weather, walls — from the engagement.

abilities.name: The Floor
abilities.desc: Take the floor: while you speak, no enemy ability may begin, and several currently running reconsider.

abilities.name: Scorched Minutes
abilities.desc: Enter the battle into the record as ash; whatever the record omits stops existing at the session's close.

abilities.name: History Rests
abilities.desc: Rest your case upon a region; nothing there may begin a war again, the clause being self-enforcing and famously tested once.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and begin the address that does not end with you; future holders will clear their throats mid-sentence.
Deliver one clause per decade; let empires draft their policies around your pauses.
Speak the summary of a century so that no historian needs to; accept their resentment as citation.
When the world's argument closes, be what holds the floor after: the silence in which nothing dares resume.

nodes.name: The First Winter
nodes.role: Season incarnate — stillness as world condition
nodes.lore: Historians keep Stillwords in the present tense; one has slipped further back. The First Winter is the stillness before the first thaw, holding office retroactively since before calendars — every winter since is quotation, every truce a thaw it permits. Glaciers are its correspondence. The quiet grammar has exactly one speaker left, and it is weather now.
nodes.playstyle: Arrive as a season, not a combatant. The field enters your winter and adopts its habits: nothing hostile begins, persists, or thaws without written permission.

abilities.name: Before Calendars
abilities.desc: Set the field to the winter before counting; durations, cooldowns, and reinforcement timetables find they have no dates to refer to.

abilities.name: Quotation Frost
abilities.desc: Any ice anywhere on the field becomes citation of you; it deepens to match the original.

abilities.name: Deferred Spring
abilities.desc: Suspend every recovery in your winter — healing, rallying, morale — until spring, whose scheduling is at your discretion.

abilities.name: Glacial Correspondence
abilities.desc: Send a glacier as a letter; it arrives in some years, unopposable, saying exactly what you still mean.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and backdate your stillness to the world's first morning; the filing will be accepted, seasons being unable to prove otherwise.
Permit one thaw per age, in writing, and attend none of them.
Be quoted by the weather verbatim for a century without once granting an interview.
Sit so still that the calendars agree to start after you; do not gloat, which would be movement.

nodes.name: The Meridian
nodes.role: Temporal axis — all timing measured from you
nodes.lore: Clocks must agree with something. When the last Unhoured let every calendar forget them, the forgetting left a line — and the world, needing one, hung its noons upon it. The Meridian is that office: the standing agreement all hours are reckoned against, held by someone no calendar can any longer name. The Throne faces it when in session.
nodes.playstyle: Do not act in time; be what time acts relative to. Haste, delay, and sequence are defined against you, which makes disagreement a rounding error.

abilities.name: Prime Noon
abilities.desc: Declare the local instant noon; every duration on the field is re-reckoned from you, generally to your advantage.

abilities.name: Reckoning Line
abilities.desc: Draw your line across the field; allies west of it act early, enemies east of it act late, and you decide which way is west.

abilities.name: Standard Time
abilities.desc: Impose your personal tempo as law; abilities faster than yours are cited for it and slowed to compliance.

abilities.name: Antemeridian
abilities.desc: Step to the morning side of the present moment; whatever harmed you there has not technically occurred, and now cannot.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and return from being forgotten as something calendars can point at without naming.
Hold noon steady through an eclipse, a war, and a committee of astronomers; only the committee will truly test you.
Preside over the Meridian Throne's every session at once, being now what it faces.
When two calendars go to war over a leap-day, absorb the day; neither will miss it, and you keep such things now.

nodes.name: The Colophon
nodes.role: Reality authority — authorship as final law
nodes.lore: Every finished book ends with the maker's mark. The Worldscribe who edits long enough stops signing pages and becomes the signature: the Colophon, shelved at the end of everything, in whose small type the world admits who has been writing it lately. Scholars who read that far report only that the mark was watching them back.
nodes.playstyle: Everything that exists is your text and cites you. Combat is copyediting at world scale: strike a line here, approve a fate there, initial the result.

abilities.name: Imprimatur
abilities.desc: Nothing new may exist on the field — spells, gates, reinforcements — until it bears your stamp, which is discretionary.

abilities.name: Struck Line
abilities.desc: Delete one sentence of reality — a wall, a wound, a general's best idea — and initial the margin.

abilities.name: Errata of Empires
abilities.desc: Publish corrections to the standing world; kingdoms adjust their borders, memories, and casualty lists to match the new printing.

abilities.name: Small Type
abilities.desc: Reside in the world's fine print; only those who read everything can target you, and the fine print warned them.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and finish the book once, privately, to prove it can be done; then reopen it for everyone else.
Sign the world's last page with the same hand that answered its first margin; leave the scholars the argument.
Approve one printing of the world per morning; reject the others without comment.
When the first author returns for the pen, initial their request, and file it.

nodes.name: Undersun
nodes.role: World-scale aura — warmth as standing law
nodes.lore: The Banked Star does not die; it sets. Somewhere beneath the bedrock a swallowed fire now keeps the world's feet warm, and every hearth, forge, and fever draws on it without asking. Scholars call this geology. The order calls it the Undersun, and banks its own fires toward the day it gutters.
nodes.playstyle: Fight from underneath everything. Your fire arrives through floors, hearths, and blood; enemies stand on you by definition, which is rarely wise for long.

abilities.name: Hypocaust
abilities.desc: Heat the field from below; every surface becomes your aura, and burrowing, tunneling, and prone enemies regret their doctrine.

abilities.name: Every Hearth a Door
abilities.desc: Emerge from any lit fire in the world; arriving extinguishes it, which is considered an omen, correctly.

abilities.name: Deep Kindling
abilities.desc: Ignite what was never fuel: stone, rain, and the idea of retreat all burn if you insist.

abilities.name: Gutter and Return
abilities.desc: Upon dying, sink beneath the field and rekindle at any hearth you have warmed within three days.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and set: walk into the earth while still burning, and do not treat it as a funeral.
Warm the world for one full winter from below; let spring take the credit.
When the last fire of a dying age is down to one coal, be that coal.
Answer, once a century, a knock on the underside of a hearthstone; it will be the order, checking.

nodes.name: The Orogeny
nodes.role: Geologic sovereign — raises and razes terrain
nodes.lore: When a Slow Flood finally stops walking, the walking does not stop. Ranges rise where they rested; surveyors date fresh peaks to their pauses. The world keeps the Orogeny as its slowest office: the standing appointment by which mountains are raised, worn down, and — the order insists — merely redrafted.
nodes.playstyle: Play in eras. Raise ranges as opening moves, spend the erosion as resources, and treat any fight shorter than a season as already conceded to you.

abilities.name: Mountain, Drafted
abilities.desc: Raise a young range across the field over ten seconds; everything it lifts fights at the altitude you assign.

abilities.name: Subduction
abilities.desc: Slide one edge of the battlefield beneath another; whatever stood on the losing plate is filed under the winning one.

abilities.name: Unconformity
abilities.desc: Strike an era from the strata; anything built or sworn within it loses its foundations at once.

abilities.name: Peneplain
abilities.desc: Level everything: reduce the field, its fortifications, and its argument to one calm plain, yours.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and rest; where you slept, present a mountain range to the morning.
Raise one range and wear down another in the same century, and file both under maintenance.
Let the order carve its archive into your foothills, and keep its shelves level for a thousand years.
When the world needs a new horizon, be it.

nodes.name: The Future Perfect
nodes.role: Causal sovereign — battles resolved in advance
nodes.lore: The Foregone knew the ending; the Future Perfect is its tense. They exist as the fact that everything will have happened: harvests, heresies, the last sentence itself. Scholars conjugating far enough forward find them standing in the grammar, patient as punctuation. Nothing surprises the world anymore; it has them instead.
nodes.playstyle: You have already won by the time you arrive; play consists of disclosing how. Enemies act freely, discover their actions were prerequisites, and file out.

abilities.name: Will Have Fallen
abilities.desc: Conjugate one enemy forward: they have already lost this fight, and their body is granted a few seconds to catch up.

abilities.name: Retrospect
abilities.desc: Fight from one hour after the battle; effects reach you only as reports, summarized, and considerably reduced.

abilities.name: Prerequisite
abilities.desc: Declare an enemy action necessary to your victory; it resolves, then contributes its full force to your next spell.

abilities.name: The Settled Question
abilities.desc: Once per day, end any engagement as history records it ended; history is open to reasonable suggestions.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and be conjugated: enter the tense where your work is finished, and keep working anyway.
Answer, from tomorrow, letters not yet written; the order files your replies under pending, which they no longer are.
Stand where the world's last sentence will have been read, and wave to the Foregone you were.
Let grammarians of every language add one tense in your honor; correct their tables gently, since you have already done so.

nodes.name: The Firmament
nodes.role: Cosmic bulwark — the sky as fortification
nodes.lore: The Adytum enclosed themselves; the Firmament encloses everything else. The world's oldest wall — the vault the stars are set in — is an office, and it is held. Nothing enters that was not allowed; nothing important leaves. Astronomers map its joints and call them constellations. The order calls them courses of masonry.
nodes.playstyle: Defend at the scale of skies. Your walls are horizons, your cells are climates, and anything thrown at anyone, anywhere you stand watch, was thrown at you.

abilities.name: Course of Stars
abilities.desc: Rearrange a constellation into a rampart overhead; while it stands, the night itself counts as your outermost wall.

abilities.name: Horizon Seal
abilities.desc: Close the sky over a region; weather, omens, and airborne assaults wait outside until reviewed.

abilities.name: Raised Horizon
abilities.desc: Raise the horizon itself as a wall; everything beyond it is postponed, and the postponement is not appealable.

abilities.name: Nothing Falls
abilities.desc: Catch every falling thing above the field — arrows, stars, verdicts — and set each into the vault as fixtures, yours.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and accept the oldest commission on the order's books: one wall, stars for tiles, everything living on the inside.
Point the brass compass upward and finally agree with it.
Mortar the sky's one true gap so gently that whatever waited outside fails to notice the lock.
Stand watch until the stars need re-setting; you will know the courses by heart, having been them.

families.name: Sorcerer
families.tagline: The blood decides; the sorcerer merely aims.
families.description: No tutor chose them and no book explains them. Sorcery arrived with the blood — in a fever, a struck bell, a house fire nobody could account for. Every Sorcerer spends their first years surviving their own gift: grounding it, starving it, apologizing for it. The great ones stop apologizing. They learn that a flaw, aimed well, is indistinguishable from a weapon.

nodes.name: Sorcerer
nodes.role: Ranged caster — volatile raw burst
nodes.lore: Every village has a story: the child who wept sparks, the granary that burned on naming-day. Sorcerers begin as accidents that lived. Hedge-wives dose them, priests test them, war-camps eventually buy them. Most spend their first years learning not to kill anyone by accident, and the rest of their lives learning to do it on purpose.
nodes.playstyle: Volatile ranged caster. Spend raw power fast, ride surges as they come, and manage a gift that grows stronger the closer it drifts toward slipping.

abilities.name: Bloodspark
abilities.desc: Hurl a bolt of raw sorcery drawn straight from the vein; damage rises with every surge suffered this battle.

abilities.name: Gutter the Flame
abilities.desc: Clamp your gift shut for one breath, purging a curse or magical binding from yourself as the power dies down.

abilities.name: Grounding Rite
abilities.desc: Kneel and bleed excess power into earth or iron, trading your next action for stability.

abilities.name: Surge Fault
abilities.desc: Passive — your spells sometimes echo a heartbeat later at half strength, whether or not you wanted them to.

progressionSteps: Survive the night your gift first wakes — the burned bed, the frightened kin, the silence after.
Find one person who does not flinch from you, and learn to cast with them in the room.
Ground a surge into cold earth without fainting, three times, witnessed by no one who might use you.
Name your power aloud. Not curse, not blessing — yours.

nodes.name: Wyrmblooded
nodes.role: Midrange caster — sustained fire pressure
nodes.lore: The dreams come first — one mountain, always seen from above. Then heat in the spit, gold weighed too long in the palm, the first scales at the nape. Wyrmblooded sorcerers are courted by armies and watched carefully by everyone else, because whatever ancestor stirs in them was never entirely human, and it is not finished waking.
nodes.playstyle: Sustained fire pressure from midrange. Build heat with every cast, wear it as armor, and grow harder to kill the longer the fight burns.

abilities.name: First Ember
abilities.desc: Exhale a gout of ancestral fire; targets left burning take deepened damage from your next spell.

abilities.name: Underscale
abilities.desc: Scales surface beneath the skin when you are struck, granting stacking armor that lasts while your heat holds.

abilities.name: Ancestor's Pulse
abilities.desc: Once per battle the older heart beats for yours, refusing a killing blow and igniting you fully.

abilities.name: Hoard-Sense
abilities.desc: Passive — you feel gold, gems, and hidden bodies through stone, the way the ancestor once did.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10 and dream the same mountain three nights running, then wake with heat in your mouth.
Trace the old rumor in your family line to a grave, a hoard, or a lie — and forgive none of it.
Let the first scales come. Do not cut them out.
Breathe fire once, deliberately, at something you chose to burn.

nodes.name: Stormveined
nodes.role: Ranged caster — high-variance burst
nodes.lore: Their moods read on barometers. Stormveined sorcerers crackle — hair lifting before they anger, candle flames leaning toward them, dice behaving strangely at their tables. Captains want them in the charge and keep them far from the powder stores. Their power is not disciplined; it is negotiated with, hourly, and it respects nothing but nerve.
nodes.playstyle: High-variance burst caster. Court wild surges instead of suppressing them, cash lucky outcomes into damage, and gamble position on lightning-fast repositioning.

abilities.name: Levin Snap
abilities.desc: Loose a jolting arc that rolls its damage twice and keeps the higher, then jumps to a second target.

abilities.name: Sideways Luck
abilities.desc: Passive — each wild surge you suffer banks a charm; spend charms to reroll any outcome near you once.

abilities.name: Hackle Field
abilities.desc: Static sheathes you; melee attackers are jolted, slowed, and briefly certain they smelled rain.

abilities.name: Ride the Fault
abilities.desc: Break apart into a crack of lightning and reform anywhere in sight, arriving before your thunder does.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10 and stand in open weather through a storm you did not summon, until it notices you.
Lose control once in public. Pay for it. Remember the exact color of the moment before.
Wager something irreplaceable on a coin toss and let the magic call it in the air.
Learn the smell of a surge coming — copper and rain — and stop flinching.

nodes.name: Cinderthroat
nodes.role: Cone caster — burning area denial
nodes.lore: In some, the wyrm settles in the lungs. Cinderthroats speak in ruined voices and glow faintly at the collarbone when angry. Siege companies rent them by the gate; villages that hear one coughing evacuate without instruction. They are the reason certain fortresses keep doors of solid stone and generals of unusual politeness.
nodes.playstyle: Positional cone caster. Manage banked breath and scorch stacks, cut battlefields into burning lanes, and hold ground no one can afford to cross.

abilities.name: Rendering Breath
abilities.desc: A slow, widening cone of furnace-heat that melts armor value away before it ever touches flesh.

abilities.name: Second Lung
abilities.desc: Bank one breath of fire; release it instantly later, even while silenced, grappled, or drowning.

abilities.name: Cauter Line
abilities.desc: Draw a burning seam across the ground that persists, splitting the field into yours and theirs.

abilities.name: Glasswake
abilities.desc: Your fire fuses soil into glass; enemies crossing your scorched ground walk slowly, on knives.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and swallow a live coal from a dragon-touched fire, and keep it down.
Hold one breath through a burning building's collapse, then walk out and speak clearly.
Reduce a fortified gate to slag while its defenders watch, and refuse the payment offered after.
Learn which of your words scorch, and stop wasting them.

nodes.name: Scalewrought
nodes.role: Frontline battle-caster — attrition tank
nodes.lore: These are the ones who stopped fighting the molt. Plate spreads over ribs and forearms; gauntlets become unnecessary, then impossible. Scalewrought walk the front rank of battles that expected no caster within reach, shrugging arrows and casting through wounds. What unsettles people is not the scale. It is how calm they have become since accepting it.
nodes.playstyle: Frontline battle-caster. Absorb hits to bank heat, cast at claw's length, and outlast enemies who mistook you for the soft target.

abilities.name: Plated Hour
abilities.desc: Scale closes over you entirely for a span; damage taken banks as heat your claws may spend.

abilities.name: Wyrmgrip
abilities.desc: Seize a foe in one taloned hand; spells cast into a held enemy cannot miss or be resisted.

abilities.name: Molt Burst
abilities.desc: Shed a layer of scale explosively, shredding everything adjacent and tearing every binding off you.

abilities.name: Slow Furnace
abilities.desc: Passive — you regenerate while standing in fire. Any fire. Anyone's.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and endure a full molt awake, keeping count of every scale that comes.
Take a blade meant for someone else and let them watch it fail against you.
Sleep once, unarmored, among people who fear you, and wake having harmed no one.
Stop apologizing for your hands.

nodes.name: Levinbrand
nodes.role: Mobile skirmisher — chain lightning strikes
nodes.lore: The Stormveined who chose the lightning over the luck. Levinbrands cross provinces between dusk and dinner and end duels before their thunder arrives. Border forts log their passage as weather rather than visitors. The speed, they will tell you, was always free; it is the standing still that has to be trained.
nodes.playstyle: Hyper-mobile skirmisher-caster. Blink through enemy lines as living lightning, chain arcs off armored targets, and bank charges from everything you evade.

abilities.name: Stepwise Lightning
abilities.desc: Become the bolt along a chosen line, striking everything on it and arriving before your own sound.

abilities.name: Chained Verdict
abilities.desc: An arc that leaps from target to target, favoring whoever carries the most metal.

abilities.name: Afterimage Charge
abilities.desc: The place you just stood detonates in static one heartbeat after you leave it.

abilities.name: Capacitor Heart
abilities.desc: Passive — every attack you evade banks a charge; spend charges to cast instantly, without pause or breath.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and outrun your own thunder on open ground, before a sworn skeptic.
Take one strike from the sky standing up, and keep whatever it leaves in your bones.
Cross an active battlefield touching the ground three times or fewer.
Practice stillness one hour a day. The speed is free; the stopping will cost you.

nodes.name: Chancewright
nodes.role: Support disruptor — probability control
nodes.lore: The Stormveined who followed the luck instead of the bolt. Chancewrights are banned from honest card-rooms by portrait and welcomed into war-tents by generals who want the enemy's plans stood next to. Around them, accidents stop being accidents and become negotiations — negotiations the Chancewright has usually opened already.
nodes.playstyle: Probability manipulator and disruptor. Load outcomes for allies, sour them for enemies, and stake your own blood when the odds need forcing.

abilities.name: Loaded Hour
abilities.desc: For a span, every random outcome nearby rolls twice; allies keep the better result, enemies the worse.

abilities.name: Fumble Clause
abilities.desc: Curse one certainty — the strap breaks, the footing slips, the sure spell sours.

abilities.name: House Edge
abilities.desc: Passive — every enemy miss near you banks a token; spend three to declare one outcome outright.

abilities.name: Wager of Flesh
abilities.desc: Stake your own blood on a spell: it casts twice if it lands, costs double if it fails.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and win a rigged game without touching the rig — bend only the luck around it.
Lose everything once, deliberately, and note exactly where the laws of chance felt strained.
Cross an active battlefield unarmed; collect other people's arrows in your coat and none in you.
Flip one coin a thousand times and record the day it starts refusing to land.

nodes.name: Voice of the Furnace
nodes.role: Siege caster — field-scale annihilation
nodes.lore: Rare enough that cities negotiate before one arrives. A Voice speaks and mortar runs; their breath is surveyed in acres afterward. Several kingdoms keep registries of the living ones, and at least two pay a standing annual fee for the simple assurance of absence. Their footprints stay warm for days.
nodes.playstyle: Siege-scale annihilation. Long wind-ups into field-erasing exhalations; reshape terrain, devour enemy fire, and make the far half of any battle uninhabitable.

abilities.name: Sermon of Ash
abilities.desc: A sustained exhalation that widens as it travels, converting the far end of a battlefield to cinders.

abilities.name: Firebreak
abilities.desc: Inhale an incoming fire spell whole and keep it, adding its strength to your next breath.

abilities.name: Kilnheart
abilities.desc: Your core burns openly; nearby allied weapons take on a working edge of flame.

abilities.name: The Long Vowel
abilities.desc: Hold one burning note; while it sounds, no flame on the field obeys anyone but you.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and unmake a siege alone — the walls, the engines, and the appetite for another.
Refuse a king's contract to burn a city, then survive whatever he sends to insist.
Write your name into a cliff face with a single word.
Find a young Cinderthroat and teach them for nothing. The fire keeps its own accounts.

nodes.name: The Molted
nodes.role: Transformed juggernaut — formation breaker
nodes.lore: The final human skin comes off whole, and the order keeps them — pale, folded, labeled — in a cold hall under the mountain. What walks out afterward still speaks, still keeps oaths, still remembers birthdays. Veterans would rather face anything else on a wall, because the Molted come on through everything.
nodes.playstyle: Unstoppable frontline engine. Wade through massed fire, convert punishment into strength, and dismantle formations at claw's length while spellwork seals the exits.

abilities.name: Second Shape
abilities.desc: Assume the between-form fully — talon, tail, and wingframe — trading spell range for irresistible reach.

abilities.name: Adamant Molt
abilities.desc: Each battle's first molt leaves a standing husk that fights on beside you for a time.

abilities.name: Furnace Blood
abilities.desc: Your blood ignites as it leaves you; whoever wounds you in melee shares the burn.

abilities.name: Graven Scale
abilities.desc: Inscribe one oath upon your plate; while you keep it, that scale cannot be pierced.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and shed the last human skin whole, then fold it yourself, without help.
Breach a shield-wall using nothing you learned from books.
Carry your shed skin to the cold hall beneath the mountain and shelve it beside the others.
Keep one human habit on purpose. The order recommends birthdays.

nodes.name: Eye of the Tempest
nodes.role: Zone controller — mobile storm fortress
nodes.lore: Elite enough that admiralties track them like weather systems, because they are one. An Eye walks inside a moving calm perhaps ten paces wide; everything beyond it is rim, and the rim is catastrophe. Ports have surrendered to nothing more than the sight of one standing dry in the harbor rain.
nodes.playstyle: Mobile fortress of weather. Anchor a traveling storm around your own calm, punish every approach, and dictate where the battle is allowed to stand.

abilities.name: Standing Vortex
abilities.desc: Anchor a hurricane to your heel; its walls travel with you and its calm belongs to you alone.

abilities.name: Barometric Drop
abilities.desc: Collapse the air over a zone — flyers fall, ears burst, and every flame dies at once.

abilities.name: Nine Bolts Waiting
abilities.desc: Hold sky-charges aloft; they fall, in order, on the next nine things to cross your rim.

abilities.name: Lull
abilities.desc: Silence the entire storm for three heartbeats, so everyone can consider what you are choosing not to do.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and walk a hurricane across open sea, then park it, whole, where you chose.
Winter alone on a peak that lightning loves, and come down carrying its patience.
End a battle with no bolt landing — the threat, held steady, sufficing.
Refuse the shrine the coast builds you. Insist on being weather, not god.

nodes.name: Hazard Saint
nodes.role: Fate warper — ally miracles, enemy ruin
nodes.lore: Mercenary companies carry their tokens; insurers refuse whole districts where one sleeps. They are called saints because prayers to luck get answered in their vicinity — promptly, precisely, and at a price the parish only tallies later. Disasters do not avoid a Hazard Saint's debtors. They reroute.
nodes.playstyle: Field-warping support. Consecrate ground where plans decay, underwrite allies' impossible attempts, and take catastrophes onto yourself to break them into inconveniences.

abilities.name: Canon of Errors
abilities.desc: Consecrate ground where nothing proceeds as planned; enemy orders arrive garbled and reinforcements arrive lost.

abilities.name: Miracle Ledger
abilities.desc: Record an ally's impossible attempt; once per day, one recorded entry simply succeeds.

abilities.name: Martyr's Odds
abilities.desc: Take a catastrophe aimed elsewhere onto yourself, then shatter it into a hundred harmless inconveniences.

abilities.name: Sainted Coin
abilities.desc: Flip: heads, your next spell is free and doubled; tails, your enemy's is. You may not look first.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and survive your own execution through a chain of accidents no court can call intent.
Settle every debt you owe to chance. A saint borrows for others now.
Be prayed to once, in earnest, and answer without letting them see the price.
Bless a hopeless charge and walk at the front of it, unarmored.

nodes.name: Shutmouth
nodes.role: Anti-caster tank — fire absorption and denial
nodes.lore: Where the Voice of the Furnace spends the breath, the Shutmouth keep it. Their vow is a shut mouth: no flame leaves the body, and every fire they meet goes in. Burning cities send for them and watch the blaze drain away like water finding a hole. They whisper, always. A raised voice might kindle something.
nodes.playstyle: Implacable absorption tank. Devour enemy fire and spellwork, grow hotter and harder with everything swallowed, and win by making the field's destruction quietly disappear.

abilities.name: Siege Diet
abilities.desc: Inhale a hostile spell or burning zone whole; its remaining strength seals inside you as stacking heat.

abilities.name: The Swallowed Vowel
abilities.desc: Hold your silence for a round; every flame on the field dims, and what the fires lose, you keep.

abilities.name: Sealed Kiln
abilities.desc: Passive — swallowed fire bakes you hard as kiln-clay; your armor rises with every flame you keep.

abilities.name: One Breath Out
abilities.desc: Exhale everything stored in one annihilating cone; your vow, your armor, and the order's patience break with it.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and eat a burning granary down to cool timbers, swallowing every ember before the roof falls.
Take the vow of the shut mouth at the order's one cold brazier, and whisper from then on.
Sit through a Voice of the Furnace's sermon and inhale it. Apologize afterward, quietly.
Carry the last fire of a dead village in your chest until you find its survivors, so somebody's warmth outlives the map.

nodes.name: Scutewright
nodes.role: Frontline support — ally armament and protection
nodes.lore: The Molted shelve their skins in the cold hall under the mountain; Scutewrights refuse the archive. Every molt goes to the forge still warm, hammered into shields, scale-coats, gates. Their charter holds that the wyrm is a yield, not a destiny, and that the human hand giving it away is the only part worth keeping.
nodes.playstyle: Frontline support-tank. Shed scale deliberately to armor allies mid-battle, anchor shield-lines with your own plate, and grow lighter, quicker, and more human with everything you give.

abilities.name: Warm from the Molt
abilities.desc: Clad an ally in freshly shed scale; it fits better than forge-work and burns the first blade that tests it.

abilities.name: Public Armory
abilities.desc: Declare your body the company armory; any ally within reach may tear away a shield's worth of scale, free.

abilities.name: Lighter by Giving
abilities.desc: Passive — every scale given this battle quickens you; fully spent, you cast human-fast, twice as often.

abilities.name: The Smith's Refusal
abilities.desc: Halt your own molt mid-change to halt all shapeshifting nearby; nothing changes form while you refuse to.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and forge your first molt into a shield while it still holds your warmth, then give it away the same day.
Stand unarmored behind your own work while a siege tests it.
Visit the cold hall beneath the mountain, view the shelved skins, and decline, in writing.
Armor someone who once feared your hands.

nodes.name: Thunderless
nodes.role: Assassin-caster — single-target instant execution
nodes.lore: The Eye of the Tempest parks a hurricane as an argument; the Thunderless consider weather a confession. Their doctrine is the bolt from a clear sky — no cloud, no warning, no sound, thunder being only lightning's apology. Border forts that log Levinbrands as weather have no column at all for what the Thunderless are.
nodes.playstyle: Surgical execution from nowhere. Sweep the sky clean, cross impossible distances as a single strike, kill the one correct target, and leave before physics files its report.

abilities.name: The Blue Bolt
abilities.desc: Strike any target you can name beneath an open sky, from anywhere beneath the same sky.

abilities.name: Apology Withheld
abilities.desc: Passive — your lightning arrives without sound, flash, or omen; wards record it in the past tense.

abilities.name: One Correct Target
abilities.desc: Study a foe for one round; your next strike ignores everything between you — walls, allies, likelihood.

abilities.name: Dry Strike
abilities.desc: Strike without heat or fire, stopping one heart while leaving the grass, the rooftops, and the treaty unburned.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and put a bolt through a weathervane from beyond its horizon, under a sky you swept clean first.
Renounce thunder. Practice until the sky agrees to keep your secrets.
Decline a war by ending its one necessary person, and let both armies walk home under clear weather.
Stand inside an Eye's hurricane, unimpressed, and leave without being rained on.

nodes.name: Lotcaster
nodes.role: Debuff controller — misfortune assignment
nodes.lore: Hazard Saints take catastrophes onto themselves and call it grace; Lotcasters call it bad arithmetic. Their doctrine is conservation: misfortune is never destroyed, only relocated, so somebody honest should choose where it lands. They draw lots for a living. The lots are people, and the order keeps its quills sharp.
nodes.playstyle: Misfortune logistics. Gather every accident, curse, and failure pending on the field, then assign each a recipient; protect allies by addressing their disasters to enemies.

abilities.name: The Drawn Lot
abilities.desc: Mark one enemy as recipient; every misfortune meant for your allies this battle arrives, collected, at that address.

abilities.name: Conservation of Ruin
abilities.desc: Passive — no mishap near you is wasted; each harm prevented banks as one assignable accident.

abilities.name: Somebody's Roof
abilities.desc: Redirect a falling catastrophe, literal or otherwise, onto a target of your choosing; witnesses agree it looked natural.

abilities.name: Short Straw
abilities.desc: Force a group of enemies to draw; one of them — the choice never matters — receives everything at once.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and walk a city's worst month out the gates piece by piece, to a place you will name to no one.
Attend a Hazard Saint's miracle, then follow the luck downhill to the stranger it landed on. Buy them dinner. Say nothing.
Draw the short lot yourself once a year, in full, so the hand stays honest.
Refuse to let a king choose the recipient. That hand stays yours.

nodes.name: Worldpyre
nodes.role: Apocalyptic artillery — terrain erasure
nodes.lore: Histories count them in single digits and disagree about those. Where a Worldpyre fought, the maps simply note glass. Scholars argue their breath is the first fire — the one the eldest wyrms carried before there were things to burn. When a Worldpyre dies, witnesses report, the pyre lights itself.
nodes.playstyle: Apocalyptic zone erasure. Slow, inexorable, terrain-rewriting devastation. Your presence renegotiates where armies are willing to exist, and every engagement becomes a question of evacuation routes.

abilities.name: The First Fire
abilities.desc: Breathe the flame the eldest wyrms remember; it does not spread — it replaces.

abilities.name: Glass Meridian
abilities.desc: Draw a horizon-long line of vitrified earth that no army will cross for a generation.

abilities.name: Ashfall Covenant
abilities.desc: For one day, everything within sight burns only with your permission.

abilities.name: Pyre Eternal
abilities.desc: Passive — should you fall, your last breath lights a fire that dies only when your body reaches home.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and breathe against a true dragon's fire until one of you looks away first.
Stand in a caldera as it wakes and breathe the eruption back down its own throat.
Spare a city you were paid, provoked, and entitled to burn — and be believed when you explain.
Burn the name your family gave the ancestor. Give the fire yours instead.

nodes.name: The Ancestor
nodes.role: Draconic avatar — battlefield-ending presence
nodes.lore: The molt completes, and the truth arrives with it: the wyrm was never behind them in the bloodline. It was ahead, waiting. What surfaces wears centuries comfortably and answers to no childhood name. Chroniclers dispute whether the sorcerer survives the becoming or merely furnishes it; the Ancestor declines to clarify.
nodes.playstyle: Draconic avatar. Flight, claimed ground, and a presence that ends most fights before they begin — devastating in the few that begin anyway.

abilities.name: Full Surfacing
abilities.desc: The last human proportions give way — wings, span, and a shadow armies recognize from stories.

abilities.name: Weight of Ages
abilities.desc: Your presence presses down like accumulated centuries; lesser wills kneel, flee, or empty their hands.

abilities.name: Hoardbind
abilities.desc: Claim ground and everything upon it; enemies on your claim move as through deep water.

abilities.name: Long Memory
abilities.desc: Wounds dealt to you are remembered against the giver's whole line, and the debt collects interest.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and finish the molt that has no other side.
Fly to the mountain from the dreams and find your own claw-marks already old there.
Hear your childhood name spoken and feel nothing in you turn toward it.
Outlive the last person who knew you human, and grieve them properly.
Begin a bloodline. Somewhere far down it, someone will dream a mountain.

nodes.name: Standing Storm
nodes.role: Storm incarnate — regional devastation
nodes.lore: Sailors insist there is weather that thinks, and the almanacs have begun agreeing. A Standing Storm appears twice in good histories — once as a person, once as a recorded meteorological event, and the dates align. Whether a body still walks at the center is a question the rain declines to answer.
nodes.playstyle: Storm incarnate. Disperse into weather and reform at will, govern the skies over whole regions, and fight as a front rather than a figure.

abilities.name: Weatherfront Body
abilities.desc: Disperse into the storm itself; blades part rain, and the rain answers back with lightning.

abilities.name: Season of Wrath
abilities.desc: Declare the weather over a region for days; the sky honors your grief or your mercy exactly.

abilities.name: The First Thunder
abilities.desc: One peal in which every plan requiring sound, sight, or steady nerve fails simultaneously.

abilities.name: Rainfall Census
abilities.desc: Passive — you feel everything your rain touches; nothing moves under your sky unnumbered.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and let the storm carry you, dissolved, a hundred miles — then reassemble unafraid.
Contest a weather-god above its own temple and settle for the draw.
Be entered twice in the same history: once as a name, once as a storm, dates matching.
Choose, once, over a place that wronged you, to rain gently.

nodes.name: The Unfated
nodes.role: Reality editor — outcome dictation
nodes.lore: Oracles skip them mid-prophecy without noticing the gap. Their pages arrive blank in books that were finished centuries ago. Historians find records of the Unfated erased not by any hand but by probability quietly withdrawing its cooperation. Whether they still choose things, or simply are what happens, remains — fittingly — undetermined.
nodes.playstyle: Outcome dictation. Unhappen events, declare endings in advance, and fight as a target no divination, prediction, or aimed fate can find.

abilities.name: Torn Page
abilities.desc: Your future cannot be read, targeted, or foretold; divinations cast at you return only weather.

abilities.name: The Unhappened
abilities.desc: Once per battle, one event that just occurred, did not.

abilities.name: Dictated Ending
abilities.desc: Declare how a duel ends before it begins; the world spends the fight arranging it.

abilities.name: Probability Zero
abilities.desc: Step briefly through an outcome no dice could reach — unharmed, elsewhere, already acting.
