nodes.lore: The Twicefought specialize in battle-echoes: the remembered hour of a dead hero, the shape of a charge that broke a line. They field soldiers no arrow can disappoint — recordings, faithful to the original down to the mud. Veterans find fighting beside a dead friend's finest hour either unbearable or holy.
nodes.playstyle: Deploy recorded fighters that replay their finest minutes. They cannot adapt, so you must: aim the past precisely at the present.

abilities.name: The Hero's Hour
abilities.desc: Summon a dead hero's remembered hour; it fights its old fight magnificently and cannot be persuaded it is elsewhere.

abilities.name: Cavalry, Remembered
abilities.desc: Replay a famous charge across the field; it tramples the living exactly where the dead once rode.

abilities.name: Faithful to the Mud
abilities.desc: Your echoes reproduce their conditions: original weather, original footing, original fear, applied to everyone standing inside the recording.

abilities.name: Played Through
abilities.desc: An echo allowed to complete its hour unbroken ends with its recorded triumph, dealt as real damage.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and record a battle from inside it; the Belfry counts survival as part of the assignment.
Summon a hero's hour before the hero's widow, and answer honestly when she asks if he is in there.
Fight beside your own recording of yourself, and do not look at it after the first exchange.
Learn the difference between an echo failing and an echo ending; only one of them is your fault.

nodes.name: Stormfetch
nodes.role: Terrain caster — recorded weather as control
nodes.lore: Stormfetches summon weather that already happened: the flood of a named year, the frost that stopped a war, one particular afternoon of lightning. The original is never harmed by the copy — the Belfry is emphatic on this — though coasts that survived a famous gale grow nervous when a Stormfetch visits.
nodes.playstyle: Reshape fights with archival weather. Slow to place, wide in effect; you win by choosing which day the battlefield is having.

abilities.name: The Named Gale
abilities.desc: Replay a catalogued storm over the field; it proceeds exactly as recorded, and you alone have read the record.

abilities.name: Old Fog
abilities.desc: Raise a remembered fog in which your allies were once brave; sight, morale, and arrows all behave accordingly.

abilities.name: The Flood of That Year
abilities.desc: Summon a historic flood in miniature; it follows its original course, and you have arranged for enemies to be standing in it.

abilities.name: Yesterday's Lightning
abilities.desc: Strike with lightning that already struck once; armor that survived the present offers no argument to the past.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and stand through a real storm while taking its impression; a copy taken from shelter is a copy of shelter.
Replay the frost of a named winter across a summer pond, and return the season unharmed.
Learn your storms' habits by heart — where the third gust goes, which wave undercuts — for the recording will not adjust to spare you.
Retire one weather forever when a town asks; some years should not be summonable within sight of their graves.

nodes.name: Gonfalonier
nodes.role: Muster commander — treaty armies under one banner
nodes.lore: The Gonfaloniers carry sealed banners heavy with ribboned treaties — a mustered company of champions from every Court, sworn for the day to one mortal will. Their doctrine is plain: war forgives no committees. A guest under the gonfalon obeys or departs. The Trothbound call this hiring friends by the hour; Gonfaloniers call it how sieges end.
nodes.playstyle: Field many guests briefly and command them absolutely. Your power is logistics: rotations, reliefs, and terms that conclude before loyalty is ever tested.

abilities.name: Sealed Banner
abilities.desc: Plant the gonfalon: all guests within its sight obey movement orders instantly and fight in formation regardless of Court.

abilities.name: Rotation of the Four
abilities.desc: Relieve tired guests with fresh ones mid-battle; each departing champion's remaining term transfers to its replacement as fury.

abilities.name: Terms of Muster
abilities.desc: Call three champions under one day-contract; they share commands, cooldowns, and an ironclad departure time.

abilities.name: The Banner Holds
abilities.desc: While the gonfalon stands planted, no guest can be banished, frightened, or turned; tear it down or endure them.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and muster champions of all four Courts under one banner for one battle; let none outshine the standard.
Draft the day-contract the Courts now call fair-and-iron; it has been copied since, never improved.
Hold a breach with guests alone for a night; command them by name, court, and hour, without once saying please.
Receive the gonfalon from a dying Gonfalonier and renegotiate every ribbon on it within the year; grief is not an extension.

nodes.name: Court Palatine
nodes.role: Fortress summoner — element-law wings as zones
nodes.lore: A Court Palatine keeps a palace with impossible wings: a parlor that has always been on fire, a stair of standing wind, a cellar the tide visits nightly. Within each wing the resident Court's law runs entire — the Palatine holding that half a welcome is an insult. Housefrith wardens call such houses occupied territory. Palatines agree, warmly.
nodes.playstyle: Deploy wings of your house onto the battlefield as zones of foreign law. Inside each, your guests are sovereign and your enemies are trespassers.

abilities.name: The Burning Parlor
abilities.desc: Unfold a wing where fire's law runs: flame cannot be quenched there, and your fire-guests cannot be harmed.

abilities.name: Tide Cellar
abilities.desc: Unfold a drowned wing; enemies fight submerged in a sea that remembers being deeper, while tide-guests move freely.

abilities.name: Gale Stair
abilities.desc: Unfold a wing of standing wind; allies climb it to vantage, and arrows entering are returned to sender.

abilities.name: Stone Gallery
abilities.desc: Unfold a gallery where stone's patience rules: enemy movement slows toward the geological, and your guests strike with buried weight.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and add a wing to your house that no mortal law survives in; live beside it calmly.
Host a full court — throne, retinue, weather — for a season, and present the household accounts with nothing missing but iron.
Walk each wing of your own house nightly wearing its law: burn, drown, blow, and stand; hosts who exempt themselves keep hotels.
Refuse the Housefrith examiners at your gate once, with perfect courtesy, in all four laws at once.

nodes.name: Fullpeal
nodes.role: Set-piece summoner — whole battles replayed exactly
nodes.lore: A Fullpeal rings an engagement through entire — every stroke in original order, hours of it, one error voiding the whole. The order holds that an edited echo is a lie, and that lies about the dead are how the other art starts. Changeringers call them worshippers of transcripts. Fullpeals do not answer; the record contains no reply.
nodes.playstyle: Commit to long, exact replays that transform the whole field. Immense if protected to completion; a broken peal returns nothing at all.

abilities.name: Ring It Through
abilities.desc: Begin a full battle-echo; the engagement replays around you in order, and grows in power each uninterrupted minute.

abilities.name: Method
abilities.desc: Hold the method: while you ring unerringly, your echoes cannot be dispelled, disbelieved, or drowned out.

abilities.name: No Substitutions
abilities.desc: Your echoes arrive with everything the record holds — allies, banners, weather, dread — or they do not arrive at all.

abilities.name: Voided Peal
abilities.desc: If your replay is broken, it ends honestly: the echo collapses, and the interrupter briefly hears everything at once.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and ring one recorded battle through from first arrow to burial detail without a substituted stroke.
Attend the Changeringers' recital, then ring the same hour afterward, whole; let the audience judge the difference.
Ring a massacre for a court of law, exactly; testimony that cannot lie has hanged better men than the guilty.
Break your own favorite recording rather than trim it once; the order admits no one who has not paid that.

nodes.name: Cellarer of Storms
nodes.role: Arsenal caster — shelved weathers, instant deployment
nodes.lore: Cellarers walk into disasters carrying bells, and walk out carrying the disaster. Their cellars shelve bottled hurricanes, the frosts of famous winters, one small labeled earthquake. The order's charge is preservation — a weather unrecorded dies with its witnesses. Groundswells call the cellars menageries. Cellarers reply that wild weather is lovely until you need some on a Tuesday.
nodes.playstyle: Fight from inventory. Every shelved weather is a spell slot; scarcity is real, so spend the right catastrophe, not the biggest one.

abilities.name: Off the Shelf
abilities.desc: Deploy any shelved weather instantly at full recorded strength; restocking requires attending another disaster personally.

abilities.name: Decanted Storm
abilities.desc: Pour out part of a stored storm as a directional blast, keeping the remainder shelved for later.

abilities.name: The Labeled Quake
abilities.desc: Uncork the small earthquake; it is small, it is labeled, and it is precisely under the enemy formation.

abilities.name: Acquisition
abilities.desc: Standing inside any hostile weather or area effect, bottle a copy of it for your cellar.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and take an impression of a disaster from inside its worst hour; the label must show your handwriting unshaken.
Build a cellar that satisfies the Courts you are not stealing weather, merely remembering it in bottles; the inspectors will test the distinction.
Trade shelf-space with a rival Cellarer at the annual exchange; arrive with duplicates and leave with nothing you already understand.
Answer a village's drought from your cellar without charge; the order audits generosity as strictly as inventory.

nodes.name: Trothbound
nodes.role: Bonded duo — one lifelong champion, total synchrony
nodes.lore: A Trothbound summons one being, once, and never needs to again: a champion met young, courted honestly, and pledged for life on both sides. The pairs grow strange together — mortals with tidal tempers, fire princes who learn to sleep. Gonfaloniers call the troth a leash with two ends. The Trothbound agree, and add: so is a handclasp.
nodes.playstyle: You and your troth-champion fight as one action: shared health, braided abilities, no other summons. Losing either half is losing the fight.

abilities.name: Braided Guard
abilities.desc: You and your champion parry for each other; damage to either may be taken by whichever of you it flatters less.

abilities.name: Courtship Gift
abilities.desc: Feed your champion its element mid-battle; it repays the gift doubled, immediately, and remembers it forever.

abilities.name: One Quarrel
abilities.desc: While you both strike one target, your blows interleave into a rhythm armor cannot answer.

abilities.name: Troth Unbroken
abilities.desc: If either of you falls, the other completes the current term at both your strengths, then grieves.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and be chosen back: the troth is offered by the champion, or it is not a troth.
Spend a year in your champion's court under its law, introduced honestly as what you are to each other.
Strike your two names from the rolls of separate summoners; the Accords list you as one name thereafter.
Outlast an argument that runs a decade; the Gonfaloniers keep a betting book on new troths, and hate paying out.

nodes.name: Housefrith
nodes.role: Aura controller — enforced truce, guarded sanctuary
nodes.lore: Housefrith wardens keep the neutral houses where rival Courts can meet, because someone must own a room the weather cannot vote in. Within their walls all power checks itself at the threshold — princes included, hosts included. Palatines call the houses cages with doilies. They answer that nothing so soothes a fire prince as an hour of being merely warm.
nodes.playstyle: Project a walking truce. Inside your bounds damage gutters, summons pause, and oaths are audible. You win fights by disallowing them.

abilities.name: Bread and Salt
abilities.desc: Offer bread and salt; any who accept cannot harm you or your allies until they leave your bounds.

abilities.name: Check Your Storm
abilities.desc: Entering your radius strips active empowerments from everyone, friend and enemy, and hangs them safely at the threshold like coats.

abilities.name: Sitting Room
abilities.desc: Unfold a sitting room mid-battle; those within cannot attack or be attacked, and the tea is real.

abilities.name: Breach of Peace
abilities.desc: The first creature to break truce inside your bounds takes every point of harm it attempted, witnessed and notarized.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and keep a house where Flame and Tide winter together; end spring with the same number of walls.
Take a storm from a gale prince at your threshold, keep it hung safely, and return it undiminished at his departure.
Be struck by a guest and answer with the law, not the poker; a house's peace must survive its keeper's temper.
Decline the Palatines' invitation to see how welcomes are really kept; decline it every year; enjoy declining it.

nodes.name: Changeringer
nodes.role: Combo summoner — spliced moments rung in sequence
nodes.lore: Changeringers ring moments out of order on purpose: the cavalry's arrival, thrice; the hero's best minute cut free of his worst hour. To them a recording is bell-metal, not scripture — history did its part, and now it can work shifts. Fullpeals accuse them of making things that never happened. Changeringers agree: that is what making means.
nodes.playstyle: Chain short echoes into sequences of your own design. Enormous flexibility, no single great summon; you assemble other people's finest seconds into hours that serve you.

abilities.name: Cut to the Charge
abilities.desc: Skip an echo to its decisive moment, summoning the impact without the approach; costs double, arrives instantly.

abilities.name: Round Again
abilities.desc: Loop one echo's best three seconds up to three times; each repetition rings thinner but faster.

abilities.name: Spliced Hour
abilities.desc: Ring two moments simultaneously as one: last winter's ice under this summer's charge; enemies must survive both at once.

abilities.name: Rough Splice
abilities.desc: Join two echoes badly on purpose; the seam screams, disorienting everything nearby that remembers either original.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and ring a sequence no hour ever contained, and make a hardened company flinch at history that never was.
Cut a drowned fleet's last hour to the thirty seconds that would have saved it, and donate the arrangement to the naval college.
Win the Belfry's tourney of arrangements with a piece the Fullpeals cannot fault for one false stroke — only for the order they arrive in.
Splice nothing into an echo that its people did not truly do somewhere, sometime; the order's one law, and the gallows behind it.

nodes.name: Groundswell
nodes.role: Site controller — wakes the land's own memory
nodes.lore: Groundswells carry no bottles. They arrive early, walk the ground, and learn what it is trying not to remember — the flood under the orchard, the battle under the barley. Woken at home, an echo comes entire, with a weight no cellar preserves. Cellarers call this foraging. Groundswells call the cellars very brave, very small weather.
nodes.playstyle: Scout terrain for sleeping history, then wake it under the enemy. Devastating on old ground, humbler on new; choose your battlefields the way generals wish they could.

abilities.name: Walk the Ground
abilities.desc: Learn every echo sleeping within a mile; old blood, old water, and old fire announce themselves loudest.

abilities.name: Wake the Flood
abilities.desc: Rouse the ground's remembered water; it rises through the soil along its original course, entire and unbottled.

abilities.name: Under the Barley
abilities.desc: Wake the battle beneath the field; its recorded lines form around your enemies, who are standing where the dying happened.

abilities.name: Let It Sleep
abilities.desc: Soothe a woken echo down early; the grateful ground holds firm beneath allies and treacherous beneath enemies thereafter.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and wake a city's founding fire one street at a time, then settle it again with nothing new burned.
Spend a season learning one meadow; when you can say what it holds in March, the order will ask about April.
Wake something a Cellarer bottled a copy of, side by side, before judges; let the ground's version speak for the doctrine.
Never take an impression again; surrender your bottles, and be trusted by the dirt.

nodes.name: The Standing Invitation
nodes.role: Grand muster — allies arrive without being called
nodes.lore: Histories count four Standing Invitations and dispute all of them. Their terms are so old, so fair, and so exactly kept that summoning becomes unnecessary: the banner is planted, and things arrive asking to stand under it. At Redwater Bridge nobody was called. The muster rolls for that day run to nine hundred names, none of them mortal.
nodes.playstyle: Stop casting summons; maintain terms instead. Allies accumulate wherever you stand your ground, faster in worse odds. Your only real cooldown is your reputation.

abilities.name: Open Muster
abilities.desc: While your banner stands, an uninvited ally arrives every few seconds, drawn by terms too good to hear about secondhand.

abilities.name: Terms Preceding
abilities.desc: Your reputation arrives before you do: enemy summons and hirelings check your terms, and some defect on the spot.

abilities.name: Nine Hundred Names
abilities.desc: Invoke Redwater: for ten seconds, everything that ever fought under your colors fights under them again, briefly and gladly.

abilities.name: Better Terms
abilities.desc: Offer an enemy's summoned or contracted creature honest improvement; the paperwork resolves in your favor unless theirs was fair.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and settle every term you ever signed until no Court holds a single unmet line of yours; the Invitation stands only on even ground.
Plant your banner in a lost battle you were not paid, asked, or advised to attend, and hold until things begin arriving.
Turn away more help than you accept, courteously; a muster anyone may join is a mob, and your terms say company.
Let the four Courts audit your whole life at once, jointly, without notice; pour the tea yourself.

nodes.name: Prince of Guests
nodes.role: Court summoner — principalities answer as family
nodes.lore: Somewhere in each principality stands a wing kept for one mortal: fireproof linens, a bed of standing wind. The Prince of Guests is royalty by pure reception — crowned nowhere, received everywhere. When they call now, the Courts do not send champions. They come themselves, the way family comes, which is to say entirely, and with opinions.
nodes.playstyle: Summon courts, not champions: thrones, retinues, weather and all. Slow, grand arrivals that reorder the battlefield's politics as thoroughly as its terrain.

abilities.name: The Court Comes
abilities.desc: Summon an entire elemental court in procession; its passage across the field is the attack.

abilities.name: Kinsright
abilities.desc: A principality intervenes to avenge harm done to you, uncontracted and unasked, as family does; you cannot invoke this, only deserve it.

abilities.name: Fireproof Linens
abilities.desc: You and your allies hold guest-standing in every element: unburned, undrowned, unburied, unblown.

abilities.name: State Visit
abilities.desc: Announce a visit upon enemy ground; protocol clears it before you — wards, traps, and illusions withdrawn like unsuitable furniture.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and be invited to all four courts in one year without requesting, hinting, or deserving it less than utterly.
Sleep one night in each principality unwarded; guests who check the locks are merely visitors.
Refuse a crown offered by a court in earnest; a prince of guests reigns only in the arriving.
Seat all four Courts at your name-day table and survive the precedence dispute; the dispute is the honor.

nodes.name: The Carillon
nodes.role: Living archive — any recorded hour, rung entire
nodes.lore: A Carillon no longer carries bells; the hours hang in them. Every echo the Belfry ever certified — and several it burned — can be rung from their standing body, entire, in order, at will. Histories dispute whether the last Carillon died. The Belfry's position is that she finished, which they insist is different.
nodes.playstyle: Your repertoire is the whole archive. Answer any battlefield with the exact hour it fears most; the cost is that you increasingly ring, rather than live.

abilities.name: The Hanging Hours
abilities.desc: Ring any echo in the archive without preparation; the right hour for this fight is always already hung.

abilities.name: Full Tower
abilities.desc: Ring three whole echoes at once, interleaved; enemies caught in all three experience history's undivided attention.

abilities.name: Sounding Board
abilities.desc: Blows against you ring you like bronze, recording the attacker; their own strike replays against them within the minute.

abilities.name: The Burned Shelf
abilities.desc: Ring one of the forbidden hours the Belfry destroyed; nothing survives unchanged, including your standing with the Belfry.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and take the whole archive into memory as the Belfry burns its duplicates behind you, shelf by shelf; you are the copy now.
Ring, on request, the hour any petitioner names, for a year and a day, refusing none and trimming nothing.
Hang your own recorded life among the rest, uncatalogued; the order will know you are ready when you cannot find it either.
Answer the question every Carillon is asked — is anyone in there — the way the truth requires: no one; everything.

nodes.name: The Almanack
nodes.role: Weather sovereign — the complete book of storms
nodes.lore: The cellar has grown into a library, and the library into a person. The Almanack holds every weather since witnesses began: the flood of every named year, each frost that mattered, the specific gale your grandmother meant. Kingdoms consult them before planting wars. Histories dispute only whether the weather now checks the Almanack before happening.
nodes.playstyle: Open the book and choose the day. Any recorded weather at any scale, promptly; your only questions are which year, and how much of it this battlefield can hold.

abilities.name: The Named Year
abilities.desc: Deploy every weather from one calendar year in sequence across the field; the year is your choice, and some years were terrible.

abilities.name: The Storm She Meant
abilities.desc: Summon the specific storm a witness remembers; it strikes with the force of the telling, which has grown.

abilities.name: Index of Frosts
abilities.desc: Apply the exact frost that once stopped an army identical to this one; precedent, correctly cited, repeats itself.

abilities.name: Out of Season
abilities.desc: Loose a weather into the wrong season; unopposed by its natural checks, it grows a size in the first minute.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and shelve the last missing year; the collection is complete when the oldest Court cannot name a rain you lack.
Lend the whole library to a burning province and take it all back after, bottle by bottle, unthanked.
Record the weather of one entire year in person, outdoors, on every coast the guild can reach; delegating a single afternoon disqualifies.
Bind your own last breath into the collection's final bottle, labeled like all the others; an almanack that exempts its keeper is a diary.

nodes.name: The Consort
nodes.role: Bonded avatar — two beings, one legend
nodes.lore: One Trothbound courted the heir of a drowning sea, and both worlds attended the wedding, armed. The Consort is what the pair became: one legend with a shoreline's temper and a mortal's stubbornness about mornings. Histories dispute which of them outlived the other. The coastal position is that neither has yet agreed to.
nodes.playstyle: Fight as one creature with two natures: mortal precision inside tidal mass. You are never flanked, rarely hurried, and impossible to widow.

abilities.name: Two Natures
abilities.desc: Alternate mortal and tidal stances every few seconds; damage taken in one is healed in the other.

abilities.name: Marriage Portion
abilities.desc: Your spouse's dowry was a sea; spend a wave of it as a weapon, a wall, or a road.

abilities.name: Parted and Rejoined
abilities.desc: Split into two combatants mid-fight, then rejoin; enemies engaged by either take the reunion as a crashing flank.

abilities.name: No Widowing
abilities.desc: If either nature is slain, the other refuses the precedent; the slain half returns with the next tide, which you may schedule.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and celebrate the hundredth year of the troth in both worlds at once; attendance is not optional for either of you.
Hold a coastline against an invading Court as a couple, and file the engagement under domestic matters.
Teach a young Trothbound pair to argue safely; the order's future is decided in other people's kitchens.
Outlive the wedding guests, the officiant, and the objections; renew nothing — the vow was drawn fairly the first time.

nodes.name: Housepeace
nodes.role: Absolute sanctuary — war cannot enter
nodes.lore: There is a house where wars go to stop, and the house has a pulse. Housepeace is the warden grown indistinguishable from the peace they keep: walk in armed and find yourself, somehow, holding a cup instead. Three empires have tested this. The house keeps their standards in the hall closet, with the umbrellas.
nodes.playstyle: Extend the house outward until the battle is indoors, and therefore over. You do not stop blows; you make them impolite, then impossible.

abilities.name: The Hall Closet
abilities.desc: Confiscate the weapons, standards, and active spells of all who enter your peace; returned on departure, mostly.

abilities.name: Come In Out of That
abilities.desc: Pull a combatant out of the fight and into the house; they may not leave until calmer, and the house decides.

abilities.name: The Guest Book
abilities.desc: All who ever sheltered under your peace are entered; entered names cannot raise arms against the house or each other inside it.

abilities.name: Perpetual Hearth
abilities.desc: Your peace persists wherever you have kept it once; old battlefields you quieted stay quiet, permanently, and count as your house.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and stop a war by being between it; both armies must camp, cool, and leave by different roads unbloodied.
Grow the house by one room for every peace kept; when you can no longer find the original walls, neither can war.
Refuse three empires' offer to charter your house as neutral ground; charters expire, and the house does not.
Die once, quietly, in the kitchen; notice that the peace does not even flicker; return to work.

nodes.name: The Otherwise
nodes.role: Counterfactual summoner — the unplayed arrangements
nodes.lore: An Otherwise rings arrangements no hour ever held — real moments, reordered into days that never dawned: the relief arriving early, the fleet catching its wind. Veterans weep at battles they now almost remember. The Belfry certifies each piece as fiction, loudly, in writing, because the alternative is admitting how many wars turn on the almost.
nodes.playstyle: Assemble the fight that should be happening from pieces of fights that did. Peerless setup and misdirection; your worst enemy is an opponent with no history.

abilities.name: Early Relief
abilities.desc: Ring the reinforcement that historically came too late, now punctual; it fights with the fervor of the pardoned.

abilities.name: Almost-Memory
abilities.desc: Enemies face the defeat they nearly suffered once; any who have ever truly lost a battle fight this one already flinching.

abilities.name: Unplayed Change
abilities.desc: Ring a change never rung: the field briefly obeys an order of events that did not occur, and you have rehearsed it.

abilities.name: Merely Outvoted
abilities.desc: Overlay one exchange with its otherwise: the missed parry lands, the fallen ally stands; the past is unchanged, merely outvoted.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and ring an hour that never struck until a room of veterans remembers it differently; then confess, and ring it again anyway.
Assemble the victory a dead general never got, from moments he truly commanded, and play it at his tomb; invent nothing but the order.
Let the Fullpeals audit every splice you have ever made against their transcripts; win on provenance, not on beauty.
Refuse to ring the otherwise of your own life; the order forgives everything but that.

nodes.name: The Sown Hour
nodes.role: Land invoker — whole regions remember on command
nodes.lore: A Groundswell walks far enough and the walking becomes planting. The Sown Hour has waked so much ground that the ground now listens for them: fields hold their old battles ready, rivers keep their floods coiled, and a stamped heel three provinces away brings the harvest up armed. Farmers leave them gifts. Generals leave them alone.
nodes.playstyle: Prepare theaters, not spells. Seed ground with primed echoes on the march, then trigger whole regions at once. Nothing about you is fast; everything about you is already there.

abilities.name: Seedfall
abilities.desc: Prime any ground you cross with a sleeping echo of itself; primed ground can be triggered from any distance.

abilities.name: Three Provinces Away
abilities.desc: Trigger every seeded echo across a region at once; you do not need to see them, and traditionally you are elsewhere.

abilities.name: Armed Acres
abilities.desc: The ground raises its remembered defenders around your allies wherever they stand on land that has ever been defended.

abilities.name: Undisturbed
abilities.desc: Still a region's echoes so deeply that no summoner, echo-caller, or necromancer can raise anything there for a year.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and walk a continent's worst ground end to end, waking nothing, seeding everything; the survey takes years, and the years are the point.
Answer an invasion without attending it; let the beaches remember the last one for you.
Be asked for by name by the dirt of a place you have never visited; the introduction travels underground.
Sow one echo you will never trigger, unmarked, as a gift to whichever future the ground prefers.

nodes.name: The Gonfalon
nodes.role: Living standard — the muster that outlives bearers
nodes.lore: The bearer dies; the banner has stopped noticing. The Gonfalon is the standard itself, kept by the world as the place help gathers: it flies where the terms are fair and the odds are not, and things arrive — Courts, strangers, weather with opinions. Whoever carries it is briefly the oldest treaty walking. It is never carried far alone.
nodes.playstyle: Play as the office: raise the standard and adjudicate what arrives. Your power is the muster itself — endless, various, and sworn to the banner, not to you.

abilities.name: Where It Flies
abilities.desc: Plant the Gonfalon anywhere; the location becomes just cause, and every fair-dealing power in range knows it.

abilities.name: The Oldest Treaty
abilities.desc: You count as signatory to every fair contract ever kept under the banner; invoke any one of their protections.

abilities.name: Dismissed to Mend
abilities.desc: No one falls while the Gonfalon flies: the dying are recalled instead — rung home like guests, to mend, and to return.

abilities.name: The Muster Entire
abilities.desc: Once an age, unfurl fully: everything that ever answered the banner answers at once, and the age remembers why.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and carry the banner until you notice the wind has stopped mattering to it; set it down; remain standing; understand.
Be succeeded while alive: hand the Gonfalon on and watch it treat your successor exactly as it treated you; this is the promotion.
Plant it once for a cause history will call wrong, and feel it refuse the ground; thereafter, let the banner do the choosing.
Become the place help gathers: not the bearer, not the terms — the fact, known everywhere, that fair help arrives. Fly.

nodes.name: The Set Place
nodes.role: Omnipresent guest — every table, every threshold
nodes.lore: In every world, tables keep one place set for someone who might come. That custom is a person now. The Set Place attends as invited — always, everywhere, by a custom older than tables — and whatever shares a meal with them cannot be an enemy until the plates are cleared. Some hosts stack dishes quickly. It rarely helps.
nodes.playstyle: Arrive anywhere hospitality has ever been offered, instantly, with a guest's full rights. Fights near any table, hearth, or shared meal bend to your law.

abilities.name: Always Expected
abilities.desc: Travel instantly to anywhere a place has ever been set for a guest; somewhere nearby, one always has.

abilities.name: Until You Rise
abilities.desc: All who sit at your table cannot fight until the meal ends, and the meal ends when you rise.

abilities.name: Guest's Portion
abilities.desc: Take the guest's share of anything present — the enemy's strength, their luck, their standing spells — one polite portion at a time.

abilities.name: Withdrawn Welcome
abilities.desc: Strip an enemy of every standing invitation: their summons, reinforcements, and safe grounds no longer receive them.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and attend, in one night, every table that ever set you a place; eat little; be seen at all of them.
Give away your wing in each principality and keep only the standing right to arrive; a guest with property is a landlord.
Sit once at an enemy's table uninvited and be, by the end of the soup, invited; this is the whole examination.
Become the reason tables keep an extra chair: not remembered — expected. Somewhere tonight a place is set; be worthy of every one at once.

nodes.name: The Aftertone
nodes.role: Eternal resonance — everything sounded, still sounding
nodes.lore: Strike any bell and listen past the note: under the fading is a floor of sound that does not fade. The Belfry teaches that this is physics. The Belfry is being polite. The Aftertone is the standing hum of everything that ever happened, held; every echo ever rung was one syllable of it, briefly lifted back into hearing.
nodes.playstyle: You no longer summon echoes; you turn up portions of the everything already sounding. Range and repertoire are total; restraint becomes your entire skill ceiling.

abilities.name: Lift the Hum
abilities.desc: Raise any past event, anywhere, into audibility and effect; nothing is stored, nothing fetched — it was already playing.

abilities.name: Sympathetic World
abilities.desc: Every resonant thing on the field — bells, blades, armor, teeth — plays your chosen hour along with you.

abilities.name: The Withheld Hum
abilities.desc: Withdraw the world's undertone from a zone: within it nothing echoes, nothing repeats, and echo-craft of every school fails, including yours.

abilities.name: First Vibration
abilities.desc: Ring the oldest sound the hum contains, from before witnesses; those who hear it briefly remember the world empty, and stop.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and stop ringing; sit with the hum until you can no longer tell which of you is sustaining the other. That is correct.
Be rung: let a young Yesterbell take your impression and play you back to yourself; approve the likeness.
Keep the world's sound through one entire silence — the Belfry will not say which — so that afterward there is an afterward.
Answer every bell rung in grief, anywhere, always, with the note under the note: still here; still sounding; nothing kept is lost.

nodes.name: The Weatherhouse
nodes.role: Sky custodian — weather is issued and recalled
nodes.lore: Weather has to be somewhere when it is not happening. It is in the Weatherhouse. What began as a cellar of bottled storms is now the world's back room: rains queue between engagements, winters hang like coats, and the office that keeps it — one keeper at a time — signs each season out and, some years, back in.
nodes.playstyle: Control what weather exists at all. Issue storms to allied theaters, decline them to enemy ones, and recall anything the sky is currently doing, anywhere, as overdue.

abilities.name: Signed Out
abilities.desc: Issue any weather in the collection to any location in the world, effective within the hour, durable until recalled.

abilities.name: Recall Notice
abilities.desc: Recall the weather an enemy is currently using, enjoying, or standing in; it returns to the house, apologizing.

abilities.name: The Back Room
abilities.desc: Step into the Weatherhouse and out of the battle; attacks meant for you are shelved, labeled, and eventually returned.

abilities.name: Closed for Inventory
abilities.desc: Suspend all weather everywhere, briefly: no wind, no rain, no lightning but yours; the sky holds its breath while you count.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and inventory the sky itself; find the discrepancies; do not publicize what the missing weathers imply.
Take the post no one appointed you to, because the door stood open and the queue of rains was getting restless.
Issue a kind year to a place history had scheduled otherwise, and log the substitution as routine.
Train no successor; leave the catalogue legible and the shelves labeled; the house has always chosen its own keeper from the queue.

nodes.name: The Anniversary
nodes.role: Recurring force — devotion kept as weather
nodes.lore: Every year on the same morning, a tide crosses one coast gently and is gone by noon, regardless of moon or war. Sailors plan by it. Lovers marry in it. It is not weather; it is an appointment being kept. The Anniversary is what remains of the Consort: two vows with the mortal parts worn away, arriving on schedule, forever.
nodes.playstyle: Schedule your presences: declare returns, then arrive at them with tidal totality. Between returns you are mild, patient, and very hard to remove from a calendar.

abilities.name: The Appointed Morning
abilities.desc: Declare a time; at that moment you arrive everywhere on the field at once, as a tide, briefly and entirely.

abilities.name: Kept Every Year
abilities.desc: Effects you place recur annually on their date, forever, without upkeep; old battlefields keep your interventions like festivals.

abilities.name: Vow Weather
abilities.desc: Around you, promises acquire weather: kept ones fair, broken ones squalls; enemy oathbreakers fight in permanent rain.

abilities.name: Soft Landfall
abilities.desc: Your arrivals harm nothing you love; the tide sorts friend from foe by long practice, and has never once been wrong.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and keep the morning through your own dissolution; the first year no one carries the vow and the tide still comes, it is you.
Add new appointments rarely — once a century at most; a calendar crowded with miracles is merely a climate.
Be forgotten as a couple and kept as a custom; attend your own festival unrecognized, annually, and find this sufficient.
Miss nothing. Ever. The whole art was always the leaving and the coming back; you are what it looks like perfected.

nodes.name: The Salt Between
nodes.role: Cosmic truce — the bond of salt, enforced
nodes.lore: Between any two who have eaten under one roof there is salt, and the salt does not expire. Housepeace kept one house; the Salt Between is the law the house was practicing for. It stands wherever hospitality was ever honestly given — a bond older than the Courts, thinner than air, and, since one quiet death in a kitchen, structural.
nodes.playstyle: Enforce the oldest truce at world scale. You do not prevent violence; you make it cost the violator their place at every table there is.

abilities.name: Salt Does Not Expire
abilities.desc: Any two beings who ever shared a meal count as truce-bound in your presence; most armies discover they are mostly bound.

abilities.name: The First Table
abilities.desc: Invoke the meal at the beginning of hospitality itself; every creature that has ever been a guest is briefly your guest.

abilities.name: Cast Out
abilities.desc: Strip a truce-breaker of guesthood everywhere: no roof shelters them, no fire warms them, no table admits them, until amends.

abilities.name: One Roof
abilities.desc: Declare the sky a roof; everyone beneath it is indoors, under house-peace, and the house is very old and very strict.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and find the first table — set before the Courts, before weather, before guests; the salt on it has not been touched. Sit.
Return to your body in the kitchen, or do not; the peace no longer requires it, and the choice is the last thing the office asks of a person.
Feed one enemy of everything you are, at your own table, well; the law must be seen to hold even against its keeper's grief.
Be the reason strangers still trust bread from strangers, everywhere, always; nothing else is asked; nothing less is enough.

nodes.name: The Untaken
nodes.role: Keeper of otherwise — the unplayed, held
nodes.lore: Every hour that struck, struck instead of others. The Untaken keeps those: the standing archive of everything real that was never arranged — retreats never sounded, mercies never shown, the whole inventory of otherwise. The world keeps them the way it keeps regret: universally, quietly, consulted at night. Histories cannot dispute them; histories are the part they did not keep.
nodes.playstyle: Fight with the weight of every alternative. Each enemy action arrives alongside your summoned account of what it could have been — and the comparison has force.

abilities.name: The Quiet Inventory
abilities.desc: Summon the unplayed version of any ability used against you this battle; yours resolves second, informed.

abilities.name: Spared, Elsewhere
abilities.desc: Show an enemy the arrangement in which they were spared; they fight the rest of the battle knowing the terms existed.

abilities.name: Sounded Retreat
abilities.desc: Ring the retreat an enemy commander never called; discipline obeys the older order, and their line withdraws in good order, confused.

abilities.name: Into Keeping
abilities.desc: When any effect on the field fails, misses, or fizzles, you may keep it; failed things enter your archive, and can be rung.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and take custody of the unplayed entire; the handover is from no one, and the inventory has been waiting for a keeper.
Keep the otherwise of your own life now, as the office requires; keep it unrung, as the order once required; both are still true.
Be consulted at night by the great and answer none of them aloud; what they do next with the silence is theirs, and recorded.
Hold every almost so that the world can bear to be only what it is; this is the whole office, and it is enormous.

nodes.name: The Light Sleeper
nodes.role: World's memory — all ground primed to wake
nodes.lore: Farmers say the earth sleeps lightly, and they say it carefully. The Light Sleeper is why: every acre of the world now holds its history at a doze — floods coiled, battles ready, first fires banked — one listener from waking. The office does not punish. It only means that nowhere, ever again, is anything that happened entirely over.
nodes.playstyle: The planet is your seeded ground. Anywhere, anything that ever happened there is one gesture from happening again; your restraint is the only reason geography behaves.

abilities.name: One Gesture
abilities.desc: Wake any echo sleeping in any ground on the world, from where you stand, at original scale.

abilities.name: Rolled Over
abilities.desc: The ground shifts beneath an army as the world turns in its sleep; formations, fortifications, and confidence rearrange.

abilities.name: Put to Bed
abilities.desc: Lay any active effect, summon, or catastrophe down into the ground beneath it; the ground files it with the rest.

abilities.name: Never Entirely Over
abilities.desc: Anything that has happened this battle — any strike, ward, or arrival — you may have happen again, once, from the ground up.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and lie down on the oldest ground there is; match your breathing to something enormous; do not wake it; do not entirely wake again yourself.
Hold the world's whole memory at a doze for one year without a single accidental waking; the year will include provocations.
Let one field finish its worst day at last, played through to quiet, and fallow forever after; even memory deserves endings.
Be the reason nothing anywhere is lost, and the reason it stays lying down; the world sleeps because you sleep lightly for it.

families.name: Cleric
families.tagline: A mortal lens for a divine and terrible light.
families.description: A Cleric is what happens when a god needs hands. Sworn at a shrine, trained in scripture and field surgery, they carry a mace in one fist and a prayer in the other, learning that faith under pressure is a muscle, not a mood. Some become the god's wrath, some its open channel — and every miracle is entered in a ledger somebody must eventually pay.

nodes.name: Cleric
nodes.role: Hybrid support — mending and radiant reprisal
nodes.lore: Every shrine keeps a ledger of novices: farm children who prayed and were answered, soldiers who bargained in a ditch and lived. The Cleric is the one who came back to pay. They learn scripture, surgery, and the weight of a mace, because a god's mercy travels through hands that work.
nodes.playstyle: A midline hybrid: close wounds with short litanies, crack the profane with a blessed mace, and bank Favor from both to fuel the next answered prayer.

abilities.name: Litany of Binding
abilities.desc: Chant a closing verse over an ally's wound; it restores health and stanches bleeding for as long as the verse holds.

abilities.name: Censured Blow
abilities.desc: Strike with a consecrated mace; against undead and the oath-broken, the impact flares for additional radiant damage.

abilities.name: Vigil Ward
abilities.desc: Raise a brief ward over an ally within reach, absorbing the next blow meant for them.

abilities.name: Kindled Favor
abilities.desc: Mending the faithful or striking the profane builds Favor; spend it to double the potency of your next prayer.

progressionSteps: Keep the vigil-night in your god's shrine, dusk bell to dawn bell, awake and silent; if the candle gutters, begin again.
Learn the Eighty Small Prayers by rote, and the field-surgeon's knots besides — the god mends through hands that know their work.
Work your first answered prayer before witnesses — a fever broken, a wound closed — and have it entered in the shrine's ledger.
Carry a stranger's corpse through unquiet country to consecrated burial, and do not set it down.

nodes.name: Warpriest
nodes.role: Frontline smiter — melee pressure and battle-blessing
nodes.lore: Some clerics learn the god answers loudest from inside a shield-wall. The Warpriest carries doctrine at mace-length: chrism on the haft, verses timed to the push of pike. Companies pay well for one and sleep better besides, for a Warpriest's blessing is applied like medicine — directly, and without asking.
nodes.playstyle: Fight in the press. Anoint your weapon, bless comrades by the shoulder-clap, and convert every landed blow into wrath the whole line can spend.

abilities.name: Anointed Haft
abilities.desc: Dress your mace with war-chrism; strikes deal radiant damage and mark the struck for your allies' next blows.

abilities.name: Shoulder-Clap Blessing
abilities.desc: Grip a comrade mid-fight to grant vigor and immunity to fear for six heartbeats.

abilities.name: Wrathful Doxology
abilities.desc: Roar a verse of judgment; enemies in earshot stagger while the faithful strike harder.

abilities.name: Penitent's Toll
abilities.desc: An overhead blow that rings like a struck bell, dazing the target and dragging its fury onto you.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10, then stand your first shield-wall from horn to rout without letting the prayer break in your mouth.
Take up the mace of a fallen warpriest and carry it home to their shrine for reconsecration; earn the right to keep it.
Bless a company on the eve of battle, and be there, still standing, to bless what remains of it after.
Shatter something unholy with your own arms — an idol, a false relic, a fane — and bring a fragment back as proof.

nodes.name: Vessel
nodes.role: Backline conduit — healing and foresight
nodes.lore: Most clerics ask; a Vessel opens. They stop shaping prayers and start hosting answers — mendings no surgeon can chart, dreams that arrive true, sentences in their mouths that belong to someone vast. The temples honor them carefully, the way one honors a door that does not fully close.
nodes.playstyle: A fragile backline channel. Position first, then choose: pour the god into a dying ally, or into three seconds of foresight the enemy cannot afford.

abilities.name: Open Channel
abilities.desc: Still yourself completely; your next miracle costs no Favor but takes double from your body instead.

abilities.name: Mending Past Craft
abilities.desc: Unmake an injury as though it never landed, restoring health beyond what surgery could explain.

abilities.name: Three Seconds Hence
abilities.desc: Glimpse the immediate future; one ally gains the dodge or parry you witnessed.

abilities.name: Borrowed Tongue
abilities.desc: Speak a sentence not your own; enemies who hear it falter, having learned something true about their deaths.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10 and fast in the sanctuary until the first true vision arrives; write it down before you understand it.
Heal a wound no surgeon would touch, and accept without complaint the ache it leaves in your own body.
Deliver an unwelcome prophecy to someone powerful, word for word, softening nothing.
Let the god speak through you once at full voice, and be recognizably yourself the morning after.

nodes.name: Judicar
nodes.role: Melee striker — single-target holy execution
nodes.lore: The crusade needs judges more than it admits. A Judicar reads the charges aloud before the blow falls — apostate priests, false saints, commanders who consecrated what they should have burned. They are licensed to sentence the anointed, which is why bishops greet them warmly and count the silver afterward.
nodes.playstyle: Build a case in combat: name crimes to stack the judgment mark, deny escape and succor, then deliver a verdict that scales with everything proven.

abilities.name: Read the Charges
abilities.desc: Name the target's offenses aloud; each charge deepens their judgment mark and amplifies your eventual verdict.

abilities.name: Verdict
abilities.desc: A two-handed sentence of a blow; damage rises with accumulated charges and the target's missing health.

abilities.name: No Sanctuary
abilities.desc: While your eyes hold them, the marked cannot be healed, hidden, or spirited away.

abilities.name: Iron Contrition
abilities.desc: Executing a marked sinner remits your own wounds, restoring health for every charge proven.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and sit the Assize of Embers: recite the crimes of ten heresiarchs from memory, and the lawful sentence for each.
Carry out a sealed sentence against one of your own order, alone, and return the seal unbroken.
Refuse a bribe worth more than your life, and enter the offer, with names, into the record.
Hear the full confession of the one you were sent to kill, and proceed unless the god stays your hand.

nodes.name: Consecrant
nodes.role: Frontline support — consecrated ground and warband blessing
nodes.lore: Where a Consecrant walks, the earth is sworn in. They hallow trenches into naves, turn a shield-wall's footing into church floor, and plant standards the dead cannot pass. Siege captains requisition them like ordnance, and old soldiers polish their boots before crossing ground a Consecrant has claimed.
nodes.playstyle: Claim ground and make it argue for you: plant standards, chain blessings down the line, and let trespassers ring the unseen bell.

abilities.name: Hallowing Stride
abilities.desc: Ground you cross stays consecrated for a time; allies standing on it resist fear and bleed slower.

abilities.name: Planted Standard
abilities.desc: Drive a blessed standard into the earth; nearby allies gain armor and the dead cannot rise in its shadow.

abilities.name: Rite of the Unbroken Line
abilities.desc: Chain a blessing through adjacent allies; while the line holds, damage is shared and none can be routed.

abilities.name: Trespass Bell
abilities.desc: Unhallowed creatures entering your ground ring a bell only you hear, taking radiant damage and standing revealed.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and reconsecrate a ruined chapel alone, threshold-stone to roof-beam, over forty days of unbroken rite.
Hold one piece of hallowed ground against desecration until relieved, however long relief takes to come.
Bury the dead of both armies after a battle, and hallow the field so thoroughly that neither side rises.
Learn the boundary-rites of three orders not your own, well enough to say where each of them errs.

nodes.name: Lazarene
nodes.role: Dedicated healer — triage, transference, and revival
nodes.lore: Named for the first one raised, Lazarenes work where medicine surrenders: plague-houses, drowned villages, the third day after a battle. Their miracles keep a ledger — every returned breath is owed, and they know precisely what a life costs. It makes them gentle, exact, and difficult to sit beside at supper.
nodes.playstyle: A ledger-keeping healer. Stay deaths rather than prevent all damage, take wounds into your own flesh, and spend banked breath on saves medicine cannot copy.

abilities.name: Ledger of Breath
abilities.desc: Every life you save is entered; spend entries to fuel miracles beyond medicine's reach.

abilities.name: Stay the Hour
abilities.desc: An ally struck down does not die for ten heartbeats; what you do with them is yours.

abilities.name: Take the Wound
abilities.desc: Draw an ally's injury into your own flesh at half its weight; both of you keep the scar.

abilities.name: Second Breath
abilities.desc: Call a soul back across the threshold within a candle's burning; it returns owing, and so do you.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and serve a full plague-season in a lazar-house, leaving only when the last bell stops ringing.
Bring back someone gone past all argument, and pay what it costs without haggling.
Sit deathwatch for a stranger from first rattle to last stillness, and learn what dying asks of the living.
Keep your ledger honest: record every life you lost as carefully as every life you kept.

nodes.name: Godspeaker
nodes.role: Control support — foresight and spoken fate
nodes.lore: The visions come whether or not a Godspeaker asks. Kings keep them close and never comfortable; generals hear how battles end before the first arrow and hate them for it. The god does not soften anything, and neither, by vow, may they — clarity is the whole office.
nodes.playstyle: Fight from prophecy: call enemy actions to cancel them, hand allies the first strike against what you foresaw, and pay the toll for every silence.

abilities.name: It Was Written
abilities.desc: Declare an enemy's next action aloud; if it comes to pass, it fails, having been foretold.

abilities.name: Thread of Hours
abilities.desc: Glimpse the fight's coming moments; allies you warn strike first against what you saw.

abilities.name: Unwelcome Truth
abilities.desc: Tell an enemy how it dies; it fights the rest of the battle knowing.

abilities.name: Prophet's Toll
abilities.desc: Each prophecy spoken this battle sharpens the next; each withheld bleeds you slowly.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and endure the Long Seeing: nine days blindfolded in the crypt while the visions run their course.
Prophesy in public, be laughed at, and say nothing at all when it comes true.
Carry a doom to a village that cannot be saved, and stay to help them meet it.
Refuse, once, to look — and learn what the god does with a closed eye.

nodes.name: Absolver
nodes.role: Elite executioner — burst elimination of the condemned
nodes.lore: When excommunication fails, the church sends its last argument. Absolvers hold that a clean death under the rite cleanses what a whole life could not, and they deliver it personally. Few are named, fewer seen twice; towns remember their visits the way coastlines remember storms — by what is missing.
nodes.playstyle: Hunt one target through anything. The rite makes you unstoppable while a sentence stands open; finish it clean, carry the sins, move on.

abilities.name: Rite of Absolution
abilities.desc: Open the rite over a condemned target; until it closes, you cannot be slowed, silenced, or turned aside.

abilities.name: The Clean Death
abilities.desc: A sanctified killing blow that cannot be survived below a quarter health; the slain cannot rise or be raised.

abilities.name: Bear the Weight
abilities.desc: Carry the target's unabsolved sins as temporary strength; carry too many at once and they begin to whisper.

abilities.name: Sealed Verdict
abilities.desc: Nothing enters or leaves a small circle around you and the condemned until one of you is finished.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40, then answer a summons that arrives with no sender, and survive the year of testing it begins.
Execute a sentence you privately believe is wrong, or refuse it before the conclave; the order keeps both kinds of scar.
Grant the full rite to someone who wronged you personally, and mean every word of it.
Surrender your birth name and enter the rolls under the name of your first condemned.

nodes.name: Hierophant of the Breach
nodes.role: Anchor support — unbreakable zone control
nodes.lore: When a wall fails, the order sends a wall. Hierophants of the Breach stand where masonry died and make the gap holier than the gate was; siege commanders request them like ordnance and record them like weather. In the annals, every breach they held is rewritten as a gate.
nodes.playstyle: Plant yourself at the worst chokepoint and deepen. The longer you hold, the harder your ground argues; movement is a last resort, almost a heresy.

abilities.name: The Ground Remembers
abilities.desc: Your consecration deepens each minute held, stacking armor, warding, and dread for anything unhallowed that trespasses.

abilities.name: Gate That Held
abilities.desc: Declare a breach a gate; allies passing through it mend, enemies passing through it burn.

abilities.name: Unceasing Vigil
abilities.desc: While you have not moved this battle, your blessings cost nothing and cannot be dispelled.

abilities.name: Censer Wall
abilities.desc: Swing the great censer in a slow arc; its smoke hangs as a wall the profane cannot cross.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and hold a breach through a full assault, until the enemy sounds withdrawal or the wall is remade behind you.
Complete the forty-verse hallowing under bombardment without dropping a syllable.
Refuse a lawful order to retreat, and be proven right by dawn.
Carry a broken company's standard back through the breach where it died, and hallow the ground where you plant it.

nodes.name: Threshold Warden
nodes.role: Elite healer — death denial and soul retrieval
nodes.lore: They stand at the door the dying use and negotiate there, lawfully, in person. A Warden can hold the door shut against a massacre or walk through it to fetch someone back — but they may also shake their head, and no verdict in the world is quieter or more final.
nodes.playstyle: Anchor the edge of a fight and intercept deaths as they happen. Your exhaustion is the true resource; refusal is a weapon you rarely draw.

abilities.name: Hold the Door
abilities.desc: No ally in your sight dies while you keep your feet; every prevented death exhausts you further.

abilities.name: Walk the Soul Back
abilities.desc: Cross after a soul dead less than a day and lead it home, paying the toll yourself.

abilities.name: Denied the Door
abilities.desc: Deny an enemy the door; it cannot die, and carries its wounds screaming until you release it.

abilities.name: Quiet Crossing
abilities.desc: Grant a peaceful crossing to the suffering; against the undying, this counts as destruction.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40, then die once, briefly, under the order's supervision, and return with the door's location fixed in memory.
Refuse to bring back a soul the whole world wanted returned, and carry the grieving's anger without defending yourself.
Sit the threshold through a massacre's aftermath, sorting the crossing from the called-back, until every soul is accounted.
Learn the far side of the door well enough to find your way blind, and never once speak of it.

nodes.name: Anathemist
nodes.role: Dread controller — binding curses and pronounced dooms
nodes.lore: A Godspeaker repeats what the god says; an Anathemist is trusted with the god's no. Their pronouncements bind — crops, bloodlines, city gates. Courts fall silent when one stands, because an anathema, once spoken, cannot be argued with, only served. Most write their dooms rather than risk saying them.
nodes.playstyle: Weaponized prophecy: lay dooms that ripen over the fight, silence what the god has cursed, and make every enemy plan cost more than it wins.

abilities.name: Anathema
abilities.desc: Pronounce a doom upon one enemy; it ripens each round until the fated blow lands twofold.

abilities.name: Interdiction
abilities.desc: Bar a place or object by decree; enemies who use it anyway are marked and weakened.

abilities.name: The God's No
abilities.desc: Countermand one enemy spell or miracle as it happens; its wielder is struck mute for a breath.

abilities.name: Written Doom
abilities.desc: Ink a sentence and seal it; whoever breaks the seal inherits the doom inside.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and copy the Register of Dooms by hand, error-free, learning what each pronouncement did to its speaker.
Pronounce your first anathema before the conclave, and stand present, years later, when it completes.
Lift a curse an elder of your order laid wrongly, and survive both the curse and the elder.
Hold an anathema unspoken on the tip of your tongue for a year, and let it die there unsaid.

nodes.name: Ordalist
nodes.role: Elite duelist — shared trials and divine verdicts
nodes.lore: Absolvers sentence; Ordalists object. Their order holds that no conclave may judge what the god can be asked directly, so they administer the asking — iron, water, fire, single combat. The accused who survives an Ordalist's trial walks free, whatever bishops wanted. The two orders share a corridor at the mother-temple and have not shared a word in a century.
nodes.playstyle: Bind yourself and one enemy into the same trial: shared flames, shared iron, shared terms. You train to survive what you inflict, and the god keeps score.

abilities.name: Trial by Iron
abilities.desc: Grip a bar of white-hot iron and offer the other end; whoever lets go first is judged, and marked accordingly.

abilities.name: Shared Ordeal
abilities.desc: Yoke yourself to one enemy; all damage either of you takes is dealt to both until one yields or falls.

abilities.name: The Finding
abilities.desc: Close a trial; the party the god finds false takes radiant damage for every wound endured during it.

abilities.name: Unscalded Hand
abilities.desc: While a trial stands open, fire does not burn you and drowning does not take you; the verdict must find you living.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and undergo all four ordeals yourself — iron, water, fire, and combat — so you know exactly what you will be asking.
Interrupt a lawful execution because the accused demanded trial, and stand as the ordeal's second against the Absolver who came to finish it.
Administer the trial of someone you are certain is guilty, and open the gate yourself when the god acquits.
Refuse to learn the outcome the conclave prefers; burn the letter unread and enter that, too, in the record.

nodes.name: Crucifer
nodes.role: Elite vanguard — advancing consecration and column blessing
nodes.lore: Hierophants hold ground; Crucifers hold that ground unclaimed is ground surrendered. Bearing the god's standard at the head of a marching column, they consecrate by advance — every stride sworn in, every halt a small apostasy. The two orders cite the same scripture at each other, verse for verse, and both are certain.
nodes.playstyle: Never stop moving forward. Your blessings live in the advance — allies who keep pace fight on holy ground, and every foot gained stays gained.

abilities.name: Raised Rood
abilities.desc: March beneath the raised rood; allies advancing with you gain armor and cannot be slowed while moving toward the enemy.

abilities.name: Ground Gained
abilities.desc: Earth you cross while advancing is consecrated behind you and cannot be desecrated this battle; retreat across it and it fades.

abilities.name: Unresting Rite
abilities.desc: While you moved this round, your prayers cost less and your column shrugs off fear; stand still and both lapse.

abilities.name: First Across
abilities.desc: Be first through a breach, gate, or ford; the crossing is hallowed at your heel, mending allies who follow and burning the profane.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and carry the great standard from the mother-temple to the frontier without once setting it down, sleeping upright against its haft.
Lead a column across ground three armies died failing to cross, and deliver it consecrated.
Argue the Doctrine of the Standing Wall with a Hierophant of the Breach before the conclave, lose on points, and march out unconvinced.
Consecrate a road the church abandoned, shrine to shrine, and walk it back to prove it holds.

nodes.name: Flagellant
nodes.role: Elite martyr-healer — pain absorbed and repaid
nodes.lore: Threshold Wardens bargain at the door; Flagellants find the whole negotiation obscene. Their doctrine is arithmetic: the world holds a fixed sum of suffering, and every lash a Flagellant takes is one that lands nowhere else. Wardens call them mad. They call Wardens clerks, and go on carrying strangers' agonies the way porters carry parcels.
nodes.playstyle: Stand where it hurts most. Draw every wound in reach into your own body, convert the pain to power, and outlast what should have killed you twice.

abilities.name: Whole Weight
abilities.desc: Take an ally's wound at its full weight instead of half; taken whole, it heals them entirely and feeds your fervor.

abilities.name: Mortification
abilities.desc: Scourge yourself before battle; every stripe banked becomes a wound an ally will not take today.

abilities.name: Fervor of Stripes
abilities.desc: Your prayers heal harder for every wound currently on your body; unbroken skin is wasted scripture.

abilities.name: Not One More
abilities.desc: While you stand, allies below half health cannot be struck; every blow meant for them finds your body, which has learned patience.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and take the Scourging Vow: one year in a plague-province, taking every pain you can carry and passing none of it back.
Carry a dying stranger's agony for a full day so they can say their goodbyes in comfort, and ask nothing after.
Tell a Threshold Warden, to their face, that their door is a counting-house, and hold their gaze while your scars argue for you.
Be flogged in a condemned stranger's place at the public post, and thank the magistrate for the exchange.

nodes.name: Gospeller
nodes.role: Elite support — binding blessings and pronounced destinies
nodes.lore: Anathemists carry the god's no; Gospellers are trusted with its yes, which the order insists is the heavier word. Their pronounced blessings bind like law — the farmer promised a harvest must plant, the soldier promised survival must charge. An Anathemist's doom can be fled. A Gospeller's blessing must be lived up to, daily, forever.
nodes.playstyle: Speak fortunes and make them true: promise allies outcomes they must then earn, lay glad fates on enemies they cannot afford, and never promise idly.

abilities.name: Glad Tidings
abilities.desc: Promise an ally they will not fall this battle; while they fight toward the enemy, the promise holds.

abilities.name: Promised Harvest
abilities.desc: Bless an ally's next act; whatever it attempts succeeds beyond intention, and the excess spills to those beside them.

abilities.name: Unbearable Blessing
abilities.desc: Pronounce a long and prosperous life over an enemy; fate begins removing them from the battle to keep the appointment.

abilities.name: The God's Yes
abilities.desc: Affirm one ally's spell or miracle as it happens; it cannot fail, be countered, or be regretted.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and copy the Register of Fortunes beside the Register of Dooms, learning what each granted blessing cost the one it graced.
Pronounce your first binding blessing before the conclave, and stand present, years later, when its keeper finally earns it.
Bless an enemy of the church sincerely, in public, and watch the blessing do what no anathema could.
Refuse to bless a king who demanded it; explain, once, that the god's yes is not for sale, and survive the explanation.

nodes.name: Ashen Saint
nodes.role: Mythic striker — final judgment made flesh
nodes.lore: Each generation is granted at most one. The Ashen Saint has been through the god's fire and come out with nothing left that burns: no fear, no favor, no appetite for mercy beyond the exact amount owed. The church canonizes them while they live — an honor invented to keep them supervised.
nodes.playstyle: Walk, judge, conclude. You are slow, inevitable, and untouchable by anything with sin on it; the daily sentence decides battles before they start.

abilities.name: Judgment Entire
abilities.desc: Pronounce final judgment on one creature each day; no armor, oath, or rival god's favor mitigates the sentence.

abilities.name: Pyre Unlit
abilities.desc: The unrepentant near you smolder without flame, and lies spoken in your presence blister the tongue.

abilities.name: Canon of Ash
abilities.desc: Where your sentence lands, the ash consecrates the ground and every witness's oath becomes binding.

abilities.name: Sainted Flesh
abilities.desc: Blows against you fall away as ash; only doubt can cut you, and yours burned long ago.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60, walk unarmed into a place your church refuses to name, and judge what rules there.
Burn on a heretic's pyre and step down from it when the argument is settled.
Accept canonization while still breathing, over the objections of everyone who loves you.
Judge yourself last, aloud and in public, and carry out whatever sentence the god sets.

nodes.name: Living Reliquary
nodes.role: Mythic anchor — walking sanctuary and mass ward
nodes.lore: They stop carrying holy things and become the holy thing carried. Pilgrim roads bend toward wherever a Living Reliquary is standing; shrines assemble around their stillness without masons; seven cathedrals already hold deeds to their bones. Armies have surrendered rather than fight across ground that walks.
nodes.playstyle: You are the sacred ground. Every ally in your shadow fights under sanctuary law; move rarely, deliberately, and let the battlefield reorganize around you.

abilities.name: Ambulatory Sanctum
abilities.desc: You are consecrated ground; every rule of sanctuary applies within your shadow, wherever it falls.

abilities.name: Pilgrim's Touch
abilities.desc: Allies who lay a hand on you shed curses, fear, and one mortal wound per day.

abilities.name: The Promised Bones
abilities.desc: You cannot be destroyed on hallowed ground, and you are always on hallowed ground.

abilities.name: Bell Beneath the Skin
abilities.desc: When you are struck, a bell tolls across the field; the faithful rally and the profane falter.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and accept the Enshrinement: a relic sealed into your living flesh, whose demands you must survive.
Hallow ground openly in the enemy's capital, and leave by the front gate.
Let pilgrims wear a path to your door and turn none away, whatever they carry.
Watch the shrine they build around your stillness outgrow your name, and stay anyway.

nodes.name: Wellspring Incarnate
nodes.role: Mythic healer — mass restoration and return
nodes.lore: The lens stops channeling the light and becomes it. A Wellspring Incarnate no longer prays for mercy; they seep it — plagues end in provinces they cross, and a battlefield's dead can rise breathing on a single exhalation. Histories argue whether each was one person or several; the wells named after them still heal.
nodes.playstyle: Radiance without effort: everything near you mends, always. The discipline is choosing what not to heal, and how much of yourself each great miracle spends.

abilities.name: Overflowing
abilities.desc: You heal everything near you, constantly; choosing who not to heal is now the discipline.

abilities.name: The Great Remission
abilities.desc: Once a season, undo a catastrophe's wounds across a mile; sleep a week for every hundred restored.

abilities.name: One Exhalation
abilities.desc: Rekindle the newly dead across the field in a single breath; each returns with your heartbeat in their chest.

abilities.name: Springhead
abilities.desc: Wherever you finally die, a healing spring will rise; you have not yet tested this.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60, then empty yourself into one miracle too large to survive, and be found alive anyway, three days on.
Close your ledger: forgive every debt of breath owed to you, by name, aloud.
End a plague by walking its province end to end, sleeping only in the sick-houses.
Let the god pour through until you cannot tell which memories are yours, and keep the ones that matter anyway.

nodes.name: The Final Word
nodes.role: Mythic controller — fate pronounced and enforced
nodes.lore: At the end of prophecy, speech stops predicting and starts deciding. The Final Word talks rarely — some not for years — because everything said comes due. Treaties hold if one merely attended the signing. Chroniclers record their sentences the way they record eclipses: exactly, and from a distance.
nodes.playstyle: An economy of absolute utterances. Hold your silence like a drawn weapon, position for the perfect sentence, and spend words the way others spend lives.

abilities.name: Pronouncement
abilities.desc: Speak a fate aloud once per battle; reality complies within the hour by the shortest road it finds.

abilities.name: The Kept Silence
abilities.desc: While you have not spoken, allies act as though forewarned and enemies as though accused.

abilities.name: Unwriting
abilities.desc: Declare one recent event untrue; the world keeps the scar but not the wound.

abilities.name: Witnessed
abilities.desc: Anything sworn in your hearing binds; oathbreakers learn what your attention costs.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and keep a decade's vow of silence, breaking it once, for a sentence the histories still argue over.
Speak your own ending aloud — date, place, and manner — and live toward it without flinching.
Refuse the god a word once: keep your mouth shut when it wants opening, and bear the cost.
Attend a war's last parley, end it with one sentence, and walk home unescorted.

nodes.name: The Proving
nodes.role: Mythic duelist — the living trial
nodes.lore: At the end of the ordeal line stands one who no longer administers trials but is one. To cross The Proving's shadow is to be weighed; guilt rises in the guilty like fever, and armies have unraveled at the border of their attention. Kings send disputed crowns to them by courier. Some crowns return.
nodes.playstyle: You are the trial. Everything that engages you is being judged as it fights; the innocent find you almost gentle, and the guilty find nothing gentle at all.

abilities.name: Weight of Guilt
abilities.desc: Enemies engaging you are weighed each round; the guiltier they are, the slower, heavier, and more flammable they become.

abilities.name: The Standing Trial
abilities.desc: Declare a battlefield a courtroom; no one leaves, lies fail aloud, and every death within is entered as a verdict.

abilities.name: Acquittal
abilities.desc: Find one creature innocent per day; it is healed whole, freed of curses, and cannot be lawfully harmed until dawn.

abilities.name: Ordeal Unending
abilities.desc: You cannot be slain by anything with a verdict pending against it; most things, examined closely, have one.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and submit yourself to the Ordeal of Ordeals: all four trials at once, unwitnessed, with the god alone keeping score.
Try a war: summon both armies' captains to a ford, weigh their causes aloud, and send home the side the god finds wanting.
Acquit someone the whole church condemned, publicly, and bear the interdicts they nail to your door without breaking one.
Stand trial yourself before the meanest village hedge-court, answer every charge honestly, and abide the sentence of people with no idea who you are.

nodes.name: Hallowtide
nodes.role: Mythic vanguard — consecration as advancing tide
nodes.lore: The march stops being a rite and becomes a tide. A Hallowtide has not halted in years — pilgrims join and drop away, wars pause to let the column through, and the ground does not unconsecrate behind them. Cartographers redraw the sacred borders annually and have petitioned, twice, for them to walk somewhere convenient.
nodes.playstyle: Perpetual advance. Your column is a moving sanctuary that nothing profane can stand in front of; the only tactical question is the route.

abilities.name: The Tide Comes In
abilities.desc: Advance each round without fail; everything unhallowed in your path is pushed back, burned, or converted to paving.

abilities.name: Wake of Sanctity
abilities.desc: Ground you have crossed remains permanently consecrated; allies fighting anywhere along your wake share your blessings at full strength.

abilities.name: Joined Procession
abilities.desc: Any willing soul may fall in behind you; while they keep the column's pace, they cannot rout, tire, or stray.

abilities.name: No Ebb
abilities.desc: You cannot be stopped, rooted, or turned; effects that would halt you instead grant the column a surge of speed.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60, then walk a border of the faith for a year and a day without halting; eat, sleep, and pray at the march.
Lead the column through the gates of a city under interdict, and leave it, block by block, reconsecrated behind you.
Let an army form across your road, and walk on; be remembered by the survivors as weather rather than war.
Pass the great standard to the pilgrim behind you and keep walking; learn that the column no longer needs it, or you.

nodes.name: The Stigmatic
nodes.role: Mythic martyr — the world's wounds, one body
nodes.lore: The scourge becomes unnecessary; the wounds arrive on their own. A Stigmatic bleeds when a village burns three provinces away, and the village, inexplicably, does not.
