Physicians who examine them retire. The church keeps their itinerary secret, because wherever they lodge, the surrounding country enjoys a health nobody local has earned.
nodes.playstyle: Absorb everything, everywhere, always. Your health is a public utility; manage the intake, spend the accumulated pain as radiance, and do not die of generosity.

abilities.name: Wounds Arriving
abilities.desc: All damage dealt to allies within the field arrives on your body instead, reduced by your accumulated scars.

abilities.name: Radiant Hemorrhage
abilities.desc: Open your oldest wound deliberately; its stored pain erupts as searing light that heals the faithful and blinds the profane.

abilities.name: Suffered Elsewhere
abilities.desc: Suffer a catastrophe's wounds from anywhere within the province; those who should have died wake bruised and owing nothing.

abilities.name: Scar Scripture
abilities.desc: Your scars are legible as scripture; allies who read them fight free of fear, doubt, and their own old pains.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and receive the first unbidden wound — a hurt from a place you have never been — and thank the god for the delivery.
Take a famine: hunger for a starving town through the winter while its granaries inexplicably stretch, and never tell them how.
Bear a massacre's every wound in a single night, alone in your cell, and be found at matins, ruined and at prayer.
Refuse healing for yourself, once and forever; your scars are the office now, and closing them would be resignation.

nodes.name: The Evangel
nodes.role: Mythic support — the promise made present
nodes.lore: Somewhere past pronouncement, the messenger and the message merge. An Evangel no longer delivers the god's yes; they are it, walking. Crops commit to ripening a valley ahead of them. The dying hold on until they arrive, then generally decline to die. Chroniclers note that history goes suspiciously well wherever they winter.
nodes.playstyle: Aura of ordained fortune: allies around you succeed slightly before they act, and the day's one great promise can bend a battle's whole shape.

abilities.name: Already Answered
abilities.desc: Prayers spoken near you are granted before they finish; allies' abilities resolve as though blessed in advance.

abilities.name: The Great Promise
abilities.desc: Once daily, promise an outcome for the battle aloud; the world begins arranging it, and every ally's action counts double toward it.

abilities.name: Good News Travels
abilities.desc: Word of your presence heals; allies who merely learn you are near mend wounds and shed despair at any distance.

abilities.name: No Ill Ending
abilities.desc: Allies cannot die badly in your presence; any death near you completes something, and the completed dead do not haunt, rot, or rise.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and outlive the Register of Fortunes: every blessing you ever pronounced fulfilled, witnessed, and ruled complete by the conclave.
Enter a city under siege carrying nothing, promise it spring, and be somewhere else, unthanked, when spring arrives early.
Bless your god's bitterest enemy with a whole heart, and make the blessing so good it converts where conquest failed.
Stop speaking blessings and notice they continue; learn what you have become, and go on becoming it.

nodes.name: The Ashfall
nodes.role: Apotheosis — judgment as weather
nodes.lore: When an Ashen Saint carries out their last sentence, the judging does not stop; it precipitates. Ash falls from clear skies on perjured courts and unrepentant cities, and the world calls it The Ashfall. One mortal at a time bears the name and walks beneath the weather, deciding nothing, delivering all of it.
nodes.playstyle: Battlefield-wide, impersonal judgment. You no longer choose targets; you set the weather, and everything under it is sentenced by what it has done.

abilities.name: Grey Verdict
abilities.desc: Ash falls across the field; every creature beneath it takes radiant damage proportional to its unanswered sins, allies included.

abilities.name: The Weather Decides
abilities.desc: You cannot be commanded, bribed, or appealed to; effects that would sway you dissipate like smoke, sentencing their casters.

abilities.name: Ashen Interval
abilities.desc: Where your ash has settled, no new sin can be committed until it is disturbed; most battles end there.

abilities.name: Judgment Unattended
abilities.desc: Once per day, sentence a place you cannot see; somewhere, ash begins to fall, and the guilty feel the change of season.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85, carry out your own sentence as the Ashen Saint's rite requires, and be the first thing the falling ash refuses to bury.
Let the church strike your name from the canon of living saints and enter it in the almanac instead.
Stand in the ashfall over a city you once loved and let it fall; the weather does not recuse itself, and neither may you.
Bear the weather for a full year without once wishing it on anyone, and it is yours.

nodes.name: The Basilica
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the living cathedral
nodes.lore: In the end the shrine finishes assembling. A Living Reliquary who stands long enough is redesignated: pilgrims stop asking their blessing and start attending them, masses are said within earshot as within walls, and cartography marks them with a cross. The person is still in there. The church finds it simpler not to say so.
nodes.playstyle: You are the fortress objective. Allies garrison you like a citadel, entire battles happen inside your sanctuary law, and sieges against you have canonical rules.

abilities.name: Nave and Transept
abilities.desc: Your sanctuary extends as halls of force; allies fight within your architecture, gaining walls, cover, and consecrated footing everywhere.

abilities.name: Right of Sanctuary
abilities.desc: Any creature that reaches you and yields is inviolate; violating this marks the violator before the god and every court besides.

abilities.name: Bells Above
abilities.desc: Your bells toll of themselves at need — alarm, rally, requiem — each peal a mass blessing or a mass dread.

abilities.name: Founded Forever
abilities.desc: You cannot be moved, and you cannot fall while one true believer stands inside your walls; someone always does.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and let the Enshrinement complete: the last relic sealed, the last wall risen, your heartbeat rescheduled as a service.
Hold a coronation, a heresy trial, and a pauper's funeral within yourself in the same week, and show no preference.
Withstand a siege as the thing besieged, and when the engines break, ring matins on time.
Answer, when the seven cathedrals present their deeds to your bones, that the property has appreciated and is no longer for sale.

nodes.name: The Watershed
nodes.role: Apotheosis — mercy as geography
nodes.lore: The Springhead promise was true. Where the Wellspring finally poured out, water rose, and kept rising, and did not stop at one spring: every healing well in the world now runs from the same source, and the source has a face. Pilgrims drink The Watershed daily on three continents. It does not diminish them.
nodes.playstyle: Continental-scale mending on a local body. Heal through every well and rainfall at once, flood the field with living water, and remember that droughts are also yours.

abilities.name: Every Well at Once
abilities.desc: Heal any creature anywhere that has ever drunk from a blessed spring; distance stopped being an argument some time ago.

abilities.name: Living Water
abilities.desc: The ground around you runs with shallow, luminous water; allies standing in it mend continuously and cannot bleed.

abilities.name: Denied the Well
abilities.desc: Deny your waters to one creature; wounds it deals stop healing anywhere in the world until it repents or falls.

abilities.name: The Source Endures
abilities.desc: Destroying your body diverts you into the nearest spring; you resurface within a day, unhurried and entirely whole.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and test the Springhead promise at last: pour out entirely, die where the ground is thirsty, and rise as what rises.
Feel every well in the world as a fingertip, and learn not to flinch when one is poisoned.
Refuse a tyrant's reservoir and water his fleeing serfs, and let the histories argue about which was the miracle.
Keep one memory of being a person — the god allows one — and choose it carefully; the water keeps nothing it is not given.

nodes.name: The Amen
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the word after the last word
nodes.lore: Every Final Word eventually speaks the ending they promised, and the histories hold their breath. What follows is The Amen: the assent that seals all speech, worn by one mortal at a time. They say nothing at all now. They are what happens to sentences when they are finished — treaties set, oaths cure, lies curdle.
nodes.playstyle: Perfect silence, absolute ratification. You act last in every exchange, make whatever has happened permanent or void, and win by ending things correctly.

abilities.name: So Be It
abilities.desc: Ratify the round as it ends: everything that went well for your allies becomes permanent until dawn.

abilities.name: Withheld Assent
abilities.desc: Decline to seal an enemy's action; unratified, it comes quietly apart, as though it had merely been rehearsed.

abilities.name: The Setting Silence
abilities.desc: Your silence hardens the air; within it, nothing new can be begun, and everything already begun concludes.

abilities.name: Last of All
abilities.desc: You always act last, and cannot be preempted; anything that would kill you must first finish everything else it started.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85, meet the ending you once spoke for yourself at the promised place and hour, and be what remains standing in the hush after.
Surrender your remaining words to the order's archive, counted and certified, and go forth with none.
Attend the signing of a peace between empires, say nothing, and be the clause neither side dares test.
Seal, at the end, the god's own promise to the world, and hold your peace forever regarding what it said.

nodes.name: The Touchstone
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the standard all truth strikes
nodes.lore: When The Proving finally stands trial and is acquitted by strangers, something fixes. The world gains a Touchstone: a still point against which everything is assayed. Oaths are sworn 'against the stone' in courts that have never seen it. False things ring false within a day's ride. The office moves; the fixity does not.
nodes.playstyle: A fixed point in every sense: immovable, incorruptible, revelatory. Enemies break themselves against you and learn, in breaking, exactly what they were.

abilities.name: Struck True
abilities.desc: Any attack against you reveals its wielder's nature aloud; concealments, disguises, and borrowed shapes shatter on contact.

abilities.name: Assay the Field
abilities.desc: Test every creature on the field at once; the false-hearted ring hollow, falter, and know that everyone heard.

abilities.name: Fixed Point
abilities.desc: You cannot be moved, transformed, aged, or unmade; the world may end, but it will be measured against you first.

abilities.name: Proof Against
abilities.desc: Choose a lie the world tells itself; while you stand, it stops working, everywhere, for everyone.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and be assayed by the god directly, alone, with no rite between you; return bearing the mark of what was found.
Let every court on the continent swear its oaths against you for a year, and feel each false one land.
Ring true when an empire's founding myth is struck against you, and stand in the wreckage of the archives afterward, unmoved.
Accept that you will never again be surprised, flattered, or deceived, and grieve it once, briefly, as the stone requires.

nodes.name: The Procession
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the rite that walks the world
nodes.lore: The column has walked long enough that walking is now what it is made of. The Procession appears in liturgical calendars, in border treaties, in the night sky — a slow wheel of stars the church swears was not there before. One mortal at a time holds the head of the column, and the world's maps politely keep up.
nodes.playstyle: March at the head of something older than armies. The battlefield reorganizes around your route; whatever refuses to make way becomes, briefly, historical.

abilities.name: Make Way
abilities.desc: Declare your route aloud; terrain levels, gates unbar, and whatever stands upon it is moved or milled under.

abilities.name: Feast Day
abilities.desc: Wherever you halt — you may now halt — the day becomes holy; allies feast, mend, and shed all lingering harms.

abilities.name: Stars in Train
abilities.desc: The Procession's constellation marches with you; by night, its light is consecrated ground wherever it falls.

abilities.name: Always Arriving
abilities.desc: You are never ambushed, cut off, or too late; the Procession has already been wherever you are needed.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and find the column waiting at your door on an unremarkable morning, patient, with your place at its head left open.
Lead the Procession once around the whole of the world, and deliver it back to the door it left by, on the day foretold.
Walk it through the capital of every faith that denies your god, harming no one, converting no one, and be argued about for a century.
Halt, at last, of your own will, for one full night; if the column stays, it is yours; if it walks on, follow.

nodes.name: The Passion
nodes.role: Apotheosis — suffering kept as a season
nodes.lore: A Stigmatic who does not die of the office becomes it. The Passion is kept now like a season: a fixed span in the world's year when all pain everywhere travels to one body and is honored there. Farmers plant by it. Torturers find their trade briefly impossible. One mortal keeps the season, and is kept by it.
nodes.playstyle: Cosmic-scale absorption on a schedule you control. Declare the season, take the world's harm into one body, and return it as light.

abilities.name: Season of Sorrows
abilities.desc: Declare the Passion open; while it lasts, no creature you can see may suffer — all of it comes to you.

abilities.name: Alms of Light
abilities.desc: Convert your carried pain to radiance and distribute it; the more you hold, the more the field is healed.

abilities.name: The Honored Hurt
abilities.desc: Wounds on your body cannot be used against you; each one is a holy day, and holy days do not bleed.

abilities.name: Kept by the Keeping
abilities.desc: You cannot die during the Passion; the season requires its keeper, and the world has agreed to the terms.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and survive a year in which every day is yours: all the world's pain, unscheduled, arriving as it pleases.
Petition the god to give the world's pain a season with borders, and offer your body as the border.
Keep the first Passion without dying, from its opening bell to its closing, and hear the world exhale when it closes.
Forgive the world for needing you; do it annually; mean it more each year.

nodes.name: The Covenant
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the standing promise between god and world
nodes.lore: An Evangel's promises eventually outnumber their heartbeats, and the arithmetic resolves into law. The Covenant is the settled terms between the god and everything else, kept in a living body: while its bearer walks, spring is enforceable, harvests are precedent, and the sun's rising can be cited. Heresy continues, of course. It just stops working.
nodes.playstyle: Living-law support: invoke the world's standing promises as instant miracles, hold enemies to terms older than their gods, and never break your own.

abilities.name: Cite the Dawn
abilities.desc: Invoke a standing term of the world — dawn, spring, harvest — and it occurs here, now, in miniature, on your side.

abilities.name: The Offered Mercy
abilities.desc: Offer an enemy the Covenant's mercy once; refused, every blessing they have ever received is withdrawn on the spot.

abilities.name: Sign After Storm
abilities.desc: Set a sign over the field after every storm you outlast; allies beneath it cannot despair or rout for a season.

abilities.name: Unbreakable Because Kept
abilities.desc: You cannot be harmed by any creature currently benefiting from the world's terms; sunlight, breath, and gravity all count.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and hear the god offer the world settled terms with your name in them; read every line before you agree.
Carry the terms to every people under the sun, and let each mark the margin; the Covenant binds only what it has met.
Hold the god to its side of the terms once, publicly, and survive being right.
Become the copy of record: when every written version burns, the terms must still be legible in how you live.

families.name: Druid
families.tagline: Speak for the green; wear what it lends you.
families.description: Before the first wall there was an accord: the people would take only what the green could spare, and the green would remember them. Druids keep that fading contract. They speak for root and beast in the courts of men, and when words fail they borrow the forest's shapes and seasons — a bear's back, a winter's patience — and settle the account themselves.

nodes.name: Druid
nodes.role: Hybrid adept — spells, shapes, and support
nodes.lore: Druids are found, not recruited. A child who wanders home late with sap in her hair and a fox's patience in her eyes; a woodcutter who set the axe down mid-swing and never picked it up. The old accord chooses its keepers, and the circles teach the chosen only what they already half know.
nodes.playstyle: Versatile beginner: lash with thorns, mend with growth, and slip into small borrowed shapes. Weak at everything, present everywhere, learning which half of the accord calls loudest.

abilities.name: Thornlash
abilities.desc: A whip of living briar strikes the target and roots them in place for two seconds.

abilities.name: Second Skin
abilities.desc: Take a lean wolf-shape for ten seconds, trading spells for speed and a worrying bite.

abilities.name: Green Whisper
abilities.desc: Coax a wound closed with hastened growth, healing an ally over six seconds.

abilities.name: Read the Loam
abilities.desc: Learn everything that crossed this ground in the last day: numbers, weight, and wounds.

progressionSteps: Answer the summons only you heard: leave the road at dusk and walk until the trees stop being scenery.
Sleep a full winter night against an elder oak and wake knowing one word of its slow language.
Keep a dying thing company until it finishes — no mercy stroke, no prayer — and understand why the circle watched you do it.
Swear the accord at the moot of three groves: take only what is spared, and answer when the green calls.

nodes.name: Skinshifter
nodes.role: Frontline shapeshifter — adaptive melee brawler
nodes.lore: The circle grants the second gift only to those who can come back from it. Skinshifters wear bear and wolf first, honest shapes with honest appetites, and learn the discipline of returning. Villages hire them against raiders and worse; the wise pay promptly, having seen what a patient person with a bear's arms can do.
nodes.playstyle: Adaptive frontline: open in bear to hold the line, break to wolf to run down the fleeing, and return to your own skin only when the work is done.

abilities.name: Ursa Mantle
abilities.desc: Assume bear-shape: doubled health, sweeping claws, and a taunt-roar that dares everything nearby to try.

abilities.name: Loping Shape
abilities.desc: Assume wolf-shape: gain sprint speed, and each bite leaves a bleed that stacks three times.

abilities.name: Marrow Memory
abilities.desc: Shifting shapes mends you; the body forgets a portion of its wounds with each change.

abilities.name: Hackles
abilities.desc: Sense hostile intent within thirty paces before it moves, even while wearing your own skin.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10 and run three nights with a wild pack, taking no kill and no shelter, until they stop watching you.
Wear the wolf until your own name sounds strange, then set it down and answer to that name anyway.
Let the circle sew your first pelt-cord and wear it always: a promise that the skin comes off.
Kill in a borrowed shape only once this year, for food, and eat all of it.

nodes.name: Grovespeaker
nodes.role: Zone controller — terrain, sustain, slow attrition
nodes.lore: When a forest needs a voice at a treaty table, it grows one. Grovespeakers spend seasons in the moot-glades, learning the twin vocabularies of growth and rot, and emerge speaking for constituencies that measure debate in centuries. Loggers and land-hungry barons have learned that an ignored Grovespeaker's silence costs more than their words.
nodes.playstyle: Patient control: raise bracken walls, root the reckless, and let slow rot make your argument. You win fights the way forests do — by still being there.

abilities.name: Raise the Bracken
abilities.desc: Grow a wall of interwoven fern and thorn along a chosen line; it burns slowly and regrows quickly.

abilities.name: Root Verdict
abilities.desc: Roots erupt to bind up to three enemies for four seconds or until each is struck twice.

abilities.name: Sap Surge
abilities.desc: Flood an ally with rising sap: strong regeneration, and their next wound closes on its own.

abilities.name: First Rot
abilities.desc: Mark a foe for decay: armor softens and wounds fester, worsening over ten seconds.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10 and sit a full session of the grove-moot without speaking; be the first human it does not adjourn for.
Plead a condemned grove's case before the men who hold the axes, and leave with the grove standing.
Tend one tree from seed through its first winter, and grieve honestly if you fail.
Learn the second vocabulary: find what the rot is saying beneath the loveliest glade, and repeat it without flinching.

nodes.name: Clawsworn
nodes.role: Melee striker — bleeds and sustained pressure
nodes.lore: Clawsworn take a vow written in nothing but scars: the shape is a covenant, not a costume. They fight in fur more than skin, keep territories like wolves, and serve as their circles' answer to armored men. The vow's price is plain — kill only what you would eat, and mourn everything you kill.
nodes.playstyle: Committed melee: stalk, open with a hamstring, and stack bleeds until the target's options are kneeling or falling. Leaving beast-shape mid-fight feels like retreat.

abilities.name: Half-Pelt
abilities.desc: Take a hybrid war-shape for twenty seconds: clawed hands, human cunning, and neither form's weaknesses.

abilities.name: Hamstring Rite
abilities.desc: A low, precise tear slows the target and deepens the bleeding of every later wound.

abilities.name: Scent of Openings
abilities.desc: Attacks against bleeding enemies gain critical chance for each bleed they carry.

abilities.name: Kill-Memory
abilities.desc: Executing a bleeding foe below one-quarter health refunds Half-Pelt and heals you for the remainder.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and bring down a stag in wolf-shape using no magic but the shape itself.
Take a territory of your own and hold it one full season against everything that contests it, in fur, alone.
Fight a rival predator to submission and let it live, so the wild learns you kill only to eat.
Swear the claw-vow over your own spilled blood: the shape is covenant, not costume.

nodes.name: Elderform
nodes.role: Flex combatant — form-cycling answers to everything
nodes.lore: The earth keeps records in bone-seams and amber, and the Elderform learn to read them aloud. They petition extinct shapes out of deep time — river-things with too many jaws, horn-backed grazers like moving hills — and pay in years of their own. Scholars call the practice necromancy's cousin. Druids call it remembering on the land's behalf.
nodes.playstyle: Form-cycling flexibility: answer each threat with a shape the world forgot, spending remembered years as your resource. Never the same beast twice in one fight.

abilities.name: Fossil Recall
abilities.desc: Assume an extinct form from your bone-ledger; each grants a body no living beast can match.

abilities.name: Antediluvian Hide
abilities.desc: While in an elder shape, ignore the first three blows from every new attacker; old skin has learned.

abilities.name: Shape Debt
abilities.desc: Swapping elder forms mid-combat refunds half the cost and staggers enemies who witness it.

abilities.name: Unwalked Gait
abilities.desc: Briefly take a shape without bones — spore-haze, eel-shadow — and pass through spaces bodies cannot.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and descend to a bone-seam where the earth keeps its dead shapes; sleep among them until one dreams of you.
Carry a fossil a hundred leagues to where the creature last lived, and speak its extinction aloud there.
Wear an elder shape for one full day and pay its tithe of years without bargaining.
Open your bone-ledger: three shapes remembered, named, and promised they will walk again.

nodes.name: Thorn Shepherd
nodes.role: Battlefield architect — walls, lanes, area denial
nodes.lore: Thorn Shepherds herd bramble the way others herd sheep, driving hedge-flocks along old boundary lines that maps stopped honoring. Border villages leave them milk and iron nails; ambitious surveyors leave them alone. Where a Shepherd has walked, fields keep their old shapes, roads narrow politely, and fences grow back overnight with opinions.
nodes.playstyle: Living-terrain control: drive briar droves across the field, pen enemies into kill-lanes, and graft armor onto allies. The battlefield's geometry is yours to rewrite.

abilities.name: Briar Drove
abilities.desc: Drive a moving wall of thorn across the field, carrying enemies with it and shredding those who resist.

abilities.name: Graft
abilities.desc: Bind living wood over an ally's wounds: temporary armor that blooms, then heals as it sheds.

abilities.name: Seed the Breach
abilities.desc: Hurl a seed that erupts instantly into full-grown hedge, sealing a gap, gate, or doorway.

abilities.name: Pollard
abilities.desc: Prune an enemy's momentum: their next three attacks are cut back to half damage.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and raise a hedge around a burning village faster than the fire can walk.
Drive a bramble-flock along a forgotten boundary for a month, sleeping inside it, losing not one cane.
Face a surveyor's armed crew at a marker stone and turn them back without a single death.
Learn each thorn's name for hunger, and feed your flock only what the accord allows.

nodes.name: Rotwright
nodes.role: Attrition caster — decay, links, anti-healing
nodes.lore: Rotwrights work the accord's unglamorous half: everything owed back to the soil, collected on schedule. They read mold like scripture and keep the mycelial ledgers that link forest to forest underground. Grain-lords hate them; healers quietly consult them. A Rotwright at a deathbed is not an omen — it is a bookkeeping.
nodes.playstyle: Attrition and inevitability: seed decay early, thread your enemies through the ledger, and let time do its honest work while you stay patient.

abilities.name: Wet Autumn
abilities.desc: Call a soft, spore-heavy rain over an area; everything hostile inside decays faster each second it stays.

abilities.name: Mycelial Ledger
abilities.desc: Thread enemies together underground; damage dealt to one is partly owed by all.

abilities.name: Sweet Rot
abilities.desc: Compost an active decay effect on an enemy into healing for a nearby ally.

abilities.name: Rust Sermon
abilities.desc: Preach to metal: armor, blades, and hinges within earshot begin to flake and fail.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and sit with one felled oak from windfall to soil, keeping a ledger of everything that eats it.
Trace a mycelial thread between two forests a day's ride apart, on foot, never losing it.
Break a false embalming: give a hoarded corpse back to the ground over its family's objections, gently.
Eat only what the rot offers you for one season, and thrive.

nodes.name: Bloodpelt
nodes.role: Apex melee — frenzy, pursuit, self-sustain
nodes.lore: Bloodpelts are what circles send when a monster starts hunting men. The pelt-cord has been re-sewn so many times it is mostly scar, and the shape comes off slower each year — a price accounted, not hidden. Lords who joke about leashing one are corrected exactly once, usually by their own huntsmen, quietly.
nodes.playstyle: Apex melee: enter the frenzy window, drink wounds as fuel, and refuse every disengage. Nothing you have marked escapes; little you catch survives.

abilities.name: Season of Teeth
abilities.desc: For twelve seconds, attack speed climbs with every bleed you inflict, without ceiling.

abilities.name: Wound-Drinker
abilities.desc: Every bleed tick on every enemy you wounded returns a portion to you as health.

abilities.name: Broken Chase
abilities.desc: Nothing slows, roots, or frightens you while pursuing a marked quarry.

abilities.name: Red Quiet
abilities.desc: On a kill, terror settles over nearby foes; those who flee bleed as if bitten.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and take the hunt no bounty could close — the beast that eats hunters — wearing the shape it fears.
Let the circle re-sew your pelt-cord with your own sinew, and do not cry out.
Spend an entire winter as beast, and return in spring answering to your name on the first call.
Refuse a king's leash in his own hall, in your own skin, politely.

nodes.name: Thousandskin
nodes.role: Shape economy — evasion, decoys, total flexibility
nodes.lore: The Thousandskin keep bound ledgers of shapes the way misers keep coin. They can be the crows above a gallows, the eel beneath the ferry, the grey dog at a traitor's hearth. Circles deploy them when truth must be witnessed by something nobody lies in front of. Their own faces, folded away and rarely worn, stop aging.
nodes.playstyle: Shape economy: rotate impossible forms to answer every threat, scatter into swarms to shed damage, and bank shapes like currency for the decisive moment.

abilities.name: Murmuration
abilities.desc: Scatter into a wheeling flock for six seconds; blows pass through, and you reform anywhere within it.

abilities.name: Borrowed Centuries
abilities.desc: Chain three elder forms in sequence without cost; the third arrives with doubled power.

abilities.name: Skinfall
abilities.desc: Step out of your current shape, leaving it fighting as a decoy for eight seconds.

abilities.name: The Unlisted Shape
abilities.desc: Once a day, become a shape you have never recorded; not even you know its limits until worn.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and hold nine shapes through a single hour of battle, ending in your own, unbled.
Complete a page of your ledger no other druid can read, and bind it in your own shed skin.
Live a month as something small and eaten-of — mouse, minnow, moth — and come back unbitter.
Witness a crime as three creatures at once, and give testimony the judges cannot dismiss.

nodes.name: Heartwood Regent
nodes.role: Siege controller — living-terrain warfare at scale
nodes.lore: A Heartwood Regent holds regency over standing forests the way stewards hold castles for absent kings — except the forest is awake, and consulted. They count rings the way clerks count taxes, wake heartwood for war only when the moot consents, and have marched whole treelines to new rivers. Two kingdoms keep treaties with individual Regents by name.
nodes.playstyle: Grand-scale control: wake the stand, give the march order, and fight from inside a moving forest. Your army was always standing there; now it agrees to walk.

abilities.name: Wake the Stand
abilities.desc: Rouse every tree in the grove to fight; the elders swing hardest and remember grudges.

abilities.name: March Order
abilities.desc: The woken forest advances as a line, carrying allies in its canopy and grinding stonework beneath.

abilities.name: Ringcount
abilities.desc: Armor yourself in accumulated years: gain one ring of damage reduction per century of forest present.

abilities.name: Crown Verdict
abilities.desc: The canopy closes overhead: no flight, no sky-sight, and arrows lose their way in the dark.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and persuade a first-growth forest to walk one league and back without losing a single elder.
Sit regency through a moot that lasts a human year, and cast your one vote well.
Turn back fire, axe, and royal charter from your wardship in the same season.
Bury your predecessor among the roots and carry their ring-staff until the forest stops grieving.

nodes.name: Carrion Gardener
nodes.role: Endgame attrition — corpse-blooms and structural decay
nodes.lore: Carrion Gardeners walk battlefields after the crows and before the historians. Their order holds a single charter: nothing wasted, no plague raised, no glory left standing long enough to fester. Generals petition to keep their dead; the Gardeners decline with terrible courtesy. Meadows across three provinces bloom where their worst arguments were won.
nodes.playstyle: Sanctified attrition: seed the field early, let every death feed your blooms, and grow stronger as the battle lengthens. Endings are your element.

abilities.name: Field Tithe
abilities.desc: Each corpse on the field sprouts a spore-bloom that fights for you until it is spent.

abilities.name: Gentle Ruin
abilities.desc: Touch a wall, engine, or gate; its next decades of decay arrive over ten seconds.

abilities.name: Patient Cloud
abilities.desc: Loose a drifting spore-fog: enemies inside weaken steadily and cannot regain health.

abilities.name: Terrible Courtesy
abilities.desc: Offer one enemy a painless withering; refusal makes every decay effect on them permanent.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and turn a fresh battlefield to meadow in one season, raising no plague and keeping no trophy.
Decline a weeping general's petition for his son's body, and be gentle enough that he thanks you within the year.
Take the charter-vow over an open grave: nothing wasted, nothing raised.
Garden the ruin of a plague-town until children can be raised on what grows there.

nodes.name: Winterjaw
nodes.role: Ambush striker — banked one-strike burst
nodes.lore: Winterjaw call the Bloodpelt's frenzy what it is: the shape holding the leash. Their answer is the fast — fur worn hungry, one strike to a hunt, the meal taken afterward in their own skin. Circles loose a Bloodpelt to run a monster down; they send a Winterjaw when it must die in its bed.
nodes.playstyle: Coiled ambush: fast to bank the Held Hunger, strike once from stillness for immense damage, and end fights before they earn the name. A missed stroke costs you the meal.

abilities.name: Held Hunger
abilities.desc: Every second spent still and every day spent fasting banks damage into your next strike; there is no ceiling.

abilities.name: Snow's Counsel
abilities.desc: Until you strike, nothing finds you by scent, sound, or divination; winter keeps your secrets.

abilities.name: No Second Bite
abilities.desc: An opening strike that kills refunds Held Hunger and leaves your stillness unbroken; the hunt simply continues.

abilities.name: Honest Fang
abilities.desc: Against prey you do not mean to eat, your claws refuse to cut; against prey you do, they cannot be turned.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and fast from first snow to thaw while hunting for others, tasting nothing; let the hunger learn who owns it.
Make one kill this year in fur: a single stroke, unwitnessed, unpursued. If it takes two strokes, fast another year.
Sit within arm's reach of a Bloodpelt's frenzy and neither join nor judge it; carry your rival home after.
Swear the winter-vow at the moot of three groves: the shape eats only what the accord serves, and never first.

nodes.name: Arkhide
nodes.role: Devoted juggernaut — one perfected elder form
nodes.lore: Thousandskin bank shapes the way misers bank coin; an Arkhide spends the whole purse once. Each chooses a single kind from the bone-ledger and wears it so faithfully the earth stops listing it among the dead. They keep its gait at market and its temper at moots. Circles call this devotion. Thousandskin call it drowning.
nodes.playstyle: Committed transformation: one elder shape, held long and deep, growing stronger for every unbroken hour worn. You have one answer to everything, and it is usually enough.

abilities.name: Sworn Shape
abilities.desc: Your chosen elder form costs nothing to hold and grows one inherited trait for every year it is worn.

abilities.name: True to the Bone
abilities.desc: Each unbroken hour in the sworn shape thickens hide and deepens instinct; shifting out forfeits all of it.

abilities.name: Extinct Appetites
abilities.desc: Nothing alive remembers how to fight your kind; enemies suffer misjudged reach, wrong instincts, and honest panic.

abilities.name: Carry the Kind
abilities.desc: Allies sheltering against your flank share your hide and your calm, and cannot be driven from the field.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and choose from your bone-ledger the one kind you will answer for; let the circle watch you close the other pages forever.
Wear the sworn shape a year entire — moots, winters, grief — shifting out only for the accord, never for comfort.
Walk it through the country where the kind last lived, and stay until the land adjusts: new trails, old fears, a niche reopening.
Answer to its name in your dreams before your own, and tell no one how long that took.

nodes.name: Wildgrave
nodes.role: Aggressive terrain — advancing green, reclaimed ground
nodes.lore: A Wildgrave remembers what the ground was before the survey. They hold the green's marches — every fallow field, every abandoned garrison — and advance them. No moot vote, no parley: the accord, they argue, was broken at the first wall, and everything since is occupation. Regents find them useful, dangerous, and impossible to seat at a treaty table.
nodes.playstyle: Territorial aggression: claim ground, green it, and fight from it with growing advantage. Every yard the wild takes back is a yard your enemies fight uphill.

abilities.name: Claim the March
abilities.desc: Declare terrain reclaimed; it greens over a minute, and while you hold it your powers cost less and hit harder there.

abilities.name: Fallow Rising
abilities.desc: Cleared or tilled ground counts as forest for your spells; the seed-bank sleeping under every field answers you.

abilities.name: Siege of Ivy
abilities.desc: Set ivy on a fortification; it climbs a season's worth each second and pulls stone with it when commanded.

abilities.name: Greenshod
abilities.desc: You and allies move unhindered through claimed ground, while enemies find every root a curb and every hedge a wall.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and take back one abandoned holding — keep, field, and road — until no stone shows and no map bothers.
Serve a season under a Heartwood Regent, obeying every ruling; leave politely, unconverted, knowing exactly what you are refusing.
Advance a treeline one full league in a year, killing no one who did not first swing steel at the green.
Bury a marker stone of your own — not where the border is, but where it will be.

nodes.name: Bitter Physic
nodes.role: Support controller — measured plagues, rationed cures
nodes.lore: Carrion Gardeners swear nothing raised; Bitter Physics never signed. Their craft is the dose — the small sickness sown early so the great one starves, a fever set to burn out a worse fever. Healers consult them by night and denounce them at breakfast. Villages that drink the bitter spring draught bury no one come autumn, and thank no one.
nodes.playstyle: Clinical attrition: diagnose the fight, dose enemies with tailored sicknesses, and ration every cure to the moment it buys most. Prevention is your damage; triage is your art.

abilities.name: The Measured Dose
abilities.desc: Afflict an enemy with a sickness sized exactly to them; stronger targets receive proportionally crueler symptoms.

abilities.name: Kindled Fever
abilities.desc: Set a small fever on an ally that burns away poisons, curses, and infections before they can take hold.

abilities.name: Bitter Draught
abilities.desc: An ally who drinks loses a tenth of their health and gains immunity to the next effect that would have dropped them.

abilities.name: Pale Cordon
abilities.desc: Ring an area in pale mold; sickness, enemies, and bad news cross it in neither direction.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and stop a spreading blight by sowing a smaller one ahead of it; then answer to the moot for the fields you sickened.
Apprentice a year to a village healer without revealing your rank; be denounced, be indispensable, be missed when you go.
Keep the kennel: culture your sicknesses as a kennelman keeps hounds — each named, each leashed, none ever slipped for spite.
Refuse the Gardeners' charter to their faces, courteously, and state your own: the small death, honestly dosed, against the great one.

nodes.name: First Predator
nodes.role: Unstoppable hunter — infinite-scaling single-target pursuit
nodes.lore: The First Predator wears the shape every prey animal remembers without being taught. Wolves lie down when it passes; nothing in the wild will meet its eye. Circles invoke it perhaps once a generation, when something has begun hunting the world itself, and afterward the histories go carefully quiet about what was seen.
nodes.playstyle: Ultimate pursuit: mark your quarry, and geography, armies, and time stop mattering. Everything else in the fight is scenery between you and the throat.

abilities.name: Original Hunger
abilities.desc: Your damage climbs the longer a hunt lasts, without cap, resetting only at the kill.

abilities.name: The Oldest Chase
abilities.desc: Mark one quarry; while you live it cannot become untrackable, unreachable, or unkillable by any means.

abilities.name: All Fangs Answer
abilities.desc: Every predator within a day's travel converges to hunt beside you until the quarry falls.

abilities.name: Prey's Memory
abilities.desc: Enemies who see you suffer the fear their ancestors learned; most kneel, some flee, none aim well.

progressionSteps: At level 60, run the Long Hunt: pursue one quarry through three seasons without losing the trail for a single night.
Find the den where the first hunger dreams, and take its shape without waking it.
Spare something at the end of a perfect hunt, once, to prove the shape has not eaten the vow.
Let the wild rename you, and answer to nothing men call you afterward.

nodes.name: The Unshaped
nodes.role: Omniform — any role at any moment
nodes.lore: The Unshaped gave their birth-shape back to the earth and did not replace it. What remains prefers forms the way weather prefers valleys — habitually, not necessarily. Two circles keep an empty chair for one; whether the chair has ever actually been empty is a question druids find funnier than anyone else does.
nodes.playstyle: Total fluidity: answer every threat by becoming its counter, flow between shapes without pause, and treat being a target as an optional condition.

abilities.name: No True Body
abilities.desc: Between shapes you are briefly nothing; blows, curses, and prophecies pass through.

abilities.name: Everything, Once
abilities.desc: Assume the exact form of any creature you can see, including its abilities, for twenty seconds.

abilities.name: Signature Absence
abilities.desc: Effects that target a creature fail to find you unless you consent.

abilities.name: Refused Finality
abilities.desc: The first killing blow each day finds you already being something it cannot kill.

progressionSteps: At level 60, give your birth-shape to the earth at the moot of three groves, and walk away as whatever comes next.
Spend a year borrowing a different shape each dawn, and want none of them back.
Pass through the eye of a needle, honestly, before witnesses.
Sit in the empty chair your circle keeps, and let them wonder ever after whether you were there.

nodes.name: Worldroot
nodes.role: Continental controller — the forest itself fights
nodes.lore: Histories disagree about whether the Worldroot is a person any longer. Their heart is planted in the oldest grove; their pulse comes up through taproots on three coasts. When a forest anywhere is put to the torch, somewhere the Worldroot's body burns too, and the reply arrives through the ground, patient and total.
nodes.playstyle: Continental presence: fight from every rooted thing at once, surfacing wherever the green touches. Battles are local affairs; you have stopped being local.

abilities.name: Continental Grip
abilities.desc: Roots answer you anywhere soil exists, seizing armies a kingdom away from where you stand.

abilities.name: The Green Immensity
abilities.desc: For one minute, all terrain in sight becomes forest, and the forest is on your side.

abilities.name: Sap of Ages
abilities.desc: Every ally touching earth regenerates as though sleeping safe in high summer.

abilities.name: One Long Ring
abilities.desc: Your death is deferred to the end of the current century; damage is recorded, not suffered.

progressionSteps: At level 60, plant your living heart beneath the oldest grove and learn to wake in every tree it touches.
Answer a burning on a coast you have never seen, through the ground, within a day.
Feed a famine from your own rings and let no one learn whom to thank.
Outgrow your name: when the histories argue whether you were ever one person, decline to settle it.

nodes.name: The Last Autumn
nodes.role: Inevitability aura — the fight ages around you
nodes.lore: Every few centuries the accord requires a final instrument, and a Rotwright's line produces one. The Last Autumn carries the year's fourth season with them; where they linger, harvests hurry, iron blushes, and empires feel their age. The histories record three. Each is remembered less as a person than as a very reasonable ending.
nodes.playstyle: Inevitability incarnate: your presence is the mechanic. Everything in the fight ripens toward its end; you decide only the order, and the mercy.

abilities.name: Everything Ripens
abilities.desc: Aura: all cooldowns, wounds, poisons, and lifespans within sight run measurably faster.

abilities.name: Kingdom Compost
abilities.desc: Declare a structure finished: it settles into fertile loam over one minute, regardless of stone or ward.

abilities.name: The Long Fall
abilities.desc: Leaves fall out of season across a chosen army; morale, armor, and certainty fall with them.

abilities.name: Mercy of Mulch
abilities.desc: A fallen ally is taken into the soil and returned at dusk, alive, smelling of rain.

progressionSteps: At level 60, ask the turning year for its last season and carry it ever afterward, so autumn arrives wherever you stand.
End something beloved that outlived its kindness — an orchard, an order, a king's long peace — and be right.
Walk unarmed through the empire that burned the moot-glades, and leave it a legend of gentle, total subsidence.
Refuse the winter: prove three times that you are the ending before the ending, and nothing further.

nodes.name: The Quell
nodes.role: Apex execution — single sanctioned endings
nodes.lore: Every age, something vast forgets how to die: a god-beast gone rabid, the last of a kind in agony, a wood-king rotting alive at the heart of his forest. The Quell is what the green sends. It comes fasting, grieves first, strikes once. Histories dispute whether it is one druid or a succession; the dying have never complained.
nodes.playstyle: Ultimate execution: study the quarry until its ending becomes obvious, then deliver that ending in one strike. Everything before the stroke is preparation; everything after is mourning.

abilities.name: The Owed Ending
abilities.desc: Mark a quarry the moot has sanctioned; against it your Held Hunger has no cap and cannot be dispelled, dodged, or outlived.

abilities.name: Grief Before
abilities.desc: Mourn the quarry before the fight; for its first minute nothing it does can harm you, since you are already at the funeral.

abilities.name: The Perfect Fang
abilities.desc: Your first strike against a marked quarry ends it outright if you have never struck it before; greatness is no defense.

abilities.name: Nothing Suffers
abilities.desc: Anything that dies within your sight dies at once of its wounds rather than slowly; this includes your allies' work.

progressionSteps: At level 60, answer a summons no druid requests: the moot of three groves has agreed that something great must be helped to die.
Give the mad god-beast of the fens its ending in one stroke, after three years spent learning what it loved.
Keep the novice's vigil again: sit with a dying thing to the finish, and understand at last why the circle watched you.
Eat of every quarry still. Weep every time. The day either stops, set down the fang and go home.

nodes.name: The Relict
nodes.role: Living monument — ecosystem ally, unbanishable bulk
nodes.lore: Histories keep the Relict in footnotes: a kind declared lost an age ago, reported again by reliable liars. The truth is a druid on the far side of devotion. Where a Relict dens, the old world resumes — companion birds return, parasites nobody mourned, prey remembering fear. Scholars dispute the sightings. The land does not read scholarship.
nodes.playstyle: Living restoration: fight as a shape the world has re-accepted — immense, unhurried, unbanishable — while the returning ecosystem of birds, swarms, and old fear fights alongside you.

abilities.name: No Seeming
abilities.desc: The sworn shape is your true form now; magic that forces, reads, or unravels shapeshifting finds nothing to take hold of.

abilities.name: The Old Company
abilities.desc: Your kind's lost retinue attends you — cleaner-birds, burrowers, following swarms — harrying enemies and tending your wounds unasked.

abilities.name: Grazing Rights
abilities.desc: Where you feed, the land yields double to allies and goes lean for enemies; the old tenancy resumes.

abilities.name: Not the Last
abilities.desc: When you fall you do not die; within the year, somewhere distant, there is a verified sighting of your kind.

progressionSteps: At level 60, stop performing the shape and be it: seven years without your born skin, until the moot forgets to send for the druid.
Let hunters hunt you and fail so honestly that the ballads make your kind cunning again.
Fill the niche your kind left empty and hold it until the wood readjusts: streams re-braiding, old seeds finally germinating.
When a true survivor of the kind is found at last, decide alone what that means, and tell no one what you decided.

nodes.name: The Greenfall
nodes.role: Mass reclamation — cities into forest overnight
nodes.lore: The histories blame plague or fire for the emptying of the inland capital; druids let them. What happened is called the Greenfall, and it walked in on two feet. Where it passes, reconquest stops being gradual: canopy comes down like nightfall, and by morning the survey does not apply. There have been two. The marches wait on the third.
nodes.playstyle: Overwhelming reclamation: convert the battlefield wholesale — streets to loam, walls to trellis — and command what grows there. Cities are a terrain type you retire.

abilities.name: Nightfall Canopy
abilities.desc: Bring the canopy down across a district; within it there is forest, there is dusk, and there is you.

abilities.name: Rootswell
abilities.desc: Worked stone across an area settles back into ground that has never heard of it — walls, roads, wards, all.

abilities.name: Root and Branch
abilities.desc: Every enemy structure you fell stands back up as an allied tree with the structure's height and a grudge.

abilities.name: No Second Survey
abilities.desc: Ground you have greened cannot be cleared, burned, or built upon while you live; each attempt feeds it.

progressionSteps: At level 60, answer a burned march with a night the maps still argue about: let one whole town wake to forest, unharmed and evicted.
Carry every evicted family's roof-beam to their new door yourself; a conquest that cannot carry beams is only fire.
Stand before the moot of three groves and answer for the Greenfall; accept the censure, and decline to promise otherwise.
Plant the marker stone you buried as a Wildgrave, watch the border arrive at it, and bury the next one farther on.

nodes.name: Feverbreak
nodes.role: Counter-contagion — plagues leashed against plagues
nodes.lore: Every plague ends the same way: one night the fever breaks everywhere at once, and the chroniclers credit frost, or prayer. The order knows better. Feverbreak walks the sick-camps with the kennel of every plague it ever leashed, and sets the tamed sickness on the wild one. Whether it survives each cure is disputed. There is always another.
nodes.playstyle: Mythic counter-contagion: unkennel tailored plagues against enemy hosts, cure by contagion, and answer every affliction on the field with a better-trained one.

abilities.name: Unkennel
abilities.desc: Loose a leashed plague at an enemy army; it spreads by their formation's own discipline and answers your whistle.

abilities.name: Like Cures Like
abilities.desc: Cure any affliction on the field by inflicting a lesser, obedient copy of it on the sufferer.

abilities.name: The Breaking Hour
abilities.desc: Declare the fever's crisis: every disease, poison, and decay in sight resolves within ten seconds — kill or cure, your call, each one.

abilities.name: Old Acquaintance
abilities.desc: Every sickness that ever touched you knows you now; diseases, blights, and miasmas decline to harm you, professionally.

progressionSteps: At level 60, walk into the century's worst plague-camp alone, unkennel everything you own, and walk out behind the last recovered child.
Break a fever the priests declared a punishment, and let the priests keep the credit; the order keeps the notes.
Catch, tame, and name the plague that killed your teacher, and never once set it loose.
Be reported dead in three chronicles while at work in four provinces, and correct neither.

nodes.name: The Downwind
nodes.role: Omnipresent hunter — predation as natural law
nodes.lore: The wild renamed the First Predator once; the world finished the job. The Downwind is not seen, it is deduced: the reason herds circle at night, the reason nothing hunts the world entire anymore, the hush that moves through a forest ahead of no visible cause. Every prey animal is born knowing it. Now, so is everything else.
nodes.playstyle: Absolute predation: you occupy the blind spot of everything alive — always behind, always downwind. Fights are hunts already won; play decides how the quarry learns it.

abilities.name: Always Downwind
abilities.desc: You are permanently undetectable until you choose otherwise; no sense, spell, or paranoia finds you first.

abilities.name: Born Knowing
abilities.desc: All creatures inherit fear of you at birth; enemies begin every fight already shaken, and no animal will serve against you.

abilities.name: The Hush Ahead
abilities.desc: Silence precedes you as terrain; within it, enemies cannot rally, signal, or hear their orders.

abilities.name: The Shortened Chase
abilities.desc: The distance between you and a marked quarry only ever decreases, whatever either of you does.

progressionSteps: At level 85, let even the wild's name for you fall away; what stalks the stalkers of the world needs no answering sound.
Go unglimpsed for a generation while every fireside tale gets you wrong; accuracy is for prey.
Cull the thing that learned to hunt First Predators, and leave no account of how.
Keep the wind's rounds: cross every wild border once a year so the born fear stays fresh; the world sets your calendar now.

nodes.name: The Loam
nodes.role: Form sovereignty — every shape on loan
nodes.lore: The Unshaped gave a shape to the earth; the Loam is what the earth made of the gift. It is the stuff shapes are cut from and, in some binding sense, still a druid. Every skinshifter's borrowed wolf is borrowed from somewhere. Circles no longer keep the empty chair; they keep a bowl of loam, damp, just in case.
nodes.playstyle: Total form authority: assume anything, lend shapes to allies, revoke them from enemies. Bodies are borrowings, and you are what they are borrowed from.

abilities.name: Lent Shape
abilities.desc: Grant any ally any shape you have ever worn; recall it whenever you please, including mid-leap.

abilities.name: Returned to Loam
abilities.desc: Revoke a borrowed form anywhere in sight; shapeshifters, glamours, and disguises return to their originals mid-sentence.

abilities.name: The Bowl of Loam
abilities.desc: Wherever a circle keeps the bowl, you may step out of it, at whatever size the room allows.

abilities.name: Nothing to Hit
abilities.desc: You keep no fixed anatomy; critical strikes, curses on flesh, and spells that name a body fail against you.

progressionSteps: At level 85, become the lending itself: when any skinshifter takes wolf-shape, be faintly, verifiably present in it.
Let the moot of three groves vote on whether you still hold rank, and attend the vote as the table.
Walk every shape you ever wore back to the country it was native to, and return each one home.
When the earth next takes a birth-shape at the moot of three groves, be the taking.

nodes.name: The Understory
nodes.role: World anchor — the green's foundation fights
nodes.lore: The Worldroot's death was deferred to the end of its century. The century ended, and every forest on three coasts put out leaves in midwinter. What remains is called the Understory: the layer beneath every wood, the part of the green no axe reaches because it is not, strictly, anywhere. Druids swear the accord touching soil; the soil countersigns.
nodes.playstyle: Foundational presence: fight from beneath everything rooted, everywhere at once. Enemies contend with the ground's own opinion of them; allies stand on ground that is actively their friend.

abilities.name: Beneath Everything
abilities.desc: Act through any rooted thing in the world simultaneously; distance is no longer among your limitations.

abilities.name: The Slow Yes
abilities.desc: Terrain grants allied requests — bridges of root, walls of trunk, doors in thickets — a moment after they are wished.

abilities.name: Midwinter Leaves
abilities.desc: Declare high summer for allies in any season or ruin: full regeneration, as though sleeping safe at home.

abilities.name: No Axe Reaches
abilities.desc: You cannot be targeted while any forest stands; damage meant for you is absorbed by acreage instead.

progressionSteps: At level 85, let the century end without deferring again, and learn with the rest of the green what you are next.
Carry three coasts' forests through a burning year without surfacing once; let kingdoms wonder why the fires kept going out.
Answer to no name at the grove-moot; be the floor it stands on, and adjourn it once, gently, to prove the point.
Keep one leaf's worth of yourself unplanted, so that a person can still step out when the green needs hands.

nodes.name: The Fourth Season
nodes.role: Seasonal aura — the year's closing made law
nodes.lore: The histories record three Last Autumns. What they cannot settle is when the third stopped being a person. Autumn now arrives on its own authority — harvests hurry, iron blushes, long summers concede — and somewhere in every autumn there is a figure walking unharvested lanes, making sure. The office cannot be refused; the year, it turns out, does not skip seasons.
nodes.playstyle: Cosmic inevitability: everything in the fight is somewhere in its autumn, and you set the date of every harvest. Mercy remains available, by appointment.

abilities.name: Harvest Date
abilities.desc: Assign each enemy a moment of harvest; at it, all their accumulated wounds, ages, and errors arrive together.

abilities.name: Iron Blush
abilities.desc: All enemy metal within your season rusts at the pace of your choosing, from patina to powder.

abilities.name: Gleaning
abilities.desc: Whatever falls in your season — lives, banners, walls — yields; allies harvest health and vigor from each ending.

abilities.name: The Year Keeps It
abilities.desc: Struck down, you are deferred, not killed; you resume with the first falling leaf, and the fight has aged badly meanwhile.

progressionSteps: At level 85, stop carrying the season and preside over it: autumn now happens because you are somewhere inside it, doing rounds.
Bring an age to harvest: let one long era end so gently that its people call the ending a festival.
Keep the customs: spare the gleaners, fill the poor's baskets first, and leave every hundredth field standing for the winter birds.
Refuse winter, still. When the year one day ends entire, be the season it trusts to close the house.

nodes.name: The Surcease
nodes.role: Execution absolute — clean endings guaranteed
nodes.lore: Who the Quell was is disputed; the Surcease is not. It is the law under the accord's floor: everything that lives is owed one clean ending, and the green keeps a keeper for it. Kings write it into their successions. Old beasts walk toward it smiling, insofar as beasts smile. Somebody, always, is wearing the office.
nodes.playstyle: Cosmological execution: your presence guarantees clean endings; you designate what finishes, in what order, and how gently. Nothing dies badly where you stand, including your enemies.

abilities.name: Law of Endings
abilities.desc: Aura: no death within your sight can be prolonged, prevented, or made cruel — not by enemy, ward, or miracle.

abilities.name: The Flat Stone
abilities.desc: Once a day, accept an offering left on stone; the giver's next death, however distant, will be a good one.

abilities.name: Granted Once
abilities.desc: Whatever rises from a death you granted falls again at once and for good; your endings are not negotiable.

abilities.name: Mourned Already
abilities.desc: Targets you have grieved for count as already dying; your strikes against them cannot miss, and their deaths cannot be undone.

progressionSteps: At level 85, outlive your legend: let the histories decide the Quell is done with the world while you are still holding the fang.
Grant the ending nobody sanctioned and everybody needed, then let the moot of three groves spend a decade deciding it agrees.
Teach your successor nothing; the office chooses as the accord chose you, and your one duty is to die well when relieved.
Be prayed to, incorrectly, in three kingdoms, and mind it less each year.

nodes.name: The Refugium
nodes.role: Sanctuary incarnate — extinction held in abeyance
nodes.lore: The Relict proved one kind was never lost. The Refugium is where the rest have been waiting. It is a druid the way a valley is a rain — technically. Where it settles, drowned kinds surface and hunted ones step out of the treeline, unhurried. Expeditions map it yearly; the maps disagree, and the mapmakers come home vague and happier.
nodes.playstyle: Walking sanctuary: the field becomes deep-time habitat that fights for you; extinct kinds hold your line while enemy maps, bearings, and certainties quietly fail.

abilities.name: Deep Preserve
abilities.desc: Terrain around you becomes refuge; allies inside cannot be tracked, starved, or finished off, and the last of anything cannot die there.

abilities.name: Turnout of Ages
abilities.desc: Call kinds from every stratum at once: a battle-line of beasts no two enemies have both studied.

abilities.name: Wrong on Every Map
abilities.desc: Enemies cannot fix your position by map, memory, or scrying; you are approached by invitation or by luck.

abilities.name: None So Lost
abilities.desc: While you stand, nothing present — kind, oath, or ally — can be reduced to none; one always remains.

progressionSteps: At level 85, let the sworn shape go at last — the kind is safe now — and learn that what remains of you is a place.
Shelter every lost kind of one drowned age through a winter that kills forests, and lose none.
Admit the first pilgrims. Refuse the first collectors. Be geography about it.
Appear on no map in the same place twice, until the gazetteers give up and reclassify you as a season.

nodes.name: The Sufferance
nodes.role: Territorial law — ground held by permission
nodes.lore: After the Greenfalls, kingdoms stopped asking whether the green could take their cities and began asking why it had not. The Sufferance is that answer, seated. Every wall now stands by permission, and the permission walks, hearing petitions at boundary stones. Farmers understand the office best: everything grows where it is suffered to, and nowhere else.
nodes.playstyle: Jurisdictional dominance: grant and revoke the ground itself. Enemy fortifications, footing, and supply exist at your pleasure; allies fight on land that wants them there.

abilities.name: Revoked Ground
abilities.desc: Withdraw permission from terrain an enemy holds; structures subside, crops refuse, wells silt, and morale reads the signs.

abilities.name: Boundary Petition
abilities.desc: Once a day an enemy force may parley at a marker stone; those who deal honestly leave alive, and bound to it.

abilities.name: Standing Permission
abilities.desc: Allies on ground you have granted cannot be starved, mired, or unhorsed; the land carries its guests.

abilities.name: The First Wall
abilities.desc: Raise the accord's memory as a rampart of living wood anywhere; it predates every siegecraft and remembers each.

progressionSteps: At level 85, become less a druid than a condition: when children ask why the forest spared their town, their grandmothers name you.
Hold court at boundary stones for a generation; evict three empires' worth of ambition and not one farmer.
Refuse worship; accept the field-edge left wild, which is all you ever asked for.
When the third Greenfall gathers, decide whether it falls. The histories record nothing of your choice — only that some walls still stand.

nodes.name: The Convalescence
nodes.role: Cosmic support — recovery made inevitable
nodes.lore: Feverbreak ended plagues one at a time. The Convalescence is what the green learned from watching: recovery itself, kept as an office. Where its holder passes, blighted fields remember appetite, burned soil takes seed, and the sick sleep through the night for the first time in years. Three medical colleges deny it exists. Their infirmaries face its road anyway.
nodes.playstyle: Cosmological recovery: everything you protect heals past where it began; battles bend toward mending, and attrition runs backward for your side.

abilities.name: Backward Attrition
abilities.desc: Aura: allied wounds, exhaustion, broken gear, and spent courage all regenerate; the longer the fight, the more whole your side.

abilities.name: Prescribed Rest
abilities.desc: Put one enemy into restorative sleep for a minute; it wakes healed, disarmed, and profoundly unwilling to continue.

abilities.name: Land's Appetite
abilities.desc: Ground you cross yields double for a season; in battle it feeds allies standing on it as a meal would.

abilities.name: The Long Mend
abilities.desc: Once a year, declare a wound of the world healing — a blight, a curse, a battlefield — and its recovery becomes certain.

progressionSteps: At level 85, outlast your own kennel: free every leashed plague into extinction, and stand hostage for the world's health yourself.
Mend one province so thoroughly that war becomes impractical there, and watch armies desert into its farms for a generation.
Sit at the deathbeds the office cannot mend, as a Rotwright would, and keep that half of the accord too.
Let the histories argue whether the age's long peace was policy or convalescence, and water the question.

families.name: Monk
families.tagline: The body is the temple; the fist is the bell.
families.description: The Monk surrendered every possession at the cloister door and kept only breath, bone, and discipline. Years of fasting, stillness, and ten thousand repetitions forged the body into an instrument that needs no blade and fears no siege. Some temper the flesh until steel means nothing; others learn the breath beneath the flesh and strike what armor cannot cover. Both roads end in the same silence.

nodes.name: Monk
nodes.role: Melee striker — unarmed, fast, self-reliant
nodes.lore: Every mountain cloister keeps a novice-roll of those who arrived with nothing and asked to be less. Village orphans, deserters, disgraced scholars — the gate does not ask. They sweep, fast, and repeat the First Form ten thousand times, learning that the body, properly instructed, is the only possession that cannot be taken.
nodes.playstyle: Chain short unarmed strikes into rhythm, weaving between blows; you have no gear to break and no weapon to lose, only tempo.

abilities.name: First Form: Falling Water
abilities.desc: A three-hit open-hand sequence; each strike lands faster than the last and refunds a sliver of stamina.

abilities.name: Measured Breath
abilities.desc: Spend a still moment to steady the lungs, cleansing one minor ailment and restoring focus.

abilities.name: Open Guard
abilities.desc: Deflect the next weapon strike with a bare forearm, taking reduced damage and no stagger.

abilities.name: Beggar's Footing
abilities.desc: Move at full speed across rubble, ice, and rooftops; poverty taught you every surface.

progressionSteps: Arrive at a cloister gate carrying nothing; whatever you still own will be burned on the threshold.
Kneel outside for three days without asking entry; the door opens for patience, never for knocking.
Surrender your name to the novice-roll and answer only to the work you are given.
Repeat the First Form until your hands finish it in your sleep, then begin learning it properly.

nodes.name: Iron Vessel
nodes.role: Frontline bruiser — armorless endurance
nodes.lore: At the tenth year some novices are led to the cold hall, where the outer discipline begins. Iron Vessels stand beneath winter falls, take the staff without flinching, and cure their skin like bell-bronze. Soldiers mock the bare chest exactly once. The cloister sends them where the fighting will be worst and longest.
nodes.playstyle: Wade in unarmored and stay there; convert punishment into steadiness, trading flourish for the certainty that you will still be standing.

abilities.name: Bellbronze Skin
abilities.desc: Years of tempering grant flat damage reduction against all physical harm; you wear no armor and need none.

abilities.name: Root Below Root
abilities.desc: Plant your stance; you cannot be knocked down, dragged, or thrown while your feet hold the earth.

abilities.name: Swallowed Thunder
abilities.desc: Absorb a blow's force into the breath and release it through your next strike as added weight.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10 and stand the Trial of the Ford: remain in the winter river until the ice accepts you.
Take one hundred staff-blows from your teachers without stepping back, counting each aloud so the count never wavers.
Sleep a full season on bare stone without fire, and rise each morning without complaint.
Shatter the cured oak striking-post with your forearm, then stand where it stood for a day.

nodes.name: Breathbinder
nodes.role: Mobile skirmisher — ki bursts, closing distance
nodes.lore: Others are led inward, to the breathing hall where nothing moves but air. Breathbinders learn that breath is the hinge between body and spirit, and a hinge can be swung. They snuff candles at nine paces, cross rooms in a stride too short to see, and speak rarely, hoarding the breath.
nodes.playstyle: Dart in, spend stored breath on sudden force, and be gone before the counterswing; your resource is patience made explosive.

abilities.name: Bound Breath
abilities.desc: Hold and compress a breath over several heartbeats, storing force you may release through any later strike.

abilities.name: The Shortened Road
abilities.desc: Step once and arrive several paces away, crossing pits, flames, and spears as if they were rumor.

abilities.name: Exhaled Edge
abilities.desc: Release a focused breath as a cutting lash of force, striking a target beyond arm's reach.

abilities.name: Reed in Current
abilities.desc: Bend around an incoming blow without moving your feet, letting it pass through where you almost were.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10 and hold a single breath through the whole of the Night Litany, from first bell to last.
Extinguish nine candles from nine paces with one exhalation, disturbing none of the smoke.
Cross the gorge bridge blindfolded, placing each foot where your breath says the rope will be.

nodes.name: Unmoved Pillar
nodes.role: Anchor tank — zone denial, punishing patience
nodes.lore: Garrisons petition the cloister for an Unmoved Pillar the way they petition for grain. One stands where the line must not break — a gate, a ford, a stair — and the line does not break there. They do not pursue. Whatever comes to move them becomes, briefly, an education in why nothing does.
nodes.playstyle: Claim a piece of ground and make it law; enemies who test you are held, slowed, and returned their own violence with interest.

abilities.name: Stance of the Last Door
abilities.desc: While stationary, enemies cannot pass through your reach; the first each round that tries is stopped cold.

abilities.name: Weight of Stillness
abilities.desc: Your calm presses outward; enemies within reach strike slower, as if moving through deep water.

abilities.name: Returned With Interest
abilities.desc: Store a portion of damage taken while rooted and deliver it back through your next palm strike.

abilities.name: Patience of Stone
abilities.desc: Each round you do not move, gain stacking damage reduction, kept until you take a step.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and hold a single doorway against all comers from dusk-bell to dawn-bell, yielding not one step.
Sit the Long Vigil: forty days at the cloister gate, moving only for breath, while pilgrims mistake you for statuary.
Stand in the path of a charge of horse and be the reason it becomes a halt.

nodes.name: Idolbreaker
nodes.role: Armor-breaker striker — demolition of the fortified
nodes.lore: When a false god's shrine must come down and no army can be spared, the cloister sends one Idolbreaker with empty hands. They study a thing until they find where it lies about its own strength, then strike there once. Stone idols, warded doors, champions in proofed plate — everything has a fault.
nodes.playstyle: Read the target, wait for the opening, then commit everything to a single decisive strike that ignores what the enemy trusted most.

abilities.name: Sutra of Breaking
abilities.desc: Your strikes treat armor, shields, and stone as if they were unfired clay, ignoring physical hardness.

abilities.name: Fault-Finding Eye
abilities.desc: Study a target briefly to reveal its structural flaw; your next strike against that flaw cannot be mitigated.

abilities.name: Third Knuckle
abilities.desc: Land a blow that seems gentle; the true force arrives three heartbeats later, deep inside the target.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and split a millstone with one bare palm, on the first and only strike you are allowed.
Enter a shrine of a devouring god and leave nothing standing above knee height, taking no relic for yourself.
Break a champion's shield, then his sword, then his nerve, and let him walk away to say so.

nodes.name: Pilgrim of Nowhere
nodes.role: Hit-and-fade skirmisher — impossible mobility
nodes.lore: Some Breathbinders notice that the road is a suggestion. Pilgrims of Nowhere walk paths that appear on no map and close behind them, arriving before the messenger who announced them. Border lords post rewards; the desperate leave rice at crossroads. Neither has any measurable effect on where a Pilgrim goes.
nodes.playstyle: Never be where the answer lands; step through walls of spears, strike from the flank that did not exist, and leave.

abilities.name: Step Between
abilities.desc: Cross several paces instantly, passing through obstacles, foes, and closed doors as though the world briefly forgot them.

abilities.name: Crossroads Memory
abilities.desc: Mark a place you have stood; once per battle, return to it from anywhere in sight.

abilities.name: Arrive Unannounced
abilities.desc: Your first strike after a step lands as a critical against any foe that has not yet seen you.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and walk from the cloister to the sea in three days, though the road takes seven.
Cross a sealed border without touching gate, wall, or river, and bring back something only the far side grows.
Stand at a crossroads at midnight until you can no longer say which road brought you there, then choose none of them.

nodes.name: Hollow Hand
nodes.role: Spirit-striker — bypasses flesh and armor
nodes.lore: The deepest breathing teaches that flesh is a curtain, and a curtain can be reached past. Hollow Hands leave no bruise and stop hearts; they quiet possessing spirits and lay restless dead with a touch. Clergy request them in unsigned letters. No one who has watched them work requests them twice lightly.
nodes.playstyle: Slip past every defense the enemy built and strike the occupant directly; armor, wards, and even flesh are someone else's problem.

abilities.name: Curtain Strike
abilities.desc: Your palm passes force through armor, shield, and skin untouched, wounding only what lives underneath.

abilities.name: Quieting Touch
abilities.desc: Press two fingers to a caster's sternum; their voice and their magic go silent for a time.

abilities.name: Strike the Tenant
abilities.desc: Deal grievous harm to spirits, possessors, and the undead by hitting the ghost rather than the housing.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and snuff a candle from a full pace away without disturbing its smoke.
Strike the demonstration bell so it sounds inside each listener's chest and not at all in the air.
Lay a restless ghost with one touch, and take nothing from the grieving but your leave.

nodes.name: Stillgate
nodes.role: Living fortification — absolute ground control
nodes.lore: There are never more than a dozen Stillgates alive, and the war-colleges of three empires chart their whereabouts like weather. When a Stillgate accepts a post, the post holds; that is the order's whole doctrine, and no siege in written memory has amended it. Armies reroute rather than test the record.
nodes.playstyle: Become the terrain; while you hold your ground nothing crosses, nothing moves you, and every plan that assumed otherwise dies expensively.

abilities.name: The Post Is Held
abilities.desc: While you remain at your chosen ground, gain immense damage reduction and force all foes in reach to face you.

abilities.name: Threshold Law
abilities.desc: Once each round, an enemy attempting to pass you is simply stopped, its momentum returned as staggering force.

abilities.name: Doctrine of Remaining
abilities.desc: Once per battle, an attack that would fell you leaves you at one breath instead, provided you have not moved.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and hold a breach alone against a named army until relief arrives, or does not.
Be offered honorable retreat by heralds three times in one night, and decline three times, courteously.
Learn that enemy maps now ink your standing-place as a fortification, and let this change nothing in you.

nodes.name: Palm of Ruin
nodes.role: Siegebreaker — single blows that end architecture
nodes.lore: Cities have paid the cloister handsomely for the assurance that no Palm of Ruin is currently traveling toward them.
