These few study a fortress the way physicians study a dying man, then conclude it with one strike. They demolish tyrannies by removing the walls tyranny requires, and they charge nothing for it.
nodes.playstyle: Spend long moments reading, then release a single strike that settles the question; everything about you is preparation for one instant.

abilities.name: One-Palm Demolition
abilities.desc: After a full round of stillness, deliver a blow that collapses gates, walls, and constructs outright.

abilities.name: Ruin Reads the Wall
abilities.desc: Perceive the fault-lines in any structure or armored foe at a glance, through stone if need be.

abilities.name: Aftershock Sutra
abilities.desc: Your great strikes echo; the target and everything touching it take a second, lesser toll one heartbeat later.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and bring down a warded citadel gate with a single strike, after nine days of silent study.
Accept a tyrant's payment to raze a village, return the coin, and perform the demolition on his hall instead.
Leave one wall of the razed fortress standing, so the survivors have shade to grieve in.

nodes.name: Roadless Saint
nodes.role: Phantom skirmisher — battlefield-wide presence
nodes.lore: A Roadless Saint no longer finds the hidden roads; the roads find them. Witnesses swear one stood in two doorways in the same breath, and both doorways agree. Generals pay for the rumor of a Saint's favor, since the reality cannot be bought, followed, borrowed, or confirmed until it has already happened.
nodes.playstyle: Treat the whole battlefield as adjacent; appear where you are needed, strike where you are not expected, and be counted twice.

abilities.name: Two Doorways
abilities.desc: Briefly stand in two places at once; both may strike, and only one was ever really there.

abilities.name: The Unwalked Way
abilities.desc: Open a hidden path a short distance; allies may follow before it closes and forgets itself.

abilities.name: Absent Step
abilities.desc: Once per round, an attack that should have hit you finds you were never in that place.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and attend your own funeral rites in a distant province, leaving without correcting anyone.
Guide a hundred refugees through a mountain pass that the pursuing soldiers swear on their lives does not exist.
Walk out of a sealed oubliette, and never mention it, even when asked by the one who sealed it.

nodes.name: Stillpalm
nodes.role: Executioner — clean, woundless single-target death
nodes.lore: Stillpalms are named in treaties. Certain wars have ended on the rumor that one had taken an interest; certain kings sleep in rooms without doors because of them. They kill without wound and without appetite, and what is more feared, they sometimes decline, and no offer improves the answer.
nodes.playstyle: Choose the one death that ends the battle and administer it precisely; everything else on the field is a distraction to be endured.

abilities.name: Stilling Palm
abilities.desc: Against a weakened foe, stop the heart outright; the body shows no wound and no violence.

abilities.name: Held Verdict
abilities.desc: Touch a foe and defer the blow; the stored death lands whenever you speak the word, hours later if you wish.

abilities.name: Unstrung Knees
abilities.desc: Strike the resolve rather than the body; enemies around you falter, slow, and lose the will to press.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and stop a bull's heart with two fingers, restart it with two more, and master the trembling afterward.
Be listed by name in a peace treaty as a weapon, and attend the signing unarmed and unintroduced.
Refuse a king's execution order to his face, and let the silence escort you out.

nodes.name: Millrace
nodes.role: Engulfing tank — pulls in, holds under
nodes.lore: The cold hall keeps a second doctrine, learned lower in the winter ford, where the current holds what the ice accepts. Where Stillgates refuse entry, Millraces grant it: let the enemy commit, close around them, keep them. One order calls the other appetite; the reply is vanity. They share a founder and have not shared a room since.
nodes.playstyle: Welcome the committed attack; wrap it, hold it, and let the drowning weight of your stillness finish what the enemy began by reaching you.

abilities.name: Closing Water
abilities.desc: Enemies who strike you or enter your reach are gripped by dragging force and cannot withdraw until you release them.

abilities.name: Grip of the Ford
abilities.desc: Seize a foe mid-swing; while held they suffer crushing pressure each heartbeat and their blows land as if underwater.

abilities.name: Fed by the Current
abilities.desc: While an enemy remains in your grip, damage you take is halved and flows back into your reserves as recovered breath.

abilities.name: The Second Lesson
abilities.desc: Release every held foe at once in a drowning surge of force, flinging them prone and breathless at your feet.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and return to the winter ford at thaw, when the river fights back, and hold it in your arms until it calms.
Let a champion strike you thrice unanswered, then hold him, gently, until his army agrees to go home.
Ask a Stillgate to move you; when neither doctrine wins by dawn, bow first, and mean nothing by it.

nodes.name: Winnower
nodes.role: Precision striker — strips arms, wards, pretenses
nodes.lore: The demolition halls parted over a single question: when the idol falls, what happens to the truth it stood on? Palms of Ruin conclude a false thing whole. Winnowers break everything about it that lies — blade, ward, title, nerve — and leave the remainder standing, unarmed and accurate. Each order considers the other's mercy the crueler one.
nodes.playstyle: Disassemble the enemy's advantages one strike at a time — weapon, armor, blessing, formation — until only the honest question of flesh and resolve remains.

abilities.name: Chaff Stroke
abilities.desc: Each strike destroys one thing the target carries, wears, or was granted: a weapon, a ward, a blessing, your choice.

abilities.name: Threshing Hands
abilities.desc: A flurry that strips one protective effect from every enemy in reach and staggers those with nothing left to lose.

abilities.name: What Remains Is True
abilities.desc: Against foes bearing no weapon, armor, or enchantment, your strikes cannot miss and cannot be reduced.

abilities.name: Winnowing Wind
abilities.desc: Exhale across a volley; arrows, bolts, and flung spells are sorted midair, and only the harmless portion arrives.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and strip a proofed champion to skin and certainty without marking the man beneath, and bow if what remains stands anyway.
Enter the counterfeit shrine and break only the seven lies in it, leaving the one honest stone for the villagers to build on.
Watch a Palm of Ruin conclude a fortress you had nearly finished winnowing, and carry what you felt to your teacher unsoftened.

nodes.name: Earthfast
nodes.role: Pursuit hunter — closes roads, denies escape
nodes.lore: Some Pilgrims walk the hidden roads far enough to meet what tends them, and come back changed in the direction of the ground. The Earthfast swear the earth-oath: no step between, ever again — and no such step taken near them, by anyone. Roadless Saints call them wardens of a door they fear. The Earthfast do not argue; they close it.
nodes.playstyle: Run the quarry down on honest ground; every blink, gate, and hidden path near you fails, and what falls out of them meets your fists.

abilities.name: Earth-Oath
abilities.desc: Within your breath's reach, nothing may teleport, phase, or step between; travelers mid-passage are spat out at your feet.

abilities.name: Shut Road
abilities.desc: Touch a door, pass, or crossing to close it for a day; the closed way refuses even those with a right to it.

abilities.name: Honest Miles
abilities.desc: On open ground you outpace horses and never tire in pursuit; distance to a fleeing foe only ever shortens.

abilities.name: Dragged to Daylight
abilities.desc: Seize a foe hidden by shadow, veil, or unreality and haul them onto plain earth, ending the effect that hid them.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and walk your last hidden road to its end, learn what sweeps it, and swear the earth-oath before it notices you have gone.
Chase a sorcerer through nine gates on foot; arrive through none of them and take him at the last, which you closed yesterday.
Refuse a Roadless Saint's shortcut with courtesy, once, while the bridge is burning.

nodes.name: Breathward
nodes.role: Last-breath guardian — no one dies unpermitted
nodes.lore: The inner path forks at the same door. Stillpalms learned to open it; Breathwards hold it shut. While the last breath is unfinished, they teach, the person is not dead — and near a Breathward the last breath can stay unfinished a long time. Kings hire them before signings. Being kept alive by one is not always a mercy.
nodes.playstyle: Fight beside the falling; hold allies on this side of their last breath, suspend enemies at theirs, and permit nothing on the field to finish dying unapproved.

abilities.name: Unfinished Breath
abilities.desc: An ally struck down within your reach does not die this round; they fight on at the threshold until you exhale.

abilities.name: Strike the Breath Home
abilities.desc: Drive a departing spirit back into its body with an open palm; the saved wake wounded, furious, and alive.

abilities.name: Suspended Sentence
abilities.desc: Pin a dying enemy at the threshold: unable to die, act, or be finished until you grant leave.

abilities.name: The Field Is Closed
abilities.desc: Once per battle, declare the field closed; for a short time nothing within your breath's reach can die, including what deserves to.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and sit a plague ward through its worst month, losing no one you were not ready to lose, and be honest about the count.
Hold a soldier at his last breath for three days until his daughter arrives, then give leave, and stay for the grief.
Stand between a Stillpalm and a named tyrant, and win the argument without either of you raising a hand.

nodes.name: Seated Mountain
nodes.role: Immovable colossus — battlefield-defining bulwark
nodes.lore: The histories admit to three. A Seated Mountain sits down and becomes geography: empires reroute roads, storms divide, and sieges starve around a figure that has stopped distinguishing itself from the hill it occupies. Pilgrims cannot always tell which weathered shape on the ridge is the one still breathing.
nodes.playstyle: Sit where the world will break and refuse to let it; you are less a combatant than a fixed fact enemies must survive.

abilities.name: Geography
abilities.desc: While seated, allies behind you cannot be targeted, and weather, spells, and charges divide around your stillness.

abilities.name: The Refusal
abilities.desc: Once per battle, decline a catastrophe; one cataclysmic attack, collapse, or working simply does not occur within your reach.

abilities.name: Erosion's Pace
abilities.desc: All damage you take is deferred and drained away slowly, as weathering, over hours you can afford.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and seat yourself where the coming war will be worst, before anyone else knows a war is coming.
Outlast a siege in which you are the objective; let the army starve around your stillness and go home.
Refuse a god's direct command to move, and be found still seated when the shrine is rebuilt around you.

nodes.name: Iron Knell
nodes.role: Cataclysmic striker — one blow, one ending
nodes.lore: The falling temple bell, made flesh. When an Iron Knell strikes with intent, the sound arrives in neighboring provinces as a single toll with no bell to blame. Their blows are recorded in the annals as dates, and what stood before each date is described in the past tense.
nodes.playstyle: Everything is wind-up for the one strike; when it lands, the battle reorganizes itself around what is suddenly no longer there.

abilities.name: The Toll
abilities.desc: Your strike sounds through everything nearby; all who hear it are staggered, deafened, and briefly unable to act.

abilities.name: One Date in the Annals
abilities.desc: Once per day, deliver a blow that permanently sunders what it hits; what breaks does not mend.

abilities.name: Resonant Marrow
abilities.desc: Your bones ring under impact; whoever strikes you takes the echo of their own blow returned.

abilities.name: The Silence After
abilities.desc: For a breath after your great strike, nothing within earshot may move, cast, or cry out.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and strike the cracked great bell of a fallen temple so it rings true once more, then never again.
Unmake with one blow a fortress that took a generation to raise, and stay a season to bury its dead.
Let the historians ask what engine did it, and let no answer survive you.

nodes.name: Tenth Step
nodes.role: Omnipresent phantom — arrives before the need
nodes.lore: Doctrine holds that nine steps cross the world and a tenth leaves it. Those who take the tenth return rarely and out of order, arriving in some accounts before their own departures. Crossroads shrines address them directly. It is considered unwise to be certain a Tenth Step is absent.
nodes.playstyle: Be everywhere the fight needs you, occasionally before it needs you; distance, walls, and sequence have stopped applying to your movement.

abilities.name: Nine Steps
abilities.desc: Cross any battlefield in nine strides, ignoring walls, wards, chasms, and everything else the world put in the way.

abilities.name: The Tenth
abilities.desc: Step outside the world entirely for a breath; return anywhere you can imagine, untouchable while gone.

abilities.name: Already There
abilities.desc: Once per battle, be retroactively where an ally needed you; the blow that struck them struck you instead, and you were ready.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and take the step your doctrine forbids, and tell no one what waited on the far side.
Arrive before your own departure, and greet yourself without flinching or asking questions.
Hear yourself prayed to at a midnight crossroads, and answer exactly once.

nodes.name: Empty Heaven
nodes.role: Transcendent executioner — ends what cannot die
nodes.lore: The last teaching of the inner path is administered by no one: climb the final stair, strike at heaven, and stand in whatever answers. Those it leaves standing walk back down owning nothing, needing nothing, and able to touch anything — gods included, who are lately difficult to find at home.
nodes.playstyle: Nothing is beyond arm's reach anymore; fight spirits, gods, and abstractions with the same open hand, and end fights by ending the will behind them.

abilities.name: Knocking at Heaven
abilities.desc: Your strikes land on anything with a spirit — ghosts, gods, possessions, curses — regardless of form, ward, or immortality.

abilities.name: Nothing to Take
abilities.desc: Owning nothing, you cannot be disarmed, cursed, possessed, or beguiled; hostile magic finds no purchase and slides off.

abilities.name: The Hollow Answer
abilities.desc: Still every spirit in reach; summons unravel, blessings fall mute, and the possessed wake as themselves.

abilities.name: Unclenched Fist
abilities.desc: End a battle without a death by striking the will to fight from every foe who can still yield.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60, climb the mountain's last stair alone, strike once at heaven, and stand in the silence that follows.
Still the spirit of something that has never died, and keep its name to yourself forever.
Give away your final possession, the self, and walk back down the stairs anyway.

nodes.name: Patient Flood
nodes.role: Engulfing colossus — swallows offensives whole
nodes.lore: Histories record valleys that drowned in windless weather and sieges that marched into a calm and were not seen again. A Patient Flood no longer grips; they merely permit approach. What enters that stillness joins it. The order keeps no reliquary — where a Patient Flood sat, there is a lake, and the lake is not asked questions.
nodes.playstyle: Sit in the path of an offensive and accept it entirely; everything spent against you is held under, and nothing you hold surfaces unchanged.

abilities.name: Permission to Approach
abilities.desc: All enemies may always reach you; all who do are slowed, held, and drained a little more each heartbeat they remain.

abilities.name: Drowned Arsenal
abilities.desc: Projectiles, spells, and charges that enter your stillness sink; store their force quietly, up to a reservoir's worth.

abilities.name: The Flood Remembers
abilities.desc: Release your reservoir once per battle as a slow, total wave that carries every enemy from the field, arranged by weight.

abilities.name: Still Surface
abilities.desc: Attacks against you disturb nothing; you suffer no stagger, no fear, and reveal no wound until you choose.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and settle yourself below the dam the tyrant built, and wait, and let the engineers discover what patience weighs.
Accept a full army's assault without answering a single blow, and be the only thing on the field by evening.
Let the drowned kingdom's survivors curse you by name, and keep that name, since they need it more than you do.

nodes.name: Threshing Floor
nodes.role: Field-wide purifier — falsehood fails in reach
nodes.lore: Old temples keep a bare circle of stone no one will roof, and sweep it, and do not discuss it. Where a Threshing Floor stands, everything within the wind of their arms is tried: forged coin crumbles, glamours drop, and stolen strength runs out of the thief. Histories dispute whether they are people or verdicts.
nodes.playstyle: Stand at the center and try everything that enters; enchantments, disguises, and false advantages fail around you while your own bare hands stay exactly what they claim.

abilities.name: The Trying Circle
abilities.desc: A standing aura: enemy enchantments, illusions, and summoned reinforcements within reach are tested each round and the false ones fail.

abilities.name: Flail of the First Harvest
abilities.desc: A sweeping two-arm rhythm striking every adjacent foe; each hit also strips one falsehood they are wearing or telling.

abilities.name: Chaff Rises
abilities.desc: What you strip does not linger: broken wards, husks, and unmade spells burst outward as blinding chaff that scours enemy eyes.

abilities.name: True Weight
abilities.desc: Your strikes against anything revealed false — construct, glamour, or lie given legs — deal harm its maker cannot mend.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and hold the bare circle at the year's turning while every liar in the province is brought before you, and try them all by hand.
Unmake a usurper's coronation by standing in the cathedral while the false regalia fails, and say nothing during or after.
Be tried on your own floor by your own students, and pass, and never tell them how near it was.

nodes.name: The Overtaking
nodes.role: Inevitable hunter — flight itself fails
nodes.lore: Every famous escape has a final page, and the final pages agree: a weathered figure, already waiting, apologizing for nothing. The Overtaking does not chase; it is what a chase becomes. The hidden roads eject the hunted at their feet, rivers deliver them, and mercy remains available, strictly on foot.
nodes.playstyle: Declare a quarry and become their horizon; wherever they run arrives at you, and everything they spend fleeing is strength you no longer must break.

abilities.name: Named Quarry
abilities.desc: Mark one foe; all movement they attempt, mundane or otherwise, brings them measurably nearer to you until one of you yields.

abilities.name: The Final Page
abilities.desc: Once per battle, be at the place your quarry flees toward before they arrive, rested and unhurried.

abilities.name: No Second Wind
abilities.desc: Fleeing foes shed speed, spells, and courage as they run; whatever they drop is gone when they turn to fight.

abilities.name: Mercy on Foot
abilities.desc: A quarry that stops, turns, and walks to you unarmed may live; the annals record it happening twice.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and end a pursuit your order began eighty years before your birth, then lay the oath to rest at the cloister gate.
Wait at the harbor for a ship that sailed to escape you, and help them moor when the sea brings it back.
Decline to overtake, once, and learn which of you the doctrine actually binds.

nodes.name: The Kept Breath
nodes.role: Mythic warden — death waits for permission
nodes.lore: There is a village in the border hills where no one has died in sixty years, and a battlefield where both armies fell and every man rose to sign the peace. Histories blame weather, miracle, or clerical error. The order knows the truth: somewhere nearby, a Held Breath has not yet finished exhaling, and nothing ends until they do.
nodes.playstyle: Carry the field's every ending in your lungs; allies cannot fall, enemies cannot conclude, and the battle ends the way you breathe it out.

abilities.name: One Long Exhale
abilities.desc: While you sustain the breath, no creature in the battle can die; wounds accrue and wait, politely.

abilities.name: Deferred Endings
abilities.desc: When your exhale finishes, you choose which of the waiting deaths occur and which are refused outright.

abilities.name: Sixty Quiet Years
abilities.desc: Your mere residence wards a place; while you sleep, eat, or garden nearby, nothing within the walls can end.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and inhale at the start of a battle two kings swore would be a massacre, and exhale when the treaty is signed.
Live one ordinary year in the village that does not die, mending fences, and let no one learn what leaves when you do.
Grant death, once, to one who has earned the rest, and hold your own breath steady while you do it.

nodes.name: The Unturning
nodes.role: Absolute anchor — the world turns around you
nodes.lore: The mountain sat; the world kept turning; something had to hold still while it did. Navigators now steer by a fixed point that is not a star, and find it truer. Where the Unturning sits, quakes conclude, wandering gods orbit rather than approach, and maps agree. The office is never empty, though no one has seen it change hands.
nodes.playstyle: Be the point the battle turns around; you do not move, cannot be moved, and everything hostile expends itself circling what it cannot shift.

abilities.name: Hub of the Wheel
abilities.desc: You cannot be moved by anything, including the world; effects that would displace you displace your attacker instead.

abilities.name: Quakes Conclude
abilities.desc: Area catastrophes — quakes, storms, cataclysmic spells — end at your reach and are refunded to no one.

abilities.name: Caught Turning
abilities.desc: Enemies that engage you are caught in the turning; each round they fight you, their footing slides sunwise to where you prefer them.

abilities.name: The Fixed Point
abilities.desc: Allies anywhere may treat your position as true north; once per battle each may arrive beside you regardless of distance.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and remain seated while the world is moved — by war, by god, by cartographer — until all three put it back.
Let navigators fix their charts to you, and never once make a liar of a sailor.
Feel the world begin to turn around your stillness, and forgive it for needing you.

nodes.name: Worldbell
nodes.role: Epochal striker — blows that date the ages
nodes.lore: Every bell ever cast is, metallurgists agree, a copy of something. When a Worldbell strikes with full intent, the copies answer: every tower from the salt coast to the ice rings once, unrung, and historians open a new chapter out of habit. The person has become the original. Ages are not counted in years; they are counted between tolls.
nodes.playstyle: Wind up rarely; when the blow lands it rings through every enemy, structure, and certainty on the field, and the date it makes is yours.

abilities.name: Strike the Original
abilities.desc: Your great blow sounds in every copy: all enemies on the field take its echo, armor and distance notwithstanding.

abilities.name: New Chapter
abilities.desc: Once per battle, end the current engagement outright: surviving combatants are separated, deafened, and reorganized as if the fight were history.

abilities.name: Heard in the Provinces
abilities.desc: Allies who cannot see you still fight within your toll: they gain your steadiness and cannot rout while the ring lasts.

abilities.name: Between Tolls
abilities.desc: While your great strike is spent, enemies who know it will return fight at a penalty; nearly all of them know.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and strike once, and hear the answer come back from towers that were never built to ring.
Outlive the calendar that dated its years from your blow, and attend the founding of the next without striking.
Hang someday in the rebuilt temple's tower — as doctrine, as warning, or as yourself — and let the monks decline to say which.

nodes.name: The Destination
nodes.role: Guardian unbound — every last moment at once
nodes.lore: Somewhere between the ninth step and the tenth, the walker stopped being a person who arrives and became the arriving itself. Every rescue that comes in the last possible moment is now attributed, correctly, to the same office. Crossroads shrines no longer petition; they thank. Scholars note the tense of those inscriptions and take up other subjects.
nodes.playstyle: Exist where you are needed, tense optional; strike from arrivals that have not happened yet and leave through departures already concluded.

abilities.name: In the Nick
abilities.desc: Whenever an ally would die anywhere, you may already be there; the killing blow becomes your opening counter.

abilities.name: Answer at the Crossroads
abilities.desc: Once per battle an ally may call your name at any distance; you arrive regardless of walls, wards, or your own whereabouts.

abilities.name: Departed Already
abilities.desc: Attacks resolve against where you were; you have been elsewhere since before the attacker decided, which courts find difficult.

abilities.name: The Crowded Instant
abilities.desc: Arrive several times into one moment; each arrival may strike once before the moment notices and moves on.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and be present at every last-moment rescue recorded in a single year, including two you have not performed yet.
Attend the dedication of a shrine to you that predates your birth, and leave the offering you remember finding there as a novice.
Arrive, at the end, wherever the world is ending, without being asked, on time.

nodes.name: The Vacant Throne
nodes.role: Ascendant god-ender — heaven kept empty
nodes.lore: Heaven is not empty, theologians insist; it is kept. At the top of the last stair stands a seat no one sits in, and a figure who owns nothing, not even the sitting. Gods do not visit. Pretenders climb occasionally; the accounts of their descents are brief. While the throne stays vacant, nothing worse can claim it.
nodes.playstyle: Fight anything that claims divinity, anywhere it claims it; your open hand outranks godhood, and your poverty is a fortress nothing bribes.

abilities.name: Outrank Heaven
abilities.desc: Your strikes treat gods, avatars, and ascended things as mortal; divinity provides them no defense, healing, or appeal.

abilities.name: The Sitting Refused
abilities.desc: You cannot be deified, worshipped, possessed, or promoted against your will; power offered to you simply is not.

abilities.name: Brief Descent
abilities.desc: Hurl a pretender from any height of power to the foot of their own stair, stripped of everything they climbed with.

abilities.name: Stilled Heaven
abilities.desc: Still every divine working on the field at once; miracles pause, avatars flicker, and prayers queue until you are finished.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and climb the last stair a second time, find the throne built since your first visit, and decline it daily thereafter.
Catch what climbs the stair wearing a dead god's face, and send it down by the fast way.
Keep the seat empty for a hundred years, including from yourself, especially from yourself.

nodes.name: Slackwater
nodes.role: Cosmic bulwark — the tide waits here
nodes.lore: Sailors keep an hour no almanac prints: slackwater, when the whole sea declines to move and wise fleets pray. The person who was a Patient Flood has become that pause. Wherever they stand, the world's violence reaches its mark, hangs, and forgets to fall. The office passes; the hour, the charts note, has never once been vacant.
nodes.playstyle: Anchor the field inside a standing pause; harm arriving anywhere near you queues, waits, and mostly drowns before it is permitted to happen.

abilities.name: The Sea Declines
abilities.desc: Within your reach, all damage from any source is suspended for a breath before landing, and yours is the deciding breath.

abilities.name: Between Tides
abilities.desc: Once per battle, hold the entire field at slack: nothing moves, falls, bleeds, or dies until you exhale.

abilities.name: Weight of the Waiting Sea
abilities.desc: Suspended harm you decline to permit sinks into you as stored force, released through your next open palm as a tide.

abilities.name: Windless Harbor
abilities.desc: Allies within your stillness cannot drown, fall, or be moved, and may breathe your patience as their own once each round.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and stand in the strait the night two navies meet; when neither fleet can persuade an arrow to fly, walk home across the calm.
Be struck from the almanacs as a navigational hazard and entered instead among the tides.
Teach the ocean to wait by waiting longer, once, where it can see you.

nodes.name: The Harrow
nodes.role: Slow world-breaker — what hardened, breaks
nodes.lore: After threshing, the harrow: the toothed patience dragged across the world to break what set too hard to grow. The rank has left the person and entered the calendar — ages end in a harrowing, priests say, and check the horizon. Whoever holds the office walks slowly, is expected nowhere, and arrives exactly where the crust is thickest.
nodes.playstyle: Advance slowly and break everything settled — fortifications, empires' certainties, the enemy's oldest defenses; nothing that has hardened may remain hard in your furrow.

abilities.name: The Furrow
abilities.desc: You advance at a walk and cannot be stopped; walls, wards, and formations you pass through are permanently broken open.

abilities.name: Teeth of Ages
abilities.desc: Your strikes ignore every defense older than a day; entrenchment, ancient wards, and long-held ground count against their owners.

abilities.name: Broken for Sowing
abilities.desc: Ground you have harrowed cannot be fortified again this age, but anything planted in it — camps, crops, causes — thrives.

abilities.name: Come the Harrowing
abilities.desc: Once per age — per battle, in practice — every enemy structure, summons, and standing spell on the field fails at once.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and walk the length of a war unhurried, breaking every wall you pass, until both sides plant rather than rebuild.
Let the priests read your footprints as a season and amend the calendar; decline the feast day they offer you.
Break the oldest hardened thing you know of, which you will find behind your own ribs, and grow whatever comes after.

nodes.name: All Roads
nodes.role: Convergence incarnate — all flight ends at you
nodes.lore: The proverb no longer names a city. Somewhere the office walks, and all roads lead to it: the escaped tyrant, the unserved sentence, the letter posted to no address. Cartographers leave one convergence off every honest map, by treaty. The person is long since beside the point; the roads have agreed among themselves, and they deliver.
nodes.playstyle: Stop pursuing; the field reorganizes so that everything guilty, fleeing, or ripe for judgment is en route to you, on schedules you set.

abilities.name: Every Road Agrees
abilities.desc: All enemy movement on the field, however directed, curves toward you; charges, retreats, and flanking maneuvers arrive at your feet alike.

abilities.name: Delivered
abilities.desc: Once per round, a foe anywhere in the battle is conveyed to arm's reach by whatever route existed; roads are resourceful.

abilities.name: The Missing Convergence
abilities.desc: You appear on no map, scrying, or memory of your route; ambushing you requires an appointment.

abilities.name: Milestones
abilities.desc: Foes brought to you arrive diminished by the distance: winded, unblessed, and separated from anything they dropped along the way.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and stand still for a year while every unfinished pursuit in the world concludes, one after another, at your feet.
Hear the proverb spoken with your meaning in a country you have never visited, and let it stay a proverb.
Walk the one road that leads away, when you find it, and do not look back to see whether it is following.

nodes.name: The Reprieve
nodes.role: Cosmic warden — the stay of execution
nodes.lore: Between verdict and stroke there is an office, and it is occupied. Every gallows-rope that snaps, every avalanche that hesitates, every heart that pauses and reconsiders is the same hand. The law-codes of four nations carry a line no scribe remembers adding: no ending is final until acknowledged. The office outlives every holder, which is, of course, the point.
nodes.playstyle: Intervene at endings anywhere the story can see you; deaths, collapses, and dooms already in motion are subject to review, and you are the review.

abilities.name: Stay Granted
abilities.desc: Undo one ending each round — a death, a collapse, a detonation — returning its subject to the instant before.

abilities.name: Acknowledged
abilities.desc: Endings you personally acknowledge become final beyond appeal; not gods, priests, or necromancy may reopen them.

abilities.name: The Occupied Office
abilities.desc: You cannot be ended while any reprieve you have granted still stands; the paperwork, such as it is, protects you.

abilities.name: Stroke Withheld
abilities.desc: Strike any blow and leave it unfallen in the air for as long as you like; negotiations improve remarkably.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and arrive at every execution held on one gray morning across four kingdoms, and leave each scaffold arguing with its own rope.
Refuse the ending of an age, once, and carry the cost of its continuing without telling anyone what it is.
Acknowledge, at last, one ending you have been refusing since before you held the office, and sit with it until morning.

families.name: Shaman
families.tagline: Every ford has a god; every god has a price.
families.description: The Shaman stands where the living end and everything else begins, speaking for both sides. Ancestors ride willingly in the marrow, lending skill and counsel; the small gods of ford, hearth, and herd accept the proper gifts at the proper times. Nothing is compelled and nothing is raised. Power is a relationship, and the Shaman keeps every one of ten thousand in good repair.

nodes.name: Shaman
nodes.role: Hybrid support — small favors, small gods
nodes.lore: Every district keeps one: the child who left barley at the ford unasked, who heard the hearth mutter and answered politely. The old speaker-for takes such children walking, teaching names, payments, and the dates that must never be missed. The pay is poor. The neighbors are ten thousand, and watching.
nodes.playstyle: Trade small courtesies for small interventions; your strength is local and relational, rising wherever you have paid attention, and paid on time.

abilities.name: Barley at the Ford
abilities.desc: Gift the nearest water-spirit; one enemy crossing, footing, or retreat fails at the worst possible moment.

abilities.name: Grandmother's Steadying
abilities.desc: A forebear rests a hand on yours; reroll one failed action as she would have done it.

abilities.name: Salt on the Sill
abilities.desc: Scatter a proper ward; minor spirits, curses, and ill dreams decline to enter for a night.

abilities.name: Ask the Resident
abilities.desc: Question a place's small god politely; learn what passed here, what waits, and what its help would cost.

progressionSteps: Notice what your village leaves at the ford, the sill, and the first furrow, and begin leaving your own.
Be caught at it by the district's speaker-for, and accept the walking apprenticeship no one ever applies for.
Learn the names, payments, and feast-days of every small god within a day's walk, and miss none.
Hear an ancestor clear its throat behind your ear, and do not turn around until invited.

nodes.name: Kinhost
nodes.role: Versatile melee — borrowed skill, ancestral counsel
nodes.lore: At the rite of the opened door, the apprentice kneels at the family stones and invites. Some forebear always volunteers — a spear-dame, a midwife, a drowned rigger — lending what a lifetime taught. Nothing is summoned and nothing is bound; the Kinhost keeps guests, and guests, well kept, work.
nodes.playstyle: Hand the reins to whichever guest the moment needs — a duelist's parry, a rigger's knots — and thank them aloud while fighting on.

abilities.name: The Opened Door
abilities.desc: Invite a willing forebear in; gain their trade's full proficiency until they take their leave.

abilities.name: Spear-Dame's Parry
abilities.desc: A war-dead guest turns aside a blow you never saw; negate one melee strike each round.

abilities.name: Borrowed Callus
abilities.desc: Your hands remember work you never did; wield any tool, weapon, or instrument as one long practiced.

abilities.name: Eyes of the Line
abilities.desc: The dead keep watch behind you; you cannot be flanked or surprised while hosting a guest.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10 and kneel three nights at your line's stones, asking nothing, until one of the dead asks after you.
Host your first guest through a full day's labor, and credit them by name to everyone you meet.
Learn the full names and standing grievances of five generations, so no guest is ever greeted wrongly.
Part with a guest on good terms, and feel the door stay open behind them.

nodes.name: Handselman
nodes.role: Utility caster — offerings, favors, spirit bargains
nodes.lore: The other road leads to market — the one held at fords and hilltops, where nothing has hands and everything has terms. The Handselman learns each small god's preferred payment: silver for the mill-spirit, a song for the well, first catch for the pike-god. The opening gift matters most. Openings always do.
nodes.playstyle: Prepare the field with gifts and standing favors, then call them due mid-fight — trips, dousings, warnings — one courtesy at a time.

abilities.name: Handsel
abilities.desc: Offer the opening gift; a spirit or place becomes willing to treat with you, whatever its prior mood.

abilities.name: Preferred Payment
abilities.desc: Know at a glance what any spirit wants; your offerings count double and are never refused as wrong.

abilities.name: Favor at the Ford
abilities.desc: Call in a small local kindness: a foe trips, a torch drowns, a door sticks, a whisper warns you.

abilities.name: Etiquette of the Unseen
abilities.desc: Your courtesy is armor; hostile spirits must parley with you a full round before they may do harm.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10 and give a year of offerings without one missed date, through fever, flood, and mourning.
Learn what the sour well was owed a century ago, pay it in full, and drink first.
Be greeted by name at a crossroads by something with no mouth, and return the greeting properly.

nodes.name: Bonechoir
nodes.role: Adaptive striker — a different master each breath
nodes.lore: Some Kinhosts keep table for a standing choir rather than one guest — a duelist dead a century, a wrestler, a poacher, a siege-cook, each lending mastery in turn. Garrison clerks despair of one soldier qualified for six trades. The choir votes on nothing. It volunteers, precisely, one lifetime at a time.
nodes.playstyle: Cycle presiding ancestors like stances; answer every problem with the specialist who solved it in life, and keep the rotation courteous.

abilities.name: Turn at the Reins
abilities.desc: Change presiding guest as a free action; each grants a distinct weapon style, stance, or craft.

abilities.name: Six Lifetimes' Practice
abilities.desc: No weapon, lock, knot, or saddle is unfamiliar; someone in the choir handled one professionally.

abilities.name: The Poacher's Quiet
abilities.desc: A hunting guest presides; your steps make no sound and your first strike from stillness bleeds.

abilities.name: Deathbed Lessons
abilities.desc: When a foe wounds you, the choir studies the technique; gain rising accuracy against that foe.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and win a formal duel in a style extinct for a hundred years, crediting your teacher truthfully at the salute.
Finish a craft-guest's unfinished masterwork with your hands and their patience, and sign it with their name, not yours.
Keep nine guests through one battle without once addressing the wrong one.

nodes.name: Yearteller
nodes.role: Support controller — precedent, counsel, the long view
nodes.lore: Every line keeps one door open for the Yearteller, who carries nine generations of births, oaths, feuds, and weather, attested by the witnesses themselves. Magistrates consult them and regret the completeness. They answer every question the same way: with what happened last time, told by someone who was there.
nodes.playstyle: Fight with hindsight as a weapon; declare precedents that blunt enemy tricks, and lend allies the benefit of every mistake already made.

abilities.name: Answered Before
abilities.desc: Negate a spell or maneuver an ancestor has witnessed; the counter is recited aloud, with attribution.

abilities.name: Nine Generations Deep
abilities.desc: Recall any detail a forebear witnessed — routes, weaknesses, weddings, weather — as though you stood there.

abilities.name: The Grandmothers Confer
abilities.desc: A round of whispered counsel; each ally may reposition or reroll one action as advised.

abilities.name: Blood-Remembered
abilities.desc: Know on sight anyone whose line has dealt with yours, and exactly how that went.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and recite your line nine generations back before the assembled stones, and be corrected on nothing.
Settle a boundary feud with the sworn testimony of the dead, accepted by both farms in daylight.
Receive a dying village's whole memory in one winter, and carry it out through the snow.

nodes.name: Totem-Carver
nodes.role: Controller — standing totems, beast-god tenancies
nodes.lore: Where the Handselman deals in favors, the Totem-Carver deals in lodgings: poles cut and carved to a beast-god's taste — cave-bear, river-pike, carrion-crane — and let for a season's offerings. No contract compels the tenant; good quarters and better manners do. Summoners find the arrangement appallingly informal. It has never once been broken.
nodes.playstyle: Shape the field with planted totems — fear here, vigor there, watchfulness behind — then fight inside the architecture your tenants provide.

abilities.name: Plant the Lodging
abilities.desc: Set a carved totem; its tenant god's aura claims the ground around it until unplanted.

abilities.name: Bear-Cave Bellow
abilities.desc: The bear totem roars; enemies on its ground are shaken, staggered, and driven from it.

abilities.name: Crane's Watch
abilities.desc: The crane totem misses nothing; allies on its ground cannot be surprised, and hidden things are pointed out.

abilities.name: Pike-Still Water
abilities.desc: The pike totem hushes its ground; enemies entering are slowed, and the first to linger is seized.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and carve your first lodging from a lightning-felled tree, with tools you made and manners you were taught.
Be shown the shape the god prefers in a dream, and carve what you saw, not what you wanted.
Keep a totem tenanted one full year with no missed offering, and be recommended by your tenant to its kin.

nodes.name: Good Neighbor
nodes.role: Territory support — the land takes your side
nodes.lore: Some Handselmen settle into a circuit and become what farmers carefully call a Good Neighbor — one who knows every small god between two market towns by name, preference, and grudge. Where they walk, wells stay sweet and fires keep their tempers. Nothing is owed. Everything is, more dangerously, appreciated.
nodes.playstyle: Prepare ground before trouble finds it; on land whose spirits know you, you are formidable — elsewhere, begin introductions immediately.

abilities.name: Names of the Land
abilities.desc: On arrival, learn the local spirits and their preferences; small favors become available within the hour.

abilities.name: Sweetwater Camp
abilities.desc: Your campsite is kept: sleep is safe, wounds knit, and nothing approaches unannounced.

abilities.name: The Ground Objects
abilities.desc: On befriended land, enemy footing fails, gates stick, bowstrings damp, and every shortcut lies.

abilities.name: Hearth-Peace
abilities.desc: Under any roof whose hearth you have greeted, the first blow aimed at you each round goes astray.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and walk your circuit greeting every spirit and well between two towns, omitting none; the omitted remember.
Win back a soured well by finding what it was owed a century ago and paying it without haggling.
Spend a night as the honored guest of a place that kills trespassers, and leave thanked.

nodes.name: Twicelived
nodes.role: Elite duelist — two minds, one body
nodes.lore: The order of the second name holds that hosting is a marriage: one forebear, chosen and choosing, for life. The pair share the body thereafter — one presiding, one watching — and the order's rolls count each member twice. Of the Doorless Hall they say only: a crowd is not company.
nodes.playstyle: Fight with doubled attention — parry while casting, watch while sleeping — and lean on one dead lifetime's mastery made second instinct.

abilities.name: The Second Name
abilities.desc: Your guest is permanent; keep two reactions each round, one theirs, one yours.

abilities.name: Four Hands on the Haft
abilities.desc: Feints, disarms, and blindside strikes fail against you; one of you has always seen it before.

abilities.name: Divided Watch
abilities.desc: One of you is always awake; you cannot be ambushed, and exhaustion accrues at half weight.

abilities.name: The Elder's Turn
abilities.desc: Once per battle your forebear seizes the moment: take a full extra action outside your turn.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and choose your one guest from the whole assembled line, and be chosen back, before witnesses living and dead.
Exchange second names at the stones, knowing the rite has no rite of undoing.
Give the guest a full day of your body each season — their walks, their songs, their grave-visits — and begrudge none of it.
Decline the Doorless Hall's open door at their own table, courteously, and be toasted for it anyway.

nodes.name: Mindhoard
nodes.role: Elite controller — total recall, nothing lost
nodes.lore: The Mindhoards swore one oath: nothing entrusted is ever let go. They keep dead cities street by street, treaties with the signatures' hesitations, famines to the last shared crust. Kings find their completeness unflattering. Of Sin-Eaters they say: a people that prunes its memory bleeds out slowly, smiling.
nodes.playstyle: Turn the battle into precedent as it happens; nothing works on you twice, and your allies inherit every lesson instantly.

abilities.name: The Winters Count
abilities.desc: Each round of battle joins the hoard; gain rising power as the fight becomes precedent.

abilities.name: Not Twice
abilities.desc: Any spell or maneuver used against you this battle fails outright on its second attempt.

abilities.name: Unflattering Account
abilities.desc: Recite a foe's true record aloud; their followers waver and your allies strike them truer.

abilities.name: In the Hoard
abilities.desc: Allies' skills, memories, and oaths cannot be drained, altered, or forgotten in your presence.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and receive a dead city entire — streets, songs, censuses — from the dead who keep it.
Correct a king's chronicle to his face, and survive because every word held.
Take the Long Count: a year reciting winters backward to the first your line remembers, arriving without a gap.
Sit across from a Sin-Eater at a wake and keep what they swallow, so that somewhere, it is still true.

nodes.name: Bellwether
nodes.role: Warding leader — the fold behind the bell
nodes.lore: The Bellwethers keep the old compacts of fold and byre — herd-gods, hound-gods, the patient gods of hives. Their rule is simple: the bell walks first into every danger. No valley records what it owes them; the herds know. Of the Redgifts they say only: whoever feeds wolves is raising wolves.
nodes.playstyle: Name your companions a fold and walk point; while you lead from the front, the covenant hardens everyone walking behind.

abilities.name: The Bell Goes First
abilities.desc: While you are foremost in danger, allies behind you take reduced harm and cannot rout.

abilities.name: Compact of the Fold
abilities.desc: Name your companions a fold; they gain herd-god endurance, and the scattered always know the way back.

abilities.name: Hound-Gods' Circuit
abilities.desc: Spirit hounds circle the fold; the first flanker each round is intercepted, loudly.

abilities.name: Milk and Firstwool
abilities.desc: Make the fold's offering; everyone in your bound is mended and cleansed of one affliction.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and bring a starving valley's herds through a wolf-winter, losing none you did not name beforehand.
Carry the bell first through a gate everyone present knows is wrong, and ring it going in.
Stand between raiders and the fold with nothing but the compact, and watch their horses refuse.
Refuse a Redgift's offered peace with the wolves, and pay for your winter the long way.

nodes.name: Guestright
nodes.role: Sanctuary controller — courtesy as fortification
nodes.lore: In four centuries the order of Guestright has never compelled, tricked, or missed a date, and the unseen know it. Their answer to a god gone bad is withdrawal: no offering, no name, no notice, until the ford weeps and treats. Godsreeves, they observe, are one bad day from being Necromancers of the air.
nodes.playstyle: Win by standing; declare truce-ground, call freely given aid, and let land that likes you refuse your enemies everything.

abilities.name: Perfect Guest
abilities.desc: Traps, wards, and hostile ground decline to harm you; you have standing wherever custom has been kept.

abilities.name: Declared Hearth
abilities.desc: Draw a circle and name it hearth; within it, no spirit or spell may do violence while parley holds.

abilities.name: Withheld Custom
abilities.desc: Name a hostile spirit's offense; every gift, aura, and power it grants others fails while it stands accused.

abilities.name: Ten Thousand Invitations
abilities.desc: Once per day, ask one great favor of the gods you have kept faith with; one always says yes.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and keep every date for seven years; the order counts, and so does everything else.
Be welcomed as a guest by something that has eaten every guest before you, and leave it a better host.
Starve a murdering ford-god by courtesy alone — village moved, name unspoken — until it weeps and treats.
Turn a Godsreeve from a door you both know they could break, armed with nothing but the custom, and be obeyed.

nodes.name: Doorless Hall
nodes.role: Elite generalist — a specialist for every moment
nodes.lore: They took their doors off the hinges at the founding, and mean it: any decent dead may lodge, a night or a decade. A different master answers every need, and none is asked to stay. Of the Twicelived they say: the dead are a nation, not a spouse, and depth is hoarding.
nodes.playstyle: Carry the broadest toolkit on any field; open each fight with the right three guests and trade them freely as problems change.

abilities.name: The Hall Is Open
abilities.desc: Begin each battle hosting three volunteers of your choosing; each grants a full mastery.

abilities.name: Right Guest, Right Moment
abilities.desc: Once per round, exchange one guest for another better suited to the immediate problem.

abilities.name: Crowded Rafters
abilities.desc: Many watchers: you cannot be surprised, and every lie told near you is recognized by whoever coined it.

abilities.name: The Whole Hall Answers
abilities.desc: Once per battle every lodger lends one heartbeat at once: a single action of overwhelming, borrowed skill.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and unhang your door before the line's stones, and burn the hinges.
Host nine strangers' dead in nine nights, learning each name, trade, and favorite chair.
Attend a Twicelived wedding-rite and hold your tongue; then go home and take in the forebear nobody chose.

nodes.name: Sin-Eater
nodes.role: Absorbing support — eats what ails others
nodes.lore: When two villages must share a well but cannot share what they did to each other, a Sin-Eater is sent for. Bread is passed over the dead; the worst is eaten; the living get on. The church keeps no rite for this, and no objection it cares to own. Mindhoards call it mutilation of the record. Sin-Eaters call it surgery.
nodes.playstyle: Eat what is hurting your allies — curses, terrors, griefs — and carry it visibly; you are strongest when heaviest.

abilities.name: Funeral Bread
abilities.desc: Eat an affliction off an ally — curse, fear, madness, poison — taking it into yourself at half weight.

abilities.name: Swallowed Grudge
abilities.desc: Consume an enemy's vengeance; whatever power their hatred, oath, or grief was feeding, it starves.

abilities.name: Strong Stomach
abilities.desc: What you carry cannot kill you; carried afflictions never stack past bearable, merely past pleasant.

abilities.name: The Table of Ills
abilities.desc: Once per battle, eat every hostile effect on your companions in one grim sitting.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and eat your first great sin at a stranger's wake, and keep it down, and keep it.
Let two villages that murdered each other share a market again, because only you remember why they could not.
Be cursed by a Mindhoard for the mercy of it, and thank them for keeping what you now carry.

nodes.name: Redgift
nodes.role: Blood-paying striker — lent fangs, honest fees
nodes.lore: The Redgifts keep the other compact: the predators' one. Wolf-gods, bear-gods, the carrion-cranes — all fed on schedule, all from the shaman's own arm, and in return the wild hunts beside the village instead of through it. Bellwethers call them wolf-feeders. The Redgifts answer: the fold stands because the wolves agree it may.
nodes.playstyle: Pay power's fee in your own blood; every invocation costs, and every cost buys teeth that something else must answer.

abilities.name: The Wolf's Share
abilities.desc: Open your arm; the pack-god strikes one foe as lent fangs, savage in proportion to what you paid.

abilities.name: Carrion Terms
abilities.desc: Promise the crane-gods first pick of the field; they harry your enemies, eyes first, until it is theirs.

abilities.name: Old Bear Rising
abilities.desc: Pay heavily; a bear-god fights beside you for a scene — uncompelled, well fed, and thorough.

abilities.name: Fees Current
abilities.desc: While your payments stand current, no beast or beast-god will harm you; their strikes refuse at the last.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and open your arm at the wolf-stone on midwinter, and be answered before the blood cools.
Keep the red calendar one full year — every date, your blood, nobody else's.
Sleep a night in the den as a guest whose fee is current, and wake unmarked among the yearlings.
Let a Bellwether watch you pay, and answer their look with the count of lambs alive because you do.

nodes.name: Godsreeve
nodes.role: Spirit-hunter — sanctions gods that break terms
nodes.lore: Custom binds both parties, or it is superstition. When a hearth sours births or a ford drowns past its due, the Godsreeve serves notice under the old custom, which the small gods are held by more deeply than any spell. Guestright calls it bullying. The Reeves speak for the drowned children, who call it late.
nodes.playstyle: Drag the unseen into the open and prosecute; strip a god's gifts, evict its tenancy, and make the field inhospitable to spirits.

abilities.name: Serve Notice
abilities.desc: Name a spirit's breach aloud; it must manifest visibly for a scene, and may be struck.

abilities.name: Distrainment
abilities.desc: Seize a hostile god's gathered offerings; wield its stolen strength against it for the rest of the battle.

abilities.name: Eviction
abilities.desc: Cast a possessor or haunt out of body, house, or field; it may not return for a year and a day.

abilities.name: Custom Has Teeth
abilities.desc: Any spirit that harms one under your protection takes the same harm back, as the old custom provides.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and prosecute your first god — the ford that took the miller's daughters — and carry the verdict home dry-shod.
Post the year-and-a-day watch on an evicted haunt, all of it, awake.
Break a door a Guestright would have knocked at, and answer for it at their table without lowering your eyes.

nodes.name: The Second Skeleton
nodes.role: Mythic duelist — two lifetimes, load-bearing
nodes.lore: Carried long enough, a guest stops being carried. The histories name a handful in whom the seam closed entirely — one continuous person across two lifetimes, the elder bones bearing weight the younger never could. Asking which of the two is alive is considered rude by the order and unanswerable by the church.
nodes.playstyle: Fight as one person with two lifetimes' instincts; wounds, watches, and burdens are shared across a frame built double.

abilities.name: Load-Bearing
abilities.desc: Blows that would fell you are taken up by the elder frame; you remain standing past mortal arithmetic.

abilities.name: Two Lifetimes at Once
abilities.desc: Mastery of everything either life ever practiced, held simultaneously, without switching.

abilities.name: No Vacancy
abilities.desc: Possession, domination, and beguilement fail outright; the house is full.

abilities.name: The Elder Hour
abilities.desc: Once per battle the forebear presides entirely: for one round, act with a dead master's full prime.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and be addressed by the stones as one name, and answer without deciding which of you speaks.
Host your guest's own forebear for a season, and learn what your marriage looks like from above.
Let the physicians declare you dead and the genealogists declare you living, and correct neither.

nodes.name: The Unforgotten
nodes.role: Mythic archive — fallen nations, standing account
nodes.lore: When the last speaker of a tongue dies, one of these wakes fluent, because the dead ask to be kept somewhere warm. The Unforgotten carry extinguished nations entire — law, lullaby, grievance. Empires have sent armies to court or kill them, and found the attempt already entered in the account, dated.
nodes.playstyle: Fight with the skills of extinct peoples and the foresight of complete records; nothing about your enemy is new to everyone you carry.

abilities.name: The Account Includes You
abilities.desc: Your dead have met your foe's people, always; begin every fight knowing their habits, oaths, and fears.

abilities.name: Extinct Techniques
abilities.desc: Strike in styles no living school counters; defenses trained against the present fail against the departed.

abilities.name: As It Is Kept
abilities.desc: Near you, glamours, forgeries, and false histories fail; things revert to what the witnesses attest.

abilities.name: Nowhere Lost
abilities.desc: Allies' minds and skills cannot be erased, drained, or taken in your presence.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and wake speaking a drowned tongue, and go find the last stones that grieve in it.
Attend the burning of a library and walk out carrying it, because its keepers died volunteering.
Recite a king's inherited crimes from his own scaffold until the crowd unbuilds it.

nodes.name: The Fold
nodes.role: Mythic protector — nothing preys within the bounds
nodes.lore: Where the Fold stands, the compact holds absolutely: within their bounds nothing preys, and predator and prey wait out the weather together, embarrassed. Refugee columns have crossed war-winters inside that walking peace. Histories dispute whether the great wolves obey the person or the office. The wolves decline to clarify.
nodes.playstyle: Walk your bounds through the worst of it; inside, allies cannot be preyed upon, and hunger of every kind waits outside.

abilities.name: Within the Wattle
abilities.desc: Declare your bounds; inside them, ambush, sniping, and every advantage of predator over prey simply fails.

abilities.name: No Wolf Here
abilities.desc: Stalking, terror, and the singling-out of the weak cannot function inside your bounds.

abilities.name: Gathered In
abilities.desc: Once per battle, every scattered or fleeing ally is drawn safely to your bounds and steadied.

abilities.name: Counted and Kept
abilities.desc: Name your fold at dusk; those named cannot fall below one breath while your bounds hold.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and walk a fleeing people through a war so that the war never quite finds them.
Pen a battle: step between two armies, declare the field fold, and be obeyed by the hungrier side first.
Winter with the wolves inside your own bounds, and share the same fire without one sheep's worth of doubt.

nodes.name: The Laid Table
nodes.role: Mythic diplomat — sanctuary wherever they sit
nodes.lore: Wherever they sit becomes the table, and the table is always laid, and the unseen come to dinner. Feuds between river-gods have ended over that bread. Historians dispute whether the table is wherever they are, or they are wherever the table is; the guests consider the question poor manners.
nodes.playstyle: Turn any ground into sanctuary and any enemy of the unseen into a dinner guest; battles end at your table or not at all.

abilities.name: A Seat for the Unseen
abilities.desc: Invite any spirit or god to sit; seated, it does no harm and grants one boon, having come for dinner.

abilities.name: Peace of the Board
abilities.desc: While your table stands, violence within its light falters; blows soften, spells hesitate, parley holds.

abilities.name: What the House Provides
abilities.desc: Food, shelter, and mending appear as ten thousand small hosts repay old courtesies at once.

abilities.name: The Great Favor
abilities.desc: Once per day, call in the largest kindness you are owed; some small god intervenes decisively.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and lay the table between two armies, seating the hearth-gods of both homelands, while the soldiers watch.
Host the feud of two rivers until it ends in the only place it could: over your bread.
Eat alone one night a year, so you remember what the table is for.

nodes.name: The Thronged
nodes.role: Mythic multitude — a nation in one frame
nodes.lore: Host enough guests for long enough and the census becomes a matter of opinion. The Thronged walk into town as one person and are remembered as a procession. Tyrants dislike them professionally: a people that was scattered, burned, and forbidden is walking around inside one polite visitor, intact.
nodes.playstyle: Bring a nation to a fistfight; meet every task with its best dead practitioner and every hardship with a thousand steadying hands.

abilities.name: A People Presiding
abilities.desc: Every action is taken by whichever of your thousands did it best in life.

abilities.name: Steadied by Thousands
abilities.desc: Wounds, terror, and despair are shared across the throng; what would break one person thins across many.

abilities.name: Ten Hundred Witnesses
abilities.desc: No deed done near you can be denied afterward; oath-breakers are known to every line you carry.

abilities.name: The Riding Out
abilities.desc: Once per battle the whole throng surges through your limbs: one act of numberless, unanimous skill.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and carry an entire fallen clan through their last feast-day, and be their hall, and wash up after.
Enter a tyrant's census as one name and be counted eleven hundred, none of them incorrectly.
Be refused a room at an inn for the noise, having sat silent all evening, and pay for the damages the dead insist they caused.

nodes.name: The Fed Silence
nodes.role: Mythic sink — catastrophe eaten, kept down
nodes.lore: In certain provinces there is a quiet that must be fed, and everyone knows the house it lives in. Villages bring it their worst year; kingdoms, discreetly, their worst century. Where it dwells, old horrors stay down — not bound, not banished. Digested. It is a very calm neighbor.
nodes.playstyle: Consume what the field cannot survive — curses, cataclysms, names — and grow heavier, calmer, and harder to move with each swallow.

abilities.name: Fed and Sleeping
abilities.desc: What you have eaten stays eaten; no art, god, or grief can restore a thing you swallowed.

abilities.name: Bring It Your Worst
abilities.desc: Once per battle, eat one ongoing catastrophe — a curse-storm, a rout, a burning — whole.

abilities.name: Heavy with Years
abilities.desc: Attacks on your mind and soul sink into the stored silence and do not come back out.

abilities.name: The Spared Seat
abilities.desc: Folk leave your seat empty by instinct; enemies must overcome dread merely to target you.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and eat the name of a feud so old that both houses believe they were always friends, and carry the truth alone.
Be fed a reign by the heir who cannot rule beside it, and bow to the better king you made.
Refuse, once, to eat, and make the village look at what it brought you.

nodes.name: The Open Vein
nodes.role: Mythic provider — hunger's fee, personally met
nodes.lore: Famine-winters end at their arm. The Open Vein pays the wild's whole fee personally, and has for years, and the gods of hunger know their taste the way herdsmen know a bell. Nothing that eats will take another while they stand offering. What this costs is not discussed in front of them.
nodes.playstyle: Bleed on purpose and buy the extraordinary; the deeper the cut, the greater the answering hunt, and you decide what you can spare.

abilities.name: The Great Fee
abilities.desc: Spend any amount of your own blood; the predator-gods answer in strict, generous proportion.

abilities.name: Known to Every Hunger
abilities.desc: Devouring things — beasts, famine-gods, drainings — will not take another creature while you stand offering.

abilities.name: Sworn on the Vein
abilities.desc: Terms sealed in your blood have never been broken by the other side; invoke one such term each battle.

abilities.name: Everything Left
abilities.desc: At death's edge, offer everything left; every god you ever fed answers at once, and they carry the fight.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and end a famine-winter at the wolf-stone with one arm and the whole of a season's nights.
Learn what your blood is worth on the far side, and never once renegotiate.
Watch the pack lay a winter's kills at your door, unasked, and understand it as thanks.

nodes.name: The Quiet Court
nodes.role: Mythic magistrate — the unseen bring their disputes
nodes.lore: Where they sit, court is quietly in session, and the small gods arrive of their own accord — plaintiff wells, defendant winds, a hearth seeking custody of a family. Findings are enforced by the custom itself, which has no officers and needs none. The living mostly notice better weather.
nodes.playstyle: Preside rather than fight; call the unseen to session, strip the convicted of station, and let outlawry do your pursuing.

abilities.name: Session
abilities.desc: Declare court; every spirit on the field must appear plainly, state its business, and abide the finding.

abilities.name: Stripped of Station
abilities.desc: Convict a hostile god; its powers, grounds, and offerings are forfeit for a year.

abilities.name: Contempt
abilities.desc: A spirit that flees your court is outlawed; every ward bars it and every hearth refuses it shelter.

abilities.name: The Custom Provides
abilities.desc: Invoke any lesser ruling ever rendered under the old custom; precedent applies, immediately.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and try a river in spate, and have the finding honored by the water while it is still angry.
Hear the case the wind has been bringing back for a hundred years, and close it.
Recuse yourself once, publicly, and let the unseen watch what the law does without you in it.

nodes.name: The Eldest
nodes.role: Apotheosis — forebear of record to all lines
nodes.lore: Trace any family honestly and far enough, and the lines converge on an office rather than a person. The Eldest is everyone's forebear of record: every stone answers them, every line's dead defer, and each holder, dying, joins the guests of the next. The office has never once been vacant. Genealogists have stopped checking.
nodes.playstyle: Fight as the head of every family at once; any willing dead of any line may preside, and all of them are willing.

abilities.name: Forebear of Record
abilities.desc: Host any willing dead of any lineage on earth; none has ever declined the Eldest.

abilities.name: The Stones Answer
abilities.desc: Anywhere you stand, the local dead treat you as their own; their ground, memory, and standing are yours.

abilities.name: Seniority
abilities.desc: Bloodline curses, house oaths, and powers of inheritance bend to your ruling; you outrank the ancestor they cite.

abilities.name: While Any Line Lives
abilities.desc: You cannot be unmade while anyone living has ancestors; the office declines to lapse.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and watch three unrelated houses trace their lines honestly, and arrive, all three, at you.
Hold the winter feast at which every family's dead attend one table, and carve.
Greet the previous Eldest among your own guests, and understand, at last, where Eldests go.

nodes.name: The Long Memory
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the world's act of remembering
nodes.lore: Above every archive there is a memory that does not burn, and it is awake. The Long Memory is the office by which the world recalls itself: what it holds cannot be made never to have been. Conquerors erase; a generation later every child somehow knows. Clerks call it providence. The dead call it work.
nodes.playstyle: Know everything the dead ever witnessed and lend it freely; near you the past is present tense and erasure runs backward.

abilities.name: On Good Authority
abilities.desc: Anything ever seen by anyone now dead is available to you on request, with attribution.

abilities.name: Erasure Fails
abilities.desc: Workings of forgetting, unmaking, and false history collapse near you; what was hidden is re-attested.

abilities.name: Remembered Valor
abilities.desc: Once per battle, the field recalls its finest hour; allies fight with the skill of everyone who ever held this ground.

abilities.name: Beyond Slander
abilities.desc: You cannot be falsified, glamoured, or misquoted; every attempt reports its author to you.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and receive the memory of the first speaker-for, passed holder to holder since before the word for it, and add one winter.
Attend the burning of a murdered people's last archive, and let the murderers discover, in a generation, that every child knows.
Be asked by a Sin-Eater's heir to surrender one memory, and refuse, gently, and keep also the asking.

nodes.name: Worldfold
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the world penned safe at night
nodes.lore: The old songs are literal: the world is a fold, the dark outside is full, and something walks the wattle-line at night. The office is why the wild suffers villages to exist, and why what circles beyond the edge stays beyond it. Shepherds everywhere set aside a fleece at shearing. None could say who told them to.
nodes.playstyle: Hold the bound of the world itself; declare ground inside the fold and nothing may prey there, whatever world it came from.

abilities.name: The Bounds Walked
abilities.desc: Declare any ground within the world's fold; nothing may prey upon it, including things from outside the world.

abilities.name: Outside the Wattle
abilities.desc: Put one enemy out; it is exiled beyond the world's edge, alone with what circles there, until you relent.

abilities.name: First Through the Dark
abilities.desc: You take the first harm of any new horror personally; having taken it, your fold is proof against it after.

abilities.name: The Flock of Nations
abilities.desc: Every settlement knows the office; their dogs, herds, hearths, and dead rally to you unasked.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and walk the world's bound once around, greeting what patrols the far side of the wattle, and renew the terms.
Fetch back the lamb that got out, whatever it had become by the time you found it.
Stand at the edge on the long night, and be the reason the world has an edge.

nodes.name: The Welcome
nodes.role: Apotheosis — hospitality as a standing force
nodes.lore: Wherever a stranger is fed, the office is present; wherever a guest is harmed, the weather takes it personally. The Welcome is hospitality made a fact of the world: fires burn taller for the offered seat, and the guest-killer finds that roofs leak, roads lengthen, and fords deepen for him, everywhere, forever.
nodes.playstyle: Arrive anywhere custom is kept, shelter whomever you name, and unmake enemies not with blows but with a world that stops hosting them.

abilities.name: Wherever Bread Is Broken
abilities.desc: Step from any kept hearth to any other, anywhere, arriving as an expected guest.

abilities.name: The World Recuses
abilities.desc: Judge a violator of guest or host; fire, water, roof, and road refuse them from this day on.

abilities.name: Sanctuary Absolute
abilities.desc: Declare a hearth; within its light no violence of any kind, by anyone, succeeds until the embers die.

abilities.name: The Owed World
abilities.desc: Ten thousand small gods keep accounts in your name; once per day the world itself does you a favor.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and let midwinter find you at every hearth that set a place for the unseen, and leave each one fuller.
Pass judgment on a king who killed a guest, and let his fires go out to say so.
Be, at the last, the knock at the door in every story where the stranger turns out to matter.

nodes.name: The Folkmoot
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the dead in permanent assembly
nodes.lore: The dead outnumber the living and have opinions, and somewhere the moot of all of them is permanently in session. The office carries it. No age is decided by the living alone anymore: wars have ended because the fallen of both sides voted, and were, for the first time anyone could recall, counted.
nodes.playstyle: Bring the weight of every dead voice to the field; contests of will become votes you cannot lose, and the fallen of both sides attend.

abilities.name: Standing of the Dead
abilities.desc: In any battle, the dead of both sides may take a side; those who listen to the dead are preferred.

abilities.name: Counted Among
abilities.desc: Each ally fights bolstered by everyone who ever loved them; the dead make surprisingly good seconds.

abilities.name: The Objection
abilities.desc: Once per round the moot objects; one enemy action is suspended while the matter is heard, and the matter takes a while.

abilities.name: Recess
abilities.desc: Once per battle the moot withdraws its consent from the violence; enemy resolve, formations, and borrowed powers collapse.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and convene the first full sitting in nine ages, and read the roll until the stars change.
Overrule a living empire's declaration of war with the recorded refusal of its own dead, spoken into the wind.
Take the chair that has stood empty nine ages, and learn that the office was never yours; you are its.

nodes.name: The Amnesty
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the past pardoned, struck, void
nodes.lore: Beyond forgetting there is a standing pardon, and someone holds it. What the Amnesty swallows is not hidden but void: the feud unhappened, the blood-guilt lifted from children not yet born. Custom in three mountain provinces keeps a saying no elder remembers coining: what has been eaten shall not be inherited.
nodes.playstyle: Annul rather than defeat; eat curses, feuds, and inherited dooms out of the world entirely, and walk lighter than you have any right to.

abilities.name: Voided
abilities.desc: Consume a curse, oath, feud, or doom; it never binds anyone again, anywhere, beginning with today.

abilities.name: Eaten Whole
abilities.desc: Swallow one hostile working outright, however large; it is not dispelled but digested, and cannot be made again.

abilities.name: General Pardon
abilities.desc: Once per day, annul every affliction, geas, and inherited penalty binding your companions, in one sitting.

abilities.name: Nothing to Avenge
abilities.desc: Powers fueled by vengeance, grievance, or old wrongs find no fuel near you; you have eaten their reasons.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and eat the founding crime of an empire, and watch it survive being innocent.
Hold the amnesty of an age: one night when anything may be brought to your door, and everything is.
Teach your successor to eat, and offer them, first and freely, everything you carry.

nodes.name: The Portion
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the share the unseen are owed
nodes.lore: From every harvest something goes missing, and no one asks, because the missing share is the arrangement. The Portion is that share, walking: the office through which the world's ten thousand hungers are fed on schedule and therefore mind their manners. Bad years happen where it has not lately been. It travels constantly.
nodes.playstyle: Stand at the center of every exchange; all power spent near you pays you a share, and everything you feed fights for you.

abilities.name: Taken First
abilities.desc: The first harm of every battle is taken by you and converted whole into payment for your gods.

abilities.name: The Set-Aside
abilities.desc: Every enemy spell, strike, and blessing pays you a share as it happens; you grow strong on their effort.

abilities.name: No Hunger Unfed
abilities.desc: Starvation, drain, and devouring effects fail near you; every appetite present has already been paid.

abilities.name: Call the Fed
abilities.desc: Once per day, everything the office has ever fed answers at once. Stand somewhere dry.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and take the portion of a whole age's harvest in one night, and deliver it, shrine by shrine, before dawn.
Stand in the granary of a starving city and be the reason the hunger takes its share from the war instead.
Go unfed yourself one year in ten, so the office remembers whom it serves.

nodes.name: The Old Custom
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the law beneath the gods
nodes.lore: Older than the gods' names is the way things were first agreed, and it is not a document; it is an office, walking. Fords take only their due because the Old Custom holds.
