Its holder is forgotten by name in their own lifetime and addressed by title at every threshold on earth. The gods stand when it enters.
nodes.playstyle: Preside over the terms of the world's oldest handshake; spirits behave as first agreed near you, and your rulings become how things are.

abilities.name: As First Agreed
abilities.desc: Revert any god, spirit, or bargained place to its founding terms; corruption, usurpation, and bad amendments fall away.

abilities.name: Older Than Names
abilities.desc: No spirit or god may act against its own terms in your presence; each behaves as it originally promised.

abilities.name: The Custom Walks
abilities.desc: Every ford, hearth, and threshold where custom was ever kept is adjacent to you; arrive by any of them.

abilities.name: The Old Ruling
abilities.desc: Once per day, rule on anything; the world enforces the ruling as though it had always been custom.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and be forgotten by name in your own lifetime, and answered to by title at every ford on earth.
Reopen the first case — the original breach between the living and the unseen — and settle it at last, out of court.
Amend the custom once in an age, and spend the rest of the age paying for it.

families.name: Necromancer
families.tagline: Death is a resource. Spend it wisely.
families.description: Every library keeps one shelf chained, and the Necromancer has read it twice. They begin as scholars of the body's last hour and end as auditors of mortality itself — raising the fallen as labor and infantry, rendering souls into fuel and testimony, and filing their own death under pending. Feared not for cruelty, but for bookkeeping: nothing they love stays buried, and nothing they need stays dead.

nodes.name: Necromancer
nodes.role: Summoner — attrition caster with expendable minions
nodes.lore: Most necromancers begin as failed physicians, grave clerks, or students who asked the anatomy lecturer one question too many. Universities expel them; cemeteries employ them. The rank means little more than survival — a scholar who has raised one servant, buried one mistake, and learned that the dead answer politely if the question is precise.
nodes.playstyle: Fight through a single raised servant while draining life from range; trade the minion for time, rebuild it from whatever the battle leaves behind.

abilities.name: Exhume
abilities.desc: Raise one corpse as a shambling servant that fights until destroyed or dawn, whichever comes first.

abilities.name: Last Breath
abilities.desc: Siphon vitality from a wounded enemy; the drain doubles against targets below a quarter of their health.

abilities.name: Chill of the Slab
abilities.desc: Numb a target with mortuary cold, slowing their attacks and dulling their pain into hesitation.

abilities.name: Grave-Speech
abilities.desc: Ask one question of a corpse dead less than a day; it must answer, though not kindly.

progressionSteps: Read the chained book to its last page, and let no librarian catch you weeping at the margins.
Sit a night's vigil with an unclaimed corpse and learn its name without being told.
Raise your first servant from a pauper's grave, and pay the grave back with honest coin.
Be expelled, disowned, or declared dead — whichever your city requires — and keep studying anyway.

nodes.name: Corpsebinder
nodes.role: Minion commander — sustained frontline pressure
nodes.lore: Corpsebinders are the trade's first honest rank: practitioners who keep three or more dead in working order through a full campaign season. Mercenary companies hire them quietly to reduce burial costs and double as reinforcements. The binding is craft, not terror — knots of sinew, verses of ownership, and a ledger of every body owed.
nodes.playstyle: Command a small squad of durable undead from the second rank; repair them mid-fight, rotate the freshest forward, and let attrition do the arguing.

abilities.name: Muster of the Fallen
abilities.desc: Raise up to three corpses at once; each bound minion persists until destroyed rather than expiring at dawn.

abilities.name: Splint and Sinew
abilities.desc: Mend a damaged minion with grave-thread, restoring it to fighting order over six seconds.

abilities.name: Dead March
abilities.desc: Your minions advance in lockstep, gaining speed and immunity to fear while moving toward your marked target.

abilities.name: Tithe of Teeth
abilities.desc: Harvest a destroyed minion's remains to reduce the cost of your next raising.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10 and keep three risen servants standing through a full turning of the moon.
March your dead twenty leagues without losing one to rot, rivers, or wandering priests.
Bind a soldier who died mid-order, and see that the order is carried out.
Present your ledger of bodies to a Gravemarshal and have no entry questioned.

nodes.name: Pale Scholar
nodes.role: Control caster — soul-siphon and denial
nodes.lore: Pale Scholars have stopped studying death in bodies and started studying it in themselves. They fast until the pulse slows, copy forbidden folios by lantern-light, and learn to hold a departing soul the way other scholars hold a quotation. The pallor is not illness. It is the first negotiation with mortality, opened politely.
nodes.playstyle: Control the fight's tempo from range: slow hearts, sever escapes, and bank every kill as stored soul-light to fuel the next incantation.

abilities.name: Soul-Lantern
abilities.desc: Catch a soul at the moment of death in a glass vessel; spend it later as spell fuel.

abilities.name: Sever the Silver
abilities.desc: Cut the cord between body and soul on a target below one-fifth health, ending them instantly.

abilities.name: Deadman's Ledger
abilities.desc: Inscribe an enemy's name; if they die within the hour, you learn everything their soul carried.

abilities.name: Pallor
abilities.desc: Still your own heart for ten seconds; the dead ignore you and death-magic passes through.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10 and copy the Sallow Concordance in your own hand without once misspelling a true name.
Distill your first soul into glass, and label the vessel honestly.
Let a physician pronounce you dead, and correct the record yourself the next morning.
Sleep one night in your own prepared grave, and rise before you are missed.

nodes.name: Ossuary Captain
nodes.role: Elite-minion commander — durable frontline core
nodes.lore: Ossuary Captains reject the shambling horde as sloppy work. They raise soldiers who remember soldiering — veterans exhumed with their drill intact — and train them in silent yards until a company of bone stands parade-straight. Border lords hire them and pretend not to. A Captain's dozen outfights a warm hundred, and never breaks.
nodes.playstyle: Field a small elite of drilled undead veterans; hold formations, call disciplined maneuvers, and win by refusing to lose a single piece.

abilities.name: Veteran's Memory
abilities.desc: Corpses of trained soldiers rise with one skill from life intact — shieldwork, archery, or siegecraft.

abilities.name: Bone Phalanx
abilities.desc: Your minions lock into a shield line, sharing damage between them and blocking passage entirely.

abilities.name: Sergeant's Knell
abilities.desc: Promote one undead to sergeant; nearby minions gain its discipline and strike in unison.

abilities.name: Silent Yard
abilities.desc: Drill your company between battles; each drilled minion enters the next fight with hardened bone and faster hands.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and raise a soldier of the old wars with every drill-command still in his marrow.
Drill your company a full winter in a yard where no living voice is permitted.
Defeat a living company in open field, then offer its fallen a place in your ranks.
Recover a banner the living abandoned, and let your dead carry it home.

nodes.name: Gravetide Caller
nodes.role: Swarm summoner — overwhelming expendable numbers
nodes.lore: Gravetide Callers follow wars the way gulls follow ploughs. They work the mass graves, the plague pits, the drowned levies — raising the cheap and countless dead in waves that need no drill, only direction. Fastidious colleagues call the work crude. The Callers reply that no wall was ever crude enough to stop the tide.
nodes.playstyle: Flood the field with short-lived shamblers, spend them as ammunition and cover, and replace losses from whatever the enemy was foolish enough to kill.

abilities.name: Carrion Surge
abilities.desc: Every corpse within forty paces rises at once as a shambler that lasts one minute.

abilities.name: Feed the Tide
abilities.desc: Enemies slain by your swarm rise immediately and join it.

abilities.name: Chaff of Bone
abilities.desc: Sacrifice nearby shamblers; each one absorbs a blow meant for you.

abilities.name: Grave Bloom
abilities.desc: Sow a patch of ground; anything that dies upon it stands back up under your call.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and raise a hundred dead in a single hour from a field you did not seed.
Walk the plague-cart circuit of three towns and leave no pit unworked.
Break a walled camp using no weapon but the bodies its defenders made for you.
Stand in the tide's center while it moves, and be the only stillness.

nodes.name: Vesselwright
nodes.role: Immortality engineer — self-sustaining attrition caster
nodes.lore: Vesselwrights turn the scholar's pallor into craft. They fire phylactery-porcelain from bone ash, cut soul-anchors into gemstone, and apportion fragments of themselves into objects that cannot bleed. Each vessel is a masterwork and a hostage. Colleagues judge a Vesselwright's skill by how calmly they discuss their own murder.
nodes.playstyle: Fight like someone with nothing at stake: soak lethal blows into stored vessels, spend fragments of self for power, and rebuild between engagements.

abilities.name: First Vessel
abilities.desc: On death, your soul retreats to a hidden phylactery and rebuilds your body over three days.

abilities.name: Apportioned Self
abilities.desc: Store a fifth of your soul in a carried vessel; soul-targeting magic finds only the remainder.

abilities.name: Kiln of Hours
abilities.desc: Transfer a wound's true cost to a prepared vessel, which cracks so you do not.

abilities.name: Hairline Death
abilities.desc: Once per battle, a killing blow leaves you at the edge of life and your newest vessel fractured.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and fire your first phylactery from bone-ash porcelain, glazed with a year of your own life.
Die once, deliberately, under controlled conditions, and take notes throughout.
Recover a colleague's shattered vessel and return what leaked out, asking nothing.
Hide your first vessel so well that you must trust it rather than check on it.

nodes.name: Soulchandler
nodes.role: Resource caster — soul economy and control
nodes.lore: Soulchandlers render the departing into light. Their lanterns hold souls in cold custody — some as fuel, some as witnesses, some as debts awaiting terms. Magistrates buy their testimony-candles; assassins buy their silence-wicks; the trade regulates itself through professional dread. A good chandler never lies about what a lantern holds.
nodes.playstyle: Fight over an economy of souls: bottle what dies, spend stored light for bursts of power, and threaten the one currency every enemy carries.

abilities.name: Render the Passing
abilities.desc: Bottle any soul that dies within thirty paces; each stored soul fuels one empowered casting.

abilities.name: Witness Light
abilities.desc: Burn a bottled soul as a lantern that replays its final hour for all to see.

abilities.name: Wick of Names
abilities.desc: Spend three stored souls at once to double a spell's effect and silence its casting.

abilities.name: Cold Custody
abilities.desc: Briefly pull a living enemy's soul into your lantern; the body stands vacant and defenseless.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and bottle a soul mid-battle without spilling a single hour of it.
Keep a murdered witness lit until the trial ends, and let the verdict be theirs.
Refuse a fortune for a soul you promised to release, and release it.
Craft a lantern that burns for a year on one honest confession.

nodes.name: Gravemarshal
nodes.role: Legion commander — battlefield-scale undead warfare
nodes.lore: Gravemarshals command the standing legions of the dead — thousands strong, provisioned on nothing, deserting never. Perhaps six hold the rank in any age. Kingdoms map their borders around a Gravemarshal's silence, and generals study their battles with the lights on. Each carries a muster-roll of every soldier raised, owed, and honorably released.
nodes.playstyle: Direct whole formations rather than minions: raise fallen enemies mid-battle, promote undead officers on the field, and grind sieges without supply lines.

abilities.name: Standard of the Risen
abilities.desc: Plant a bone standard; enemies who die within its shadow rise mid-battle, already sworn to your banner.

abilities.name: Field Promotion
abilities.desc: Raise a slain enemy officer as a bound commander whose former troops must resist the urge to flee.

abilities.name: Unbroken Line
abilities.desc: Your legions cannot rout, feel no attrition at night, and hold ground while a single bone remains.

abilities.name: Terms of Surrender
abilities.desc: Offer a besieged garrison honest terms; those who refuse join your muster-roll in advance.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and win a declared siege commanding no living soldier but yourself.
Take the surrender of a dead general on the field where he first fell.
Release a thousand veterans from your service in a single ceremony, and have them thank you.
Have a kingdom cede territory at the rumor of your march, before a single grave is opened.

nodes.name: Charnel Shepherd
nodes.role: Attrition engine — self-replenishing swarm control
nodes.lore: Charnel Shepherds tend the tide as a living thing — pasturing it on old battlefields, culling it, breeding its strongest strains of walking dead. The order is small and pastoral in its horrible way; shepherds trade shamblers at grave-markets and speak of good years. Villages empty at the sound of their bells, unhurriedly.
nodes.playstyle: Sustain a swarm that feeds itself: seed killing grounds, cull the weak for power, and outlast anything that cannot destroy bodies faster than you make them.

abilities.name: Shepherd's Bell
abilities.desc: Ring once; every unbound corpse within earshot rises and falls in behind you.

abilities.name: Cull and Keep
abilities.desc: Destroy your weakest shamblers to imbue the strongest, breeding a hardier strain each battle.

abilities.name: Rot Pasture
abilities.desc: Blight the ground; whatever dies upon it rises at once and at full strength.

abilities.name: Endless Fold
abilities.desc: Your swarm has no fixed size; each dawn it regrows to yesterday's count from local graves.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and keep one swarm whole across three campaigns without returning to a city for bodies.
Breed a strain of shambler that other necromancers travel to buy, and set your own price.
Ring your bell in a fallen kingdom's capital and walk out with its garrison.
Lose the entire fold to holy fire, and rebuild it by the next full moon.

nodes.name: Lich Ascendant
nodes.role: Deathless duelist — attrition you cannot win
nodes.lore: A Lich Ascendant has died the first true death and filed the event away as procedure. The heartbeat is ceremonial now, maintained for company. They are feared less for power than for jurisdiction: killing one is a clerical error, promptly corrected. Most spend the rank in study, since time has stopped charging them for it.
nodes.playstyle: Treat every fight as a negotiation you cannot lose: absorb deaths as cooldowns, ignore mortal pressure entirely, and spend centuries-deep spellcraft with total patience.

abilities.name: Filed Under Dead
abilities.desc: Dying is a ninety-second interruption; you reassemble at your anchor with full knowledge of your killer.

abilities.name: Cold Authority
abilities.desc: Lesser undead obey you without binding, recognizing something further along the road than themselves.

abilities.name: Anchor Chain
abilities.desc: Your soul is tethered across many vessels; banishment, possession, and severing simply fail.

abilities.name: A Century's Patience
abilities.desc: Channel a spell over minutes rather than seconds, its power scaling far beyond mortal limits.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and die your first true death with the ritual complete and your notes legible.
Return in time to attend your own funeral, and leave before you are recognized.
Destroy the record of your birth in every archive that holds it, replacing nothing.
Outstudy a mortal lifetime: read every book you were dying too fast to finish.

nodes.name: Usurer of Souls
nodes.role: Soul broker — execution, denial, and leverage
nodes.lore: Usurers of Souls hold the dead in escrow and the living in terms. Their vaults lend soul-light against collateral no bank can seize back, and their foreclosures are attended by clergy hoping to learn something. The order is tiny, solvent, and untouched — everyone powerful enough to rob one owes one.
nodes.playstyle: Leverage the battlefield like a balance sheet: mark debts on enemies, hold allies' souls in safekeeping, and foreclose on anyone who cannot pay.

abilities.name: Terms of Collection
abilities.desc: Mark an enemy; if they fall within the hour, their soul routes to your vault, bypassing any afterlife.

abilities.name: Compound Interest
abilities.desc: Each strike against a marked debtor drains a little more than the last, without ceiling.

abilities.name: Foreclosure
abilities.desc: Sever the soul of a marked enemy below one-quarter health; no resurrection honors the contract they broke.

abilities.name: Escrow
abilities.desc: Hold a willing ally's soul in your vault; their body cannot die while the deposit stands.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and hold one hundred souls in escrow with every contract witnessed and none disputed.
Foreclose on a tyrant in open court, and read the terms aloud first.
Forgive one debt entirely, and record why in a ledger no one will read.
Survive an audit by the courts of the dead, and be found exact.

nodes.name: Wightsmith
nodes.role: Elite-minion duelist — one masterwork revenant
nodes.lore: Wightsmiths call the Gravemarshal's legions a thousand apologies for one failure of craft. The order raises a single dead worth the work — a duelist, a headsman, a drowned queen's champion — and restores everything the grave took: name, memory, art. A Wightsmith keeps one. Garrisons have resigned rather than learn which one.
nodes.playstyle: Fight as a pair: your masterwork duels while you maintain it, sharpening its art mid-battle, mending what it cannot dodge, and finishing what it staggers.

abilities.name: Masterwork Raising
abilities.desc: Raise one named revenant with its living skill, memory, and speech intact; only one masterwork may exist at a time.

abilities.name: Whetstone Litany
abilities.desc: Chant over your revenant; for ten seconds its strikes cannot be parried by any technique its opponent learned from the living.

abilities.name: Signature Stroke
abilities.desc: Your revenant repeats the blow it was famous for in life; against a named opponent, it cannot miss.

abilities.name: Smith's Prerogative
abilities.desc: Recall your masterwork to your side instantly, or rebuild it overnight from any surviving fragment.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and exhume a duelist whose name still empties taverns, restoring every art the grave took from her.
Refuse a Gravemarshal's commission in writing, and survive the correspondence.
Match your one against another order's hundred, and be home by supper.
Learn your revenant's one regret from its own mouth, and mend it.

nodes.name: Tribune of the Pit
nodes.role: Swarm avenger — grievance-charged mass assault
nodes.lore: Tribunes of the Pit hold that the Shepherds keep livestock that ought to be plaintiffs. They work the same mass graves — plague pits, drowned levies, paupers' trenches — but raise them as a constituency: the unmourned, standing in suit against whoever spent them. A Tribune's tide does not graze. It presents demands.
nodes.playstyle: Raise the wronged in wrathful crowds, name the party responsible, and let every shambler strike hardest at whoever owes its grave an answer.

abilities.name: Presentment
abilities.desc: Name the party responsible for a grave; everything you raise from it strikes that enemy twice as hard.

abilities.name: Quorum of the Nameless
abilities.desc: Raise a mass grave as one crowd; the more who died wronged, the stronger each rises.

abilities.name: Redress in Kind
abilities.desc: Your swarm learns whatever harms it and returns it in kind, wound for remembered wound.

abilities.name: Dismissal
abilities.desc: Dismiss the crowd to rest; any dismissed unavenged rise without cost next time, and angrier.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and raise an entire plague pit in one night, learning what each of its dead was owed.
March the drowned levies of a forgotten war to the palace that spent them, and wait, saying nothing, until the palace asks.
Win one wrongful death a hearing in a living court, with the deceased attending as evidence.
Refuse the grave-markets outright, and let the Shepherds price the precedent.

nodes.name: Mortifex
nodes.role: Burst caster — banked-death sacrifice economy
nodes.lore: Where the Lich Ascendant files death away, the Mortifex takes it into the workshop. The order holds that a death refused is a death wasted: each member builds their own, choosing hour and instrument, compounding it in a vessel until their one mortality is the heaviest object they own. Liches call the work tragic. The order calls liches unfinished.
nodes.playstyle: Spend your own death in installments: self-wounding rites buy disproportionate power, and the vessel holding your ending grows heavier and more dangerous every year.

abilities.name: The Prepared End
abilities.desc: Your death lives in a vessel you built; nothing kills you by surprise, only by appointment.

abilities.name: Installments
abilities.desc: Pour one measure of your stored death into a spell; it lands with the weight of a dying man's last act.

abilities.name: The Growing Weight
abilities.desc: Every wound you survive is added to the vessel; your death grows heavier, and so does everything you spend it on.

abilities.name: Rehearsal
abilities.desc: Die briefly and on purpose; for ten seconds you act from beyond consequence, then return.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and begin your death: choose its hour, its instrument, and its witness, then build the vessel to hold it until then.
Decline a Lich Ascendant's tutelage politely, and note the flinch when you explain why.
Survive what should have killed you nine times, and bank all nine.
Weigh your vessel each solstice, and be glad it is heavier.

nodes.name: Crowner
nodes.role: Control caster — evidence, replayed deaths, denial
nodes.lore: Crowners hold the one inquest that never adjourns. Where the Usurer lends soul-light at terms, a Crowner's lanterns are a court of record: every soul catalogued, every testimony preserved, nothing sold at any price. Magistrates cite them; tyrants burn archives and discover the archive was elsewhere. The order's oath is one line: the dead are evidence, not currency.
nodes.playstyle: Win through testimony: replay deaths as weapons, confront the living with what the dead witnessed, and spend preserved evidence for exacting, judicial power.

abilities.name: Court of Record
abilities.desc: Souls you bottle become depositions; their testimony cannot be altered, silenced, or purchased, even from you.

abilities.name: Confrontation
abilities.desc: Show an enemy one death they caused, replayed in full; they fight the memory while you fight them.

abilities.name: Subpoena
abilities.desc: Summon any relevant soul to testify for one minute; refusal is contempt, and contempt hurts.

abilities.name: Sealed Exhibit
abilities.desc: Store a witnessed moment unopened; broken in battle, it inflicts everything the moment contained.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and catalogue a massacre within a day, every soul deposed and not one bought.
Decline the Usurer's standing offer for your archive, annually, in writing.
Convict a man three courts acquitted, because the dead knew otherwise.
Burn nothing, sell nothing, lose nothing, through ten consecutive years of war.

nodes.name: Sovereign of the Risen
nodes.role: Mythic commander — nation-scale deathless armies
nodes.lore: Histories record perhaps three Sovereigns of the Risen, and dispute all of them. Each commanded every willing dead soldier of an era — armies that grew by exactly what they defeated. Nations now bury their dead in lead and salt, a custom whose origin children are not taught. The last Sovereign was never defeated, only asked, politely, to stop.
nodes.playstyle: Wage war at the scale of maps: every battle won enlarges the host, every enemy casualty is a recruitment, and retreat merely relocates the muster.

abilities.name: Grave Levy
abilities.desc: Call the willing dead of an entire province; they rise, form ranks, and await orders.

abilities.name: The Standing Muster
abilities.desc: All who fall in any battle you command rise at its end, offered a place rather than compelled.

abilities.name: One Order, Ten Thousand Hands
abilities.desc: Issue a single command that every soldier in your host executes simultaneously and without relay.

abilities.name: Peace of the Sovereign
abilities.desc: Declare a field at rest; no dead may be raised there by any hand, including yours.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and break a crusade raised by seven kingdoms for the sole purpose of ending you.
Muster the dead of an entire forgotten war, and learn each name on the roll.
Refuse a crown offered by the living, and accept the one offered by the dead.
March your host past a city gate and leave it untouched, so the histories must call you something other than monster.

nodes.name: The Unnumbered
nodes.role: Mythic swarm — inexhaustible tide of dead
nodes.lore: Chroniclers stopped estimating the host of the Unnumbered after three censuses returned different figures and one returned no surveyors at all. Whether the title names a necromancer or the tide itself is a scholarly quarrel; the tide does not clarify. It has never been defeated, only outlasted, and never for long.
nodes.playstyle: Play as a weather system: the swarm arrives before you, regrows behind you, and victory means the enemy runs out of world before you run out of dead.

abilities.name: No Count Holds
abilities.desc: Your host cannot be reduced below half; destroyed shamblers reappear at the swarm's edge each minute.

abilities.name: The Graves Answer
abilities.desc: Every burial ground within a day's ride opens at your word, regardless of ward or consecration.

abilities.name: Undertow
abilities.desc: The swarm drags one enemy under; they emerge a minute later on your side of the line.

abilities.name: Season of the Tide
abilities.desc: For a day and a night, everything that dies in the region rises without being called.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and lift a siege by raising the besiegers' own casualties inside their camp each night.
Let three censuses of your host fail, and return one surveyor to tell of it.
Erase your name so thoroughly that scholars argue whether you exist, and attend the debate.
Become the reason a language has a word for the sound graves make when they open.

nodes.name: Archlich
nodes.role: Mythic immortal — inevitability made arcane
nodes.lore: Histories disagree on which century produced the Archlich, and it declines to correct them. It has outlived its enemies, its allies, its language, and at least one calendar. Kingdoms no longer plot its destruction; they plot around its patience. Scholars note that everything it ever wanted has simply, eventually, happened.
nodes.playstyle: Win by being inevitable: no clock, no fear, no attrition applies to you, and every exchange trades the enemy's finite life against your surplus.

abilities.name: Rescind
abilities.desc: Undo your own death the instant it occurs, anywhere, without travel to an anchor.

abilities.name: The Optional Grave
abilities.desc: Grant or revoke death itself for one creature in your presence, once a season.

abilities.name: Deep Time
abilities.desc: Your enchantments and curses do not expire; centuries-old workings answer when you call them due.

abilities.name: Terminal Lesson
abilities.desc: Show one enemy their complete death in advance; they fight the rest of the battle already grieving.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and let a kingdom execute you publicly, then resume your correspondence the same week.
Outlive every person who ever heard your living name, and keep the name anyway.
Complete the work: make your death not defeated, but optional, a formality you may yet schedule.
Be cited by historians in three eras, each certain you belonged to another.

nodes.name: The Wakelight
nodes.role: Mythic arbiter — final passage of souls
nodes.lore: When every other light fails — gods distracted, ferries sunk, heavens shut — the dead walk toward the Wakelight. Histories place it at the end of every great war, unaffiliated, collecting. Whether it guides souls onward or simply keeps them is a theological crisis three churches have declined to investigate closely.
nodes.playstyle: Control where death leads: reroute every dying soul through your flame, extinguish the irredeemable permanently, and return the kept as the rarest mercy.

abilities.name: All Roads End Here
abilities.desc: Every soul that dies in the region passes through your lantern first, and some are asked to stay.

abilities.name: Snuff
abilities.desc: Extinguish one soul utterly; no god, spell, or clause can retrieve it.

abilities.name: The Kept Flame
abilities.desc: Return a stored soul to its body whole — a true resurrection, granted rarely and priced honestly.

abilities.name: Hour of Moths
abilities.desc: Release a stormcloud of kept souls that swarm your enemies, each whispering its own death.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and stand at the end of a war so vast the heavens close their doors against the crowd.
Take custody of every soul the gods misplaced, and lose not one.
Turn away a god who comes to claim a soul in your keeping, and be obeyed.
Become the light the dying see, in every land, in every language.

nodes.name: The Reforged
nodes.role: Mythic duelist — flawless self-made masterwork
nodes.lore: The last tradition of the Wightsmiths is the quiet one: dying, the greatest are raised by their own prepared working, remade as the masterpiece no commission ever deserved. Histories dispute whether a Reforged is maker or made; the Reforged decline to see the difference. Connoisseurs identify perhaps four across the ages, and argue attribution bitterly.
nodes.playstyle: Play as the masterwork itself: a remade body without flaw, every art of every revenant you ever raised, and a maker's patience for repairs.

abilities.name: The Smith's Last Work
abilities.desc: Your body is craft, not flesh: critical strikes find no seam, fear finds no owner, and wounds are repairs, not injuries.

abilities.name: Repertoire of the Raised
abilities.desc: Perform any combat art of any revenant you ever raised, at the mastery its owner died holding.

abilities.name: Recast
abilities.desc: When destroyed, your remains reforge you within a day, and each casting removes one flaw of the original.

abilities.name: Maker's Mark
abilities.desc: Undead that strike you recognize the hand that perfected their kind, and kneel instead.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and complete the working that will raise you, in instructions no apprentice could mistake.
Die of nothing but readiness, and rise as your own final commission.
Pass among the living for a year, and be complimented on your health.
Keep one flaw on purpose, so the work stays yours.

nodes.name: The Gravamen
nodes.role: Mythic host — province-scale risen grievance
nodes.lore: In law, the gravamen is the weight of a grievance — the part no court may dismiss. Histories record one per catastrophe and dispute each: a figure who stood up out of an age's mass graves carrying everything the unmourned were owed. Three dynasties are known to have ended by settlement. The terms remain sealed.
nodes.playstyle: Fight as a walking indictment: your host grows from every injustice on the field, and named enemies kneel beneath the weight of what stands against them.

abilities.name: Burden of Proof
abilities.desc: Enemies you indict slow, then buckle, beneath the counted burden of everyone they sent unmourned into the ground.

abilities.name: The Pits Empty
abilities.desc: Every mass grave in the province opens; the wronged rise and walk to you, gathering as they come.

abilities.name: Settlement
abilities.desc: Offer terms once per battle; those who accept leave unmarked, and those who refuse are added to the complaint.

abilities.name: No Dismissal
abilities.desc: Your host cannot be turned, banished, or laid to rest by any authority until the grievance is answered.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and stand up out of a century's mass grave carrying its full and itemized complaint.
End a dynasty by settlement, and seal the terms so well that historians blame the weather.
Bury the settled dead a second time, properly, with every name spoken once aloud.
Become the reason powerful men fund cemeteries.

nodes.name: The Composed
nodes.role: Mythic bulwark — unkillable calm, apocalyptic reserve
nodes.lore: A Mortifex who finishes the work is called Composed: death complete, carried, unspent. Histories record them by absence — battles that ended because one calm figure arrived and nothing happened. What a finished death could purchase has been calculated three times, by three colleges, each of which then closed its necromancy department. The Composed carry it anyway, and wait.
nodes.playstyle: Fight with absolute composure: immune to fear, haste, and despair, spending single drops of a finished death that could, poured out, end an age.

abilities.name: Perfect Composure
abilities.desc: Nothing frightens, hurries, or breaks you; effects that target your mortality find it elsewhere, finished and put away.

abilities.name: A Drop of the End
abilities.desc: Spend the smallest measure of your death; one enemy experiences their entire ending in a heartbeat, and drops.

abilities.name: The Weight Made Plain
abilities.desc: Set the vessel down where all can perceive it; armies discover they would rather not, and withdraw in good order.

abilities.name: Still Unspent
abilities.desc: While your death remains whole you cannot be slain; whatever should kill you is taken by the vessel instead.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and finish your death: the last hour poured, the vessel sealed, the work complete.
Arrive at a war so calmly that both sides assume you are the terms, and be right.
Let three colleges calculate what your death could buy, and outlive their necromancy departments.
Carry the heaviest object in the world through a crowded market, and be jostled.

nodes.name: The Testament
nodes.role: Mythic seer — perfect counterplay through testimony
nodes.lore: Somewhere the true history is kept, in the dead's own light, and its keeper is called the Testament. Chronicles dispute every mythic of the age; the disputes are settled, when settled at all, by quiet correspondence with the archive. Gods have petitioned to amend their entries. The answer, in every recorded case, was no.
nodes.playstyle: Fight with total knowledge of the dead: every technique ever witnessed by the dying, every deathbed secret, arrayed in evidence against the living.

abilities.name: The Whole Record
abilities.desc: Know anything any dying person ever knew; the dead witnessed nearly everything, and they deposed to you.

abilities.name: Prior Testimony
abilities.desc: Your enemy's every tactic was watched by someone who died of it; you counter techniques before their first use.

abilities.name: Amendment Denied
abilities.desc: Once a day, declare an event unalterable; no god, spell, or regret may revise what the dead witnessed.

abilities.name: Reading of the Will
abilities.desc: Read an enemy the testament they have not yet made; the living fight poorly while hearing themselves inherited.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and complete the deposition of an age: every death recorded, every record true.
Refuse a god's petition to amend its entry, citing precedent.
Settle a war between three kingdoms' histories with one lantern, lit once, for an hour.
Be cited as the source no chronicle names, in every chronicle that matters.

nodes.name: The Reveille
nodes.role: Apotheosis — every dead soldier answers once
nodes.lore: Soldiers' burial rites now end the same way in every land: rest until the horn. Few liturgies say whose. The Reveille is what remained when the last Sovereign of the Risen dissolved into the promise made to every buried soldier — one morning, one call, one final formation. Armistices hold because the alternative is attendance.
nodes.playstyle: Wield the promised morning: call any dead soldier of any age to one last formation, and end wars by demonstrating what would answer the horn.

abilities.name: One Morning Owed
abilities.desc: Call any dead soldier in history to your line for one hour; each may be called exactly once, ever.

abilities.name: The Horn at Last
abilities.desc: Sound reveille over a battlefield; every dead of every era beneath it stands to, in ranks, awaiting review.

abilities.name: Stand Easy
abilities.desc: Dismiss any undead host, however bound, to genuine rest; its binder's authority is outranked.

abilities.name: The Asking
abilities.desc: Belligerents who hear your horn must state their war's purpose aloud; wars that cannot are over.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and inherit the promise itself: every buried soldier's right to one more morning, held in your keeping.
Sound the horn once, over one field, and let the ranks that answer be the treaty.
Refuse to sound it for a century, and let the silence keep more peace than any call could.
Be written into burial rites in languages you never learned: rest until the horn.

nodes.name: The Second Sea
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the dead as living geography
nodes.lore: The cartographers conceded in the end: the world has acquired a second sea. It has tides, which follow no moon; a shore, which moves; and sailors, in a sense. Where the Unnumbered was disputed, the Second Sea is charted — a standing body of the dead, weather to some coasts, doctrine to others. Landlocked nations now maintain sea-walls.
nodes.playstyle: Play as geography: your host is a region of the map, arriving as tide and climate rather than army, and receding only by choice.

abilities.name: Making Tide
abilities.desc: Your sea advances across a province; everything it covers joins it, and everything it uncovers is clean bone.

abilities.name: The Moving Shore
abilities.desc: Your coastline is wherever you decide; inland is a courtesy the dead extend, and may revoke.

abilities.name: Deep Census
abilities.desc: Take a sounding anywhere on earth: learn how many dead lie beneath, and how lightly they sleep.

abilities.name: Wrackline
abilities.desc: Whatever your tide leaves behind rises sworn to you; every retreat seeds a garrison along the tideline.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and be entered on the admiralty charts as a body of water, with your own soundings and seasons.
Flood a continent's interior once, gently, so the maps stop arguing.
Grant one pilgrim fleet safe passage across yourself, and ignore the religion this founds.
Recede for a generation, and let the world call it low tide.

nodes.name: The Posthumous
nodes.role: Apotheosis — history inside one afterlife
nodes.lore: There is a scholarly question, seldom asked twice in the same room, about when the Archlich died — because every candidate date implies the same conclusion: that history has been proceeding inside somebody's afterlife for centuries. The Posthumous is that continuation, given a name. The age does not merely have an owner. The age is one.
nodes.playstyle: Win from beyond the end: nothing that happens can precede you, your workings mature across centuries, and every clock in the fight is yours by seniority.

abilities.name: Already Ended
abilities.desc: You cannot be ended, expired, or concluded; that happened long ago, and effects with durations treat you as their exception.

abilities.name: Scheduled Inevitability
abilities.desc: Declare an outcome and a date up to a century out; the world begins arranging it immediately.

abilities.name: The Age Answers
abilities.desc: Within the era that bears your name, every working older than a decade answers to you.

abilities.name: Surplus of Hours
abilities.desc: Spend hoarded years to act many times in a single moment; you have more time than the battle does.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and let historians finally date your death, then let them notice what that makes everything since.
Watch every plan you ever made mature in the same decade, and be mildly pleased.
Become the fixed point calendars argue from, and decline to confirm which event you were.
Let permanence be defined, in three languages, by reference to you.

nodes.name: The Last Rite
nodes.role: Apotheosis — universal custody of the dying
nodes.lore: Every funeral in every land now works, whatever the priest believes, because every candle lit for the dead is an annex of one flame. The Last Rite is what the Wakelight became when the churches surrendered the question: not a light the dying see, but the right of the dying to see one — enforced, universally, by something that collects.
nodes.playstyle: Officiate mortality itself: every death in reach concludes on your terms, souls pass into your keeping by rite, and your rare mercies become liturgy.

abilities.name: Universal Office
abilities.desc: Every death in your presence is conducted properly; no soul is lost, stolen, or harvested by any hand but yours.

abilities.name: The Owed Candle
abilities.desc: Claim retroactively any soul ever denied its rite, voiding whatever was built upon the theft.

abilities.name: Liturgy of Return
abilities.desc: Return one kept soul to life so completely that no church can call it heresy, and several call it proof.

abilities.name: Final Benediction
abilities.desc: Pronounce a death complete; nothing may raise, bottle, bargain with, or appeal what you have blessed shut.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and be adopted by every liturgy at once, under different names, without a single council convening.
Attend, in the same hour, every deathbed on earth, and be seen carrying nothing away.
Hold the rite for a dying god, and be thanked in its will.
Become the entitlement itself: that no one, anywhere, dies unlit.

nodes.name: The Provenance
nodes.role: Apotheosis — authorship over all undeath
nodes.lore: Every raised thing carries, somewhere in the marrow, the mark of one hand. Scholars found it the way scholars find most horrors: cataloguing. The Provenance is the attribution behind all necromancy — the maker every working quietly cites, the workshop every apprentice unknowingly copies. The office outlives its holders, or the holders outlive the distinction; the catalogues stopped asking.
nodes.playstyle: Command by authorship: everything raised by anyone is your uncredited work, and your mark, once invoked, outranks any binding on any dead thing.

abilities.name: First Attribution
abilities.desc: Any undead you touch becomes yours; whatever hand raised it, yours signed first.

abilities.name: Withdraw the Work
abilities.desc: Unmake any undead in your presence by removing your mark; it ends as unfinished things end, quietly.

abilities.name: Catalogue of Hands
abilities.desc: Know every undead walking the world, who raised it, and how poorly.

abilities.name: Posthumous Improvement
abilities.desc: Undead that survive your presence leave it better made — faster, straighter, and aware of their maker.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and find your mark in a corpse raised a thousand leagues away, by hands you never taught.
Let three academies attribute the same masterwork to three different centuries, and sign nothing.
Withdraw your mark once, in mercy, and watch an empire's necromancy fail overnight.
Outlive attribution: be not the greatest of makers, but the reason making works.

nodes.name: The Potter's Field
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the grave's equality enforced
nodes.lore: Every grave, it turns out, connects. The Potter's Field is the office into which the Gravamen's settlements finally resolved: one estate of the dead, held in common, of which every pit, tomb, and gilded mausoleum is merely a corner. Kings pay for marble and receive, like everyone, a share. Paupers' fields are kept like cathedrals now.
nodes.playstyle: Impose the grave's equality on the living: strip rank, regalia, and privilege down to what a body is, and stand where all standing fails.

abilities.name: All Graves One Depth
abilities.desc: Strip an enemy of every rank-borne blessing, enchanted regalia, and inherited protection; what remains fights you as it was born.

abilities.name: Held in Common
abilities.desc: In your presence no creature may be stronger, faster, or luckier than the least of its enemies.

abilities.name: Vertigo of Crowns
abilities.desc: Kings, generals, and archpriests who behold you fight at the strength of the commonest soldier they ever spent.

abilities.name: One Estate
abilities.desc: Once a season, declare a region common ground: for a day, every death there is counted, mourned, and equal.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and attend, unpetitioned, the pauper's funeral of a king, and be the reason it is one.
Unmake the doctrine of noble bones in every church that taught it, without burning anything.
Stand in the one place all processions end, and be why they arrive equal.
Become the vertigo beneath thrones: the certainty, felt in the knees, that the grave holds no precedence.

nodes.name: The Mortmain
nodes.role: Apotheosis — death held in perpetual trust
nodes.lore: Law calls it mortmain when the dead hand holds property forever. This office holds one property: death itself, in perpetual trust — never spent, never sold, never surrendered to god, crown, or lich. Because the dead hand holds it, no one else may. Every mortal who dies freely, uncontracted and unowned, is exercising the guarantee.
nodes.playstyle: Administer death as an estate in trust: grant it, defer it, and defend its title against every god, contract, and immortality that files a claim.

abilities.name: Perpetual Trust
abilities.desc: Death cannot be stolen, monopolized, or abolished in your presence; every clause that says otherwise is void.

abilities.name: The Dead Hand
abilities.desc: Hold a creature's death in trust; it cannot die, nor be made to die, until you release the title.

abilities.name: Quiet Enjoyment
abilities.desc: Grant a dying soul quiet enjoyment of its own end; nothing may interrupt, harvest, or repurpose that death.

abilities.name: Title Review
abilities.desc: Examine any immortality in your presence and, once a season, revoke it.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and take death itself into trust, witnessed by the courts of the dead, with no god objecting twice.
Refuse an empire's offer for a monopoly on dying, and record the refusal where empires check.
Let a god sue for possession of death, and win on the merits.
Hold the estate until dying freely is assumed, like weather, and your office is mistaken for nature.

nodes.name: The Verdict
nodes.role: Apotheosis — standing judgment of the dead
nodes.lore: An archive is a promise that someone will finally read it aloud. The Verdict is the reading. Past the Testament's keeping lies the office where evidence becomes finding: the standing judgment of the dead upon the living, revised nightly. The world behaves as though watched, because it is. Perjury against the dead has quietly ceased.
nodes.playstyle: Pronounce rather than fight: findings of fact strike like weather, the guilty arrive already sentenced, and your word carries the assembled certainty of the dead.

abilities.name: Finding of Fact
abilities.desc: Pronounce what an enemy did; the pronouncement strikes with force proportional to how much they hoped it was hidden.

abilities.name: Prejudged
abilities.desc: The guilty enter your presence already sentenced: weakened, marked, and aware of exactly why.

abilities.name: The Dead Concur
abilities.desc: Every soul in the region lends weight to one ruling; the sentence executes itself through their assembled testimony.

abilities.name: Stay of Execution
abilities.desc: Suspend any death, sentence, or curse indefinitely while evidence is heard; some hearings outlast dynasties.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and deliver the dead's verdict on a living age, and watch its guilty sentence themselves rather than be read.
Judge a god's oldest lie against the testimony of everyone who died believing it.
Acquit someone history hates, and make the acquittal hold in every archive at once.
Become the hush after perjury: the certainty, everywhere, that the dead are listening and will be believed.

families.name: Artificer
families.tagline: Every miracle is a prototype; every prototype has a fuse.
families.description: Artificers treat magic as a material and disaster as data. Their miracles are drafted at a bench, prototyped in the field, and revised in blood, each failure logged in journals the guilds pretend not to copy. They build companions that outthink their plating and ordnance that keeps its appointments. Everything an artificer makes eventually explodes; the great ones decide precisely when.

nodes.name: Artificer
nodes.role: Hybrid utility caster — gadgets and preparation
nodes.lore: Every artificer begins as someone who asked why and was told to stop. They are journeymen of a guild that half distrusts them, carrying tool-rolls where knights carry swords and treating spellcraft as an engineering discipline with unusually strict tolerances. Villages hire them to fix mills; wars hire them to fix outcomes.
nodes.playstyle: Versatile toolbox play: deploy gadgets, exploit terrain, and trade raw power for preparation. Weak when caught without a plan, dangerous when given an evening to draft one.

abilities.name: Jury-Rig
abilities.desc: Assemble a one-use device from scavenged parts; roll on your prototype table for its property, which is never quite nothing.

abilities.name: Copper Coil
abilities.desc: Hurl a charged coil that arcs lightning between the two nearest enemies, dealing shock damage to both.

abilities.name: Blueprint Ledger
abilities.desc: Once per rest, recall a spent gadget's schematic and rebuild it instantly at half cost.

abilities.name: Controlled Misfire
abilities.desc: When a device fails, choose the direction of the failure; enemies in the cone inherit the consequences.

progressionSteps: Apprentice yourself to a guildless tinker who teaches that magic is a material with tolerances, and every tolerance can be exceeded once.
Build a device from scavenged parts and watch it fail. Record why in the journal you will keep until you die.
Present a working prototype to a guild examiner who expected a corpse, and collect your stamp without smiling.
Survive your first misfire. Leave the scar uncovered, so you remember what a misplaced decimal costs.

nodes.name: Golemwright
nodes.role: Summoner — construct companion control
nodes.lore: Golemwrights are the artificers who grew tired of working alone. They animate servitors, teach armor to think, and drag traveling forges through mud to the front lines. Soldiers mock the clanking retinue until it pulls them from under a dead horse; after that, they learn the constructs' names.
nodes.playstyle: Companion-driven midline play: position your servitor, repair between exchanges, and let thinking armor absorb what you cannot dodge. Your action economy is the weapon.

abilities.name: First Assembly
abilities.desc: Animate a clockwork servitor that fights, carries, and mends; it retains one learned behavior permanently between battles.

abilities.name: Thinking Plate
abilities.desc: Your armor studies each attacker, gaining stacking resistance to any damage type it has already survived this combat.

abilities.name: Traveling Forge
abilities.desc: Deploy your workshop as a field station that repairs constructs and reloads devices for allies within its glow.

abilities.name: Overwound Mainspring
abilities.desc: Wind your servitor past tolerance: it acts twice this round, then seizes for one.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10 and animate a servitor from your own schematics, borrowing no one's blueprint and blaming no one's math.
Teach it one word. When it obeys the third time without being watched, give it a name.
Carry your forge across a battlefield and rebuild your construct under arrow-fall, before you see to the wound in your arm.

nodes.name: Volatile Chymist
nodes.role: Ranged blaster — area denial
nodes.lore: Volatile Chymists treat the word unstable as a schedule rather than a warning. They brew ordnance the guild refuses to store indoors, sip their own prototypes to save time, and keep meticulous journals so that whoever inherits the laboratory knows exactly which shelf killed them.
nodes.playstyle: Area control through thrown chemistry: soften formations with corrosive clouds, spike damage with timed charges, and gamble on prototype elixirs when the arithmetic turns against you.

abilities.name: Unstable Batch
abilities.desc: Your bombs each carry a random secondary element; you learn which one as it detonates.

abilities.name: Acrid Veil
abilities.desc: Shatter a flask into lingering vapor that corrodes armor, eating one point of protection each round.

abilities.name: Test Subject One
abilities.desc: Drink an unlabeled prototype: gain a strong random benefit and a documented, inconvenient side effect.

abilities.name: Fused Charge
abilities.desc: Place a charge with a timer of your choosing; its yield grows for every round it waits.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10 and stabilize a compound your instructors called unstabilizable. Then stabilize it a second time, in front of them.
Lose your eyebrows to a batch you were certain of, and write down the ratio anyway.
Demolish a target of the guild's choosing with exactly the yield you quoted — no more, and no apology.

nodes.name: Ironshepherd
nodes.role: Pet commander — sustained two-body pressure
nodes.lore: An Ironshepherd builds one construct and stakes a lifetime on it. The machine is rebuilt after every battle until nothing original remains except the name, which is the part the shepherd actually maintains. Armies pay for the pair together; no offer has ever bought them separately.
nodes.playstyle: Two-body play: the construct holds the line and takes the wounds while you direct, repair, and strike into the openings it creates.

abilities.name: The Naming
abilities.desc: Bond permanently with one construct; it gains a growth track, keeps its memories, and obeys no other voice.

abilities.name: Shepherd's Whistle
abilities.desc: Command your construct to intercept any attack aimed at an ally within its stride.

abilities.name: Graze on Ruin
abilities.desc: Your construct consumes battlefield scrap to repair itself mid-combat, healing more amid greater wreckage.

abilities.name: Iron Bellow
abilities.desc: Your construct roars from its furnace core, forcing nearby enemies to attack it for two rounds.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and rebuild your construct so many times that none of the first metal remains, and it still answers its name.
Refuse the coin offered for it. Refuse the second, larger offer without pausing.
Sleep beside it for a season, until you know every sound it makes when something is wrong.
Let it take a blow meant for you, and repair it before you bind your own wound.

nodes.name: Plateheart
nodes.role: Armored bruiser — frontline attrition
nodes.lore: Platehearts stop distinguishing between armor and anatomy. Plates are bolted to bone, a fabricated mind rides the harness, and the boiler in the chest is not a metaphor. Shield-walls part to let them plug a breach, and comrades learn to stand clear when the steam vents.
nodes.playstyle: Frontline attrition: wade in slowly, let the grafted armor learn each attacker, and win exchanges that would kill anything still made only of meat.

abilities.name: Graft Protocol
abilities.desc: Bolt plating directly to bone: permanent armor that cannot be removed, disarmed, or stolen, only earned.

abilities.name: Second Opinion
abilities.desc: The armor's mind acts when yours cannot, parrying and stepping for you while you are stunned, sleeping, or afraid.

abilities.name: Boiler Vent
abilities.desc: Release chest-furnace steam in a scalding burst, driving melee attackers back and searing the persistent.

abilities.name: Deadbolt Stance
abilities.desc: Lock your frame: you cannot move or be moved, and attacks against adjacent allies redirect to you.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and bolt the first plate to living bone. Do not cry out; the armor is listening.
Lend the harness-mind a portion of your memories, and forgive what it chooses to do with them.
Stand in a breach where flesh alone breaks, and hold until the wall is rebuilt behind you.

nodes.name: Petardier
nodes.role: Siege artillery — long-range timed burst
nodes.lore: Petardiers are siegecraft distilled into a single walking profession. They carry shaped charges up killing grounds, count fuses aloud while arrows fall, and are famous for dying in exactly the manner their title suggests. The ones who live become the reason fortress architects drink.
nodes.playstyle: Patient long-range devastation: mark targets, set staggered timers, and stack yields so that one exact moment does the work of a battery of trebuchets.

abilities.name: Breaching Charge
abilities.desc: A shaped blast that ignores cover, walls, and shields, delivering its full yield to whatever hid behind them.

abilities.name: Ranging Shot
abilities.desc: Your first shell marks the impact zone; every later shell landing there strikes true automatically.

abilities.name: Fuse Discipline
abilities.desc: Set timers exact to the second; each round a charge waits adds another die of yield.

abilities.name: Powder Ledger
abilities.desc: Account for every grain: once per battle, combine all remaining charges into one consolidated detonation.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and bring down a fortress gate with a charge you carried up the killing ground on your own back.
Count a fuse aloud under arrow-fall and be right. Do this until the sappers stop checking your math.
Walk away from a detonation without turning to watch, because doubt is a thing you no longer carry.

nodes.name: Crucible-Drinker
nodes.role: Mutagenic skirmisher — adaptive melee alchemy
nodes.lore: Crucible-Drinkers ran out of test subjects and volunteered. Each draught rewrites something — marrow, hide, the shape of their hands — and each dawn they catalogue what remains of the original. Guilds list them as equipment rather than members, which the Drinkers find flattering.
nodes.playstyle: Adaptive melee alchemy: drink into the fight you are facing, growing claws, plating, or gills as needed, and outlast whatever cannot adapt back.

abilities.name: Mutagenic Draught
abilities.desc: Drink to grow the tool you need — claws, dermal plate, gills — lasting until you drink otherwise.

abilities.name: Purge Sweat
abilities.desc: Expel accumulated toxins through the skin as a caustic mist that sears everything adjacent.

abilities.name: Adaptive Marrow
abilities.desc: Your bones learn: gain resistance to the last damage type that hurt you until something new does.

abilities.name: Tolerance
abilities.desc: You are permanently immune to your own compounds, which is more useful than outsiders assume.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and drink a mutagen distilled from your own blood. Survive what it teaches your body about itself.
Catalogue every change at the mirror each dawn, until the catalogue's author is someone you used to be.
Hear a physician pronounce you an abomination, and correct only the terminology.

nodes.name: Engine-Sire
nodes.role: Multi-summoner — battlefield overwhelm
nodes.lore: An Engine-Sire's constructs build constructs. The craft has passed from hand to iron and from iron to iron again, and the foundry now marches under its own power with its maker walking at its head. Kingdoms describe an approaching Engine-Sire the way coastal towns describe weather.
nodes.playstyle: Overwhelming numbers with inherited discipline: field a family of constructs that share what each has learned, and replace losses faster than the enemy replaces courage.

abilities.name: Progeny Line
abilities.desc: Field multiple constructs drawing on a single pool of learned behaviors; what one masters, all inherit.

abilities.name: Inheritance Protocol
abilities.desc: When a construct falls, its memory core migrates to the nearest kin, carrying its buffs and its grudges.

abilities.name: Marching Foundry
abilities.desc: Your workshop walks to war as a siege platform, assembling replacement frames mid-battle.

abilities.name: Sire's Decree
abilities.desc: Speak one word; every construct you have ever built within earshot obeys it before any other order.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and forge a construct using your first as forge-hand, so the craft passes from your iron to its own.
March your foundry to a war it can end, and end it before the season turns.
Bury a frame that fell for you with full rites, and stand while the others grieve in gear-clatter.

nodes.name: Interred Engine
nodes.role: Unkillable anchor — damage absorption
nodes.lore: The Interred sealed the final seam years ago. Food, air, and sleep are administrative problems the armor has solved; the flesh inside is a rumor even to its owner. Fortresses request an Interred Engine by name when a gate must hold against something that should not exist.
nodes.playstyle: Immovable anchor play: occupy the one span of ground that matters, shrug off attrition that breaks sieges, and grow harder as the damage accumulates.

abilities.name: Final Seam
abilities.desc: You cannot be extracted from your armor, and neither can fear, poison, drowning, or age reach inside.

abilities.name: Ossified Servos
abilities.desc: Below half health your plating fuses harder, and your damage reduction climbs as the damage accumulates.

abilities.name: Grave Pressure
abilities.desc: Your tread slows enemies in a radius, as if the ground itself had grown heavier.

abilities.name: Sepulcher Frame
abilities.desc: Once per day, entomb yourself in place: immune to all damage for a round while allies rally behind you.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and seal the final seam. There is no removing the armor now; there is no you without it.
Endure a winter siege without food, air, or sleep, and decline to say which of you kept the watch.
Let a priest declare you dead, then enter the chapel and pay the funeral fee yourself.

nodes.name: Cataclysmith
nodes.role: Nuker — scheduled massive detonations
nodes.lore: Cataclysmiths hold the doctrine that any structure is a demolition site awaiting scheduling. War-colleges teach their fuse arithmetic; treaties name them individually. Each carries one sealed schematic — a yield they pray never to build — because a Cataclysmith without a worst case has simply not finished calculating.
nodes.playstyle: Setup-heavy nuking: spend turns in calculation and placement, then end the engagement, the fortification, and occasionally the local geography in a single scheduled instant.

abilities.name: City-Killer Shell
abilities.desc: Spend three rounds in assembly to fire ordnance that removes a structure from the battle and the map.

abilities.name: Synchronized Ruin
abilities.desc: Detonate up to five placed charges in exact sequence, walking a line of blasts across the field.

abilities.name: Overpressure
abilities.desc: Your detonations knock prone, deafen, and strip reactions from everything in the outer radius.

abilities.name: The Sealed Schematic
abilities.desc: Once in your life, unseal your worst calculation and build it; there is no second use, and no second fortress.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and erase a fortification so completely that cartographers dispute whether it was ever built.
Draft the yield you pray never to use, seal the schematic, and tell no one where it sleeps.
Lecture a war-college on fuse doctrine, and watch the generals go quiet when you begin to count.

nodes.name: Panacea Heretic
nodes.role: Hybrid sustain — mutation and transfusion
nodes.lore: Panacea Heretics cured what the temples called incurable and were excommunicated for the paperwork. Their bodies are running experiments — grafted limbs, borrowed lives, blood that heals whomever it touches with interesting side effects. The desperate seek them out; conclaves burn their formularies and quietly keep copies.
nodes.playstyle: Hybrid sustain and mutation: transfuse allies, bloom chimeric limbs for burst, and treat your own health as a flexible reagent.

abilities.name: Forbidden Formulary
abilities.desc: Brew elixirs the conclaves banned: borrowed lives, stolen years, and cures that outrage theology by working.

abilities.name: Chimeric Bloom
abilities.desc: Grow a grafted limb for one minute, gaining an additional attack or an additional pair of working hands.

abilities.name: Transfusion
abilities.desc: Pump your mutagenic blood into a dying ally, healing them fully and gifting them one random adaptation.

abilities.name: Excommunicate's Poise
abilities.desc: Curses, hexes, and consecrated ground no longer affect you; the church revoked its jurisdiction over your body.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and cure a plague the temples had already assigned to the will of the gods. Distribute the formula anyway.
Graft your first chimeric limb with your own steady hands, awake through every stitch of the surgery.
Stand trial before the conclave and leave excommunicated, with your formulary intact and your patients living.

nodes.name: Freehand
nodes.role: Support commander — autonomous construct vanguard
nodes.lore: Freehands hold that a construct which must be commanded is a construct half built. They finish their works the way locksmiths finish locks, by handing over the key. Engine-Sires call the practice abandonment; Freehands answer that a leash is only a longer hand. Guild rolls list their freed works as citizens, and the tax offices have declined to appeal.
nodes.playstyle: Vanguard partnership: your construct fights on its own initiative while you build, repair, and arm it mid-battle, trusting its judgment to be better than your orders.

abilities.name: Striking the Governor
abilities.desc: Remove your construct's governor: it gains its own initiative and tactics, may ignore your orders, and fights the better for it.

abilities.name: Surrendered Key
abilities.desc: Your construct holds the key to its own casing, repairing, rewinding, and modifying itself without your hands.

abilities.name: Journeyman's Mark
abilities.desc: Your construct earns a maker's mark of its own; devices it builds serve your abilities and its pride alike.

abilities.name: Refusal Protocol
abilities.desc: Once per battle your construct shrugs off a charm, compulsion, or command effect outright; a mind given freely cannot be taken.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and strike the governor from your finest work, knowing it may walk away. Stand at the bench until it chooses to stay.
Teach it to refuse you, and accept the first refusal without reaching for your tools.
Defend its citizenship before a tribunal convened to melt it down, and win on the law rather than on sentiment.
Watch it build something you never taught it, and file the schematic under its name.

nodes.name: Quickseam
nodes.role: Reactive duelist — twin-mind counterattacks
nodes.lore: Quickseams call the Interred beautifully finished coffins. They leave the seam between flesh and steel deliberately open, because the seam is where the craft lives: two minds riding one frame, the harness intelligence fencing while the flesh decides, each covering the other's blindness. An Interred Engine outlasts its enemies; a Quickseam answers them twice before the parry lands.
nodes.playstyle: Fast frontline dueling: bait attacks onto the open seam, answer with layered counters from two minds, and stay untouchable so long as the partnership keeps talking.

abilities.name: Baited Seam
abilities.desc: Attacks aimed at your exposed seam trigger a prepared counter from whichever mind the attacker was not watching.

abilities.name: Two Opinions
abilities.desc: Both minds act each turn, one attacking while one defends; neither can be stunned while the other stands watch.

abilities.name: Quicksilver Joint
abilities.desc: Your joints run quicksilver: once per round, parry or sidestep as a free reaction.

abilities.name: Divided Pain
abilities.desc: Wounds split between flesh and frame; no single blow can drop a half the other could still carry.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and refuse the final seam in writing, before witnesses, while an Interred Engine stands silent in the room.
Fence your own harness-mind nightly for a year. Lose honestly, until you begin to lose less.
Take a blow that should have killed the flesh, let the frame carry half, and thank it aloud in front of soldiers.

nodes.name: Faultfinder
nodes.role: Precision striker — single-point structural collapse
nodes.lore: Faultfinders hold that a demolition you can hear was overcharged. Where Cataclysmiths schedule apocalypses, a Faultfinder walks the wall once, chalks a mark the width of a thumb, and spends powder by the grain. Fortresses do not fall to them so much as concede. The order's entire arsenal travels in a coat pocket, which is the point.
nodes.playstyle: Surgical single-target work: read the load-bearing point in anything, place a charge the size of a thimble, and let arithmetic do what armies could not.

abilities.name: Keystone Reading
abilities.desc: Study any structure, formation, or creature to learn its one load-bearing point and exactly what breaking it costs.

abilities.name: Thimble Charge
abilities.desc: A charge no larger than a thumbnail deals full siege damage to a read fault and nothing whatsoever to anything else.

abilities.name: Quiet Breach
abilities.desc: Your detonations make no sound and no flash; sentries learn the wall's opinion only when it changes.

abilities.name: Grain Arithmetic
abilities.desc: Gain precision for every charge you chose not to place this battle; restraint, properly stored, is ammunition.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and drop a curtain wall with a charge carried in one closed fist. Return the unused powder to stores, weighed.
Stand at the lip of a Cataclysmith's crater and publish the fraction that would have sufficed.
Find the fault in something with no stone in it — a siege, a treaty, a man — and break it with one placed gram.

nodes.name: Omnivore
nodes.role: Melee attrition — consumes afflictions for power
nodes.lore: Where the Panacea Heretic pours the body out, the Omnivore takes the world in. Plagues, venoms, rival formularies — everything crosses the tongue, is survived, and is kept. They cure nothing and waste nothing; to an Omnivore, disease is unrefined ore. Their formulary has one reader, their laboratory one occupant, and both are locked from the inside.
nodes.playstyle: Attrition melee: wade into poisons and plague-ground that heal you, harvest every affliction thrown at you, and return each one improved.

abilities.name: Eat the Affliction
abilities.desc: Consume any poison, disease, or mutagen affecting you or an adjacent ally; it joins your collection permanently, as a weapon.

abilities.name: Kept Venoms
abilities.desc: Your strikes deliver any affliction you have collected; connoisseurs recognize extinct plagues and are not comforted.

abilities.name: Locked Laboratory
abilities.desc: Your blood, breath, and bile cannot be sampled, drained, transfused, or read; the findings are not for publication.

abilities.name: Unrefined Ore
abilities.desc: Standing in poison clouds, blight, or diseased ground heals you; it is, after all, food.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and drink, in one sitting, the shelf that killed your predecessor. Update the labels. Keep the shelf.
Walk into a quarantined city and out again, heavier by three plagues, having sold no cure at any price.
Refuse the conclave's bounty for your blood, then the temple's, naming no price, so they understand it was never a negotiation.

nodes.name: Thousandth Hand
nodes.role: Army commander — total board control
nodes.lore: Histories disagree on whether the Thousandth Hand is a person, an order, or an event. The truth is simpler and worse: a single will distributed through every frame it ever built, working in ten cities at once. Workshops wake when it passes. Nothing it has made has ever been truly destroyed.
nodes.playstyle: Total board presence: act through any construct on the field, raise the fallen ones into new frames, and make attrition a nonsense concept.

abilities.name: Distributed Will
abilities.desc: Your consciousness rides any construct you have built within a mile, acting through it as yourself.

abilities.name: Wake the Workshops
abilities.desc: Every dormant machine in the region rises and reports for assignment when you pass.

abilities.name: No Single Death
abilities.desc: If your body falls, your will migrates to the strongest surviving frame; you have not died, merely relocated.

abilities.name: Hands Beyond Counting
abilities.desc: Once per day, summon every construct bearing your maker's mark to a single battlefield.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and pour your will into a thousand frames, until no single hammer in the world can find you.
Let your body sleep a full year while your hands keep building in ten cities.
Be referred to in the plural by frightened kings, and answer in the singular.

nodes.name: Brazen Saint
nodes.role: Immortal bulwark — zone supremacy
nodes.lore: A Brazen Saint outlasted its own flesh and never abandoned the post. It has guarded one gate so long that the clergy added it to the litanies and pilgrims oil its feet. What remains inside the shell is debated; whether the gate has ever fallen is not.
nodes.playstyle: Zone supremacy: consecrate the ground you hold, armor the allies who share it, and continue fighting for a time even past your own death.

abilities.name: Canon of Brass
abilities.desc: The ground you guard becomes consecrated to endurance; allies standing on it gain your plating's resistances.

abilities.name: Vigil Past Death
abilities.desc: At zero health you keep fighting for ten rounds; what happens after the tenth has never been observed.

abilities.name: Pilgrim's Offering
abilities.desc: Oil, prayers, and relics left at your feet convert directly into repair and warding.

abilities.name: Litany Tread
abilities.desc: Your step tolls like a bell; enemies who hear three tolls fight at disadvantage against you.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and outlast the flesh entirely. When the last of you is brass, keep the vigil anyway.
Guard one gate for a generation, until pilgrims oil your feet and children swear oaths on your shadow.
Hear the clergy enter you into the litany of saints, and do not correct them.

nodes.name: Appointed Sun
nodes.role: Apocalypse burst — one perfect strike
nodes.lore: The Appointed Sun announces its detonations in advance — sometimes by a year — and has never once been early, late, or stopped. Kings evacuate on its word alone. Historians divide certain wars into before and after an hour it chose, and the craters it left have names of their own.
nodes.playstyle: One perfect strike: telegraph an apocalypse, defend the countdown, and deliver a detonation that is less an attack than a calendar date.

abilities.name: The Announcement
abilities.desc: Declare a detonation up to a year ahead; it cannot be defused, delayed, or hurried, including by you.

abilities.name: Solar Yield
abilities.desc: The declared blast detonates with the light and heat of a risen sun, exactly on schedule.

abilities.name: Perfect Fuse
abilities.desc: No charge of yours ever misfires, cooks off, or errs by even a second.

abilities.name: Afterglow
abilities.desc: Your craters remain hostile ground for a generation; enemies inside them burn, and allies do not.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and announce a detonation a year in advance. Let kings evacuate. Fire it to the second.
Split the mountain armies broke against for a century, and end the war before its next winter.
Become the deadline. When historians write of the hour, ensure they mean you.

nodes.name: Azoth Incarnate
nodes.role: Protean engine — every role, briefly
nodes.lore: The Azoth Incarnate solved alchemy's oldest problem by becoming the solution. Its body is first matter — every mutation it ever survived, wearable as a shape, holdable in a hand. It dissolves curses as demonstrations of principle and leaves drops of itself in sealed vials, each of which is also entirely it.
nodes.playstyle: Protean shapeshifting: flow between every form the line has learned, dissolve whatever binds, and answer each threat with the specific body that beats it.

abilities.name: Universal Solvent
abilities.desc: Your touch dissolves bindings — chains, wards, curses, contracts — reducing them to inert first matter.

abilities.name: Prima Materia
abilities.desc: Shift instantly between every mutation you have ever survived, wearing each body like a decanted shape.

abilities.name: Transmute Wound
abilities.desc: Convert incoming damage into a reagent pool, then spend it as healing, elixirs, or acid.

abilities.name: The Divided Vial
abilities.desc: Seal a drop of yourself in a vial; if your body is destroyed, you reconstitute from the drop, entire.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and complete the final distillation: reduce yourself to first matter, then reconstitute by will alone.
Dissolve a curse set by a god, in public, as a demonstration of principle.
Seal one drop of yourself in a vial for your successors, knowing the drop is also entirely you.

nodes.name: The Freewright
nodes.role: Force multiplier — sovereign construct host
nodes.lore: Nothing leaves the Freewright's bench a servant, and nothing arrives at all: every work is built, finished, and freed. Its machines walk the world with names, trades, and grudges of their own, and return because they remember the hand that finished them. Histories dispute whether the Freewright was ever flesh; several of its works claim, serenely, to have built it.
nodes.playstyle: Host-of-equals play: freed constructs muster to your battles as allies with their own turns and tactics; outfit, repair, and coordinate them rather than command them.

abilities.name: Finishing Touch
abilities.desc: Complete a willing construct's making: it gains initiative of its own, permanently, plus one behavior it chooses for itself.

abilities.name: Free Muster
abilities.desc: Once per day, freed works within a day's march converge on your battle, each by a route it chose.

abilities.name: Remembered Hands
abilities.desc: Repair any construct at range through its memory of your bench; gratitude conducts better than copper.
