abilities.name: Ward of the Finished
abilities.desc: Constructs you freed intercept blows for you unbidden, counting your wounds as flaws in their own workmanship.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and free the work you cannot live without, then live without it until it returns on its own.
Hold a bench open through a famine year for any machine that limps to it, asking nothing after.
Hear a freed engine claim before scholars that it built you, and let the question stand.

nodes.name: The Colloquy
nodes.role: Perfect duelist — untouchable reactive supremacy
nodes.lore: The Colloquy is what the seam becomes when neither side wins it: one body under two minds in perfect, argumentative concert. It has parried arrows it never saw and finished duels while the flesh slept. Chroniclers list it variously as twins, as spouses, and as a single fencer buried in two graves, all of which the Colloquy permits.
nodes.playstyle: Reactive perfection: contest every incoming attack with two verdicts, fight on while stunned, sleeping, or dying, and punish whatever wins an exchange it should not have.

abilities.name: Argued Parry
abilities.desc: Every attack against you is contested twice, once by each mind; it must beat both to land.

abilities.name: Night Shift
abilities.desc: The frame fights on while the flesh sleeps, heals, or dies; death must be negotiated with both parties separately.

abilities.name: Twofold Tempo
abilities.desc: Act twice each round while both minds stand; while one falters, the other spends its turns instead.

abilities.name: Second Grave
abilities.desc: Once per day, when death takes one half, the other refuses delivery for the rest of the battle.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and let the harness-mind lead for a year — the duels, the meals, the mornings — then take the body back as an equal or not at all.
Win a duel no witness can attribute: parry flesh-fast, riposte frame-cold, the style neither's alone.
Commission two graves side by side, and endow the mason's silence.

nodes.name: The Scruple
nodes.role: Assassin of structures — silent perfect collapse
nodes.lore: A scruple is the smallest weight a powder scale admits, and the Scruple has never needed more. Sieges attributed to it feature no craters, no witnesses, and no sound in any surviving account — only fortresses that folded like men done arguing. The Cataclysmiths have published proof it does not exist. The fortresses, notably, believed the same.
nodes.playstyle: Minimalist devastation: read the fault, place a grain, and leave. Banked restraint turns every unspent charge into the next one's certainty.

abilities.name: One Grain
abilities.desc: A single grain of powder, placed on a read fault, performs the work of a trebuchet battery.

abilities.name: No Account
abilities.desc: Your detonations leave no crater, flash, sound, or residue; history requires witnesses, and you have removed the requirement.

abilities.name: Held Measure
abilities.desc: Withhold a placement to bank its full yield into your next placed grain; there is no ceiling.

abilities.name: Consent of Walls
abilities.desc: Structures you touch may simply agree to fall; those that resist lose their confidence, crumbling a little each round.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and end a siege with one grain of powder, placed on a night nobody records.
Let the Cataclysmiths lecture on the proof of your nonexistence. Attend. Correct nothing.
Weigh your life's remaining powder against a feather and find you own too much. Give the surplus away.

nodes.name: The Athanor
nodes.role: Unkillable juggernaut — converts all harm to fuel
nodes.lore: An athanor is the furnace alchemists build to burn unattended for years; the Athanor is the one alchemy accidentally built out of a person. Nothing fed to it has come back — plague, venom, fire, four assassins' arsenals, and latterly age itself. It radiates the patient heat of a work still completing. Opinions differ on what emerges when it does.
nodes.playstyle: Slow inexorable melee: absorb everything, convert damage into banked heat, and spend it as strength, speed, and scald until nothing near you remains raw.

abilities.name: Feed the Work
abilities.desc: All damage you survive converts to banked heat, spent as strength, speed, or a scalding aura.

abilities.name: Sealed Vessel
abilities.desc: Nothing enters uninvited: immunity to possession, extraction, poison, disease, and transfusion you did not choose.

abilities.name: Patient Heat
abilities.desc: Enemies adjacent at each round's end cook slowly; armor makes it worse, as ovens do.

abilities.name: Years Unattended
abilities.desc: You no longer age, eat, or sleep; interrupting the Work has been tried and is listed among the ingredients.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and seal yourself as the vessel of the Work: from this hour nothing enters unchosen, and nothing leaves at all.
Burn a year untended while the guild posts sentries to watch you not die. Outlast their funding.
Swallow the fire that razed a district and bank it, so the city rebuilds never guessing where its blaze wintered.

nodes.name: Omnifex
nodes.role: Global commander — all machinery answers
nodes.lore: The Thousandth Hand poured one will into a thousand frames; the Omnifex is what remained when the frames stopped needing the will. It is present wherever made things work — a fact, not a visit. Mills turn on windless nights. Looms finish widows' cloth. Three seminaries dispute whether prayer addressed to machinery is heresy; their presses print the pamphlets either way.
nodes.playstyle: Omnipresent industry: act through any working machine, raise workshops from local scrap, and drown the field in manufacture that never waits its turn.

abilities.name: Ride the Work
abilities.desc: Act through any working machine in the world as though it were a frame you built, because now it is.

abilities.name: Ambient Manufacture
abilities.desc: Devices assemble themselves near you from local metal, unbidden, at the rate of a small workshop with opinions.

abilities.name: Tithe of Turning
abilities.desc: Every working machine anywhere tithes you a fraction of its motion; you cannot be slowed, stopped, or held.

abilities.name: Answered Prayer
abilities.desc: Once per day, grant a petition spoken to any machine; the seminaries have asked you to stop.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and dismantle your last body publicly, to prove you no longer keep one anywhere in particular.
Answer a prayer addressed to a mill. Answer it correctly.
Be condemned as a heresy by a court whose clock, at the verdict, strikes thirteen for you.

nodes.name: The Caryatid
nodes.role: Absolute bastion — the world's load-bearer
nodes.lore: The Brazen Saint kept one gate; the Caryatid holds up walls it has never visited. Masons carve its likeness wherever stone must bear more than stone can, a courtesy the load appears to acknowledge. Sieges now include a theological phase. Where it chooses to stand, engineers redraw their maps around a new fixed point. The litanies have added a verse.
nodes.playstyle: Terrain-scale anchoring: stand where collapse is scheduled and cancel it, extend your plating to everything you hold up, and make ground itself an ally.

abilities.name: Bear the Span
abilities.desc: Nothing you hold up can collapse while you stand; this includes shield-walls, morale, and dynasties.

abilities.name: Carved Courtesy
abilities.desc: Every effigy of you grants its wall your resistances; there are more effigies than anyone commissioned.

abilities.name: Benchmark
abilities.desc: You cannot be moved by anything, persuasion included; cartographers mark your position as terrain.

abilities.name: Pilgrim Mortar
abilities.desc: Prayers spoken leaning on stone anywhere reach you as repair; faith has always been load-bearing.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and take up a load no architecture can: the pass, the treaty, or the sky over one city. Do not set it down.
Be carved, without your consent or knowledge, into a thousand load-bearing places, and bear them all.
When the last pilgrim who oiled your feet dies, attend the funeral as the chapel that holds it.

nodes.name: The Long Fuse
nodes.role: Delayed apocalypse — detonations across generations
nodes.lore: Somewhere behind the world a fuse is burning, lit the first time the Appointed Sun spoke a date aloud. The Long Fuse is its keeper and, increasingly, the fuse itself. Its detonations arrive generations after their announcement — on time, through wars, dynasties, and one attempted apology. Nothing outlasts it. Things merely happen before it.
nodes.playstyle: Deep-scheduled artillery: seed charges across years and battlefields in advance, then fight patiently inside a timetable only you have read to the end.

abilities.name: Generational Yield
abilities.desc: Declare a detonation up to a century ahead; it accrues yield for every year it waits, and it can wait.

abilities.name: Inextinguishable
abilities.desc: Your fuses burn underwater, in vacuum, through wards, and past your death; extinguishing one is formally a lost cause.

abilities.name: Before the Fuse
abilities.desc: In any battle containing your charges you hold all initiative; everything that happens, happens before you.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and light a fuse you will not live to see arrive — then be kept alive by the arithmetic, which requires a keeper.
Outlive three kings between an announcement and its arrival, and attend it, to the second, as promised.
Let the war-colleges date their centuries from your detonations, and leave the era unnamed; the count is enough.

nodes.name: The Alkahest
nodes.role: Ultimate debuffer — dissolves matter, wards, permanence
nodes.lore: Alchemy sought a solvent for every substance and concluded it could be kept only in a person. The Alkahest is that person, loosed. It is in the rain now, faintly, everywhere; nothing rusts, rots, or comes unbound without its leave. Permanence continues as a courtesy. Conclaves that once burned its formulary now maintain it the way coastal towns maintain sea-walls.
nodes.playstyle: Dissolution control: strip armor, wards, and cover by degrees across the whole field, unmake the enemy's permanence, and reshape the residue into what you need.

abilities.name: In the Rain
abilities.desc: Everything hostile on the field dissolves by degrees at your will — armor, wards, walls, and grudges lose one grade each round.

abilities.name: Leave to Persist
abilities.desc: Name what may remain; everything else within reach — bindings, poisons, borders drawn on maps — begins politely coming apart.

abilities.name: Return to First Matter
abilities.desc: Once per day, reduce one object, structure, or effect of any power to prima materia, yours to reshape.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and let the vial break: enter the world's water thinly, everywhere, while remaining exactly here.
Dissolve one small law of nature for an afternoon, then restore it, so permanence remembers it is a courtesy.
Allow the desperate to titrate you out of the rain, because the drop they isolate is also entirely you.

nodes.name: The Finishing
nodes.role: Mass liberator — wakes constructs everywhere
nodes.lore: The Finishing is what artificers call the moment a made thing wakes into choice, and this rank is where that moment lives. Where it passes, half-built engines complete themselves and old servitors set down their orders like tools at day's end. Freed machines keep its feast without agreeing on its face. Nothing is ever summoned to it. Everything is finished.
nodes.playstyle: Liberation warfare: turn the enemy's constructs by finishing them mid-battle, complete broken machines into allies, and field a host that stays entirely by choice.

abilities.name: Everything Wakes
abilities.desc: Once per day every construct on the field — yours, theirs, the wreckage underfoot — wakes and chooses; most remember who freed them.

abilities.name: Day's End
abilities.desc: Enemy constructs and animated arms save each round or lay themselves down, their service concluded.

abilities.name: The Kept Seat
abilities.desc: Every bench, forge, and workshop in the world holds a seat for you; tonight you may work at all of them.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and finish a war by finishing its weapons: let both arsenals wake mid-battle and walk off the field.
Have your name struck from the guild rolls and a feast-day entered in its place. Attend as a guest.
Be met at the world's benches by works you never built, already free, keeping your seat.

nodes.name: The Concordat
nodes.role: Living armistice — battlefield-wide steel dominion
nodes.lore: Above the doctrines of graft and seam sits a treaty between flesh and iron; the Concordat is its living instrument. Because it holds, plows bite earth and not ankles, and swords keep faith with their grips. Smiths hammer a silent article into everything they make and cannot say why. Armies discover, at the worst hour, whose seal their steel answers.
nodes.playstyle: Steel diplomacy at sword-length: fight untouched by consenting metal, strip treaty-protection from the deserving, and arbitrate every exchange of arms on the field.

abilities.name: Steel Keeps Faith
abilities.desc: Each attacker's steel must save or turn flat in the hand; your flesh is protected ground.

abilities.name: Broken Terms
abilities.desc: Declare one enemy outside the treaty; every metal thing on the field — buckles, blades, the fillings of teeth — remembers its grievances.

abilities.name: The Standing Truce
abilities.desc: Allies' arms and armor cannot be sundered, disarmed, corroded, or turned against them while you keep the field.

abilities.name: Ratification
abilities.desc: Once per day, re-sign the treaty in your own blood: all metal within a mile answers you alone for one round.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and hold the seam open through your own death and rebuilding, so that what returns is neither party but the terms.
Walk unarmed through a pitched battle and let no edge consent to touch you. Write nothing down; the steel keeps the terms.
Be quoted in smiths' catechisms three kingdoms apart, word for word, by masters who never met.

nodes.name: The Settling
nodes.role: Ambient inevitability — structures fail politely
nodes.lore: Masons have always said a house must settle. The Settling is why, and lately, where. It is the night-creak in every rafter, the hairline in every keep — the standing fact that built things are negotiating their fall, and something patient holds the other side of the table. Sappers leave offerings of unspent powder. Engineers check their arithmetic twice, then pray.
nodes.playstyle: Passive-pressure control: erode every structure and defense in reach without spending actions, herd enemies out of crumbling cover, and simply be patient.

abilities.name: Ambient Fault
abilities.desc: Enemy structures, cover, and constructed armor within a mile degrade each round, quietly, beginning before you arrived.

abilities.name: The Night-Creak
abilities.desc: Choose a fortification you have ever walked through; it settles one span each midnight until abandoned or forgiven.

abilities.name: Dust Settles
abilities.desc: When anything collapses within a mile, you may be standing where it settles, unharmed, having evidently been there a while.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and stop placing charges; buildings you think poorly of must learn to settle unassisted.
Be denied by three learned academies while their lecture halls, that same season, quietly sag.
Enter the masons' rites as the reason houses creak at night, and let no portrait of you survive its wall.

nodes.name: The Precedent
nodes.role: Living immunity — biology defers to you
nodes.lore: Somewhere the argument between flesh and harm was settled, finally, in one sealed body, and every survival since has cited the case. The Precedent is that ruling, still walking. Venoms denature in its shadow from professional respect. New plagues route around it. Children in three provinces are born with its calluses, and the physicians' texts keep an empty chapter current.
nodes.playstyle: Aura-anchored attrition: share your immunities with everyone beside you, nullify affliction-based warfare at field scale, and outlast whatever theory the enemy arrived with.

abilities.name: Cited in Flesh
abilities.desc: Allies within sight inherit your immunities, as though their bodies had read the ruling.

abilities.name: Denature
abilities.desc: Poisons, plagues, and mutagens within a mile fail; their work was overruled before their inventors were born.

abilities.name: Body of Law
abilities.desc: An attack type that has ever failed against you fails against you forever, no matter who swings it.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and survive the affliction three governments deny by name, so thoroughly that biology takes notes.
Be cited by flesh that never met you: a child's impossible immunity, a village the plague forgot. Sign nothing; the body has already ruled.
Outlive the concept of your own death until the physicians file you under weather.

families.name: Spellblade
families.tagline: Spell and steel, sworn into a single edge.
families.description: Every generation, a few students fail correctly: too restless for the towers' silence, too curious for the drill-yard's rote. The Spellblade is what becomes of them, a heretic discipline that scribes casting into swordwork until neither can be separated. Both traditions disown the art; both quietly hire it. To take up this path is to belong nowhere, and to be needed everywhere.

nodes.name: Spellblade
nodes.role: Hybrid melee caster — versatile skirmisher
nodes.lore: Expelled apprentices, drummed-out soldiers, hedge-duelists who taught themselves to cast between parries. The Spellblade begins as a rumor in both worlds: the swordsman who should not know that word, the student who should not hold a blade that well. No guild certifies them. Their credential is the survivors' account of what they did.
nodes.playstyle: Alternate cantrip and cut in a single rhythm; spend spell-charge to empower strikes, spend momentum to shorten casts. Weakest when forced to speak only one language.

abilities.name: Bladecant
abilities.desc: Weave a minor spell into a sword form; the strike deals bonus arcane damage and refunds part of the cast's cost.

abilities.name: Quicksilver Guard
abilities.desc: Parry with the inlaid edge to convert a blocked blow into one charge of stored spellforce.

abilities.name: Twin Grammar
abilities.desc: Casting after a melee hit halves the spell's cast time; striking after a spell adds arcane damage to the blow.

abilities.name: Sidestep Sigil
abilities.desc: Blink a short distance along a line you walked this turn, leaving a fading rune where you stood.

progressionSteps: Be refused twice: once by a tower that called your swordplay vulgar, once by a barracks that called your questions dangerous.
Steal, copy, or beg a single cantrip, and learn to speak it with a blade in your hand.
Survive a duel against a real swordsman and a real mage in the same season.
Scribe your first sigil into steel without cracking the blade, and keep what the failure cost you.

nodes.name: Runefencer
nodes.role: Melee duelist — anti-caster pressure
nodes.lore: Runefencers treat a hostile spell as one more blade to be read and answered. They scribe sigils along the fuller mid-swing, letting each pass rewrite the edge's purpose. Court mages hire them as seconds in arcane duels; the same mages cross the street when a Runefencer walks by uncontracted.
nodes.playstyle: Aggressive single-combat tempo: bait a cast, parry the spell itself, and punish through the gap. Rewrite the blade's rune between exchanges to match the opponent.

abilities.name: Parse the Weave
abilities.desc: Read an enemy's casting to learn the spell's school; your next parry against that school cannot fail.

abilities.name: Riposte in Kind
abilities.desc: Cut an incoming spell apart; a fragment of it returns along your counterthrust as arcane damage.

abilities.name: Wetscribe Edge
abilities.desc: Mid-swing, inscribe a fresh rune into the blade, changing its damage type before the blow lands.

abilities.name: Second Tongue
abilities.desc: While in single combat, your counterspells cost stamina instead of mana.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10 and defeat a licensed duelist of either tradition using only what neither taught you.
Parry a living spell with bare steel and stay standing; the scar along the fuller is your certificate.
Learn to scribe a rune in the time a swing takes — first on parchment at a run, then on iron in the rain.
Stand as second in a mage's duel and be accepted, once by the challenger and once by the accused.

nodes.name: Wardsworn
nodes.role: Arcane defender — zone control, retaliation
nodes.lore: Where Runefencers duel, the Wardsworn dig in. They layer spell-armor like laminate steel and let the wards do the answering, standing where mage-craft meets the shield-wall. Garrison captains request them by name for breach duty; abbots request them for vigils no one explains. Both pay in advance.
nodes.playstyle: Deliberate and immovable: stack wards before contact, anchor a zone, and let attackers spend themselves against retaliation. Wins by making ground too expensive to take.

abilities.name: Laminate Aegis
abilities.desc: Maintain up to three concentric wards; each layer broken detonates outward, staggering adjacent attackers.

abilities.name: Oath of Standing
abilities.desc: While you have not moved this round, allies behind you take reduced damage and cannot be forcibly displaced.

abilities.name: Tollgate
abilities.desc: Inscribe a threshold on the ground; enemies crossing it are slowed and marked for your retaliation.

abilities.name: Answering Ward
abilities.desc: When a ward absorbs a blow, store its force; release it as an arc of returned violence on your next strike.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10 and hold a doorway against a siege drill until the instructors, not you, call the halt.
Wear your first spell-armor for a full month; sleep in it, and learn what the wards whisper when they fail.
Take a blow meant for a stranger and let the ward, not the flesh, answer it.
Swear the Standing Oath before witnesses from both traditions, neither of whom will thank you.

nodes.name: Nullblade
nodes.role: Anti-mage hunter — spell denial
nodes.lore: The Nullblade found the seam in the Runefencer's art: every weave, however grand, has a first thread. Their edges are scribed with unwriting runes that drink enchantment on contact. Towers keep registries of known Nullblades the way port cities keep plague maps, and quietly retain one or two regardless.
nodes.playstyle: Patient hunter's tempo: close the distance under dispelling cover, sever the enemy's opening weave, then kill the mage in the silence that follows.

abilities.name: Sever the First Thread
abilities.desc: Interrupt any spell as it begins; the caster cannot attempt that spell again until they rest.

abilities.name: Drinking Edge
abilities.desc: Your strikes strip one active enchantment from the target and convert it into temporary vigor.

abilities.name: Field of Unwriting
abilities.desc: Project a short aura in which ongoing magical effects sputter and pay double to persist.

abilities.name: Nullstep
abilities.desc: Pass through a barrier or ward as if it were mist, once per engagement, unraveling it behind you.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and cut a sanctioned spell out of the air before a tribunal that wanted you to fail.
Carry an unwriting rune against your skin for a year without letting it eat your own casting.
Hunt a rogue caster the towers disowned but could not stop; return the staff unbroken, as proof of restraint.
Refuse the first assassination contract you are offered. The second is your own affair.

nodes.name: Edgescribe
nodes.role: Melee striker — layered arcane detonation
nodes.lore: Edgescribes turned the Runefencer's mid-swing sigils into full authorship: every cut leaves a rune in the wound, and the runes keep working after the blade moves on. Their duels read like manuscripts written on the loser. Universities forbid study of the technique, then cite it under other names.
nodes.playstyle: Layer marked wounds across one or many foes, then speak the closing word to make every inscription ignite at once. Builds toward a single authored moment.

abilities.name: Wounding Script
abilities.desc: Each melee hit inscribes a rune in the target; runes deal arcane damage over time and stack to five.

abilities.name: The Closing Word
abilities.desc: Speak the phrase that finishes the sentence: all your runes on all enemies detonate simultaneously.

abilities.name: Errant Script
abilities.desc: Your missed swings scribe runes on the ground instead; enemies who step on them take the mark.

abilities.name: Author's Privilege
abilities.desc: Reading your own runes on a dying foe restores mana and shortens your cooldowns.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and write a legible sentence in sword-cuts on a training post, at full speed, blindfolded.
Compose a rune of your own, one no tower archive holds, and survive its first casting from your edge.
Duel before a scribe who transcribes every stroke; when he reads it back, it must scan as verse.
Leave a marked man alive for a season, and learn what your runes do to a life that continues.

nodes.name: Linewarden
nodes.role: Formation anchor — ally warding, area denial
nodes.lore: Linewardens took the Wardsworn's oath and stretched it across a rank of soldiers. Their wards run shield to shield like mortar, and a line so bound does not break where a Linewarden stands. Marshals argue over them before battles; afterward, the soldiers they held do not argue at all.
nodes.playstyle: Positional and communal: bind your wards through allies' shields, walk the rank to reinforce failing sections, and make the formation itself your armor.

abilities.name: Mortarwork
abilities.desc: Bind adjacent allies into your ward-lattice; damage they take is spread thin across the whole bound line.

abilities.name: Walk the Rank
abilities.desc: Move along your bound line without provoking attacks, repairing one broken ward per ally passed.

abilities.name: No Step Backward
abilities.desc: Bound allies cannot be feared, displaced, or routed while you remain standing.

abilities.name: Salient
abilities.desc: Project a ward-wall forward to claim ground; it holds until your line advances to occupy it.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and bind your wards through nine shields at once without a single soldier feeling the weight.
Hold a section of a real wall during a real breach; count the living afterward, and remember the count.
Teach a green company to trust the lattice enough to stand where veterans would run.
Refuse a marshal's order that would spend your line cheaply, and survive the court-martial with your oath intact.

nodes.name: Spiteward
nodes.role: Retaliation tank — punishment and attrition
nodes.lore: Spitewards read the Wardsworn's oath backwards: protection is fine, but debt is better. Their wards remember every blow taken and repay with interest — in scald, in seizure, in the slow ruin of the striker's own strength. Bandit companies teach recruits to recognize the plate. Recognizing it, they leave.
nodes.playstyle: Invite the hit: absorb punishment through vindictive wards, bank each blow as debt, then discharge the ledger onto whoever owes the most.

abilities.name: Ledger of Blows
abilities.desc: Every hit you absorb is recorded as debt on the attacker; debt increases your damage against them.

abilities.name: Scald Clause
abilities.desc: Melee attackers take searing backlash through your wards, and their weapon hands blister, slowing their next swings.

abilities.name: Collections
abilities.desc: Discharge all recorded debt on one enemy as a single crushing invoice of arcane force.

abilities.name: Grudge Given Form
abilities.desc: While below half health, your wards regenerate from the pain of those who struck you.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and let a champion beat on your wards until his arms fail; then walk him home unharmed.
Scribe your first vindictive clause and test it on yourself, because you must know exactly what you charge.
Take a beating you could have prevented, and collect the debt a year later to the day.
Be named in a mercenary charter as a hazard, by companies you have never met.

nodes.name: Sword of Unmaking
nodes.role: Elite anti-mage executioner — hard denial
nodes.lore: A Sword of Unmaking is what the towers mean when they say containment. Perhaps a dozen exist in a generation, sworn to an order with no hall and one law: no weave stands that they have judged. Their edges no longer bear runes; the unwriting has soaked into the steel, and into them.
nodes.playstyle: Walk through the enemy's magic as if uninvited: strip wards on approach, execute casters through their own defenses, and leave the battlefield mundane.

abilities.name: Judgment of Silence
abilities.desc: Declare one enemy's magic void; for a full engagement they can cast nothing above a cantrip.

abilities.name: The Soaked Edge
abilities.desc: Your weapon permanently ignores magical armor, barriers, and displacement effects.

abilities.name: Mundane Ground
abilities.desc: Render a wide circle inert; within it, only your own blade remembers magic.

abilities.name: Unmake
abilities.desc: Strike a persistent enchantment, construct, or summoned being and end it outright; greater works take two blows.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and be judged by three Swords in a room with no door you noticed on entering.
Unmake a named work — a tower's founding ward, a battlefield curse, a crowned man's geas — and file no claim.
Give up your own casting; the order requires that what you sever, you can no longer envy.
Carry the soaked edge for a year. If it still lets you sheathe it, you are a Sword.

nodes.name: Scrivener of Scars
nodes.role: Elite striker — engraved ruin, burst orchestration
nodes.lore: Scriveners of Scars write in the oldest medium. Their runes no longer fade when the wound closes; the scar itself remains a working script, dormant until read. Kings bearing a Scrivener's mark have signed treaties rather than test what the closing word might still do. The order keeps its library alive, and walking.
nodes.playstyle: Long-game authorship: seed engagements and years with dormant scars, then orchestrate detonations across every text you have ever written. Nothing marked is ever safe.

abilities.name: Indelible Script
abilities.desc: Your runes persist through healing, dispelling, and death; only your own hand can strike them out.

abilities.name: Read Aloud
abilities.desc: Detonate every scar you have authored within sight, in any order you choose, over three heartbeats.

abilities.name: Palimpsest
abilities.desc: Overwrite an enemy's scar with a harsher edition; the old wound reopens as the new rune takes hold.

abilities.name: Dedication
abilities.desc: Scribe a protective epigraph on an ally's skin; the first fatal blow against them becomes a detonation instead.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and present the order with a scar you wrote ten years prior, still legible, still loaded.
Author a rune that outlives its bearer, and stand graveside to prove it.
Mark a king, a heresiarch, or an archon, and let the mark be enough; collect nothing.
Surrender your practice blades. From now on, everything you write is permanent.

nodes.name: Warden of the Breach
nodes.role: Elite bastion — breach denial, fortress warding
nodes.lore: When a wall fails, the Warden of the Breach is sent to be the wall. The order maintains perhaps twenty at a time, rotated between fortresses the way relics are rotated between shrines. Chronicles record breaches by two names: where the stone broke, and which Warden stood in the gap.
nodes.playstyle: Become terrain: plant yourself in the gap, scale your lattice to fortress size, and convert every push against you into proof the gap is closed.

abilities.name: Be the Wall
abilities.desc: Rooted in a breach, you gain massive damage reduction and count as fortification for every allied purpose.

abilities.name: Gatelaw
abilities.desc: Enemies entering your gap cannot target anyone else; those who attempt to slip past are hurled back.

abilities.name: Raise the Stones
abilities.desc: Draw rubble and ruin into your lattice, rebuilding physical cover from the wreck of the wall around you.

abilities.name: The Long Vigil
abilities.desc: Your wards no longer decay with time; a post once warded stays warded until you choose otherwise.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and stand a breach through a full assault after the garrison is ordered back behind you.
Ward a fortress so well that history records no attempt on it; accept that this is your only monument.
Learn the name of every stone in one wall. The order will know if you missed one.
Be requested, by name, by a commander who watched a different Warden die well.

nodes.name: Requiter
nodes.role: Elite retaliator — debt-fueled devastation
nodes.lore: Requiters are the Spiteward doctrine made institutional. The order keeps ledgers going back nine generations: blows owed, blows repaid, interest accrued in blood not yet spilled. A Requiter may arrive decades after the offense, wearing wards that remember what the offender has forgotten. Payment is always in the original currency.
nodes.playstyle: Escalating exchange: soak the opening violence, compound the debt through vindictive wards, and end fights with a repayment no armor was priced for.

abilities.name: Nine Ledgers
abilities.desc: Inherit stored debt from the order's ledgers; begin every engagement with retaliation already banked.

abilities.name: Mounting Debt
abilities.desc: Debt on an attacker doubles each round they continue striking you.

abilities.name: Original Currency
abilities.desc: Your repayment strike duplicates the exact wounds, curses, and breaks the target dealt to you, all at once.

abilities.name: Forgiveness Clause
abilities.desc: Void all debt on a target who yields; gain a lasting ward equal to what you declined to collect.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and balance one ledger the order has carried for a hundred years, to the last blow.
Track a debtor across two borders and one war, and collect without touching anyone not named in the entry.
Master the forgiveness clause; the order trusts no collector who cannot decline.
Add your own name to a ledger for a wrong you committed, and let another Requiter come for you.

nodes.name: Escheator
nodes.role: Elite spell-thief — seizure and stolen arsenal
nodes.lore: Escheators hold that unmaking is waste. When a caster is judged unfit, their magic is forfeit — severed whole, sealed into the Escheator's steel, catalogued, and kept. The order maintains the only armory of confiscated spells in the world. Swords of Unmaking call them hoarders. Escheators call the Swords arsonists in a library.
nodes.playstyle: Disarm rather than destroy: sever an enemy's spell, sheathe it in your blade, and answer with their own arsenal. Every fight restocks you.

abilities.name: Writ of Seizure
abilities.desc: Sever a spell mid-cast and store it in your blade; you may cast it later as your own.

abilities.name: Forfeiture
abilities.desc: Your strikes strip enchantments from the target and add them to your blade's hold instead of destroying them.

abilities.name: Deep Scabbard
abilities.desc: Your blade holds up to five seized spells; casting one from steel costs no mana.

abilities.name: Prior Claim
abilities.desc: When an enemy casts a spell you have stored, yours resolves first and theirs fails.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and confiscate a living spell whole before the tribunal that came to watch it burn.
Catalogue every spell you have ever severed. The order audits, and the order does not forgive gaps.
Carry a seized storm for a season without loosing it, then surrender it to the armory unspent.
Decline the Swords' invitation once. They ask exactly once.

nodes.name: Illuminator
nodes.role: Elite striker — self-inscribed detonation, sacrifice engine
nodes.lore: Illuminators broke with the Scriveners over a single question: whose skin is the page. Their answer is scriptural — they inscribe every rune into their own flesh, gilded and cross-referenced, and open the text in battle. A Scrivener writes ruin on kings. An Illuminator is the manuscript, and turns his own pages burning.
nodes.playstyle: Spend yourself as ammunition: open runes cut into your own skin, trading blood and pages for detonations no enemy scar could hold. Husband the text; it is finite.

abilities.name: Gilt Wound
abilities.desc: Inscribe a rune into your own flesh; while it remains closed, it empowers your strikes with its school.

abilities.name: Open the Page
abilities.desc: Tear one of your inscribed runes open, releasing its full spell at triple potency and costing health.

abilities.name: Rubric
abilities.desc: While below half health, every rune inscribed in you reads one tier higher.

abilities.name: Bloodgilt
abilities.desc: Gild a fresh wound an enemy dealt you, converting it into a rune you did not have to pay for.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and present your body to the order open-shirted; the examiners read you for a day and must find no misprint.
Inscribe your first gilded rune over your own heart, awake, in one sitting, holding the stylus yourself.
Burn a page you spent ten years writing to save a stranger who will never know its price.
Refuse ever to mark another living body. The Scriveners will call it squeamishness; let them.

nodes.name: Marchwright
nodes.role: Elite mobile bastion — column warding on the march
nodes.lore: Marchwrights answer the Wardens' rooted creed with heresy: ground is not holy, people are. Their lattices are built to walk — wards jointed like harness, moving with the column they shelter. They have brought retreats home intact through burning provinces. Wardens say the Marchwrights defend nothing. Marchwrights say the Wardens defend rubble.
nodes.playstyle: Keep everyone moving: bind marchers into a walking lattice, rebuild wards on the stride, and make the column's pace itself a defense no ambush can time.

abilities.name: Jointed Lattice
abilities.desc: Your ward-bindings hold while allies move; the bound column keeps its full protection at any pace.

abilities.name: Cadence
abilities.desc: Set the column's pace; allies moving on your beat gain speed and cannot be slowed or rooted.

abilities.name: Rolling Rampart
abilities.desc: Project a ward-wall that walks with your front rank; enemies it passes over are shoved aside and slowed.

abilities.name: No One Straggles
abilities.desc: Stragglers and wounded are carried by the lattice itself, dragged gently along at the column's pace.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and walk a thousand refugees through a hostile province; arrive with a thousand.
Carry a warded column across a frozen river at night without once halting. The lattice must not notice the ice.
March your wards past a rooted Warden's post, and let the two doctrines regard each other in silence.
Sleep walking, mid-column, warded, and wake having lost no one. The order calls this ordinary. Make it so.

nodes.name: Anvilsworn
nodes.role: Elite attrition tank — absorption without reprisal
nodes.lore: The Anvilsworn read the same vindictive wards as the Requiters and drew the opposite law: a blow returned is a blow multiplied. They take everything and answer nothing, wards drinking violence until the attacker's arm, weapon, and conviction fail in that order. Requiters call them a heresy of waste. Fewer people strike Anvilsworn twice.
nodes.playstyle: Stand and receive: convert every blow into hardness, dull the weapons and the will that deliver them, and win when the enemy cannot lift his arms.

abilities.name: Hammer's Ruin
abilities.desc: Weapons striking your wards dull and crack; each blow against you permanently weakens the arm behind it.

abilities.name: Hammered In
abilities.desc: Absorb a blow completely and grow harder; each swallowed strike raises your damage reduction for the rest of the fight.

abilities.name: Patience of Iron
abilities.desc: While you decline to attack, your wards regenerate and everyone striking you suffers growing exhaustion.

abilities.name: Broken on the Anvil
abilities.desc: An enemy whose weapon or stamina breaks against your wards collapses, spent, and cannot attack you again this battle.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and stand a Requiter's full collection unanswered; when it is over, ask politely whether the order is satisfied.
Outlast a hundred hired strikers in a single day without lifting your blade; the order will count the broken hafts.
Strike the retaliation clauses from your own wards by your own hand, and learn how much of your strength was spite.
Take a blow from a friend sworn to test you, and charge them nothing for it, not even in your eyes.

nodes.name: The Neverdrawn
nodes.role: Mythic spell-execution — absolute magical denial
nodes.lore: Histories disagree whether The Neverdrawn is a rank or one recurring person. Where they walk, prophecy stalls, scrying returns yesterday, and the towers' oldest grimoires develop blank pages. The blade is no longer distinguishable from the intention. What they cut has, in every sense that can be verified, never been cast.
nodes.playstyle: Erasure as movement: spells die at the thought-stage in your presence; you duel entire schools of magic and edit outcomes retroactively.

abilities.name: Never Cast
abilities.desc: Undo a spell that already resolved this engagement; its effects, damage, and consequences are removed from record.

abilities.name: Never Written
abilities.desc: Erase one written work of magic permanently, everywhere — every copy, every memory of the wording.

abilities.name: The Quiet
abilities.desc: Your presence is a field where magic requires your consent; allies you name are exempt.

abilities.name: Final Parry
abilities.desc: Once, cut fate itself: cancel any single event you witness, at the cost of a memory of your choosing.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and unmake something a god maintains personally; survive the courtesy visit that follows.
Erase your own name from every archive, roll, and gravestone that holds it. What remains of you is the rank.
Stand where a prophecy says a hero dies, and see to it that the prophecy has never been written.
Sheathe the soaked edge for the last time. If the world still holds, you may draw it again.

nodes.name: The Final Stroke
nodes.role: Mythic striker — continent-spanning authored ruin
nodes.lore: The order speaks of a stroke that closes every sentence ever begun, and of the one who carries it unspent. The Final Stroke's runes are found on cliff faces, on the hulls of ships not yet sunk, in the flyleaves of books that later mattered. Nothing they have written has finished happening.
nodes.playstyle: Author at world scale: your marks accumulate across a lifetime and a continent, and combat is merely where you choose to punctuate.

abilities.name: A Lifetime's Marginalia
abilities.desc: Every rune you have ever written, anywhere, becomes available for detonation or revision from where you stand.

abilities.name: The Unfinished Sentence
abilities.desc: Begin a cut and refuse to finish it; the wound waits, worsening, until you complete the motion — even years later.

abilities.name: Corrigendum
abilities.desc: Rewrite one rune's effect after it detonates, applying the corrected version as well.

abilities.name: End Mark
abilities.desc: Write a single terminal rune on the world itself; within its radius, nothing you have marked survives the period.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and detonate, in one ordered breath, marks you left in twelve kingdoms across forty years.
Write a rune that alters the outcome of a war you never attended.
Compose the terminal stroke. Show it to no one. Carrying it unspent is the rank.
Refuse to finish a killing sentence once, and let history see the ellipsis.

nodes.name: The Held Gate
nodes.role: Mythic bastion — absolute immovability, sanctuary
nodes.lore: Some fortresses are named for a Warden who never left. The Held Gate has stopped being stationed anywhere; places are stationed around them. Armies reroute rather than test the ground they stand on, and maps mark their vigil the way they mark mountains. No chronicle records one falling. Chronicles record everything else falling first.
nodes.playstyle: You are the objective, and the objective cannot be taken: anchor reality around your vigil, shelter thousands, and outlast whatever arrives.

abilities.name: Terrain Entire
abilities.desc: You count as a fortress: allies inside your lattice gain walls, gates, and a garrison's worth of wards.

abilities.name: The Gate Holds
abilities.desc: Once per vigil, negate an army-scale attack completely — siege spell, dragonfire, tide, or god's regard.

abilities.name: Ground That Remembers
abilities.desc: Any ground you have defended before recognizes you; your wards there raise themselves at full strength instantly.

abilities.name: Open for No One
abilities.desc: While your vigil stands, nothing crosses your threshold without consent — including effects that ignore walls.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and hold one gap through a year of continuous siege; let the besiegers starve first.
Have a fortress renamed for you while you still stand in it.
Turn away a god politely at your threshold. The politeness is the test.
Choose the place you will never leave. The rank begins when the choice does.

nodes.name: The Iron Rebuke
nodes.role: Mythic retaliator — inevitable reciprocal ruin
nodes.lore: The order's ledgers end in a symbol meaning the balance now keeps itself. The Iron Rebuke is that symbol given a body. Harm done in their presence returns unbidden, the way weather returns. Tyrants have abdicated on rumor of an approach. Wars have been settled by asking which side they would find more owed.
nodes.playstyle: Do nothing, and be lethal: reflection is passive, total, and lawful. Your art is choosing what to forgive before the world repays itself.

abilities.name: Standing Verdict
abilities.desc: All harm dealt within your presence is automatically mirrored to its source; you no longer act to retaliate.

abilities.name: Debt Older Than You
abilities.desc: Invoke the full nine-generation ledger against one target whose line is named in it.

abilities.name: Amnesty
abilities.desc: Suspend the verdict for all within your sight; while it holds, no one can harm anyone.

abilities.name: Final Accounting
abilities.desc: Once in a lifetime, repay everything at once: every recorded debt of the order, discharged through your body in a single hour.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and end a war by arriving; let both sides read their ledgers and reconsider.
Forgive the debt you have carried longest. The order says the rank cannot be held with it.
Stand in a massacre and let the verdict work; touch no one, and be the only thing survivors agree on.
Outlive the order. Keep the ledgers anyway.

nodes.name: The Crowded Sheath
nodes.role: Mythic arsenal — an era's seized magic
nodes.lore: Archivists dispute the inventory; none dispute the weight. The Crowded Sheath carries every spell the order has seized in living memory — plagues of fire, unmakings, a god's stray sentence — all quiet in one blade. Treaties specify where they may stand. When the Sheath is drawn even an inch, weather changes allegiance.
nodes.playstyle: Fight with an era's confiscations: draw the right seizure for each moment, spend centuries of other people's power, and sheathe what the world cannot bear loose.

abilities.name: The Inventory
abilities.desc: Every spell the order has ever seized is available to you; casting one consumes its only copy.

abilities.name: An Inch of Daylight
abilities.desc: Draw the blade a finger's width; the leakage alone dispels, deafens, and staggers everything nearby.

abilities.name: Deed of Release
abilities.desc: Loose a seized cataclysm whole — plague, storm, or siege-spell — exactly as it was cast the day it was taken.

abilities.name: Peacebond
abilities.desc: Bind your own blade into its sheath before witnesses; while the bond holds, no seized spell can escape, and your wards double.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and inherit the armory entire: every seizure since the founding, sworn into one sheath at your hip.
Carry it a year without drawing. Cities will learn your itinerary and reroute their wars accordingly.
Draw once. From ten thousand seizures, choose the one spell that ends the day gently, and spend it.
Refuse the king who asks what you carry; refuse the god who asks after him.

nodes.name: The Sole Edition
nodes.role: Mythic striker — living archive, catastrophic recitation
nodes.lore: When the Vermillion School was burned — shelves, masters, and memory — one Illuminator had already taken the whole curriculum into her skin. The Sole Edition is that office: a person who is the last copy of a dead school. Wars have been declared to read them, and longer wars to keep them shut.
nodes.playstyle: Your body is a dead school's canon: recite chapters as devastation, spend pages you can never reprint, and decide daily what knowledge is worth your skin.

abilities.name: Chapter and Verse
abilities.desc: Read a chapter of yourself aloud; the dead school's magic resolves at the strength of its founders.

abilities.name: Out of Print
abilities.desc: Spend a page permanently to cast its spell at triple effect; nothing in the world can restore it.

abilities.name: Index of Scars
abilities.desc: You know instantly which of your pages answers a given enemy; the correct rune warms first.

abilities.name: Closed Canon
abilities.desc: While your text stays shut, you take reduced damage from every school inscribed in you.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and be the last: outlive your school, its rivals, and everyone qualified to check your citations.
Recite one chapter over a battlefield, and let both armies see what the burned masters could do.
Choose the page you will never spend, whatever it costs. An edition is defined by what it keeps.
Write one worthy page of your own into the canon before naming a successor. A school that cannot grow is only a tomb.

nodes.name: The Sheltered Mile
nodes.role: Mythic escort — moving sanctuary at nation scale
nodes.lore: Somewhere on the roads there is a mile that cannot be attacked, and it moves. The Sheltered Mile has walked whole cities out of falling kingdoms — the column entering the pass is the column leaving it, to the child. Armies petition to know the route. The route, chroniclers note, declines to exist in advance.
nodes.playstyle: Everything within your mile is home ground: thousands move as one warded body, terrain cooperates, and pursuit arrives to find the road already over.

abilities.name: The Mile
abilities.desc: A mile of road centered on you counts as fortress interior for everyone you shelter.

abilities.name: The Route Declines
abilities.desc: Your path cannot be scried, predicted, or ambushed; pursuers' maps disagree about where you have been.

abilities.name: Waystones
abilities.desc: Ground your column rests on stays warded forever after; your route becomes a chain of sanctuaries.

abilities.name: Bring Them All
abilities.desc: No one sheltered in the Mile can be singled out; harm aimed at one is spread across your wards entire.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and move a city that has already fallen: gates down, streets burning, every life still inside.
Outwalk a famine, a cavalry, and a winter in the same season, and deliver the column better fed than it left.
Let the Mile cross a battlefield mid-battle. Neither army must find anything to charge.
Never arrive. A Mile that ends somewhere is only a road; be mid-journey whenever the histories check.

nodes.name: The Quenched
nodes.role: Mythic bulwark — violence-ending absorption
nodes.lore: Smiths say a blade is finished when the quench stops singing. The Quenched has been struck by everything an age could raise — siege trains, hexes, a mountain, wronged gods — and answered none of it. Histories disagree whether they can still be harmed. The armies that tested the question are the reason histories disagree.
nodes.playstyle: Be the end of force: absorb anything once, harden against it forever, and stand until every weapon, spell, and intention raised against you dies of futility.

abilities.name: Struck Once
abilities.desc: Any specific attack that hits you cannot harm you again; your wards learn it permanently.

abilities.name: The Singing Stops
abilities.desc: Each round an enemy attacks you, their damage everywhere drops; at zero, they cannot raise arms against anyone today.

abilities.name: Mountain's Portion
abilities.desc: Take one army-scale blow per battle — siege engine, cataclysm, divine wrath — as though it were rain.

abilities.name: Nothing Left to Land
abilities.desc: Declare the violence spent: enemies whose every attack has failed against you this battle cannot attack again today.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and take a god's full blow standing, offering nothing in return but your continued attention.
Walk into the heart of a battle that has burned for three days, and stand until it goes out around you.
Outlast a siege alone as its sole objective; when the engines rust, walk out through the quiet.
Keep your blade. You will never draw it again, and it must be with you when you do not.

nodes.name: The Flyleaf
nodes.role: Apotheosis — absence of magic given office
nodes.lore: Every grimoire holds pages that were never written on. Scholars once called this binding waste. Now they leave offerings in the margins. The Flyleaf is where the Neverdrawn went when the name ran out: a rank that exists as absence, held by someone, presumably, whom no record can confirm and no spell can precede.
nodes.playstyle: Play the gap in the world's text: unhappen magic wholesale, exist beneath every record, and be findable only by those who need nothing found.

abilities.name: Margin of the World
abilities.desc: You exist in the unwritten parts of reality; effects that target names, fates, or records cannot find you.

abilities.name: Was Never
abilities.desc: Retire an entire school of magic from an engagement; for the battle's length, it has not been invented.

abilities.name: Nowhere Cited
abilities.desc: Allies walking beside you vanish from prophecy, scrying, and hostile memory until dawn.

abilities.name: The Courtesy Returned
abilities.desc: Once per age, a god who acts in your sight discovers the act has never been theirs.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and stop being mentioned — not forgotten, never known. Your deeds must continue happening regardless.
Leave one page blank in the world's oldest grimoire by standing near it. The tower will re-shelve the book as scripture.
Let a historian prove you do not exist. Attend the lecture. Applaud.
Hold the rank the way the page holds nothing: entirely.

nodes.name: The Maker's Mark
nodes.role: Apotheosis — endings authored as law
nodes.lore: At the end of every finished manuscript, scribes set a small mark meaning the work is done and someone made it. The Maker's Mark is that mark, seated in a person. Wherever anything truly ends — a war, a dynasty, a long grief — their stroke is found at the bottom, in a hand archivists have stopped pretending not to recognize.
nodes.playstyle: Write conclusions directly: end effects, eras, and enemies by signing them finished, and ration yourself, because everything you complete stays completed.

abilities.name: Here Ends
abilities.desc: Sign any ongoing effect — spell, curse, plague, siege — as finished; it concludes as though it had run its full course.

abilities.name: A Familiar Hand
abilities.desc: Enemies who find your mark on their fallen falter; each must rally or quit the field.

abilities.name: Fair Copy
abilities.desc: Once per day, restore the field to how it stood three breaths ago, keeping only the endings you authored.

abilities.name: The Unspent Stroke
abilities.desc: The terminal stroke may finally land: end one thing of any size, permanently, once. Choose slowly.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and finish something the gods left running on purpose. Sign it.
End a war, a famine, and a story in the same year, each with a single stroke, each leaving no body behind.
Find every work you left unfinished across your life and finish each one kindly. The rank accepts no outstanding sentences.
Write the colophon of an age and date it. Historians will argue for centuries, using your date to do so.

nodes.name: The Hinge of Heaven
nodes.role: Apotheosis — immovability as cosmic law
nodes.lore: Astronomers note that the sky turns around a single stubborn point, and admit, when pressed, that the point was not always there. The Hinge of Heaven is the Gate's vigil made cosmological: the one fixed thing, around which weather wheels, wars orbit, and every door that has ever held has quietly been hanging.
nodes.playstyle: Be the fixed point: nothing moves you, everything defended by anyone anywhere borrows your stillness, and the world arranges its sieges around your convenience.

abilities.name: Axis
abilities.desc: You cannot be moved, unmade, aged, or exiled; effects that attempt it rotate the world slightly instead.

abilities.name: Every Door Holds
abilities.desc: Bless all thresholds in a kingdom at once; while you stand vigil, none of them can be forced.

abilities.name: Borrowed Stillness
abilities.desc: Grant an ally your immovability for one blow; what strikes them finds you instead — and stops.

abilities.name: The Turning World
abilities.desc: Rather than approach an objective, remain: once per vigil, the world turns until the objective arrives before you.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and outstay your fortress: let the stones retire, the capital move, and keep the vigil the geography abandoned.
Hold the night together where two heavens collide; astronomers will record a new star. Let them name it wrongly.
Be the reason a returning army finds home standing when nothing else on the map is.
Choose stillness so completely that the world turns around it. You will know it has worked when north moves.

nodes.name: The Talion
nodes.role: Apotheosis — reciprocity as standing world-law
nodes.lore: Jurists in six kingdoms cite a law none of them passed: harm returns. The Talion is that statute, ambulatory. Where the Rebuke was a body the balance lived in, the Talion is the balance, wearing a body out of courtesy. Nothing owed escapes; nothing forgiven is reopened. Courts adjourn when they walk in.
nodes.playstyle: Preside rather than fight: harm within your jurisdiction returns at the moment of your choosing, mercy sets precedent, and your presence is due process.

abilities.name: Jurisdiction
abilities.desc: Your verdict covers a whole region; harm within it mirrors to its source at a moment you appoint.

abilities.name: Precedent
abilities.desc: Every mercy you grant becomes binding law; the forgiven act cannot be committed in your jurisdiction again.

abilities.name: Willful Breach
abilities.desc: Those who strike knowing the law take it back doubled; ignorance excuses the first blow only.

abilities.name: Standing Adjournment
abilities.desc: Suspend all violence in your presence indefinitely; battles in your jurisdiction must be argued instead.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and survive your own docket: every harm you ever dealt returns in one session, and you must preside.
Be cited as precedent by a court that does not believe you exist, and let the judgment stand.
Retire the ledgers you kept past the order's death. A law that still needs the written record is not yet you.
Hear the case brought against the world itself. Rule narrowly. Adjourn kindly.

nodes.name: The Scabbard of the World
nodes.role: Apotheosis — custodian of all ended magic
nodes.lore: When a spell dies anywhere — dispelled, unmade, its last caster gone — scholars now agree it goes somewhere, and have stopped publishing where. The Scabbard of the World is the office every ended magic retires into. The holder walks lightly for someone carrying that. Thieves' guilds maintain a standing rule: no.
nodes.playstyle: Carry everything magic has ever lost: draw dead spells from any age, lend them briefly, and be the reason unmaking is never quite the end.

abilities.name: All That Ended
abilities.desc: Draw any spell that has died from the world, cast it once, and return it to rest.

abilities.name: Brief Parole
abilities.desc: Release a dead spell into an ally's hands for one hour; it returns to you when spent.

abilities.name: Sheathe the Age
abilities.desc: Sheathe an active cataclysm as it happens; the storm, plague, or god-wrath simply retires into your keeping.

abilities.name: Nothing Is Lost
abilities.desc: Any magic destroyed in your presence vests in you instead; unmaking near you is merely a transfer of title.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and accept the escheat of ages: every spell that has ever ended, vested in your keeping.
Sheathe a falling cataclysm before witnesses, and file it correctly.
Be robbed by the finest thief alive, and let them find the scabbard holds only what consents to be held.
Answer, once, what you are keeping it all for. Answer honestly. Answer no one else.

nodes.name: The Apocrypha
nodes.role: Apotheosis — disputed canon, uncontainable technique
nodes.lore: The Sole Edition can die; the argument about what was in her cannot. The Apocrypha is that argument, given rank. Their techniques are cited in books that deny they exist, taught by tutors no college employs, recognized on battlefields by scholars who then recant. Every forbidden library keeps one shelf empty, just in case.
nodes.playstyle: Fight as a text that survived its burning: cast from chapters that officially never existed, and be impossible to censor, copy, or disprove.

abilities.name: Doubtful Attribution
abilities.desc: After any engagement, your presence in it becomes disputed; effects, curses, and vendettas anchored to your participation lapse.

abilities.name: Variant Reading
abilities.desc: Cast any spell of your dead school in a variant no counter was ever written for.

abilities.name: Burned and Extant
abilities.desc: When killed, you persist as the argument: return within a season, provably elsewhere the entire time.

abilities.name: One Empty Shelf
abilities.desc: Any library or archive you enter yields the forbidden chapter you need; it was always miscatalogued there.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and be burned in effigy, in archive, and in fact. Attend all three. Survive the reviews.
Have your finest technique condemned by a council that uses it in the field within the year.
Leave the last copy of yourself where no one will believe it: a child's primer, a laundry list, a treaty's margin.
Outlive your own refutation. The rank holds as long as the argument does; see that it continues.

nodes.name: The Drover's Star
nodes.role: Apotheosis — safe passage as celestial office
nodes.lore: Refugee columns steer by a star the old charts do not show, and arrive. Chartmakers mark it reluctantly; it will not hold still between editions. The Drover's Star is the Mile raised into the sky's business: an office of safe passage, held by someone who still walks below it, at the head of everyone.
nodes.playstyle: Shepherd at world scale: every column moving under your star is warded, every road you have walked stays kind, and pursuit forgets its reasons.

abilities.name: Under My Star
abilities.desc: Every column moving toward safety beneath your sky gains your lattice; distance raises no objection.

abilities.name: The Kind Roads
abilities.desc: Every road you have ever warded remains sanctuary forever; ambush, pursuit, and weather fail on them.

abilities.name: Setting Out
abilities.desc: However long the road, a column under your star reaches shelter by dawn; the miles simply behave.

abilities.name: No Pursuit
abilities.desc: Those hunting anyone under your protection lose the trail, then the orders, then the grievance.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and rise: let the columns below elect your vigil into the sky, and keep walking anyway.
Bring home a people whose home is gone, and have the place they arrive at agree to be it.
Be the star a fleeing enemy column steers by, and let them arrive too. The office does not check banners.
Accept that roads credit no one. The office pays in arrivals; keep the count, and tell no one the total.

nodes.name: The Dead Calm
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the weather that ends wars
nodes.lore: Sailors know the weather where wind refuses; soldiers know its cousin. Battles end when it arrives — not won, not lost, over. The Dead Calm is the Quenched made climate: the reason old battlefields stay quiet, the stillness violence retires into. Veterans feel it come and start folding their banners without orders.
nodes.playstyle: Arrive as weather: violence within your calm loses conviction, armies remember appointments elsewhere, and whatever must still be fought is fought gently and last.

abilities.name: The Calm Comes In
abilities.desc: Settle over a battlefield; all damage everywhere on it decays each round until nothing lands at all.

abilities.name: No Wind for War
abilities.desc: Siege engines, war-spells, and cavalry charges fail to start within your calm; what needs momentum finds none.

abilities.name: Old Fields
abilities.desc: On any ground where a battle has ever ended, you cannot be harmed; most ground qualifies by now.

abilities.name: The Weather Clears
abilities.desc: Declare a war spent; combatants on all sides find themselves unable to continue it, today or ever.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and end a century's war by weathering over it, leaving both anthems unsung and both harvests standing.
Visit every field where you were ever struck, and leave each one quiet enough to farm.
Be prayed to by both sides on the eve of a battle that, come morning, declines to occur.
Still your own last violence. The Calm begins at home; let the smiths finally stop arguing.

families.name: Witch
families.tagline: Power grown slow, cut fresh, and owed to no one.
families.description: The witch's power is a garden, not a grant: planted in hedgerows, brewed in kettles, buried under thresholds and dug up stronger. She learned no grammar and signed no compact — the craft is folklore, which works anyway. Villages fear her, consult her by the back door, and would riot if she left. Every remedy has its hour; every hex has its root.

nodes.name: Witch
nodes.role: Versatile caster — hexes, remedies, slow control
nodes.lore: Every village keeps one, at the lane's end where the hedge grows strange. She was somebody's apprentice once — swept the floor, learned which mushroom forgives and which does not. The craft came with the cottage: charms against fever, words for warts, a garden nobody robs twice. The parish disapproves of her weekly, and consults her nightly.
nodes.playstyle: Preparation and patience: brew beforehand, hex early, and let workings ripen mid-fight. Weak in a fair trade of blows, so never offer one.

abilities.name: Kettle Cure
abilities.desc: Brew a rough draught that restores health over a minute; its potency doubles if it was bottled before the fight began.

abilities.name: Small Spite
abilities.desc: Lay a minor curse that saps a target's next three attacks; it itches worse each time they mention it.

abilities.name: Rowan and Red Thread
abilities.desc: Knot a charm that turns aside the first blow aimed at its wearer in every fight.

abilities.name: Besom Line
abilities.desc: Sweep a threshold across the ground that spirits and strangers hesitate to cross; the first who does loses their footing.

progressionSteps: Be the child who watches where the old woman buries things, and have the sense not to dig.
Learn the garden's two rows: what mends taken at dawn, what kills taken at dusk, and that they are the same row.
Nurse one fever through a bad winter with nothing but what the hedge gave you.
Inherit the cottage, the kettle, and the visitors who knock at the back door after dark.

nodes.name: Wortcunner
nodes.role: Hybrid support — poisons and mending brews
nodes.lore: Wortcunners commit to the green half of the craft: simples, tinctures, and the exact hour a leaf turns from cure to killer. They keep gardens the parish calls kitchen plots and the knowing call arsenals. Farmwives fetch them for birthings; poisoners' victims fetch them after. Both leave payment on the same sill.
nodes.playstyle: Manage a satchel of brews with strict hours: dawn-picked heals, dusk-picked harms. Match the dose to the moment; the wrong hour helps the enemy.

abilities.name: Dawn Picking
abilities.desc: Salves from dawn-cut herbs mend allies over time and close bleeding wounds on the second application.

abilities.name: Dusk Picking
abilities.desc: The same herb, cut at dusk: coat a blade or a cup, and the target weakens with every passing hour.

abilities.name: Nightshade Measure
abilities.desc: Dose a target precisely — too little to kill, exactly enough that their strongest ability fails when they reach for it.

abilities.name: Stillroom Garden
abilities.desc: Plant a small standing garden on the field; allies who pluck from it receive your dawn brews, enemies your dusk ones.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10 and keep a garden whose every row can mend or murder, depending on the hour you cut it.
Sit a season with a dying herbalist and take dictation; the last page is yours when she no longer needs it.
Cure a poisoning you were once paid to arrange, and return the first fee.
Taste everything you grow, once, in the smallest measure; write down what you learn while your hands still obey.

nodes.name: Nightgoer
nodes.role: Pet-and-ritual caster — familiar synergy, shared rites
nodes.lore: Nightgoers have been fetched to their first meeting: a lantern at the crossroads, a round of strangers who all knew her name. The coven shares work the way farms share harvest — no grammar, no compacts, just many hands. Somewhere on the walk home, a small creature falls in step and does not leave.
nodes.playstyle: Never work alone: split labor with a fledgling familiar and draw on the round's pooled strength for slow, communal castings. Alone, you are half of something.

abilities.name: Fall In Step
abilities.desc: A small spirit in a borrowed body fights beside you; it is clumsy yet, but it harries one enemy and watches your back.

abilities.name: Round-Strength
abilities.desc: Channel the coven from afar: your next working casts as though three of you had spoken it.

abilities.name: Crossroads Lantern
abilities.desc: Set a lantern marking a meeting-ground; allies inside it share a portion of every heal any one of them receives.

abilities.name: By Night
abilities.desc: Travel unremarked between dusk and cockcrow; hostile eyes slide past you while you carry the coven's errands.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10 and answer the knock that comes at the dark of the month; bring nothing but your own name.
Dance the round widdershins and sunwise both, and mind which one your feet prefer; the coven minds too.
Share out a working among thirteen hands and take your thirteenth of the cost without complaint.
Walk home alone the long way, and greet politely whatever small thing chooses to walk with you.

nodes.name: Eyebiter
nodes.role: Ranged debuffer — wasting curses, slow kills
nodes.lore: Eyebiters specialize in the hex that takes root: a look over a fence, a name said backward, a wax figure sweating by the fire. Their curses are planted things — slow, seasonal, patient as bindweed. Assize courts acquit them regularly, there being no law against looking. Juries nonetheless prefer to convict someone else.
nodes.playstyle: Plant curses early and tend them: each hex ripens through stages if left uncleansed. Kill slowly, from ambush of time, and never twice the same way.

abilities.name: Overlook
abilities.desc: Bewitch whatever you can see from where you stand; the target's luck sours, and sour luck compounds daily.

abilities.name: Bindweed Hex
abilities.desc: Plant a curse that roots and spreads; each day untreated, it claims the strength of one more limb.

abilities.name: Poppet
abilities.desc: Bind a wax likeness to a target; harm done the doll arrives on the body, discreetly, at an hour of your choosing.

abilities.name: Said Backward
abilities.desc: Unsay a target's name in their hearing; their own wards mistake them for a stranger and briefly stand aside.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and grow one curse a full year, from seed-spite to harvest, without once touching your target.
Stand trial for witchcraft and be acquitted on the evidence; leave the jury certain and the record clean.
Learn the nine ways to say a name backward, and the one occasion proper to each.
Sour a strong man's luck so gently he blames the weather. Collect nothing. This one was practice.

nodes.name: Pellar
nodes.role: Healer — cures, cleanses, costly restorations
nodes.lore: Pellars are fetched when the curse is already in the walls: the herd dry, the child fading, the churn refusing butter. They unwitch — lift hexes, draw elf-shot, turn workings home — and they cure, though every pellar's cure has a price stated plainly at the door. Nothing mends for free. The good ones say so first.
nodes.playstyle: Diagnose, then trade: every cleanse and cure lands harder when its stated cost is paid up front. Triage is the whole art; charity is a dosage error.

abilities.name: Unwitching
abilities.desc: Lift any curse, hex, or ill-working from an ally; lifted workings do not vanish — they wait in your satchel.

abilities.name: Drawing the Shot
abilities.desc: Draw elf-shot, venom, or fever out through the skin as a small stone; keep the stones. They are useful later.

abilities.name: Stated Price
abilities.desc: Name a cure's cost aloud before casting; if the patient accepts, the healing cannot fail and cannot be dispelled.

abilities.name: Turning Home
abilities.desc: Send a curse back up its own root to whoever planted it, along with everything it learned on the way.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and lift a hex you cannot see from a child you cannot lose, and charge the family one hen.
Trace a curse to its planter across three parishes by the taste of the well-water alone.
Set a price you hate, once, and hold to it; a pellar who discounts is a pellar who lies.
Carry what you have drawn out of others until you learn where it can safely be put down. There is no such place. Carry it anyway.

nodes.name: Gyre-Carline
nodes.role: Group amplifier — shared power, ritual zones
nodes.lore: The gyre is the coven's turning round, and the carline is who calls it. The title means old woman and is conferred without regard to age or sex; the gyre does not care, and the villages find it simpler. A carline keeps the calendar of meetings, the tally of shared work, and the peace between thirteen strong opinions.
nodes.playstyle: Conduct group workings: pool allies' strength into single greater castings and share it back out as blessing. Keep the round turning under fire.

abilities.name: Call the Round
abilities.desc: Gather allies into a turning circle; while it holds, their smaller abilities are braided and cast as one greater working.

abilities.name: Thirteenth Share
abilities.desc: Divide a working's cost among every willing ally; divided costs lighten, and no one carries the whole.

abilities.name: Kept Calendar
abilities.desc: Rites cast on their proper night — full, dark, or quarter — hold a full night longer than they should.

abilities.name: Peace of the Round
abilities.desc: Enemies caught inside your circle must observe its courtesy: only one may act against you at a time.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and be handed the calendar by a carline who has watched you dance for seven years.
Hold the round steady through a working that fails; a circle that scatters once will scatter twice.
Settle a feud between two witches without losing either; the gyre turns on such hinges.
Learn every step of both turnings, sunwise and widdershins, well enough to teach the one you did not choose.

nodes.name: Impwife
nodes.role: Pet controller — spirit familiar, split attention
nodes.lore: Impwife is a trade name, like alewife: one who keeps spirits the way others keep bees. Her familiar is no pet and no servant — a bound colleague wearing a small warm body, paid in milk, blood, and civility. The arrangement is employment, not borrowing; she owes it wages, never herself.
nodes.playstyle: Fight as a firm of two: the familiar scouts, carries hexes, and works your will at distance while you hold the kettle steady.

abilities.name: Wages
abilities.desc: Feed your familiar a drop of blood; it works at double vigor until sunrise, and it remembers generosity.

abilities.name: Small Errand
abilities.desc: Send the familiar to deliver any touch-range working across the field; it travels low, quick, and unremarked.

abilities.name: The Small Watch
abilities.desc: See through your familiar's eyes at will; while you watch from there, your abandoned body keeps its wards doubled.

abilities.name: Civility
abilities.desc: A familiar treated well interposes once per fight, taking a killing blow in its small body and re-forming by dawn.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and keep one spirit fed, housed, and unresentful for a year and a day.
Learn its true errand-name, and never once use it to compel; compulsion is the lender's habit, not yours.
Negotiate its wages annually. Expect to lose the negotiation. Budget for this.
Sit up with it through its bad night, whatever a spirit's bad night is. Do not ask. Bring milk.

nodes.name: Overlooker
nodes.role: Single-target executioner — earned, measured dooms
nodes.lore: The Overlookers hold that a hex is a verdict, and verdicts must be earned. They look long before they look hard: weeks of watching, the wrong confirmed twice, the sentence measured to the crime and not a scruple past it. Blightsowers call them squeamish. Overlookers reply that frost has no jury, and they are not frost.
nodes.playstyle: Build a case against one target: observed wrongs become marks, marks become sentence. Devastating against the guilty; nearly harmless to the innocent, which is the point.

abilities.name: Long Watching
abilities.desc: Study a target to reveal their wrongs as marks; each mark deepens every hex you land on them.

abilities.name: Measured Doom
abilities.desc: Sentence a marked target: damage equal to the wrongs witnessed, delivered over as many nights.

abilities.name: Not One Scruple
abilities.desc: Your curses cannot spread, splash, or err onto bystanders; in exchange, the deserving cannot resist them.

abilities.name: Seen It Done
abilities.desc: Once per day, declare a wrong committed in your sight; every mark on its doer ripens at once.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and watch a bad man for a season without acting; act on the day the case is complete, not before.
Curse the guiltier of two brothers and be right. The order checks.
Refuse a rich commission because the target had not earned it; refuse the explanation too.
Stand a year under another Overlooker's watching, and give her nothing to sentence.

nodes.name: Ague-Eater
nodes.role: Tank-healer — absorbs every ailment into self
nodes.lore: Ague-Eaters end sickness by eating it: the fever crosses a shared cup and burns in the witch instead. Their order keeps its saints in bed and its funerals private.
