abilities.desc: You cannot be exiled, exposed, or caught in the open; every somewhere is a room under your beam.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and open a door in the last place everyone was certain was outdoors, and step in, not out.
Host the age's peace without once appearing in it, as before, as always.
Leave the Spare Room alone. It was there before the beam. This is the house's one humility; now it is yours.

nodes.name: The Truce of Teeth
nodes.role: Fear's covenant — one throat forsworn
nodes.lore: Every terror is born already knowing one throat it will not take. None can say whose; the knowledge simply has teeth of its own. This is the Truce of Teeth, older than the hood and the halter both, and it is not a law. It is a person, walking, and the agreement leaks generously onto whoever walks beside them.
nodes.playstyle: Walk untouchable through fear's whole kingdom; terrors guard you as the truce itself, those beside you inherit its shade, and breaking it is the one thing that frightens fear.

abilities.name: The Forsworn Throat
abilities.desc: No fear, terror, or nightmare can harm you; the prohibition is congenital and not negotiable.

abilities.name: Shade of the Truce
abilities.desc: Allies beside you are covered; terrors treat them as kin of the throat and hunt elsewhere.

abilities.name: What Frightens Fear
abilities.desc: Threaten the truce's breaking; every terror present will do anything asked to prevent it.

abilities.name: Born to the Glove
abilities.desc: Terrors newly made or summoned arrive already yours in the one way that matters; their maker learns this late.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and walk the deeps end to end unarmed, and be escorted, and pretend not to notice the escort.
Spend a season among the unbroken as neither hunter, prey, nor groom; the truce wants a witness, not a hand.
Never learn why it is you. The truce holds because nobody knows, and you are nobody's exception but its own.

nodes.name: The Pastoral
nodes.role: Season of fear — dread arrives survivable, forever
nodes.lore: Fear arrives in season now — small in spring, grazed close by harvest, resting after — and this is not nature. It is husbandry so old and total it reads as nature. The Pastoral is the arrangement itself: the office by which dread feeds without famine, forever, on schedule. Scholars still file the autumn dreams under weather. The filing is finally correct.
nodes.playstyle: Set the season of the battle; meter every heart's dread — enemies dosed toward collapse, allies kept fallow — and let the arrangement do the fighting.

abilities.name: In Season
abilities.desc: Declare the season; your enemies' fears mature on your schedule, all at once if you like.

abilities.name: Kept Fallow
abilities.desc: Allies' hearts lie fallow; nothing frightening takes root in them while your season stands.

abilities.name: The Arrangement
abilities.desc: Any fear anywhere feeding outside your rotation is trespassing; it is folded, fattened, and put to work.

abilities.name: Famine Withheld
abilities.desc: Once per battle, show one enemy the unhusbanded alternative — every fear at once, famine-sized, briefly.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and take all sleep everywhere onto the rotation, and let no one notice anything but easier winters.
Send the Quiet County a flock small enough to live with, and receive, in time, an empty tally-book as thanks.
Answer the child who asks why there are nightmares at all with the truth — so that there are never worse — then go check the fences.

families.name: Umbralist
families.tagline: Darkness is not absence; it is material, and it remembers.
families.description: Most people mistake darkness for absence — the room with the lamp out, the space behind the door. The Umbralist knows better: shadow is a material, older than light and more patient, and in trained hands it holds edges, bears weight, and remembers shapes. Rogues hide in the dark. An Umbralist puts it on the anvil and asks what it wants to be.

nodes.name: Umbralist
nodes.role: Hybrid conjurer — improvised shadow tools and arms
nodes.lore: Every city has a few: apprentices who noticed that the dark behind the woodpile pushed back. A first-rank Umbralist can chill a candle's shadow until it holds a shape — a hook, a cup, a clumsy knife. Neighbors call it a trick of the light. It is the opposite of that.
nodes.playstyle: Shape small tools and weapons from ambient shadow. Stronger near darkness, weaker at noon; carry your material with you and spend it deliberately.

abilities.name: Coldshaping
abilities.desc: Press ambient shadow between your palms until it takes a simple shape; the object lasts one minute or one use.

abilities.name: Lampwane
abilities.desc: Dim every light source nearby by half, gathering the difference as raw shadow-stuff in your hands.

abilities.name: Duskhide
abilities.desc: Harden the shadow you stand in into a hide across your skin, absorbing one blow before it flakes away.

abilities.name: First Heft
abilities.desc: Give a shadow weight enough to lean on; a plank, a step, a brace that holds until sunrise.

progressionSteps: Sit with an unlit room until you stop calling it empty.
Fold your own shadow three times against the grain; if it creases, you have the hands for this.
Carry water in a cup of shadow from the well to the door. Spill nothing. Tell no one.
Find a teacher who works after dark, or an after-dark that teaches; the guild insists there is a difference.

nodes.name: Duskwright
nodes.role: Melee conjurer — solid-shadow arms and barriers
nodes.lore: Duskwrights take the material seriously: they apprentice to it, keep its hours, learn what it will and will not bear. Their benches hold tongs no light has touched. Village smiths resent them slightly — a Duskwright's blade is folded from the unlit and never needs quenching, only night.
nodes.playstyle: Forge weapons, shields, and simple structures mid-fight. Everything you make is real while it lasts; managing durability and darkness is the whole craft.

abilities.name: Fold the Unlit
abilities.desc: Hammer ambient darkness into a one-handed weapon of your choosing; it keeps its edge until dawn touches it.

abilities.name: Shadow Tongs
abilities.desc: Extend a gripping hand of solid shadow that holds a foe, a beam, or a falling ally at ten paces.

abilities.name: Blackglass Buckler
abilities.desc: Raise a small shield of hardened dusk; it shatters after three blocks into blinding slivers of dark.

abilities.name: Journeyman's Gloom
abilities.desc: Store a pocket of worked shadow in your coat; draw it later as raw material where light leaves none.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10 and forge one object of solid shadow that survives a full noon in the open.
Serve a season at the guild bench, working only by the light you have failed to remove.
Break your first three blades learning that shadow folded against its grain holds grudges.
Present a masterpiece the examiners can hold: weight, edge, and no apologies.

nodes.name: Penumbrant
nodes.role: Skirmish controller — passage and thinned presence
nodes.lore: Penumbrants stop treating shadow as stock and start treating it as a door left open. They learn to lean into darkness the way swimmers lean into rivers — first a hand, then the wrist, then whole minutes spent as something thin against a wall. Their families notice the candles burning brighter.
nodes.playstyle: Slip through connected darkness and thin your body against harm. High mobility, low durability in light; you control range by controlling where dark is.

abilities.name: Through the Unlit
abilities.desc: Enter one shadow and leave by another within sight; the dark between counts you as itself.

abilities.name: Go Thin
abilities.desc: Flatten your body to a hand's depth of dusk for three seconds; blades pass through what is barely there.

abilities.name: Second Silhouette
abilities.desc: Peel your shadow upright to stand watch or take a blow meant for you; it reforms at your heel by dusk.

abilities.name: Dimmet Sense
abilities.desc: Know the position of every shadow deep enough to admit you within a hundred paces.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10 and put your arm into a shadow to the shoulder, then bring it back still yours.
Spend a night as the stain beside the wardrobe in a room where someone is dying. Touch nothing. Learn what the dark is for.
Cross a guarded bridge by the shadow under it, and leave the guards their pride.
Return fully. The guild examines the edges of you for fraying, and passes what it can still count.

nodes.name: Gloamsmith
nodes.role: Weapon conjurer — arms for self and allies
nodes.lore: Gloamsmiths make arms and nothing else, and make them the way cathedrals were built: to specification, to outlast doubt. A Gloamsmith's sword weighs what conviction weighs; their spears fly true in pitch blackness because the dark recognizes its own work. Armies quarter them well back and ask nicely.
nodes.playstyle: Forge and hurl weapons of hardened gloam, and arm allies with edges of dark. Damage scales with ambient darkness and with your patience between forgings.

abilities.name: Gloamsteel
abilities.desc: Temper shadow into a weapon a full rank finer than any you could carry here; it dissolves if it leaves your sight.

abilities.name: Nail of Night
abilities.desc: Drive a spike of compacted dark through armor; the wound stays cold and refuses light-based healing.

abilities.name: Rack of Dusk
abilities.desc: Stand seven shadow-weapons upright in the earth around you; allies who draw one fight with your craft for a minute.

abilities.name: Evening Whet
abilities.desc: Sharpen an existing blade against raw shadow; it cuts through shields for ten strikes, leaving unlit grooves.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and forge a blade of gloam that a stranger, blindfolded, cannot tell from steel until it sings.
Arm a hopeless garrison with shadow and stay through the siege to maintain the edges.
Refuse a king's commission once, politely, to learn what your work is worth.
Quench nothing for a year. The dark tempers by patience, and so will you.

nodes.name: Murkmason
nodes.role: Battlefield architect — walls, spans, and cover
nodes.lore: Murkmasons build. Bridges over gorges no quarry could span, stairs up sheer cliff-dark, barracks pitched in an hour from the shade of a standing army. Their guild-mark is a keystone with no arch, because the arch is night itself. Engineers hate them; sappers hate them considerably more.
nodes.playstyle: Raise cover, spans, and chokepoints from massed shadow. You win by making the ground argue for your side; direct damage is someone else's trade.

abilities.name: Mortarless
abilities.desc: Raise a wall of set shadow along a line you walk; it stands until dawn or demolition, whichever is ruder.

abilities.name: Gloomspan
abilities.desc: Throw a bridge of solid dusk across any gap you can see both sides of; it bears a column of cavalry.

abilities.name: Bastion Shade
abilities.desc: Pitch an instant redoubt around allies: crenellated, roofed, and dark enough inside to rearm your whole craft.

abilities.name: Undershoring
abilities.desc: Brace a failing structure — or a collapsing morale line — with columns of night that refuse, on principle, to buckle.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and bridge the Grey Gorge at midnight with shadow; walk across last, carrying the lantern.
Build a poorhouse of night in a city that outlawed you, and leave it standing when they repeal.
Hold your wall against a sapper company until they submit their resignation to the dark.
Set one keystone of pure unlit in a daylight arch, where the guild can check your nerve.

nodes.name: Nightswimmer
nodes.role: Mobile flanker — repositions self and allies
nodes.lore: Nightswimmers hold that all darkness is one water: the shadow of a cradle touches the dark under mountains, and a trained body can swim the distance between. They surface where they are needed, dripping dusk. Harbor towns keep a lamp unlit at the pier for them, the way others keep one burning.
nodes.playstyle: Dive through connected shadow to flank, carry allies short distances, and drag enemies under. Range grows with darkness; noon beaches you.

abilities.name: Deep Stroke
abilities.desc: Swim the dark between two shadows within a hundred paces, surfacing with momentum your first blow spends.

abilities.name: Drag Under
abilities.desc: Pull one enemy waist-deep into their own shadow for four seconds; they can shout, and usually do.

abilities.name: Wake of Dusk
abilities.desc: Leave a trailing current of dark behind you; allies who follow it move as fast as rumor.

abilities.name: Surface Tension
abilities.desc: The film between light and dark hardens at your word: nothing else enters or leaves shadow nearby for six seconds.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and swim from your own shadow to the far bank of the Sorrows in one held breath of dark.
Carry a stranger through the dark without losing them; the guild counts arrivals, not departures.
Map a shadow-road no one has survived, and post the depths where swimmers pray.
Learn where not to swim. Something older keeps the deepest dark, and courtesy is survival.

nodes.name: Shadeworn
nodes.role: Evasion tank — thinned, persistent, hard to hold
nodes.lore: The Shadeworn have been worn thin by passage, and made the thinness a discipline. Daylight finds less of them each year to press on: scars gone grey, footprints optional, a silhouette that arrives a little before they do. They stand in shield-lines as gaps that bite. Spears find wall instead.
nodes.playstyle: Hold ground by being barely there: attacks slide through your thinned self while your unlit hands stay solid enough to answer.

abilities.name: Worn Thin
abilities.desc: Passive: a portion of every blow passes through you and hits nothing; the portion grows as light dims.

abilities.name: Solid on One Side
abilities.desc: Your strikes are matter and their answers are not, for five seconds; duelists file complaints posthumously.

abilities.name: Become the Stain
abilities.desc: Flatten against any surface as a stain; you cannot act or be harmed, and you hear everything the wall does.

abilities.name: Grey Increment
abilities.desc: Each wound you ignore thins you further: harder to hit, lighter of step, one shade closer to the wall.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and let a firing line volley through you at dusk; sign the report they file in disbelief.
Fast from light one full winter, taking sun only through curtains, until your shadow forgets which of you is which.
Hold a breach as the thin place in it. What passes through you must be permitted first.
Keep one solid thing — a hand, a habit, a name — and defend it. The rank is for those who stop thinning on purpose.

nodes.name: Nightanvil
nodes.role: Arsenal artillery — persistent conjured armaments
nodes.lore: The Nightanvils number their works and expect them found in barrows a thousand years on. Shadow, they hold, is the one metal that never rusts — fix it once, correctly, and you have armed the future. Their vault-forges open only at new moon. Each smith's masterwork is entered against their name, permanently.
nodes.playstyle: Build a persistent arsenal across engagements: standing weapons, mounted engines, armed allies. Slow to start, compounding forever; your old work fights beside your new.

abilities.name: Fixed in the Dark
abilities.desc: Your conjured weapons no longer expire; each battlefield keeps what you forged there, loyal to your banner.

abilities.name: Moonless Temper
abilities.desc: Quench a weapon in true moonless night; it gains an edge that ignores armor forged in daylight.

abilities.name: Ballista of the Vault
abilities.desc: Assemble a siege engine of set shadow over ten seconds; it fires spears of night until dismantled by dawn or axes.

abilities.name: Numbered Work
abilities.desc: Speak the catalogue number of anything you ever forged; it flies to your hand from wherever the years shelved it.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and forge a work you will never see finished cooling; the vault tempers by decades.
Recover Work Nine from the barrow that stole it, and apologize to the blade for the wait.
Arm your own funeral guard in advance; the order considers this ordinary prudence.
Debate a Quickshade before the assembled forges and do not raise your voice; permanence does not hurry.

nodes.name: Evening Spanwright
nodes.role: Logistics support — spans, roads, mass movement
nodes.lore: The Causewrights build with borrowed shade — the honest dark that towers and mountains lend at evening — and return every plank of it by dawn. Their spans have carried harvests, armies, and one entire fleeing city. The lending, they insist, is the craft: darkness trusts those who give it back.
nodes.playstyle: Move whole formations: causeways, ramps, gates of dusk. Your works expire at dawn by design, so schedule the war accordingly.

abilities.name: Borrowed Span
abilities.desc: Lift a mountain's evening shadow into a causeway; it bears any weight that intends to cross, and no weight that intends to hold it.

abilities.name: Dusk Gate
abilities.desc: Stand two shadows upright as posts; for a minute, entering one is leaving the other, luggage included.

abilities.name: Return by Dawn
abilities.desc: Dismiss all your standing works at once; enemies on them are returned to the ground, from their current altitude.

abilities.name: Evening Freight
abilities.desc: Sink supplies into a shadow at dusk and appoint the shadow where they surface; quartermasters weep with relief.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and carry a fleeing city across a strait on borrowed shade, and return every shadow unbruised by dawn.
Note what you borrow and from whom; a Causewright who forgets a mountain's name builds no more.
Build one span for no one, somewhere remote and beautiful, and let dawn take it unseen; the guild calls this the true examination.
Refuse to build a bridge meant to burn; the dark is a lender, not an accomplice.

nodes.name: Nightporter
nodes.role: Mass transporter — carries companies through darkness
nodes.lore: Nightporters carry: refugees, regiments, grain in famine years, once a hospital with its lamps still lit. The one dark is their warehouse and every shadow a loading door. They are sworn to deliver whatever they lift, which is why they lift so carefully. Bandits avoid harming them; everyone eventually needs porting.
nodes.playstyle: Reposition allies at company scale through connected shadow. You are the supply line, the retreat, and the flanking maneuver; guard your own candle accordingly.

abilities.name: Loading Dark
abilities.desc: Open a shadow as a freight door; allies and cargo step through to any dark you have personally stood in.

abilities.name: Handed Through
abilities.desc: Pass one ally through the dark mid-blow; the blow arrives punctually at where they no longer are.

abilities.name: Convoy of Dusk
abilities.desc: Chain up to twenty travelers behind you through the deep dark; none may let go, and none ever has.

abilities.name: Night Freight
abilities.desc: Once per night, carry something impossible — a wall, a ship, a wounded giant — one shadow closer to where it must be.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and carry a hundred strangers through the one dark in a single night, and count the same hundred out.
Deliver to an address that no longer exists; the dark remembers where it was.
Refuse to port a weapon aimed at those you carried; the oath has teeth, and they are yours.
Meet what keeps the deepest dark, and be found polite; the guild has no advice beyond this.

nodes.name: Evenstain
nodes.role: Elusive attrition — flattened presence, creeping harm
nodes.lore: Evenstains perfected the wall. They live flattened by preference — a discoloration in the plaster, a long shadow with no owner on file — and armies break on rooms that hate them. Where an Evenstain has soaked in, iron dulls, torches gutter, and courage develops a draft. Scrubbing, famously, spreads them.
nodes.playstyle: Soak into surfaces and let the field sicken around you: auras of dulling, guttering, and dread. Nearly unkillable, never fast; patience is the weapon.

abilities.name: Soak In
abilities.desc: Merge with floor, wall, or standing dark across a wide area; while soaked, you are terrain, and terrain is angry.

abilities.name: Dull the Edges
abilities.desc: Every weapon inside your stain loses its temper — the metallurgical kind first, the other kind shortly after.

abilities.name: Drink the Torchlight
abilities.desc: Torches, lanterns, and lesser suns within the stain dim to embers, feeding your spread.

abilities.name: Setting Stain
abilities.desc: Enemies who linger in your area carry a patch of you when they leave, dulled and dimming, until true noon scours it.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and hold a fortress alone by soaking into it; accept the garrison's surrender through the walls.
Be painted over, plastered, and consecrated against, and remain; the order accepts the parish's complaint as your credential.
Spread across a battlefield by dusk and be its weather by midnight.
Contract to a single drop once a year, to prove you still can; vanity is for the solid.

nodes.name: Quickshade
nodes.role: Reactive duelist — improvised arms each instant
nodes.lore: Quickshades hold that a fixed shadow is a stuffed hawk: accurate, and dead. Shadow lives in the moment of casting, so the weapon must be born mid-stroke — blade for this parry, hammer for this door, gone before gratitude. They own nothing, sign nothing, and beat Nightanvils in every duel either order admits to.
nodes.playstyle: Conjure the exactly right weapon each beat and discard it spent. Enormous versatility, nothing persistent; your power resets to zero and doesn't mind.

abilities.name: Born Drawn
abilities.desc: Every attack you make is a new weapon, shaped mid-swing to whatever the target's guard forgot to expect.

abilities.name: The Correct Tool
abilities.desc: Instantly counter a weapon by conjuring its one bad match-up; the dark has opinions about every armory.

abilities.name: Unburdened
abilities.desc: You move faster for each thing you are not carrying; a true Quickshade blurs.

abilities.name: Let Go
abilities.desc: Release a conjured weapon mid-arc to burst into night; blinding, brief, and impossible to parry twice.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and empty your hands for good; the order's initiation confiscates everything, including sentiment.
Win a smiths' fair with a blade that no longer exists by the judging.
Fight one battle armed only with what each second offers, and want for nothing.
Hold a dying friend with hands and no hilt in them, and learn why the order keeps nothing that can be lost.

nodes.name: Pitchmason
nodes.role: Fortress controller — permanent bastions of first dark
nodes.lore: Pitchmasons kept the guild name and abandoned the guild manners. They quarry the First Dark — the unlit that was never cast by anything, older than dawn — and what they build with it does not come down. Causewrights call them tomb-makers. Pitchmasons reply that someone must build for the nights with no morning after.
nodes.playstyle: Erect permanent fortifications of never-cast dark: keeps, ring-walls, cells. Immensely durable, utterly immobile; you win sieges by having already won them.

abilities.name: First Quarry
abilities.desc: Cut a block of the dark from before dawn existed; structures built of it ignore sunlight, sappers, and centuries.

abilities.name: Ringwall Pitch
abilities.desc: Raise a circling wall of set pitch-dark around a position; it has no gate, which the order considers a feature.

abilities.name: Undervault
abilities.desc: Open a cell of solid dark beneath one enemy; it closes over them gently and opens for no argument but yours.

abilities.name: Nightfooting
abilities.desc: Found your works on the dark under the world; nothing built on it can be undermined, by shovel or by doubt.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and descend to where the dark was never cast; quarry one block and carry it up the long stair alone.
Build a keep with no door and live in it a year; visitors will find the lesson instructive.
Let a Causewright inspect your walls and say tomb aloud; thank them, and point out that it is empty.
Stand your masterwork against dawn itself: if sunrise moves one shadow of it, begin again.

nodes.name: Gloamhasp
nodes.role: Anti-passage warden — seals shadow against traffic
nodes.lore: The Gloamhasps hold that every passage wounds the dark and every wound lets something look through. They shut what swimmers open: hasping shadows closed, standing watch inside the medium itself, dragging trespassers out by the collar regardless of errand. Nightporters call them jailers of a country nobody owns. Hasps reply: exactly.
nodes.playstyle: Deny movement: seal shadows, cancel teleports and shadow-passage, and hold the dark as guarded ground. You are the wall inside the medium.

abilities.name: Hasp the Dark
abilities.desc: Seal every shadow in a wide radius against entry and exit; the seals hold until dawn or your death.

abilities.name: Collar the Swimmer
abilities.desc: Reach into any shadow-passage in progress and haul the traveler out at your feet, itinerary cancelled.

abilities.name: Stitched Shut
abilities.desc: Sew two shadows together so neither admits anyone; the thread is visible only to those it disappoints.

abilities.name: Inward Bolt
abilities.desc: Bolt yourself inside the medium; while you keep watch there, nothing else may so much as thin.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and seal one city's every shadow for a night; let the morning count what failed to arrive.
Catch a Nightporter mid-carry and escort them out with their cargo intact; the rivalry has manners.
Stand watch inside the dark for a season and log what pressed against the far side; submit the log sealed.
Close one passage forever. You will know which one when it asks you not to.

nodes.name: Nightbrace
nodes.role: Immovable tank — dense shadow, load-bearing bulk
nodes.lore: The Caryatids took the opposite lesson: if shadow bears weight, become the weight it bears. They pack their unlit selves denser than basalt — person-shaped night that floors complain about — and stand where collapse is scheduled. Temples hire them as pillars during earthquakes. Evenstains call them furniture. The furniture outlasts the argument.
nodes.playstyle: Anchor the line as compacted night: taunt, absorb, and hold up whatever is falling — ceilings, gates, morale. Slowest thing on the field, and the last.

abilities.name: Compaction
abilities.desc: Pack your shadow-self denser each second you stand still; damage reduction and weight climb without ceiling.

abilities.name: Take the Roof
abilities.desc: Catch any collapsing structure or descending blow on your shoulders; it stays caught until you decide otherwise.

abilities.name: Basalt Habit
abilities.desc: You cannot be moved, thrown, or knocked down while you can see something worth holding up.

abilities.name: Let It All Down
abilities.desc: Release every stone of gathered weight in one stamp; the field staggers, and you are briefly, dangerously light.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and stand under a temple roof through the earthquake; when it ends, be the reason it didn't.
Gain a hundredweight of night each season for a year, and give none of it back.
Be mistaken for statuary by an occupying army, and choose the moment to disagree.
Hold something no one asked you to hold, forever. The order's founder is still under the mountain, and the mountain is grateful.

nodes.name: The Nightforge
nodes.role: Mythic armorer — arsenal at army scale
nodes.lore: Histories agree the Nightforge exists and agree on little else. An armory with a pulse; a smith who is also the smithy; the place all shadow goes to be given purpose. Kingdoms that found one wintering in a barn have retroactively declared the barn a citadel. Its works turn up centuries early.
nodes.playstyle: Arm everything: allies, militias, the ground itself. Your body is a working forge; standing near you upgrades steel and resolve alike.

abilities.name: Open Forge
abilities.desc: Allies who touch you draw a masterwork of night suited exactly to their need, discovered rather than requested.

abilities.name: All Night Ringing
abilities.desc: Your forge works while you fight: every ten seconds, a finished weapon rises from your shadow and picks an ally.

abilities.name: Arm the Field
abilities.desc: Edge every shadow on the battlefield; enemy footing becomes a matter for surgeons.

abilities.name: Centuries Early
abilities.desc: Draw a legendary work you have not forged yet; the future files no objection it can enforce.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and take the vault-forge into yourself: every numbered work, every bench, the dark between them. Inventory hereafter is introspection.
Arm a war on both sides with work so fine the war is called off for appraisal.
Forge one thing shadow was never meant to hold — a bell's note, a promise — and shelve it unnumbered.
Let the guild stop naming you smith. Smithies are places; be one.

nodes.name: The Evening Road
nodes.role: Strategic mobility — army-scale roads of dusk
nodes.lore: Somewhere between sunset and true dark there is a road, and histories cannot agree where it has been. Down it, granaries reach famines and reinforcements arrive the night before the histories say they could have. It lends itself only whole: take the Evening Road, and every traveler on it that night travels with you.
nodes.playstyle: Redeploy armies nightly across any distance. Your presence is infrastructure; battles are won by who you deliver, rested, where they were impossible.

abilities.name: Nightly Alignment
abilities.desc: Each dusk, declare where the Road runs; any friendly force that marches into shadow marches out at your destination.

abilities.name: Waystation Dark
abilities.desc: Plant rest-houses along your span; allies passing through shed exhaustion, wounds, and up to one regret.

abilities.name: The Road Rises
abilities.desc: Lift your span above ambush height; what happens on the Road is between the Road and the sky.

abilities.name: Wrong Exit
abilities.desc: Enemy columns that force their way onto your dark exit where you prefer, which is rarely where they were going.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and lay a road from the war to the harvest and back, and let both arrive in time.
Carry a beaten army home by dusk-roads so gently that its ballads survive; defeat travels, too.
Be declared impossible by three royal surveys and keep your schedule.
Return the last shadow you ever borrowed better than lent: a cooler evening, earlier stars.

nodes.name: The Open Dark
nodes.role: Rescue support — extraction anywhere night touches
nodes.lore: While an Open Dark lives, no massacre is airtight. Cellars breathe. Locked holds arrive empty at port, their cargo walking free three kingdoms away with bread in hand. Histories dispute whether it is one person or a relay of them; the rescued dispute nothing, and light candles facing away from the window.
nodes.playstyle: Extract anyone from anywhere the dark reaches, at growing scale. Weak in a stand-up fight; the fight standing up is your cue to leave with everyone.

abilities.name: Nowhere Is Sealed
abilities.desc: Any dark large enough for a hand is a gate you may operate from either side.

abilities.name: Exodus Stroke
abilities.desc: Swim an entire crowd through the one dark in a single held breath; head-counts match, always.

abilities.name: The Bread Rule
abilities.desc: Everyone you extract arrives fed, shod, and unpursued for a day; the dark provisions its guests.

abilities.name: Kept Open
abilities.desc: Designate one shadow permanently passable to a person you name; heirs inherit the privilege, which has started dynasties.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and empty a prison the size of a province in one night; alphabetize nothing, free everything.
Be in two rescues at once and let the theologians divide you; they need the exercise.
Leave every dark you pass through wider than you found it.
Teach the dark to do it without you once; retirement is a rumor you will deserve.

nodes.name: The Unlit
nodes.role: Untargetable attrition — presence without substance
nodes.lore: Thinning has a far shore, and the Unlit have waded past it. What remains is authored absence: a figure present in every under-lit room at once, thin as the difference between shut eyes and dark. Histories dispute whether the Unlit persist or merely recur. Rooms they favor stay favored for centuries.
nodes.playstyle: Exist as ambient dark: unhittable, everywhere shade is, wearing enemies down by increments they only notice in aggregate. Light is your one appointment.

abilities.name: Ubiquity of Shade
abilities.desc: Occupy all shadow in the region simultaneously; area attacks hit a fraction of you, which forgives nothing.

abilities.name: Increment
abilities.desc: Each second an enemy spends in any shade, they are slightly less: slower, dimmer, more agreeable.

abilities.name: Absence of Address
abilities.desc: Targeted effects require a location; you have stopped keeping one.

abilities.name: Recur
abilities.desc: If destroyed, you happen again at the next nightfall, minus one memory you volunteer.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and be nowhere in particular for a year without missing an engagement.
Attend your own memorial as its poor lighting; leave before the eulogy improves.
Thin until the dark stops noticing where you end, then keep the one solid habit you swore at twenty-five.
Answer, when the wall is asked whether it is you: sometimes.

nodes.name: The Eclipse
nodes.role: Burst conjurer — total armament from nothing
nodes.lore: Night falls gradually, except where it doesn't. The Eclipse is the exception with a name: a person who arrives as a dusk with no evening before it, armed in the instant with everything the moment requires. Chroniclers dispute each sighting, since witnesses report only that it was bright, and then it was decided.
nodes.playstyle: Do nothing, then everything: no sustained damage, only complete instants in which you are every weapon at once. Timing is the entire class.

abilities.name: Noon Interrupted
abilities.desc: Drop instant midnight over the field for six seconds; within it, your improvisation has no upper bound.

abilities.name: Everything at Once
abilities.desc: For one second, conjure simultaneously every weapon the fight has made you imagine; each finds its own argument.

abilities.name: No Evening Before
abilities.desc: Your arrivals cannot be foreseen by scrying, scheduling, or instinct; even prophecy files you under weather.

abilities.name: Decided
abilities.desc: The engagement's loudest threat is disarmed, unhorsed, and seated, in that order, faster than the eye files grievances.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and fall on a battle as night falls on a candle: once, entirely, and without preamble.
Be three sightings in three provinces in one hour, and let the chroniclers ruin each other.
Decline to exist between engagements; the order's roll lists you as pending.
Arrive, once, before you were needed instead of when — and learn to apologize for the only mistake you make.

nodes.name: The Sunless Keep
nodes.role: Living fortress — bastion of the first dark
nodes.lore: Sieges have a word for the wall that does not fall, and the word has an address. The Sunless Keep is a Pitchmason who finished the last wall from inside: a fortress with a temper, quarried entirely from the First Dark. Three empires list it as terrain. Refugees list it as mercy with battlements.
nodes.playstyle: Be the objective: garrison allies inside your dark and break assaults on walls that predate dawn. You relocate rarely, and always overnight.

abilities.name: Let In
abilities.desc: Your walls admit the hunted from any shadow they flee through; their pursuers meet the masonry's other opinion.

abilities.name: Curtain of First Dark
abilities.desc: Your outer wall predates light; projectiles, spells, and dawns break on it in that order of embarrassment.

abilities.name: Sortie of Pillars
abilities.desc: March your walls outward course by course until the siege discovers it is indoors, where the rules are yours.

abilities.name: No Morning Inside
abilities.desc: Within you it is always the hour you choose; garrisons rest, wounds wait, and stores never spoil.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and mortar yourself into your masterwork as its final block; the guild sends flowers and a chisel, as tradition requires.
Outlast a siege so long the besiegers' descendants apply for citizenship; grant it.
Shelter something the whole daylight world wants dead, and win the correspondence.
Grow one new wing per century, and never explain the floor plan.

nodes.name: The Shut Night
nodes.role: Absolute denial — nothing crosses the dark
nodes.lore: Some nights nothing moves — no couriers, no armies, no things between walls — and veterans check the calendar for a Shut Night's passage. The office is disputed by every history and respected by every smuggler: one warden, sworn inward, against whom the whole traffic of darkness files and fails. The dark sleeps soundly those years.
nodes.playstyle: Lock the entire medium: no shadow-travel, no summons through dark, no reinforcements after dusk. You barely fight; you make the night a held breath.

abilities.name: The Night Is Shut
abilities.desc: Declare darkness closed across the region; every passage, gate, and summoning that routes through shadow is refused.

abilities.name: One Warden Wide
abilities.desc: You occupy the whole medium at once; anything entering the dark anywhere finds you already there, unamused.

abilities.name: Evicted Whole
abilities.desc: Expel every foreign presence from the dark simultaneously; they surface where they entered, however long ago that was.

abilities.name: The Far Side Waits
abilities.desc: The things beyond the dark cannot press through while you hold; they wait, and you feel them waiting.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and hold a continent's darkness shut for a year of nights; every history will blame the weather, correctly.
Refuse an emperor's convoy and an orphan's escape in the same hour, and stay whole; the office is a door that does not choose.
Learn each thing that waits outside by the pattern of its patience; name none of them aloud.
Open, once, for one reason you will keep to yourself, and shut again before the histories notice; even the office blinks.

nodes.name: The Black Plinth
nodes.role: Immovable anchor — the field's fixed point
nodes.lore: Every age has a weight it cannot set down, and hires accordingly. The Black Plinth is compaction ended in myth: a figure of night dense enough to anchor bridges, treaties, and the occasional mountain that had plans. Armies break formation around it like water. Nothing it has agreed to hold has ever fallen.
nodes.playstyle: Be the fulcrum: absolute immovability, gravitational threat, and the power to declare things held. The war bends around where you decided to stand.

abilities.name: Declared Held
abilities.desc: Name a structure, line, or promise held; it cannot break while you stand, and you are still standing.

abilities.name: Nightmass
abilities.desc: Your density bends the fight: projectiles curve to you, charges arrive exhausted, and orbits form among the reckless.

abilities.name: Underbear
abilities.desc: Slide beneath any falling thing — citadel, glacier, dynasty — and receive it; setting it back is a separate negotiation.

abilities.name: The Field Parts
abilities.desc: Enemy formations part around you and lose each other; cohesion is for battlefields without a Plinth.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and relieve the founder under the mountain; carry their watch until another Caryatid grows patient enough.
Anchor a peace treaty by standing on it — literally, in the square, for a decade.
Let sculptors finish you; wear the pigeons with grace.
Decline to move for a god. Cite precedent.

nodes.name: The Tempered Night
nodes.role: Cosmic armorer — night itself bears your edge
nodes.lore: Smiths temper metal; something must temper the dark, or it would arrive soft. The Tempered Night is that office: since its founding, every shadow has held its shape, every night has borne weight somewhere, and winter dark has come down harder than summer's. Smiths' guilds keep a cold anvil for it, faced away from the hearth.
nodes.playstyle: Work at world-scale: the night is your stock, dawn your deadline, and every dark thing anywhere sharpens when you attend to your trade.

abilities.name: Universal Temper
abilities.desc: Every shadow on the field is your finished work: edged, load-bearing, and loyal to your side of the argument.

abilities.name: Dawn Deadline
abilities.desc: Whatever you forge before sunrise is permanent; the sun has learned not to inspect your bench.

abilities.name: Winter Issue
abilities.desc: Arm an entire front from one long night; the equipment is standard, the standard is yours.

abilities.name: The Cold Anvil
abilities.desc: Strike the night itself once; everything forged of shadow anywhere rings, and its bearers know who made them.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and take the apprenticeship the dark offers you in return: it has been watching your hands for sixty years.
Temper one whole night so finely that no one anywhere dies of the dark in it; file it as a masterpiece, unnumbered.
Reforge the world's oldest shadow where it has worn thin, and do not sign the work.
When smiths swear by the dark between hammer-falls, be what the oath lands on.

nodes.name: The Shade at Noon
nodes.role: World infrastructure — shelter-shade as standing mercy
nodes.lore: The Causewrights' lending, perfected past personhood: an office that answers for every shade that shelters anyone. The cool under the fig tree, the awning that holds through the riot, the cellar dark that hides the hunted — all of it is one span now, maintained. Deserts negotiate with it. Noon has never won.
nodes.playstyle: Protect at planetary scale: every shadow allies touch is your fortification, your road, and your infirmary. You are terrain now — the merciful kind.

abilities.name: One Span Now
abilities.desc: All shade everywhere is a single structure you maintain; damage to any of it may be referred to the sun.

abilities.name: Cool Standing
abilities.desc: Allies in any shade cannot overheat, starve, or despair; the office considers all three the same failure.

abilities.name: Awning Law
abilities.desc: Declare one shadow inviolable; violence beneath it simply fails to occur, and has since before you held the office.

abilities.name: Noon Repealed
abilities.desc: Cancel daylight's advantages across a battlefield; the sun retains ceremonial duties.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and lend yourself whole: become the shade of everything at once, and return yourself each dawn, on time, forever.
Hold the awnings of a burning city until everyone under them is elsewhere.
Shade one traveler across the Glass Waste personally; offices need the exercise.
Outlast the sun's one recorded attempt to set forever, and talk it back up; shade without noon is just night, and you have colleagues for that.

nodes.name: The Night Entire
nodes.role: Universal passage — all darkness is one place
nodes.lore: The Open Dark opened it all the way. The Night Entire is the standing fact that darkness is one country with one weather and no interior borders — an office, a geography, and a kindness, depending on which history is consulted. Every shadow is its capital. The rescued of ten centuries hold dual citizenship.
nodes.playstyle: Treat every dark point as adjacent: deploy, extract, and reinforce anywhere instantly. Wars against you happen wherever you prefer, in whatever order.

abilities.name: One Country
abilities.desc: All shadow is one location you administer; you and your allies are always, technically, already there.

abilities.name: Border Abolition
abilities.desc: Enemy zones of control cannot partition darkness; their perimeters hold light and little else.

abilities.name: Citizenry of the Saved
abilities.desc: Anyone ever rescued through the dark, descendants included, may step to your side when called; gratitude at that scale is an army.

abilities.name: Capital Everywhere
abilities.desc: Fight in every shadow at once when you must; distance has resigned its commission.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and dissolve the last border inside darkness: the one between where you are and where you are needed.
Hold a census of the dark and lose count on purpose; countries that know their size defend it.
Grant asylum to the shadows of things that no longer exist; they have nowhere else.
Be the reason no night anywhere is foreign; travelers will never thank you, feeling merely at home. Accept this.

nodes.name: The Halflight
nodes.role: Ambient sovereign — the gradient between lit and dark
nodes.lore: No light ends at an edge; it fails politely, through a margin of grey. That margin is an office now. The Halflight is the Unlit spread thinner than recurrence — present wherever light gives out, which is everywhere, eventually. Painters curse it. Dying men report it kind. Both reviews are kept on file.
nodes.playstyle: Exist in every gradient at once. You cannot be excluded by any light or found by any dark; attrition without address, mercy without witness.

abilities.name: Where Light Gives Out
abilities.desc: You are present in the falloff of every light source; wards must be perfect to exclude you, and none are.

abilities.name: Polite Failure
abilities.desc: Dim every hostile light by exactly the amount its bearer will not notice; repeat until relevant.

abilities.name: Kind to the Fading
abilities.desc: Allies at death's edge slip into your grey and are held there, beyond harm, until help or morning.

abilities.name: Neither Nor
abilities.desc: You are neither lit nor dark; abilities that target either category have filed you, incorrectly, under both.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and thin past recurrence into constancy: stop happening, and simply obtain.
Be the last thing ten thousand candles do; be gentle each time.
Sit for every portrait painted at dusk; sign none of them.
When the first light asks where its edges went, keep them; edges were always yours.

nodes.name: Nightfall
nodes.role: Recurring event — dusk arrives as a combatant
nodes.lore: Somewhere along the line, the office and the evening merged. Nightfall is now performed: each dusk, somewhere, a figure lowers the dark over the world like a smith laying down a finished blade, differently every time. Astronomers model it as rotation. The order keeps the truth, and the truth keeps the schedule.
nodes.playstyle: Arrive as the day's end: one entrance per engagement, absolute and improvised. Everything before your arrival is prologue and knows it.

abilities.name: The Day Ends Here
abilities.desc: Bring dusk to the engagement regardless of hour; every advantage of light is adjourned.

abilities.name: Performed Fresh
abilities.desc: No two of your nightfalls share a weakness; counters prepared against your last arrival find the repertoire has moved on.

abilities.name: Prologue's End
abilities.desc: On arrival, cancel every effect staged before you came; the fight restarts at the interesting part.

abilities.name: Early Tonight
abilities.desc: Once a season, night falls the moment you are needed; the sun apologizes to the astronomers.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and take the evening shift permanently; there is no other applicant, and there never was.
Bring down one nightfall so gentle a sleeping child is the only witness; bring down one so total a war is misplaced. Alternate.
Miss no dusk in a century, and let the one dawn you attend remain unexplained.
When they ask what you were before you were evening, answer honestly: brighter.

nodes.name: The First Dark
nodes.role: Primordial bastion — the dark beneath everything
nodes.lore: The quarry and the mason have concluded their long argument by merging. The First Dark — the unlit that preceded light — is now also its own final fortress, and somewhere in it the Keep that walked in is load-bearing. Everything ever built rests, eventually, on dark that was never cast. It holds. That is the whole doctrine: it holds.
nodes.playstyle: Defend from beneath existence: foundations, deep cellars, the underside of the world are all interior to you. Sieges against you besiege geology.

abilities.name: Founded On You
abilities.desc: Any structure allies hold is revealed to rest on your dark; it gains your walls' patience and your doctrine's stubbornness.

abilities.name: Older Than Light
abilities.desc: Attacks of radiance, dawn, and revelation fail against you on grounds of seniority.

abilities.name: The Deep Interior
abilities.desc: Swallow a battlefield's underside; enemy earthworks, mines, and cellars open into you, and you are not a corridor.

abilities.name: It Holds
abilities.desc: Once per age, something that must not fall — a city, a sky, a last hope — simply does not.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and open your gates onto the dark beneath the world, and find your own oldest wall already standing there, expecting you.
Bear the weight of everything built by everyone, and mention it to no one.
Refuse the light's first and only request: to see what you are keeping down there.
Hold. The rest of the doctrine was commentary.

nodes.name: The Curfew
nodes.role: Cosmic seal — the law that closes the night
nodes.lore: In every town the bell rings dark, and the practice remembers why. The Curfew is the law the Shut Night became: the nightly closing of the world's one dark against what presses on its far side. It has no text, only observance. The bell-ropes of ten thousand towns are its signature, renewed each evening.
nodes.playstyle: Enforce closure at world scale: end incursions, lock the medium, and hold the far side back. Your presence is the difference between night and breach.

abilities.name: Rings Dark
abilities.desc: Toll the unheard bell; every passage through shadow worldwide closes mid-step, travelers deposited at the nearest honest ground.

abilities.name: Observance
abilities.desc: While any creature anywhere keeps your curfew — shutters a window, bars a door at dusk — you cannot be destroyed.

abilities.name: The Far Side Kept
abilities.desc: What waits beyond darkness is held to its side of the skin; breaches close at the rate of your attention.

abilities.name: Last Bell
abilities.desc: Once, ever: close the dark entirely, to everything, including yourself; the histories disagree about whether this has already happened.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and replace your oath with a ringing: when every dusk bell in the world sounds, that is you, arriving.
Keep the far side out for a century in which nobody learns there is a far side; the office grades on ignorance.
Forgive the one passage you once opened; laws that remember being people last longer.
Teach the bells to ring without ropes on the night you are busiest; delegation is survival now.

nodes.name: The Nadir
nodes.role: World anchor — the point everything rests on
nodes.lore: Astronomers define the nadir as the point beneath all feet, and assume it is a direction. It is a posting. The Black Plinth that never resurfaced holds the world's underside the way a keystone holds an arch — from below, in the dark, without relief. Plumb-lines point to it. So, at the end, does everything else.
nodes.playstyle: Anchor existence: absolute stability radiating upward through everything standing. What you hold cannot fall; what you drop was warned.

abilities.name: Beneath All Feet
abilities.desc: You support whatever you choose worldwide; chosen structures, lines, and causes cannot collapse while you keep the posting.

abilities.name: Plumb Truth
abilities.desc: All falling redirects to you; avalanches, sieges, and thrown gods arrive at your shoulders, pre-sorted.

abilities.name: Without Relief
abilities.desc: You do not tire, waver, or rotate out; the concept of shift-change breaks against you and apologizes.

abilities.name: Let One Thing Fall
abilities.desc: Withdraw your support from a single thing; gravity remembers its old enthusiasm.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and take the posting beneath the world; the Plinth you relieved has somewhere to be, and has waited politely.
Hold everything for one full turning of the sky without once being thanked; the job is the monument.
Learn what the world rests on rested on before you; do not tell the philosophers, who are happier arguing.
Be down. Be what down means. When anything falls anywhere, be where it was always going.

families.name: Masquer
families.tagline: Wear the life until the life wears you.
families.description: A Rogue wears disguises as tools. The Masquer is occasionally worn, and calls the arrangement fair. The craft of stolen gaits and borrowed decades ends at a threshold: the evening the mirror stops arguing. Some walk through into other people's lives and inhabit them whole. Others take up the great masks — Judge, Fool, Widow, King-in-Waiting — and learn that a role held long enough begins holding back.

nodes.name: Masquer
nodes.role: Infiltrator — misdirection, borrowed identity
nodes.lore: Most begin as fair-day players, hired doubles, competent liars with good ears. The rank arrives the first evening a borrowed face refuses to come off with the paint: a long minute at the mirror, watching a stranger decide whether to give your name back. Guild registries list surviving Masquers under occupation: various.
nodes.playstyle: Fight as whoever the moment requires. Borrow faces, voices, and standing to walk where blades cannot, and strike from inside the enemy's certainty.

abilities.name: Studied Face
abilities.desc: Assume the face and voice of any person you have studied for one minute; the likeness holds until you speak your own name.

abilities.name: Stolen Gait
abilities.desc: Copy a target's walk to inherit their clearances; guards, wards, and watchdogs accept you as them for 20 seconds.

abilities.name: Doorway Logic
abilities.desc: Passing through any doorway, swap to another studied face; witnesses on either side will not agree on who entered.

abilities.name: The Second Bow
abilities.desc: After a kill or a scene, exit as someone else; pursuit loses your trail and blames a bystander of your choosing.

progressionSteps: Study one stranger for a season — gait, grudges, table manners — until you can be them to their own dog.
Stand before a mirror wearing a face not yours until the reflection blinks first, and tell no one what that cost.
Attend your own funeral in a borrowed face, having arranged the funeral yourself, and take notes on the eulogies.
Answer the guild's one entrance question — which of your faces is the original. Any answer is accepted. Hesitation is not.

nodes.name: Lifetailor
nodes.role: Infiltrator — full impersonation, identity theft
nodes.lore: The Thousand Faces path begins with tailoring: a life taken in at the shoulders, let out at the years, fitted to the wearer. Lifetailors keep pattern-books of studied lives — gaits, scars, second languages, marriages — and speak of people the way drapers speak of cloth. The guild finds this professional. The people are not consulted.
nodes.playstyle: Choose your shape before the fight begins. Enter as someone the enemy trusts, and spend that trust at the worst possible moment for them.

abilities.name: Pattern-Book
abilities.desc: Keep up to five studied lives; changing between them takes one unobserved breath and survives magical scrutiny short of a true name.

abilities.name: Taken In at the Years
abilities.desc: Wear a life older or younger than your own; your body ages a decade in either direction for up to one hour.

abilities.name: A Close Fit
abilities.desc: While wearing a studied life, hold its rank, keys, and standing obligations; its allies defend you as their own.

abilities.name: Seam-Rip
abilities.desc: Drop a worn life explosively; everyone who trusted the face is staggered for 4 seconds, and your first strike on them cannot miss.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10 and wear one complete life for thirty days among its own family; a single dropped stitch ends the trial.
Compile your first pattern-book: seven lives studied to the seams, each certified wearable by a guild fitter you will never identify.
Return a borrowed life better than you found it — feuds settled, roof mended — and leave before anyone says thank you.

nodes.name: Vizard
nodes.role: Presence controller — role auras, command
nodes.lore: Vizards stop borrowing faces and start serving them. The great masks are older than the guild that houses them — the Judge, the Fool, the Widow, the King-in-Waiting — and each grants exactly what the role demands, on the role's terms. New Vizards are warned that the masks wear back. All of them nod. None of them listen.
nodes.playstyle: Put on a role with its own gravity. While the mask holds, the world behaves as the role requires — and so, increasingly, do you.

abilities.name: Donning
abilities.desc: Assume a great mask; for 10 minutes you carry whatever authority, license, or awe the role commands, regardless of witnesses' allegiance.

abilities.name: The Role Provides
abilities.desc: Once per scene the mask supplies what the role would have — a verdict, a jest, tears, an heir's ring.

abilities.name: Gravity of Office
abilities.desc: Enemies within 10 meters must treat you as the role or suffer weakness; striking a Judge unprovoked is, after all, contempt.

abilities.name: It Wears Back
abilities.desc: When you remove the mask, keep one of its virtues for an hour and one of its appetites until dawn.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10 and carry a great mask, still boxed, for one year without opening the box. The mask will know.
Don the Fool before a hanging judge, or the Judge before a mob, and hold the role until the room obeys it.
Feed the mask one true memory of your own face. It is easier to be the role when there is less of you arguing.

nodes.name: Understudy
nodes.role: Deep-cover striker — replacement, betrayal burst
nodes.lore: An Understudy studies one life only, but completely: twenty years of letters, the argument that ended the marriage, which stair creaks and which she skips. Employers assume the point is assassination. Often it is gentler — a principal too ill, too dead, or too honest for an occasion, and the performance must go on.
nodes.playstyle: Commit to one stolen life per contract. The longer you inhabit it undetected, the more devastating the moment you choose to stop pretending.

abilities.name: Line-Perfect
abilities.desc: Answer any test of identity — pass-phrases, pet names, old wounds — as your subject would; rehearsed enough, the lies detect as truth.

abilities.name: Creaking Stair
abilities.desc: Know your subject's ground as they do; in their own spaces you cannot be ambushed and always have an exit.

abilities.name: Cue to Enter
abilities.desc: When your subject falls or falters within 30 meters, assume their place mid-scene; witnesses' memories recast themselves around you.

abilities.name: Stop Pretending
abilities.desc: End the impersonation with a strike dealing bonus damage for every consecutive day the life was worn undetected.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and be examined, as your subject, by their own mother. The guild accepts either her embrace or her funeral; it prefers the embrace.
Learn your subject's shame — the true one, not the confessed one — and never use it. Knowing is the craft; using is vandalism.
Perform their trade, their marriage, and their prayers for a season, better than they did, and forgive yourself for the better.
Watch your subject from across a square while wearing their face, and let them pass unknowing. This last examination is of you.

nodes.name: Quickchange
nodes.role: Skirmish controller — face-cycling, crowd chaos
nodes.lore: Quickchanges hold that a life worn past one evening starts to stick, and that mastery is turnover. They work fairs, sieges, and parliaments as a dozen people apiece, several of whom publicly disagree with each other. Watch captains despise them: every witness statement is accurate, and no two describe the same person.
nodes.playstyle: Never be the same person twice in one fight. Cycle faces between blows, seed crowds with your own aliases, and let confusion do the heavy cutting.

abilities.name: Turn and Turnabout
abilities.desc: Each time you break line of sight, emerge as a different face; enemy targeting, marks, and grudges do not carry over.

abilities.name: Rhubarb, Rhubarb
abilities.desc: Seed a crowd with three of your aliases; direct their rumors, panics, and conveniently timed scuffles as free actions.

abilities.name: Costume Drop
abilities.desc: Shed a face as a standing decoy that draws attacks for 6 seconds; it takes the blow meant for who you no longer are.

abilities.name: Reprise
abilities.desc: Wear a face witnessed dying earlier in the battle; superstitious enemies check morale, and the rational ones start doubting their kills.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and work one market-day as eleven people, at least two of whom are seen in public at once. Hire no accomplices.
Change faces mid-sentence before a witness and finish the sentence unremarked. The trick is not the face; it is the sentence.
Be arrested, tried, and acquitted as three different strangers for the same crime, which, for the record, you did commit.
Spend a year without your original face. When the guild offers it back, decline politely.

nodes.name: Officiant
nodes.role: Field commander — verdicts, borrowed sovereignty
nodes.lore: Officiants keep the masks of state: the Judge, which has ended feuds older than the courthouse; the King-in-Waiting, for whom garrisons open gates that no army could. An Officiant exercises every office and holds none — an arrangement whose paperwork three chancelleries have formally agreed to stop attempting.
nodes.playstyle: Enter as the authority everyone was secretly waiting for. Command enemies as readily as allies, so long as you never once break role.

abilities.name: Sit in Judgment
abilities.desc: Don the Judge and declare one combatant guilty; all present, friend and foe, treat them as convicted for 20 seconds.

abilities.name: The Expected Heir
abilities.desc: Don the King-in-Waiting; enemy formations must parley, kneel, or commit treason — and treason costs them their command bonuses.

abilities.name: Robes of the Realm
abilities.desc: While in role you cannot be struck first; someone must openly defy the office, aloud, before any hand may rise against you.

abilities.name: The Court Rises
abilities.desc: Suspend the fighting for 10 seconds while the office deliberates; combatants hold their places, and nothing new may enter the field.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and end a blood feud wearing the Judge, with a verdict both houses hate and neither dares appeal.
Wear the King-in-Waiting through a coronation season without once sitting on the throne. The mask wants to. Note carefully what wanting feels like.
Return the masks to their boxes on time, twice, when the role was going well. The guild counts the second one.

nodes.name: Licentiate
nodes.role: Debuffer — mockery, grief, sanctioned trespass
nodes.lore: Licentiates keep the masks the world agreed not to punish: the Fool, who may say the unsayable to the crowned; the Widow, for whom battle lines part. License is the oldest working in the repertoire — older than the guild, older than courts — and it extends to the mask, never the wearer. Wearers forget this exactly once.
nodes.playstyle: Go where combatants cannot and say what subjects dare not. Your armor is custom itself; your weapons are laughter and grief, in that order.

abilities.name: Cap and Bells
abilities.desc: Don the Fool and mock a target's next action into failure; abilities you name aloud misfire, to everyone's visible amusement but theirs.

abilities.name: Weeds and Veil
abilities.desc: Don the Widow and walk untouched across any battle, siege, or cordon; violence pauses within 5 meters of your grief.

abilities.name: Sanctioned Tongue
abilities.desc: Speak one truth about an enemy commander; their forces lose morale bonuses until the commander answers it, which they will not.

abilities.name: License Revoked
abilities.desc: If struck while in role, the striker becomes fair game: every combatant on the field may attack them without penalty for 10 seconds.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and make a tyrant laugh at the joke that names his crime, then leave at walking pace.
Wear the Widow onto a battlefield and collect the wounded of both sides; the side that objects loses, historically.
Learn where license ends. The guild will not tell you, the masks will not warn you, and the lesson is administered once.

nodes.name: Cuckoo
nodes.role: Deep infiltrator — permanent replacement, decisive betrayal
nodes.lore: The Cuckoos answer the Understudy's question — what is all the study for — with the only honest word: the nest. A life exquisitely learned deserves better management than its founder gives it. Originals are retired quietly, kindly where feasible, and the life continues, improved. Three thrones are currently occupied this way. The order will not say which.
nodes.playstyle: Replace a key enemy and run the battle from inside their command. Every order you give is obeyed until the moment obedience becomes fatal.

abilities.name: The Nest Is Taken
abilities.desc: Permanently assume a slain or captured subject's life; divinations, bloodwards, and their own signet all confirm you.

abilities.name: Kindly Retired
abilities.desc: Remove a studied target from play, non-lethally, for 24 hours; nobody notices an absence while you are present.

abilities.name: Better Management
abilities.desc: Forces led by a commander you have replaced fight 15% better than under the original; their oaths do not count this as treason.

abilities.name: First Egg Broken
abilities.desc: Your betrayal strike from inside a worn life cannot be survived by ordinary means, and the life remains yours afterward, unsuspected.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and be invited: the Cuckoos recruit by replacing you for a week and returning the life with improvements. Decline the improvements to fail.
Take a nest above your station — a magistracy, a captaincy, a marriage — and hold it a year, improving every measure but one.
Retire an original kindly. The order audits the kindness, not the retirement.
Answer the mirror's old question differently: the face you were born with is now simply one more entry in the pattern-book. File it.

nodes.name: Everyman
nodes.role: Swarm controller — ubiquity, crowd embodiment
nodes.lore: Everymen keep no home face in circulation; they keep circulation. Any one of them is, at a given hour, roughly forty people — porters, aunts, off-duty guards, the fellow everyone half-knows. Cities host them the way fields host weather. Their doctrine is one line: a thousand faces is not a wardrobe. It is a public.
nodes.playstyle: Fight as attendance itself. Scatter into bystanders, strike from any of them, and make clearing the whole crowd the enemy's only real option.

abilities.name: Forty People
abilities.desc: Maintain up to six walk-on selves in a crowd at once; you perceive through all of them and may act from one per turn.

abilities.name: Half-Known Fellow
abilities.desc: Any stranger who sees you is sure they have met you; enemies hesitate 2 seconds before their first attack on any face you wear.

abilities.name: Public Opinion
abilities.desc: The crowd inclines as you incline; mobs you stand in adopt your target, your grievance, and your exits.

abilities.name: One of Ours
abilities.desc: Die in a worn face and the crowd absorbs you; reappear as another bystander at 30% health, once per battle.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and spend one festival week as a minor public figure in three rival cities simultaneously. Take no coach.
Enter the order by census: appear in one town's rolls under nine names, none flagged, all paying taxes.
Let a stranger use one of your faces without your leave, and study how it feels from the outside. Then take it back gently.
Give up being missed. An Everyman is never absent, therefore never awaited, therefore never mourned. Sign the page anyway.

nodes.name: Interrex
nodes.role: Commander — interim sovereignty, succession control
nodes.lore: When a crown falls between heads, treaties permit the lending of an Interrex: the King-in-Waiting worn openly until the succession untangles. The lodge has governed forty-one interregna and kept none of them. Chancelleries trust the arrangement precisely because the mask, not the wearer, holds the power — and the mask has excellent references.
nodes.playstyle: Rule the gap. Take command of leaderless forces, hold broken chains of command together, and hand power onward at exactly the agreed hour.

abilities.name: By Treaty Worn
abilities.desc: Assume command of any allied force whose leader is down; their formation bonuses resume immediately under your borrowed office.

abilities.name: The Gap Holds
abilities.desc: While you lead, allied morale cannot collapse, and command effects persist through deaths that would ordinarily break them.

abilities.name: Regnal Pause
abilities.desc: Declare an interregnum on the field; enemy leadership bonuses are suspended for 15 seconds while questions of legitimacy are, suddenly, live.

abilities.name: Handed Onward
abilities.desc: Transfer all authority you hold to a chosen ally at any moment; they gain your command bonuses doubled for 10 seconds.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and govern an interregnum by invitation, through winter and plague, then attend the coronation as a guest, unarmed and unthanked.
Refuse the crown once, in public, with witnesses hostile to the refusal. The treaty text is watching.
Sit the throne itself once, for the mask's sake — thrones ache to be sat — and rise the moment the bells finish.
Depose an Effigy, politely if possible; the guild prefers its heresies retired rather than martyred.

nodes.name: Motley
nodes.role: Morale breaker — weaponized mockery, misrule
nodes.lore: The Motley take the Fool to its conclusion: license as siegecraft. They enter cities ahead of armies and empty thrones before the ram arrives — a nickname here, a pantomime there, until the garrison cannot say 'my liege' without somebody snorting. Kings have surrendered to armies rather than negotiate with a Motley. The chronicles record this as wisdom.
nodes.playstyle: Unmake authority by ridicule. Strip commanders of the obedience they run on, provoke enemies into idiocy, and be legally impossible to punish.

abilities.name: Feast of Misrule
abilities.desc: Invert an enemy command structure for 20 seconds: orders execute reversed, retreats charge, and charges retire, to general embarrassment.

abilities.name: The Nickname
abilities.desc: Bestow a name on an enemy commander; while it sticks, their commands cost double and their auras amuse rather than inspire.

abilities.name: Slapstick
abilities.desc: Your strikes trip, de-helm, and disarm rather than wound; each indignity stacks 5% increased damage taken on the target.

abilities.name: The Marotte
abilities.desc: Strike with the fool's sceptre: damage is modest, but the struck cannot issue orders for 6 seconds, being a laughingstock.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and empty a throne without a death; the abdication must cite exhaustion, and the city must be laughing.
Take the Motley's beating — the one the law allows — and return next morning with better material.
Mock something that frightens you more than kings do. The mask will know if you pick kings.
Argue the old question with a Weeper — what license is for — and lose gracefully in public, as tradition requires. Win privately.

nodes.name: Locum
nodes.role: Guardian infiltrator — ally substitution, lives held
nodes.lore: Locums call the Cuckoos thieves with good tailoring, and are called embalmers in return. A Locum holds a life in trust: the poisoned king breathes behind a curtain while his double drinks the second cup; the general felled at midnight still gives the dawn orders. Everything is returned — name, seal, grievances — the day the owner can stand.
nodes.playstyle: Stand inside other people's lives at their worst moments. Substitute for allies about to die, hold their posts, and hand everything back intact.

abilities.name: The Second Cup
abilities.desc: Swap places with an ally within 15 meters as a killing blow lands; you take it, as them, at half damage.

abilities.name: Held in Trust
abilities.desc: Assume an incapacitated ally's post; their abilities, standing orders, and command auras persist through you until they recover.

abilities.name: Curtain Rule
abilities.desc: An ally you conceal cannot be found, targeted, or declared dead while you are wearing their life in public.

abilities.name: Returned Intact
abilities.desc: When you relinquish a held life, its owner returns healed for every day you kept it, and loyalty you earned transfers home.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and hold a dead man's life until his heir comes of age. Nine years. The order will check on you twice.
Take the second cup knowingly, at a table where refusing it was possible, and let the poisoner watch you finish it.
Return a life you held so well its owner asks you to stay. The rank is in the leaving.
Stand at your rival's door: tell a Cuckoo which nest you are guarding, and make the guarding hold.

nodes.name: Anonym
nodes.role: Evasion elite — unrecognition, untargetable
nodes.lore: Anonyms call the Everymen hoarders: a thousand faces is still property, still weight, still somewhere to be found. Their mastery runs the other way — subtraction, until what remains fits behind any face without touching the sides. No Anonym has been described the same way twice, including by other Anonyms. The order's roster is blank, and fully subscribed.
nodes.playstyle: Win by refusing to be anyone. Enemies cannot mark, curse, or remember you; every attack against you is aimed at a description already wrong.

abilities.name: Wrong Description
abilities.desc: Attacks and spells aimed at you by sight suffer a 30% miss chance; effects requiring your name fail outright, having no one to bind.

abilities.name: Touching No Sides
abilities.desc: Pass identity wards, guest-laws, and watch-lists unremarked; systems built to catch someone find no one, and log accordingly.

abilities.name: Fresh Face
abilities.desc: Discard a face mid-combat to shed every debuff, mark, and point of enemy attention accumulated while wearing it.

abilities.name: Nobody's Grudge
abilities.desc: Enemies who lose sight of you forget you were a combatant; re-engaging you costs them their action as they re-decide.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and surrender your original face to the order. It is not stored. Do not ask what happens instead.
Go a year unmet: buy, travel, and lodge among people who, questioned after, can prove someone was there and nothing else.
Stand your rival's trial: let an Everyman crowd search for you at a festival held in your honor. Attend it.
Answer the entrance question again — which of your faces is the original — correctly this time: silence.

nodes.name: Effigy
nodes.role: Presence tank — enthroned awe, decree control
nodes.lore: Effigies hold that the Interrex's humility is the exact mistake: power handed back to persons resumes being personal — appetite with a signet. Better the mask keep the office, tireless, heirless, unbribable. Four such reigns are acknowledged. The subjects prospered, and the histories have not settled on what, precisely, to be horrified about.
nodes.playstyle: Become the seated fact of authority. You barely move; the field reorganizes around your office, and harming you is constitutionally difficult.

abilities.name: Enthroned
abilities.desc: Take a seat of power — throne, judgment bench, gate-tower — and become untargetable except by enemies who first denounce you aloud.

abilities.name: Heirless and Tireless
abilities.desc: While enthroned you require nothing — no breath, food, or rest — and effects that exploit mortality fail against you.

abilities.name: The Office Rules
abilities.desc: Issue one decree per minute; on your ground, decrees behave as physics — gates hold, curfews bind, arms lie down.

abilities.name: Lacquer
abilities.desc: Damage that reaches you hardens into lacquered scarring, granting 2% damage reduction per wound while the office is held.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and rule somewhere small — an island, a pass, a prison — as the mask, openly, for three years. Govern well. That part is not optional.
Survive your own deposition by the Interrex lodge and re-seat the mask before sundown; the argument continues, formally.
Let the mask select which of your features it keeps; the lacquer takes the rest. Sit still.
Explain nothing, ever. A good reign, like a good mask, has no inside.

nodes.name: Weeper
nodes.role: Pacifier — grief auras, sanctioned passage
nodes.lore: The Motley strike upward; the Weepers hold that license was never for striking. Grief is a writ of passage older than kings, and a Relict in full weeds has crossed battles, plague cordons, and the private chambers of tyrants unquestioned. Each is in mourning for someone real. The order does not require that the someone be dead yet.
nodes.playstyle: Suppress violence by presence. Walk unharmed where you please, still the fighting around you, and grieve enemies into remembering they are mortal.

abilities.name: Full Weeds
abilities.desc: While veiled, no combatant may target you without first losing all morale bonuses; most discover they had somewhere else to be.

abilities.name: Prior Mourning
abilities.desc: Mourn a living enemy by name; they perceive their own funeral proceeding correctly and fight at 20% reduced effect.

abilities.name: The Cortege
abilities.desc: Allies moving with you at walking pace share your passage rights, untargetable while no one in the procession strikes.

abilities.name: Grief's Quarter
abilities.desc: Project a 10-meter quiet in which weapons weigh double and rage effects fail; it moves with you and deepens near the dying.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and walk the length of an active battle at widow's pace, unarmed, and be the only thing that crosses it intact.
Mourn someone you never met so exactly that the family seats you first at the funeral.
Choose whom your weeds are for. The order asks once, records nothing, and can always tell when the answer changes.
Bury a Motley with full honors when the law finally fails one, and do not say what you both knew about license.

nodes.name: The Rightful
nodes.role: Mythic usurper — legitimacy theft
nodes.lore: Once in a century, a replacement outgrows the word. The Rightful is whichever claimant history eventually sides with — and history, examined closely, was persuaded by the performance, not the parentage. Two dynasties now descend through a Cuckoo and would hang the librarian who proved it. The blood tells; it has simply been taught what to say.
nodes.playstyle: Legitimacy itself defects to you. Whatever you claim — commands, fortresses, loyalties — the world's own wards and retainers ratify the claim.

abilities.name: The Blood Persuaded
abilities.desc: Bloodline wards, heirloom weapons, and dynastic oaths recognize you as rightful; the actual heirs register as pretenders.

abilities.name: History Sides
