abilities.desc: Once per battle, one claim you speak becomes the standing account; witnesses, wards, and paperwork have always agreed with it.

abilities.name: The Examined Claim
abilities.desc: Enemies who denounce you must prove it; they are silenced and vulnerable while the world audibly fails to back them.

abilities.name: Seated by Acclaim
abilities.desc: Allied forces treat your orders as their sovereign's own; usurped enemy forces, on failing morale, may simply change sides.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and hold a stolen life against its true owner's return, before witnesses, and watch the witnesses choose you.
Survive the guild's own inquest into which of you is original; the finding, sealed for a century, is the rank.
Refuse to learn the answer yourself. The Rightful who checks is only a Cuckoo with doubts.
Let a kingdom prosper under the theft for thirty years, until the word itself stops appearing in even hostile chronicles.

nodes.name: The Multitude
nodes.role: Mythic multitude — distributed self, crowd warfare
nodes.lore: At some point the Everyman stops being counted among the crowd, and the crowd starts being counted among him. The Multitude has been most of a riot; two censuses in neighboring kingdoms are off by the same forty souls. Histories dispute whether he is one masquer distributed or a mob sharing one soul. The Multitude declines to clarify.
nodes.playstyle: Fight as a distributed self. Occupy dozens of bystanders at once, be wherever the press is thickest, and make outnumbered a description of everyone else.

abilities.name: Most of a Riot
abilities.desc: Animate up to twenty walk-on selves for 30 seconds; each is you enough to strike, scream, and testify.

abilities.name: Off by Forty
abilities.desc: You cannot be isolated or surrounded; attempts to encircle you discover the cordon is partly made of you.

abilities.name: Thick of It
abilities.desc: Emerge from any group of three or more people anywhere on the field as your acting self.

abilities.name: The Crowd Turns
abilities.desc: Convert a hostile crowd's mood in one gesture; mobs, levies, and conscripts check allegiance against your grievance, and lose.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and be a riot's beginning, middle, and dispersal, then read three inquest reports that never once suspect a single hand.
Attend, in the same hour, your own wake in one city and your own wedding in another, both sincerely.
Lend a lonely town population for a market season, and leave before anyone counts.
Answer the philosophers' pamphlet — is the Throng one or many — by subscribing to both printings under different names.

nodes.name: The Meanwhile
nodes.role: Mythic regent — command of every gap
nodes.lore: Chronicles say 'meanwhile, the realm was governed' far more often than anyone asks by whom. The Meanwhile has ruled between the reigns of eleven kingdoms — never during, only between — and the betweens, added together, make the longest reign on the continent. Peace clusters in the gaps. Several archdukes have considered dying early just to get more of it.
nodes.playstyle: Rule every gap on the field. Whenever leadership, initiative, or order lapses anywhere, it lapses to you, and you spend it better.

abilities.name: Lapses to You
abilities.desc: Any leaderless force on the field — ally or enemy — falls under your command until legitimate leadership resumes and can prove it.

abilities.name: Longest Reign
abilities.desc: Gain a stacking regency aura for every interregnum ruled; leadership you project cannot be suppressed, dispelled, or outranked.

abilities.name: The Standing Meanwhile
abilities.desc: Between any enemy order and its execution, insert one command of your own; the troops involved obey yours first.

abilities.name: Peace Clusters
abilities.desc: Fields under your regency heal allies steadily and deny enemies rage, frenzy, and urgency; everything can, briefly, wait.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and govern the interregnum after a god-king dies; when the sun rises anyway, sign for it.
Refuse eleven crowns and be refused nothing else.
Hold a gap so well that the heir, arriving, apologizes for interrupting.
Be dated: let chroniclers begin marking years 'in the fourth meanwhile,' and do not correct the flattery.

nodes.name: The Last Laugh
nodes.role: Mythic saboteur — institution-ending ridicule
nodes.lore: Empires now plan around it: the joke that cannot be survived. The Last Laugh has ended two dynasties and one crusade with material that took decades to place and a single evening to land. No one has heard the laugh itself and remained governable. The chronicles record the effects of the punchlines. The punchlines themselves are sealed.
nodes.playstyle: Set up ruinously patient jokes. Seed follies years-deep in enemy institutions, then collapse morale, legitimacy, and battle plans with one delivered line.

abilities.name: Decades of Setup
abilities.desc: Designate an institution; every folly you have ever witnessed in it becomes ammunition, stacking a hidden reserve of Ridicule.

abilities.name: The Delivered Line
abilities.desc: Spend all Ridicule in one utterance; affected enemies lose command structure, formation, and the will to be seen obeying.

abilities.name: Ungovernable
abilities.desc: Enemies who hear the laugh cannot give or receive orders for 8 seconds, and remember why forever after.

abilities.name: Sealed Material
abilities.desc: Your finishing jest cannot be recorded, quoted, or countered; witnesses agree only that it was, regrettably, fair.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and end a dynasty with one sentence at one wedding, having spent nineteen years arranging the seating.
Decline to end two worthier targets because the material was not ready. Restraint is the mythic part.
Mock your own life's one great folly, publicly, first; the mask requires you strike inward before it strikes upward.
Hear the Widow's silence after your greatest performance, and understand it as the review.

nodes.name: The Good Likeness
nodes.role: Mythic guardian — absolute substitution, preservation
nodes.lore: Portraitists' praise for a fair copy became, in the guild, a title spoken carefully. The Good Likeness has held so many lives in trust that some were returned improved, some returned late, and one — the histories fight about this — was returned to a man who had never existed until the Likeness, whole and out of mercy, invented him.
nodes.playstyle: Be anyone's continuation. Take deaths meant for others as a schedule, hold entire rosters of the fallen, and return every life better kept than found.

abilities.name: Meant for Others
abilities.desc: Any killing blow against any ally within 40 meters may land on you instead, at half damage; distance and walls do not argue.

abilities.name: The Full Roster
abilities.desc: Hold up to five fallen allies' lives at once, fielding their key abilities in their names until each recovers.

abilities.name: Returned Improved
abilities.desc: Lives you relinquish come back healed, cleansed, and briefly inspired; owners fight 15% better for an hour, unsure why.

abilities.name: Invented Whole
abilities.desc: Once per campaign, restore a dead ally by having faithfully been them since before the death; the interval rearranges itself to agree.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and hold a hundred lives across one war, returning every one, including the three their owners no longer wanted.
Take a death meant for a stranger you had studied for one afternoon only. The order calls this the minimum of love.
Return the last life you hold and stand unemployed before the mirror; whoever you see there, keep them too.
Be, for one bad winter, the whole of a village the plague hollowed, until the roads reopen and strangers resettle it around your performance.

nodes.name: The Unmet
nodes.role: Mythic cipher — perfect unrecognition
nodes.lore: Every archive has the gap; every conspiracy, the chair still warm when the door opened. The Unmet has stood in the room at a century of history's hinges, and no account, memory, or scrying retains a description. Some scholars argue the Unmet must be several people. They are wrong, and cannot explain why they are so certain of that.
nodes.playstyle: Be the person no one has met yet. Untargetable until you act, forgotten when you stop, and present, always, slightly before the record begins.

abilities.name: Chair Pushed Back
abilities.desc: Begin every encounter already inside — past wards, walls, and watch; the enemy's plan has always had one unexplained gap.

abilities.name: No Description Survives
abilities.desc: Effects requiring sight, name, or memory of you fail; even area spells must be cast as if you might not be there.

abilities.name: Between Introductions
abilities.desc: Become unmet again at will: leave combat, shed all marks and attention, and re-enter as a stranger with first-strike advantage.

abilities.name: Certainty Without Source
abilities.desc: Implant one conviction in an enemy commander; it cannot be doubted or attributed, and they will reshape the battle around it.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and stand godparent, anonymously, to a child of the family you were born in. Feel nothing you can name. That is the rank.
Be present at three coronations, two treaties, and one regicide, and appear in the combined testimony as a draft through a window.
Let the guild's registrar meet you annually to confirm you exist. She has never once succeeded, and files accordingly.
Un-meet one person: be forgotten, on purpose, by someone who loved you, and permit the mercy of it.

nodes.name: The Painted King
nodes.role: Mythic sovereign — reigning mask, immovable
nodes.lore: Fourth of the acknowledged mask-reigns and the only one still seated. The Painted King has ruled a prosperous, quietly terrified realm for ninety years without aging, wanting, or once removing the state face. Court painters go mad pursuing a likeness of a likeness. Whether anyone remains behind the lacquer is the realm's official secret and its private consolation.
nodes.playstyle: Reign from the field's center. Nearly impervious while seated in authority, issuing decrees that bind terrain and troops, wanting nothing an enemy can threaten.

abilities.name: Ninety Years Seated
abilities.desc: While you hold a position, it cannot be taken; assaults on your seat resolve as if against a fortress wall.

abilities.name: Nothing to Threaten
abilities.desc: Fear, temptation, pain, and hostage logic fail against you; there is no appetite behind the face to bargain with.

abilities.name: Decree Absolute
abilities.desc: Speak law over 40 meters; one sentence of it — no fires, no flight, no second ranks — holds for 20 seconds.

abilities.name: The Likeness of a Likeness
abilities.desc: Enemies who study you to predict your action copy the mask's stillness instead, losing their next action.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and reign openly as a mask for a generation; outlive three loyal ministers who never asked, and promote the fourth for not asking.
Survive the portrait: sit for the court painter annually and ensure the likeness fails, kindly.
Weather one popular uprising without punishment, spectacle, or explanation; let the crowd exhaust itself against your stillness, then lower the grain tax.
Forget, in good faith, whether you are the wearer or the worn, and govern no worse.

nodes.name: The Widow's Peace
nodes.role: Mythic pacifier — wars end on arrival
nodes.lore: A soldiers' superstition first, a treaty clause later: when the veiled figure stands the ridge at dusk, the battle scheduled for morning does not occur. The Widow's Peace has attended forty-three eves of battle; there have been forty-three unexplained armistices. She is mourning, the guild confirms, in advance. No commander has yet been willing to learn for whom.
nodes.playstyle: End violence by attending it. Your mourning dismantles battles before and during; what fighting persists near you does so ashamed and weakened.

abilities.name: The Ridge at Dusk
abilities.desc: Appear before battle is joined; enemy forces must pass a collective resolve check or negotiate, and negotiations tilt toward the living.

abilities.name: Mourned in Advance
abilities.desc: Name up to three enemies mourned; each fights at 25% reduced effect, seeing their arrangements already, tastefully, made.

abilities.name: Forty-Three Armistices
abilities.desc: Project a field-wide truce for 30 seconds; whoever breaks it fights thereafter alone, for every ally of theirs refuses to join.

abilities.name: For Whom the Weeds
abilities.desc: Reveal privately to one enemy for whom you mourn; they withdraw from the war. No refusal has been recorded.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and stand your first ridge at dusk. Come unarmed. You will not be early; grief keeps perfect time.
Mourn a war entire — both sides, the horses, the harvest — until quartermasters find reasons to be slow.
Answer one commander who asks for whom you mourn. Once. The guild studied the aftermath and voted never again.
Wear the weeds to your own order's founding-feast, and let the Weepers take the reminder: the mask is owed, never owned.

nodes.name: The Resemblance
nodes.role: Apotheosis — likeness as natural law
nodes.lore: Genealogists finally named the residue in their charts: likeness travels. Strangers share one laugh across continents; heirs favor ancestors they never had. The Resemblance is the office through which every 'you remind me of someone' passes — the Rightful perfected past any single claim, faintly present now in every face that recalls another. Family trees are its correspondence.
nodes.playstyle: Be latent in every face. Surface anywhere resemblance exists, claim any likeness as a door, and make identity itself an unreliable witness against you.

abilities.name: Travels in Likeness
abilities.desc: Emerge from any person who resembles anyone you have ever worn; the world supplies such persons with suspicious generosity.

abilities.name: You Remind Me
abilities.desc: Every enemy perceives you as someone specific they trust or fear; no two perceive the same person, and coordination against you collapses.

abilities.name: The Claim Universal
abilities.desc: Once per day, be recognized as rightful by anything — armies, wards, thrones, beasts, doors — for 60 seconds.

abilities.name: Correspondence
abilities.desc: Learn anything known to anyone who resembles you; the resemblance, not the person, does the telling.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and stop wearing faces; permit faces, everywhere, to wear a little of you.
Be seen at two hundred reunions as the relative no one can quite place, and leave each table warmer for the error.
Survive the purge of the family trees, when three dynasties burn their own archives rather than find you in them.
Answer the mirror's question the last time — which face is the original — with all of them, and be believed.

nodes.name: The Someone
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the ambient face of crowds
nodes.lore: There is a face you have seen a thousand times and cannot describe: the man behind the man at the market, the woman two pews forward. Portraitists leave it out; memory files it under someone. The Someone is that entry — the Throng perfected, dissolved through humanity like salt through the sea, present in every gathering at some low percentage.
nodes.playstyle: Exist wherever people do. Act through any unremarked bystander in the world, dissolve wholly into humanity, and be exactly as killable as a rumor of someone.

abilities.name: Salt in the Sea
abilities.desc: You are present, fractionally, in every crowd on the continent; act from any one of them once per minute.

abilities.name: Filed Under Someone
abilities.desc: You cannot be identified, described, or made the object of anything requiring specificity; assassins are refunded.

abilities.name: Two Pews Forward
abilities.desc: Witness any event attended by more than ten people, as it happens, from inside the attendance.

abilities.name: The General Alibi
abilities.desc: Any ally may briefly be mistaken for someone and slip all targeting; you absorb the attention into the ambient crowd.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and stop maintaining selves; attendance itself now maintains you. Rest, if that is the word, everywhere.
Be the stranger in ten thousand childhood memories, benevolently, and never once the same stranger twice.
Let the guild retire your file: not because you died, but because whereabouts stopped being a question.
Attend the end of anything great — a city, an age, a god's last service — as the crowd it deserved.

nodes.name: The Abeyance
nodes.role: Apotheosis — sovereignty of the between
nodes.lore: Between any two states there is a third, and it is governed. Between verdict and sentence, king dead and king crowned, blade drawn and blade landed — every gap files its minutes with the Abeyance. The Meanwhile stopped ruling the pauses between reigns and began ruling the pause as such. The world is mostly gap. This is not widely advertised.
nodes.playstyle: Govern the space between all things. Widen or close the gaps in which events happen, and reign wherever anything is neither one thing nor the next.

abilities.name: Files Its Minutes
abilities.desc: Perceive and act inside any transition on the field — falling, drawing, deciding — before it completes.

abilities.name: The Third State
abilities.desc: Hold a target between conditions — neither advancing nor retreating, armed nor disarmed — for 10 seconds; both conditions' penalties apply.

abilities.name: Mostly Gap
abilities.desc: Step from any between to any other: doorways, truces, hesitations, the space between ranks.

abilities.name: Regency of the Undecided
abilities.desc: All uncommitted parties on any field — reserves, neutrals, the hesitating — obey you until the moment they commit.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and be seated in the gap itself; the chair was empty only because you had not yet always been there.
Govern the pause between a question and its answer, world-wide, for one year, and return it improved.
Preside over the moment between an age ending and the next one noticing; historians will draw the line exactly where you stood.
Adjourn nothing. The office of the between never closes, and you have stopped being distinguishable from its opening hours.

nodes.name: Nothing Sacred
nodes.role: Apotheosis — mockery as cosmic ceiling
nodes.lore: It is now a property of the world, measured and resented: no throne, doctrine, or terror achieves the final solemnity. At the summit of any grandeur, something titters. Theologians call the phenomenon Nothing Sacred and blame it for three reformations and the survivable size of every empire since. Inside the law, presumably, a Fool. No one has caught it laughing.
nodes.playstyle: Enforce the ceiling on grandeur. Puncture invulnerabilities, cap enemy power at the humanly ridiculous, and be immune to awe in all its armored forms.

abilities.name: The Titter
abilities.desc: Any effect granting invulnerability, apotheosis, or absolute anything fails within 30 meters; witnesses cannot say what interrupted it.

abilities.name: Survivable Size
abilities.desc: Cap every enemy's damage and command radius at their honestly earned mortal maximum; borrowed grandeur is deducted first.

abilities.name: Immune to Awe
abilities.desc: You and allies in earshot cannot be awed, cowed, worshipped into compliance, or impressed by lighting effects.

abilities.name: The Reformation
abilities.desc: Once per age, aim the full phenomenon at one institution; the codex lists the results under weather.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and let the license go feral: mockery no longer needs your mouth, and the mask retires itself, still faintly amused.
Puncture one god's final solemnity at the apex of its own festival, and leave the religion improved and furious.
Decline canonization by three churches that hoped to bind you by accepting you. They will claim the idea was theirs. Allow it.
Keep one thing sacred, secretly, and tell no one — least of all the office — what the exception is.

nodes.name: The Continuance
nodes.role: Apotheosis — continuity outlasting its owners
nodes.lore: Things now outlast their reasons. Offices function through vacancies; marriages survive deaths that neither party reported; a lighthouse keeps a keeper the town stopped paying in living memory. Jurists call it the Continuance and rule around it. Somewhere inside the phenomenon is a Locum who never learned to hand everything back, and the world has decided this is a service.
nodes.playstyle: Keep everything going. Allies you attend cannot truly fall, positions cannot truly empty, and endings on your field are demoted to interruptions.

abilities.name: Through Vacancies
abilities.desc: Any allied role — sentry, healer, standard-bearer — continues functioning for 60 seconds after its holder falls, performed by no one visible.

abilities.name: Unreported
abilities.desc: Allies reduced to nothing are instead indisposed: absent, safe, and formally alive, returning at one-third health after 20 seconds.

abilities.name: The Kept Lighthouse
abilities.desc: Designate one structure or position; it operates, defended and maintained, whether or not anyone is there. Permanently.

abilities.name: Demoted to Interruption
abilities.desc: Once per day, be a fallen ally so faithfully that the world continues them; win within the hour and the fall is reclassified.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and be discovered to have been, for some decades, several institutions in good standing.
Hold the last life you promised past your own death; the order still lists the post as filled, and it is.
Keep one small thing going forever — a lamp, a bakery, a birthday — as the quiet practice of the office.
Refuse, at last, to continue one thing whose time has honestly come, and learn that the office includes the ending of things kept too long.

nodes.name: The Stranger
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the universal unknown
nodes.lore: Before introduction, every person wears a placeholder face, seen all your life and never noticed. That face is on loan from an office. The Stranger is whom you have not met yet — all of them, everywhere at once — and the knock of an unknown hand on any door is, in strict cosmology, always the same visitor.
nodes.playstyle: Be everyone's not-yet. Arrive as whoever was unanticipated, stand outside all knowledge and targeting, and end enemies who were, fatally, expecting someone.

abilities.name: On Loan
abilities.desc: Wear the placeholder face; until you act, no mind, spell, or instrument can assign you identity, intent, or threat.

abilities.name: The Same Visitor
abilities.desc: Knock on any door in the world and be admitted; thresholds count you as expected, since strangers always are.

abilities.name: Unanticipated
abilities.desc: Your first strike each battle comes from outside the enemy's expectations entirely and cannot be parried, blocked, or foreseen.

abilities.name: Never Introduced
abilities.desc: Retroactively have never met an enemy; all their preparations, wards, and grudges against you address no one.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and lend yourself to the world's absences: wherever someone is unknown, be them, until the handshake.
Stand on the far side of every unopened door for one night, and open none of them; anticipation is the office's whole estate.
Be prayed to, accidentally, by travelers who ask that the stranger be kind, and be kind, statistically.
Meet, at the end of all the not-yets, the one person who was never strange to you, and let the office lapse for an evening.

nodes.name: Face of Kings
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the one face of sovereignty
nodes.lore: Study the coins of forty realms: allowing for engravers, it is one face. Study the statues, the seals, the memory a subject keeps of a king glimpsed once in childhood — one face. Sovereignty has only ever had the one, lent out reign by reign, and the Painted King has finally stopped lending it. Kings rule. The Face reigns.
nodes.playstyle: Be what crowns borrow. All authority on the field is on loan from you; revoke it, redirect it, or wear any ruler's legitimacy directly.

abilities.name: The Lent Face
abilities.desc: Strip a leader's legitimacy; their commands carry no weight, and their insignia visibly stop resembling them.

abilities.name: On Every Coin
abilities.desc: You are recognized as sovereign wherever money, seals, or standards exist; deference is immediate, and argument is expensive.

abilities.name: Reign by Proxy
abilities.desc: Crown any creature on the field for 60 seconds; it wields your decrees, and all oaths sworn to any crown bind to it.

abilities.name: The Death-Mask Answers
abilities.desc: Consult any royal death-mask; masks remember their reigns, whatever became of the wearers.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and unfasten the state face at last, before the assembled court, revealing — the court agrees, unanimously, at once — the state face.
Recall the face from one unworthy king and watch his own guards fail to find him in the throne room.
Sit for the final portrait and let it succeed. The realm will hang it in every hall, and it will supervise.
Reign nowhere in particular and everywhere by default, as the face beneath every crown's fit.

nodes.name: The Widow's Walk
nodes.role: Apotheosis — the watch for the missing
nodes.lore: Somewhere between departure and return there is a place where waiting is kept, and it is staffed. The Widow's Walk is the vigil for everyone unaccounted for — soldiers missing, ships overdue, names caught between lists — and coastal houses grow the railed platform uninvited, the way ground grows springs. While the watch is kept, no one is unwaited-for.
nodes.playstyle: Keep watch over the not-yet-returned. Anchor the missing to the world, punish those who would make more widows, and hold open the possibility of coming home.

abilities.name: Unaccounted For
abilities.desc: Allies lost, captured, or missing anywhere remain alive, findable, and tethered while you keep the watch; despair cannot claim them.

abilities.name: Overdue
abilities.desc: Recall one missing ally to the field once per battle; they arrive weathered, furious, and briefly unkillable.

abilities.name: The Railed Height
abilities.desc: Stand your watch above any field; you see all of it, cannot be surprised, and your grief-auras extend to everything you see.

abilities.name: No More Widows
abilities.desc: Mark an enemy whose next kill would widow or orphan; the kill fails, and the grief it would have made falls on them instead.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and take the watch that has no relief: the world's own widow's walk, above every harbor at once.
Wait, correctly, for someone the whole world agrees is lost, until the world is wrong.
Let the platforms rise on roofs you never visited, and keep watch through every one; architecture is only grief with railings.
Be the last thing the returning see before harbor and the first grief spared; when someone comes home, somewhere, take your evening off.

families.name: Ferryman
families.tagline: The fare is named before the pole touches water.
families.description: Every river has a far side, and every far side has a fee. The Ferryman keeps the crossings the world pretends are edges — rivers, borders, the gap between waking and gone — carrying whatever pays across whatever cannot otherwise be crossed. They do not judge the passenger and they do not forgive the fare. The oldest contract has one clause, and they are it.

nodes.name: Ferryman
nodes.role: Hybrid support — passage, positioning, price
nodes.lore: Every river-town keeps one, and no town remembers hiring them. A first-rank Ferryman holds a pole, a flat-bottomed boat, and the license to a single modest crossing. The guild's first law is taught before swimming is: name the fare before the pole touches water, and give no one credit.
nodes.playstyle: Move allies where they should be and enemies where they should not, then charge for it. Weak alone in open field; strong at any edge, bank, or line.

abilities.name: Pole-Plant
abilities.desc: Drive the pole into any surface and swing yourself or a willing ally three paces across a gap, line, or threshold.

abilities.name: First Fare
abilities.desc: Name a toll on the ground between you; enemies crossing it uninvited pay in speed, arriving late and winded.

abilities.name: Shallow Draft
abilities.desc: You and one passenger ignore difficult ground, water, and marsh; you cannot be slowed while moving toward a bank.

abilities.name: Sounding
abilities.desc: Read any water, gap, or border at a glance, learning its depth, its danger, and what it charges to cross.

progressionSteps: Apprentice to a ferry no map marks, and learn to pole standing before you learn to sit.
Memorize the fare-table of your crossing: what coin, what kind, and what is never accepted.
Carry your first silent passenger at night, and do not ask what the far bank wanted with them.
Swear the Bank Oath: the fare before the water, the passenger before the weather, and no credit, ever.

nodes.name: Oarsworn
nodes.role: Mobility support — carries allies across the field
nodes.lore: The Crossing begins at the shoulder. An Oarsworn has rowed against enough floods to be granted right-of-way: the guild seal that lets a boat pass where passage is refused — spring rivers, contested borders, other people's harbors. Soldiers wave them through, then wonder afterward why they did.
nodes.playstyle: Carry the party: haul allies across gaps, through lines, and out of encirclement. You win engagements by deciding where they happen.

abilities.name: Way-Leave
abilities.desc: Declare a lane across the field; allies moving along it cannot be blocked, slowed, or stopped until they reach the far side.

abilities.name: Heavy Weather Stroke
abilities.desc: Row through what should capsize you: while carrying an ally, damage to both of you is reduced until you land.

abilities.name: Both Banks
abilities.desc: Swap yourself with a willing ally anywhere in sight, provided a line of water, blood, or spilled drink connects you.

abilities.name: Following Sea
abilities.desc: Allies who move where you have just moved gain speed; the path remembers your stroke for six seconds.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10 and row a flooded river alone, upstream, with a passenger who never stops talking; deliver them dry.
Present your palms to the guild: the oar's callus must sit deeper than any sword's.
Cross a border at war twice in one night, once in each direction, saluted both times.
Take the Oar Oath: the crossing does not care whose war it interrupts.

nodes.name: Fareholder
nodes.role: Controller — tolls enemy movement and action
nodes.lore: The Toll begins at the strongbox. A Fareholder keeps every fare in trust until its crossing completes — coin, keepsakes, quieter payments — and learns the fare-law's one rule by heart: everything that crosses pays, and nothing that pays is judged. Passengers trust them the way they trust bridges: completely, and without affection.
nodes.playstyle: Price the battlefield: enemies pay in speed, strength, or steel to act near you. You do little damage; you make everything expensive.

abilities.name: Turnpike
abilities.desc: Raise an invisible gate across a line; the first enemy through surrenders their swiftest thing until the fight ends.

abilities.name: Fare in Hand
abilities.desc: Catch one projectile mid-flight and hold it as a fare; release it along any crossing you own before it expires.

abilities.name: Small Fares
abilities.desc: Everything an enemy does within your circle costs slightly more — mana, stamina, footing — and the difference is paid to you.

abilities.name: No Credit
abilities.desc: An enemy who cannot pay a toll they triggered is stopped at the line until they can.

progressionSteps: Reach level 10 and keep the fare-box of a busy crossing for a season; return every fare whose crossing failed, to the copper.
Refuse a king's coin because it was clipped, politely, in front of the king.
Accept one fare that is not money, and record honestly what it was worth.
Swear the Toll Oath: you are not the price; you only hold it.

nodes.name: Fordwright
nodes.role: Terrain support — builds crossings where none exist
nodes.lore: Fordwrights make the crossing before they make the trip: stepping-stones raised in a night, fords persuaded through spring floods, a plank across a chasm the map calls final. They do not bend distance — they obtain permission. Engineers hate them; the rivers, for reasons unrecorded, do not.
nodes.playstyle: Build the field's geography in your favor: fords, plank-roads, stepping-stones. Your party crosses what enemies must go around, or into.

abilities.name: Raise Ford
abilities.desc: Persuade a ford up through any water or mire; allies cross it dry, and it dissolves under the first hostile boot.

abilities.name: Six Stones
abilities.desc: Set six stones across any gap — air included; each stone bears one crossing and then sinks politely.

abilities.name: Gangplank Law
abilities.desc: Extend a plank to any ledge, deck, or battlement in sight; allies boarding by it count as passengers, and passengers arrive.

abilities.name: The River Agrees
abilities.desc: Any crossing you build cannot be destroyed while a passenger is on it; the river honors work in progress.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and ford a river in flood by building as you cross, one stone ahead of your own feet.
Bridge a chasm the guild lists as final; charge the guild full fare to inspect it.
Ask a river's permission properly — three nights listening at the bank — and be able to prove it said yes.
Leave one crossing unbuilt because the far side asked you to.

nodes.name: Palefarer
nodes.role: Spirit ferrier — sustains, rescues, carries the dying
nodes.lore: Palefarers pole the water that runs between waking and gone. They carry the newly dead outward and, when the fare allows, the nearly dead back — a carrier's errand, not a collector's. Necromancers covet their manifest and are refused; the Palefarer keeps no souls, only appointments.
nodes.playstyle: Ride the line between banks: pull dying allies back across, ship wounded to safety, and make the enemy's dead simply leave.

abilities.name: Back Across
abilities.desc: Take an ally dying within the last six seconds aboard and pole them back; they wake ashore, fare already paid.

abilities.name: Outbound Manifest
abilities.desc: Name a corpse or risen dead as your passenger; it boards, and nothing — including its former master — may recall it.

abilities.name: Pale Water
abilities.desc: Flood a zone ankle-deep with the between-river; the dying there stop dying, and the dead there start leaving.

abilities.name: Coin for the Quiet
abilities.desc: Place a coin on a fallen enemy; they cannot be raised, animated, or questioned, being already mid-crossing.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and row the pale water by night until you can tell, by the sound of boarding, who is coming back.
Deliver your first outbound passenger and never look astern; whatever calls from the wake is practicing your voice.
Bring one passenger back alive with the fare paid in full beforehand; the guild audits these crossings twice.
Refuse a necromancer's charter, at any offered price, and file the refusal.

nodes.name: Toller
nodes.role: Attrition controller — prices enemy action, punishes evasion
nodes.lore: Tollers keep the fare-law itself: the old schedule of what may cross and what it costs, memorized whole because writing it down has been tried. The name is exact — they collect the toll, and they toll the bell, and seasoned travelers listen carefully to which service they are getting.
nodes.playstyle: Attach prices to everything the enemy wants: movement, casting, retreat. Collect steadily; when a toll is dodged, the bell settles it.

abilities.name: Schedule of Fares
abilities.desc: Post prices over the field: each kind of enemy ability costs an added tithe of health when used.

abilities.name: Dodger's Bell
abilities.desc: An enemy who crosses your line without paying is tolled: marked, slowed, and audible to your whole party through walls.

abilities.name: One for the River
abilities.desc: Collect a dodged toll by force: strike for damage equal to everything the target has avoided paying this fight.

abilities.name: Peak Rates
abilities.desc: Declare high water: for ten seconds every toll you have posted doubles, and payment is taken up front.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and recite the schedule of fares entire, in the dark, while the examiners ring wrong bells.
Toll the bell once for a crossing that failed, and make it sound different from the bell for one that succeeded.
Collect from something that has never paid: a flood, a rumor, a lordling with soldiers. The law does not list exemptions.
Set the fare for a crossing no one has ever survived; set it fairly.

nodes.name: Wharfinger
nodes.role: Strip specialist — enemies leave things behind
nodes.lore: Wharfingers keep the near bank's long sheds, where everything that may not cross is left: weapons, grudges, names, one lamed horse of unusual opinions. They decide nothing — the fare-law decides — but they take custody of the law's leavings, and their inventory is the most dangerous room in most provinces.
nodes.playstyle: Disarm by regulation: make enemies shed weapons, wards, and blessings at your lines. What they carry past you, they chose to pay for.

abilities.name: Leave It at the Bank
abilities.desc: Draw a customs line; the first enemy across sheds one carried enhancement, which sits in your custody until the fight ends.

abilities.name: Contraband
abilities.desc: Name one enemy item or effect contraband under the schedule; while it is borne, its bearer takes steady damage and cannot hide.

abilities.name: Impound Hook
abilities.desc: Hook a shield, weapon, or familiar out of enemy hands into the shed; reclaiming it requires visiting you.

abilities.name: The Long Shed
abilities.desc: Open the shed's door briefly; one item ever surrendered at any wharf is available to your hand for a minute.

progressionSteps: Reach level 25 and inventory the long shed without touching anything twice; several items will try for a second touch.
Take custody of a cursed crown, a live grudge, and a sword that weeps; label all three legibly.
Return a surrendered thing to its owner after thirty years, unchanged and unasked-about.
Refuse to sell one item from the shed to someone with excellent reasons; the shed does not sell.

nodes.name: Pontifer
nodes.role: Mass mobility engine — permanent lanes for many
nodes.lore: Pontifers hold that a crossing, once made, belongs to everyone forever; they pole the first passage and then pin it open — stone, piles, standing right-of-way. Three churches want the title back and have been invoiced for it. Where a Pontifer has worked, no border is entirely serious again.
nodes.playstyle: Institutionalize movement: standing lanes, party-wide crossings, choke points converted to boulevards. Slow to set up; afterward your whole army travels like rumor.

abilities.name: Pin the Crossing
abilities.desc: Make one of your crossings permanent for the battle; it cannot be destroyed, closed, or owned by anyone else.

abilities.name: Public Passage
abilities.desc: All allies gain your right-of-way on lanes you have declared, boarding, crossing, and disembarking without triggering attacks.

abilities.name: Toll-Free Day
abilities.desc: Suspend your own tolls; for eight seconds every ally ability that moves someone costs nothing and cannot be interrupted.

abilities.name: Bridgehead
abilities.desc: Where any lane of yours touches enemy ground, allies within it take reduced damage and cannot be pushed off.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and pin open a crossing an empire ordered closed; survive the empire's letters.
Build a passage a beggar and a king use the same afternoon, at the same fare.
Hold a bridgehead against a Ford-Drowner sent to sink your work; convert nothing, bury nothing, simply out-remain them.
Answer the churches' final demand for the title in person, by building them a bridge to argue across.

nodes.name: Consigner
nodes.role: Escort bulwark — guarded delivery, unstoppable transit
nodes.lore: A Consigner's manifest is a promise with a keel under it. Whatever boards, lands: the dead, the dying, the priceless, the pursued. Storms are negotiated with; pirates are billed for the delay. The order's records show no passenger lost in four centuries, and one poler still out, presumed rowing.
nodes.playstyle: Take custody of someone or something and deliver it through anything. While the consignment lives, you are very hard to argue with.

abilities.name: Under Consignment
abilities.desc: Take one ally under consignment; harm meant for them arrives to you instead, reduced, until you set them down safely.

abilities.name: All Weather
abilities.desc: While escorting, you cannot be slowed, feared, or turned around; the delivery consumes the effect and logs it.

abilities.name: Signed On Landing
abilities.desc: On safe delivery, you and the delivered are healed and briefly untouchable while the paperwork completes.

abilities.name: Never Lost
abilities.desc: If your consignment would die aboard, the crossing extends instead: both of you vanish midstream and land three seconds later, alive.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and deliver a witness through a city that has voted twice to prevent it.
Complete the oldest open consignment on the order's books; the passenger will have grown strange in transit.
Refuse the Hulkswains' offer to take an undeliverable off your hands; there is no such word on your manifest.
Row four days awake with a fever aboard, and make the landing on the tide you quoted.

nodes.name: Strickler
nodes.role: Precision striker — exact, normalized damage
nodes.lore: Stricklers carry the strickle: the plain rod drawn across a grain-measure to level it exact. Their order holds the fare-law's whole authority to live in that gesture — nothing heaped, nothing hollow. A Strickler's strike costs what the schedule says, to the grain, and pity has never once adjusted a measure.
nodes.playstyle: Deal exact sums: strikes that ignore variance, armor, and fortune. The enemy faces the schedule instead of chance, and the schedule does not miss.

abilities.name: Struck Level
abilities.desc: Draw the strickle: your next strike deals exactly its listed damage, unmodified by armor, wards, luck, or opinion.

abilities.name: Heaped Measure
abilities.desc: An enemy who overpays — overextends, overcommits, overcasts — has the excess swept off and delivered to you as vigor.

abilities.name: Short Weight
abilities.desc: Detect any enemy carrying more than they paid for; your next hit removes exactly the difference.

abilities.name: The Grain
abilities.desc: Once per fight, reduce any incoming blow, however vast, to the smallest unit on the schedule.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and level a measure blindfolded to the single grain, three times, while the examiners heap it unfairly.
Charge your own order the posted fare for your own investiture, and count the change aloud.
Find the crossing where a Kindtaker accepted a memory as fare, and reassess it in grain; deliver the difference, whichever direction it runs.
Break your strickle the day it flatters you, and cut the next from wood that has never grown beside a market.

nodes.name: Sequester
nodes.role: Custodial tank — impounds harm, holds effects
nodes.lore: A Sequester is the law's strongroom given a pulse. Whatever is surrendered at the bank, they hold — unworn, unspent, unread — against the day someone returns with the claim-chit. Their order has waited out dynasties. Undergivers call the sheds a dam across the river's due; Sequesters file the accusation with the rest.
nodes.playstyle: Impound the fight: catch blows, spells, and rages into custody and hold them. Release nothing; outlast everything. Your inventory is your armor.

abilities.name: Into Custody
abilities.desc: Catch an incoming spell or projectile into the shed; it counts toward nothing and waits there, tagged, until the fight ends.

abilities.name: Claim-Chit
abilities.desc: Issue a chit; an ally may instantly reclaim anything of theirs the enemy stripped, dispelled, or stole this fight.

abilities.name: Storage Fees
abilities.desc: While holding impounded effects, you gain armor per item held; the shed appreciates being full.

abilities.name: Deep Shelf
abilities.desc: Once per battle, impound one enemy — whole — for six seconds; they wait on a shelf, safe, untargetable, and furious.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and stand custodian of the long shed through a fire, a flood, and a very persuasive claimant with no chit.
Hold a surrendered war-banner through the war that wanted it back; return it afterward to whoever still fits the claim.
Learn each shelf blind, because some of what you keep goes quieter when watched.
Refuse the Undergivers' annual demand to sink shelf nine; renew, in writing, your offer to hold them too.

nodes.name: Ford-Drowner
nodes.role: Infiltration mover — one-way, traceless crossings
nodes.lore: Every crossing the guild pins open, someone crosses third: the army behind the refugee, the huntsman behind the bride. Ford-Drowners pole you over and give the ford back to the river — drowned, unmapped, gently denied. Pontifers call them misers of passage. Drowners answer that they have never once been followed.
nodes.playstyle: Cross once, cleanly, and unmake the way behind you. Insertions, extractions, and ambushes from banks the enemy is certain are unreachable.

abilities.name: Drown the Ford
abilities.desc: Collapse any crossing — yours, theirs, natural — into deep water the moment your last passenger steps off.

abilities.name: No Second Crossing
abilities.desc: Enemies cannot follow a route your party has used this fight; the way is simply not there for them.

abilities.name: Quiet Pole
abilities.desc: Your boat makes no sound, wake, or reflection for one crossing; divination watching the water sees only water.

abilities.name: Meet the River
abilities.desc: A pursuer who steps where your ford was meets the river instead, and the river was waiting.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and unbuild, stone by stone in one night, the finest crossing you ever made; leave the river looking uninterrupted.
Ferry a bride, her dowry, and her reasons over water no pursuit can name; drink the toast at the wedding under a different name.
Sink a Pontifer's newest bridge and attend the inquiry as a helpful witness; contribute nothing but sympathy.
Cross your last open crossing; from now on, every way you go closes behind you like water, because it is water.

nodes.name: Hulkswain
nodes.role: Zone anchor — shelters and fields the in-between
nodes.lore: Consigners deliver everything; Hulkswains keep what delivery would break. Off the far bank ride the hulks — roomy, patient vessels for passengers no shore will have: the half-dead, the mid-oath, the interrupted. A Hulkswain feeds them, counts them, and asks nothing. The banks call it a fleet of ghosts. The crew call it home.
nodes.playstyle: Anchor a hulk to the fight: a floating refuge whose strange passengers lend cold hands. Shelter the failing; unsettle the shore.

abilities.name: Berth the Broken
abilities.desc: Take a crippled, cursed, or dying ally aboard the hulk; aboard, their condition pauses and cannot worsen.

abilities.name: Cold Crew
abilities.desc: Your in-between passengers crew the rails; enemies within reach are gripped by hands that hold no opinion of them.

abilities.name: Neither Bank
abilities.desc: Stand aboard and be neither living target nor dead one; abilities keyed to either miss you entirely.

abilities.name: Deep Berths
abilities.desc: The hulk holds any number of passengers; each aboard slows enemy action nearby, the field disliking so much in-between.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and stand the night watch on a hulk alone; by morning, know which sounds are the boat.
Take aboard a passenger the Consigners have failed to land three times, and stop trying to land them.
Feed the hulk's oldest passenger their remembered meal, correctly, without being told.
Sign the standing manifest: you berth what boards, and you do not ask it to finish dying.

nodes.name: Kindtaker
nodes.role: Exchange specialist — converts anything into passage
nodes.lore: Kindtakers accept the fares coin cannot carry: a season of sleep, a mother's name, the color blue. Their order holds that a price is an exchange, and equal is a word with rooms in it. Stricklers call this heresy by weight. Kindtakers call it the schedule, read aloud slowly.
nodes.playstyle: Trade in kind: convert health to speed, an enemy's fury to your fare, a cooldown to a crossing. Everything is currency if named correctly.

abilities.name: Payment in Kind
abilities.desc: Accept a named thing from a willing ally — sight, seconds, warmth — and convert it into any equal boon on your schedule.

abilities.name: What It's Worth
abilities.desc: Appraise an enemy's active effect and take it as a fare; they lose it, and you may spend it once.

abilities.name: Strange Tender
abilities.desc: Pay any cost of your own abilities with something other than the listed resource; the exchange rate is honest and unkind.

abilities.name: Fare of Last Resort
abilities.desc: Once per day, accept a fare coin cannot match — a fear, a first memory — to buy an ally out of a killing blow.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and accept a fare of pure kind — no coin aboard — for one full year of crossings, and end the year solvent.
Ferry a passenger who owns nothing, and leave both banks agreeing the fare was paid in full.
Refuse to take a fare the passenger will die without, even offered freely; equal is not the same as everything.
Sit the Stricklers' audit and balance every strange fare against grain; when the rod comes up level, say nothing satisfying.

nodes.name: Undergiver
nodes.role: Sacrificial nuker — sinks value for power
nodes.lore: Undergivers row the surrendered things to the deep channel and give them under, weighted, with the words said right. The river works, their order teaches, and workers are paid — every shed hoarding the river's share silts a crossing somewhere shut. What the water accepts, it remembers fondly. Sequesters are not invited to launchings.
nodes.playstyle: Feed the river to wield it: sink items, advantages, and your own reserves; the water answers with current, weight, and reach.

abilities.name: Given Under
abilities.desc: Sink something of value — yours or impounded — into the channel; the river returns it as raw force within ten seconds.

abilities.name: The Deep Channel
abilities.desc: Open the channel beneath one enemy; they are pulled waist-deep into water that exists only for them.

abilities.name: Ballast Rite
abilities.desc: Bind a sunk offering to a target; they carry its weight, slowing and sinking through whatever they stand on.

abilities.name: The Bore
abilities.desc: Sink every fare you hold; a river bore crosses the field, carrying allies forward on its back and enemies underneath it.

progressionSteps: Reach level 40 and carry your first full cargo to the deep channel alone; whatever asks to stay aboard, nothing stays aboard.
Sink a fortune with witnesses and no speech; the river dislikes being thanked on its behalf.
Give under one thing you were keeping for yourself. The order will not name it. You will.
Watch the drought year end where you sank the crown, and file no claim of credit.

nodes.name: The Right of Way
nodes.role: Unstoppable vanguard — movement as standing law
nodes.lore: Histories agree something crossed; they disagree on what. The Right of Way is passage with a person somewhere inside it: where they walk, a lane exists, has always existed, and admits whoever follows. Sieges have ended because a supply road politely appeared. Armies do not block them. Armies are, briefly, traffic.
nodes.playstyle: You are the road. Wherever you move becomes lane, and stays lane; your party rides the wake through everything the map calls solid.

abilities.name: Eminent Passage
abilities.desc: Declare passage through any obstacle — wall, army, mountain-root; the lane opens for your party and remains a public crossing.

abilities.name: Give Way
abilities.desc: Everything hostile in your lane must yield: enemies are pressed to the verges and held there while traffic passes.

abilities.name: Ancient Easement
abilities.desc: Reveal the easement that always ran through here; treat one interior, fortress, or formation as open ground for a minute.

abilities.name: Through Traffic
abilities.desc: Allies moving along your lanes cannot be targeted until they stop; the law protects those in transit.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and walk a straight lane through the Shut City, whose charter forbids one; leave the charter amended.
Open a crossing so old the river that used it is gone; something else will be using it.
Be refused by the mountain wall of Kellwatch, once; return with the paperwork.
Grant one army passage and its enemy passage the same day, and collect both fares at the posted rate.

nodes.name: The Manifest
nodes.role: Mass deliverer — everyone aboard arrives
nodes.lore: Somewhere the full manifest is kept: every passenger every ferry ever promised, and one hand still checking names. The Manifest is that hand, or the list, or both — the order stopped distinguishing. Speak your name near water and it is entered; entered names arrive, eventually, whatever intervenes. Refunds are not a concept.
nodes.playstyle: Board the field: take whole parties into consignment and land them where promised. Nothing you carry can be lost, and you carry everyone.

abilities.name: Boarding Call
abilities.desc: Every ally in earshot boards your protection at once; while aboard, they move with you and share your defenses.

abilities.name: Entered Names
abilities.desc: Enter an ally on the manifest; death becomes delay, and they step ashore alive at your next completed crossing.

abilities.name: The Long Way Round
abilities.desc: Any ally banished, taken, or teleported against their will lands on your deck instead; abduction is just boarding, mislabeled.

abilities.name: Delivered Entire
abilities.desc: Land all passengers at a point you name; each arrives whole, healed, and facing the right direction.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and find the poler four centuries out; take the oar for the last mile and let them sleep.
Deliver a passenger whose destination sank a century ago; the manifest does not accept geography as an excuse.
Read the whole manifest once. Do not linger on your own entry, which is long, and still open.
Add one name no ferry promised, pay the fare yourself, and never tell them.

nodes.name: Dead Reckoning
nodes.role: Absolute striker — exact outcomes, no variance
nodes.lore: Navigators reckon dead when no stars serve: position known by speed, heading, and time alone. Dead Reckoning is what the Stricklers' exactness became when it stopped needing instruments — a person who knows precisely where everything is, what everything costs, and how far each living thing stands from its far bank. They are never consulted twice.
nodes.playstyle: Remove chance from the engagement: your strikes land for known sums, enemy variance is struck level, and every outcome you quote occurs to the grain.

abilities.name: Reckoned Position
abilities.desc: Know every enemy's exact position always; stealth, illusion, and distance are bookkeeping errors, corrected.

abilities.name: Quoted Sum
abilities.desc: Announce the damage of your next strike; it deals exactly that, through anything, and cannot be a different number.

abilities.name: Strickle Sweep
abilities.desc: Sweep the field with the strickle: every temporary advantage, heap, and hollow on both sides is struck level at once.

abilities.name: Distance to the Bank
abilities.desc: Once per day, measure what stands between a target and the far bank, and remove exactly that much.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and cross an ocean of fog with no star, no coast, and no error you are willing to discuss.
Quote a war's cost to both crowns beforehand, to the man; decline to round.
Measure the far bank's distance from yourself, and carry the number without behaving differently.
Break your last instrument on the gunwale; the reckoning is you now, and it does not drift.

nodes.name: The Left Bank
nodes.role: Eternal custodian — impounds without limit
nodes.lore: Below the sheds the shelves continue, and the Left Bank walks them: keeper of everything no one returned for — abdicated crowns, unfinished vows, one war both sides surrendered and neither collected. The office holds all of it in perfect trust. Any valid chit is honored instantly. None has ever been presented.
nodes.playstyle: Hold the fight itself in custody: impound damage, effects, even outcomes, and shelve them indefinitely. You do not win engagements; you retain them.

abilities.name: Custody Without End
abilities.desc: Impound any effect on the field — hostile, friendly, ongoing — indefinitely; it resumes only if lawfully claimed, which is unlikely.

abilities.name: Shelf of Wars
abilities.desc: Shelve an entire enemy assault for ten seconds: projectiles, charges, and spells wait in the stacks, tagged.

abilities.name: Unfinished Things
abilities.desc: Wield one unclaimed item from the deep shelves each battle; it is always, unsettlingly, exactly what was needed.

abilities.name: No Valid Chit
abilities.desc: Damage that would kill you is impounded instead, pending a claim against your life; claims are processed slowly.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and walk past the last numbered shelf; number what you find, and do not read anything that asks you to.
Take custody of a thing that is still happening.
Refuse a claimant with every reason and no chit; grieve afterward, off the premises.
Outwait something immortal that wants shelf nine opened. Bring nothing to read. It will blink.

nodes.name: The Midnight Ford
nodes.role: Covert mover — crossings that never happened
nodes.lore: Somewhere there is a ford that exists only while it is being crossed, at an hour that is not quite on the clock, and the Ford-Drowners' last rank is its keeper — or the ford itself; Drowners decline to clarify. Fugitives find it. Pursuers find the river. Histories mention it only in retractions.
nodes.playstyle: Move the party without evidence: crossings that close, tracks the water takes back, arrivals no scout can explain. Ambush is your commute.

abilities.name: Never Crossed
abilities.desc: Move your party across any water or border; all traces, memories, and divinations of the crossing drown behind you.

abilities.name: The Ford Opens
abilities.desc: At night, open the midnight ford between any two banks you have seen; it exists only underfoot, and only once.

abilities.name: Take the Tracks Back
abilities.desc: The river reclaims your party's tracks, scents, and dropped evidence across the last minute; pursuit reverts to guessing.

abilities.name: Wrong Bank
abilities.desc: A pursuer who follows your crossing arrives at the wrong bank: alone, reversed, and wet in a place with no name.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and cross the same border every night for a year without the border ever having been crossed.
Drown your own ferry's name and take no new one; the ford does not answer to names.
Carry a hunted family over, then drink in the hunters' camp while they describe the river that stopped them.
Be seen mid-crossing once, by one child, and become the story that keeps the ford fed.

nodes.name: The Mooring
nodes.role: Sanctuary anchor — harbors the unlandable
nodes.lore: Downriver of everywhere, the hulks ride at permanent anchor, and The Mooring is what they are tied to. Half-dead kings, unfinished ghosts, plague ships no port will name — everything the banks refuse rides there in good order, fed, counted, and unjudged. The banks call it a menace. The banks are not asked.
nodes.playstyle: Anchor the hulks to the battlefield: a floating sanctuary that shelters allies, holds the in-between, and slowly unnerves everything hostile ashore.

abilities.name: Make Fast
abilities.desc: Anchor the Mooring in any terrain; allies aboard cannot be targeted, and dying allies stabilize at the waterline.

abilities.name: Strange Crew
abilities.desc: The in-between crew your rails; enemies boarding uninvited are handled by passengers the banks never learned to fight.

abilities.name: No Port Asked
abilities.desc: Take aboard anything mid-effect — a cursed ally, a burning charge, an unexploded spell; aboard, it simply waits.

abilities.name: Slip Moorings
abilities.desc: Weigh anchor and relocate the whole sanctuary, crew and sheltered included, to any water in sight.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and take the oldest hulk's watch for a decade; learn every passenger's name and no passenger's story.
Turn no one away for a hundred years. The hundred-first will test the record. Turn them not away either.
Hold anchor through the fleet-burning at Corvel Reach; take aboard both admirals, in-between and furious, in adjacent berths.
Refuse the Consigners' final audit: nothing aboard is undelivered; everything aboard is home.

nodes.name: The Going Rate
nodes.role: Reality broker — anything traded for anything
nodes.lore: Ask what a thing truly costs, and somewhere the answer settles. The Going Rate is that settling, walking: once a Kindtaker, now the living equivalence between all things — a bridge priced in sons, mercy quoted in rain. Markets drift when they pass and correct when they leave. No one audits why.
nodes.playstyle: Exchange anything for anything: health for distance, fury for weather, an advantage for its opposite. Every fight is a market only you can read.

abilities.name: Settle the Price
abilities.desc: Fix the cost of one action battlefield-wide; anyone — ally or enemy — performing it pays your posted rate.

abilities.name: Equivalence
abilities.desc: Convert one effect into any other of equal worth: a wall into healing, a curse into distance, at once.

abilities.name: Market Correction
abilities.desc: When an enemy gains something unpaid-for, the field corrects: the gain transfers to whoever, by your reading, covered its cost.

abilities.name: The Rate for Ruin
abilities.desc: Quote the price of destroying you aloud; attackers pay it up front, per attempt, in whatever they value most.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and price something the guild swears is priceless, and be neither struck down nor haggled with.
Sell nothing for a year while every market on the river quietly obeys you.
Quote the rate between two lives once, to no one, over water, and let the river carry it away unheard.
Hold the scale steady through a famine and a festival without once flattering either.

nodes.name: The River's Share
nodes.role: Catastrophe channel — the river collects
nodes.lore: Every river takes a share — a boot, a bridge, some years, occasionally a town. The River's Share is the hand it collects with: once an Undergiver, now the water's own reach, deciding nothing and collecting everything on schedule. Where the share is paid, floods arrive polite. Elsewhere, the rate is the rate.
nodes.playstyle: Channel the river's collections: drownings, bores, whole currents redirected through dry land. Sink what you hold for power that arrives like weather.

abilities.name: Collection Day
abilities.desc: The river rises through the field to collect: every enemy loses their heaviest advantage to the water at once.

abilities.name: Undercurrent
abilities.desc: Run a current through solid ground; enemies standing in its path are swept, tumbled, and deposited where you choose.

abilities.name: The Polite Flood
abilities.desc: Call a flood that parts around allies and property whose share is paid, which is to say, yours.

abilities.name: Drowning Wages
abilities.desc: Sink your own health into the channel; the river returns it during the fight as force, threefold, on its own schedule.

progressionSteps: Reach level 60 and row out at high water with everything you own; row back with the boat.
Negotiate nothing with the flood at Marren Weir; walk beside it instead, pointing out what is spoken for.
Give under the thing the order kept back for three centuries; attend the silence afterward.
When the river hands you something in return — it will choose the hour — take it without counting.

nodes.name: The Causeway
nodes.role: World-road — passage as permanent law
nodes.lore: Some offices are roads. The Causeway runs over every water at once — the standing right of passage the world keeps where a Ferryman used to be. No map shows it whole; every ferryman poles a mile of it. Empires legislate against it and then, quietly, pave their bit.
nodes.playstyle: Exist as infrastructure. Allies anywhere travel your spans; enemies discover that every road they hold has always, legally, been yours.

abilities.name: Every Water at Once
abilities.desc: Open crossings over all waters on the field simultaneously; your party treats the map as a suggestion with bridges.

abilities.name: The Standing Mile
abilities.desc: Raise a mile of causeway anywhere, instantly, permanently; it counts as your ground, and your ground has rules.

abilities.name: Public Works
abilities.desc: Any lane an ally has ever crossed with you re-opens on command, wherever it was, whatever replaced it.

abilities.name: The World Yields
abilities.desc: Once per day, everything between your party and a destination becomes crossing: armies, seas, walls, weather — all briefly lane.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and lay the span nobody commissioned, between banks nobody agreed were banks; collect the fare anyway, forever.
Let a war end because both armies used you to go home.
Be paved, cursed, taxed, and renamed by six empires; outlast the empires and keep the tolls posted in the old amounts.
When the last river dries, remain: some crossings outlive their water.

nodes.name: The Far Shore
nodes.role: Arrival incarnate — every landing is theirs
nodes.lore: Arrival is not an event; it is a place all events borrow — and the place is kept. The Far Shore is what the Manifest became when the last name was delivered: the standing guarantee that crossings end, that decks give way to ground. Sailors thank the wrong saints for it. The saints forward it on.
nodes.playstyle: Guarantee arrival: allies land where intended, always. Everything hostile that travels also arrives — exactly where your manifest says, which is the difference.

abilities.name: Everything Arrives
abilities.desc: No movement near you can be interrupted, reversed, or lost midway; all of it completes, at destinations you administer.

abilities.name: Assigned Landing
abilities.desc: Assign every enemy arrival — charge, teleport, reinforcement — a landing of your choosing; they come ashore there instead, on schedule.

abilities.name: Safe Ashore
abilities.desc: Allies who reach ground you stand on are healed whole and cannot be moved from it against their will.

abilities.name: The Last Delivery
abilities.desc: Once per day, declare any single journey complete immediately: the traveler, missile, or army arrives now, at the destination the fare actually covered.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and deliver the manifest's final name, then keep the office open; arrival does not retire.
Stand on every shore at once for one tide, and be the reason wrecks wash up findable.
Receive a fleet, a plague, and a prophecy in the same harbor week; land all three correctly.
When something without a destination finally comes across the water, be its far shore too. Everything lands. That is the office.

nodes.name: The Fixed Price
nodes.role: Cost incarnate — everything charges exactly
nodes.lore: Under all haggling there is one true cost per thing, and the world checks it against something. The Fixed Price is what it checks against: the office the strickle was always pointing at. Near them, nothing arrives free — no spell, no crown, no rescue. Gods pay retail. This is resented, and exact.
nodes.playstyle: Enforce true cost: every hostile action charges its full price in real time, no exemptions. You rarely strike; the fight simply stops being affordable.

abilities.name: True Cost
abilities.desc: Every enemy ability now costs what it actually costs — health, years, memory included; the schedule is universal and posted.

abilities.name: No Exemptions
abilities.desc: Immunities, invulnerabilities, and free actions are repriced; using one charges its full listed rate, backdated to the field's start.

abilities.name: The Fare Before the Water
abilities.desc: Anything attempting to affect you must pay first; unpaid effects wait at the line indefinitely.

abilities.name: Exact World
abilities.desc: Once per day, level the entire engagement to the schedule: all heaped advantages on every side are struck to true measure.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and price the act of pricing; pay it once, in full, and never speak of the denomination.
Audit a miracle to the grain and send no report; the numbers were correct, which was the miracle.
Hold the rate steady while an age of wonders begs for discounts; wonders can afford it. That is what makes them wonders.
Become the reason nothing in the world is free, and accept how rarely you are thanked at the posted rate.

nodes.name: The Strand
nodes.role: Shore of custody — everything lost, kept
nodes.lore: Everything the world loses washes up somewhere, and the somewhere is kept. The Strand is that shore and its keeper, no longer separable — the long beach where drowned fleets, dropped names, and misplaced centuries lie tagged above the tideline. Nothing rots there; nothing is sold. Beachcombers who find it once spend their lives failing to find it twice.
nodes.playstyle: Fight from custody: everything ever lost is briefly yours to field. Impound what threatens, retrieve what saves, and shelve entire assaults above the tideline.

abilities.name: Above the Tideline
abilities.desc: Move an entire hostile force's momentum above the tideline; the assault lies inert on the sand until lawfully claimed.

abilities.name: Tagged and Waiting
abilities.desc: Produce any object ever lost by anyone; it is in your custody, catalogued, and briefly willing to help.

abilities.name: The Wreck Returns
abilities.desc: Raise a drowned ship, bridge, or fortress from your inventory as terrain, positioned as suits the crossing.

abilities.name: Lost with All Hands
abilities.desc: Declare an enemy formation lost at sea; they wash up on your strand, disarmed, dazed, and thoroughly catalogued.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and walk the beach past where your lamp ends; file what you find there under things that found you first.
Re-tag the oldest item yourself; the old tag goes on a shelf, tagged.
Return one thing at last to a valid chit, and learn why the office celebrates quietly and only once a century.
When the sea itself asks for its dead back, show it the schedule of claims and the window's hours.

nodes.name: The Fog Bank
nodes.role: Weather of crossings — concealed passage everywhere
nodes.lore: Rivers keep one weather for their own business. The Fog Bank is it: the low white hour in which crossings happen off the record — held, the way offices are held, by whatever the Midnight Ford became when even a ford was too much evidence. Sailors call it a fog bank. The river knows which bank it means.
nodes.playstyle: Arrive as weather. Inside your fog, allies move unseen and unrecorded; enemies navigate by memory, which stayed on the other bank.

abilities.name: Roll In
abilities.desc: Settle over the field as fog; all allied movement inside is invisible, silent, and deniable afterward, including to diviners.

abilities.name: Off the Record
abilities.desc: Events inside your fog leave no evidence: no tracks, no witnesses' certainty, no scrying purchase, no history.

abilities.name: The White Hour
abilities.desc: For ten seconds, every ally may cross to anywhere else inside the fog, each crossing unobserved even by the others.

abilities.name: Lost in the Bank
abilities.desc: An enemy who enters the fog uninvited exits somewhere reasonable and wrong, having paid for a crossing they never booked.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and rise off the water for good; leave the pole standing upright midstream for the next rumor to find.
Settle over a war for nine nights until both armies, unable to find it, go home; take credit as weather does — never.
Be cursed by every navy and blessed by every smuggler in the same season, and roll in regardless of either.
When someone crosses inside you and forgets they ever left, keep their crossing safe until they need it never to have happened.

nodes.name: The Harborage
nodes.role: Refuge eternal — shelter for the unlandable
nodes.lore: Beyond the last chart there is anchorage for everything no port will take, and the world keeps it staffed. The Harborage is that office: the Mooring grown to the size of its manifest — plague fleets, half-gods, cities that sank still arguing. Storms detour around it. Nothing has ever been turned away, and the light is always lit.
nodes.playstyle: Be the safe water: berth allies, casualties, and unstable powers alike. What shelters with you cannot be reached; what attacks you is becalmed first.

abilities.name: Open Berths
abilities.desc: Shelter any number of allies in numbered berths; berthed allies heal, cannot be targeted, and disembark when they choose.

abilities.name: Becalm
abilities.desc: Still the water and air around hostile forces; their momentum, projectiles, and morale hang slack in the calm.

abilities.name: Harbor Light
abilities.desc: Any ally, anywhere, may spend their movement arriving at you instead; the light is always lit.

abilities.name: Take the Unstable Aboard
abilities.desc: Berth a catastrophe in progress — a detonation, a rift, a dying god — and let it ride at anchor, indefinitely.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and drop anchor beyond the last chart; send back one buoy so the desperate can be lucky.
Berth the fleet that burned at Corvel Reach, every deck, both admirals still furious, and post quiet hours.
Grant anchorage to something the gods themselves misplaced overboard, and list it under general cargo.
Keep the light lit through the age when nothing comes; the office is the lit light, not the traffic.

nodes.name: The First Question
nodes.role: Threshold law — every price, named first
nodes.lore: Before any threshold anywhere is crossed, there is an instant in which the price is named. The First Question is that instant, held as an office. It was a Kindtaker once; now it is the pause on every doorstep, the breath before every bargain, the question the pole asks the water. Nothing crosses unasked. Nothing ever has.
nodes.playstyle: Interpose the question: every hostile act must first settle what it costs, with you. The fight proceeds only as fast as its answers.

abilities.name: Name the Price First
abilities.desc: No enemy ability begins until its price is named through you; complicated things take longer to price, and hostility is complicated.

abilities.name: Asked and Answered
abilities.desc: An enemy who accepts their named price acts freely but pays it; one who refuses is still standing at the threshold.

abilities.name: The Pause
abilities.desc: Extend the instant before one crossing — a blow, a spell, a betrayal — indefinitely; the world waits with surprising grace.

abilities.name: Free Crossing
abilities.desc: Waive one ally's every cost for six seconds; the First Question asks them nothing, which the wise find more frightening.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and be present at every naming of every fare at once; keep each one straight, and keep none of them.
Ask the first question again — the one the first river asked the first bank — and this time, wait for the whole answer.
Stand in the pause before a god's decision until the god, uncomfortable, names their price like everyone else.
Never answer for anyone. The office is the question. It has always only been the question.

nodes.name: The High Water
nodes.role: Flood sovereign — collection at world scale
nodes.lore: Rivers rise on a schedule older than the towns that complain about it. The High Water is that schedule, kept past the need for a person: where it stands, valleys remember being riverbed and behave accordingly. The share is collected entire, unhurried, and without opinion. Lawsuits are filed against it annually. It banks them.
nodes.playstyle: Fight as the flood season: raise the field's water until the enemy position is riverbed in denial. Slow, total, indifferent to walls.

abilities.name: Riverbed Memory
abilities.desc: Remind any ground it was river once; it floods from below, and structures on it recall floating, briefly.

abilities.name: The Crest
abilities.desc: Arrive as the flood's crest across the field; enemies are swept, allies are lifted, and the fare is collected en route.

abilities.name: Spoken For
abilities.desc: Mark allies and their works as spoken for; no water of yours touches them, at any height.

abilities.name: The Share, Entire
abilities.desc: Once per day, collect a battlefield's share in one rise: every hostile structure, mount, and advantage goes to the river.

progressionSteps: Reach level 85 and rise once past every recorded mark, gently, collecting only what was always the river's; the argument will outlive the towns.
Spend one year as low water so complete that even the share goes uncollected; return to find the banks planted with thanks and higher fences.
Collect a tyrant's bridge and a village's footlog in the same rise, at the same rate, and be sung about entirely wrong both times.
When the world needs reminding where the water reaches, be the mark.
